The lecture introduces Discrete Stochastic Processes, emphasizing that the primary challenge in probability is creating appropriate models for real-world problems rather than merely solving well-posed mathematical exercises. Real-world probability deals with uncertainty in often non-repeatable situations, while mathematical probability relies on models with specified axioms. Games of chance are easier to model because they are repeatable. Flawed models, even with correct mathematics, can lead to disasters, as illustrated by financial crises caused by experts using poor models. The professor quotes Whitehead: “Seek simplicity and distrust it,” urging that simple models be questioned.

The course focuses on discrete stochastic processes, defined as probability models where sample points represent functions of time, with discrete time and discrete-valued random variables. Topics include counting processes, Poisson processes, renewal processes, Markov processes, random walks, and martingales. These are useful in communication, networks, computer systems, queuing, risk management, and many other fields.

The lecture reviews probability axioms. A probability model consists of a sample space, a collection of events (subsets closed under countable unions and complements), and a probability measure. Axioms: the probability of the entire sample space is 1; probabilities are nonnegative; for disjoint events, the probability of their union equals the sum of their probabilities. Consequences include the empty set having probability 0, the complement rule, and the union bound.

Independence is defined: events A and B are independent if the probability of their intersection equals the product of their probabilities. Combining models via Cartesian product with independence yields a valid model. The issue of indistinguishable outcomes, like rolling two white dice, is addressed by treating them as distinguishable to assign probabilities.

A random variable is a function from the sample space to real numbers, requiring that sets {ω: X(ω) ≤ x} are events. This ensures the distribution function F(x) = P(X ≤ x) exists, is non-decreasing, starts at 0, and approaches 1. Random variables may be discrete (having a probability mass function), continuous (having a density), or neither; the distribution function handles all cases. The professor encourages developing rigorous proof skills to reason about complex systems.

The Drive concept is a pass-game combination involving two receivers from the same side: a 10-12 yard basic (in-cut) route and a 3-4 yard shallow crossing route trailing underneath. It creates a triangle read for the quarterback and stresses linebackers. The concept is similar to the shallow cross but adds a tight end route to create a rub. It performs well against man coverage, as receivers stay on the move, and against Cover 4, where the basic-post combination binds the field safety, potentially opening a deep throw or a numbers advantage underneath. It struggles against Cover 2 and Cover 3 due to multiple underneath defenders outnumbering the routes. Route adjustments differ: against man, receivers stay on the move; against zone, they sit in open voids. The quarterback’s progression is: peek the post pre-snap, then read go route, shallow cross, basic, and check-down. Variations include pairing with a bunch formation to create picks against man coverage, and attaching it to the backside of schemes for a quick outlet against blitz.

This document describes the Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificate and the Key Distribution System (KDS) interface used to retrieve certificate information for AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization-Secure Nested Paging (SEV-SNP) technology. It defines terms including ARK (AMD Root Key, the root CA), ASK (AMD SEV Key, the intermediate CA), VCEK (leaf certificate), TCB, SPL, and KDS. The product name is determined via CPUID and used in certificate fields and URLs. The certificate chain consists of the ARK, ASK, and VCEK. CA certificates and the Certificate Revocation List (CRL) are available at https://kdsintf.amd.com. VCEK certificates are X.509v3, generated on request, with a validity period from one day before issuance to seven years after. Extensions describe TCB components; the hardware ID length is 64 bytes for Family 19h processors and 8 bytes for Family 1Ah. The KDS HTTP interface provides endpoints to retrieve a VCEK certificate for specified SPL values, the certificate chain in PEM format, and the CRL in DER format. Rate limiting and error codes apply. The service allows pre-fetching certificates by requesting any SPL within its legal range, enabling local caching for future firmware updates.

Hybrid NbN/Si-SiGe microwave quantum circuits were fabricated with coplanar waveguide (CPW) resonators on a 100 nm NbN film sputtered on a Si/Si₀.₇Ge₀.₃ wafer. The device layout includes four resonators; two λ/4 resonators are studied. Fabrication involved a buffered oxide etch dip, reactive DC sputtering of NbN, e-beam lithography, CF₄/Ar dry etching, and a novel deep etching step using SF₆/C₄F₈ that etched 1 μm into the SiGe buffer layer in the CPW gaps to shift substrate-vacuum interfaces away from high electric fields and reduce loss. TEM/STEM imaging showed epitaxial SiGe layers but oxidation in the Si cap layer. Two samples (S1, S2) with identical geometry were measured over four cooldowns across two years. Fundamental resonance frequencies were approximately 5.04–5.60 GHz. Power-dependent spectroscopy at 50 mK gave internal quality factors (Qᵢ) for S1 from 860 (single-photon regime) to 1064 at higher powers, and for S2 from ~500 to 600. Qᵢ saturation at low photon numbers was observed in later measurements, and Qᵢ remained stable over two years, demonstrating long-term robustness. An RLC circuit model extracted kinetic inductance and other parameters. Comparison with other Ge/SiGe resonators showed comparable Qᵢ; NbN provides magnetic field tolerance and a high superconducting gap frequency. Loss analysis indicated that two-level system (TLS) losses contribute, but the dominant loss mechanism is power-independent scattering loss from structural imperfections and wafer conductivity. Temperature-dependent measurements (150 mK to 1.7 K) revealed a blue shift then red shift in resonance frequency, attributed to TLS and quasiparticle losses, respectively. Power-temperature measurements confirmed thermal saturation of TLS defects. The discussion notes that Si/SiGe heterostructures are promising for low-loss quantum circuits; the calculated relaxation time for a gatemon qubit using this wafer is ~14 ns, indicating need for further optimization. The work demonstrates a CMOS-compatible platform with reproducible high Qᵢ and stability, and the deep etching strategy effectively mitigates losses, bridging superconducting and semiconductor qubit technologies.

The present invention relates to a vehicle sensing system that uses one or more radar sensors with a two-dimensional array of transmitting (Tx) and receiving (Rx) antennas. The antennas are arranged in multiple rows and columns, not in a single row or column. A control applies two-dimensional multiple input multiple output (2D MIMO) processing to the outputs of the receiving antennas, creating an enhanced two-dimensional virtual aperture that provides improved angular accuracy and resolution in both horizontal and vertical directions simultaneously, without time-multiplexing. In an illustrated embodiment, the array includes 12 Tx antennas and 16 Rx antennas, specifically three rows of four Tx antennas and four columns of four Rx antennas, achieving 192 virtual receivers. Other arrangements are possible, preferably with at least four Tx and six Rx antennas (24 virtual receivers), more preferably at least eight Tx and ten Rx antennas (80 virtual receivers), and most preferably at least twelve Tx and sixteen Rx antennas (192 virtual receivers). The system detects objects exterior to the vehicle and can be used in driver assistance systems such as autonomous driving, automated parking, blind spot detection, cross traffic alert, lane change assist, automatic emergency braking, pedestrian detection, turn assist, and intersection collision mitigation. Optionally, the radar sensing system may be combined with image data from exterior cameras, fusing the data to enhance object detection. The system may generate alerts or control vehicle systems like steering or braking upon detecting an object of interest.

Ethereum’s enshrined Proposer–Builder Separation (ePBS) with dual deadlines creates a free option problem: builders can withhold blobs after commitment to avoid losses if external market signals turn unfavorable, leaving slots empty and degrading liveness. The paper provides a theoretical and empirical study. The option value and exercise probability increase with volatility, option window length, and the share of CEX-DEX arbitrage value in blocks. Historical data show an average 0.82% missed block rate (34.6% of all missed blocks) for an 8-second window, but rates spike to 5.5% daily during high volatility. The option is more profitable when CEX-DEX arbitrages dominate block value. Mitigations include shortening the option window (reducing exercise probability but sacrificing scalability) and imposing penalties (static or dynamic), both shown to reduce exercise probabilities. A dynamic penalty mechanism using online gradient descent can adapt to conditions, achieving low exercise rates with modest average penalties.

The 2025 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine was awarded to Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, and Shimon Sakaguchi for discovering regulatory T cells (T-regs). T-regs prevent the immune system from attacking the body, calm it after infection or wound healing, and prevent fetal rejection. Sakaguchi discovered T-regs in 1995. Brunkow and Ramsdell identified a mutation causing autoimmune disease in mice, later linked to a gene Sakaguchi found, and revealed human mutations in 2001. The prize is 11 million Swedish kronor. Scientists aim to harness T-regs for cancer and overactive immune conditions. The Karolinska Institute announced the prize on October 6.

The speaker, soon to leave office and resume the title of citizen, thanks Vice President Mondale, his Cabinet, and especially the American people. He expresses confidence in the U.S. to meet future challenges due to its inner strength, principles, political system, and people's ingenuity.

He reflects on the presidency: powerful yet constrained, requiring support and consent of the people through Congress and institutions. Every American has a right and duty to shape the nation's future; press and public scrutiny are vital. The government now serves 230 million and leads globally.

He warns that doubt in government fuels single-issue and special interest groups, distorting the national interest; the common good is everyone's responsibility. Therefore, the presidency must remain strong, as the President represents all the people.

He pledges support for the new President-elect. He then addresses three issues as a world citizen: nuclear destruction, planetary stewardship, and human rights.

Nuclear threat: 35 years after Hiroshima, the risk persists and grows as superpower arsenals expand and other governments may acquire weapons. An all-out war would unleash a World War II's destruction every second, killing more in hours than all past wars. The U.S. must stay strong but also work with all nations to control and reduce nuclear arms. Success requires public concern and demands. Rocket technology also enables peaceful space exploration, showing Earth's unity and fragility.

Environmental stewardship: dangers include mineral depletion, topsoil erosion, pollution, and population growth, threatening air, water, and land. Without action, the world in 2000 will sustain less life. Acknowledging realities is the first step; resource problems can be solved with courage and foresight.

Human rights: enhancing freedoms through democracy and fighting deprivation, torture, terrorism, and persecution is crucial. The struggle transcends differences. The U.S. must perfect rights at home: education, medical care, ending discrimination, jobs, and freedom from injustice and religious intolerance.

He describes the era as a time of transition with tensions, resource competition, and stresses. He urges adherence to American values, which are necessities. Quoting the Declaration, he says democracy is unfinished; each generation must renew its meaning. For this generation, life is nuclear survival, liberty is human rights, and the pursuit of happiness is a planet devoted to nourishment.

He will ensure a smooth transition, continue praying for American hostages in Iran, and asks for prayers. He will return to the South, reflect, and work as a citizen for the nation's founding values. He expresses gratitude and bids farewell.

Treatment options for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) are limited, and resistance to androgen signaling inhibitors and taxanes is common. Androgen receptor (AR) wild-type and splice variants ARv567 and AR-V7 differentially associate with microtubules (MTs); ARv567 is MT-associated and sensitive to taxanes, while AR-V7 shows reduced MT association, constitutive nuclear activity, and correlates with taxane resistance. A computational method tracks EB1 comets to measure MT polymerization dynamics and infer pause and shortening behaviors. In M12 isogenic prostate cancer cell lines, AR-V7 expression increased MT growth speeds by over 40% compared to AR-wt, and spatial MT organization differed. Patient-derived organoids were established from primary, micro-metastatic, and distant metastasis tissues. Reducing Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor concentration helped select tumor cells, as benign cells were more dependent on it. Androgen-independent circulating tumor cells (CTCs) can be as small as 6.6 µm in diameter, smaller than typical CTCs, and express PSMA. Paclitaxel treatment suppressed fast-polymerizing MTs and reduced overall polymerization rates in breast cancer cells. pVHL and GSK3β cooperatively regulate MT stability; loss of pVHL or GSK3β-mediated phosphorylation of pVHL increases MT turnover, while GSK3 inhibition attenuates turnover in quiescent cells. Drug resistance can be assessed via circular Hough transform to detect MT bundling, and by correlating live-cell MT dynamics with gene expression signatures. The approach aims to anticipate resistance and inform personalized therapy by matching MT dynamics patterns to drug susceptibility.

Hungary, a country of 9.7 million people with a negative natural increase rate, has a multiparty parliamentary democracy and an economy that shifted from agriculture to industry and services, experiencing recession and later recovery under Prime Minister Viktor Orbán’s policies. Public education, compulsory from ages six to sixteen, involves a free choice of school policy with selective admissions, rigorous secondary examinations, and a structure spanning pre-primary through post-secondary levels. General education teacher preparation requires bachelor’s or longer undivided programs with practical training, while special education teacher training is a four-year specialized university program followed by a two-year compulsory traineeship and continuous in-service training.

Hungary established its special education system in 1802 and the first special education teacher college in 1906. A committee of professionals diagnoses disabilities and recommends placement, though parents make the final decision. This study developed a method to select AI-detected chest X-ray (CXR) abnormalities for urgent reporting to support faster lung cancer diagnosis. Two cohorts were used: a retrospective cohort of 1,282 patients with confirmed lung cancer and an abnormal CXR, and a prospective cohort of 13,802 primary care CXRs where an AI system (Annalise Container CXR, detecting 124 findings) ran in shadow mode. Findings were initially grouped into CRITICAL, HIGH, and STANDARD priority categories. Three prioritisation strategies were evaluated using prevalence ratios between cohorts. Strategy 1 (19 findings with ratio >5) achieved 92.82% sensitivity and 87.21% specificity. Strategy 2 (all HIGH findings with ratio >2) achieved 97.27% sensitivity and 62.68% specificity. Strategy 3, incorporating clinical judgement, selected 32 findings and achieved 95.87% sensitivity, 79.11% specificity, and 99.95% negative predictive value, assuming a 1% detectable cancer prevalence in the referral cohort. The approach combines empirical prevalence data with clinical review to balance sensitivity and NPV, providing a reproducible framework for AI integration into radiology workflows. Limitations include regional data and reliance on assumed prevalence; future directions involve external validation and patient involvement.

Donchian Channels, invented by Richard Donchian decades ago, consist of an upper band (high of the last N bars) and a lower band (low of the last N bars). The article omits the optional middle band. Donchian, born in 1905, is regarded as a pioneer in quantitative analysis and the “father” of trend following; he never wrote a book but discussed the indicator in a newsletter. The indicator is popular but markets have changed, becoming less trending and faster, especially stocks. Donchian Channels are traditionally used as a trend-following indicator for commodities and currencies, but not for stocks. The Turtle experiment also used a variation. Curtis Faith backtested two Donchian Channel strategies on currencies, commodities, and Treasuries from 1996 to 2007, achieving CAGRs of 29.4% and 57.2%, though over a short period. Testing a simple trend-following strategy on the S&P 500 (1960–October 2021, long only, no dividends) yielded an unleveraged CAGR of 4.57% versus buy-and-hold’s 7.15%, with lower maximum drawdown. Optimization suggested around 40 days for the upper band and a shorter lower band, reducing drawdown further but lowering returns. The article then inverted the indicator to a mean-reversion approach on SPY (1993–October 2021). Optimizing entry lookback periods from 5 to 50 days showed 15 days as best, though all periods worked. A 5-day lookback produced a 9.16% CAGR, roughly matching buy-and-hold, with small drawdowns and a high win rate; this was previously an overnight strategy. The article notes Donchian Channels work better as trend-following on commodities and currencies because those markets move up and down frequently, unlike stocks, but trend-following entails large drawdowns. Donchian Channels and Bollinger Bands appear similar but are not identical and can yield different backtest results. Overall, Donchian Channels function as a trend-following indicator in commodity/currency markets and as a mean-reversion indicator for stocks.

The defendant Solomon Montlake appealed his conviction for first-degree grand larceny. A prior trial ended when the judge dismissed the jury after the prosecution's case, following repeated instances of the prosecutor accusing defense counsel of being a criminal. At the second trial, the court overruled Montlake's plea of former jeopardy. The appellate court held that a trial judge may discharge a jury during trial for a substantial reason, and here the dismissal was a proper exercise of discretion, particularly because the defendant had earlier moved to withdraw a juror. The court also found that permitting cross-examination of a defense alibi witness about unpaid rent was an unwise exercise of discretion but not reversible error. However, the trial court's instruction on the alibi defense was fundamentally erroneous. The judge charged that the jury could not acquit based on alibi unless it established "that the defendants could not have been at the place where the crime is alleged to have been committed," which required excluding even a bare possibility of presence. The appellate court stated that the burden of proof on alibi is not on the defendant; if the alibi evidence, together with all other proof, raises a reasonable doubt as to presence, acquittal is required. Because the erroneous instruction was prejudicial, the judgment of conviction was reversed and a new trial granted.

The lecture continues the discussion on pseudorandom graphs, focusing on n, d, lambda graphs: d-regular graphs where all eigenvalues except the top one are at most lambda in absolute value. The expander mixing lemma states that a small lambda implies the discrepancy property (edges between vertex sets are close to random expectation). Examples beyond random graphs are given via Cayley graphs, constructed from a group and a symmetric subset S. A specific example is the Paley graph, a Cayley graph of Z/pZ (p prime ≡1 mod 4) with S as quadratic residues. Its eigenvalues are computed explicitly: eigenvectors are powers of a p-th root of unity, and eigenvalues are exponential sums. Using Gauss sums and squaring, the non-top eigenvalues are shown to be ±(p+1)/2, small relative to the degree (p-1)/2, confirming pseudorandomness. For Abelian groups, eigenvalues correspond to Fourier coefficients; for non-Abelian groups, representation theory plays a similar role.

The equivalence between discrepancy (DISC) and eigenvalue (EIG) conditions for Cayley graphs is then examined. For general graphs, DISC does not imply EIG (counterexample: a large random d-regular graph plus a small K_{d+1} component has discrepancy but second eigenvalue d). However, for Cayley graphs, a theorem by Conlon and Zhao states that DISC(ε) and EIG(8ε) are equivalent. The proof uses Grothendieck's inequality: there exists a constant K such that the supremum of a bilinear form over unit vectors in a ball is at most K times the supremum over ±1 vectors. From DISC, the bilinear form with ±1 vectors is bounded by 4εdn. By symmetrizing using group rotations, the eigenvalue condition (supremum over unit vectors) is bounded by 8εd, yielding EIG.

Finally, the lecture addresses how small lambda can be for fixed d and large n. The Alon-Boppana bound states that the second largest eigenvalue λ₂ ≥ 2√(d-1) − o(1). Two proofs are given. The first uses the Courant-Fischer characterization: construct a vector centered at a vertex v with weights (d-1)^{-i/2} for vertices at distance i<r, zero otherwise; the Rayleigh quotient yields at least 2√(d-1)(1−1/(2r)). Choosing two vertices at distance ≥2r gives two such vectors with disjoint supports; a linear combination orthogonal to the all-1's vector yields the bound. The second proof (trace method) lower bounds closed walks of length 2k from a vertex by the number in an infinite d-regular tree, which is at least the k-th Catalan number times (d-1)^k. Using the trace of A^{2k} and letting n,k→∞ with k=o(log n), one obtains max(|λ₂|,|λ_n|) ≥ 2√(d-1) − o(1). The number 2√(d-1) is the spectral radius of the infinite d-regular tree. The bound is tight, with graphs achieving it, and open problems remain. The next topic will be graph limits.

The passage details SD card command protocols. CMD55 (APP_CMD) indicates that the following command is an application-specific command (ACMD), with rules for defined/undefined and legal/illegal ACMDs. CMD6 is a switch function command used to change access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit; mode 0 checks support, mode 1 sets functions. High-Speed mode (25 MB/s) is enabled via CMD6. CMD8 checks interface voltage conditions. SDHC/SDXC cards use block addressing with fixed 512-byte block length, while SDSC uses byte addressing. Clock can be stopped, requiring 8 clock cycles after transactions. CRC7 protects commands/responses, CRC16 protects data. Command classes (CCC) define supported commands. Responses include R1, R1b, R2, R3, R6, and R7. Speed classes (2, 4, 6, 10) and UHS/Video speed grades define performance using Allocation Units (AUs) and Recording Units (RUs), with parameters Pw, Pm, and FAT update times. CMD20 controls speed class recording for SDXC. Card status, SD status, and task status convey error and state information.

A Simple Moving Average (SMA) is a technical analysis tool that calculates the average closing price of a security over a specified period, smoothing price data to help identify trend direction. The formula sums closing prices over “n” periods and divides by n. A rising SMA indicates an increasing price trend, while a falling SMA indicates a decreasing trend. Long-period SMAs can serve as potential support or resistance levels.

Backtests of moving average crossover systems show that short-term SMAs (e.g., 5-day) are more profitable when buying after the close crosses below the average, indicating mean-reversion tendencies. For long-term SMAs, buying when the close crosses above the average performs better, supporting trend-following. The best result was buying on a cross above the 200-day SMA and holding for 200 days, yielding an average 10.93% per trade (excluding dividends). Longer holding periods generally improved returns.

The SMA is a lagging indicator because it uses past prices. Shorter periods increase sensitivity to price changes and generate more frequent trades, while longer periods reduce sensitivity and trade frequency. Compared to the Exponential Moving Average (EMA), the SMA has more lag because it weights all prices equally, whereas the EMA emphasizes recent prices. The SMA can be misleading on stocks with seasonal or cyclical patterns, as it may not reflect underlying fluctuations. Its starting point can influence values, especially in volatile markets. An SMA of exactly zero is theoretically possible only if all closing prices in the period are zero, which is practically impossible. The SMA can be applied to non-price data like volume or economic indicators to identify trends. In strongly trending markets, the SMA confirms trend direction; in range-bound markets, it may produce false signals.

This study compared a chest radiograph-based biological aging clock (CXR-Age) with first-generation (Horvath Age) and second-generation (DNAm PhenoAge) epigenetic clocks in 2,097 participants from the Project Baseline Health Study. CXR-Age correlated moderately with chronological age (r=0.50), while epigenetic clocks correlated highly (r≈0.93–0.95). CXR-Age acceleration was not significantly associated with epigenetic age accelerations. CXR-Age acceleration was significantly associated with higher coronary artery calcium, lower pulmonary function (especially DLCO % predicted), and reduced physical function and increased disability. DNAm PhenoAge acceleration showed similar associations with cardiovascular disease and frailty, but these were attenuated in younger adults, whereas CXR-Age associations remained robust in adults as young as 45. Horvath age acceleration showed no significant associations. Plasma proteomic analysis found CXR-Age acceleration associated with decreased abundance of CDH13 and ApoD; DNAm PhenoAge acceleration associated with 13 proteins, including CDH13. Manual review of chest radiographs showed low CXR-Age acceleration images were clearer, while high acceleration images often had lung abnormalities. The results suggest CXR-Age captures broad aging processes and may enable opportunistic screening using routine chest radiographs.

This study developed and evaluated PhenoID, a two-step natural language processing pipeline to automatically extract and normalize phenotypic findings from dysmorphology physical examination notes in electronic health records. A purpose-built EHR form with structured buttons and free-text boxes was used to collect observations. A corpus of 890 organ system observations was manually annotated by four clinical genetics physicians with Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms, achieving an inter-annotator F1 of 0.844. The PhenoID pipeline consists of an extractor module, a Bio-ClinicalBERT-based sequence labeler using a BIO schema to detect spans of abnormal findings while ignoring normal ones, and a normalizer module, a transformer classifier that maps each extracted span to the most specific HPO term ID. To handle disjoint and overlapping mentions, two heuristics (Noisy-BIO and Recast-BIO) were applied. The normalizer was trained on annotated data supplemented with generated examples from HPO preferred terms and synonyms. On a held-out test set, PhenoID achieved an F1 score of 0.717 for normalization, outperforming six existing systems (txt2hpo, Doc2HPO, NeuralCR, PhenoTagger, PhenoBERT). When provided with gold-standard spans, the normalizer reached an F1 of 0.82, approaching human performance. Error analysis revealed that common normalization errors stemmed from imperfections in the HPO ontology, descriptive clinical language, misplaced model attention, and prediction of hypernyms. The extractor correctly ignored 98.4% of negated (normal) findings. The authors conclude that improving span extraction and enhancing semantic understanding of the ontology are key future directions, and note the limitation of data from a single institution.

Averaging down is a trading method where an investor buys additional shares of a stock after its price has fallen, lowering the average purchase price. This reduces the price increase needed to reach breakeven or profit. For example, buying 100 shares at $45 then another 100 at $30 lowers the average cost to $37.50, requiring only a 25% rise to break even instead of 50%. However, the stock may continue falling, increasing losses. The strategy can be part of a scale-in entry plan, but it is not a complete strategy on its own; it may serve more as a psychological comfort. Its suitability depends on the investor's timeframe: long-term investors who understand the company may use it to accumulate shares at lower prices, while short-term traders may find it risky because they cannot easily distinguish temporary dips from serious declines. A backtest on SPY using RSI signals and splitting equity into two 50% buys showed that averaging down produced a smoother equity curve, improved trading metrics, and better risk-adjusted returns compared to no averaging down, with less time in the market and reduced drawdowns. The passage concludes that stocks are the best asset class for averaging down due to their tendency for mean reversion, and that backtesting is essential to reduce failure risk.

The background describes optical detection of range (LIDAR) using techniques such as chirped detection and phase-encoded detection, and notes that 3D point clouds can be generated by such systems. The summary of the invention provides a method for automatic classification of objects represented by 3D point clouds. The method includes obtaining a 3D point cloud of an object's surface, extracting a surface normal at a point to define a translational and rotational invariant coordinate system, and extracting feature variable values. A first classification statistic (e.g., spin image) and a second classification statistic (e.g., covariance matrix) are computed. The closest match of the first statistic to a set of N classes estimates a first class; similarly, the second statistic estimates a second class. If the first and second classes differ, a third classification statistic (e.g., iterative closest point) is computed based on a closest fit between the point cloud and model point clouds for only the first and second classes. The object is assigned to the class with the closest fit, and a device is operated based on the assigned class. An apparatus includes a laser source, splitter, optical coupler, optical detector, and a processor configured to perform the method steps. The detailed description further explains chirped detection, hardware embodiments, k-d trees, point cloud generation, and the classification statistics.

New research in PNAS demonstrates that harnessing competition among pathogens can extend the life of existing drugs and prevent drug resistance. Drug resistance, which hinders control of HIV, tuberculosis, and malaria, arises from mutations that allow pathogens to survive treatment, but resistant pathogens often have a resource acquisition cost. Researchers manipulated a nutrient in mice infected with malaria parasites, using dietary intervention alongside traditional drugs. Limiting the nutrient prevented drug-resistant strains from emerging, while providing it led to treatment failure in 40% of mice. The effect relied on competition: resistant parasites survived when alone but were suppressed when sensitive parasites were present. This ecological approach could allow continued use of drugs even when resistance is present. Future work involves identifying resources for which resistant strains have greater needs and developing intervention strategies, potentially during drug development to extend a drug's lifetime.

This study used Mendelian randomization to investigate causal relationships between gut microbiota, plasma metabolites, and fibromyalgia. Six gut microbiota taxa showed causal effects on fibromyalgia: family Enterobacteriaceae, genus Butyricicoccus, genus Coprococcus1, and order Enterobacteriales were associated with reduced risk, while genus Eggerthella and genus Ruminococcaceae UCG005 were associated with increased risk. No reverse causality was detected. Eighty-two plasma metabolites were causally associated with fibromyalgia, including known metabolites, metabolite ratios, and unknown metabolites. Pathway enrichment analyses identified primary metabolic pathways: caffeine metabolism (involving AFMU, 7-methylxanthine, 1-methylxanthine), alpha-linolenic acid metabolism (involving EPA and SDA), and synthesis/secretion/inactivation of GLP-1 and incretin (involving D-mannose, EPA, oleoyl-EA). Mediation analysis indicated that 2,3-dihydroxypyridine and palmitoylcholine mediate the effect of Enterobacteriaceae and Enterobacteriales on fibromyalgia, with mediation proportions of 14.91% and 12.34% respectively. The study suggests dietary interventions such as limiting caffeine, increasing omega-3 fatty acids, adopting a low glycemic index diet, and reducing high-oxalate foods. Limitations include lack of demographic subgroup data, European ancestry of GWAS datasets, and the need for further experimental validation.

The RSI, ADX, and IBS are technical indicators used for short-term trading. ADX measures trend strength without indicating direction; backtesting indicates a 5–10 day period and a strong-trend threshold of 30–40. IBS is a mean-reversion indicator (0–1) where low values are bullish and high values are bearish. A simple IBS strategy on QQQ (buy when IBS < 0.2, sell when > 0.8) showed a profit factor of 1.92. Backtests of an IBS strategy on QQQ yielded an average gain of 0.78%, CAGR 12.1%, and risk-adjusted return of 32% with 38% time invested. An RSI strategy on SPY produced a CAGR of 7.5% and risk-adjusted return of 18% with 41% time invested. An ADX-only strategy on SPY had a CAGR of 6.5% and risk-adjusted return of 10.3% with 63% time invested. Combining two of the indicators on SPY resulted in 270 trades, average gain 0.86%, risk-adjusted return 56% with 14% time invested, and only one losing year (2018). The Chaikin Oscillator was developed by Marc Chaikin in the 1980s. It measures accumulation or distribution and is distinct from the Chaikin Money Flow Indicator. The indicator oscillates around zero and aims to measure the momentum of stock moves. Its calculation involves four steps: determining a money flow multiplier using the closing price, calculating money flow volume, updating the Accumulation/Distribution Line (ADL), and subtracting a longer exponential moving average (EMA) of the ADL from a shorter one. The Amibroker code is: MFM = ((Close – Low) – (High – Close)) / (High – Low); MFV = MFM*Volume; ADL = MFV + Ref(MFV,-1); CO = EMA(ADL,3) – EMA(ADL,10). The short EMA reflects short-term momentum, the long EMA longer-term momentum. Signals are generated via bullish or bearish divergences and crosses above or below the zero line; above zero indicates buying pressure, below zero selling pressure.

Quantified tests on the S&P 500 were conducted. A strategy buying when the oscillator crosses above zero and selling when it crosses below zero, with optimized 10- and 20-day averages, yielded a CAGR of 2.4% over twenty years. Flipping the criteria (buy on cross below zero, sell on cross above zero) improved results due to mean reversion; using a 10-day short-term and 50-day long-term average produced 287 trades, an average of 0.54 per trade, a profit factor of 1.76, and a max drawdown of 37%. Bearish divergence occurs when price makes a higher high but the oscillator does not, signaling reduced buying pressure; bullish divergence occurs when price makes a lower low but the oscillator forms a higher low, suggesting a possible upward reversal. Both require confirmation via oscillator crossing into negative or positive territory.

Another strategy applied a two-day RSI to the Chaikin Oscillator (3- and 10-day EMAs), buying when the RSI reading is below 5 and selling when the close exceeds the prior day’s high. This resulted in 216 trades, an average of 0.3% per trade, a profit factor of 1.6, and an 18% max drawdown. A third strategy required the stock’s two-day RSI below 20 and the Chaikin Oscillator above zero, selling on a close above yesterday’s high; it also produced 216 trades, 0.3% average per trade, a profit factor of 1.6, and a 17% max drawdown. The author found no significant profitable strategy among ten tested, but notes the oscillator may still gauge buying or selling pressure, with positive values indicating accumulation and negative values distribution. The Chaikin Oscillator’s use of EMAs of the ADL is similar to MACD methodology, identifying momentum, potential trend reversals, and accumulation/distribution.

The present disclosure relates to an autonomous vehicle management system (AVMS) that controls autonomous vehicle operations safely using artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning techniques. The AVMS receives sensor data from onboard or remote sensors, builds and continuously updates a consistent internal map representing the vehicle’s state and its three-dimensional environment, and generates a plan of action based on the internal map, a goal, and safety considerations. The plan identifies a sequence of actions, and the AVMS controls vehicle systems (e.g., braking, steering, propulsion) to execute them.

The internal map is a multi-layered graph data structure storing objects and their attributes at different resolutions, enabling efficient querying and compact storage. The AVMS uses AI models such as convolutional neural networks for object detection and classification, and reinforcement learning (RL) for action selection.

Safety is improved through several techniques. The AVMS can dynamically control sensor behavior by sending instructions to change what data is captured or communicated (e.g., field of view, resolution, data rate, zoom). This allows on-demand detailed sensing for specific maneuvers. The system simulates “what-if” scenarios by modifying parameters of the internal map to project possible future situations, then determines safe actions by analyzing both the current and simulated maps. For supervised learning models, the AVMS generates a confidence score indicating how statistically similar an inferring data point is to the training dataset; predictions with low scores may be overridden. For RL models, a Safety Sanity Index (SSI) provides a safety performance indication, and interruptible commands can override unsafe actions selected by the RL agent. Additionally, the AVMS outputs information about planned future actions and the reasons for those actions to a user via a vehicle interface, increasing trust and allowing manual override if needed.

The AVMS comprises subsystems including a sensors interface, localization, perception, planning, controls, and information. Localization determines the vehicle’s position using sensor data and map matching. Perception builds the internal map and performs object detection, classification, and tracking. Planning generates the plan of action, evaluates what-if scenarios, and controls sensor behavior. Controls executes the plan by commanding vehicle systems and performs dynamic bounds and fail-safe checks. The information subsystem determines and communicates feedback to the user. The internal map can also be sent to cloud-based applications for analysis.

The present disclosure relates to ACK/NACK feedback in wireless networks with multiple transmission reception points (TRPs). A base station may send a user equipment (UE) information indicating physical downlink control channel (PDCCH) monitoring occasions for each TRP, whether ACK/NACK feedback across TRPs is allowed, and if allowed, rules for performing ACK/NACK feedback bundling. The base station may also send a downlink assignment index (DAI) definition indicating whether DAIs transmitted by the TRPs are joint (counting grants across all TRPs and carriers) or independent (counting grants per TRP). The UE receives this information, determines a codebook size based on the PDCCH monitoring occasions and DAIs, and transmits either a joint ACK/NACK feedback on a physical uplink control channel (PUCCH) according to the bundling rules, or multiple individual PUCCHs to separate TRPs. Bundling rules may specify that a joint ACK is sent if data from at least one TRP is successfully received, or a joint NACK if data from both TRPs fails, among other configurations.

C-BerryTrans is a C++ code that computes the anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC) directly from WIEN2k output. It evaluates the Berry curvature (Ω) using the Kubo formula, extracting eigenvalues and momentum-matrix elements from first-principles calculations. The Ω is integrated over the full Brillouin zone: for AHC, weighted by the Fermi–Dirac distribution; for ANC, weighted by an entropy function. The code avoids Wannier interpolation by working directly with DFT eigenfunctions, aiming for higher accuracy. Calculations of Ω are parallelized over k-points using OpenMP, and band-resolved Ω is stored in binary files to reduce memory and enable efficient post-processing. Post-processing computes AHC or ANC for user-specified ranges of temperature and chemical potential. Input parameters include the WIEN2k case directory, crystal structure number, chemical potential window, temperature range, k-mesh size, spin-polarization flag, and parallelization settings. A dedicated module generates the k-point list for the full Brillouin zone. The code includes a visualization module for Ω-weighted distributions. Validation was performed on Fe, Pd, Fe₃Al, and Co₂FeAl, with results compared to literature. The implementation uses standard C++ libraries and is interfaced with WIEN2k, but can be adapted to other DFT packages.

The passage proposes a hybrid method-of-moments (MoM) and generalized scattering matrix (GSM) framework for multiscale electromagnetic problems where antennas interact with large surrounding structures, such as implantable antennas, reflector antennas, and radome-enclosed arrays. Existing MoM and T-matrix hybrids are inefficient for electrically large irregular structures. The new framework inverts roles: the large environment is discretized and solved by MoM, while the antenna is represented by its GSM. This reduces unknowns by encapsulating antenna details and allows exploitation of GSM advances like Wigner translation/rotation theorems, array synthesis, and modular reuse. The framework can be extended to a GSM-PO hybrid (full-coupled, capturing higher-order interactions) and a GSM+T-matrix hybrid. It provides a unifying paradigm for multiscale analysis with plug-and-play modularity. The formulation decomposes total fields into incident, scattered, and antenna fields. The structure is modeled by PMCHWT integral equations with RWG basis functions, yielding ZI = V, where excitation includes incident and antenna contributions. Antenna fields are expanded in spherical vector waves, and the GSM relates incident and outgoing wave coefficients via a linear mapping involving port S-parameters, receiving, transmitting, and scattering matrices. Coupling operators link the MoM system and GSM, with the antenna incidence vector expressed as a = -U4I + ai.

The lecture restates the Weierstrass M-test: if functions \(f_j\) on a set \(S\) satisfy \(|f_j(x)| \le M_j\) with \(\sum M_j\) convergent, then \(\sum f_j\) converges uniformly. An example \(\sum \cos(160jx)/4^j\) converges uniformly on \(\mathbb{R}\) and its limit is continuous. For a power series with radius of convergence \(\rho\), the series converges uniformly on any closed interval strictly inside \((x_0-\rho, x_0+\rho)\), proved via the M-test with \(M_j = |a_j| R^j\). Consequently, within the radius of convergence, a power series can be differentiated and integrated term by term. The differentiated series has the same radius of convergence, so the original series is infinitely differentiable and its derivatives equal the term-by-term derivatives. The Weierstrass approximation theorem states that any continuous function on \([0,1]\) can be uniformly approximated by polynomials. The proof reduces to the case where \(f(0)=f(1)=0\), extending \(f\) by zero outside \([0,1]\). Polynomials \(p_n(x) = \int_0^1 f(t) q_n(t-x)\,dt\) are constructed, where \(q_n(t) = c_n (1-t^2)^n\) and \(c_n\) normalizes the integral over \([-1,1]\) to 1. The \(q_n\) are nonnegative, integrate to 1, and converge uniformly to 0 on \(|t| \ge \delta\) for any \(\delta>0\), acting as an approximation to the identity. Using uniform continuity and boundedness of \(f\), \(p_n\) is shown to converge uniformly to \(f\).

The Supreme Court heard arguments in a challenge by counselor Kaley Chiles to Colorado’s 2019 Minor Conversion Therapy Law, which bans conversion therapy for minors. A majority of justices appeared sympathetic to her claim, with some suggesting the case be sent back to lower courts rather than striking the law immediately. The 10th Circuit had upheld the ban as regulating conduct, subject to rational basis review. Chiles’s lawyer argued the ban prohibits helping minors with state-disfavored goals and could silence speech. The Trump administration also urged striking the law, citing no tradition of regulating purely speech-based treatment. Colorado’s solicitor general defended the law as a bipartisan measure addressing harm, regulating medical treatment without stopping viewpoint expression. Justices debated standing, as Colorado had not enforced the ban against Chiles; Justice Sotomayor questioned a credible threat of prosecution. Justice Jackson noted a long tradition of regulating medical treatments. Justice Alito called the law “blatant viewpoint discrimination” and questioned whether medical consensus could be ideological. The argument left open whether the Supreme Court should apply strict scrutiny or remand for lower courts to do so, with Sotomayor, Jackson, and possibly Barrett favoring remand. Justice Kavanaugh did not ask questions.

A cost-effective, culture-independent citizen science approach was developed to sample the microbiome in household drinking water across China. College student volunteers collected 50 tap water samples from 19 provinces between December 2020 and August 2021, including opportunistic samples after extreme weather events (2021 Henan Floods and Typhoon In-Fa). A protocol using Corning syringe filters and disinfection procedures was employed. DNA extraction and PCR amplification targeted the 16S rRNA gene V4 region; 22 of 50 samples tested positive for microbial DNA. Metabarcoding of pooled positive samples yielded 7,635 Amplicon Sequence Variants, revealing a diverse microbiome. Pathogenic bacteria (Mycobacterium spp., Acinetobacter spp., Legionella spp.) were detected in all PCR-positive samples. Post-event samples from Zhengzhou and Changzhou additionally contained Salmonella enterica and toxin-producing Microcystis spp. The study underscores citizen science's utility for microbial monitoring and informs public health strategies for water safety.

The present application is a continuation of U.S. patent application Ser. No. 16/804,326, which is a continuation of Ser. No. 15/367,793, claiming priority to provisional applications 62/263,050 and 62/265,181. The invention relates to automated sortation systems, particularly robotic systems for sorting objects. Background notes that conventional systems rely on human workers to singulate and sort objects into fixed collection bins, leading to inefficiencies, high space requirements, and high costs. Partially automated solutions like tilt-tray conveyors have high per-divert costs. Manual sortation cells reduce divert costs but still require all cells to have the same bin designations, limiting total system bins.

The invention provides methods and systems for processing objects using a programmable motion device. An object is acquired from a plurality of mixed objects at an input area, identifying indicia are perceived, an intermediate station is dynamically assigned to a destination location based on the indicia, and the object is moved toward that intermediate station. A processor dynamically assigns intermediate locations, which are associated with destination locations. The relationship between intermediate containers and destinations is not fixed and changes during sortation based on heuristics. Embodiments include multiple sorting stations fed by input conveyors, with robotic systems placing objects into bins that are dynamically assigned. Completed bins are placed on output conveyors. Perception units (cameras, scanners) identify objects. A central controller manages assignments.

Further embodiments include shuttle wing sortation stations. An articulated arm picks an object, drops it through a drop camera unit for identification, and the object falls into a first carriage on a track. The first carriage moves to one of multiple shuttle wing sections, each having a carriage that reciprocates along a track between rows of collection bins. The carriage dumps the object into an assigned bin. Bins can be removed in pairs via drawers. Systems can scale by adding more wings and robots, with dynamic bin allocation using historical data to optimize cycle times and throughput. The system can signal when bins are full and allocate bins to minimize costs across the network.

A $1.476 million state pilot was in the House budget but not the final signed budget; DCDEE offers grants up to $50,000 for up to 10 colleges to run academies from October 2025 to July 2026. Counties operating academies include Buncombe, Cabarrus, Catawba, Davidson, Davie, Durham, Johnston, McDowell, Rowan, Stanly, and Wayne. Wayne and Johnston counties’ classroom-ready academies, funded by the Camber Foundation, graduated 63 and 26 students respectively, with many entering child care jobs or further education. Stanly County’s classroom-ready academy had 13 graduates. McDowell County’s teaching credential academy, funded by a Dogwood Health Trust grant, graduated six students, four of whom went directly into classrooms. Durham County’s bilingual teaching credential academy, funded by Duke Community Affairs and Durham PreK, lasted six weeks, drew 140 applicants for 20 slots, and cost $1,264 per student. Graduates can start careers debt-free with transferable credits, improving long-term prospects.

The passage details the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. It defines MSR protocol functions: AP reset hold request/response, GHCB GPA registration (preferred and register), page state change request/response, run VMPL request/response, hypervisor feature support request/response, termination request, and unregister GHCB GPA. GHCB GPA registration is mandatory for SEV-SNP guests before first VMGEXIT, with options to query a hypervisor-preferred GPA or register a specific one; registration automatically unregisters any previous GPA. The page state change NAE event uses a structure in the GHCB shared buffer to request private/shared page state changes or PSMASH/UNSMASH hints, with progress tracked via cur_entry and cur_page fields and error codes in SW_EXITINFO2. Negotiation examples show hypervisors setting VMCB offset 0x00a0 with protocol version and encryption bit, and guests using CPUID and MSR protocols to determine encryption bit and GHCB version. Supported NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access, Page State Change, and SNP Guest Request. Standard VMGEXIT handling involves copying register state to/from GHCB, setting VALID_BITMAP bits, and processing hypervisor error responses. The SNP Guest Request NAE event uses shared request/response pages for firmware requests, with sequence number management and rate limiting. The document also specifies the Secrets Page Guest Reserved Area format for communicating message sequence numbers and AP jump table addresses between operating environments, and an EFI configuration table GUID for passing secrets and CPUID pages.

Smart contracts are defined as a set of promises specified in digital form, including protocols, with parties performing against them. They may not be smart (not AI) and may not be legally contracts. Technically, they share cryptography, decentralization, and consensus features with Bitcoin, but Ethereum uses an account-based balance ledger with state transitions instead of UTXO, is Turing complete, supports multiple programming languages (mainly Solidity), and stores transactions, state, storage, and receipts in four Merkle trees. Blocks are ~14 seconds. Ethereum’s founder, Vitalik Buterin, launched it with a presale that raised $18 million; Joe Lubin and the Ethereum Foundation each kept about 9.5%, and 80% was sold publicly. Ethereum’s monetary policy has been changed twice (block rewards reduced from 5 to 3 to 2 ETH), showing it is not immutable. Its inflation rate is higher than Bitcoin’s.

Key platforms include Ethereum ($22B market cap), EOS ($5B, raised $4.2B in an ICO, uses delegated Byzantine fault tolerance), NEO (China-associated, also delegated Byzantine fault tolerance), and Ethereum Classic. DApps currently have low usage: the most active gambling dApp had 1,500 users in 24 hours. ICOs raise funds to build networks; tokens are often issued before functionality, are fungible and transferable. $28 billion has been raised across ICOs; one study says 59% fail within nine months, and another estimates 25% are scams.

Larry Lessig presents four points on contract law. First, a contract is a promise or performance given in exchange for a promise or performance; even a vending machine transaction has express terms (e.g., price) and implied terms (e.g., the drink is safe). Second, the state is always a third party, policing contracts for legality, effects, terms, and taxation. Third, contract law allocates risk and requires an enforcement system; blockchain can substitute for weak legal systems or lower transaction costs, enabling contracts like automatic flight-delay insurance. Fourth, ambiguity in contracts has value because negotiating every low-probability outcome is costly; smart contracts force specification of all outcomes, which can increase transaction costs and block certain contracts. Challenges include courts’ ability to interpret code and the need for lawyers to understand code.

The lower highs and lower lows pattern signals a downtrend but is primarily a short-term reversal pattern. Testing on SPY, GLD, and TLT using a one-bar lower high and lower low entry at close with exits from 1 to 10 days showed better returns with longer holding periods due to long-term upward drift. The pattern is a reversal pattern. A two-day consecutive lower high and lower low pattern slightly improved average gains in SPY but not in GLD or TLT. A final backtest entering on the third consecutive lower low and lower high in stocks showed increased average gain and profit factor, with a low max drawdown of 9.9% for a one-day hold. The pattern works well as a short-term reversal in stocks. The pattern is characterized by consecutive candlesticks with lower highs and lower lows, indicating a momentum shift. Trading rules involve pattern identification, entry points, backtesting, confirmation signals, and risk management.

In Morris v. Scott, the plaintiff sued for malicious prosecution, alleging the defendant maliciously and without probable cause complained to a magistrate, causing arrest and trial, and the plaintiff was acquitted. The lower court nonsuited the plaintiff because the declaration lacked averments that the justice or court of special sessions had jurisdiction. On error, the court held that an action on the case for malicious prosecution lies even if the court had no jurisdiction, provided malice and falsehood are the gravamen and the arrest is alleged as a consequence. Authorities such as Goslin v. Wilcock and Smith v. Cattel support this. Additionally, under 2 R.S. 456, 2d ed. § 16, case may be brought for trespasses affecting person or personal property, giving a right to elect between case and trespass. The judgment was reversed and a venire de novo ordered.

The court denied the plaintiffs’ motion to enforce a settlement agreement. The plaintiffs, former D.C. Department of Corrections employees, alleged wrongful termination in retaliation for speaking to the media. Before trial, the parties reached a tentative agreement and the court dismissed the case without prejudice. The plaintiffs later sought to enforce a settlement they claimed included both a $625,000 payment and their re-enrollment into the retirement system. The defendants agreed to the monetary amount but disputed that re-enrollment was part of the settlement.

Applying District of Columbia contract law, the court found that while the parties mutually assented to the $625,000 payment, there was no meeting of the minds on re-enrollment. The defendants’ statements and actions showed uncertainty and no final agreement on that issue. The plaintiffs’ evidence—an assurance that “no problems were anticipated” and a retirement deposit application form—did not establish mutual assent. The absence of a written agreement further indicated no binding settlement on re-enrollment. The court also rejected the plaintiffs’ argument that they had an unconditional statutory right to re-enrollment, because the case was never tried and the defendants had not admitted the terminations were unjustified.

The court declined to enforce a separate settlement as to plaintiff Ms. Thomas, accepting the plaintiffs’ position that the settlement was indivisible. The court gave the plaintiffs until September 9, 2002 to accept the $625,000 offer without retirement benefits or to reject it, after which the case would be set for trial.

Collagen supplements are used for cosmetic and health benefits as natural collagen production declines with age. Collagen is a crucial protein, about 30% of the body's protein, made from amino acids and nutrients like vitamin C, zinc, and copper. There are 28 types; types I-V are most common. Supplements are sourced from animals (marine, bovine, porcine, chicken) and often hydrolysed for better absorption. They contain types I, II, III. Benefits may include improved skin growth, reduced wrinkles, firmer skin, stronger nails, bone strengthening, joint pain relief, muscle support, and possibly thicker hair (limited mouse studies). Dosages: 2.5g daily for joint pain and skin hydration, 5g for bone density in osteopenic postmenopausal women, 15g for muscle mass with resistance training, up to 40mg for joint health. A diet rich in protein, vitamin C, and bone broth supports natural collagen production. The passage also discusses matcha tea's potential health benefits and anti-ageing supplements, defining anti-ageing as healthy internal ageing. A controlled human malaria infection study in semi-immune Gambian adults, classified as sero-high or sero-low based on pre-existing antibody levels, revealed that sero-low individuals had higher peak parasitaemia, more symptoms, and shorter latency. Whole transcriptome analysis identified var genes as the primary differentially expressed genes between groups. Var expression entropy was significantly lower in controllers (sero-high individuals with long latency and low parasite multiplication rates), indicating a restricted repertoire. In vivo var gene turnover rates were high, with group A var genes showing the fastest transition rates. In vitro, parasite isolates from sero-low individuals converged rapidly to a high-entropy steady-state var expression pattern, while sero-high isolates took longer and retained memory of the initial state. Pre-existing antibodies recognized a broader range of PfEMP1 domains in sero-high individuals, and this breadth was negatively associated with infection markers. Post-infection, sero-low individuals showed a significant increase in recognized PfEMP1 domains, whereas sero-high individuals did not. Pre-existing antibody levels were moderately negatively correlated with var expression during infection, particularly for group A and B PfEMP1s. No direct correlation was found between the intensity of var gene expression and subsequent antibody acquisition. The findings support a model where intrinsic var gene switching maintains a diverse repertoire as a bet-hedging strategy, with immune selection shaping expression in individuals with stronger pre-existing immunity.

They spread through malvertising and social engineering, use innocent-sounding lifestyle names, and resist uninstallation by redirecting users to fake pages. Google removed the extensions and disabled them on affected devices after Trend Micro’s report. The Midline Option is an option play where the quarterback reads an interior defensive lineman to decide whether to hand off to a dive back (fullback) hitting the A-gap or keep the ball through the B-gap. Its primary strength is that the offense does not have to block one defender, instead reading an interior lineman rather than an edge defender. It complements inside and outside veer offenses and uses wingback motion as eye candy to deceive defenses. The main weakness is that the quarterback takes many hits, requiring a rugged quarterback. The passage provides blocking assignments against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts. Variations include Flexbone Midline, which spreads the defense by replacing the tight end with a Z receiver, and Midline "Follow," where a wingback acts as an extra lead blocker for the quarterback on keep plays, used in short-yardage situations by programs like Army, Navy, and Air Force.

Soccer formations strategically place players for effective defense and attack. Choosing a formation depends on the number of players (often set by age-specific rules), player skills, and the coach's comfort with tactics. The game's evolution, influenced by the Offside Law, has led to fewer forwards, more equal spacing, greater all-around skills, higher fitness, and more short passes. In full-sides (11-player) games, with a goalkeeper assumed, formations are designated by the number of defenders, midfielders, and forwards (e.g., 4-3-3, 4-4-2), always totaling 10 field players. Recent variations include 4-3-2-1 and 4-6. For younger age groups with fewer players, U.S. Soccer recommends formations like 3-2-3 for 9-a-side, while 7-a-side may use 2-2-2 and 4-a-side may use 2-1. Introducing formations helps young children transition from mob-ball to team play. Coaches must understand position names, player placement, and tactics, and diagram the formation for implementation.

The passage discusses the value of design patterns for distributed systems, including learning from others' mistakes, establishing a shared vocabulary, and enabling reusable components. It then introduces single-node container patterns: the sidecar pattern (augmenting an application container, e.g., adding HTTPS to a legacy service or dynamic configuration), the ambassador pattern (brokering interactions between the application container and external services, e.g., sharded Redis or service brokering), and the adapter pattern (modifying an application container's interface for consistency, e.g., monitoring with Prometheus, logging normalization with Fluentd, or health checks). Multi-node patterns are then covered: replicated load-balanced services for stateless services, including session tracking and application-layer caching with Varnish and SSL termination with nginx. Finally, sharded services are described for stateful services, using sharded caches to increase data capacity, with considerations for cache hit rate and system performance, and the option of replicated sharded caches for resilience. Examples include deploying sharded Memcached with an ambassador or a shared routing service, and sharding functions based on hashing.

The newly inaugurated President, called from retirement, acknowledges the historical tendency of candidates to break promises and notes that some may doubt his sincerity, but asserts that his forthcoming administration will prove his commitment. He places his chief confidence in Almighty Power. He states that the Constitution rests on the people, making the government a democracy whose leading principle is the greatest good to the greatest number. American sovereignty is limited to powers expressly granted by the governed; all men are equal, and no government by divine right exists. The Constitution grants and withholds powers, and individuals possess unalienable rights, including freedom of faith, speech, and due process, which derive from their nature as human beings, not from charters.

Disputes have arisen over constitutional interpretation, particularly regarding legislative power, but most have been settled by popular sanction, and errors are attributed to the difficulty of ascertaining framers’ intent rather than sinister motives. The greatest danger is not governmental usurpation of ungranted power but the accumulation of power in one department, especially the executive, which could create a despotism. He observes a tendency toward monarchy and pledges to arrest it and restore the government’s health.

He identifies defects in the Constitution, notably the eligibility of a President for a second term, which fosters love of power and corruption. He renews his pledge never to serve a second term. He argues that a fair construction does not make the President part of the legislative power; the veto is a conservative power intended to protect the Constitution, guard against hasty legislation, and prevent majority combinations that violate minority rights. He considers settled points of constitutional dispute as recognized by repeated actions of the branches and general will.

He warns that executive patronage and control over officers who handle public money effectively subject the treasury to the President’s disposal, creating a monarchical danger. He proposes remedies: making the Treasury Secretary independent and removable only upon demand of the popular legislative branch, forbidding federal officers from interfering in elections beyond voting, and never using the public press to shield wrongdoing. He states that schemes of finance and the mode of keeping public treasure should be left to the immediate representatives of the people, and he opposes an exclusively metallic currency as harmful to the poor and to national character.

Regarding the District of Columbia, he affirms that its people are free American citizens, not subjects, and that Congress’s exclusive jurisdiction is only to secure the General Government’s functions; legislation should conform to their interests. He stresses the necessity of keeping all government departments and state authorities within their proper orbits, and warns that collisions between states are especially dangerous. The Confederacy must be preserved by forbearance; citizens of one state must not attempt to control the domestic institutions of another, as such agitation produces only bitterness and threatens disunion and civil war. Union is the most important interest.

He encourages states facing financial difficulties to fulfill their engagements, as their credit is part of the whole country’s credit. He emphasizes that the spirit of liberty must be constantly nurtured; without it, no governmental structure can preserve freedom. He distinguishes the true spirit of liberty, which is mild and scrupulous, from the false spirit of party, which is harsh, vindictive, and leads to dangerous executive power. In foreign relations, he intends to preserve friendly intercourse with all nations, maintain peace without sacrificing rights or honor, and observe justice and liberality toward Native Americans.

He calls for a mitigation of party violence, warning that parties beyond ensuring vigilance become destructive of public virtue and liberty. He desires a union of the whole country, not a party, and will exert his influence to prevent an Executive party in the legislature. He expresses profound reverence for the Christian religion and the conviction that sound morals and religious liberty are connected to true happiness, commending the country to God. He takes leave, pledging to discharge his duties with confidence in the people’s support.

Riverton Investment Corp. (RIC) sued the United States for a tax refund, disputing the IRS's disallowance of deductions for payments made to buy back stock from management employees. The IRS characterized the payments as non-deductible stock redemptions, while RIC argued they were deductible compensation. The case hinged on whether the stock was "transferred" to the employees in the 1980s under the Management Stockholder's Agreement (MSA). The court found Paragraph 9 of the MSA ambiguous regarding whether its restrictions would lapse upon a liquidation, merger, or reorganization. Because the paragraph was ambiguous, the court admitted parol evidence, which showed the contracting parties intended the restrictions on to whom and at what price the stock could be sold to be permanent. The court held these were non-lapse restrictions that prevented a "transfer" of the stock from occurring. Consequently, the 1990s payments were not redemptions, and RIC was entitled to deduct them. The court sustained RIC's objections, rejected the Magistrate Judge's recommendation, and entered summary judgment in favor of RIC.

The passage traces the shift from procedural programming to object-oriented programming, which elevated data and reusability alongside algorithms. This led to design patterns like the “gang of four” book, providing reusable interface-based patterns. The rise of open source software underscored community-driven development, particularly for distributed systems and container technology. The book focuses on patterns for distributed systems, beginning with single-node patterns that group containers on one machine.

The sidecar pattern augments an application container by sharing resources; examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy service, synchronizing configuration, and providing process monitoring. The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between the application container and external services, enabling client-side sharding (e.g., sharded Redis), service brokering for portability, and request splitting for experiments. The adapter pattern modifies the application container’s interface to conform to a standard, such as adapting monitoring for Prometheus, normalizing logs with Fluentd, or adding rich health checks.

Multi-node patterns address distributed systems. The replicated load-balanced service pattern uses identical replicas behind a load balancer, with readiness probes to manage traffic. Session tracking can direct a user’s requests to the same replica. Application-layer replicated services introduce caching layers (e.g., Varnish) and SSL termination (e.g., nginx) as separate replicated tiers, improving performance and security. Rate limiting can be added at the caching layer.

Sharded services partition state across multiple replicas, each handling a subset of requests, with a root routing traffic. Sharded caching increases storage capacity but requires consideration of cache hit rate and the impact of shard failures on performance. Replicated sharded caches combine replication within each shard for resilience. The passage includes Kubernetes-based hands-on examples for deploying these patterns.

Ida C. Scott, a married woman, sued to enjoin enforcement of a judgment against her real estate. The judgment had been obtained by John R. House for goods sold and delivered, without first obtaining a judgment against her husband. The Nebraska Supreme Court affirmed the injunction. Under Comp. St. 1911, ch. 53, sec. 1, a married woman’s property is not liable for necessaries furnished the family until an execution against the husband has been issued and returned unsatisfied. The stipulated facts showed no such judgment against the husband existed. This study applies spherical fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (SFAHP) to evaluate and rank the impact of digitalization on higher education quality. Five criteria are considered: technological infrastructure, accessibility of digital resources, pedagogical integration, student engagement, and adaptability and innovation. Nine education experts provided pairwise comparisons using spherical fuzzy judgment matrices. The SFAHP analysis yielded priority weights: pedagogical integration ranked highest (0.236), followed by student engagement (0.212), accessibility of digital resources (0.203), adaptability and innovation (0.184), and technological infrastructure (0.165). The study focuses on Vietnam's higher education context. The findings indicate that pedagogical integration and student engagement are the most critical factors for enhancing online education quality. The paper suggests strategic emphasis on integrating teaching methodologies with technology, fostering student engagement through interactive and personalized learning, ensuring equitable access to digital resources, and investing in technological infrastructure and professional development. The study acknowledges its reliance on expert evaluations and recommends future research incorporating broader stakeholder perspectives.

SCDNR biologists satellite-tagged a 12-foot-2, 820-pound pregnant female tiger shark named Harry-Etta in St. Helena Sound. This was her third encounter; she was previously tagged in 2013 and 2015. Offensive linemen play a selfless, stat-less position, protecting teammates and enabling touchdowns without seeking the spotlight. The offensive line is the driving force of any productive offense, responsible for run blocking (creating creases, handling blitzes and stunts) and pass protection (keeping the quarterback safe from various defensive pressures). The five players line up on the line of scrimmage, hence the name. Common nicknames include Hogs, Bruisers, and Big Uglies. Required skills are run-blocking, pass-blocking, athleticism, strength, awareness, and technique. Typical body type is 6'2–6'8, 300–340 pounds, with a thick, sturdy, lengthy build. Notable players: center Jim Otto (Raiders, 210 consecutive games, double zero jersey), guard John Hannah (Patriots, 7-time All-Pro), and tackle Anthony Munoz (Bengals, Hall of Fame). The offensive line is often scapegoated during struggles, but its steady play is the top factor in offensive success, allowing star skill players like Patrick Mahomes, Derrick Henry, and Davante Adams to excel.

A 2010 fossil find by an elk hunter in Montana led to a new elasmosaur species from 70 million years ago. Manufacturing occurs at the Fremont Factory, Gigafactory Nevada, Gigafactory New York, Gigafactory Shanghai, and under-construction Gigafactory Berlin and Gigafactory Texas. The lecture introduces algebraic structures leading to finite fields. It covers groups, subgroups, cosets, Lagrange's theorem, and quotient groups. Groups are defined by axioms including a permutation property; finite cyclic groups are isomorphic to Z_n. A subgroup is a subset that is itself a group under the same operation. Examples in Z_10 include {0,5} (isomorphic to Z_2) and the even integers {0,2,4,6,8} (isomorphic to Z_5). In the integers Z, nZ is a subgroup. Cosets are translates H+g; distinct cosets partition the group and have the same size. Lagrange's theorem states that the size of a subgroup divides the size of a finite group. Cosets form a quotient group under coset addition; e.g., Z mod nZ is isomorphic to Z_n, and the cosets of 2Z in Z (even and odd integers) form a group isomorphic to Z_2.

Fields have two operations, addition and multiplication. Under addition, they form an abelian group with identity 0. The non-zero elements form an abelian group under multiplication with identity 1, and the distributive law holds. Examples include real numbers, complex numbers, and the binary field F_2. Prime fields F_p, for prime p, consist of {0,1,...,p-1} with mod-p addition and multiplication. The proof that F_p is a field relies on the fact that the product of two non-zero elements mod p cannot be zero (since p is prime), ensuring closure and the existence of inverses via the permutation property. Every finite field with p elements is isomorphic to F_p. Every finite field contains a prime subfield isomorphic to F_p for some prime p, called the characteristic. In a field of characteristic p, adding any element to itself p times yields 0. Characteristic 2 is common in digital communications, where addition and subtraction coincide.

Polynomials over a field F are expressed as f(x) = f_0 + f_1 x + ... + f_m x^m with coefficients in F, where x is an indeterminate. The degree is the highest index with a non-zero coefficient; the zero polynomial's degree is defined as minus infinity to preserve the sum-of-degrees formula for multiplication. The set of all polynomials is denoted F[x]. Addition is component-wise. Multiplication is convolution of coefficients. Under addition, F[x] is an abelian group. Under multiplication, it is commutative with identity 1, but not all elements have inverses. The invertible polynomials (units) are the non-zero degree-0 polynomials (non-zero constants). Higher-degree polynomials lack inverses because the degree of a product would be at least the degree of the non-constant factor.

The HID AMDI0095 binds a driver to the TMPM device. A page migration driver sets PAGEMIGRATION_EN in IOMMU_MMIO_CNTRL_1 once. The TMPM interface uses a ring buffer (RB) for parallel commands.
