The passage reports the development and testing of a new clinician-administered Language Phenotype Assessment (LPA) designed to evaluate language comprehension in young children. Existing assessments were found unsuitable for assessing the three language comprehension phenotypes (Command, Modifier, Syntactic) in children aged 2–4 years due to overcomplexity, reliance on vocabulary, or picture-based responses. The LPA consists of 15 items using toy-animal manipulatives and brief instructions, with each item requiring correct completion of at least three out of four tasks. It was administered to 116 typically developing children aged 1.5–7 years and 79 children diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) aged 2–8 years. In neurotypical children, LPA scores increased linearly with age, plateauing around 5 years. 50% attained the Command Phenotype by 1.6 years, the Modifier Phenotype by 3.0 years, and the Syntactic Phenotype by 3.7 years. All neurotypical children acquired the Command Phenotype by 3 years, Modifier by 4 years, and Syntactic by 5 years. A parent-reported Language Phenotype Evaluation Checklist (LPEC) with a similar structure showed a strong correlation with LPA scores (r=0.78). In children with ASD aged 5 years and older, only 39% achieved the Syntactic Phenotype per LPA, compared to all neurotypical peers. The LPA demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha=0.92), excellent test-retest reliability (r=0.96), and very high inter-observer agreement (Kappa=0.97). The authors suggest the LPA could enable early identification of language deficits, monitor therapy progress, and shift focus from vocabulary to syntactic language development.

The long snapper is a specialized football position requiring perfection, essential for punts, extra points, and field goals. They snap the ball to holders (about 7 yards) and punters (about 15 yards) with pinpoint accuracy and consistent spin. Skills needed include accuracy, consistency, balance, athleticism, and physicality. The typical body type is 6'1-6'3, 230-250 pounds, with a thick build comparable to a linebacker. NFL teams reserve one roster spot for a long snapper. Errors are unacceptable; a blocked punt results in a win about 90% of the time. Long snappers also cover punts and make tackles. The position is abbreviated LS, with deep-snapper referring to punts and short-snapper referring to extra points/field goals. Notable players include Zak DeOssie (2007-2019, two Super Bowls, two Pro Bowls) and Don Mulbach (2004-2020, second in Detroit Lions games played, two Pro Bowls). Their work does not appear on stat sheets but is critical for scoring and field position.

The present technology relates to robotic systems with multi-gripper assemblies configured to selectively grip and hold objects. A transport robot includes an end effector having addressable vacuum regions, each independently capable of providing vacuum gripping via an array of suction elements. A vision sensor device captures image data of objects, and a controller identifies target objects and selects which vacuum regions to activate. The robot can grip multiple objects simultaneously or sequentially and release them similarly. A force detector assembly may measure grip characteristics, and a vacuum source provides negative pressure. Methods include receiving image data representative of a group of objects, identifying one or more target objects, selecting addressable vacuum regions based on the identified targets, and commanding the transport robot to cause the selected vacuum regions to hold and transport the objects. The vision sensor device can verify object positions, and if an initial grip is insufficient, the system can perform a regripping action. During transport, grip is monitored, and if it falls below a threshold, responsive actions are taken. The robotic system can be used in environments such as warehouses for unloading, transferring, and loading packages.

A national poll from EducationNext shows support for charter schools dropped 12 points in one year, from 51% to 39%. Support for universal vouchers is 45%, a bounce from last year but consistent with prior years. Tax-credit scholarships remain the most popular form of school choice at 55%, also a one-year bounce. The charter school decline occurred across parties and racial groups, with no clear explanation; the question’s wording about “formation” may be a factor, as communities have fought charter expansion. Partisan divides shifted: last year more Democrats favored vouchers, now more Republicans do. A “Trump effect” shows Republicans more likely to support an issue if told Trump backs it, while Democrats react oppositely, though Trump’s net influence is nearly nil. The poll reflects a breakdown in bipartisan education consensus, but approval of local public schools remains similar across parties.

The Trump administration announced it will continue much of the Obama administration's nuclear policy but take a more aggressive stance toward Russia, warning of "unacceptably dire costs" for any limited nuclear attack in Europe. The nuclear posture review does not call for a net increase in strategic nuclear weapons, contrasting with Trump's earlier tweet. It labels North Korea a "clear and grave threat" and says any nuclear attack would end the regime, while casting China as a potential nuclear adversary. Trump said the strategy aims to make nuclear use less likely and strengthen deterrence against non-nuclear attacks. Arms control groups criticized the review as reckless and blurring the line between nuclear and conventional war. The U.S. will follow Obama's modernization blueprint and adhere to the New START treaty, with Russia expected to meet warhead limits. The review sees little prospect for further arms control due to Russian actions. Trump's doctrine ends Obama's push to reduce the nuclear role, seeking a fuller deterrent. It cites Russia's "escalate to de-escalate" doctrine as lowering the first-use threshold. The administration proposes modifying a small number of Trident missiles with smaller-yield warheads and, longer-term, developing a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile.

The lecture discusses pointwise and uniform convergence of sequences of functions. Pointwise convergence means for each fixed x, f_n(x) → f(x). Uniform convergence means f_n gets close to f across the entire set simultaneously: for any ε>0, there exists M such that for all n≥M and all x, |f_n(x)−f(x)|<ε. Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence, but not conversely.

An example is f_n(x)=x^n on [0,1]. It converges pointwise to f(x)=0 for x∈[0,1) and f(1)=1, which is discontinuous. It converges uniformly on any [0,b] with b<1, but not uniformly on [0,1]. Another example is a sequence of tent functions on [0,1] that converge pointwise to 0, but their integrals are always 1, so the limit of integrals does not equal the integral of the limit.

Three questions about interchanging limits are posed: If f_n → f (pointwise or uniformly) and each f_n is continuous, is f continuous? If f_n are differentiable and derivatives converge, is f differentiable and does the derivative of the limit equal the limit of derivatives? If f_n are integrable, does the limit of integrals equal the integral of the limit? The answers are yes under uniform convergence, but no under only pointwise convergence, as demonstrated by the examples.

Theorems are proved: The uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous (via an ε/3 argument). The integral of the uniform limit equals the limit of the integrals. For continuously differentiable functions, if f_n → f uniformly and f_n' → g uniformly, then f is differentiable and f' = g (using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus).

Finally, the Weierstrass M-test is stated: If |f_j(x)| ≤ M_j for all x, and Σ M_j converges, then Σ f_j converges absolutely and uniformly on the set. This provides a way to guarantee uniform convergence of series of functions.

A WIRED article reviews carry-on luggage after a personal bad experience with checked bags at Dulles airport. The article, updated October 2025, tests multiple bags. A favorite suitcase is described as stylish, fuss-free, with hidden pockets, compression straps, interior stabilizer, three handles, water-resistant nylon, and attractive colors. Peak Design Roller Pro is a hybrid hardshell/softshell with a drawbridge opening, VersaPack fabric, retractable compression straps, carbon-fiber handle, expandable 34–39L, but heavier and warranty could be simpler. Travelpro Maxlite 5 costs just over $100, weighs 5.4 lbs, has an exterior toiletry pocket, strong zippers, but handle extensions may stick and main grab handle is single-stitched. Rimowa aluminum suitcases are nearly indestructible, have a cult following, tight seal, strong wheels. Antler roller bag features a zip-up hardshell front pocket with padded laptop/iPad sleeves, smooth nearly silent wheels, adjustable handle, recycled polyester lining, and fits US/European carry-on sizes. For kids, State Logan carry-on offers durable prints, a front pocket for iPads, side straps for blankets. Briggs & Riley soft-sided expandable carry-on has a lifetime no-questions-asked warranty, ballistic nylon, low-profile wheels, padded handles, and an interior garment bag. Yeti Crossroads 35L roller bag uses 700-denier nylon and polycarbonate shell, large fixed wheels, multiple pockets, sturdy zippers. Beis weekender has a removable bottom compartment/packing cube, laptop sleeve, trolley pass-through, key leash, many pockets, but is heavy when full and light colors soil easily. Take Off suitcase is a miniature roller with removable wheels to fit under seats; bumpers are durable, handle extends 21 inches, but it may hit taller users' heels, wheels rattle loudly, and it's not much lighter. Tom Bihn Aeronaut 45 converts from duffel to backpack to shoulder bag, made of 1,050-denier ballistic nylon with YKK zippers, hidden backpack straps, comfortable cross-body strap, very durable. Six Moon Designs travel backpack has a square shape to max carry-on space, comfortable for long distances, adjustable straps, well-considered pockets, webbing, and stretchy pouch. Aer Travel Pack 3 is a backpack/briefcase/tech organizer with clamshell main compartment, separate laptop compartment, compression straps, fits under airplane seat, but water bottle holder is small. Other bags noted: a leather-accented bag with Hinamoto wheels, Aer's pricier carry-on with wheel locks, Casetify luggage (cute, customizable, but smaller and expensive), and Amazon Basics hardside carry-on (functional, light, but inferior wheels and zippers). Tips include the TSA 3-1-1 rule (liquids ≤3.4 oz in one quart-sized clear bag per person), softshell vs hardshell trade-offs (softshells have pockets and expandability but can be permeable and slashable; hardshells lighter but less flexible), checking airline size requirements with a tape measure and choosing soft-sided if unsure, and the testing process (at least two flights per bag, assessing materials, weight, size, durability, wheels, handles, straps, zippers).

The De'Longhi Rivelia automatic latte maker is discounted by $200 to $1,300. It features a touchscreen for selecting milk-based drinks like lattes and flat whites, and automates the entire process. The hopper is swappable to hold two bean types. A "bean adapt" function allows dialing in settings per bean and brewing a test cup. Its milk frother produces silky micro-foam, though not as hot as a steam wand. The study examines B.C.'s carbon tax revenue neutrality, assessing if revenues are offset by tax reductions and the higher taxes collected. Revenue neutrality was promised in 2008. B.C.'s tax is a model for federal carbon pricing by 2018 due to alleged revenue neutrality.

Imran Mohammad, a Rohingya refugee recognized by UNHCR, recounts spending four birthdays in Manus detention. He arrived on October 29, 2013, at age 19. He was placed in Delta compound, sharing a narrow shipping container with three Somali men. The compound held around 300 men, with only five toilets and one washing machine. Detainees lined up for meals, toilets, showers, and razors, often in extreme heat or rain, and sometimes waited over 12 hours to wash clothes. Washing powder and razors were scarce. He later moved to Mike compound, which held over 400 men. Rooms were metal shipping containers without air-conditioning, while the laundry had six. A TV room fit only 50 men, causing fights. He experienced hunger, hid apples to eat later, and fell asleep with a pen in his mouth. On his 20th birthday, he was denied a phone call despite unused phones. He coped by avoiding crowds, spending time with teachers, and focusing on learning, adopting the motto “the pen is mightier than the sword.” He states that suffering is immense and that they sought safety in Australia but received pain, anguish, and death.

Historically, solar eclipses often evoked fear, interpreted as divine anger (ancient Greeks), apocalypse (Vikings), or a dragon devouring the sun (ancient Chinese). In 1878, despite scientific predictability, some Americans in the path of totality believed it was Judgment Day, leading to a tragic murder-suicide. The Gospels describe a darkening sky at the crucifixion, though astronomers dismiss an eclipse then. Some Christians still fear the upcoming Aug. 21 eclipse as an end-times sign, but a cloistered nun reassures callers it is not a bad omen, and her monastery plans to enjoy watching it. In Islamic tradition, Muhammad taught that an eclipse coinciding with his son's death was merely a sign of God, not tied to human events. Author David Baron notes that even non-religious people find total eclipses profoundly awe-inspiring, an alien experience that taps into the brain's religious sense, evoking a feeling of human smallness in the universe.

A funnel-web spider, the world's most venomous, was found in a Springwood home. Bec Sheedy's mother spotted it. Funnel-webs are common on Australia's east coast but rarely seen. Their venom can kill a human in 15 minutes by shutting down the nervous system. Bite symptoms include nausea, muscle cramps, sweating, and numbness. The Australian Museum recorded 13 deaths. No fatalities have occurred since antivenene was developed in 1981. The spiders are defensive, not aggressive; their venom is lethal only to insects, other spiders, and primates. They inhabit cool, damp areas and can survive underwater. Males are currently wandering for mating. Paul Hare advises immediate hospital treatment if bitten, wearing gloves while gardening, and avoiding putting hands into pool filters. Australians are urged to leave them alone as they control pests. The risk of dying from a bite is extremely low, with car accidents on the way to hospital being more likely.

KGI’s Ming-Chi Kuo predicts the 2017 Apple Watch will retain the same form factor as previous models, marking three generations with the same design. It will feature LTE connectivity and come in 38mm and 42mm sizes, with LTE and non-LTE versions. The original design was polarizing; the only prior change was a slight thickness increase. A major redesign would be a large undertaking. With LTE, a size reduction is unlikely. Ben Lovejoy speculates a non-LTE version could be thinner or have longer battery life, and Apple might prioritize slimness. The author would prefer a thinner watch.

The Triangle (1-3-1) offense attacks a Diamond & One defense by placing the star player in the high post, isolating them against the chaser, who is skilled at pass denial but unprepared for post defense. On the high post entry, baseline O4 assumes a short corner, the weakside wing a low post, and the two outside players form a two-guard front. The star can drive right or left, with drop pass options to O3/O4 or O2/O4 for layups, while guards rotate into two-guard front or 2-1-2 alignments. If no shot is available, the star makes a kick-out pass to O1 or O2 (or O1/O3 from left alignment) for open shots or dribble penetration. O4 can flash to the middle as an alternative. Against defensive overplay, the star releases opposite for a lob pass; if unavailable, O4 flashes. Success requires execution, coordination, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Drills include 1-on-1 post isolations and scrimmaging. Scouting opponents, varying alignments, and attacking weak defenders are recommended. The Diamond & One is a combination defense with four zone defenders and one player in strong pass denial against the opponent's scoring ace.

A tough playoff loss: the team played well but gave up too many third-period chances, failing to execute late and surrendering a two-goal lead. After Juneau's goal, they couldn't clear. Detroit battled hard. Frustrating loss, but the team will rebound and everyone is doing good.

President Madison's proclamation of September 1, 1814, condemns the British invasion of Washington, D.C., where they destroyed public buildings and archives, and the plunder of Alexandria after a fort's loss. It cites a British commander's threat to destroy coastal towns, falsely claiming retaliation for U.S. actions in Upper Canada, which the U.S. denies. The proclamation declares these acts violate civilized warfare and leave no safety but in determined resistance. Madison exhorts all citizens to unite, orders civil and military officers to be vigilant, and authorizes calling militia for defense. He appeals to patriotic duty, recalling the fathers' establishment of independence now to be maintained by their sons.

A recent music education graduate living at home with no income is starting a three-month minimum-wage job earning $1,600 per month. They owe $1,700 in tuition, $600 for certification exams, and need to save for a car and apartment. Their mother demands $480 monthly for rent and phone, imposed after an incident where the writer's hearing problems caused them to miss a request for help, leading to the mother screaming and demanding payment. The writer mentions a past incident where the mother took $3,000 from a $5,000 refund check and kept the remainder. The writer feels stuck and wants to handle the situation without ruining the relationship. The response describes the difficult transition after college and offers four suggestions: use the remaining income after paying the mother to pay off debts or save; consider a second job, such as waiting tables, to earn extra money; take time to experiment and not rush into a career, possibly trying different work; and be honest, noting that the mother's described behavior is not normal and if true she needs help, but also questioning if the writer bears some responsibility, asking what the mother would say about the strained relationship.

He noted no flashbacks, expected a tight game, and felt his line generated chances but needed to execute more. He recounted two-handing an opponent on the foot for persistent talking. He mentioned a puck rolling onto Osgood's back, a player putting a hand on it, and uncertainty about the rule; it did not go in. He supported a timeout because forwards weren't out as long as the defensemen, and they failed to clear the puck, leading to a bounce for the opposition. The paper proposes a new argumentation semantics for deontic argumentation that handles weak permission, addressing limitations of grounded and stable semantics. Deontic argumentation deals with establishing obligations, permissions, and other normative positions. Weak permission is defined as the failure to derive an obligation to the contrary, but standard semantics fail to justify weak permissions when conflicting obligations exist.

A Deontic Argumentation Theory consists of facts and rules. Arguments include natural arguments built from rules and facts, and imaginary arguments representing weak permissions for any literal. Attacks are defined, with imaginary arguments attacked by arguments for the contrary obligation. The proposed wp-semantics is based on the argumentation semantics for Defeasible Logic and uses a fixed-point construction to determine sets of wp-acceptable (justified) and wp-rejected arguments. An imaginary argument is acceptable if all attacking arguments are rejected; a natural argument is acceptable if supported and all attackers are undercut or rejected.

The wp-extension is proven unique, conflict-free, and no argument is both justified and rejected. In wp-conflictual theories where two obligations conflict and their subarguments are justified, both weak permissions become justified, making the literal weakly facultative. This contrasts with grounded and stable semantics, where such weak permissions are not justified. The wp-semantics extends grounded semantics, as every grounded-justified argument is also wp-justified.

The rationale discussed is that conflicting obligations from the same legal system without resolution mechanisms should cancel out, leading to weak permissions, avoiding unavoidable sanctions. The approach distinguishes weak permission from strong permission. Related work is reviewed, noting that prior frameworks largely neglect weak permission. The paper concludes that the semantics successfully characterizes weak permission in unresolved conflicts.

This study used the Multiphase Optimization Strategy (MOST) framework to develop a mobile health platform for increasing sleep duration in children with insufficient sleep. In the optimization phase, 97 children aged 9-12 years (mean 11.5y, 51% female, 29% Black, 56% White) with baseline weeknight sleep <8.5 hours were randomized in a 2^5 factorial design to test five components added to a core intervention of sleep tracking and weekly feedback: sleep goal (guideline-based ≥9.25h or personalized ≥45min above baseline), child-directed loss-framed financial incentive ($70 endowment, $2 deducted per night goal not met), caregiver-directed loss-framed incentive, screen time reduction messaging, and daily routine messaging. The optimization criterion was a ≥30-minute increase in weeknight sleep duration. No single component achieved this criterion. Interaction analysis identified two combinations that met the criterion. The top-ranked combination included the core intervention plus caregiver-directed incentive, screen time reduction messaging, and daily routine messaging (either sleep goal), increasing sleep by 39.6 minutes during the intervention and 33.2 minutes during follow-up. The second-ranked combination included core plus caregiver incentive and daily routine messaging (either sleep goal), increasing sleep by 32.0 and 26.6 minutes. The child-directed incentive was not favorable and redundant. Caregiver-directed incentive was effective in top combinations. Guideline-based sleep goal was reasonable as default. Both messaging components contributed, though screen time messaging could be removed without severely compromising effectiveness. Limitations include single-site, predominantly White sample, fewer sleep data nights for Black participants, short follow-up, and single-sensor tracker. The study concluded that optimal settings are sleep tracking, feedback, a sleep goal, caregiver-directed loss-framed incentive, and messaging to reduce screen time and establish daily routines.

This study couples atomistic nanoindentation simulations with orientation-resolved Schmid factor mapping to examine slip system activation in single-crystalline α-titanium at 10 K, 300 K, and 600 K for [0001], [10-10], and [2-110] orientations. Molecular dynamics used an EAM potential and a rigid spherical indenter (radius 12 nm, velocity 20 m/s, depth 4 nm). Load–displacement curves showed a sharp pop-in for [0001] and smoother plasticity for prismatic orientations. Contact pressure decreased with increasing temperature. Dislocation analysis revealed dominant basal a-type dislocations, with pyramidal ⟨c+a⟩ slip becoming more active at higher temperatures. A martensitic HCP-to-BCC phase transformation occurred beneath the indenter, most pronounced at low temperatures. Schmid factor maps correlated high resolved shear stress regions with plastic zones. Shear strain was localized at 10 K and more diffuse at 600 K. Surface morphologies included a circular pile-up for [0001], a symmetric dual-lobe pattern for [10-10], and asymmetric pile-up for [2-110], consistent with activated slip systems. Dislocation density was highest for [0001] and increased with temperature, while prismatic orientations showed lower densities that decreased with temperature due to enhanced recovery. The results link stress distribution, slip system activation, and surface features, providing a mechanistic framework for temperature-sensitive deformation in hcp Ti.

The present invention relates to processing mobile payments when disconnected from payment servers. A computer-implemented method for facilitating offline transactions includes: receiving, by a first user device, an offline payment request from a merchant payment system via a first local communications connection; providing a payment approval message to the merchant payment system via the local connection, causing the merchant payment system to store the message and provide offline transaction information to a payment server; and providing, by the first user device, the offline transaction information to the payment server when connected via a network. The payment server includes an offline status repository storing enablement status of an offline mode for multiple user devices associated with an e-wallet, and the offline mode is only enabled for one device at a time to prevent offline transactions from more than one device. The method further includes determining that an instruction to transfer the offline mode to a second user device has been received, and disabling the offline mode on the first user device. A corresponding computer system with program instructions is also disclosed. Offline payments may be made when network connectivity is unavailable. The e-wallet stores payment information, and the offline payment mode is set for only one user device per e-wallet to prevent overdrawing. The offline mode can be transferred between devices via local communications even when both are offline. When connectivity is restored, the payment server processes the offline transaction, using transaction IDs to avoid duplicate processing.

The present application is a continuation of prior applications and relates to a tonneau cover for pickup trucks. The tonneau cover includes a base panel attached over the truck bed and a plurality of panel sections that are selectively movable to allow bed access. A first panel section is pivotally attachable to the base panel, and a second panel section is pivotally attached to the first. Each panel section has a latching assembly with first and second pinch latch assemblies located adjacent the truck’s side walls. Each pinch latch assembly comprises a latch handle portion (with a latch, latch handle, spring pocket, and guide tab) and an inner pinch handle portion (with a handle and slot receiving the guide tab). A spring in the spring pocket biases the latch toward a latched condition. Applying force to draw the handles together overcomes spring resistance, moving the latch to an unlatched condition. A longitudinally extending connector attaches the inner pinch handle portions of both pinch latch assemblies, so that moving one inner pinch handle causes the other to move, unlatching both sides simultaneously. When force is removed, the springs return the latches to the latched condition.

The tonneau cover may further include a vertical support gusset assembly that stows under a panel section and pivots upward to engage a latch, holding folded panel sections upright. A hinge assembly between panels includes a hinge seal with a spacer, hinge seal rods in cavities, and hinge brackets. Side rails attach to the truck bed walls and have logistic tracks for adjustable clips that receive the latches, as well as rail brackets for securing the rails. A securement system uses a channel bracket on the base panel to hold folded panels upright, with a buckle and strap to secure them. Lights may be integrated into cavities of the inner pinch handles.

The High Post Split Offense is a simple, long-standing offense effective from youth to professional levels. It uses a 2-3 high player alignment, quick high post splits, down screens, and back cuts, making it difficult to guard. The offense provides scoring opportunities for all five players, preventing the defense from focusing on one or two players and eliminating weakside help. It also offers strong offensive rebounding.

The basic option begins with a guard passing to the high post and splitting the post. Reads and counters include: if defenders play tight and don't switch, a handoff on the split; if they drop off anticipating a switch, a fake split; if they sag off, a direct basket cut; and if they automatically switch, both cutters go same side.

When the split doesn't yield a shot, wings set down screens for guards. The high post can feed the cutters or screeners rolling to the basket, or isolate for a shot or drive. Down screen counters include: curl if the defender chases and trails; basket curl if the defender chases out late; fade if the defender cheats over the screen; back cut if the defender cheats over early; screen and roll if defenders switch; and slip the screen if defenders show and recover. Switching can lead to post or wing isolation mismatches.

After the split, the high post can face up in triple threat position, isolated one-on-one. Against overplay, a lob pass or wing feeds are options. The high post position can be occupied by the best triple threat player. When the defense focuses on shooters, strong post ups are used.

Entry variations include Flop (back cut) Entry, Wing Pass Entry, Wing Double Away Entry, and Post Single/Double Screen. Offensive rebounding requires anticipation, determination, and hustle; players must box out and assume shots will miss. Success depends on spacing, execution, coordination, non-verbal communication, timing, and defensive recognition. Individual skill development is essential, and even if not using the offense, knowing how to defend it is important.

A semiconductor device manufacturing method involves arranging a plurality of interconnect structures on a carrier substrate, encapsulating them in a first encapsulant, and thinning to expose external connectors. Packaged semiconductor devices, such as processor dies or memory cubes, are bonded to the interconnect structures via direct copper-to-copper bonding or solder bonding. An underfill material is provided, and the devices are encapsulated in a second encapsulant, which may also serve as a molded underfill. The second encapsulant is thinned, the carrier substrate is debonded, and external connections are formed on the exposed redistribution layer conductive structures. In some embodiments, a single universal interconnect structure is used instead of discrete structures, and a series of redistribution layers is formed over it before bonding semiconductor dies. The methods produce multi-chip modules, including multi-die integrated fan-out packages, with package sizes exceeding 70 mm by 70 mm to support high-performance computing applications. The use of known good interconnect structures, low-temperature bonding, and matching coefficients of thermal expansion between components and printed circuit boards reduces stress and delamination, improving component-level and board-level reliability.

The court granted summary judgment to defendant Waste Away Group, Inc. on plaintiff Paula Norrell's Title VII claims for gender discrimination. Norrell alleged failure to promote and disparate impact. She established a prima facie case of failure to promote: she is female, applied and was qualified for the combined district sales manager position, was rejected, and the job went to a male (Terry White). Waste Away articulated a legitimate, non-discriminatory reason: White was more qualified, having previously held the same combined district role, outside sales experience, and better organizational skills, while Norrell lacked outside sales experience, required supervision, and had limited Montgomery market knowledge. Norrell's evidence of pretext—a request to train White, supervisor Malphrus's alleged discriminatory remarks (deemed stray and by a non-decisionmaker), and a crude remark by decisionmaker Johnson (isolated and unrelated to the decision)—was insufficient to show the employer's reason was pretextual. The court found no genuine issue of material fact and declined to second-guess the business decision. Norrell abandoned her disparate impact claim. Final judgment was entered for defendant, with costs taxed to plaintiff.

The Triangle Post Offense, created and refined by Tex Winter, is a system based on defensive recognition rather than set plays. It relies on sound principles, precise court spacing (15–20 feet), and execution of fundamentals. The offense consists of a sideline triangle on one side of the court and a two-man game on the weakside, involving all players at all times. Its three components are entry, sideline triangle, and weakside two game. Offensive options are dictated by defensive deployment, requiring players to recognize and attack defensive alignments. Spreading the defense prevents double-teaming and opens one-on-one post play, drives, and cuts. The system features numerous entries (e.g., guard outside/inside cuts, dribble clear, off guard cut, post pop, base screen, ball reversal, dribble weave) and sideline triangle actions such as strong post ups, post splits, high post splits, post isolation, corner screen-and-roll, and solo cuts. The weakside two game offers pass and dribble series with reads and counters for various defensive responses (chasing over, going behind, switching, showing, cheating, trapping). Automatic counters address defensive overplay like fronting the post, sagging off, double-teaming, denying reversal or back door passes. Building the offense requires whole-part-whole teaching, breakdown drills, and individual skill development. Game strategies include scouting opponents, educating players on anticipated reads, and varying entries. The offense’s spacing and constant movement make it difficult to defend, and even teams not using it should understand how to defend it.

Bollinger Bands, developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s, analyze volatility and potential trend changes. They consist of a central moving average with upper and lower bands calculated by adding and subtracting a multiple of the standard deviation. The indicator helps visualize volatility, estimate reversals, or trend continuation. Implementing it in a systematic trading system requires time and backtesting. Disadvantages include false signals, reduced effectiveness in range-bound markets, signal delays due to historical data, and sensitivity to time period and settings. Default settings use a 20-period moving average, but these can be modified. A breakout strategy aims to capitalize on breaches of the bands. In TradingView, calculation via Pine Script uses ta.sma() for the moving average and ta.stdev() for standard deviation, with bands formed by adding/subtracting the deviation value. Effectiveness depends on the trading rules defined. An example on the H4 timeframe with 100% capital showed considerable return but uncomfortable drawdown, requiring further research. Developing a strategy on TradingView is straightforward, and Bollinger Bands can serve in Breakout, Mean Reversion, or Squeeze strategies, providing valuable information for analysis.

The TPS7H5001-SP is a full-featured, dual-output, current-mode controller optimized for Si and GaN DC-DC converters, featuring integrated synchronous rectifier outputs and programmable dead time. The TPS7H5002-SP is a single-output controller with integrated synchronous rectification, configurable dead time and leading edge blank time, and selectable maximum duty cycle (75% or 100%). The TPS7H5003-SP is a single-output controller with fixed 50 ns dead time and leading edge blank time, and selectable maximum duty cycle. The TPS7H5004-SP is a dual-output controller for push-pull and full-bridge topologies, with configurable leading edge blank time and fixed 50% maximum duty cycle. All devices include soft-start, hiccup-mode overcurrent protection, external fault protection, slope compensation, and thermal shutdown.

The coach reflects on a crucial win that kept his team in the series. He downplays an incident, noting quality chances followed and the opponent tied the game. He mentions an earlier own-goal on a delayed powerplay. They skated better and got more involved, a positive, but it was just one period; they aim to improve in the second, where the opponent dominated. He stresses "less is more," doing what they do, embracing the opportunity. The Rucchin line had two quality overtime chances and won a key faceoff. He praises a big kid who scored by stopping in front, rewarding doing things right. The opponent has good, competitive players; their leading scorer normally shuts down top lines. When Oates, Sykora, Kariya play together, that's perceived as the top line, but they match Rucchin against Madden. The team was more physical because they skated. He emphasizes possessing the puck and playing offense over defense. They've been consistent since Christmas: road games Kariya with Rucchin; home games with Oates. They didn't skate in the first two games, generating no offense; skating lets them pressure and play territorial. Last night was more even. He distinguishes individual and team career phases, commending an elite player's pride and professionalism. Competitors, like their goaltender, rally after mistakes. They had a good regular season with many one-goal wins, but allowed more than expected in the series. They tightened up after tying the game, building confidence. They aren't here by luck; they learn to play in tight situations. Bryan Murray's advice: never think things are good, because then they aren't. They need resiliency to regroup and be themselves. Media praise turned to criticism, but only the dressing room matters. Success is about team, not individuals, with Scott Stevens as figurehead. A player improved after being asked to turn and put his stick down; it's about timely decisions, not risk-reward. Keep the foot on the gas. The plan is simple: do what you know under pressure. They're trying to get the series back to a best-of. He ignores media notes, advising players not to read papers, though they do. It's about their preparation and pride. Yesterday was the first chance to do that; now another opportunity, just one game. Faceoff wins earn ice time, as with Pahlsson and Krog. Tomorrow's game will be at a higher level; they must manage the puck and stay controlled emotionally. The speaker, about to take the oath of office, acknowledges the sacred trust conferred by the people and consecrates himself to their service. He emphasizes that the democratic principle needs no apology and that good government depends on limiting partisan zeal and merging it into patriotism. The executive branch is transferred, but the government remains of all the people, and animosities should yield to acquiescence in the popular will and concern for the general welfare. He calls for abandoning sectional prejudice and renewing devotion to the Constitution, which should be administered in the spirit of amity and mutual concession. He pledges a just construction of the Constitution, respecting the division of federal and state powers. Every citizen shares the obligation to preserve the Constitution; voters exercise a public trust and must scrutinize public servants. Public expenditures should be limited to actual needs, and simplicity and economy encouraged. Foreign policy should adhere to independence, peace, and neutrality, avoiding entangling alliances, following the policy of Monroe, Washington, and Jefferson. Finances must be sound to secure business and labor, with revenue adjusted to relieve unnecessary taxation and prevent surplus. The public domain must be protected from unlawful occupation. Indians should be treated fairly as wards, with education and civilization toward citizenship; polygamy in Territories must be repressed. Laws against immigration of a servile class with repugnant customs should be enforced. Civil-service reform should be enforced to ensure merit and competency over partisan reward. Jane Goodall died on October 1 at age 91. The author recalls a 1990 conversation. Goodall studied chimpanzees in Gombe National Park for nearly 30 years, revealing their social complexity. She assembled a unique chimp skeleton collection. Her team retrieved bodies, used insects to clean bones, and documented each skeleton’s sex, age, weight, and life history. This allowed study of how individual development affects skeletal features, offering a new perspective for analyzing ancient hominid fossils. When asked about implications for early hominids, Goodall said, “We just don’t know.” She stressed not wasting anything, having collected skeletons from the start. Flo, a dominant matriarch who died in 1972, had a skeleton larger than most yet weighed less than a stockier male, illustrating the difficulty of estimating body weight from bones. Flo’s bone loss pattern differed from human osteoporosis; her skeletal strength aligned with observations of her giving birth near age 50. Only recently has evidence for menopause in older female chimps been found. Her collection continued to provide scientific insights even as she shifted to activism.

The author recounts that the second week of motherhood was the most difficult. After initial support and endorphins fade, sleep deprivation sets in, causing emotional fragility. Breastfeeding becomes painful with raw, bloody nipples, and prescription pain medication runs out. Babies had weight-gain issues due to low milk supply or allergies, leading to feelings of failure. Loneliness increases as the mother leaves, the husband returns to work, and visitors stop. The baby cries due to growth spurts, and the author cannot soothe her. Emotional rawness leads to fights with the partner over minor issues. The baby refuses to sleep at night, wanting only to eat or be held, making the author feel like an object. The situation eventually improves.

This paper examines the feasibility of cross-partisan education policy amid heightened political polarization. It notes that education, traditionally bipartisan, has become a focal point of political activism due to pandemic learning loss, the racial reckoning of 2020, increased parental scrutiny, and eroded trust in institutions. Despite federal gridlock, meaningful state-level policy changes with cross-party support are occurring.

The paper identifies five key factors common to successful cross-partisan initiatives:

1. **Easy to Communicate for Broad Appeal**: Policies that are simple to understand and grounded in widely held values gain momentum. Examples include the science of reading movement, spurred by the *Sold a Story* podcast, which led to laws in 15 states, and efforts to address the teacher shortage through apprenticeship programs using federal funds in states like Tennessee.

2. **Responsive to Local Context**: Success requires visible, credible local champions and solutions that feel tailored to community needs. The Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact, which began with military families, and state career and technical education programs in Idaho and North Carolina illustrate locally driven, cross-partisan efforts.

3. **Political Cover**: Policymakers need protection when taking risky positions. Teachers’ public dissatisfaction with reading curricula provided cover for science of reading legislation. In Virginia, a mandated seven-year deadline for revising history standards created urgency that helped a politically diverse board unanimously approve compromise standards after a contentious process.

4. **Both Sides Get a Win**: Allowing each side to claim victory facilitates progress. Teacher pay raise proposals in red states, often coupled with school choice expansion, and the surge in civics education legislation across 43 states demonstrate how differing political goals can be satisfied simultaneously.

5. **Using Media as an Accelerant**: Credentialed journalism can rapidly raise awareness and catalyze policy change. The *Sold a Story* podcast’s 3.5 million downloads and subsequent media coverage accelerated reading policy reforms. Similarly, media attention amplified the parent empowerment movement, increasing parental engagement and demand for transparency and options.

Additional strategic considerations include understanding the political landscape, managing expectations about traditional bipartisanship, establishing a shared definition of the problem, gauging the level of urgency, assessing the effect on frontline school staff, and framing issues as expanding opportunities rather than narrowing them. Experts caution against value signaling, mission creep, and failing to prioritize, and stress the importance of understanding opponents’ values.

The paper concludes that despite polarization, cross-partisan progress in education policy is achievable. State-level successes provide a blueprint, emphasizing clear communication, local support, political cover, mutual wins, and strategic media use. Education policy remains a potential unifying force and catalyst for positive societal change.

The double top pattern is a bearish reversal price action formation consisting of two swing highs at approximately the same level, with a swing low between them. It appears at the end of an uptrend or a prolonged pullback in a downtrend, signaling a potential downward reversal. The two highs form a resistance level; a neckline connecting the swing low to the preceding swing low acts as support. A break below the neckline suggests the uptrend may be over. Traders may close long positions or open short positions upon the neckline break, possibly waiting for a retest. Profit target is estimated by measuring the pattern's height and projecting it downward from the neckline. Stop loss can be placed in the middle of the pattern (better reward/risk) or above it (safer but poorer ratio). Trading rules include identifying an existing uptrend, ensuring both swing highs are within 3% of each other, and waiting for a significant volume break below the neckline. Coding a double top backtest is difficult. Research by Thomas Bulkowski, using 500 stocks over 5 years, found that only 39% of double top formations reach their target, compared to 68% for double bottoms. The stock market's tailwind (inflation and productivity) makes shorting difficult. Thus, the double top pattern strategy is a tough formation to trade.

This systematic review and meta-analysis included five studies from Ethiopia (2016–2023) and found a pooled Chikungunya seroprevalence of 12.35%. The highest district-level prevalence was in Debub Ari (51.58%) and the lowest in Lare (6.25%). Risk factors included occupation (farmers had higher prevalence), education (those with formal education had higher prevalence), and age (adults generally higher, though one study reported highest in 5–14 years). Sex-based prevalence was inconsistent across studies. The meta-analysis showed significant heterogeneity (I²=97.72%), partly explained by test type (ELISA vs. RT-qPCR). No publication bias was detected. The authors note the limited number of studies and recommend considering these factors for control and prevention strategies.

The book addresses building distributed systems using containers and container orchestration, assuming reader familiarity with these technologies. It provides patterns to simplify design, improve reliability, and enable reuse. The introduction explains that modern applications demand distributed systems for availability, reliability, and scalability, and traces the evolution from single-purpose machines to client-server and distributed architectures. Containers and orchestrators are presented as foundational building blocks that enable reusable patterns, analogous to how object-oriented patterns advanced software development. Patterns offer shared vocabulary, learning from past mistakes, and reusable components.

Single-node patterns involve tightly coupled containers co-located on one machine. The sidecar pattern augments an application container by adding functionality like HTTPS, configuration synchronization, or monitoring without altering the original container. The ambassador pattern brokers communication between the application container and external services, such as sharded storage proxies, service discovery, or request splitting for experiments. The adapter pattern modifies the application container’s interface to conform to standardized monitoring, logging, or health-check interfaces, promoting consistency across heterogeneous applications. These patterns stress parameterization, clear API definitions, and documentation for modular reuse.

Multi-node patterns address loosely coupled components across machines. The replicated load-balanced service pattern uses identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer, with readiness probes to manage traffic. Variations include session tracking via consistent hashing and adding caching layers (e.g., Varnish) or SSL termination (e.g., nginx) as separate replicated tiers. The sharded service pattern is introduced for stateful services where data size exceeds a single machine’s capacity, with each shard handling a subset of requests. A sharded cache design is begun, noting the need to consider why sharding is required and the cache’s role in the architecture.

A follow-through day is a market-timing concept developed by William J. O’Neil to signal a change from a downtrend or market correction to a new uptrend. It occurs during a correction when a major index (e.g., S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow) closes significantly higher than the previous day with greater volume, on Day 4 or later of an attempted rally.

The process begins with a rally attempt. Day 1 is any day the index gains in price, or a “pink rally day” where it closes slightly down but in the top half of its range. The rally attempt remains valid as long as the index does not make a new low. On Days 2 and 3, the intraday low must not fall below Day 1’s low; if any rally day’s low goes below a previous rally day’s low, the attempt fails and restarts. A follow-through day can occur from Day 4 onward, characterized by a big gain and higher volume, confirming a new uptrend. Best signals typically appear between Day 4 and Day 7, though later ones have worked.

The signal is not perfect; investors should study leading stocks and sentiment and not immediately become fully invested. Early failure signs include: if an additional follow-through day closes above the low of the prior follow-through day, one may hold; if the index falls below the low where Rally Day 1 began, the follow-through day has completely failed (a sell signal). Since the early 1900s, no bull market has started without a follow-through day, though not all such days led to bull markets.

A backtest on the S&P 500 (using SPY) with an exit after n-days showed poor short-term results because the market has been mean-reverting, making buying on weakness preferable. Results improved slightly with a filter (e.g., 25-day RSI below 55). O’Neil focuses on individual stocks, not index trading, so results might differ on stocks. The backtest concludes follow-through days are not particularly useful for short-term index traders.

Using follow-through day analysis can help investors enter a new bull market ahead of economic news, as equity markets lead economic cycles. The backtest rules require: Day 1 closes higher, Days 2 and 3 lows not below Day 1’s low, and on Day 4 a gain of at least 0.75 of the 25-day average high-low range, with buying at the close.

The passage discusses motivations for splitting applications into multiple containers on a single machine: resource isolation, team ownership, and separation of concerns. It then presents single-node container patterns. The sidecar pattern augments an application container with additional functionality, such as adding HTTPS to a legacy service, dynamic configuration synchronization, process monitoring (topz), or building a simple PaaS. The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between the application container and external services, enabling sharded service access, service brokering across environments, and request splitting for experimentation. The adapter pattern modifies the application container’s interface to conform to a standard, used for monitoring (e.g., Prometheus exporter), logging normalization (e.g., Fluentd), and health checks.

The passage then covers multi-node distributed patterns. Replicated load-balanced services use identical replicas behind a load balancer, with readiness probes, and can be extended with session tracking, caching layers (Varnish), and SSL termination (nginx). Sharded services distribute requests to specific replicas based on a sharding function, often used for stateful services like caches. Sharded caches increase memory utilization but require careful key selection and may use consistent hashing to minimize remapping during scaling. The passage also describes deploying replicated sharded caches and shard routing services.

The lecture presents lower bounds for the predecessor problem. It surveys historical results: Ajtai (1988) gave an Ω(√log w) bound; Miltersen introduced communication complexity and proved bounds like Ω(∛log n); Beame and Fich (1999) and Xiao independently proved bounds of Ω(log w / log log w) for some n and Ω(√log n / log log n) for some w; Sen (2003) gave a clean round-elimination proof; Patrascu and Thorup (2006–2007) provided a tight trade-off involving space. The lecture focuses on the colored predecessor problem (reporting only the color of the predecessor) and the communication complexity perspective: Alice is the query algorithm with input x (the query), Bob is the data structure (memory) with input y (the data structure). Messages correspond to memory reads, with Alice sending log s bits (address) and Bob responding with w bits (word). The round elimination lemma states: if there is a protocol for a problem f^(k) (Alice has k inputs, Bob knows i and y, goal is f(x_i, y)) with Alice speaking first, error δ, and m messages, then there is a protocol for f with Bob speaking first, error increased by O(√(a/k)), and m−1 messages. By splitting the input appropriately (word into chunks for Alice→Bob, or data items into subtrees for Bob→Alice) with k = Θ(at²) or Θ(bt²), each elimination increases error by O(1/t). Iterating eliminates all messages, leading to contradiction unless the number of rounds t is large. The resulting lower bound for colored predecessor with polynomial space is Ω(min(log_a w, log_b n)), which simplifies to Ω(min(log_w n, log w / log log n)). This matches fusion trees and Van Emde Boas up to a log log factor.

During Supreme Court oral argument, several justices appeared willing to allow trial courts to limit attorney-client discussions during overnight recesses while a defendant testifies, prohibiting direct discussion of testimony but permitting collateral trial strategy matters. The case involves David Villarreal, convicted of murder after the trial judge barred his lawyer from discussing his testimony overnight. Villarreal argued this denied effective assistance of counsel, but Texas courts affirmed. His attorney, Stuart Banner, contended the line between testimony and strategy is unworkable and would chill defense lawyers. Justices Jackson and Kagan suggested a line can be drawn, while Gorsuch discussed prohibiting coaching. Texas prosecutor Andrew Warthen said even advice on mumbling or eye contact constitutes impermissible coaching. Justice Barrett proposed a rule barring discussion of testimony content or delivery manner but allowing strategic consequences. The Court may choose between Texas's proposed line—disallowing "management" of testimony but allowing indirectly related matters—and the U.S. government's bright-line rule against any discussion of testimony. The government clarified that advising a plea bargain would be permissible under its rule.

The Piotroski F-Score strategy, developed by Stanford professor Joseph Piotroski, is a stock selection method using financial analysis to identify undervalued stocks with strong fundamentals. It calculates a score from 9 criteria covering profitability, liquidity, and efficiency, each scored 0 or 1. Stocks scoring 8–9 are considered to have strong financials, while scores of 0–4 indicate poor financials. The strategy is popular among value investors and also useful for growth stock selection, but it is not a guarantee of success and should be used with other research. Benefits include simplicity, objectivity, risk reduction, and portfolio diversification. Establishing a winning strategy involves setting investment goals, researching the market, calculating the F-Score, making informed decisions, diversifying, and monitoring regularly. Backtesting on historical data is recommended to evaluate performance. Alpha Architect backtested the F-score on NYSE stocks (1974–2014, top 40% by market value). For stocks scoring at least 6, Alpha Architect’s modified version returned 13.3% annually, the original Piotroski score 12.6%, and the S&P 500 11.2%, with similar standard deviations. When applied to the cheapest 20% of stocks with scores above 6, returns were 15.9%, 15.2%, and 11.2% respectively. ValueSignals tested Piotroski scores on European stocks (June 1999–2011) without value sorting. Alexander Eriksen’s master’s thesis studied the score on Norwegian and Swedish stocks (1997–2011) with annual rebalancing, comparing Piotroski’s method, a contrarian strategy, and a combination, using portfolios of 10 “good” and “bad” stocks. The blog hosting this article has over 1200 articles with trading rules, compiled into a purchasable package with plain English logic for Python backtesting. Premium strategies are also offered for a fee. Implementing the Piotroski F-Score in a portfolio involves determining goals, calculating the score, identifying high-scoring stocks, conducting additional research, selecting stocks, diversifying, monitoring, and rebalancing.

The NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU family includes GA102 and GA104, fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm process with 28.3 billion transistors and a 628.4 mm² die. The full GA102 GPU contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, 10752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores. The SM doubles FP32 processing by enabling FP32 operations on both datapaths. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput and support concurrent execution of RT with graphics or compute workloads. Third-generation Tensor Cores introduce sparsity support and TF32 precision, offering up to 5x training throughput over the previous generation. Memory configurations include GDDR6X on GeForce RTX 3090 and 3080, and 48 GB GDDR6 on RTX A6000 and A40. GA102 features third-generation NVLink, PCIe Gen 4, and ROPs integrated into GPCs (112 total). The unified L1 cache/shared memory is 128 KB per SM, configurable. Compared to Turing, Ampere delivers up to 1.7x faster raster performance, up to 2x faster ray tracing, and up to 1.9x higher power efficiency. GeForce RTX 3090 targets 8K HDR gaming, RTX 3080 provides up to 2x the performance of RTX 2080, and RTX 3070 rivals RTX 2080 Ti. RTX A6000 and A40 accelerate professional rendering, AI, and compute workloads.

This study compared immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines in healthy controls and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients treated with methotrexate (MTX), abatacept, or rituximab. Rituximab-treated individuals showed near-total loss of anti-S antibodies. Abatacept treatment significantly reduced S-specific and neutralizing antibody levels, while MTX did not significantly lower antibody responses, though a subset trended lower. The number of RBD-specific B cells was similar across control, MTX, and abatacept groups, but abatacept reduced B cell activation, impaired class switching to IgG, and altered memory B cell differentiation. S-specific CD4+ T cell frequencies were decreased in MTX-treated subjects and trended lower with abatacept. Abatacept also diminished production of IL-2, IFNγ, and IL-21 by S-specific T cells, with co-expression of IL-21, IL-2, and IFNγ highly reduced in both MTX and abatacept groups. Expression of IL-21 or IFNγ correlated with serum antibody levels. Age and time post-vaccination did not account for the diminished responses. The findings indicate abatacept limits vaccine efficacy by impairing T cell help for B cells, leading to reduced high-titer, class-switched neutralizing antibodies, and support temporary cessation of abatacept before vaccination when clinically manageable.

Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund Danantara will launch at least eight waste-to-power projects by the end of October, beginning in Jakarta and expanding to 33 municipalities across Java and Bali. Each plant will process 1,000 tonnes of waste daily, generating 15 megawatts of electricity, with capital costs of 2–3 trillion rupiah per facility. Danantara will finance and oversee the projects, while state utility PLN will purchase the electricity. The government has removed tipping fees and local governments will provide land. The initiative aligns with Indonesia’s 2025–2034 electricity plan targeting 453 MW from waste-to-energy, requiring $2.72 billion in investment, and reflects Danantara’s dual mandate of financial returns and national priorities like pollution control and energy security.
Delta Air Lines intends to acquire up to an additional 32% of Grupo Aeroméxico at MXP$43.59 per share, pending approvals. It owns 4.1% and an option for 8.1%, targeting up to 49%.

This study developed and psychometrically evaluated an Arabic version of the Orthognathic Quality of Life Questionnaire (OQLQ). The OQLQ, originally in English, measures quality of life in patients with dentofacial deformities undergoing orthognathic surgery. The translation process involved forward and back-translation, expert committee review, and pilot testing. The study included 74 adult patients from a private practice in Saudi Arabia, with a subset of 15 completing test-retest reliability and 12 providing paired pre- and post-surgery data. Reliability was assessed via internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.92, excellent) and test-retest correlations (overall Spearman’s correlation 0.859, excellent; awareness of dentofacial deformity domain 0.601, good). Validity was supported by significant correlations between overall OQLQ scores and both satisfaction with surgical treatment (VAS) and subjective appearance improvement after surgery. Responsiveness was demonstrated by significantly lower overall OQLQ scores after surgery compared to before surgery in both the full cohort and the paired subgroup, with the facial esthetics domain also significantly improved in the paired analysis. The Arabic OQLQ was found to be conceptually similar to the original, reliable, valid, and responsive for assessing quality of life changes following orthognathic treatment.

MTN and four banks plan to raise a combined GH¢4.67 billion on the Ghana Stock Exchange within six months, a historic test. The Supreme Court will hear arguments on October 14 in a case considering whether the ex post facto clause applies to restitution under the federal Mandatory Victims Restitution Act. The clause prohibits ex post facto laws and traditionally applies only to criminal punishments. Defendant Holsey Ellingburg, who robbed a bank, argues that restitution under the MVRA is criminal because it is imposed as part of a criminal sentence, uses criminal procedures, gives victims little role, and failure to pay results in incarceration. The MVRA describes restitution as serving punitive purposes, and the Supreme Court has called it a criminal sanction. The government concedes restitution is criminal. A court-appointed amicus argues the evidence is insufficient. The author guesses the justices will not uphold the sentence enhancement.

Stephen Pearse, an angel investor and former CEO, introduces himself and his background in telecommunications, IT, and health science. He states that out of every 10 startups, about one will succeed, defined as returning at least 10x to investors, while three may yield a moderate return and six will fail. He explains that a startup must plan for an exit, either going public or being sold, and must always state the intention to go public to secure investment. He describes how startups can develop products faster than large companies because employees are motivated by stock.

Pearse discusses the importance of a powerful elevator pitch to cut through noise, emphasizing the need for a hook, simplicity, and inducing greed in investors. He advises keeping presentations to 20 minutes, using pictures, and avoiding technical rat holes. A pitch should include the hook, solution, magic/technology, business model, competition, management, financials, status, and an offer. He stresses presenting customer and business benefits over technical features, boiling value down to saving or making money. The presenter must show passion, confidence, and engage the audience.

He provides examples of a bad pitch and a good pitch. He advises raising money when it is not needed, orchestrating pitches in parallel to create a feeding frenzy, and prioritizing a venture capital firm's brand and network over minor equity dilution. He highlights the critical importance of cash flow, the likelihood of pivoting, and that speed of execution is more important than patents. He notes the importance of the team, focus, and leadership, concluding that investors primarily offer network connections rather than hands-on help.

This systematic review synthesized evidence on how personality traits influence student satisfaction and success in online higher education. Following Cochrane and PRISMA guidelines, databases were searched for peer-reviewed studies (January 2000–June 2024) that used recognized personality assessments (Big Five or Myers-Briggs types) and measured satisfaction and/or success (grades/completion). After screening, 23 studies were included, all classified as level 4 evidence.

Three themes emerged. Theme 1 examined the interaction between personality and online education. Five studies on GPA found conscientiousness, openness, agreeableness, and emotional stability positively correlated with GPA, while neuroticism generally correlated negatively; extraversion did not influence GPA. Two studies assessing both GPA and satisfaction using Myers-Briggs found no significant personality effect on GPA but did find effects on satisfaction, with introverts preferring online classes and extraverts preferring face-to-face. Four studies on satisfaction found conscientiousness positively influenced satisfaction; agreeableness and openness were also positively related, while neuroticism was negatively related. Two studies on assignment preferences found extraversion correlated with interactive elements, agreeableness with higher satisfaction across assignments, and conscientiousness with satisfaction with media assignments. One study on learning engagement found extraversion, agreeableness, openness, and conscientiousness positively associated with engagement, while neuroticism had a negative relationship; adaptability mediated engagement for some traits.

Theme 2 compared personality across different class formats. Two studies on satisfaction found extraversion linked to higher satisfaction in face-to-face classes, and in online/blended formats, extraverts were less likely to recommend fully online courses, while feelers and intuitives were more satisfied with discussions. Two studies on grades found high conscientiousness significantly related to higher grades regardless of format. One study on grades and satisfaction found neurotic students performed better and enjoyed face-to-face settings more, while emotionally stable students succeeded in all formats; extraverts preferred face-to-face but had lower grades there.

Theme 3 evaluated personality and choice of class format. Three studies found students high in conscientiousness, agreeableness, and openness were more likely to adopt online education, while those high in neuroticism were least likely. Students choosing online courses had higher GPAs, and conscientiousness predicted higher grades in both settings.

The review noted all included studies were low evidence level and none examined occupational therapy programs. Findings reinforced that neuroticism is most negatively related to online success/satisfaction, while agreeableness and conscientiousness are generally beneficial. Educators should consider personality traits, employ universal design for learning, and support self-regulated learning to accommodate diverse learners. Limitations included low evidence levels, the search timeframe, and geographic variability. Future research should develop and test interventions and address the gap in occupational therapy education.

Turing GPUs introduce hardware support for VirtualLink, a USB-C alternate mode delivering power, display, and data over a single connector for VR headsets, simplifying setup and enabling small form factor devices. NVLink replaces MIO/PCIe for SLI, providing up to 100 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth on TU102, enabling new display topologies but not 3-way/4-way SLI.

Turing features RT Cores that accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray/triangle intersection tests, offloading the SM and enabling real-time ray tracing. A hybrid rendering model combines rasterization and ray tracing, using ray tracing for reflections, refractions, and shadows. Denoising algorithms reduce required rays per pixel. RT Cores deliver over 10 Giga Rays/sec, about 10x faster than Pascal software emulation.

Tensor Cores power NGX deep learning features: DLSS (Deep Learning Super-Sampling) uses a neural network trained on 64x supersampled images to produce high-quality output from lower sample counts, improving performance; DLSS 2X mode approaches 64xSS quality. Other NGX features include InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Mesh Shading introduces Task and Mesh Shaders with cooperative thread models, enabling efficient culling, level-of-detail selection, and procedural geometry generation, reducing CPU draw call bottlenecks. Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows shading rate to vary per 16x16 pixel region, supporting content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading (TSS) decouples shading from screen space, storing results in texture space for reuse, improving temporal stability and VR efficiency. Multi-View Rendering (MVR) expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection to up to four views per pass, supporting canted VR displays and single-pass cascaded shadow maps.

Turing TU104 and TU106 GPUs include RT Cores, Tensor Cores, and the new SM architecture. TU104 has 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one NVLink link; TU106 has 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 36 RT Cores, and no NVLink. The Tesla T4 uses a TU104 variant with 2560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores for inference. A new RTX-OPS metric weights peak operations by typical hybrid rendering workload distribution: Tensor 20%, FP32 80%, RT 40%, INT32 28%. Ray tracing improvements include ray-traced shadows with contact hardening, ambient occlusion, and reflections, demonstrated in games like Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider.

This study investigated Colombian university students' perceptions and preferences between online learning (OL) and emergency remote education (ERE). OL is defined as an intentionally planned, flexible modality using ICT, while ERE emerged as a temporary crisis response to the COVID-19 pandemic, characterized by synchronous interaction and limited planning time. The research question asked: What are students' perceptions and preferences about/between OL and ERE?

A case study was conducted at a medium-sized private university in Colombia's Caribbean region. Participants were 88 undergraduate students who had experienced both OL courses (designed pre-pandemic) and ERE courses (designed during the emergency). Data were collected via a survey with 14 items rated on a 1-10 scale across dimensions such as content quality, interaction, assessment, feedback, time, resources, and technical support. The add-on preferential groups (APG) model was used to analyze preferences and perceptions, supplemented by permutation tests and content analysis of open-ended questions.

Descriptive statistics showed OL received higher average scores than ERE on most items, with statistically significant differences in 10 of 14 items, particularly in time for independent/asynchronous activities, learning assessment strategies, and content quality. APG analysis revealed that over 70% of students held positive perceptions of both modalities. However, students preferred OL over ERE for most dimensions: over 57% preferred OL for time for independent/asynchronous activities (65.34%), assessment strategies (61.39%), and content quality/quantity (60.23%). The exception was student-student interaction, where preferences were nearly equal (OL 50.01%, ERE 49.99%), and a slightly higher percentage perceived ERE as more effective for this dimension. Permutation tests confirmed significant differences between groups.

Content analysis of open-ended responses identified advantages of ERE: adaptation during COVID-19, comfort/flexibility, cost savings, ICT use, effective learning, peer interaction, and instructor contact. Disadvantages included lack of organization/structure, insufficient instructor preparation, excessive content, and need for more dynamic technological resources. For OL, advantages were structure/organization, comfort/flexibility, learning effectiveness, interaction, and ICT use. Disadvantages included need for improved student-instructor interaction, more varied activities, reduced content overload, and more synchronous sessions.

The study concluded that students generally perceive both modalities positively but rate OL higher. ERE was valued for synchronous peer interaction. Findings highlight the need for ongoing instructor training in pedagogical and technological competencies, design of authentic assessments, and creation of spaces that promote interaction in both modalities to inform post-pandemic learning design.

Digital leaders use data-driven objectives to align their organization around shared goals, with transparent methodology and clear connection to strategy, creating a "North Star" vision. Implementation involves a combined top-down and bottom-up process for buy-in. However, even leaders sometimes struggle with over-analysis, risking loss of human intuition. Digital laggards fail to connect goals with strategy, leading to misalignment and a "culture of genius" where individuals pursue their own priorities. Data culture aligns organizations vertically (through metrics linking individuals to company goals) and horizontally (via common data models and transparent access enabling collaboration). Digital leaders emphasize data culture as central, adopting a learning mindset, transparent data access, and clear metrics. Their culture aligns beliefs, values, and actions consistently. Laggards show misalignment between espoused values and behavior; changing mindsets is challenging and requires compelling reasons. Transformation is possible, as some leaders have transformed. Mature firms exhibit advantages in outcomes and data culture, valuing learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement. Organizations fall into four patterns: data novice (recognize need but lack culture/systems), insight ready (accepting culture but insufficient architecture), tech enabled (have technology but lack experimentation culture), and data reliant (over-rely on data, discouraging critical thinking). Companies can target actions to improve. Keystone Strategy is a consulting firm specializing in technology-led strategy and digital transformation.

This statistical analysis plan (SAP) details methods for analyzing data from Zealand Pharma A/S protocol ZP4207-17086, a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled, parallel-arm trial of dasiglucagon versus placebo and GlucaGen® in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus. The primary objective is to demonstrate superiority of a single 0.6 mg dasiglucagon injection over placebo in treating hypoglycemia. Secondary objectives include comparing dasiglucagon to GlucaGen®, and assessing safety and pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles.

The study includes a screening period, a treatment period (Day 0–1), and a Day 28 follow-up. Sample size is 20 patients for dasiglucagon, 10 for placebo, and 10 for GlucaGen®, providing 90% power for the primary endpoint using a 2-sided log-rank test at 5% significance.

Analysis sets are: Safety analysis set (randomized patients receiving ≥1 dose, analyzed as treated), Full analysis set (FAS; all safety set patients, analyzed as randomized), and Per protocol set (PPS; FAS without relevant protocol deviations). The primary efficacy analysis uses FAS, with a secondary analysis on PPS. Safety analyses use the safety set.

The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery (first increase ≥20 mg/dL from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose). It is analyzed via Kaplan-Meier methods and a stratified log-rank test (stratified by age group and injection site), with censoring at 45 minutes for non-recovery or rescue IV glucose. Sensitivity analyses include no censoring for rescue, censoring at rescue time, and linear interpolation of recovery times. A discrete-time Cox proportional hazards model is used descriptively. Covariates are age group (6–11, 12–17 years) and injection site (abdomen/thigh).

Secondary efficacy endpoints include plasma glucose recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes (analyzed by Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test) and plasma glucose changes from baseline at those time points (analyzed by ANOVA). A hierarchical testing procedure controls multiplicity for dasiglucagon versus placebo comparisons; GlucaGen® comparisons are not part of the hierarchy.

PK parameters (Cmax, Tmax, AUC, etc.) are calculated by non-compartmental analysis using Phoenix® WinNonlin®. Plasma glucose pharmacodynamics are assessed via AUE0-30min. Safety analyses cover extent of exposure, local tolerability, adverse events (TEAEs coded with MedDRA), laboratory tests, vital signs, ECG (including QTcF categorical analysis), and immunogenicity (anti-drug antibodies). All statistical tests are 2-sided at 0.05 significance level, performed with SAS® 9.4 or higher. The SAP notes changes from the protocol, including reworded primary analysis and added sensitivity analyses.
