The GA10x memory subsystem uses GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron, which employs PAM4 signaling to double data rate by transmitting two bits per clock edge. GDDR6X achieves over 900 GB/sec bandwidth, with up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and 936 GB/sec peak on GA10x GPUs, a 52% improvement over TU102. MTA encoding limits signal transitions to improve SNR. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft DirectStorage, enables GPU-based lossless decompression, offloading CPU work and improving I/O performance up to 100x over hard drives, reducing load times and enabling detailed open worlds. The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU, based on GA10x Ampere architecture, delivers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, 5x AI training throughput with sparsity, 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, and supports vGPU. Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC for 8K60, HDMI 2.1 for 8K60 and 4K120, HDCP 2.3, fifth-gen NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-gen NVENC. GeForce RTX 30-series GPUs provide up to 2x performance in shading, ray tracing, and AI, with second-gen RT Cores and third-gen Tensor Cores. The RTX A6000 offers 48GB GDDR6, 10,752 CUDA Cores, and improved rendering and compute performance. EDR technology on GDDR6X detects and replays transmission errors, aiding overclocking stability.

The Russell 2000 Index is a market-weighted index tracking approximately 2,000 small-cap U.S. stocks, representing about 10% of total U.S. market capitalization. It is a subset of the Russell 3000 Index. The index rebalances annually on the fourth Friday of June; the exact date varies, so traders should check Russell’s website. Rebalancing adjusts the index constituents—adding stocks that meet criteria, removing those that do not, and adjusting weights—to maintain accurate representation of the small-cap segment. This buying and selling can cause temporary market imbalances. A trading strategy exploits an observed abnormal outperformance during this rebalancing period: buying at the close of the first trading day after June 23rd and selling at the close of the first trading day of July. Backtesting from 1988 using the cash index (^RUT, excluding dividends) shows an average gain of 1.34% over an average holding period of six trading days, well above random periods. Over the same window, the S&P 500 gained an average of 0.85%. The Russell 2000 typically shows no positive performance up to June 23rd, and June is generally a poor month for the stock market, making the end-of-June rally notable. A hedged version (50% long Russell 2000, 50% short S&P 500) produced an average gain of only 0.23%, with flattish performance and poor results in the first 12 years.

During a government shutdown, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) has identified between 4,132 and 4,232 federal workers for layoffs. The President returns the bill "An act making appropriations for the improvement of certain harbors and rivers" to the House with objections. The bill appropriates $1,378,450 for over forty separate objects, many local. He argues the Constitution does not grant the Federal Government power to construct internal improvements or appropriate money for that purpose. No express grant exists, and the power is not a necessary and proper incident to any granted power. A broad construction would lead to consolidation of power, threatening the republican system. Several predecessors denied this power.

He distinguishes permissible appropriations for lighthouses, beacons, buoys, and piers on ocean and lake shores connected to foreign commerce, but objects beyond that line, unconnected to foreign commerce or Navy protection, raise difficulty. A predecessor attempted to confine expenditures below ports of entry or delivery, but that restriction was evaded because ports can be established on unimportant rivers and many exist only on paper with no actual foreign commerce. Applying a sound restriction to only ports with real foreign commerce, the bill contains appropriations for over twenty objects at places never declared ports of entry or delivery, with no record of foreign merchandise arrivals or vessel clearances. It includes rivers with no foreign commerce, creeks called harbors benefiting only local neighborhoods, and improvements that advantage one place at the expense of another.

Sanctioning the bill would concede a general power for internal improvements, removing constitutional limitations. Practical evils include consolidation of power, local benefits at the common Treasury's expense, sectional feelings, destruction of legislative harmony, combinations for wasteful spending, a scramble for public money, injustice to states that self-funded improvements, and oppression of states that deny the power. A large portion of the Union would see the national treasure unequally disbursed for small sections. These evils would multiply with the country's expansion. The framers wisely withheld such power from the Federal Government.

Even absent constitutional objections, the bill appropriates between $1,000,000 and $2,000,000 for non-pressing objects during a foreign war, when Congress authorized a loan or Treasury notes. Wisdom dictates husbanding means and avoiding public debt. If enacted, the principle would lead to annually increasing appropriations and drains, resulting in increased debt or taxation. He therefore withholds approval.

The passage discusses the established rule that damages for the detention of a fishing vessel are measured by the loss of its probable catch. It references numerous domestic cases and international tribunal decisions, including The Hope On (Chile) and the Col. Lloyd Aspinwall (Spain). The Bering Sea Commission, which resolved claims of Canadian sealers against the United States, adopted this rule after thorough examination. Awards in cases such as the Favorite, Alfred Adams, and Triumph show that compensation was based on estimated catch; for example, the Triumph award of $15,450 corresponded to the value of 1,928 skins at $8 each. The passage also states the principle that a government agent may not forcibly enroll aliens from a peaceably engaged friendly ship into public service without consent, citing Hall's International Law.

The passage discusses a short-term trading pattern in the SPY (S&P 500 ETF) where it tends to be higher the day after a decline (red day) and lower after a rise (green day). This is attributed to mean reversion, the concept that asset prices revert to their long-term average, as opposed to momentum which follows trends. A simple strategy was backtested: buying after a red day and selling after a green day, using dividend- and split-adjusted SPY data. The backtest showed that the red day strategy yielded impressive returns, with higher CAGR, less time in the market, better risk-adjusted returns, and less than half the maximum drawdown compared to the green day strategy. The conclusion is that the S&P 500 is highly mean reverting in the short term, while trend following/momentum remains effective over longer timeframes.

A PEN America report recorded 22,810 book banning instances in U.S. public schools from 2021–2025. A climate of fear exists among librarians. Historically, higher education was indifferent to Banned Books Week, but now book banning is widespread. Examples: Franciscan University banned a book about the Virgin Mary’s sex life and demoted a chair; New College of Florida discarded its gender studies library, celebrated by conservatives. At military academies, the Trump administration removed books; at the Naval Academy, 20 were banned for "wrongthink." Trump’s executive orders aim to extend censorship to all colleges. In St. Louis & San Francisco Railroad Company v. Conarty, the Arkansas Supreme Court affirmed a judgment for the plaintiff, Fannie M. Conarty, as administratrix of her husband's estate. The husband, a switchman, was fatally injured when his engine collided with a coal car that lacked a draw-bar and coupler. The action was brought under the Federal Employers' Liability Act and Safety Appliance Act. The court ruled: (1) The case could not be removed to federal court because the Employers' Liability Act validly prohibits removal. (2) The amended act permits only one suit for the benefit of the widow and next of kin, which may include compensation for both pecuniary loss and the deceased's pain and suffering. (3) The car, loaded with coal for interstate shipment but diverted to Fort Smith for heavy repairs, was still in use in interstate commerce when the injury occurred, so the Safety Appliance Act applied. (4) The defective coupler was the proximate cause of the injury; the collision would not have injured the deceased if the coupler had been in place, even though he was not attempting to couple. (5) The widow's testimony about the amount of contributions she received was admissible because it was collateral to the liability issue and only concerned the amount of damages. The judgment was affirmed.

This work investigates the ultimate precision limit for continuous-wave interferometry with time-dependent signals. Using pure squeezed-state inputs with finite bandwidth ∆Ω, the spectral quantum Cramer-Rao bound is ¯Sδ ˜ϕδ ˜ϕ[Ω] ≥ 1/[(∆Ω/π) n(n+2)], where n is photon flux per mode. For n≫2, this yields Heisenberg scaling (∼1/n). Precision increases with inverse bandwidth and inverse square of photon occupancy. The bound is achievable with a nonlinear estimator using two homodyne detectors in quadrature: δ ˜ϕ(t) = (˜qout1(t)² − ˜qout2(t)²) / ((V+−V−)∆Ω/π). Intuitively, homodyne variances oscillate out of phase with the signal, and rectifying and subtracting recovers the signal.

The Rubber Band trading strategy is a simple, contrarian/mean-reversion approach for trading stocks. It aims to identify overbought or oversold market conditions where the price is likely to snap back toward the mean. Traders may use indicators such as Keltner Channels, Bollinger Bands, or momentum oscillators. The price of a security tends to revert to the mean after moving significantly away, regardless of trend direction. The strategy requires a contrarian mentality: buying when the market is battered and negative sentiment is high, and selling when euphoria is high. A common indicator is the Keltner Channel with a 20-period and 10-period ATR setting. When price trades above the upper band, a reversal down to the mean is likely; when below the lower band, a reversal up is likely. A buy setup occurs when the price bar opens and closes below the lower band, potentially confirmed by a bullish reversal candlestick like a hammer. The profit target is the middle band or just before the upper band. A sell setup occurs when price is above the upper band, confirmed by a bearish reversal candlestick like a shooting star, with a profit target at the middle band or just before the lower band. A backtested example from April 2013 on XLP showed 328 trades, average gain per trade 0.45%, CAGR 6.1%, time in market 20%, profit factor 2, and max drawdown 16%. The strategy works mainly on stocks, not gold or commodities.

Chronic hepatitis C (CHC) leads to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, with complications including type 2 diabetes (T2DM). HCV infection is a T2DM risk factor; clearance may reduce risk. This study evaluated their prognostic value in CHC-associated cirrhosis with T2DM. The study included 56 patients with both conditions (group A), 85 with cirrhosis only (group B), and 85 with T2DM only (group C) from Fu yang Second People's Hospital (2018-2021). Group A was divided into poor (23) and good (33) prognosis after 6 months. Blood parameters (ALB, AST, ALT) and cell counts (platelet, lymphocyte, mononuclear, neutrophil) were measured. NLR, PNI, PLR were calculated: NLR=neutrophil/lymphocyte; PNI=ALB(g/L)+5×total lymphocyte count; PLR=platelet/lymphocyte. First admission lab data were used.

TeraAgent is a distributed simulation engine that extends the agent-based modeling platform BioDynaMo to overcome its single-server limitation. It enables scale-out execution by spatially partitioning the simulation space across multiple servers using MPI, leveraging the local interaction characteristic of agent-based models. Key contributions include a tailored serialization mechanism (TeraAgent IO) that avoids pointer deduplication, full deserialization, endianness conversions, and schema evolution, allowing direct use of received buffers with full mutability of data structures. A delta encoding scheme compresses inter-server communication by exploiting the gradual attribute changes across simulation iterations. The engine supports distributed initialization, incremental neighbor search grid updates, and load balancing via global and diffusive methods. Evaluation shows TeraAgent simulates 250× more agents than BioDynaMo, achieves an 8× higher agent update rate per CPU core than Biocellion, and improves visualization performance by 39×. Median serialization performance increases by 110× and deserialization by 37×; delta encoding reduces data transfer by up to 3.5×. TeraAgent scales to 501.51 billion agents on 84096 CPU cores. It allows seamless transition from laptops to supercomputers without requiring model code changes for many simulations.

Soil-transmitted helminth (STH) infections affect over one billion people, and the WHO recommends preventive chemotherapy (PC) alongside sanitation and hygiene education. After five years of PC, impact assessment surveys (IAS) estimate prevalence to decide whether to continue PC, with a suspension threshold of less than 2% prevalence. The cost of IAS is challenging for endemic countries. Model-based geostatistical (MBG) methods can improve survey precision. The paper proposes using baseline prevalence data, environmental covariates, and PC history to design more cost-efficient IAS. The approach fits a geostatistical model to baseline data to predict a prevalence surface, then projects it forward using a multi-state Markov model that estimates transition probabilities between five endemicity classes based on the number of effective PC rounds (coverage ≥75%). A local thinning step scales down the baseline surface to generate a best-guess impact prevalence surface. Candidate survey designs, defined by number of schools, children per school, inclusion function, and minimum spacing, are evaluated by simulating from this surface and comparing classification accuracy and cost against classical methods. The methodology was applied to Kenya, Zimbabwe, and Sierra Leone. Kenya’s longitudinal data were used to estimate transition probabilities. Projected impact surfaces matched actual surfaces well for Kenya but less so for the other countries due to differing endemicity levels. Simulation results showed that MBG designs achieved equivalent accuracy to classical designs with substantially smaller sample sizes, reducing survey costs by an average of 80% (91% in Zimbabwe, 86% in Kenya, 62% in Sierra Leone). The MBG approach can deliver impact assessments with higher accuracy at much lower cost, potentially reducing survey expenses to one-fifth of classical surveys, and provides fine-scale prevalence maps useful for identifying residual hotspots.

This study investigated combining plasma biomarkers (Aβ42/40, p-tau181, NfL) with MRI, demographics, APOE4, and composite cognitive scores to predict rates of cognitive decline in non-demented individuals using machine learning. Data from ADNI were divided into Cohort 1 (without Aβ42/40) and Cohort 2 (with all three plasma biomarkers). A two-stage framework applied ridge linear regression to MRI data to derive an MRI score, then used random forest regression with all predictors. Four models were compared: basic (demographics, APOE4, baseline cognitive scores), plasma (basic + plasma biomarkers), MRI (basic + MRI), and combined (all). For memory decline (ADNI-MEM), the combined model achieved the highest correlation (0.50), significantly outperforming basic (0.38), plasma (0.45), and MRI (0.46) models. For executive function, language, and visuospatial domains, adding biomarkers did not significantly improve predictions except for language where the combined model improved over basic. Feature importance showed MRI score and baseline cognitive scores were top predictors; among plasma biomarkers, NfL and p-tau181 were important, while Aβ42/40 had low importance. Predicting decline separately in cognitively unimpaired (CU) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) groups was more challenging in CU, with lower correlations. Survival analysis using predicted ADNI-MEM decline rates stratified risk of progression to MCI/dementia in both CU and MCI individuals, with the combined model showing the highest C-index (0.76 CU, 0.79 MCI) and high hazard ratios for the fastest decline tertile. The study concludes that plasma biomarkers, especially combined with MRI and cognitive scores, can predict domain-specific cognitive decline and dementia progression, though predictive power is limited in non-memory domains and early stages. The focus on AD-specific biomarkers may limit generalizability to other dementias.

A method for displaying a marker element in a virtual scene is performed by a terminal. The terminal renders a display interface of the virtual scene containing virtual items. Marker indication information is obtained, indicating a target virtual item marked by a user account for team members to view. Graphic data of a marker element is obtained based on the marker indication information; the marker element indicates the target virtual item's location to team accounts. The marker element is rendered and displayed at a designated location around the target virtual item in the display interface. The marker element may be displayed when the target virtual item is within a visible distance of the current virtual object. Distance information indicating the distance between the target virtual item and the current virtual object may also be obtained and displayed around the marker element. The distance information can include straight-line distance, horizontal distance, or height difference. A thumbnail map may display a marker icon at the target virtual item's location. In a team mode, a first terminal can mark a target virtual item and send a marking request with the item's identifier to a server. The server detects whether the target virtual item is within the visible distance of the current virtual object of the first terminal and/or a second terminal of a teammate. If so, the server transmits marker indication information to the respective terminal(s), which then obtain and render the marker element. The marker indication information may include a target marker type selected by the marking user, and the graphic data is obtained accordingly. Marker elements for different marking users may be distinguished. The marker element may be removed after a preset duration, either by server instruction or by the terminal's timer. Pairs trading is a market-neutral strategy that involves simultaneously buying and selling two highly correlated financial instruments, typically stocks, to profit from temporary mispricing. The price difference between the pair is called the spread; traders aim to short the outperforming stock and buy the underperforming one when the spread diverges, expecting it to converge. The strategy originated at Morgan Stanley in the 1980s and is a subset of statistical arbitrage. Jim Simons’ Medallion Fund uses market-neutral strategies for uncorrelated returns.

Advantages include not needing to predict overall market direction and the potential to profit in up, down, or sideways markets. However, market neutrality does not eliminate risk, as leverage is often used. Disadvantages include pairs wandering apart out-of-sample, sudden spread shifts, shorting costs, slippage and commissions (four transactions per trade), black swan events, and the fact that positions are not truly market-neutral because they involve two different stocks. Correlation can be a poor measure of pair quality; cointegration, which measures the variability of the difference, is often preferred.

The passage discusses special education teacher shortages in the U.S., particularly in high-poverty districts, and the use of emergency certifications. The court denied the defendants' motion for summary judgment. Plaintiff Toy Lykins, an employee subject to a union security clause requiring payment of dues, sued the union alleging that his compulsory payments were being used for purposes other than collective bargaining, contract administration, or grievance adjustment, violating his First Amendment rights. The court found jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1337(a) and later noted that § 1331 also applied after a statutory amendment eliminated the amount-in-controversy requirement. The court held that a justiciable controversy existed because plaintiff alleged his money was being spent for impermissible purposes and he could not identify specific expenditures without an accounting. The court rejected the union's argument that plaintiff failed to exhaust remedies under § 201(c) of the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act, finding that plaintiff had requested an accounting, the provided reports were insufficient, and he had no duty to attend union meetings. The court determined that sufficient governmental action existed because the union shop clause operated under the National Labor Relations Act. To avoid constitutional questions, the court interpreted the NLRA as not authorizing expenditures of dissenting employees' dues for political or ideological causes, relying on Supreme Court decisions in Street, Allen, and Abood. The court did not decide which specific expenditures must be refunded, leaving that for further factual development. The order required plaintiff to amend his complaint to plead jurisdiction, denied summary judgment, set discovery deadlines, and scheduled a pretrial conference. A subsequent order amended the memorandum to reflect the elimination of the amount-in-controversy requirement for federal question jurisdiction but confirmed jurisdiction remained proper.

Recruited by Chris Chelios and Ken Holland, he joined Detroit, won the Stanley Cup, and hopes to repeat. The coach still does a wonderful job and is respected, but it's time to call it quits. He enjoys it more without controversy and with more awareness.

The lecture focuses on implementing linear shift-invariant systems described by linear constant coefficient difference equations using digital networks. Such equations relate delayed output and input sequences, and under the assumption of causality, they can be solved for the current output as a linear combination of past outputs and delayed inputs. Implementation requires three basic operations: delay, multiplication by scalars, and addition.

A block diagram notation represents delay with a box labeled \(z^{-1}\), multiplication with a branch showing a coefficient, and addition with a summer. An alternative signal flow graph notation uses directed branches between nodes; node variables equal the sum of incoming branch outputs. For linear systems, branch outputs are the input multiplied by a gain (scalar or function of \(z\)). A first-order example \(y(n) = a y(n-1) + x(n)\) is shown in both notations.

The flow graph corresponds to a set of linear equations expressible in matrix form: the vector of node variables equals the transpose of a coefficient matrix times that vector plus a source term. By separating branches into non-delay (coefficient) and delay (\(z^{-1}\)) types, the matrix equation decomposes into a set of coupled first-order difference equations. This shows how an \(n\)th-order equation is broken down into first-order equations.

An example illustrates node numbering and computability: a network is computable if nodes can be evaluated sequentially, which requires the coefficient matrix to have no non-zero elements on or above the main diagonal. Non-computable networks contain delay-free loops and cannot be computed in sequence, though the equations remain solvable. The lecture concludes by noting that subsequent lectures will cover common structures for IIR and FIR digital filters.

Ron Washington will not return as Angels manager in 2026 after the team declined his contract option. He missed more than half of the 2025 season following quadruple bypass heart surgery. Interim manager Ray Montgomery also will not get the full-time role. The Angels will search for their sixth manager in nine years. Washington said general manager Perry Minasian told him the decision was based on team performance, not his health. The Angels went 36-38 before Washington left and finished 72-90, their 10th consecutive losing season. Washington was 99-137 in two seasons with the team. He stated he would like to continue managing or join a coaching staff. Albert Pujols and Torii Hunter are considered strong candidates for the managerial position. Washington previously managed the Rangers, leading them to two World Series appearances, and was part of the Braves' 2021 World Series championship coaching staff.

IDC views IT-based simulations, modeling, and data analytics as key enablers for industrial enterprises facing disruptive changes. Virtual processes accelerate product development and manufacturing, supporting analysis of raw materials, supply chains, energy, sustainability and new digital products, services, business models. HPC technologies are becoming prerequisites for modern simulations; public cloud and HPCaaS offer scalability, can replace in-house HPC. Competitiveness hinges on integrating data as a single source of truth across the product lifecycle. Recommendations: virtual product development as part of digital transformation; holistic data strategy with a single common database; evaluate HPC operating models (on-premises, HPCaaS, hybrid) based on utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security, skills; prioritize scalability, security and energy efficiency in HPC solutions; leverage external expertise. Findings based on a December 2021 survey of 200 decision makers in German, Austrian, Swiss industrial enterprises with over 500 employees.

The Ayoub Sisters, young classical musicians, credit their free music education in Scotland for their success. Laura Ayoub emphasizes the value of fully funded lessons and ensembles, and regrets that some children may miss such opportunities. Highland Council, one of 22 local authorities charging for tuition, transferred its service to a charity. Duncan Chisholm argues all children should have free access, calling charges unacceptable. Only Renfrewshire among the ten non-charging councils increased spending, pledging £200,000 to remove cost barriers. Clackmannanshire doubled fees to £524 yearly, and West Lothian is consulting on cuts. Campaigns Save Our Strings and Develop not Dismantle, backed by musicians, aim to protect music education. John Wallace warns council music services could cease, and the EIS reports music teacher numbers fell from 1,100 to 640 in a decade. The Youth Music Initiative guarantees primary tuition up to Primary 6, but Fiona Hyslop says local councils decide on additional charges. Campaigners find this insufficient. Sarah Ayoub states music education benefits all careers.

A new Gallup-Walton Family Foundation poll finds more than 1 in 4 U.S. public school teachers lack basic materials or staffing support, significantly affecting job satisfaction. Two-thirds report shortages of teaching assistants, aides, or paraprofessionals; 62% lack mental health resources or special educators. Job satisfaction is 77% among teachers with adequate resources versus 44% among those without. The survey, conducted in three waves (1,989 teachers in Oct-Nov 2024, 2,046 in Jan 2025, 2,167 in Apr-May 2025), also found that while 72% have equipment to teach effectively, 24% lack classroom furniture, 25% lack laptops/computers, and 35% lack printing supplies. One in three teachers say the ordering process is difficult. Shortages of furniture are similar across income levels (23% in wealthier schools vs. 25% in low-income), but wealthier schools report more paraprofessional shortages (68% vs. 64%). Low-income schools are more likely to lack laptops (34% vs. 18%) and printing resources (43% vs. 28%). About half of teachers say professional development is not grounded in student needs; collaborative planning and observing other teachers are cited as most valuable, yet only 1 in 3 get that opportunity. Special education coordinator Jessica Saum highlighted the impact of paraprofessional shortages. The Walton Family Foundation provides financial support to The 74.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture and fabricated on TSMC's 7nm N7 process, features 108 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), 6912 FP32 CUDA Cores, and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores. It includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache. The new Tensor Cores support TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data types, and introduce fine-grained structured sparsity (2:4 pattern) that can double math throughput. TF32 operations accelerate FP32 data by up to 10x over V100 FP32, while FP16/FP32 mixed-precision delivers 2.5x V100 Tensor Core performance (5x with sparsity). FP64 Tensor Core operations provide 2.5x V100 FP64 throughput. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) allows secure partitioning of a single A100 into up to seven GPU Instances with isolated memory paths. Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth across twelve links. The GPU supports PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, asynchronous copy instructions, asynchronous barriers, and task graph acceleration. A100 delivers significant speedups over V100 for AI training, inference, and HPC workloads.

The Japan Society of Technology Education (JSTE) developed a new framework, “The New Framework of Technology and Engineering Education for Creating a Next Generation Learning” (NGTE), to clarify the role of technology and engineering education in STEAM education in Japan. This was prompted by the global rise of STEM/STEAM education, ITEEA’s STEL, and Japan’s increasing focus on STEAM as transdisciplinary learning integrating STEM and Arts, based on Yakman’s theory. JSTE had previously published “Technology Education in the 21st Century” (1999, 2012), which influenced national curriculum revisions.

A survey of 1,656 junior high students in Japan found positive perceptions of ‘Technology’ classes but revealed insufficient exploratory activities and weak connections between design problem-solving and the development of abilities for technological innovation and governance. In response, NGTE defines the goal of technology and engineering literacy as acquiring these abilities. Its objectives enhance generic competences across three layers: as individual, engaging with others, and life and social development. The scope includes individual technologies (materials and processing, energy conversion, biological cultivation, information) underpinned by engineering sciences, and a new ‘Technological Systems’ content integrating cyber and physical technologies for Society 5.0. The Triple-Loop Model of engineering design process comprises Needs Exploration, Seeds Exploration, and Creation Loops. A STEAM learning model centers on engineering design to create technological artifacts, connecting science, arts, and mathematics.

Evaluation of the draft NGTE showed agreement among JSTE members, though the definition of “engineering” was revised to encompass both engineering science and the engineering design process. The framework aligns with Zuga’s five curriculum categories. The development process involved ascertaining learner status, interpreting it against societal changes, and proposing curriculum revisions, with academic societies expected to influence national curriculum revision through collaboration with MEXT. Future tasks include validating the framework through classroom practice and reforming teacher education.

Elliott Management, holding a 6% stake, stated NXP Semiconductors is worth $135 per share intrinsically, above Qualcomm's $110 offer. Elliott said the offer caps NXP's valuation and took advantage of a depressed stock price. It highlighted NXP's growth in automotive and industrial markets and retained UBS for analysis. Qualcomm rejected a $103 billion Broadcom bid, which Broadcom would pursue regardless of the NXP deal. NXP shares rose nearly 1% premarket.
Following a 2-0 midweek loss at Spurs, United host Huddersfield with Sanchez's debut to strengthen top-four spot as Spurs face Liverpool. Mourinho will update on Fellaini fitness and Pogba issues.

Robert Cyrus Garrison was convicted of first-degree rape and sentenced to 30 years. The only error raised on appeal was the trial court's instruction under 57 O.S.Supp.1969, § 138, which the Court of Criminal Appeals had previously held unconstitutional in Williams v. State. The court found the instruction erroneous but not reversible, and modified the sentence to 15 years, stating that good time credits should not be considered by the jury.

On March 8, 2019, the Committee adopted the Fiscal Year 2020 Variable Compensation Plan, which provides eligible executive officers variable cash payments based on achievement of specified revenue performance goals, with threshold, base operating plan, and stretch levels. Puri $650,000 (68%), Debora Shoquist $250,000 (29%), and Timothy S. Teter $250,000 (29%). The descriptions are qualified by the filed exhibits.

On March 13, 2019, Tesla, Inc. appointed Zachary Kirkhorn as Chief Financial Officer, succeeding Deepak Ahuja. Kirkhorn, 34, had served in Tesla's finance department since 2010, most recently as VP of Finance, Financial Planning and Business Operations. He will receive $12 million in stock options and $4 million in restricted stock units, vesting over four years. Also on that date, Tesla appointed Vaibhav Taneja, 41, as Chief Accounting Officer. Taneja had been Corporate Controller since May 2018, previously held roles at Tesla and SolarCity, and worked at PricewaterhouseCoopers. He will receive $6 million in stock options and $2 million in restricted stock units, vesting over four years.

The Port Hardy Secondary School (PHSS) Seniors Girls soccer team qualified for provincials at the Island Championships. They beat Duncan Christian School 6-1, lost 5-4 to Glenlyon Norfolk, then defeated St. Andrews 3-1 in overtime after a 1-1 tie, securing their first provincial berth. They placed second after losing the final 4-3 to Glenlyon Norfolk, but were the only team to score against them. The team will compete in the BC Single A High School Provincials in Penticton from May 31 to June 3. Players look forward to traveling and tough competition; coach Jim Buchan wants them to represent the school well and leave everything on the field.

In 1843, the British government stated the Sandwich Islands occupation was unauthorized and would be investigated. Indirect causes included American predominance, Anglo-French rivalry, French introduction of a rival religion, and the British consul's aim to break American influence for a sovereignty settlement. Native sentiment favored the U.S., which first acknowledged Hawaiian autonomy via Capt. Jones's unratified but morally binding treaty and showed goodwill. A Hawaiian embassy (William Richards and Timoteo Haalilio) sought recognition of independence. In Washington, they communicated with Mr. Webster on Dec. 14, 1842; he replied on the 19th, recognizing Hawaiian independence, opposing foreign interference, and deeming a formal treaty unnecessary. The President informed Congress on Dec. 30; Mr. Calhoun later confirmed recognition. In London, the ambassadors secured a Nov. 28, 1843 convention between France and Britain, reciprocally agreeing to consider the Sandwich Islands independent and never take possession. The convention did not guarantee autonomy against third powers and lacked the spirit of Webster's declaration.

The speaker accepts the Republican Party's presidential nomination, acknowledging the responsibility to interpret the party platform and voice the faith of its millions of adherents. He affirms belief in party government as opposed to personal or autocratic rule, crediting the constitutional system of representative popular government for American achievement and stability. He warns that a transition from party to personal government has historically preceded the failure of republics.

He commits to restoring representative popular government under the Constitution, criticizing the wartime expansion of executive power and the failure to return to constitutional methods after the emergency. He envisions a cooperative relationship among the executive, cabinet, Vice President, and Congress, with the Senate resuming its deliberative authority.

On international relations, he states that Senate Republicans acted to preserve American independence and nationality against a proposed world super-government. He pledges to hold American nationality unimpaired, not to hold aloof from world responsibilities, but to seek tranquil friendship. He promises a formal peace declaration once a Republican Congress acts. He advocates reduced armaments, an association of nations for peace through justice and international law, and keeping America free from entangling military alliances. He rejects any surrender of rights to a world council or military alliance that could summon American sons to war without a direct call of national honor. He proposes approaching other nations to build a new relationship that commits moral forces to peace while preserving American freedom.

Domestically, he stresses the need for understanding among labor, management, and capital, and calls for maximum production, linking high wages to full efficiency. He warns that underproduction is a crime of omission and that mounting wages without increased production lead to ruin. He advocates a return to normalcy, deflation to restore the dollar's value, and government economy to relieve tax burdens and set an example of thrift. He calls for a nationwide drive against extravagance and a return to simplicity of living.

He addresses transportation, criticizing government operation of railroads for inefficiency and pledging to encourage private rehabilitation, adequate facilities, and highway development. He supports water transportation, American maritime eminence, and free use of the Panama Canal for American shipping.

He pledges renewed concern for agriculture, encouraging cooperative associations for farmers, facilitating marketing, and opposing government neglect or socialistic practices. He supports irrigation, reclamation, and development of Alaska.

He briefly endorses a budget system, a protective tariff, a strong merchant marine, an ample navy, a small but prepared army, expanded trade, immigration standards focused on citizenship, child-labor and women's employment protections, federal action against lynching, housing solutions, honoring Liberty and Victory bonds, tax revision, and guaranteeing rights for Black citizens. He calls for a plain understanding with Mexico regarding border respect and protection of American citizens.

He insists on honest enforcement of all laws, including the Eighteenth Amendment, regardless of personal opinion, while acknowledging the right to seek modification or repeal. He honors the service of World War veterans and pledges to aid the disabled. He supports women's suffrage, expressing confidence in the enfranchisement of women and urging acceptance of the new responsibility. He concludes by pledging fidelity to country and God, and accepts the nomination.

An audit found former Duquesne School District superintendent Barbara McDonnell and four employees misused district funds, authorizing $41,000 in no-interest loans without board approval, with McDonnell taking $22,000. The audit cited undocumented $1.3 million in transportation reimbursements and $180,000 overpayment, and referred the matter to the State Ethics Commission.

Dave “Sully” Sullivan, an IAM special representative, reflected on a five-year campaign that organized Maine lobstermen into Lobster 207, a union local and cooperative formed in 2013. Lobstermen faced depressed prices, global supply chain consolidation, and regulatory pressures, and lacked a coordinated voice. After a lobsterman’s brother suggested meeting the Machinists, Sullivan and organizer Joel Pitcher held open meetings, brought lobstermen to the IAM’s Winpisinger Center for training, and built membership through face-to-face outreach. Lobster 207 achieved political victories, including a law protecting licenses during military service, defeating a dredging project with the Sierra Club, and helping defeat a Right to Work bill. To address economic pressures and antitrust restrictions, they incorporated a statewide marketing co-op, the Maine Lobstering Union (MLU). In 2017, members voted to purchase the wholesale operations of Trenton Bridge Lobster Pound for $4 million, financed by a Bank of Labor loan and line of credit, unsecured loans from other IAM locals, a seller note, and a backup letter of credit from the IAM Grand Lodge. The acquisition gave Lobster 207 an existing wholesale business, which expanded from buying from 30 boats to 130 member boats and marketed “union lobster.” Future plans included statewide purchasing expansion and profit-sharing for members who sold through the MLU. Sullivan prepared to discuss lessons learned for organizing self-employed workers with the IAM international president.

The US beat Panama 4-0 in a World Cup qualifier. Christian Pulisic scored early after a long move, then assisted Jozy Altidore's first goal. Altidore added a penalty and Bobby Wood scored. The win ended a three-match winless streak, moving the US to third place with 12 points, two ahead of Panama. Goal difference improved their chances for an eighth straight World Cup, with a win at Trinidad and Tobago likely securing it. Pulisic, playing centrally, was key, involved in 11 of the US's 14 hex goals.

The passage draws parallels between Declaration of Independence grievances and Trump's actions. It says Trump's authoritarianism disregards rule of law and checks and balances. Trump's deference to generals violates civilian control of the military. The Founders resented the king's obstruction of immigration; the passage states immigration causes economic growth, citing Turkey's Syrian refugees. Trump's attacks on the Mueller investigation, DOJ, and judges undermine judicial independence. Trump blames immigrants for wage stagnation, but economists blame union destruction.

The lecture discusses capabilities as a method for privilege separation. It describes the confused deputy problem, where a Fortran compiler with extra privileges was tricked into overwriting files because it implicitly used all its privileges—an example of ambient authority, where access decisions rely on implicit process attributes like user ID. Capabilities are presented as an alternative: unforgeable references to objects with specific rights, removing ambient authority. Unix file descriptors serve as capabilities, unforgeable because the kernel maps integers to a per-process table.

The Capsicum system uses capabilities for sandboxing. It adds a capability mode (cap_enter) to FreeBSD that disallows global namespace operations (e.g., absolute path opens) and requires operations through file descriptors (e.g., openat). Network access and process management also become capability-based, using pre-opened connections and process descriptors (pdfork). A library provides lch_start to safely initialize a sandbox by clearing memory and explicitly passing capabilities, along with fd lists for naming descriptors. Applications like tcpdump and gzip are sandboxed by entering capability mode before processing untrusted input, with capability masks restricting operations (e.g., write-only, no seek). Limitations include developer reliance, the need for complete system call coverage, and helper services like Casper for operations such as DNS. The UID still matters for directory lookups in capability mode to preserve Unix permissions. Capsicum offers finer-grained control than Linux’s seccomp, which filters system calls rather than object-specific rights.

Warren Buffett is reportedly eyeing a $10 billion deal for the petrochemical unit OxyChem, per WSJ. It could be Berkshire’s largest since its $11.6 billion Alleghany purchase in 2022. Berkshire has $344 billion cash. Buffett, 95, will step down as CEO at end of 2025, succeeded by Greg Abel. Berkshire owns a 28.2% Occidental stake. Buffett previously said he wouldn’t take full control.

The Magic Formula strategy, popularized by Joel Greenblatt, selects stocks by ranking companies based on return on capital (ROIC) and earnings yield (EY). Stocks with the best combined rank (lowest sum of the two ranks) are chosen. ROIC measures how well a company manages its capital; earnings yield is the inverse of the P/E ratio. Implementation involves identifying a stock universe, ranking by these metrics, and selecting top stocks, either passively or actively. Backtests: Greenblatt’s 1988–2004 test on the 3,500 largest US stocks showed the top 30 stocks returned 30.8% annually versus the S&P 500’s 12.4%. A later backtest from 1999–2023 showed returns more than double the S&P 500 but with higher drawdown and underperformance from 2014. Nordic academic studies found positive results. Criticism includes recent lower returns, small-cap bias, and exclusion of transaction costs. The strategy aims to minimize risk by focusing on financially strong companies, but risks include potential underperformance, reliance on historical data, and sector concentration. Performance can be evaluated using total returns, alpha, and volatility.

Roundhill Investments relaunched its meme stock ETF under the ticker MEME on Wednesday. The previous MEME ETF launched in late 2021 and closed two years later, coinciding with a peak in the Nasdaq Composite and a subsequent nearly 10% decline in the Nasdaq and over 96% drop in the broad market. CEO Dave Mazza said meme stocks have grown into a revolution and the actively managed ETF can rotate quickly into stocks dominating the conversation. BTIG’s Jonathan Krinsky noted the relaunch could be a sign of market exuberance. The new ETF’s largest holding, a stock that finished last year below $2, has surged nearly 450% this year; quantum computing stocks are also among top holdings. The ETF fell more than 2% in afternoon trading.

Alpha-N Performance modified a standard M4 Coupe with bespoke engine software to 560 hp, borrowed GTS gearbox software, differential, and stability control settings, added Öhlins coilovers, 20-inch OZ wheels, carbon fiber hood, front bumper, rear wing, and Recaro seats. The car lapped the Nürburgring in 7:20 (bridge to gantry), versus M4 GTS's 7:28. Price undisclosed, likely cheaper than used GTS.

The lecture presents the design of digital IIR low-pass filters using impulse invariance and bilinear transformation, applied to analog Butterworth filters. The analog Butterworth filter is defined by the squared magnitude function 1/(1+(jΩ/jΩ_c)^(2N)), with cutoff frequency Ω_c and order N. Its magnitude is 1/√2 at Ω=Ω_c, monotonic, and drops more sharply for larger N. Poles lie on a circle of radius Ω_c in the s-plane; a stable filter uses left-half-plane poles.

Digital specifications are: passband edge 0.2π with ripple ≤1 dB (magnitude ≥10^(-0.05)), stopband edge 0.3π with attenuation ≥15 dB (magnitude ≤10^(-0.75)). For impulse invariance, analog frequencies are related by Ω=ω/T, initially neglecting aliasing. Solving the two constraint equations yields N=5.8858 and Ω_c T=0.70474. N must be an integer, so N=6 is chosen. To compensate for aliasing, the passband specification is exactly met, giving Ω_c T=0.7032. The parameter T is shown to be irrelevant. The resulting digital filter meets the passband spec and exceeds the stopband spec.

For the bilinear transformation, critical frequencies are pre-warped (with T=1), giving analog passband edge 2 tan(0.1π) and stopband edge 2 tan(0.15π). Solving yields N=5.3..., so N=6 is chosen. The stopband specification is exactly met, resulting in Ω_c=0.76622. The digital filter meets the stopband spec and exceeds the passband spec. Comparing the two designs, the bilinear transformation provides better attenuation at higher frequencies due to frequency warping. The lecture notes that these procedures extend to other filter types via frequency transformations.

The document consists of a note from Chichkine to Chargé d’Affaires Wurts, a certification by Secretary of State John Hay (Sept. 1, 1900) that annexed documents are true copies, and a deposition of Capt. George O. Baker. Baker, 58, of Dartmouth, master mariner, went to sea in 1848, became master in 1863, made about 15 voyages, last six years in Ochotsk and Japan seas. He states the Ochotsk whaling season is mid-August to mid-October, when rugged northerly/easterly gales make whaling useless. Best whaling: Sept. 1–20. He sailed in the Cape Horn Pigeon 8 years under agent William Potter, 2d. Fair average catch: 6–10 whales. If at Vladivostok on Oct. 1 with rugged weather, he would not return but sail directly to San Francisco. 9 whales yield ~10,000 lbs bone and 900 barrels oil. Species: right whales.

Walmart workers can earn a degree for $1 a day; Walmart covers remaining tuition, fees, books. All US employees eligible after 90 days. Degrees: associate's or bachelor's in business or supply chain management, from University of Florida, Brandman, or Bellevue. Guild Education provides coaching and credit for paid trainings. 1.4M eligible, 68,000 expected in 5 years. No penalty for leaving/failing. Follows wage hike, increases pressure on competitors.

Defensive ends are the most prioritized position on a defense, valued for their rare combination of size, strength, and athleticism to disrupt opposing passing attacks. They line up on the end of formations, on the edge of the offensive line. Their role includes stopping the run and pressuring the quarterback through sacks, batting down passes, hurrying throws, or hitting the quarterback. Required skills are strength, quickness, recognition, and consistent technique. The typical body type is 6’3–6’7, 270–290 pounds, with a lengthy, big, athletic build. Elite defensive ends allow defenses to pressure without blitzing and defend the run with lighter boxes. Notable players include Reggie White (second all-time in sacks with 198), Bruce Smith (all-time sack leader with 13 seasons of 10+ sacks), and Dwight Freeney (known for speed and quickness). The abbreviation is DE.

Thokozani Khupe, newly elected leader of an MDC breakaway faction at an extraordinary congress, accused male political rivals of cowardice for criticizing her formation's elected leaders. Spokesperson Witness Dube said Khupe is unfazed by men uneasy with women's gender mainstreaming, and the party has 50-50 gender representation in its standing committee. The election of Linda Masarira as national spokesperson angered some members who considered her an outsider, but Khupe defended Masarira's credentials and constitutional eligibility. Khupe cut ties with Nelson Chamisa, accusing him of hijacking the party after Morgan Tsvangirai's death. Chamisa sought a court interdict to stop Khupe from using the MDC trademark; judgment was reserved. The Zimbabwe Electoral Commission requires name/symbol disputes to be resolved before nomination day.

Utah County hired Kathryn N. Nester, a former federal public defender, to represent Tyler James Robinson in the fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk. Robinson may face the death penalty. The defense contract is expected to cost $750,000; prosecution, $600,000. A commissioner said taxpayers will pay.

Sierra Linarducci's father invested $10,000 in bitcoin when it was $4,000 per coin. Its value quadrupled, now covering her entire wedding. The family uses a BitPay card for vendors. Bitcoin recently reached $16,000, but it is volatile; it dropped 20% after hitting $11,000. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said those who buy bitcoin will "pay the price." Personal finance experts compare bitcoins to trading cards, advising investing only what one can lose. Certified financial planner Ian Weinberg called it a gamble. However, investor Salil Pitroda believes bitcoin may become a store of value like gold, and blockchain technology offers benefits. The bride feels fortunate about the timing.

The team rebounded from two poor road losses with home wins from depth lines, and now has improved legs and puck movement, playing like their successful playoff road form. They aim to create more chances while staying defensively smart, using speed and puck skills, buoyed by early road confidence.

The passage describes the preparation of materials on fisheries, natural resources, population distribution, commerce, military geography, and colonial relations, to be presented graphically. It notes the assembly of material on strategic frontiers in Europe (due February 15), a general outline of international law, and economic surveys covering nations' strengths and weaknesses, trade barriers, financial and industrial data, and goods distribution (due end of January/February 15). A study of Russo-German commercial relations is planned to prevent economic penetration of Russia. Specialists are investigating other subjects with reports due January to mid-February. Material will be edited into brief, readable form with briefs for the peace conference, avoiding bulk. Costs cover only necessary expenses. A memorandum of December 22, 1917, discusses the Allied military situation and the Berlin-Bagdad project. It lists Allied opportunities (Russian invasion of Alicia, protection of Serbia, etc.) and results: the Russian army is non-offensive, Germany occupies non-Russian territories, Rumania, Serbia, and Montenegro are occupied, and Austro-German forces are deep in Italy. Invasion of Austria-Hungary is impossible. The Allies hold Saloniki but cannot use it offensively; if held, it blocks a branch of the Berlin-Bagdad project. The capture of Bagdad controls Mesopotamia and blocks the line to the Persian Gulf (threat to India). The capture of Palestine nullifies the Suez Canal threat. The separation of Arabia removes the Red Sea threat. Germany has lost the project's terminals; if Saloniki, Jerusalem, Bagdad, and Arabia remain in non-German hands, defense possibilities exist.

Britons average 16,000 relatives; North West 20,000; South East, South West, East Anglia fewer. Adults know 1% of family. Seven million used home-testing kits. Most thought they had six cousins. Released for DNA Day.

The TLV321x devices feature a Power-On Reset (POR) circuit that holds the output low for up to 32µs after the supply voltage crosses 1.65V, after which the output reflects the differential input. The basic comparator outputs logic low when VIN < VREF and logic high when VIN > VREF, with a propagation delay measured from the input midpoint. Overdrive voltage (VOD), the input voltage beyond VREF, affects propagation delay; smaller overdrive (especially <100mV) increases delay. Rise and fall times are measured between 20% and 80% of the output waveform. To prevent chatter when the input slowly crosses the threshold, external hysteresis can be added. The devices have 1.8mV internal hysteresis; external hysteresis uses positive feedback. Hysteresis is characterized by threshold voltage (VTH), offset voltage (VOS), and hysteresis window (VHYST). An inverting comparator with hysteresis requires a three-resistor network referenced to VCC, with equations for trip voltages and total hysteresis. A non-inverting comparator with hysteresis uses a two-resistor network and a reference voltage (VREF), with equations for the rising and falling thresholds. A low-side current sensing application uses an amplifier and comparator to alert when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1V. Design recommendations include using a 0.1µF low-ESR ceramic bypass capacitor directly at the supply pins to prevent ringing, ensuring a stable power supply, treating output edges as high-speed logic, placing the bypass capacitor close to the supply pin with a solid ground plane, avoiding parallel output and input traces, adding series resistance at inputs close to the device, and optionally adding a <100Ω series output resistor for damping. Controlled impedance traces with back-terminations are suggested for long distances. The document also provides information on documentation updates, support resources, trademarks, ESD caution, revision history, and mechanical/packaging/orderable details.

This document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. It defines the GHCB as a 4KB shared memory area used to exchange register state during Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs). The GHCB MSR protocol enables version negotiation, feature advertisement, and requests (e.g., CPUID, page state change, AP reset hold, GHCB registration) before the GHCB page is established. Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature support via a bitmap, adds SEV-SNP support, and includes enhancements like XSS MSR handling and restricted injection. The specification details required NAE events, their associated GHCB state, and error handling. It also covers the SEV-SNP secrets page guest reserved area, the EFI Confidential Computing Blob configuration table, page state change operations, AP creation, multi-VMPL support, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and termination requests. Revisions document additions such as 64-bit message sequence numbers, new error codes, and clarifications for interrupt injection and AP booting.

Lasik treatment is a common, pain-free eye surgery that permanently corrects vision, eliminating the need for glasses or contact lenses. Results are immediate, with no bandages or stitches, and most activities can be resumed within 24 hours after consulting a surgeon. It reduces long-term expenses by avoiding frequent eye check-ups, glasses updates, and replacement costs for lost lenses or glasses.

On August 21, a total solar eclipse called the "Great American Eclipse" will cross the U.S. from Oregon to South Carolina. The moon will block the sun for nearly 1.5 hours, creating umbral (total) and penumbral (partial) shadows. It is the first coast-to-coast total solar eclipse in 99 years. Cities in the path include Salem, Kansas City, Nashville, St. Louis, and Charleston. Enthusiasts are booking hotels.

The passage outlines diplomatic actions during World War I, including: the sinking of the Argentine ship Toro and the Luxburg affair; visits by the American fleet to South American ports; cooperation with Brazil in patrolling the South Atlantic; revocations of neutrality and severances of relations with Germany by various Latin American nations (Brazil, Costa Rica, Peru, Uruguay, Ecuador, and others); declarations of war on Germany and Austria-Hungary by Brazil, Panama, Cuba, and others; disposition of seized German ships; a proposed Latin-American congress; a wheat purchase convention. The District Court of Appeal of Florida denied W.K. Neuman's petition for a writ of certiorari, finding no departure from the essential requirements of law in the circuit court's denial of his challenge to the Board of Adjustment's refusal to grant a variance for a fence/wall at his residence.

The Zipper offense, originating from the 1960s Celtics, is a basketball offense found in nearly every NBA playbook. It is unique for using a down screen on the ball side. The offense begins with a dribble clear entry to a wing, as shooters break high off down screens set by the posts. The point guard then has options to drive, pass to the shooter, or feed the screener posting up. It creates opportunities for shooters, point dribble penetration, and post ups, while enabling quick ball reversal and weakside attack. Phases cover point isolation, down screen execution, post isolation, ball reversal, and offensive rebounding, with specific reads and counters for defensive responses. Variations include Curl, Blocks, Back, and sideline out-of-bounds plays. The Zipper can flow into continuities such as motion, flex, triangle post, and side screen actions. Proper execution requires coordination among ballhandler, screener, and receiver, and it emphasizes offensive rebounding with two weakside rebounders. The offense is commonly defended, so preparation against it is advised.

Researchers developed MeTro, a highly elastic surgical glue made from a natural protein. It seals wounds in 60 seconds when treated with UV light and contains a degrading enzyme adjustable to healing time. MeTro works on tissues that expand and contract, like lungs, arteries, and heart, and has been tested on rodent and pig lungs. It can be squirted directly onto wounds. Next steps involve clinical testing.

The President addresses Congress, citing Lincoln's "Let us have faith that right makes might" as the nation's essential faith, which should guide domestic and foreign policy and won the war. He defines democracy as the individual's right to just treatment, says it faces a final test as the Old World embraces autocracy, and asserts the US manifest destiny to lead. The US can assist by exemplifying just laws that balance labor rights and property, and by defending weak nations. Refusing this role would dishonor the founders.

He urges Congress to remedy domestic injustices to counter global chaos, as the US is the sample democracy. Postwar recovery is slow abroad but promising at home; serviceable legislation is needed. He recommends a budget system with a single appropriations committee in each house cooperating with the Departments and Treasury. He vetoed a prior budget bill on constitutional grounds; the House revised it, and he now urges passage.

Financially, ordinary receipts for fiscal 1920 were $6,694,000,000 (up $1,542,000,000 from 1919), net ordinary expenditures fell from $18,514,000,000 to $6,403,000,000, and gross public debt declined from $26,596,000,000 (August 1919) to $24,175,000,000 (November 1920). Bank holdings of war securities decreased, freeing credit for agriculture, industry, and commerce, due to debt reduction and better distribution of securities. The Treasury has withdrawn from the credit market. However, $7.5 billion in war debt matures in two and a half years ($2.5 billion floating, $5 billion Victory Notes and War Savings Certificates). Sound policy requires reduced spending, maintained tax receipts, and retiring the floating debt and part of the Victory Loan before maturity. He stresses rigid economy, avoiding indefinite appropriations, and notes over a billion dollars in extra expenditures authorized last Congress. Transportation Act payments to railroads (over $600 million paid, $650 million estimated) have limited floating debt retirement.

He calls for immediate tax revision, especially simplifying income and profits taxes to reduce taxpayer burden and clarify liability. He urges ample provision for medical care, vocational training, and placement of sick and disabled veterans, referencing proposals from the Treasury and the Board for Vocational Education.

He reiterates needs: encouraging dyestuffs and related chemicals; promoting agricultural production, marketing, and rural life; a cold storage law limiting storage time, requiring disposal methods, and mandating date marking on released goods; marking the entry price on interstate cold storage shipments; and stating the producer's price on packing cases for interstate commerce. He also recalls a recommendation for federal licensing of interstate corporations.

The immediate legislative need is removing obstacles to the people's ambitions and strengthening justice through law or mediation. He suggests a loan to Armenia like wartime Allied loans, supervised by a US commission or commissioner to deter revolutionary tendencies. He notes the Philippines have maintained stable government, fulfilling the condition for independence, and urges granting independence as promised. He concludes that his message is a confession of faith, the faith of America and the future.

Memorandum from Leo Pasvolsky to President Roosevelt about upcoming talks with British Colonial Secretary Colonel Stanley (visiting Jan 15-18). Stanley's visit focuses on the Anglo-American Caribbean Commission, but informal discussions on dependent territories may occur. The U.S. seeks only exploratory talks. Six topics are outlined with British and U.S. positions: 1) Trust territories vs. colonies: British assimilate them; U.S. wants distinction and international trusteeship. 2) Goal: British favor self-government within empire; U.S. favors independence with option to remain. 3) Accountability: British accept limited accountability tied to control; U.S. wants universal accountability. 4) Declaration of Standards: British oppose; U.S. favors. 5) Regional Advisory Commissions: British favor advisory commissions; U.S. favors principle but undecided on participation. 6) Relation to General International Organization: British view unknown; U.S. view not yet decided. A background memo is attached.

Bruce Bochy will not return as manager of the Texas Rangers after a three-year stint that included the franchise's first World Series title in 2023, followed by two seasons without a playoff berth or winning record.
