Peace must be founded on an equality of rights among nations, without distinction between big and small, powerful and weak. Right must rest on common, not individual, strength. Equality of territory or resources is impossible, but an equality of rights is expected; mankind seeks freedom of life, not balances of power. A deeper principle is that governments derive their just powers from the consent of the governed, and no right exists to transfer peoples between sovereignties as property. For example, there should be a united, independent, autonomous Poland, and security guaranteed to peoples under hostile governments. Any peace not accepting this principle will be upset, as populations will rebel and the world will sympathize. Stability requires tranquility, justice, freedom, and right. Every developing people should be assured a direct outlet to the sea, if necessary through neutralized rights of way. The seas must be free in law and fact; freedom of the seas is indispensable for peace, equality, and cooperation. This may require radical reconsideration of international rules. Free, unthreatened intercourse is essential. Defining and securing this freedom is not difficult if governments sincerely agree. The issue is connected to limiting naval armaments and cooperating navies, which opens the wider question of limiting armies and military preparation. These questions must be faced with candour and accommodation; peace requires concession and sacrifice. Preponderating armaments cannot continue. Statesmen must plan for peace as they planned for war. The speaker, as a responsible head of government, speaks without reserve, confident of reflecting the people’s wishes and hoping to voice the silent masses suffering death and ruin.

Seasonality in trading refers to regular price patterns at specific times. Silver exhibits seasonality, with January and July being the best months (positive 69.5% and 63.6% of the time) and June and September the worst (31.8% and 54.4% positive). The seasonal trading strategy involves going long silver from December to February and July to August, holding for 5 months total. Backtested since 2001, it returns an extra 3.9% per year over buy and hold, with a risk-adjusted return of 26.93% versus 7.33%, and reduces maximum drawdown from -71.65% to -23.34%. The seasonality may be due to industrial users placing orders at the start of the year.

The device operates with an internal or external voltage reference, selected by the INTREF_DIS bit. The internal reference has a nominal 4.096V output and requires a minimum 4.7µF decoupling capacitor on the REFIO pin. Its initial accuracy can be degraded by thermal stress, such as soldering. For an external reference, apply 4.096V to the REFIO pin and place a minimum 10µF capacitance between REFCAP and REFGND.

The device features an active-high alarm output for input and AVDD alarms. The input alarm compares the ADC input against user-programmable high and low thresholds with a common hysteresis setting. The AVDD alarm has fixed thresholds of 4.7V (low) and 5.3V (high). Each alarm has an active flag and a tripped flag.

The device uses a multiSPI digital interface and supports three functional states: RESET, ACQ, and CONV. A data transfer frame begins on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends on the rising edge. The device supports various data transfer protocols, including legacy SPI-compatible modes and source-synchronous modes, with options for single or dual SDO-x output. Multiple devices can be connected in a daisy-chain topology.

The device has nine configuration registers. Input commands for register write operations must be 32 bits long. The output data word can include appended flags such as device address, input range, alarm flags, and parity bits.

The present disclosure describes video encoding and decoding methods enabling a single bitstream to be used by both standard dynamic range (SDR) and high dynamic range (HDR) systems. An encoder receives an HDR master and a reference SDR master of the same video. In one embodiment, the encoder finds a color volume transform that converts HDR values into SDR values such that, when those SDR values are processed by emulated target SDR display operations, they substantially match the reference SDR values. The encoder then encodes the SDR values into a bitstream and generates metadata identifying the transform. An SDR system decodes and displays the SDR values directly, while an HDR system decodes the SDR values and uses the metadata to perform an inverse color volume transform to reconstruct HDR values for display. In another embodiment, the encoder encodes HDR values into the bitstream and provides metadata indicating how an SDR system can convert decoded HDR values into SDR values that match the reference SDR master. The color volume transform can be found by varying candidate transforms, converting HDR values, emulating SDR display operations, and selecting the transform that minimizes the difference between the resulting presentation SDR values and the reference SDR master. The transform may be represented as parameters of a parametric function, a scaling factor, a 3D lookup table, or three 1D lookup tables. The scaling factor can be derived from the relationship between SDR and HDR luma components, and when a power function transfer function is used, the scaling factor can be computed as (Y_S / Y_H)^(1/γ), allowing direct scaling of chroma components. Metadata items communicate the transform or inverse transform to decoders.

A model, Ella Ravenscroft, used sunbeds once or twice a week for two years, spending about 12 minutes under UV lights. After her mother noticed two moles on her stomach had grown, she sought medical advice and had them surgically removed, later having two more removed. She was left with scars but realized the danger of skin cancer. She now warns against sunbed use and uses fake tan instead. Studies show sunbed use increases melanoma risk by 16 to 20 percent. Nearly 500 people are diagnosed with melanoma annually in Greater Manchester, and around a fifth die. Most moles are benign, but changes in colour, shape or texture can be an early sign of melanoma. People are advised to monitor their skin for any unusual changes, such as a mole that changes size, shape or colour, itches, bleeds, or a sore that does not heal, and to consult a doctor promptly.

This study analyzed CSF-tDNA using CAPP-Seq in 24 advanced lung cancer patients with suspected leptomeningeal disease (LMD). Across 81 CSF, blood, and tissue samples, CSF-tDNA variant allele fractions (VAFs) were significantly higher than plasma ctDNA VAFs (median 32.7% vs 1.8%, P<0.0001), with a positive correlation between compartments (Spearman’s ρ=0.45, P=0.03). For LMD diagnosis, CSF-tDNA sensitivity was 91.7%, compared to 81.8% for cytology and 80.0% for MRI; 4 of 9 cytology-negative samples had detectable CSF-tDNA. Detectable CSF-tDNA was associated with worse overall survival (HR=7.1, P=0.02). In patients progressing on targeted therapy, resistance mutations were common in plasma but rare in time-matched CSF, indicating spatial heterogeneity. In a prospective osimertinib cohort (N=12), post-treatment CSF-tDNA VAF was prognostic for CNS progression (HR=6.2, P=0.009). The findings suggest CSF-tDNA detection may improve LMD diagnosis, prognostication, and inform compartment-specific therapeutic strategies.

Hexane is a hydrocarbon solvent (n-hexane) made from crude oil, a gasoline constituent. It has pure (lab) and solvent-based (industrial) types. Solvent-based hexane extracts vegetable oils, but is costly and toxic; an alternative uses sodium hydroxide and methanol, though high moisture is a drawback. Serum S-IgG, NC-IgG, and pseudovirus neutralization against Wu01, BA.4/5, and BQ.1.1 were measured. S-IgG was detected in 95.6% of participants; 94.4% reported at least one vaccination, 45.7% reported prior infection, and 67.7% were vaccinated per German recommendations. S-IgG levels increased with the number of S-antigen contacts and were lower with drug immunosuppression. NC-IgG was detected in 24.0% of participants and was the strongest predictor of S-IgG levels in multivariable regression, followed by number of vaccinations, time since infection, time since vaccination, drug immunosuppression, and number of infections. Neutralizing activity was detectable in 94.4% against Wu01, 84.9% against BA.4/5, and 73.8% against BQ.1.1. Geometric mean ID50s were 1,440, 243, and 55, respectively, representing a 23.6-fold reduction against BQ.1.1 compared to Wu01 and a 4.2-fold reduction compared to BA.4/5. S-IgG levels were the most predictive factor for neutralization against all variants. For BQ.1.1, 59.6% of individuals with S-IgG <1000 BAU/ml lacked detectable neutralization. Bayesian network analyses identified direct predictors including S-IgG, NC-IgG, number of infections, and age. The study concludes that high S-IgG seroprevalence coexists with moderate vaccination compliance and that BQ.1.1 exhibits substantial immune escape, underscoring the need for improved vaccine uptake to mitigate COVID-19 risk.

Intraday trading involves buying and selling a financial instrument (stocks, futures, or forex) within the same trading day. In the US stock market, pattern day trading rules set by FINRA designate a pattern day trader as someone executing four or more day trades within five business days, provided those trades represent over six percent of total trades in the margin account. Such traders must maintain a minimum equity of $25,000 in their margin account and are limited to a maximum of 4x leverage. Trading with less capital and higher leverage may be possible via stock CFDs outside the US, as CFD trading is prohibited in the US.

Success requires a backtested trading plan with a statistical edge. Recommended intraday trading rules include: educating oneself about the market, setting realistic goals, avoiding herd mentality, choosing a reputable broker regulated by a tier-1 authority (considering fees and compensation schemes), trading only very liquid stocks (often large-cap), studying company fundamentals and forthcoming news, using a quantified and automated trading system to remove emotions, and periodically reviewing trading results in sample sizes.

Intraday traders primarily use technical analysis strategies and indicators such as moving averages, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and RSI, though the passage notes it may be naive to expect these indicators to work on intraday strategies. Most intraday traders lose money; profitability is possible only with a quantified, backtested edge. Backtesting intraday strategies is challenging and time-consuming compared to daily data strategies, and intraday strategies are less likely to pass out-of-sample backtests due to noise between the open and close.

Bulk SrTiO3 undergoes an antiferrodistortive transition at ~105 K to a non-polar tetragonal phase. Further cooling leads to a quantum paraelectric regime where long-range ferroelectric order is suppressed by quantum fluctuations. Using four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy with a cryogenic stage down to ~20 K, polarization is mapped via asymmetry in Kikuchi band intensities. Below the antiferrodistortive transition, local polar nanodomains emerge, with a characteristic size of ~20 nm and periodic spatial ordering at a ~25 nm length scale. Upon cooling below ~40 K into the quantum paraelectric regime, these nanodomains fragment into smaller (~14 nm), more disordered clusters, and the periodic ordering is lost. Temperature-dependent measurements show that polar nanodomains nucleate around the antiferrodistortive transition, grow and self-organize down to ~69 K, then reverse trend with increasing fragmentation and loss of periodic correlations at lower temperatures, resembling a re-entrant disordering. Quantum paraelectricity in SrTiO3 is thus characterized by the evolution of polar nanodomains through a re-entrant transition, rather than a complete absence of polarization. These polar textures may underlie anomalous low-temperature properties and could be relevant to superconductivity in doped SrTiO3.

Nonfarm payrolls fell by 33,000 in September due to hurricanes, though average wages rose. Walgreens and CVS shares each dropped 4.9% after a report that Amazon may sell prescription drugs. Costco fell 6% on lower gross margins. A North Korea missile test report added to worries. For the week, major indexes rose over 1%.

Fior Markets published a report on the global Cooking Oil market covering 2017 to 2022. It includes industry trends, segmentation, growth, market share, revenue, leading players, and regional analysis for the USA, Europe, Japan, China, India, and Southeast Asia. The report addresses market drivers, restraints, opportunities, forecasts, and profiles, using primary and secondary research and expert input. It also covers supply chain, trade, and strategies.

PIMS staff protested for a fifth day, demanding separation from SZABMU. Protesters forced the VC out of his office and sealed it. Senior consultants joined. The VC offered to resign but emphasized patient care for 20,000 daily visitors and visited Parliament. CADD and Law ministers met movement representatives; the Law Minister directed the bill be tabled for PM approval, with all stakeholder reservations resolved after Finance Ministry observations were rectified. The PM agreed in principle to separation, and the CADD minister urged ending the strike. Protesters, citing past broken promises, voted to continue. JI and CDA representatives expressed solidarity.

This mapping review evaluated fieldwork education literature from the last 30 years against the AOTA Occupational Therapy Education Research Agenda – Revised (2018), levels of education, and levels of fieldwork. Of 1,619 articles screened, 67 met inclusion criteria. Results showed a disproportionate focus on Level II fieldwork for occupational therapy students, with 36 of 67 papers addressing this area. The literature predominantly addressed only two categories of the Education Research Agenda: Instructional methods (23 papers) and Learner characteristics and competencies (31 papers). Significant gaps were identified, including a lack of research on OTA fieldwork, Level I fieldwork, and the agenda categories of Theory building, Signature pedagogies, and Promotion of diversity, inclusion, and equity. The authors note the need for a collaborative effort to address these underrepresented areas.

The speaker notes the team is accustomed to loud arenas and starting series on the road, but the media attention is unusual compared to Anaheim. Coach Babcock emphasizes sticking around and making things difficult. The team has had many one-goal games and persevered, but the last game lacked that, and they intend to be more greasy. They failed to challenge the opponent's defense, making it easy, and need more shots on Brodeur. The team is patient, level-headed, and sticks to its plan despite adversity. They were too passive and hesitant, expecting harder skating and work. Frustrated, they acknowledge the opponent's strong system and know they haven't shown their best. The solution is simple: play harder, skate, and work better next game.

Archaeologists discovered a 4,400-year-old tomb near Cairo's pyramids. It likely belonged to Hetpet, a high-ranking woman official from the 5th Dynasty. Wall paintings show her observing hunting and fishing, and a monkey reaping fruit and another dancing before an orchestra. Mission leader Mostafa Al-Waziri believes she had another tomb in Giza's western necropolis, and excavation is underway.

Dinbych, previously unbeaten, faced a well-drilled Wrexham. Wrexham earned a losing bonus point. Dinbych had more territory and possession but were frustrated by Wrexham's defence. Wrexham scored first through James Price's converted try. Dinbych replied with Tom Seddon's try converted by Dan O'Sullivan. James Weston's unconverted try put Wrexham ahead again, but an O'Sullivan penalty left it 12-10 at half-time. In the second half, Aidyn Jones scored an unconverted try to give Dinbych the lead, then Owain Davies crossed for a converted try. Jack Ratcliff's converted try brought Wrexham close, but Dinbych retained possession to win. Dinbych 2nds gained a losing bonus point at Flint.

Peruvian police are evaluating expulsion of U.S. citizen John Dougherty and Canadian Jennifer Moore for inciting protests against Hudbay Minerals' Constancia mine. The interior ministry says they entered as tourists but incited townspeople, disrupting public order. Hudbay suspended operations in November amid protests. No comment from foreigners or Canadian embassy.

Turkey's education administration is unitary and centralized, with policies determined centrally and decisions applied top-down. Appointments often consider political views over competencies. Fundamental components like accountability, transparency, democracy, participation, efficiency, and flexibility are generally not taken into consideration. The study notes that PISA exam reports and GDP averages show Turkey falling far behind the OECD average.

The study aims to introduce a contemporary education administration model as an alternative. It uses a mixed-method, exploratory sequential design, collecting qualitative data from literature and OECD reports, and quantitative data via a questionnaire from teachers and administrators in Seyhan district. The research examines education administration models in 16 OECD countries where PISA and GDP averages are above OECD averages, finding they commonly use local education boards based on good governance principles.

Survey findings indicate that a majority of participating teachers and administrators prefer local administration over central administration. Most want education managed through elected boards/commissions rather than directorates. They favor boards that include diverse stakeholders such as teachers, principals, parents, students, education supervisors, union representatives, and local government representatives. A majority also believe many duties should be handed over from the central government to local education units.

The study concludes that managing educational institutions with Local Education Boards will solve structural problems and proposes a Local Education Boards model, encompassing various councils and commissions, as an alternative to the current directorate-based system.

The lecture recaps the derivation of the collective Thomson scattering spectrum, where scattered power depends on the spectral density function S(k,ω), which contains frequency-resolved information via electron density fluctuations. Using a test particle formalism, S(k,ω) is expressed in terms of electron and ion components, with susceptibilities χ_e and χ_i that scale with α² (α = 1/kλ_De). For a Maxwellian distribution, the susceptibilities involve the plasma dispersion function w(ξ), where ξ = ω/(k v_Tj).

Taking the limit α² → 0 (scattering wavelength smaller than Debye length) makes χ_e and χ_i vanish, recovering the incoherent spectrum proportional to the electron distribution function with no plasma response. For arbitrary α, high-frequency modes (ξ_i ≫ 1, ξ_e ≫ 1) yield electron plasma wave resonances at ω² = ω_pe² + 3(T_e/m_e)k², with peak positions sensitive to density and temperature, and broadening related to Landau damping.

Low-frequency modes (ξ_e ≪ 1) are examined. When zT_e/T_i < 3, ion acoustic waves are damped and do not appear; the spectrum resembles the ion distribution function. When zT_e/T_i ≫ 1, ion acoustic resonances appear at ω² = k² [α²/(1+α²)] (zT_e/m_i + 3T_i/m_i), damped by electrons. The total cross-section (Salpeter approximation) shows that for α ≪ 1 the electron feature dominates, while for α ≫ 1 the ion feature dominates, affecting which feature is experimentally accessible.

Electron-ion drift (relative drift velocity V_d) shifts the electron distribution, causing asymmetric damping of ion acoustic peaks; the asymmetry can be fitted to extract V_d·k and thus local current density J·k. Ion acoustic spectra can yield electron temperature, ion temperature, ion flow velocity, and drift velocity, but not electron density directly (which requires electron plasma waves). Collisions damp coherent features and modify the spectrum. Finite collection volume and time can cause spatial averaging of temperature or velocity gradients, broadening peaks and leading to misinterpretation of temperature. Finite collection angle mixes different k-vectors, smearing spectra. Mitigation often requires smaller collection volumes or lenses, which reduce signal and necessitate more powerful lasers, though laser power is limited by budget and plasma instabilities.
A federal judge declined to delay an order allowing transgender enlistment from January 1, 2018. The Pentagon prepares to comply; the White House says DOJ reviews legal options.

NVIDIA RTX IO uses Microsoft’s DirectStorage API to enable GPU-based lossless decompression, keeping data compressed from NVMe SSDs to the GPU, reducing CPU load and improving I/O performance by a factor of two. It leverages Turing and Ampere GPU compute, DMA, and copy engines for decompression beyond Gen4 SSD limits, offloading dozens of CPU cores.

The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU, based on GA10x Ampere architecture, delivers up to 2X FP32 throughput, 2X ray-tracing throughput, and 5X (10X with sparsity) AI training throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000. It has 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, PCIe Gen4, three DisplayPort outputs, and supports vGPU and Quadro Sync. It is compatible with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere architecture supports 8K60 and 4K120 displays via DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, and HDMI 2.1 with DSC 1.2a or 4:2:0. The fifth-generation NVDEC decoder supports hardware-accelerated decoding of MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, with AV1 providing 50-55% bitrate savings over H.264. GA10x GPUs are the first with AV1 hardware decode, enabling 8K60 HDR playback with low CPU usage. The seventh-generation NVENC encoder provides hardware encoding quality exceeding x264 Fast and on par with x264 Medium, supporting up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC encoding.

GA10x Ampere architecture provides up to 2X performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection performance and support ray-traced motion blur and concurrent ray tracing with shading or compute. Third-generation Tensor Cores implement structural sparsity for doubled effective throughput. GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling achieves up to 19.5 Gbps data rates, yielding 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth on GeForce RTX 3090.

GeForce RTX 3090 features GA102 GPU, 82 SMs, 10496 CUDA Cores, 24GB GDDR6X, and is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX. GeForce RTX 3070 uses GA104 GPU, delivers performance faster than RTX 2080 Ti, and uses GDDR6. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X detects transmission errors and replays them, causing performance plateauing when overclocking limits are reached.

NVIDIA RTX A6000 includes GA102 GPU with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-gen RT Cores, 336 third-gen Tensor Cores, 48GB GDDR6, and supports NVLink for 96GB combined memory. It offers hardware-accelerated motion blur and AI denoising, with performance improvements over RTX 6000 in SPECviewperf, rendering, HPC, and deep learning workloads.

A bug in Atlassian software like Jira and Confluence exposes private AWS server keys through a vulnerable proxy, enabling SSRF attacks to steal secret access codes. NIST rated it 6.1 severity; fixes exist. Security researcher Robert Wiggins found over a dozen major companies running outdated, exposed deployments. After being contacted, EE, Insider, Easy Metrics, a US HHS agency, IEEE, Ronin, and A&E Networks fixed or shut down their servers. At least three unnamed companies remain vulnerable. Updating Atlassian software is advised.

Singapore Airlines will restart non-stop flights between Singapore and Newark in fall, reclaiming the world’s longest flight title. The route, last flown in 2013, begins October 12, covering approximately 9,000 nautical miles (9,537 statute miles), surpassing Qatar Airways’ Doha-Auckland route. Flight time is 18 hours 45 minutes Singapore-bound and 18 hours 25 minutes return. The airline will use the new ultra-long-range Airbus A350-900ULR, configured with 161 seats: 67 business class and 94 premium economy, with no standard coach. Initially three weekly flights (Tuesday, Friday, Sunday) will increase to daily after a second aircraft enters service. Singapore Airlines has 21 A350-900s and 46 on order, including seven ULR variants, with first delivery in September. Newark becomes the fifth U.S. airport served, joining Los Angeles, New York JFK, Houston, and San Francisco. The airline also plans to deploy A350-900ULRs on Los Angeles-Singapore non-stop flights later.

NVIDIA Corporation reported quarterly revenue of $1,305 million and net income of $246 million for the three months ended October 25, 2015. For the nine months ended October 25, 2015, revenue was $3,609 million and net income was $406 million. Total assets were $7,174 million as of October 25, 2015. The company recorded restructuring and other charges of $8 million and $97 million for the three and nine months ended, respectively, related to the wind-down of its Icera modem operations.

England qualified for the 2018 World Cup but performed poorly in a 1-0 win over Slovenia. Manager Gareth Southgate’s cautious 4-2-3-1 formation, featuring a defensive lineup with Eric Dier and Jordan Henderson, stifled attacking players like Harry Kane, Marcus Rashford, and Raheem Sterling. Dele Alli, suspended for that match, is England’s only viable No. 10; Sterling belongs on the wing. Upcoming friendlies against Brazil and Germany offer a chance to adopt a more adventurous approach with three centre-backs, pushed-up wing-backs (Danny Rose and Kyle Walker), and Henderson and Dier as protection, unleashing Alli, Rashford, and Kane. Without tactical change, England risk another early tournament exit.

In the Court of Claims, Berenice M. Brubaker (later substituted by Ralph Hartwell Brubaker) sought damages for the appropriation of real property for the St. Lawrence River project. Claimant originally owned approximately 365 acres near Massena, bisected by Middle Road. About 183 acres north of Middle Road were zoned agricultural; the land south was zoned industrial and burdened by two easements.

Four appropriations occurred:
1. May 19, 1955: all land north of Middle Road (Parcels 148 and 185) was taken.
2. June 12, 1956: a permanent flooding easement of 0.15 acres (Parcel 2202) within an existing drainage easement.
3. April 1, 1957: 25.34 acres in fee (Parcel 2159) with a limited reservation for farm use and access, separating a 57-acre portion.
4. May 1, 1957: an easement for transmission lines over 55.38 acres (Parcel 2169), reserving use only if it did not interfere with the Power Authority.

Claimant’s experts valued the whole property before takings at $331,200–$368,275, including enhancement from the project. The State’s experts gave lower values, excluding project-caused increases. Applying United States v. Miller, the court held that for the first taking, there was no proof the land north of Middle Road was probably within the project’s original scope, so any enhancement from the project could not be considered. The court found the highest and best use was industrial despite agricultural zoning, and awarded $32,000 with specified interest.

For the later appropriations south of Middle Road, the court determined the land was adjacent and not originally within the project, so enhancement by proximity was compensable. Awards were: $100 for the flooding easement; $39,750 for Parcel 2159 (including $12,675 direct damage and $27,075 consequential damage to the separated western portion); and $27,700 for Parcel 2169, as the easement destroyed the market value of the remaining interest. No consequential damage was found for the remaining property from the last two takings. The court viewed the premises and noted the claim had not been assigned.

This passage is the front matter of an ebook edition of a 1902 Foreign Relations of the United States volume concerning whaling and sealing claims against Russia. It describes the ebook's features (portability, full-text search, offline access) and citation guidance. The contents list a translation of a memorandum to arbitrator T. M. C. Asser regarding the seizure of four American vessels. Two letters follow: Secretary of State John Hay forwards to Senator Lodge a dispatch from Herbert H. D. Peirce transmitting the translation; Peirce requests that the translation be printed as a public document. The passage concludes with the opening of the memorandum presenting the U.S. claims for indemnity.

A display device includes a substrate, a pixel electrode, an opposing electrode, an encapsulation portion on the opposing electrode, and a planarization layer on the encapsulation portion. The encapsulation portion includes at least one organic layer and at least one inorganic layer alternately deposited. The planarization layer includes a portion covering an edge portion of the encapsulation portion. A first angle between an edge side surface of the planarization layer and the substrate surface is larger than a second angle between an edge side surface of the encapsulation portion and the substrate surface. The planarization layer may include an organic material. The organic layer in the encapsulation portion is covered by the inorganic layer. The first angle may be equal to or more than about 70 degrees. An upper surface of the planarization layer may be entirely flat. The display device may further include a pattern on the planarization layer, such as a touch electrode or touch wiring. The substrate includes a display area and a peripheral area, and the pattern may include a portion in the peripheral area. The edge portion of the encapsulation portion has an upper surface with a gradually decreasing height. The edge side surface of the planarization layer may be substantially curved or substantially flat. The planarization layer may expose a portion of the encapsulation portion. The planarization layer maximizes the flattened area, allowing pattern formation with reduced dead space and reduced parasitic capacitance between the opposing electrode and the pattern.

Spotify, Comcast, and Oracle recently announced co-CEO structures. About 1.2% of Russell 3000 companies use this model, a figure that has remained steady. Research indicates dual-CEO firms posted a 9.5% average annual shareholder return from 1996 to 2020, outperforming single-leader companies' 6.9% gain. However, the approach poses challenges such as unclear responsibilities and potential power struggles. Experts emphasize that clear role definitions and alignment are critical. Examples include Netflix, which has long-term co-CEOs, and Chipotle, which reverted to a single CEO. At Comcast, Mike Cavanagh joins Brian Roberts as co-CEO, with succession planning noted as a possible motive. Observers caution that when a new co-CEO works alongside an incumbent, an imbalance of power can persist, and founders like Larry Ellison at Oracle may still be seen as the ultimate authority.

Texas public school administrators, parents and education experts worry that a new law replacing the STAAR test with three exams per year could increase student stress and testing time. The law aims to ease pressure by replacing the single STAAR with shorter beginning, middle and end-of-year tests and banning practice tests. However, some fear three tests will triple pressure. The law requires the Texas Education Agency to study reducing the weight of testing on school accountability ratings, but the report isn't due until 2029-30 and implementation isn't required. The new system launches in 2027-28; schools can choose from TEA-approved assessments for the first two tests, while TEA creates the third. Scores will be released within two days. Experts say the system will likely resemble the current one and codify existing district practices. Accountability ratings, which are high-stakes and can lead to sanctions, will continue to heavily depend on the end-of-year test. Critics argue the ratings ignore extracurriculars and other student success measures. HB 8 instructs TEA to track pre-K, extracurriculars and workforce training but not factor them into ratings. There are concerns that all three tests may follow STAAR's strict lockdown protocols, causing student illness and anxiety. Florida's shift to three tests resulted in increased testing minutes. Some educators worry the ban on practice tests removes a tool that reduced anxiety and want teacher input in creating the new exam. Districts using MAP tests, which are adaptive and less stressful, hope the menu includes such assessments. Parents and superintendents emphasize that a relaxed testing environment is key to reducing stress.

In this work, microscale four-point probe measurements inside a scanning electron microscope are used to directly measure the electrical resistivity of grain interiors and individual Si and Mg2Si precipitates in overaged Al-Mg-Si alloys with varying compositions and heat treatments. The grain interior resistivity, which includes the Al solid solution and nanoscale precipitates, is found to depend on the heat treatment rather than the alloy composition; samples with different compositions subjected to the same heat treatment exhibit similar grain interior resistivity. Measurements across individual micron-scale precipitates show that Si and Mg2Si precipitates contribute equally to the effective resistivity, and the precipitate identity has negligible effect. The bulk resistivity is described by a linear relation with total solute (Mg+Si) content, where the slope and intercept depend on the heat treatment condition. Thus, the alloy resistivity is quantified by the precipitate volume fraction and annealing condition, with contributions from vacancies, dislocations, and grain boundaries considered negligible due to low densities.

Bitcoin rose to a six-week high on Tuesday, up 4.4% to $9,340.88, amid positive headlines about major financial institutions entering the cryptocurrency space. The total crypto market cap reached $427 billion, the largest since early March. Goldman Sachs hired a head of digital asset markets, and Barclays explored a trading desk. A Thomson Reuters survey showed one in five financial institutions considering trading crypto within 12 months. Trading volume hit $28 billion, the highest since February 10. However, regulatory challenges persist.

The UCLA offense creates easy layups and problems via high post rubs and down screens if not defended. Two defensive strategies are presented. Basic NBA Show & Recover: against the high post rub, the cutter is forced behind the screen; the screener's defender shows and recovers, while weakside defenders pack in. On down screens, a show-and-recover is used. All Out SOS Disruption: the defense traps the wing on the first pass, exploiting the point guard's low-post cut to hinder ball reversal. After a trap, rotations follow the near player concept, and final match-ups apply SOS principles with specific helpside positions. Switching is disfavored because it leads to a mismatch.

DWI arrests in Wichita Falls are down, with only 5 over St. Patrick’s Day weekend. Year-to-date arrests dropped from 39 in 2016 to 25 this year. Sgt. Harold McClure credits increased awareness and ridesharing. Uber and Lyft arrived last summer; 4 of top 10 St. Patrick’s Day destinations were bars. A student called ridesharing a safer, cheaper option. McClure also noted police presence encourages smart decisions.

This study presents a bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) in STEM education research from 2020 to 2024, using citation analysis of 35 journal articles retrieved from the Dimensions database with the keywords “ai” AND “stem education.” Publication trends show a significant increase in 2024, with 15 articles receiving 234 citations (average 15.62 citations per article), while earlier years had no cited publications. The United States led with 9 documents and 103 citations, followed by China (5 documents, 0 citations). The most cited authors were Nesra Yannier, Kenneth R. Koedinger, and Scott E. Hudson, each with one article cited 55 times. The most cited journal was the International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education (55 citations). The top-cited article was “Active Learning is About More Than Hands-On: A Mixed-Reality AI System to Support STEM Education” (55 citations). Carnegie Mellon University was the most cited institution (55 citations). The analysis highlights AI’s opportunities in personalized learning, advanced analytics, and instructional automation, while noting challenges such as ethical concerns, the need for AI literacy, and student engagement issues. The study provides an overview of key trends, influential works, and leading contributors in the field.

A majority of Supreme Court justices appeared willing to reverse lower court rulings that Rep. Michael Bost lacked standing to challenge an Illinois law allowing mail-in ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted up to 14 days later. Former Solicitor General Paul Clement proposed broad candidate standing, but Justice Kagan suggested a test requiring candidates to show the law puts them at an electoral disadvantage relative to the old rule, without needing to prove likely loss. Kagan's view gained traction, while Justices Sotomayor and Jackson argued Bost lacked standing because his safe seat made loss inconceivable. Clement argued Bost met Kagan's test due to imperiled margin of victory and added monitoring costs. Illinois Solicitor General Notz initially agreed with Kagan's test but later clarified that diminished margin alone is insufficient; standing requires impact on election outcome or reputational injury from an extreme law. Justice Kavanaugh raised concerns about remedy, and government counsel warned that denying pre-election standing would force post-election litigation and that an outcome-determinative test would favor major parties. The passage also lists other Supreme Court cases on restitution, undelivered mail, double jeopardy, attorney-client discussions, conversion therapy, and malpractice actions.

Benjamin Franklin’s prevention advice applies to natural disasters. While tornadoes, hurricanes, and earthquakes cannot be prevented, improved preparations and infrastructure can protect lives and health. Hurricanes Maria, Harvey, and Irma revealed lasting health hazards: Maria caused a humanitarian crisis in Puerto Rico with no power and limited resources; Houston floodwaters contained bacteria, E. coli, lead, and arsenic; industrial and hazardous waste sites released toxic chemicals; mold infested waterlogged homes and schools; floodwaters bred mosquitoes, raising West Nile and Zika risks; unstable structures, downed power lines, and lack of air conditioning led to eleven nursing home deaths; mental stress and economic damage persisted. The impact could have been reduced with prevention. America needs innovative solutions before, during, and after disasters. Authorities should elevate preparedness, educate the public, harden infrastructure, secure hazardous sites, strengthen seawalls, trim trees, and make electrical grids storm resistant. Florida utilities used concrete poles and water gauges, but Irma still cut power to half of customers, taking ten days to restore.

The Trump administration proposes a $100,000 fee for new H-1B visas, threatening thousands of college jobs. U.S. colleges and universities employed over 16,000 H-1B workers as of June 30, 2025. The administration argues the program is abused to avoid hiring Americans; employers say it is necessary. Universities use it for academic staff, researchers, and doctors. Nearly half of the 16,797 approved visas at colleges were at 50 institutions. The proposal does not affect current holders, and it is unclear if universities must pay the fee for new applications. Universities are exempt from the annual cap. Hanan Saab of the AAU says the directive allows exemptions for national interest hires, which she believes includes higher education. If the fee applies, experts say colleges will struggle to afford it. The National Postdoc Association warns the fee would create an enormous barrier and benefit competitors.

Y-Cross is a drop-back pass concept from the Air Raid offense, run from various formations with play action. It is a weak-side flood for deep and intermediate passes, using a post, crossing route (by TE or slot receiver), and running back flat to the boundary, with backside tags like smash. It excels against man coverage and Cover 4, but is less effective versus Cover 3 due to the post safety. Coaching points: Against man, TE releases inside Sam and over Mike to 18-22 yards; fullback flares; tailback check-down off Will, staying on move on out cut; X post over free safety; Z 15-yard speed cut dig, staying on move. Against zone, tailback sits down and Z finds open voids with tempo. Quarterback progression: post, deep crosser, then check-down or backside dig. Against two-high, read free safety: if he plays downhill, throw post; if he honors post, high-low Will linebacker, throwing crosser if Will lacks depth or checking down if he sinks. Variations include reading post-wheel first, using a slot receiver, or adding a curl-flat tag to the field, which requires a strong-armed quarterback.

Two Democratic candidates in targeted Southern California GOP House districts won state party endorsements at the convention. Dave Min secured the nod to challenge Rep. Mimi Walters after a floor fight, while Hans Keirstead was endorsed to unseat Rep. Dana Rohrabacher despite united opposition. No candidate for governor or U.S. Senate reached the required 60 percent threshold. In three other targeted Republican districts, preferred candidates also fell short. The endorsements allow candidates to be listed as party-endorsed on sample ballots. Min’s opponents gathered signatures to force a voice vote, but the endorsement was ratified. Keirstead’s opponents attempted a floor vote but missed the signature submission deadline. Party delegates favored Kevin de Leon over Sen. Dianne Feinstein, though she leads in public polls. In the governor’s race, Lt. Gov. Gavin Newsom led with 37 percent, but no endorsement was made.

Investing.com features headlines on AMD’s surge after an AI chip deal with OpenAI, a bubble scenario for the S&P 500 to 9,000 in 2026, and gold rallying above $3,900/oz. The site notes seasonal weakness and institutional rebalancing are adding market pressure, with diminished liquidity, thin volume, tax loss selling, and fading earnings momentum. Technical analysis discusses yields topping, potential further drops, TLT’s bullish divergence, and a weaker dollar as bullish for commodities. It promotes ProPicks AI strategies, stating 3 of 4 global portfolios beat benchmarks year-to-date. Risk disclosures caution about high trading risks and that data may not be real-time or accurate.

The passage is a comprehensive guide on EUR/USD trading. It states that EUR/USD is the most traded currency pair, highly liquid, and influenced by interest rates, economic data, and central bank policies. A specific trading strategy is provided with rules: backtested on Yahoo Finance data, holding one day, resulting in 713 trades and a 53% gain per trade. The article emphasizes backtesting as the best approach. It covers fundamental analysis (interest rates, inflation), technical analysis (moving averages, indicators), and market sentiment. Optimal trading times are during the European/US session overlap (12:00–15:00 GMT). Various trading styles are discussed: position trading (long-term, based on macroeconomics), day trading and scalping (short-term, difficult, 90% fail), swing trading (days to weeks, using indicators). CFDs and forex pairs are mentioned, with leverage amplifying gains and losses. Choosing a regulated broker with platforms like MetaTrader 4/5 is advised. Demo accounts are recommended for practice before live trading. Risk management includes stop-loss orders, position sizing (risking 1–5% per trade), and diversification. Common mistakes include lack of a backtested plan, excessive leverage, inadequate risk management, and not using a demo account. The article notes that EUR/USD is not easy to trade, most traders lose money, and the authors do not trade it themselves.

Fifty-two farmers, mostly minority Uzbeks, were kidnapped from three villages in Darz Ab district, Jowzjan, while working. Police blame the Taliban, who control the area. Elders and police are negotiating; if talks fail, an operation will follow. The Taliban spokesman could not confirm the incident. The motive is unclear. Police say no Islamic State presence, only Taliban.

A Tennessee woman's video of her son Keaton recounting bullying at middle school prompted support from athletes and entertainers. Keaton said he was called ugly, had milk poured on him, and ham put down his clothes. The video got over 18 million views, and a fundraiser raised over $29,000. Supporters included Delanie Walker, Kelsea Ballerini, Dale Earnhardt Jr., and Snoop Dogg.

This study compared prodromal health conditions and drug prescriptions before diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) using the THIN primary care database (20,214 AD, 28,222 PD, 4,682 DLB, 20,214 controls) and replicated selected findings in the UK Biobank. All three diseases showed higher frequencies of memory problems, tremor, confusion, hallucinations, sleep disorders, constipation, anxiety, depression, falls, hypotension, urinary disorders, and weight loss compared to controls in the 0–5 years before diagnosis. Autonomic dysfunction (constipation, urinary disorders, hypotension) was more strongly associated with PD and DLB than AD. Memory problems were more frequent in AD, tremor in PD, and hallucinations, confusion, falls, and depression in DLB. Drug prescriptions revealed lower use of antihypertensives (agents acting on renin–angiotensin system, calcium channel blockers, diuretics) and antidiabetics before all three diseases. Statin prescriptions were lower before PD compared to AD and DLB; this difference persisted after adjusting for confounders and in UK Biobank replication. In PD patients, those who developed dementia within five years after diagnosis had higher pre-diagnosis use of statins, laxatives, antidepressants, and antipsychotics. The findings highlight long prodromal phases with disease-specific and shared features, and suggest differential associations with lipid-lowering therapies.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended June 30, 2015. The company designs, manufactures, and sells electric vehicles, powertrain components, and energy storage products. Total revenues for the three months ended June 30, 2015 were $955.0 million, up from $769.3 million in the prior-year period, driven by increased Model S deliveries. Net loss was $184.2 million, compared to a net loss of $61.9 million a year earlier. Gross margin declined to 22.3% from 27.7%, primarily due to product and regional mix shifts, manufacturing costs related to dual-motor production, and lower ZEV credit revenue, partially offset by higher lease-related revenue. Research and development expenses rose to $181.7 million, and selling, general and administrative expenses increased to $201.8 million, reflecting expansion of retail, service, and Supercharger infrastructure and Model X development.

Cash and cash equivalents totaled $1.15 billion at quarter-end. Operating cash flow was negative $291.3 million for the six months ended June 30, 2015, compared to positive $57.1 million in the prior year, due to higher inventory and operating expenses. A review of 18 Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR) countries' Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) from 2016–2021 assessed reporting comprehensiveness on health-related Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) targets and indicators. All VNRs indicated established monitoring mechanisms; 11 reported on all 17 SDGs, with comprehensiveness associated with higher country income. Seventeen VNRs noted prioritized and adapted targets, but only eight explicitly mentioned 2030 country targets. Nine VNRs reported on data availability, and limited data availability was a common challenge, often described in terms of human resource capacity, low data quality, lack of statistical tools, limited transparency, and lack of disaggregation.

Reporting on specific health-related indicators varied by type and income level. High-income countries reported the highest proportion of mortality and morbidity indicators (60%), while low- and middle-income countries reported the lowest for means of implementation. Middle-income countries reported more risk factor and determinant indicators than high-income countries. The most commonly reported indicators were maternal mortality ratio (100%), neonatal mortality rate (83%), under-5 mortality rate (78%), access to improved drinking water (78%), new HIV infections (72%), and total unemployment rate (72%). Trend data were less common; only Qatar reported trends across all SDG3 indicators. Data routinely reported to WHO were often not included in VNRs. Reporting was higher for indicators derived from disease surveillance and civil registration and vital statistics systems than from routine health information systems or national surveys.

The findings confirm commitment to SDG monitoring but highlight weak national health information systems, limited data availability, and analytical capacity as challenges. Strengthening regulatory frameworks, data collection capacities, civil registration and vital statistics systems, and population-based surveys are key to improving access to quality data for achieving health-related SDGs.

European scientists are launching International Coccolithophore Day on October 10 to highlight microscopic plankton called coccolithophores. These single-celled algae, smaller than dust, capture carbon, produce oxygen, and build calcium carbonate plates that sink to the seafloor, forming chalk and limestone layers that record Earth’s climate history. They generate over 1.5 billion tonnes of calcium carbonate annually, storing atmospheric carbon dioxide in deep-sea sediments. The initiative is led by the Ruđer Bošković Institute, the Lyell Centre at Heriot-Watt University, NORCE, MARE at the University of Lisbon, and the International Nannoplankton Association. Research includes studying how coccolithophores pull CO2 from the air and how warmer, more acidic oceans may alter this process; tracking their life cycles, viruses, and grazers to understand carbon movement; examining bacterial interactions that influence seawater chemistry; tracing how aerosol-driven fertilization shapes their distribution; and using fossil plates to date rocks and reconstruct ancient oceans. Climate change threatens their survival by altering seawater temperature, chemistry, and nutrients. The campaign aims to raise awareness that these tiny organisms play a vital role in carbon regulation, oxygen production, and marine ecosystem health, and to inspire ocean literacy, policy focus, and public engagement.

The device requires an integrated high-bandwidth, low-noise, stable amplifier buffer to drive the ADC input. It operates with an internal or external voltage reference using an internal buffer, selected via the INTREF_DIS bit. The internal reference provides a nominal 4.096V output; when used, the REFIO pin is an output requiring a minimum 4.7µF decoupling capacitor to REFGND. Smaller capacitors increase noise and degrade SNR/SINAD. The internal reference is factory-trimmed but its accuracy can shift due to mechanical or thermal stress, particularly from soldering. Multiple reflows cause additional shifts; soldering the device in the second pass minimizes stress. The internal reference is temperature compensated. For external reference mode, apply 4.096V to REFIO as an input, and the internal buffer drives the REFCAP pin, which requires a 10µF minimum capacitance to REFGND and a 1µF capacitor close to the pin for high-frequency decoupling. The buffer output has a typical temperature drift of 0.5ppm/°C (max 2ppm/°C).

The ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar and unipolar ranges, outputting straight-binary format. The device features an active-high alarm output with two alarm types: input alarm and AVDD alarm. The input alarm compares the ADC input against user-programmable high and low thresholds with hysteresis. The AVDD alarm uses fixed thresholds of 4.7V (low) and 5.3V (high). Both alarms have active and tripped flags; active flags clear at conversion end if the condition is gone, while tripped flags clear only after reading the ALARM_REG register. Alarm flags can be read via the ALARM pin, internal registers, or appended to the output data.

The device has three functional states: RESET, ACQ, and CONV. RESET is entered by pulling RST low, with two reset types (application or power-on reset). ACQ state acquires the input signal, and CONV state starts on the rising edge of CONVST/CS, using an internal clock. The device ignores further CONVST/CS transitions until conversion completes. A NAP low-power mode is available in ACQ state.

The multiSPI digital interface uses a data transfer frame starting at the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ending at the rising edge. A frame requires 32 SCLK cycles for a valid write; shorter frames are invalid for writes but valid for reads, and longer frames use the last 32 bits as the command. Input commands include NOP, register read/write operations. The output data word contains the conversion result, with optional appended flags for device address, input range, alarms, and parity. Data transfer protocols for writing are SPI-00-S (default), SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, or SPI-11-S, selected via SDI_MODE bits. For reading, options include legacy SPI with single or dual SDO-x, and source-synchronous (SRC) protocols where the RVS pin provides a data-synchronous clock. The clock source can be external or internal. Dual SDO mode uses two data lines to halve the required SCLK cycles. Multiple devices can be daisy-chained by connecting SDO-0 of one to SDI of the next, with shared CONVST/CS and SCLK, requiring 32×N SCLK cycles per frame.

The device has nine configuration registers for device ID, reset/power control, SDI/SDO control, data output control, range selection, and alarm thresholds/hysteresis. An application example shows an 8-channel analog input module using the ADS8681W with a differential multiplexer, achieving fast settling (5µs to 1% accuracy) and supporting various industrial voltage/current ranges. The alarm function with hysteresis can be used for temperature sensing with an NTC thermistor to prevent false triggers. Power supplies AVDD and DVDD require decoupling capacitors; PSRR improves with proper decoupling. Low-power modes include NAP and power-down, with specified wake-up times. PCB layout recommendations include separating analog and digital sections, placing bypass capacitors close to pins, and using appropriate decoupling on REFCAP and REFIO.

The 5-Day Low of The Range Strategy goes long at the close when IBS is below 0.25 and the close is below the lowest low of the previous 5 days, exiting after 5 days. From January 1993 to today, it produced 309 winners in 517 trades, an average return of 0.46% per trade, a 60% win ratio, and larger average winners than losers. Profitability peaks at 3-7 days, with a 10.76% annualized return over 510 market days versus 2826 days for buy and hold. The average 5-day period return was 0.11%. Recently, performance has lagged. A short-selling adaptation using a 0.75 or 0.9 criterion on today's range yielded almost 10%, though short strategies are less profitable. In another period, 102 trades resulted in 68 winners and a 0.98% average return per fill.

The passage discusses gold and gold trading strategies. Gold is a precious metal used for jewelry, ornaments, exchange, and store of value, known since 3400 BCE. Gold trading involves speculating on gold prices via futures, options, spot markets, stocks, CFDs, and ETFs; most trades are cash settled without physical delivery. Prices fluctuate due to supply/demand and political, social, and economic unrest. Gold is also used as a hedge and considered a safe haven asset, as its price is minimally influenced by political choices, interest rates, and inflation, and can negatively correlate with stocks and bonds. Historically, gold became a medium of exchange around 1500 BC in Egypt, later used as coins across the Mediterranean. The Bretton Woods agreement in 1946 set gold at $35/oz and made the USD gold-backed, but the system was abandoned when gold supply was insufficient for paper money, leading to floating exchange rates. Gold futures trading began on COMEX in 1974, and online trading emerged in the 1980s. Gold trading strategies are difficult due to dependence on macro news. A weekend swing trading strategy backtested on GLD ETF from late 2004 to September 2021: buying at Thursday's close and selling at Friday's close yielded an average gain of 0.14% and a profit factor of 1.4. Buying Thursday's close and selling Monday's open gave 0.19% per trade with a profit factor of 1.3, not considered very tradeable. Adding one simple parameter improved results to an acceptable level for a small position. The strategy shows promise, and better entries/exits might be achieved during daytime. FAQs note gold trading uses various instruments, most trades cash settled, and gold acts as a hedge.

Princeton scientists and international collaborators developed an AI tool called Diag2Diag that fills in missing plasma data with synthetic, highly detailed information. It uses sensor input to predict readings that other diagnostics cannot capture, especially in the crucial plasma edge (pedestal) region where stability determines performance. By reducing reliance on bulky hardware, Diag2Diag promises to make future fusion reactors more compact, affordable, and reliable. The AI enhances plasma monitoring and control, helping future commercial fusion systems operate continuously. The research, published in Nature Communications, used sensor data from the DIII-D National Fusion Facility. Diag2Diag can boost diagnostics like Thomson scattering, which measures electron temperature and density but cannot capture fast-evolving instabilities or edge plasma details. The synthetic data aligns with real-world data and is more detailed than actual sensors provide. The tool also supports the magnetic island theory for suppressing edge-localized modes (ELMs): it generated evidence of simultaneous temperature and density flattening in the pedestal region when resonant magnetic perturbations are applied. This understanding is crucial for commercial fusion reactor development. Diag2Diag could have broader applications in spacecraft, robotic surgery, and other fields where diagnostic data is missing or limited. The research team included Azarakhsh Jalalvand, Egemen Kolemen, SangKyeun Kim, Qiming Hu, and others from Princeton University, PPPL, Chung-Ang University, Columbia University, and Seoul National University.
In State v. Nelson, the Washington Court of Appeals reversed and remanded.

If so, it sends a first section to the first device and a second section to the second device. Each device provides audible commands for completing its section’s remaining inspection items, receives audible updates on completion, and sends those updates to the site computer. The site computer forwards the updates to the host computer. The inspection assistance devices include a headset and a portable computer device. The system may also include an inspection plan editor for creating or modifying inspection plans.

The professor introduces a "decision mentality" for analyzing poker, emphasizing expected results over actual outcomes. Using a credit card roulette story, he illustrates that Emily should thank Matt, who intended to pay for her, rather than Steven, who actually paid, because over time randomness averages to expected value. He stresses that good decisions can yield bad results and vice versa, so players should analyze decisions without outcome bias.

Three levels of poker reasoning are presented. Level one is "my hand versus your hand," exemplified by a player putting an opponent on a specific hand like pocket kings, which is mathematically unfounded. Level two is "my hand versus your range of hands" (exploitative play), where one builds a probability distribution of an opponent's possible hands and makes the most positive expected value decision. An example calculates equity against a tight opponent's range, leading to a fold. Level three is "my range versus your range" (optimal play), where one considers their own range from the opponent's perspective and calls with a frequency that makes the opponent indifferent to bluffing, preventing exploitation. Optimal play is compared to a Nash equilibrium; it profits from opponents' strictly suboptimal deviations, while exploitative play involves mind games.

The "Who's Taller?" game demonstrates that without forced bets, no one would play, illustrating why blinds are necessary to motivate action. Stack size is measured in big blinds, and effective stack size considers the smallest stack among remaining players. Position, defined relative to the button, matters because later positions face fewer opponents to steal blinds. Equity is the fraction of the pot a hand expects to win, calculated over unknown cards or opponent hand distributions, with tools like PokerStove recommended.

The professor advises always raising (not calling) when first to enter a pot, to give oneself a chance to win the blinds uncontested. A raise size of 2.25 big blinds is suggested for tournaments. With effective stacks of 12 big blinds or fewer (with antes) or 10 big blinds (without antes), going all-in is recommended instead of raising. Beginners often err by not raising and by being too scared to go all-in. Position-based opening hand ranges are provided, starting very tight from early position (e.g., under the gun: premium pairs, ace-king) and widening significantly in later positions (up to 55% of hands on the button). Suited and connected cards gain value in later positions. Opening from the small blind is compared to the button, noting the disadvantage of being out of position post-flop. The ranges are conservative to help beginners avoid difficult post-flop situations. A final test hand demonstrates all-in decisions and equity calculations using Nash ranges and PokerStove, showing that king-queen suited has sufficient equity to call against two all-in opponents.

The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted limitations of central-laboratory RT-PCR testing, including long turnaround times, reliance on nasopharyngeal swabs (NPS) that caused patient discomfort and sampling inconsistencies, and challenges for certain patient groups. Early point-of-care (POC) RT-PCR platforms still required NPS eluate transfer, introducing cross-contamination risks and biohazard exposure, and were difficult for non-laboratory trained staff. Saliva emerged as a reliable, non-invasive sample type that could be self-collected, avoiding NPS drawbacks. The MicroGEM Sal6830™ SARS-CoV-2 Saliva Test, the first saliva-based RT-PCR POC test with emergency use authorization, uses patient self-deposited saliva directly into a sealed cartridge, minimizing sample handling and capturing intact virions. A study assessed whether non-laboratory trained healthcare workers could use Sal6830™ accurately and confidently. Blinded sample testing at 1.9× limit of detection showed concordant results (one invalid). In a clinical comparison with the Cepheid Xpert Xpress CoV-2/Flu/RSV test, positive percent agreement was 87.2%, negative percent agreement 97.2%, and overall agreement 93.3%. A usability questionnaire indicated the system was easy to use, well integrated, and inspired confidence, with no technical support needed. The study concluded that Sal6830™ can be operated accurately and easily by non-laboratory trained healthcare workers in POC settings.

Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017, with 155 mph winds, torrential rains, and floods, destroying the electricity grid, infrastructure, and causing over $82 billion in damages and $780 million in agricultural losses. Indirect deaths are important in emergencies, but mortality counts are hindered by inconsistent cause-of-death determinations. Previous excess death studies for Maria had limitations, such as a short timeframe, few causes, and ignoring population displacement. This research proposes a semiparametric Poisson regression model to estimate emergency-related deaths, incorporating intra-annual variability, population displacement, and causes including non-communicable diseases, while capturing the duration of mortality effects by cause. The model uses pre- and post-emergency period indicators, cause-of-death indicators, their interactions, a smooth function of day-of-year, and year trends. Coefficients are estimated via penalized likelihood maximization with REML. Excess deaths are computed as the difference between model predictions with and without the emergency period, using a population size unadjusted for displacement to avoid double-counting.

The passage examines whether judges are good historians, prompted by the Supreme Court's two-step test in New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass’n v. Bruen for Second Amendment challenges. Step one asks if the plain text covers the conduct; if so, step two requires the government to show the regulation is consistent with historical tradition. Critics like Justice Breyer and Judge Reeves argue this burdens judges with impractical historical work, as courts are staffed by lawyers, not historians, and judges sift evidence differently. The author contends the question is wrong: judges are lawyers who decide cases, not historians. Adjudication always involves historical questions—what happened and what the law was—so history is part of a lawyer's toolkit. Originalists acknowledge that looking further back increases uncertainty, but they argue the judge's role minimizes the problem. Legal evidence is durable, and the law provides tools like burden-shifting to resolve uncertainty. In Bruen, step one (defining "people," "keep," "bear," "arms") is straightforward and largely settled by precedent. Step two involves identifying historical traditions; the Court has recognized traditions like prohibiting dangerous weapons. While some historical work is needed at the margins, many cases will be easy, and genuine traditions are evidenced by durable sources like statutes and treatises. Moreover, efforts to compile historical evidence have increased. When historical records are silent, historians can say so, but judges must decide cases. The law's burden-shifting framework—claimant shows plain text coverage, then government proves historical tradition—illustrates how lawyers confront uncertainty. The passage rejects supplementing history with means-ends scrutiny, as that would cast judges as legislators, a role the Court rejected. It concludes that the past is not a foreign country but integral to law; understanding it is essential for complete legal knowledge.

When a soccer player is injured and the referee does not stop play, players may kick the ball out of bounds as an act of sportsmanship, an unwritten rule. If no immediate goal threat exists, either team can do this. After the injury is attended, the referee restarts with a throw-in for the team that did not kick the ball out. Sportsmanship is shown by throwing the ball back to the other team, typically backward to a defender. Neither team should take advantage; the receiving team must wait for the thrower to return to position, and the ball should not be challenged until the defender has clear possession. A similar courtesy applies when the referee stops play for an injury: the dropped ball is passed backward to the opponent, who must then send it backward before resuming an attack.

Ovarian cancer claims more lives than all other gynaecological cancers combined. In the UK, thousands of women are diagnosed only after reaching emergency care, and just one in three cases is identified at the earliest stages. Jo Stanford of Ovarian Cancer Action says late diagnosis stems from difficulties getting timely appointments and being dismissed by healthcare providers. She notes 90% of women are unaware of the four main symptoms, and one in four mistakenly believe a smear test detects ovarian cancer. There is no screening test; a CA-125 blood test is not used for routine screening but can be discussed with a doctor if symptoms are dismissed.

The four main symptoms are persistent bloating, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, urinary urgency or frequency, and persistent pelvic or abdominal pain. Other signs include persistent lower back aches, ongoing digestive discomfort/bloating/nausea, unexpected postmenopausal bleeding, and unusual tiredness. Stanford advises that while these symptoms likely do not indicate cancer, women should trust their sense of normal and seek help if something feels off.

Ovarian Cancer Action provides a free online symptom checker and a downloadable symptoms diary to help women identify patterns and present evidence to doctors, reducing dismissal. Research shows many women prioritize others’ health; two-thirds would act immediately on a breast lump, but fewer than one in four would on ovarian cancer symptoms. Early detection gives a 95% survival rate versus 16% at stage four, yet less than a third of cases are diagnosed at stage 1 or 2. Stanford rejects the term “silent killer,” noting over 87% of stage one patients had symptoms, and awareness can improve survival. Everyone should know the signs to encourage loved ones. Ovarian cancer is the sixth most common cancer in UK women, more common than cervical cancer.
