Hendrik Bessembinder's 2017 study examined whether stocks outperform Treasury Bills. It found that most stocks fail to beat one-month Treasury Bills over their lifetime. Between 1926 and 2015, only 43% of equities had returns higher than Treasury Bills, and just 86 of 26,000 stocks accounted for half the total return. While the overall stock market has historically delivered about 10% annual returns, this performance is driven by a small minority of stocks. The median stock performed poorly, and the odds of randomly picking a winning stock are low. Bessembinder's bootstrap simulations confirmed that picking a random stock likely results in selecting a loser. The Valueline geometric index, representing the median stock, has underperformed the S&P 500 drastically since 1990. A similar pattern was observed in Norway, where only 18 large companies explained the entire value creation on the Oslo Stock Exchange from 1985 to 2017. The research concludes that most stocks do not outperform Treasury Bills. The recommended solution for investors is to buy a passive fund, or if investing in individual stocks, to ensure diversification.

This study examines how TRNC Presidents' discourses on history, identity, and education have shaped education policies. Education in the TRNC strengthens Turkish Cypriot identity and social belonging. The education system evolved through Ottoman, British colonial, 1960 Republic, and post-1974 phases, with the Turkish model and national identity construction emphasized after 1983. The Turkish Cypriot Education Council's decisions have been pivotal in structural reforms, teacher training, curriculum, and identity shaping. History textbooks often presented a Turkish identity-centered, polarizing narrative emphasizing conflict with Greek Cypriots, though since the early 2000s, EU harmonization and bicommunal projects prompted more reconciliatory, multi-perspective reforms, with setbacks due to political sensitivities. Presidential discourses directly shaped education: Rauf Denktaş stressed national identity and integration with Turkey; Mehmet Ali Talat focused on EU harmonization and reforms; Derviş Eroğlu emphasized educational cooperation with Turkey and technical education; Mustafa Akıncı promoted multiculturalism, peace, and intercommunal dialogue; Ersin Tatar highlighted national identity and integration with Turkey. Key policy elements include strengthening national identity, Turkish as medium of instruction, cooperation with Turkey, internationalization of higher education, and balancing secularism and religious education. The study concludes that presidential discourses and Council decisions jointly drive reforms, recommending future policies adopt a multi-perspective, scientifically neutral, long-term strategic framework independent of political ideology, while considering local needs and educational autonomy.

The speaker, chosen by a free people, expresses gratitude and dedicates himself to their service. As executor of the Federal Constitution, he will execute laws, superintend foreign and confederate relations, manage revenue, command forces, and communicate with the Legislature. He will administer laws within Executive limits, seek peace and fair friendship with foreign nations, and show forbearance. He will respect states' reserved powers. He will manage public revenue with strict economy to extinguish the national debt and prevent profligacy, aided by Congressional appropriation and accountability rules. Taxation should equally favor agriculture, commerce, and manufactures, with exceptions for products essential to independence. Internal improvements and knowledge diffusion are important. He will not enlarge standing armies in peace, keep military subordinate to civil power, gradually increase the Navy, preserve military infrastructure, and improve discipline. The national militia is the defense bulwark; as long as government secures rights, armed freemen are invincible. He will pursue a just, liberal policy toward Indian tribes. Public sentiment demands reform: correcting patronage abuses that conflict with election freedom and counteracting causes of unfaithful or incompetent appointments. He will select diligent, talented men, valuing integrity and zeal over numbers. Acknowledging his diffidence, he looks to predecessors' examples, seeks aid from other branches and citizens, and relies on divine providence for the country's care.

Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov, at an India-Russia relations event, said India's SCO accession significantly boosted the group's political profile and ability to stabilize Central/South Asia and resolve the Afghanistan crisis. He praised India's independent foreign policy for global security. On Afghanistan, he deemed the US force strategy ineffective, noting NATO's failure to curb extremism and drug trade. He denied supporting the Taliban, stating contacts were only for citizen extraction and pressuring talks under UN criteria. He regretted the US rejecting the Moscow Process for the Six Plus One group, and said resolution requires all stakeholders: government, Taliban, neighbours. He criticized the Kabul Process as too large, advocating a smaller group including Central Asian countries.

Michael Ben’Ary, an assistant U.S. attorney, was fired last week during a terrorism prosecution. A letter on his door said a false social media post by pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly, alleging he was an ally of former Deputy AG Lisa Monaco, led to his termination. The letter warned that DOJ leadership is removing career officials, making America less safe, and is more concerned with punishing perceived enemies than protecting national security. It also referenced pressure to indict James Comey.

The team will approach the game as if the opponent is playing for its life. Focus is on a good start to avoid a rough night. The opponent has home playoff success. They want to end the series, opponent wants to extend. No chatter, and a topic hasn't come up.

A digital accessibility workshop was designed and delivered in India for 73 participants (33 software engineers, 28 educators, 12 UX designers) to address the lack of accessibility training in the region. The one-day workshop followed a three-phase model (preparation, execution, post-workshop reflection) and included five instructional modules: Accessibility Basics, Accessibility Design, Accessible Software Engineering, Accessibility Testing and Reporting, and Teaching Accessibility. Hands-on activities, assistive technology demonstrations, case studies, and tool demos were provided. Pre- and post-surveys assessed changes in knowledge, attitudes, and confidence. Post-workshop feedback indicated high engagement and effectiveness: all participants would recommend the workshop, 90% agreed it was highly effective and engaging, and 52% reported a significant shift in their perception of accessibility. Participants expressed interest in advanced topics such as AI in accessibility, inclusive design for diverse users, and organizational strategies. Recommendations for future workshops include distributing pre-workshop materials, customizing content by role, incorporating case studies, and providing continued engagement opportunities. The workshop demonstrated the effectiveness of experiential learning in building accessibility capacity among Indian computing professionals and educators.

Yandex (NASDAQ:YNDX) announced it will report second quarter 2018 financial results on July 26, 2018, and hold a conference call at 8:00 a.m. U.S. Eastern Time. Call and replay numbers and a webcast link are provided.

The passage describes e-Maintenance (predictive maintenance) as part of e-Manufacturing, using real-time monitoring for near-zero downtime and degradation prediction. Web-enabled systems monitor, analyze, compare, reconfigure, and sustain assets, linking intelligent decisions to e-business tools. Remote assessment integrates sensors, reasoning agents, wireless, and virtual interfaces. Web-enabled and infotronics technologies support integration with SCM and ERP. E-Maintenance is a pillar for e-Manufacturing and e-business integration, promising increased reliability, optimal asset performance, and seamless supplier/customer integration. Research needs are listed.

Reconfigurable maintenance ties production quality to customer requirements, requiring system configuration to minimize deviations and offset demand changes. A tool assesses production possibilities. Quality is affected by configuration changes; tolerance and maintenance policies impact quality and costs. The proposed reconfigurable maintenance system enables intercompany cooperation by sharing diagnostic knowledge and service activities, improving reconfiguration efficiency. Collected data supports reliability, sustainability, serviceability, and safeguard factors.

Modular reconfigurable maintenance systems ensure reliability via scheduling and optimization, with system-wide communication for remote maintenance and cost reduction. Modular subsystems use distributed architectures based on maintenance policies, and monitoring modules use sensors, radio signals, and data analysis. An enterprise reconfigurable modular maintenance system detects adverse conditions for preventive/remedial measures, with maintenance policy varying with system changes. A knowledge base and expert system interpret historical data to identify symptoms, trends, and degradation causes, expanding the knowledge base for efficient corrective actions.

The conclusion notes that mass customization faces competitive pressures, requiring a reconfigurable maintenance system to handle adverse conditions and ensure production configuration reliability.

The passage describes ways to use Alexa for cleaning tasks. You can create a cleaning schedule with the Cleaning Buddy skill. You can set up voice purchasing to order cleaning supplies from Amazon using a four-digit code. You can automate vacuuming by connecting robot vacuums like Neato or Roomba to Alexa and using voice commands. For laundry, you can use the Laundrapp service for pick-up and delivery in select US cities, or install skills like Good Housekeeping or Stains Be Gone for stain removal advice.

New England Patriots wide receiver Malcolm Mitchell caught six passes for 70 yards in Super Bowl XVI. He overcame significant literacy struggles that became apparent in college, when he could not read at the level of his peers or even read movie captions. He started from scratch by reading children's books like The Giving Tree, teaching himself grammar and reading skills, and practicing reading like he practiced football. This led to a passion for literacy. He launched Read with Malcolm, a youth literacy initiative that promotes book ownership and reading in underserved communities. He will receive the Promise Hero Award from America's Promise Alliance. Mitchell graduated from the University of Georgia with a communications degree, was a fourth-round draft pick, and authored a children's book, The Magician's Hat. He grew up in a single-parent household in Valdosta, Georgia, with an older brother who steered him from poor decisions and a younger sister who kept him level-headed. His mother, Pratina Woods, encouraged him to lead and do what is best. His organization aims to address the fact that 61 percent of low-income families have no age-appropriate books at home, and children with the lowest reading scores account for 65 percent of non-graduates. Mitchell's favorite children's books are The Giving Tree and Exclamation Mark; his favorite authors include J.K. Rowling and Robert Green. He now reads multiple books at once. He advises struggling youth to never give up, view each day as an opportunity to be their best, and overcome adversity with relentless effort. Receiving the award motivates him to continue visiting schools and spreading the message that reading can change lives.

Using white light interferometry and atomic force microscopy, this work investigates topographic defects introduced by electropolishing on highly polished polycrystalline bulk Nb samples. Electropolishing creates sharp intergranular sloped steps with heights up to 70 nm and slope angles reaching ~50°. Surface roughness increases with electropolishing removal, and sequential electropolishing shows that steps form at the end of the process, likely due to orientation-dependent oxide growth or dissolution, with step characteristics primarily controlled by relative grain orientation rather than removal depth.

These geometrical defects are analyzed within London theory for their impact on superconducting radio frequency cavity performance. The sloped steps cause magnetic field enhancement and superheating field suppression. The superheating field suppression factor depends on slope angle, step height, and coherence length; the magnetic field enhancement factor depends on the ratio of step height to penetration depth and slope angle. Measured slope angles and step heights can substantially degrade the achievable peak magnetic field, more than previously expected. As coherence length shrinks with impurity alloying, superheating field suppression becomes more severe, while magnetic field enhancement becomes less severe due to increased penetration depth.

Simulations of impurity diffusion around the sloped-step geometry show that the impurity concentration is reduced at the bottom of the step—where vortex nucleation is preferred—because the larger interior angle provides greater volume for impurities to expand into. This effect is significant when the diffusion length is comparable to or smaller than the step height, potentially compromising the uniformity of shallow impurity profiles from treatments like low-temperature baking or nitrogen infusion. The reduction in intergranular step height from electropolishing compared to buffered chemical polishing may explain the better response of electropolished cavities to such treatments. The findings highlight the need for surfaces smoother than “mirror-smooth” to achieve field limits near the superheating field and motivate the use of microscopic theories to predict defect impacts on high-field performance.

British police declared a major incident after a man and a woman in their 40s were found unconscious in Amesbury, near Salisbury, and hospitalized in critical condition from an unknown substance. Counterterrorism officers are working with local police. Police are keeping an open mind and it is not yet clear if a crime was committed. Health officials say there is no wider risk.

In this adversary proceeding, plaintiff D.A.N. Joint Venture III, L.P. sought to deny the Chapter 7 discharge of debtor Ambrozy Jerry Fasolak under Bankruptcy Code sections 727(a)(2), (a)(3), (a)(4), and (a)(5). The bankruptcy court held a final evidentiary hearing and ruled in favor of the debtor.

Background: The debtor, 72, had owned A & F Corporation for over 30 years. In March 2002, he signed a personal financial statement showing net worth of $2,742,000. Shortly after, he retired and his son took over the business. In 2002-2003, the debtor and his wife purchased a Florida lot and built a home. In November 2003, A & F Corporation filed Chapter 11 (later converted to Chapter 7). On December 1, 2003, the debtor's wife sold their Pennsylvania home and received $194,814.07; four days later, $364,780.80 was deposited into her Bank of America account. Also on December 1, 2003, the debtor filed a Chapter 13 case in Pennsylvania, which was voluntarily dismissed in March 2004. On July 9, 2004, he filed the present Chapter 7 case in Florida. His schedules initially omitted prior bankruptcies, his stock in A & F Corp., and income from the corporation; these were later amended.

The court found that the plaintiff failed to meet its burden of proof on all counts.

Under § 727(a)(2) (fraudulent transfer/concealment), the plaintiff showed that the debtor transferred $8,600 from his account to his wife's SunTrust account, deposited his paychecks into her account, and traded a car titled in his name for a truck titled in his wife's name. The debtor's wife held bank accounts with substantial sums, and the debtor's schedules listed minimal assets. However, the court found the evidence did not establish that the debtor acted with actual intent to hinder, delay, or defraud creditors. It was not clearly shown that the funds in the wife's accounts originally belonged to the debtor; the wife testified some funds were her separate property. The debtor had retired and was forgetful; his wife handled finances. The court concluded the transfers were equally likely related to the debtor's withdrawal from business and financial affairs.

Under § 727(a)(3) (failure to keep records), the plaintiff did not identify any specific missing records. The wife testified she produced all requested records, and the debtor said no documents were required from him. Business records were left at the corporation's premises after its bankruptcy conversion.

Under § 727(a)(4) (false oaths), the debtor acknowledged inaccuracies in his original schedules: failure to disclose prior bankruptcies, stock interest, and income. He also gave deposition testimony about closed bank accounts that was inaccurate. The court found these false statements were not made with intent to deceive. The stock interest was disclosed elsewhere; the income was modest consulting fees; the closed account was a short-term construction account he forgot; and the transfers to his wife were household funds. The court evaluated the testimony and found the errors resulted from mistake or misunderstanding, not fraudulent intent.

Under § 727(a)(5) (failure to explain loss of assets), the plaintiff relied on the 2002 financial statement showing $2.7 million net worth. The court found the plaintiff did not establish that the debtor owned specific property in 2002 that was missing and unexplained. The A & F Corp. interest was liquidated in its own bankruptcy, and the "personal effects" were not itemized.

Therefore, the court ordered final judgment for the debtor, denying the complaint and allowing the discharge.

The passage discusses the Supreme Court case concerning President Trump's firing of FTC commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter and the precedent Humphrey's Executor. The court seems likely to uphold the firing. Humphrey's Executor arose from FDR's 1933 firing of FTC Commissioner William Humphrey; the court then held that the FTC's duties were quasi-legislative and quasi-judicial, not executive, allowing Congress to limit removal. Modern critics and Justice Scalia have criticized the decision. In Seila Law v. CFPB, the court applied Humphrey's specific analysis, finding the CFPB's single-director structure and executive powers (rulemaking, enforcement, adjudication) did not meet the standard for independence. The author expects the court to similarly examine the modern FTC's powers. The FTC has changed since 1935, gaining more rulemaking and enforcement authority and becoming more partisan. Professor Crane argues the FTC now acts primarily as an executive law enforcement agency, not legislative or judicial. A recent stay involving the NLRB and MSPB indicated the government is likely to show those agencies exercise considerable executive power, similar to the FTC. The court may not completely renounce Humphrey's Executor, partly due to concerns about the Federal Reserve's distinct independence. The court's order in Slaughter's case separated the question of the removal statute's constitutionality from whether Humphrey's Executor should be overruled, suggesting a "mend it, don't end it" approach.

In a SONA debate speech, DA Leader Mmusi Maimane accused the ANC government and President Zuma of being "the enemy of the people," citing the Esidimeni tragedy (94 deaths), Marikana, and the heavy security and violence during the SONA. He claimed the ANC's radical economic transformation rhetoric is a cover for elite self-enrichment, with land reform and BEE corrupted for cronies. He described a "Lost Generation" of millions of unemployed youth. He then outlined the DA's Rescue Plan, which includes: building a lean, efficient state; education reforms (teacher training, school vouchers, National Education Inspectorate); expanded student funding and free vocational training; private sector apprenticeships and government internships; labour reforms exempting small businesses and youth from minimum wage; a Jobs & Justice fund; stopping the nuclear deal; partly privatizing SOEs; land reform through title deeds and farm equity schemes; adding 50,000 police; a health plan with free basic services; and anti-corruption measures like halving ministries and cutting perks. He called for moving forward with hope.

MIT researchers developed a more accurate prime editing system that reduces errors by 60-fold. Prime editing is a CRISPR-based method that corrects faulty genes by making a single-strand cut and inserting a corrected sequence via an RNA template, but it can introduce unintended mutations when the old DNA strand reattaches. The MIT team, led by Vikash Chauhan with senior authors Phillip Sharp and Robert Langer, engineered Cas9 mutations based on a 2023 observation that certain mutated Cas9 proteins cut one or two bases away, destabilizing the old strand and promoting error-free incorporation. They identified mutations that lowered the error rate to 1/20th of the original, then combined pairs to achieve 1/36th. Incorporating an RNA-binding protein to stabilize the template further reduced errors, yielding the vPE editor with an error rate 1/60th of the original—from about 1 in 7 to 1 in 101 for common edits, and from 1 in 122 to 1 in 543 for a more precise mode. Tests were performed in mouse and human cells. The team is now working on improving efficiency and delivery to specific tissues, and they anticipate the tool will be adopted in research labs. The study was funded by the Life Sciences Research Foundation, the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, and the National Cancer Institute.

After ICE arrests in Austin, Austin ISD lawyers directed staff not to share unvetted resources or discuss controversial issues on district property, warning of state lawmaker scrutiny. The memo followed 51 detentions that heightened student anxiety. Board Vice President Paul Saldana criticized it as contradictory and conservative. Superintendent Paul Cruz posted general immigrant student resources. Education Austin distributed explicit Know Your Rights documents and lawyer names, asserting the information is not political. The union will hold a news conference Wednesday, and the board will discuss the memo.

A 13-year-old girl was shot in the thigh while sitting in a garage with others in Guildford, Sydney, on Tuesday night. She is in serious but stable condition. Police believe the shooting was not random.

Horse polo originated in Persia over 20 centuries ago and spread through the Middle East, Central Asia, and the Far East. The modern game stems from India, where it was called "pulu" (referring to the wooden ball), and was brought to England by British travelers, then to the U.S. Today there are about 250 polo clubs in 43 states. The Milwaukee Polo Club, located in Hartland (26 miles west of Milwaukee), is an extension of the original 1923 formation and has been at its current site for over 20 years. Thomas Esser handles marketing. Polo acquired a "Sport of Kings" image, but Esser aims to change that perception. MPC considers itself "blue collar" polo, with members including nurses, students, bartenders, and retirees. Matches are accessible: $5 tickets (kids free), and visitors can meet players and horses. Games consist of six seven-minute chukkers with a half-time divot stomp, lasting about two hours. Outdoor polo is fair-weather for safety; if rain threatens footing, play is canceled, but members still show horses and talk to fans. Club members emphasize horse welfare: 70-80% of a player's ability depends on the horse, and horses are treated as teammates, not tools. Work is limited, with down days after hard chukkers, and proper horsemanship is essential. The club's summer season began June 18. Contact: 262-222-2870 or 262-951-8029, milwaukeepoloclub.com.

The speaker emphasizes living in the present and focusing on preparation, focus, and execution rather than momentum. He states that not winning is devastating because in a salary cap world, opportunities to reach the Final are rare and require injury luck, referencing Pavel, Nick, and Rafi. He believes in accepting decisions and thought a player was excellent. Both teams have depth, which is necessary to win consistently; relying on one or two players makes a team vulnerable. He stresses the importance of drafting (Jimmy Nill) and development (Kirk Fraser), noting contributions from Helm, Ericsson, Abby, and Leino. The coaching staff reviewed forecheck issues and concluded that executing and avoiding turnovers is critical. Goalies have performed better at home, and Ozzie must be good with team help. Team building is about winning together, sacrificing, and blocking shots, not just socializing. He urges enjoying the rare opportunity and notes the series is very close between two strong teams, hoping for a favorable outcome.

The paper studies many-to-one two-sided matching with ordinal preferences and ties. Standard stability (participant-justified envy-freeness) can be unfair to teams. Recent work introduced team-EF1 (envy-freeness up to one participant) from fair division, but team-EF1 and participant-justified EF may be incompatible. The authors propose team-justified EF1, which disregards envy from a team toward another when the envied participants prefer the other team. Using stochastic dominance (SD), they define team-justified SD-EF1. Two warm-up algorithms are given: one guarantees team-justified SD-EF1 and participant-EF but may be unbalanced; another uses an auxiliary one-to-one instance with team-slots to achieve team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified EF, and balancedness, but not swap stability. The main algorithm (Algorithm 3) iteratively expands participants’ eligibility sets and computes a matching that lexicographically maximizes team-slot values in round-robin order, then optimizes participants’ preferences. It returns an allocation satisfying team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified EF, balancedness, and Pareto optimality (hence swap stability). The algorithm runs in polynomial time and generalizes both the round-robin algorithm (when participants are indifferent) and the Gale–Shapley algorithm (with strict preferences). With augmented tie-breaking, it is group-strategyproof for participants: no group can misreport preferences to all strictly benefit. The algorithm extends to settings with team quotas and preferences for being unassigned, yielding a mechanism that is stable, Pareto optimal, group-strategyproof for participants, and satisfies an extended team-justified SD-EF1 notion.

Digital laggards prioritize short-term optimization of existing initiatives, with narrow training and a risk-averse, transactional culture marked by a lack of trust. Digital leaders foster a learning mindset, though they also struggle to balance risk-taking with practical short-term demands. A pharmaceutical company case study shows how creating a localized, controlled experimentation environment can foster innovation in a regulated industry. Digital leaders believe in data transparency, making data widely available and discouraging hoarding, while digital laggards tightly control data access on a need-to-know basis, often hoarding data as a source of power and favoring business judgment over data-driven decisions. Digital leaders embrace measurement to learn, using data-driven metrics to provide flexibility and autonomy, whereas digital laggards set aspirational goals ungrounded in data, leading to a focus on adherence to process over objective measurement. Digital leaders use data-driven objectives to create shared goals and align the organization vertically and horizontally, while digital laggards fail to clearly connect goals with strategy, causing misalignment. Digital leaders emphasize data culture as central, aligning beliefs, values, and actions, while laggards show misalignment between espoused values and behavior. Changing engrained mindsets is noted as the most challenging part of transformation. Organizations tend to fit into one of four patterns—data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant—and can target focus areas accordingly.

Sen. Mark Warner, top Intelligence Committee Democrat, says Republicans are trying to impugn the Mueller investigation and FBI. He calls the Nunes memo part of a campaign to undermine the probe. Warner and Burr were denied early access. Warner criticizes the memo's methodology and reckless use of classified data. A party-line House vote blocked the Democratic memo, which Warner calls partisan. Warner says the Senate Russia probe is vital for cyber defense; the President's inaction endangers the country.

Penny stocks are defined by the SEC as stocks below $5. They mostly trade over-the-counter (OTC) and on the Pink Sheets, not on formal exchanges like NYSE or Nasdaq. The OTC market serves small companies that cannot or do not want to meet exchange listing requirements. Penny stocks are considered bad investments because many companies have unproven business models, are illiquid, and are very volatile. Most penny stocks end up worthless. They lack financial disclosure: Pink Sheets stocks are not required to file reports with the SEC, and there are no minimum standards beyond a $0.01 price and not being in bankruptcy. Low liquidity leads to high costs from bid-ask spreads (slippage) and commissions. Information is scarce, as few brokers cover OTC stocks. While penny stocks themselves are usually legitimate businesses, the thinly traded market exposes them to scams. Three typical scams are: the "know-it-all" scam, where self-proclaimed gurus sell secret formulas or courses promising winning strategies (no such shortcuts exist); the pump and dump, where promoters artificially inflate the stock price in illiquid markets and sell into the hype, making penny stock trading a zero-sum game; and the dump and dilute scam, where a company issues shares to raise money but does not use the proceeds for the business, sometimes using inverse stock splits to deceive investors. The passage strongly recommends avoiding penny stocks altogether, noting that almost all fail and success stories are likely due to scams. Traders are warned they are more likely to be prey than predators in these unregulated markets.

The ATR trailing stop is a technical indicator introduced by J. Welles Wilder that helps traders set dynamic stop-loss levels based on price volatility. It uses the average true range (ATR), a volatility measure, to adjust stops according to market conditions. Calculation involves multiplying the ATR value by a multiplier, typically 3.5, then subtracting the result from the previous close for long positions or adding it for short positions, establishing tighter stops in volatile markets. The indicator aids in determining exit points, protecting profits, minimizing losses, and can also provide entry signals by assessing breakouts or reversals based on trailing stop levels. It is applicable to stocks and futures. The ATR trailing stop signals potential trend reversals when price consistently breaches its levels; ATR bands derived from ATR values help identify breakouts and gauge volatility intensity. Its relationship with volatility allows setting stop levels reflective of prevailing price volatility. Risks include that it does not account for past performance and price movements, focusing on current volatility dynamics, so traders should incorporate other analyses. The cross point, where price intersects trailing stop levels, indicates potential market changes and can prompt position reassessment.

Texas A&M has had a first-round pick in every NFL draft since 2011. Christian Kirk, who left early, is the Aggies' best chance to extend the streak. He is projected as a fringe first-round pick; USA Today ranked him the fourth-best receiver, with only Calvin Ridley and DJ Moore projected in the first round. Kirk said carrying on the tradition means a lot. The draft is at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, but Kirk will be in Arizona. Other A&M prospects include safety Armani Watts (mid-round) and receiver Damion Ratley (late rounds). Defensive tackle Zaycoven Henderson's draft stock fell after a December arrest. The Aggies' low number of potential picks is attributed to poor 2013 and 2014 recruiting classes. The first round is Thursday, followed by rounds two and three Friday, and four through seven Saturday.

Drew Faust, Harvard's first female president, will step down June 30, 2018, after 11 years. She plans a sabbatical to return to scholarship. Hired in 2007, she succeeded Lawrence Summers, who left amid faculty conflict. Faust restored trust, fostered collaboration, expanded aid, and championed arts and sciences. The campaign raised $8 billion, surpassing its goal. Challenges included backlash over club crackdown, diversity demands, soccer team suspension over lewd report, and endowment loss. She will focus on protecting research funding, attracting talent, and advancing inclusion. A search committee will find a replacement.

Peter Lynch is a retired money manager who managed Fidelity’s Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990, achieving 29.2% average annual returns, more than double the S&P 500. He advocated value investing and is known for “invest in what you know” and “ten baggers.” His early life included caddying at a golf club, where he heard investment talk, and his first stock purchase helped fund his education. After joining Fidelity as an analyst, he took over the Magellan Fund when it had $20 million in assets and 40 stocks, expanding it to $14 billion and 1,200 companies by his retirement in 1990. He outperformed the S&P 500 in all but two years.

Lynch’s strategy centered on understanding a business, ignoring short-term market moves, and focusing on fundamentals. He categorized companies into six groups: slow growers, moderately growing, fast growing, cyclical, turnarounds, and asset plays. He preferred simple companies with clear business models, boring names, low analyst coverage, and spin-offs, while avoiding hot stocks, diversified companies, and those with high institutional ownership. He analyzed fundamental indicators such as P/E ratio. His portfolio typically allocated 30–40% to growth stocks, 10–20% to moderately growing and cyclical stocks, the rest to turnarounds, and 1% to minor potential companies. He reviewed holdings quarterly, never held cash, sold when price rose without fundamental improvement, and bought more on dips if fundamentals were sound, viewing a 25% drop as a buy signal. The passage notes he had access to extensive analytical resources at Fidelity.

The Vice President of the Ghana Football Association, George Afriyie, was dismissed by the Executive Committee. The decision follows a rumoured rift with GFA President Kwesi Nyantakyi, which began when Afriyie called Nyantakyi greedy over financial disagreements and Nyantakyi suspected Afriyie of colluding with a critic. Afriyie had announced his intention to contest the 2019 GFA presidency. His sacking clarifies the political divide and is expected to embolden his challenge. Previous vice presidents sidelined by Nyantakyi lost influence in football circles. Afriyie was also removed as head of the Black Stars Management Committee two weeks earlier. Some Executive Committee members publicly backed Nyantakyi, and Winfred Osei replaced Afriyie. Nyantakyi has not confirmed if he will seek re-election, but the sacking fuels speculation he may run again to protect his legacy.

Alphabet, which owns YouTube, will pay $24.5 million to settle a lawsuit brought by Donald Trump over his post-January 6, 2021, ban. Of that, $22 million goes to Trump, who will direct it to the Trust for the National Mall and a White House ballroom. The remaining $2.5 million goes to co-plaintiffs including the American Conservative Union and others. YouTube suspended Trump's account after the Capitol riot and lifted restrictions in March 2023. Trump sued YouTube, Twitter, and Meta in July 2021. He previously settled with Meta for $25 million and X for $10 million, totaling over $57 million from post-ban cases. Alphabet admitted no liability.

Lenders to the Dabhol Power Company (DPC), meeting in Singapore, appointed Stone & Webster to evaluate the cost of suspending the project's second phase. Enron India's managing director suggested a temporary suspension. DPC indicated willingness to reduce its rate of return from 16 to 11 percent. The Godbole renegotiation committee stated DPC's return on equity should not exceed 16 percent. DPC appealed to the Bombay High Court to stay a Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC) order restraining escrow account activation and arbitration, arguing MERC lacked jurisdiction. Lenders formed a committee, including IDBI, ICICI, SBI, and foreign banks, to negotiate with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB). Reports said other states could not afford DPC's power, and private power producers expected an early resolution after the Prime Minister's comments. Enron sought assurance on Phase I power drawal before suspending Phase II. Activist Medha Patkar called for a judicial inquiry.
Scientists urge listing cheetahs as Endangered on the IUCN Red List, citing low southern Africa population estimates and 91% historic range loss.

Michigan State Superintendent Michael Rice is retiring after a career in education, having led since 2019. In a recent interview, he emphasized that students need more instructional days, not fewer. Rice criticized state flexibility that allows schools to count up to seven professional development days as instructional days, meaning students may receive far less than the required 180 days. He urged lawmakers to change this, noting that prior to 2019-20, professional development did not reduce instructional time. Schools can also use up to 15 online instruction days, which many students struggle with. Rice acknowledged Michigan’s educational challenges, including flat NAEP performance and low early literacy, but cited progress: additional funding for vulnerable students, increased preschool enrollment, and a record 82% graduation rate. However, the state has not fully achieved any of its Top 10 Strategic Education Plan goals. He pointed to Mississippi’s reading gains as a model, where mandatory LETRS training for teachers and literacy coaches, along with protecting instructional time, led to significant improvement. Michigan has funded LETRS training for thousands of teachers but Rice wants it mandatory for K-5. Teacher shortages are improving due to state investments in stipends, scholarships, and grow-your-own programs, with the number of people preparing for the profession rising from 9,500 in 2017 to 18,000 annually, though shortages persist in the most challenged communities.

Vector-borne diseases, particularly mosquito-borne ones, are a growing global concern, with dengue cases in the Americas surpassing 7 million by May 2024. Climate change and human mobility are facilitating the spread of competent mosquitoes into temperate regions like Europe. In the Basque Country, no autochthonous cases have been recorded, but imported cases and Aedes albopictus and Aedes japonicus populations have increased. This study models the relationship between ovitrap egg counts and environmental factors (temperature, humidity, precipitation) using data from 2016–2023 for the provinces of Gipuzkoa and Bizkaia (Araba excluded due to insufficient positive eggs). Data were pre-processed by averaging the 20 highest egg counts per province over 14-day intervals, imputing missing values as zero, and smoothing. Models compared include Generalized Linear Model with Gaussian distribution, SARIMAX, Random Forest, and Conditional Inference Trees, with lagged variables improving performance. Temperature showed the strongest correlation with egg counts (lag -1). On training data, Random Forest performed best (R² 0.98), but on test data, GLM generalized better (R² 0.85 Gipuzkoa, 0.81 Bizkaia). Bizkaia test performance was lower due to unusually high 2023 egg counts. Predictions for 2024 indicate lower mosquito abundance. The study underscores the importance of continuous surveillance and incorporating vector data for forecasting in non-endemic regions.

Libby Kane reflects on her college experience eight years post-graduation. She regrets not taking advantage of opportunities or realizing her time for adventure. She argues that such touching, often called "the Rub" or "the Stroke," is assault and a form of harassment, though euphemisms obscure its nature. She notes that she never lost a hearing while visibly pregnant, attributing this to others' fear of upsetting a pregnant woman rather than her legal skill. Ryan points out that the Pregnancy Discrimination Act and EEOC guidance recognize pregnancy-based harassment, including unwelcome physical conduct, as unlawful discrimination, yet belly touching is rarely addressed. She calls for explicit policies prohibiting touching a pregnant person without consent, to be included in HR manuals, training, and workplace harassment policies. She acknowledges her own past ignorance toward pregnant colleagues and urges the legal profession to end this practice.

In McGillivray v. Eramian, the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court upheld a jury verdict for the plaintiff. The plaintiff was injured when a splinter from the sliding floor of the defendant's bowling alley entered his finger as he delivered a ball with his hand close to the floor. Evidence showed the floor was uneven, wavy, with rotten wood, pulled nails, and warped boards; the flooring was used and several years old. The plaintiff did not touch the floor, and the splinter was projecting. The court held that the jury could find the defendant negligent for failing to maintain the floor in a reasonably safe condition, including failing to plane worn and splintered areas as customary. It also ruled that the plaintiff was not contributorily negligent as a matter of law, because his bowling style was not shown to be unusual, and he had not observed the splinter beforehand. The trial judge properly refused requested instructions that would have assumed facts for the jury. Judgment for the plaintiff for $750 was affirmed.

This study analyzed cross-sectional data from the COVID-PCD participatory cohort study, including 747 people with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) from 49 countries, to examine diagnostic test use, recall, and associated factors. Most participants (92%) reported diagnostic testing. Among those aged ≥5 years, 49% reported nasal nitric oxide (nNO) measurement, 75% reported biopsy, and 58% reported genetic testing. Test use varied widely by country; for example, genetic testing was reported by 70% in France and 38% in Switzerland. Recall of tests also differed, with the highest non-recall for nNO (18%) and lowest for biopsy (8%). Only 36% of participants aged ≥5 reported all three tests (nNO, biopsy, genetics). Multivariable logistic regression showed that diagnosis after 2010 was associated with higher odds of reporting nNO (OR 2.2), biopsy (OR 3.2), and genetic testing (OR 4.7) compared to diagnosis before 2000. Participants with situs abnormalities were less likely to report nNO (OR 0.5), biopsy (OR 0.5), and genetic testing (OR 0.7). Age at diagnosis was not associated with testing. The study highlights international variation in PCD diagnostics, with many individuals having incomplete work-up, particularly those diagnosed earlier or with situs abnormalities. The authors suggest that clinicians should review and potentially supplement testing to improve diagnostic characterization for personalized medicine.

On July 4, a massive flash flood on the Guadalupe River struck Camp Mystic in Kerr County, Texas, killing 25 campers, two counselors, and the camp director; one camper remains missing. Counselors Chloe Childress and Katherine Ferruzzo were hailed as heroes for trying to save the girls in their cabin. In the aftermath, parents including Matthew and Wendie Childress (Chloe’s parents) and Blake Bonner (father of 9-year-old Lila) organized to advocate for tighter camp safety regulations. With the help of a pro-bono lobbying team, they met with Gov. Greg Abbott, Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, and House Speaker Dustin Burrows on Aug. 14, sharing their daughters’ stories. Abbott then called a second special legislative session, making camp safety the top priority. Lawmakers introduced House Bill 1 and Senate Bill 1, which required overnight cabins to be moved out of floodplains, camps to install alert systems and follow weather warnings with radios, and staff to be trained on emergency plans including evacuation routes to higher ground. The bills passed the House and Senate on Aug. 21. On Sept. 5, Abbott signed the bills into law at a ceremony, using multiple Sharpies so parents could keep them as mementos. The parents felt they had accomplished something positive and honored their daughters, but they continued to grapple with profound grief, acknowledging that the new laws could not bring their children back.

The Third Circuit vacated the district court's order denying Prava Chatterjee's petition to set aside a settlement and release of a maritime death claim arising from the 1975 collision of the S.S. EDGAR M. QUEENY and S.S. CORINTHOS, which killed her son, a crewmember. The court held that the validity of the special power of attorney is governed by Indian law, not federal maritime law, due to a conflict between Indian and Pennsylvania fraud law. The validity of the release is governed by federal maritime law, and the strict scrutiny standard of Garrett v. Moore-McCormack Co. applies to settlements by a seaman's relatives, placing the burden on shipowners to prove the release was executed freely, without deception or coercion, and with full understanding. The district court did not abuse its discretion in excluding the transcript of a prior Calcutta Commission because the shipowners lacked an opportunity to cross-examine and the petitioner was not shown unavailable. However, the district court's denial of a new commission to take testimony in India, without stating a reason, was an abuse of discretion that, combined with other rulings, deprived Mrs. Chatterjee of a fair opportunity to present evidence on forgery, fraud, and ratification, violating due process. The case is remanded with directions to invoke a commission under Rule 28(b) to take testimony in India.

On regulatory frameworks, the passage highlights challenges from rapid AI advancement, including misinformation, deepfakes, bias, and difficulties fitting new technologies into existing legal structures. Challenges persist at macro-levels (industry-government communication gaps, lack of international consensus) and micro-levels (risks like jailbreaking prompts identified only in practice). The passage calls for partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers, forward-looking regulations, and a governance framework combining top-down and bottom-up approaches, with responsibility shared by all stakeholders. The speaker, having just returned from a fourteen-thousand-mile trip, addresses Congress to report on the Crimea (Yalta) Conference. He states the conference had two main purposes: to bring about Germany's defeat with the greatest speed and smallest Allied losses, and to continue building a foundation for international accord to secure lasting peace. He notes that at Teheran only military plans were made, but at Yalta specific political agreements were reached.

Key outcomes include: arrangements for more frequent contacts among foreign ministers every three or four months; agreements on the occupation and control of Germany after victory, including the complete destruction of its military power and the prevention of Nazi or Prussian militarism revival; settlement of the remaining differences on the International Security Organization, ironing out the ten percent unresolved after Dumbarton Oaks; and addressing political and economic problems of liberated areas. Unanimous agreement was reached on every point, achieving a unity of thought.

The speaker details that unconditional surrender means temporary control of Germany by Britain, Russia, France, and the U.S., each occupying a zone coordinated by a Control Council in Berlin. It means the end of Nazism, the Nazi Party, militaristic influence, punishment of war criminals, complete disarmament, disbanding of armed forces, dismemberment of the General Staff, and reparations in kind (plants, machinery, raw materials) to avoid past money-reparation mistakes. The objective is to secure peace by removing Germany's ability to wage aggressive war.

He describes the destruction witnessed at Yalta and Sevastopol, emphasizing that German militarism and Christian decency cannot coexist.

Regarding the international organization, the Americans proposed a voting procedure for the Security Council that was unanimously adopted; details will be announced soon. A United Nations conference will meet in San Francisco on April 25, 1945, to create a charter. The U.S. Senate has been kept advised, and a bipartisan Congressional delegation will attend. World peace is not a party question.

On liberated areas, the three powers agreed that political and economic problems are a joint responsibility. They will help people establish democratic processes, with interim governments representative of democratic elements and free elections as soon as possible. The U.S. must share responsibility for keeping peace; decisions will involve compromise.

The Polish question was resolved with the objective of a strong, independent, prosperous Poland with a government selected by its people. The existing Provisional Government will be reorganized on a broader democratic basis to include democratic leaders from Poland and abroad, recognized as the temporary government, and pledged to hold free elections with universal suffrage and secret ballot. Poland's boundaries were a compromise: compensation in the north and west for losses east of the Curzon Line, with the western border to be fixed at the final peace conference. Most of East Prussia goes to Poland, and Danzig becomes Polish.

France, though not a participant, was invited to accept a zone of control in Germany, join as a sponsor of the San Francisco conference, become a permanent Security Council member, and share responsibility over liberated areas. Agreement was reached on Yugoslavia.

The conference concerned only the European war. In Malta, combined British and American staffs planned increased attacks against Japan. The speaker warns that the war against Japan is not won; a long, costly struggle remains, and unconditional surrender of Japan is essential, with Japanese militarism to be wiped out as thoroughly as German militarism.

On his return, he met with King Farouk, Emperor Haile Selassie, and King Ibn Saud, gaining valuable face-to-face exchanges. He praises the armed forces and stresses that the conference was a turning point. The nation must choose between world collaboration or another conflict. The groundwork of a plan for peace has been laid, though no plan is perfect and will need amendment. Peace requires insistence, work, and sacrifice. The conference sought to end unilateral action, exclusive alliances, spheres of influence, and balances of power, substituting a universal organization for all peace-loving nations. He expresses confidence that Congress and the American people will accept the results as the beginning of a permanent structure of peace.

The instructor previews upcoming course logistics: a short problem set due next Tuesday, a closed-book quiz a week from Thursday covering statistical basics through statistical process control and control charting, with one page of notes and a calculator allowed, and statistics tables provided. The lecture reviews the relationship between hypothesis tests and control charts. A control chart is a running hypothesis test assuming a Gaussian distribution under the null hypothesis. Control limits are set based on a chosen false alarm probability (alpha), with the average run length for false alarms (ARL₀) defined as 1/alpha. When a process mean shifts (alternative hypothesis), the probability of a missed alarm (beta) arises. The average run length to detect a shift (ARL₁) is 1/(1−beta). Changing sample size n alters beta and the control limits but not alpha, which is set a priori. Increasing n tightens the sampling distributions, reduces beta, and moves control limits closer together to maintain the same alpha. Operating curves relate sample size, shift size, and beta or ARL₁.

A single alarm point cannot distinguish a false alarm from a true alarm; investigation is required. Common practice includes checking measurement equipment first, examining historical data for trends, and consulting operators. Some users wait for a second consecutive alarm to reduce the effective false alarm rate.

Process capability is introduced, distinguishing control limits from specification limits. When a process is in control, its mean and variance characterize it. Tolerances define upper and lower spec limits; parts within are conforming. A quality loss function, often quadratic, penalizes deviation from a target, encouraging both mean centering and variance reduction. The process capability ratio CP equals (USL−LSL)/(6σ). CPK is the minimum of (USL−μ)/(3σ) and (μ−LSL)/(3σ), accounting for off-target means. Examples illustrate CP and CPK values: CP=1, CPK=1 when centered with spread equal to spec width; CP=1, CPK=0 when off-center; CP=2, CPK=1 with tighter spread but off-center; CP=2, CPK=2 when centered. CPK values correspond to nonconforming part probabilities: CPK≈1 gives ~1 in 1,000; CPK≈1.33 gives ~4σ; CPK≈1.67 gives ~5σ; CPK=2 gives ~6σ (parts per billion). A six-sigma capability provides robustness against mean shifts, e.g., a 2σ shift still leaves 4σ to the spec limit (~32 ppm nonconforming). The expected quality loss function separates variance and mistargeting contributions.

The lecture concludes with a preview of alternative control charts for situations with sample size one or continuous measurement, such as moving average, exponentially weighted moving average, and cumulative sum charts, which aim to detect small shifts more rapidly. Autocorrelation and sampling time considerations are noted.

Drug repurposing identifies new therapeutic uses for existing drugs, reducing development time and cost, and accounts for about one-third of drug approvals. Elsevier’s Biology Knowledge Graph (EBKG) is built from both open access (OA) and controlled access (CA) literature using proprietary NLP. The study compared OA and CA contributions to relations relevant to drug repurposing for rare diseases and drug-target interactions. OA and CA contributions are roughly equal at the relation level, though CA has more asserted statements. The OA share has grown since 2006, now exceeding 50% for rare disease relations. Rare diseases with many relations tend to have a majority in OA, but drug-target relations show no such bias. Most relations in both OA and CA are supported by a single reference; relations with four or more references are almost entirely OA. The absolute number of CA-only relations continues to grow, but the fraction declines as OA grows faster. There is no difference in citation rate or time to first citation between OA and CA. Single-reference relations are accumulating exponentially in both corpora, with 85% from peer-reviewed literature. The yearly proportion of uncited relations declined until 2000 and then stabilized. Retracted articles are more common in CA journals. Uncited relations predominantly originate from original research articles. The findings indicate that half of all knowledge graph relations are uncited, equally distributed between OA and CA, and additional confidence measures beyond reference counts are needed.

The PGA848 is a monolithic, high-voltage, high-bandwidth, precision programmable gain instrumentation amplifier with a single-ended output. It combines a high-speed current-feedback input stage with an internally matched gain resistor network and a four-resistor differential amplifier output stage. Eight binary-gain settings from 0.5V/V to 100V/V are selected via digital pins A0, A1, and A2. It is designed for factory automation, analog input modules, data acquisition, test and measurement, and semiconductor test.

The linear operating input voltage range extends within 3V of either power supply, maintaining excellent common-mode rejection. The valid common-mode range depends on input common-mode voltage, differential voltage, gain, and reference input voltage.

A typical application drives a single-ended input SAR ADC (ADS8860). The circuit accepts single-ended or differential input signals, with independent input and output power supplies: ±15V for the input stage and a unipolar 5.3V supply for the output stage, shared with the ADC supply. The REF6250 provides a 5V reference for the ADC. The PGA848 REF pin is set to the ADC midscale voltage (2.5V) using a precision resistive divider buffered by an OPA192 op amp. Three filters are used: an input EMI/RFI filter, a CFB capacitor (75pF) in parallel with the internal 6.67kΩ feedback resistors (nominal cutoff 318kHz), and a charge reservoir filter at the ADC inputs. The overall front-end provides a nominal –3dB bandwidth of 318kHz and –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. The OPA192 buffer uses a dual-feedback configuration with RISO=20Ω, RF=2kΩ, CF=2nF for stability, achieving 86° phase margin.

Power supply recommendations: nominal performance is specified with ±15V input-stage and output-stage supplies, with VICM and VREF at mid-supply. Output-stage supplies are clamped to stay within input-stage supply levels. Supply voltages higher than 40V (±20V) can permanently damage the device.

Layout guidelines include symmetrical input paths, low-ESR 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitors close to supply pins, routing input traces away from supply/output traces, minimizing leakage and parasitic capacitance on DA_IN+ and DA_IN– pins, and keeping distance from thermal sources.

This study investigates the oxidation of pure tungsten (W) in dry air at temperatures from 400°C to 1050°C, and the sublimation of WO₃ powder, to assess degradation relevant to fusion reactor plasma-facing components. Oxidation kinetics transition from parabolic (diffusion-controlled) to linear (surface-reaction-controlled) regimes. Activation energies are 180.4 ± 3.8 kJ/mol for parabolic and 117.5 ± 3.3 kJ/mol for linear oxidation. Sublimation of WO₃ exhibits an activation energy of 335.8 ± 17 kJ/mol. Specimen geometry affects linear oxidation rates: higher perimeter-to-area ratios increase measured rates due to preferential oxidation at edges, where oxide is brittle and spalls easily. Oxide scale microstructure, characterized by XRD, Raman spectroscopy, and SEM, consists of a thin inner WO₂ layer (~30–50 nm), a middle WO₂.₇₂ layer (10–20 µm), and an outer layer of WO₂.₉/WO₃ phases. The WO₂.₇₂ layer remains dense and does not thicken beyond ~20 µm, while the outer layer develops voids and cracks. Cracking is linked to Pilling-Bedworth ratio stresses and thermal expansion mismatch, and is more prevalent in thicker WO₃ regions. Grain orientation influences oxidation rate, with {100} planes oxidizing faster, and cavity formation aligns with grain boundaries between differently oriented grains. The presence of a WO₂ layer may explain low detritiation efficiency observed in JET tungsten tiles, as WO₂ is predicted to act as a tritium permeation barrier. These findings inform dust generation, oxide spalling, and detritiation challenges for fusion device maintenance, accident scenarios, and waste handling.

Disclosed are systems and methods for adapting radiotherapy treatment plans using biological and/or physiological data extracted from real-time imaging (e.g., PET, MRI, SPECT). Biological data may include tracer uptake values (SUV), PET tracer kinetics, tissue metabolism, oxygenation, genetic expression (e.g., HER2), blood flow, and morphological changes. Treatment plan updates may modify dosimetric objectives, target geometry, fractionation patterns, number or duration of sessions, and dose distributions. Methods also evaluate treatment plans by comparing real-time data to pre-approved ranges, using plan quality indices (PQI) and dose-volume histograms (DVH). Bounded DVH curves can be generated by simulating shifts of a patient target volume within a radiation-firing zone and calculating dose families. Notifications (e.g., PASS/GO, FAIL/NO GO) indicate whether to proceed, adapt, or terminate treatment. Adaptive radiotherapy may be online (plan updated at session start), real-time (continuously updated during treatment), or offline (updated between sessions based on prior session data).

Among surveyed pharmacies, 40% of pharmacists reported EPT awareness. Awareness was significantly associated with willingness to dispense nameless prescriptions (48% vs. 18% for unaware pharmacists). Overall willingness to dispense nameless EPT was 30%. Neighborhood socioeconomic vulnerability was not associated with willingness to dispense. Among pharmacists willing to dispense, 28% used the name "Expedited Partner," 34% used double prescriptions or refills under the index patient, and 6% required the partner's name; 31% were unwilling or terminated the call. Common refusal reasons were unfamiliarity with EPT (62%) and belief a patient name was legally required (28%). Only 46% of fillable prescriptions adhered to New York State guidelines. Insurance was usable in 86% of potentially fillable prescriptions.

Logistic regression showed national chain pharmacies had higher EPT awareness (aOR 2.58) compared to non-chains. Higher SVI quartiles were positively associated with EPT awareness (aORs 2.62, 3.53, 3.74 for second, third, and fourth quartiles vs. lowest). Chlamydia incidence rates were not significantly associated with awareness or willingness. No significant associations were found for willingness to fill EPT prescriptions by pharmacy type, chlamydia rate, or SVI quartile.

The study concludes that pharmacist awareness of EPT is limited, willingness to dispense nameless prescriptions is low, and adherence to state guidelines is suboptimal. Higher socioeconomic vulnerability was unexpectedly associated with greater awareness but not with willingness to fill. Barriers include unfamiliarity, legal misconceptions, and lack of pharmacy-level resources. The findings highlight the need for targeted education, policy interventions, and integration of electronic prescribing to improve EPT access.

The present disclosure provides a machine learning model scaling (MLMS) system that selects and interchanges ML models (subnets) in an energy- and communication-efficient manner while adapting to real-time changes in system constraints. The MLMS system includes an MLMS engine with an MLMS interface (MLMSI) for user configuration, a subnet selector, and a performance auditor. A user supplies an ML configuration containing a supernet (an overparameterized model from which subnets are derived), application quality metrics, system constraints, and performance auditor settings. The performance auditor monitors context information—mode of operation, system state, physical environment, and networking environment—and triggers a subnet search when a status change is detected. The subnet selector performs a search (e.g., using NAS or multi-objective evolutionary algorithms) to find candidate subnets that meet performance and new hardware constraints. An energy-efficient swap strategy then selects the replacement subnet with the greatest overlap in pre-trained parameters relative to the currently deployed subnet, minimizing memory write overhead. This is accomplished by vectorizing subnet configurations and computing transfer costs. The algorithm first identifies candidate subnets with similar performance and that satisfy additional constraints, then chooses the one with minimal data transfer cost. The MLMS system is agnostic to the specific search method and weight-sharing approach. Use cases include IoT devices, drones, edge computing, and federated learning, where the system adapts models to changing power, environmental, or hardware conditions. The passage also provides background on AI/ML, neural networks, and example hardware architectures.

Market Basket, a New England supermarket chain founded in 1917, grew under family leadership. A feud between the families of brothers George and Mike Demoulas led to a 1990s lawsuit granting George’s side, led by Arthur S., a 50.5% stake. Mike’s son, Arthur T., became CEO in 2008, running a low-price, high-volume, no-debt model with profit-sharing, bonuses, promotion from within, and strong customer and supplier relationships. By 2014, the company had 71 stores, 25,000 non-unionized employees, and $4.6 billion in revenue.

In 2013, a board shift gave control to Arthur S.’s side. The board curtailed Arthur T.’s authority, then fired him and two senior executives in June 2014, appointing interim co-CEOs. Headquarters and warehouse employees, truck drivers, and store workers staged a six-week walkout and boycott demanding Arthur T.’s reinstatement. Customers and vendors supported the protest, causing sales to drop over 90%. The board fired some protest leaders, and return-to-work ultimatums were ignored.

On August 27, 2014, Arthur T. and his family agreed to buy the 50.5% stake for $1.6 billion, financed with debt. Arthur T. was reinstated with full operational authority. Operations quickly resumed, and employees received bonuses. The company now faced significant debt, raising questions about its ability to maintain low prices, high wages, and growth.

The Stack Offense compacts players into two stack alignments near the free throw line, using three ball handlers and two stationary screeners. On penetration, ballhandler pops off post screen. O1 penetrates, O2 pops off O4; if stopped, passes to O2, stacks below O4. O2 penetrates wing, O3 pops off O5. If overplayed, back cut; if defender anticipates pop, O2 rolls; if post defender shows, O4 rolls. Drive; baseline drive, drop pass. If passing lane overplayed, back cut; O4 may screen. O1 feeds cutter or O4 stepping out; if not, pass to O4, return. O2, O4 re-establish stack, O1 penetrates a wing.

Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved over 27% power conversion efficiency, but performance and stability depend on thin-film morphology. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is used to analyze grain boundaries, defects, and residual lead(II) iodide, but manual interpretation is labor-intensive and subjective. To address this, the authors introduce PerovSegNet, a lightweight segmentation framework built on YOLOv8-seg, tailored for SEM images of perovskite and lead iodide films. It incorporates two novel modules: Adaptive Split-Dilated Convolution with Shuffle Block (ASDCB) for multi-scale feature fusion via dilated convolutions and attention-based channel recalibration, and Separable Adaptive Downsampling module (SAD) for capturing fine-scale textures and large-scale structures. A dataset, PerovData, was constructed from 40 manually labeled SEM images augmented to 10,994 images. UMAP analysis confirmed class separability among perovskite, lead iodide, and defects. PerovSegNet achieved state-of-the-art segmentation accuracy: mAP@0.5 of 87.25% and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 79.96%, outperforming Mask R-CNN variants and Cascade InternImage-XL, while reducing parameters and GFLOPs by 24% and 25% compared to the YOLOv8x-seg baseline. Ablation studies showed both modules improved performance, especially for defect segmentation (accuracy rose from 33% to 64%). Qualitative evaluation demonstrated sharper boundaries and fewer missed detections. The framework also enables automated quantification of grain area and count, and correlation analysis on literature data linked perovskite area positively (r=0.78) and defect count negatively (r=-0.32) with power conversion efficiency, suggesting potential for data-driven process optimization. Limitations include observational correlations, class imbalance, and need for further acceleration for inline use.

The article demonstrates backtesting a momentum trading strategy in Python. Momentum is an investing factor that aims to benefit from ongoing trends. The passage discusses skinimalism, a skincare trend emphasizing a streamlined routine with only essential products. Dr. Hazel Parkinson, a GP, describes it as simplifying to a few high-quality items that serve the skin’s needs, embracing natural texture and long-term support rather than multi-step routines with potentially clashing active ingredients. Skinimalism focuses on targeted, multitasking products that respect the skin barrier. Benefits include protecting the skin barrier, reducing irritation and sensitivity, especially for sensitive or aging skin that is thinner and drier. It may also enhance wellbeing by reducing overwhelm from social media and marketing, and it is more sustainable with less waste and lower cost. However, skinimalism is not for everyone. People with acne or pigmentation may still need specific ingredients like retinoids or azelaic acid, but without extra steps. For acne, a gentle cleanser, non-comedogenic moisturizer, and a targeted active are recommended. Eczema-prone skin benefits from a minimalist routine prioritizing barrier repair with fragrance-free emollients and ceramide-rich moisturizers. Rosacea requires a minimal routine with soothing cleanser, anti-inflammatory moisturizer, SPF, and a calming active. Hyperpigmentation should be treated with consistent use of a well-chosen active plus daily SPF. Menopausal skin may need richer moisturizers and actives like vitamin C or retinoids, with thoughtful layering. For healthy skin, one can add a retinoid or exfoliant 1–2 times weekly, focusing on individual needs. Transitioning involves eliminating products gradually over 2–4 weeks. The text then introduces upcoming content on foods and nutrients for healthy skin and coconut oil for hair. It ends with site information: the page is peer reviewed by clinicians, invites sharing thoughts in a community, states that community views are not medical advice, and offers a symptom checker.

The Evening Star is a bearish reversal candlestick pattern used in technical analysis. It consists of three candles: a tall bullish candle, a small candle that gaps above the first, and a bearish candle that closes below the midpoint of the first candle. The pattern forms during an upward price swing and signals a potential price reversal. Its reliability increases when the gap between the first and second candles is significant and the third candle is longer than the first. Traders often confirm the pattern with trendlines, resistance levels, and momentum oscillators. Exit methods may include profit targets, technical indicators, or stop-loss orders. Success depends on accurate identification, confirmation, and a solid risk management plan; the pattern does not guarantee market movement.

Backtesting the Evening Star requires specific rules. All 75 candlestick patterns have been defined and backtested, with code available for Amibroker or Tradestation. Benefits include profiting from potential downtrends. Risks include false signals, market volatility, over-reliance on technical analysis, lack of diversification, and losses without proper risk management. Timeframes vary based on trading style and risk tolerance. The strategy can be adjusted for different market conditions by remaining flexible. Indicators such as RSI, stochastic oscillator, and Bollinger Bands can complement the pattern. An AAPL chart example showed profitable trades using a stop loss above the pattern and a profit target at the next support level. The article also outlines pros and cons, key components, rules, guidelines, tips, and strategies, though specific lists are not provided.

US public education historically adopted business practices, such as bureaucratic structures and IQ-based categorization, to organize schools and supply skilled workers. The 1983 report *A Nation at Risk* prompted efforts to professionalize teaching through standards and certification, but this did not improve teacher pay or student test scores. The 2001 No Child Left Behind Act introduced business-like accountability, requiring standardized testing, annual yearly progress (AYP), and sanctions for failing schools, including conversion to charter schools. Charter schools produced mixed results, increased segregation, drained high-performing students from public schools, and yielded no widespread academic gains.

The medical model, rooted in eugenic beliefs, assumes learning success depends on innate biological traits and uses diagnosis to identify defects. This can foster fixed mindsets, stigma, and stereotype threat, which impair academic performance and psychological adjustment in students with diagnosed learning disabilities. Reframing diagnosis as self-discovery and problem-solving can mitigate these effects.

Problem-solving is defined as an agent’s interaction with its environment to minimize error and maintain homeostasis, observed across biological scales and in computational systems. Human problem-solving relies on explanation and error correction. Children naturally exhibit a scientific method-like process of theory, exploration, and explanation, supporting the child scientist theory. Perception itself is constructed through predictive heuristics developed via environmental interaction. Metacognition, analogous to teaching and peer review, enables reflection and improved learning. Declines in student performance are linked to reduced metacognitive support.

Education should be restructured around a recursive problem-solving model based on the scientific method, applied at student, teacher, and administrative levels. All students would receive mentors to foster self-directed learning, with progress assessed against personal goals rather than norms. This approach aims to replace business-modeled systems, empowering students to become self-regulated learners.

A single case study examined the effect of anti-seizure medication (ASM) changes and seizures on smartphone touchscreen interactions in a man in his late twenties with refractory right temporal lobe epilepsy. He used the TapCounter app for six months, recording over 718,000 interactions. During a five-day epilepsy monitoring unit admission with video-EEG, ASMs (lamotrigine and perampanel) were tapered and withdrawn. Touchscreen data were analyzed using joint-interval distributions (JIDs) of inter-touch intervals. Cluster-based permutation tests compared pre-tapering, tapering, and post-tapering periods, and the day of a focal to bilateral tonic-clonic convulsion versus three preceding days. Results showed significant differences: ASM tapering increased the probability of fast next-interval dynamics, which reversed after medication restart. The convulsion day showed increased probability of slow next-interval dynamics, likely reflecting post-ictal effects. The authors suggest smartphones can track medication- and seizure-related behavioural changes unobtrusively, but note the need for cohort studies to generalize findings.

The study investigates chemical etching of Cd1-xZnxTe1-ySey (CZTS) crystals with varying selenium content (y = 0, 0.02, 0.06, 0.1) using a 5% bromine-methanol solution. Cutting and mechanical polishing produce a damaged surface layer that must be removed to achieve detector properties. Etching trajectories and average rates were determined. A sharp decrease in etching rate (approximately 20%) was observed even at low selenium concentration (y ≈ 0.02) compared to CZT (y = 0), providing direct evidence of crystal matrix hardening. This effect is explained by a thermodynamic model relating the etching rate reduction to the negative excess Gibbs energy of CZTS formation. With increasing selenium content, the etching rate continues to decrease, but the differences between higher-selenium samples diminish. Factors such as temperature, stirring, surface roughness, and the presence of the damaged layer influence etching dynamics. The findings are relevant for optimizing processing methods for CZTS-based semiconductor detectors.

Germany has a population of about 83.2 million, with 72.3 million native Germans and 10.9 million immigrants, and a high urbanization rate. Its education system originated with Prussian mandatory schooling in the 19th century, later standardized under Nazi rule, and after World War II West Germany adopted a three-tiered secondary system: Hauptschule (vocational), Realschule, and Gymnasium (university preparation). East Germany had a free, unified system, but after reunification the three-tier model became the norm, with education governed by individual states.

Special education schools (Hilfsschulen) emerged in the 1920s to prepare students with disabilities for low-wage vocational roles. The Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Culture (KMK) later established specialized schools for specific disability categories. Currently, about 577,000 students attend one of seven special school types, while inclusion in general schools remains limited: 33.6% of children with disabilities are included in elementary and 14.9% in secondary schools. Students with mild disabilities may attend general schools, but those with severe disabilities often go to Sonderschule. Mobile Special Education Services provide support in some schools. Qualification for special education involves evaluation and an individualized plan.

Teacher training involves a two-phase model: university studies (bachelor’s and master’s) followed by a paid, two-year in-school induction (Referendariat). Special education teachers receive more pedagogy and behavior management training and typically work in Hauptschule or Realschule, rarely in Gymnasium.

Laws such as the General Equal Treatment Act (2006) and the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (2008) promoted inclusion. Some states, like North Rhine-Westphalia, passed laws merging or closing special schools. Current challenges include balancing inclusion with specialized settings, unstable funding, teacher attitudes affecting social integration, negative perceptions of MTSS/RTI implementation, and the fact that about half of included secondary students attend Hauptschule, which offers limited job opportunities.
