This study investigates the similarity between mammographic density predictions from deep learning models on standard dose and low dose (approximately 10% radiation) mammograms, using the ALDRAM dataset of paired images from women aged 30–45 and models trained on the PROCAS dataset (standard dose and simulated low dose images). Two ResNet-18 models were trained for each dose level, and predictions were compared. Averaging predictions across CC and MLO views and across multiple trained models improved similarity between standard and low dose predictions. No significant effect of patient age or variation in actual dose ratio was found. Larger absolute differences between standard and low dose predictions were associated with higher mammographic density and smaller breast area; low dose models tended to predict lower density than standard dose models at small breast areas. Differences between CC and MLO predictions on low dose images and large differences between separate low dose model predictions were also indicative of greater standard–low dose variation. The distribution of absolute differences showed no notable outliers. The results indicate that low dose mammography can yield density predictions highly similar to standard dose, particularly when averaging views and models, but systematic differences remain, especially for dense breasts and small breast area.

The passage introduces GroceryDB, an open-source database of over 50,000 food products from Walmart, Target, and Whole Foods, analyzed using a machine learning-based Food Processing Score (FPro). FPro translates nutrient concentrations from nutrition facts into a continuous index (0 to 1) indicating degree of processing. The distribution of FPro scores across stores shows that minimally-processed items are a small fraction, with Whole Foods offering more minimally-processed and fewer ultra-processed items compared to Target and Walmart. FPro variability differs by food category; some categories like cereals and snack bars show wide ranges, while others like jerky and chips have limited processing choices. Comparison with USDA databases suggests GroceryDB provides a representative sample of the food supply.

Analysis reveals that a 10% increase in FPro is associated with an 8.7% average decrease in price per calorie, though this relationship varies by category. For example, soups and stews show a 24.3% decrease, while milk and milk substitutes show an increasing trend. Ingredient lists are organized into trees, and an Ingredient Processing Score (IgFPro) ranks ingredients by their contribution to ultra-processing. Additives like sodium tripolyphosphate and corn syrup have high IgFPro, while xanthan gum and guar gum have lower scores. Oils such as olive oil and flax seed oil are associated with lower processing, whereas palm oil and vegetable oil blends signal ultra-processing.

The continuous FPro score captures variability that categorical classification systems miss, enabling detailed analyses of processing distributions and price relationships. GroceryDB and the accompanying TrueFood platform aim to help consumers make informed substitutions and support public health initiatives. Limitations include reliance on nutrition facts alone, which may miss matrix-level changes, and the need for more comprehensive chemical data.

Tecomaria capensis (Cape Honeysuckle) is a scrambling shrub or small tree up to 6 m, with compound leaves and orange-red trumpet-shaped flowers. It has lighter orange and pale yellow varieties. Conservation status: Least Concern. It occurs in thicket and forest margins in southern and eastern South Africa and tropical Africa. It is browsed by game, visited by sunbirds, butterflies, and bees, and hosts hawkmoth larvae. Traditional uses: treating fever, pain, sleeplessness, chest ailments, dysentery, and promoting milk flow. Nursing mothers wear isixhoxho necklets made from its wood, carved into pendants with blue and white beads, as a status symbol at social functions. Growing: well-drained soil, compost, mulch, regular water until established, prune in late winter.

The lecture examines the economics of spam and security, shifting from technical aspects to why attackers compromise systems. While some attacks are ideological, many have strong economic motivations. Spam persists because sending it is extremely cheap and even very low conversion rates can yield profit. The spam ecosystem is divided into advertising (getting users to click links), click support (DNS and web server infrastructure to present spam sites), and realization (payment and delivery of goods).

For advertising, sending a million spam messages costs about $60. Empirical studies show massive drop-offs: out of 350 million messages, only about 10,000 clicks and 28 purchase attempts occurred. Defenses like IP blacklists, micropayments, computational puzzles, and CAPTCHAs have limitations. Attackers circumvent them using botnets (costing roughly $0.10 per U.S. host, $0.01 in Asia), compromised webmail accounts ($0.01–$0.05 per account), and IP address hijacking. CAPTCHAs are defeated by outsourcing to cheap human labor or services like Mechanical Turk at about $0.001 per solve.

Click support involves registering domains, running DNS and web servers, and often using redirection sites or botnets as servers. Affiliate programs handle back-end tasks and are decentralized, making takedowns difficult. Only a few registrars host domains for many affiliates, but there is no single choke point at this layer.

Realization involves payment processing through a chain: customer, merchant, payment processor, acquiring bank, association network (e.g., Visa), and issuing bank. Spammers properly classify transactions and actually ship goods to avoid high fines for misclassification or excessive chargebacks (threshold around 1%). Only about 30 acquiring banks were observed over two years, presenting a potential financial choke point. After the paper’s publication, Visa classified pharmaceutical sales as high-risk and tightened operating guidelines to explicitly forbid illegal sales, leading to some impact. The researchers addressed ethical considerations, noting they made test purchases and destroyed the goods. The lecture also notes that some companies now engage in “hackbacks,” using legal arguments like trademark infringement to take down botnets.

After a remand from the Third Circuit, the court scheduled a retrial for Willie Tyler on obstruction of justice charges. Tyler moved to dismiss the indictment on Confrontation Clause, Double Jeopardy, and Due Process grounds. The court denied all motions.

On the Confrontation Clause claim, Tyler argued that a hearsay statement by the victim to a detective was inadmissible under Crawford. The court found the statement would not be offered for its truth but to show the victim would have communicated with a federal officer, and the Third Circuit had previously held it was a verbal act, not hearsay.

On double jeopardy, Tyler argued that a prior state prosecution and the vacatur of his convictions barred retrial. The court held that dual sovereignty permits federal prosecution after a state trial, and the vacatur resulted from legal error, not insufficient evidence, so retrial is not barred.

On due process, Tyler alleged outrageous government conduct: that the prosecutor prompted a witness to falsely claim DEA adviser status, and that the government suppressed exculpatory evidence in violation of Brady. The court found no evidence the adviser testimony was fabricated, and Tyler failed to show prejudice or willful misconduct regarding the undisclosed statement.

Hurricane Helene’s unprecedented flooding in September 2024 severely damaged four school buildings in western North Carolina. In Henderson County, Atkinson Elementary took on two inches of water; after floor replacements, students returned from the Boys & Girls Club in December 2024. Mitigation includes increased vegetation, drainage fixes, and sturdier flooring. In McDowell County, Old Fort Elementary flooded and closed for repairs until the 2025-26 school year, with students merging into another school. Upgrades included new flooring, doors, and higher-installed HVAC units, and students returned August 25, 2025. In Watauga County, 70% of Valle Crucis School flooded, displacing students to three community institutions for the remainder of 2024-25. A new school under construction was delayed by an overstretched workforce; the historic rock facade may be saved pending FEMA/insurance. In Yancey County, Micaville Elementary closed permanently, with students moved to Burnsville Elementary and classroom expansions underway. Communication relied on local radio, and Starlink and bus radios are now in place. Infrastructure concerns persist, and the high school served as an emergency command center.

The Volvo was in self-driving mode with a human backup driver when it hit 49-year-old Elaine Herzberg as she walked a bicycle outside a crosswalk. She died at a hospital. Uber suspended all road-testing in Phoenix, Pittsburgh, San Francisco, and Toronto. The CEO expressed condolences and is cooperating with investigators. The NTSB and NHTSA sent investigators. Police said the vehicle was traveling about 40 mph and hit Herzberg immediately as she stepped onto the street; neither she nor the backup driver showed impairment. No fault determination has been made. Expert Bryant Walker Smith said the fatality could harm the technology's image and prompt more state and federal regulations. The article notes a prior 2017 Uber test vehicle crash in Tempe without serious injuries, and a 2016 Tesla Autopilot fatality where driver inattention and design limitations were factors. Federal autonomous vehicle guidelines are voluntary, with states like Arizona taking a hands-off approach and California requiring incident reports. A safety advocate sent a letter to the Transportation Secretary concerned about oversight, and said the crash should remind Congress to craft legislation to prevent future tragedies.

Operation Mongoose (1961-1962), a covert program to overthrow Castro, was run by a Special Group (Augmented) with Lansdale as operations chief and CIA handling military, sabotage, propaganda. In 1964, the Special Group 5412 became the 303 Committee under Bundy. The Special Group and 303 Committee approved covert actions under Kennedy and Johnson. The Church Committee found only 14% of CIA projects were reviewed case-by-case. The 303 Committee could alter or reject CIA proposals; State Department objections could modify or nullify them. In 1969, Nixon required annual reviews and automatic termination after 12 months. In 1970, NSDM 40 created the 40 Committee, adding the Attorney General, and required DCI policy approval for major covert operations and annual reviews. The 40 Committee's formal meetings declined; it reviewed about 25% of CIA projects, focusing on major ones. Nixon in 1970 ordered a coup in Chile without Committee approval. The 1974 Hughes-Ryan amendment required presidential findings and congressional notification for each covert action.

The professor, Hong, a theoretical physicist, introduces the quantum field theory (QFT) course. The goal is to develop concepts, formalism, and techniques for quantum dynamics of fields, culminating in quantum electrodynamics. QFT describes three of four fundamental interactions, is used for quantum gravity, and has applications across physics, serving as a universal language. The course is the first of a three-semester sequence, focusing on fundamental concepts; it can be standalone for experimentalists. The outline is a rough roadmap.

QFT has a reputation for difficulty, but the professor argues it is not difficult if learned correctly. The difficulty is conceptual, not computational. Intuition is built through examples, as in quantum mechanics. Three pieces of advice: (1) QFT is quantum mechanics with infinite degrees of freedom; many difficulties arise from gaps in quantum mechanics understanding (e.g., Heisenberg picture). (2) Formalisms were designed to solve concrete physical problems; understanding those problems aids comprehension. (3) Intuition develops through experience; after problem sets, reflect on what was learned. Most learning occurs outside class; lectures provide guidance. Notations in lectures differ from textbooks like Peskin and Weinberg.

Chapter 1 discusses why QFT is considered, starting with classical field theories and the principle of locality. Locality states that physical effects propagate point-to-point, with no action at a distance. Fields are the mathematical device realizing locality, associating dynamical variables with each point in space. Maxwell's equations and Einstein's general relativity are local equations, involving only fields and finite derivatives at the same point. Fields can be scalar, vector, tensor, or spinor. Notation conventions are set: mu runs 0-3, x is a four-vector, spatial vector x, c=1, hbar=1.

The action principle for classical fields generalizes classical mechanics. The action is the time integral of the Lagrangian, which is the spatial integral of a Lagrangian density L that depends locally on fields and their first derivatives. Only first time derivatives are allowed to keep equations of motion second order in time. Canonical momentum density and Hamiltonian density are defined analogously. The equation of motion from extremizing the action is partial L / partial phi_a - partial_mu (partial L / partial (partial_mu phi_a)) = 0, assuming vanishing boundary terms. For simplicity, translational and Lorentz invariance are assumed.

Examples include Maxwell theory, Einstein gravity, and scalar field theories. The simplest is a real scalar field with action S = integral d^4x ( -1/2 partial_mu phi partial^mu phi - V(phi) ). The momentum density is pi = phi_dot, and the Hamiltonian density is 1/2 pi^2 + 1/2 (nabla phi)^2 + V(phi). The equation of motion is partial^2 phi + V'(phi) = 0. The simplest V(phi) cases: a linear term gives an external force; a quadratic term 1/2 m^2 phi^2 yields the Klein-Gordon equation (partial^2 + m^2) phi = 0. Higher-order terms lead to nonlinear equations.

A CNN article reports on the ages at which children around the world receive their first cell phones. Sara Zaske's daughter Sophia had no phone in Germany, where few classmates owned one, but in the US she was the only fourth-grader without a smartphone. Zaske plans to give her a flip phone next year and delay a smartphone until high school. Studies show: In Europe, 46% of children aged 9-16 owned a smartphone (2015 study); children were sensitive to costs, using Wi-Fi and switching off mobile data. In Italy and the UK, smartphone use was restricted at school, while in Denmark they were used for class activities. In the US, 45% of 10-12 year olds had a smartphone with a service plan (Nielsen report), and 42% of children 8 and under had tablets (Common Sense Media). In South Korea, 72% of 11-12 year olds owned a smartphone, spending 5.4 hours/day. In Taiwan, cell phone use rose from 45% of 11-year-olds to 71% of 15-year-olds. In Turkey, 19.5% of parents said the optimal age was 6-11, 59.8% said 12-17, and 3.3% said no need until 18. In South Africa, 81% of secondary students owned or had access to a mobile phone. In Ghana, 18.8% of boys and 12.9% of girls owned a mobile phone; in Malawi, 10.4% of boys and 6.2% of girls. In Australia, the median age for first mobile phone was 8, with ownership rising from 31% to 43% in a year. The American Academy of Pediatrics states there is no "right" age, and recommends no digital media for children under 18-24 months except video-chatting, limiting screen time to one hour per day for ages 2-5, avoiding screens one hour before bedtime, keeping meal times screen-free, monitoring content, and not using media as the only way to calm a child.

This paper introduces a quantum algorithmic framework for generalized linear model (GLM) sparsification, targeting a broad class of regression problems. The framework replaces a large dataset with a much smaller weighted subset (a sparsifier) that approximately preserves the total loss for all candidate solutions, enabling efficient approximate optimization. The core technical contribution is a quantum algorithm for computing multiscale leverage score overestimates (MLSO), which serve as importance scores for sampling. The algorithm, QMLSO, builds on quantum leverage score approximation and iteratively refines weights across multiple scales, starting from an initial coarse weight estimate. A quantum initialization procedure constructs a suitable starting weight by modifying loss functions.

The main result is a quantum algorithm (QGLMSparsify) that, given query access to the data matrix and a family of proper loss functions, constructs an ε-approximate sparsifier of size Õ(n/ε²) with high probability. Its runtime is Õ((r√(mn)/ε + n^ω + nr²) · log(smax/smin)), where r is row sparsity, m is the number of data points, n is dimension, and smax, smin define the range of loss values. This achieves a quadratic speedup in m over the fastest classical algorithms. The sparsifier is built by quantum importance sampling: preparing many copies of a quantum state with amplitudes proportional to MLSO values, and using quantum sum estimation to determine reweighting.

The framework applies to loss functions that are L-auto-Lipschitz and lower θ-homogeneous (pL, θ, cq-proper), which includes ℓp loss (p ∈ (0,2]) and γp loss (including Huber). As a result, quantum speedups are obtained for linear regression, multiple regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, Huber regression, ℓp regression, and γp regression. For linear, multiple, and ridge regression, the algorithm also subsumes prior quantum results. The work focuses on approximately minimizing the loss function, not on statistical estimation from random samples.

Digital Foundry's analysis of Monster Hunter World across PS4, Xbox One, PS4 Pro, and Xbox One X found shared strengths including detailed monster and character models, high-resolution textures, and good shadows. Weaknesses include reduced visual contrast producing a flat, washed-out image, barely noticeable HDR, frequent clipping, missing collision detection, and poor motion blur.

On base consoles, PS4 runs at 1080p, Xbox One at 864p, both with uncapped frame rates often below 30 fps; Xbox One performs worse with lower frame rates and ragged frame times.

On PS4 Pro and Xbox One X, three modes are available. In Resolution mode, Pro uses checkerboard 1800p, One X renders native 1728p with smoother edges but missing distant visual assets; Pro runs faster. In Frame-rate mode, both are 1080p, One X again lacks some assets, frame rates are uncapped (30-60 fps), with One X averaging 46 fps versus Pro's 43 fps in the Ancient Forest, and significantly higher in Astera. In Graphics mode, both are 1080p with extended LODs, missing assets appear on One X, and One X runs 6-10 fps faster than Pro.

Overall, the game is a technical disappointment, lacking optimization especially on Xbox One X, though gameplay remains enjoyable.

The Flex offense "Pick the Picker" is a screening game using strong baseline and down screens. Its continuous screening action forces defenses to handle two screen types simultaneously, and patient teams create open shots. The continuity provides offensive rebounding with two weakside rebounders. In the basic continuity, O1 passes to O2 as O5 steps to the corner; O3 uses O5's baseline screen while O1 down screens for O5. O2 can shoot, feed O3 on the baseline cut, pass to O4 in the corner, or hit O5 popping out. On ball reversal, O2 passes to O5, O1 goes to the corner, O4 comes off O3's baseline screen, and O2 down screens for O3. A corner pass leads to post isolation. Against defensive overplay, options include back cuts, weakside lobs, pump fakes, drop passes, and back door plays. Entries include the High Post Rub (O1 to O3, O5 back screens for O1), Weakside Shuffle Cut (O1 to O3, O5 back picks for O2), and Dribble Clear (O1 dribble clears O3 into a zipper action). The "Pop" variation adds a weakside double screen, allowing the corner receiver to pop to the elbow off a down screen with three options: low, high, or pop. Offensive rebounding requires anticipation, determination, and hustle rather than size and strength; players must be aggressive, anticipate misses, get inside, and avoid waiting behind.

This memorandum is a periodic update on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring from June to November 2000. Governments worldwide are opening generation markets to foreign investors, unbundling state-owned utilities, and introducing wholesale and retail competition. In Europe, the EU Directive is driving market opening, with mergers and consolidation among utilities. Central and Eastern European countries are pursuing privatization and restructuring, often linked to EU accession. In Asia-Pacific, recovering economies are resuming unbundling and restructuring plans, though independent power producers face challenges. Latin American privatizations have slowed due to currency fluctuations and ownership limits, with some countries advancing transmission privatizations. In the Middle East and Africa, governments are increasingly allowing independent power projects and considering partial privatization, while regional transmission links are being developed. The memo provides detailed country-by-country summaries for each region.

This study analyzed 24,849 patients with soft-tissue sarcomas (STS) including heart cancer from the SEER 18 registries (2000–2018), focusing on six histological subtypes: liposarcoma (LiS), giant cell sarcoma (GcS), leiomyosarcoma (LeS), myxofibrosarcoma (MyS), spindle cell sarcoma (ScS), and synovial sarcoma (SyS). The objective was to determine mortality rates and predict overall survival for different treatments and sarcoma types using nomograms.

Median age at diagnosis was 59 years; 56% were male, 82% white. At diagnosis, 12% had metastatic disease, 73% had a single primary tumor. Treatments received: surgery (82%), radiotherapy (42%), chemotherapy (19%), primary systemic therapy (14%). Median survival varied: GcS 42 months, ScS 44 months, LeS 62 months, LiS 76 months, MyS 71 months, SyS 74 months.

Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significant survival differences: MyS had the highest overall survival (75%), ScS the lowest (37%). Multivariable Cox models indicated that increasing age, male sex, non-white race, advanced cancer stage, and higher tumor grade increased mortality. Surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy significantly reduced mortality across most sarcomas; primary systemic therapy showed a contrary effect. Surgery reduced mortality by 71% in MyS (HR 0.29). Distant stage had a 3.66-fold higher hazard of death versus localized stage.

Nomograms for single-treatment modalities predicted: with chemotherapy, 5-year survival was 55% without and >80% with treatment; with surgery alone, 5- and 10-year survival exceeded 90% versus 45% and 25% without; radiotherapy alone did not significantly improve survival. In MyS, treatments yielded an 85% survival improvement; in GcS, 5-year survival was 18% (chemotherapy), 10% (radiotherapy), and 25% (surgery). Nomogram calibration showed good correlation between predicted and observed probabilities.

Limitations included absence of data on surgical margins, recurrence, radiotherapy details, some histological subtypes, and potential confounders, as well as short follow-up and need for external validation. The study concluded that surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy improved survival, while older age, male sex, non-white race, and advanced stage negatively affected survival, and MyS had better outcomes than ScS.

This lecture introduces the course 14.271 Industrial Organization, co-taught by Glenn Ellison and Tobias, with guest lectures by Jean Tirole. The course covers IO theory and empirical work, structured as 12 topics typically covered in two lectures each: theory on Wednesdays and empirical work on Mondays. IO is described as inherently theoretical because antitrust questions cannot be tested with natural experiments, but empirical IO is essential for testing model assumptions and effect sizes.

The first topic is monopoly pricing. A single-product monopolist maximizes profit by setting marginal revenue equal to marginal cost, leading to the Lerner index: (P−MC)/P = −1/elasticity of demand. Markups depend on demand elasticities, not demand levels. The standard diagram shows profit, consumer surplus, and deadweight loss. Reasons monopolies may be undesirable include deadweight loss, productive inefficiency, quality distortions, rent seeking, and equity concerns. In IO, income effects are typically ignored by assuming quasi-linear preferences.

Multiproduct monopoly pricing introduces a diversion ratio. When a monopolist sells two goods, the optimal markup for one good includes an extra term reflecting how a price change affects sales of the other good, multiplied by the other good's margin. Pricing must be considered as a system. In the substitutes case, markups exceed the single-product Lerner index. In the complements case, prices may be set below the inverse elasticity, potentially below cost (e.g., printers and ink, newspapers and ads, Google paying Apple for default search engine placement).

Product quality choice is analyzed with heterogeneous consumers whose types are uniformly distributed. The monopolist chooses quality to equate the marginal cost of quality to the marginal valuation of the marginal consumer. A social planner would equate it to the average consumer's valuation. Two distortions arise: the monopolist focuses on the marginal rather than average consumer, and the quantity sold is lower than the social optimum. In a homogeneous population model, the marginal and average consumer coincide, so the monopolist provides the socially optimal quality.

Durable goods are examined in a two-period model with forward-looking consumers. With commitment power, the monopolist sets a high price in period 1 and commits to no sales in period 2. Without commitment, any plan to walk down the demand curve is undermined because consumers anticipate price cuts. A simple model shows that if the constraint is non-binding, the optimal second-period cutoff would exceed the first-period cutoff, a contradiction. This occurs because units already planned for period 2 have zero marginal cost for period 1 sales. Thus, constant high pricing is optimal with commitment. Real-world price drops may stem from preferences for exclusivity, changing costs, or commitment problems. The Coase conjecture states that as the time between price changes shrinks to zero, a durable-goods monopolist without commitment loses all market power, with price dropping instantly to marginal cost and profits going to zero. Reasons the conjecture may not hold include infrequent price changes, inflows of new high-value customers, boundedly rational consumers, and strategic solutions like renting, most-favored-customer clauses, or capacity constraints. Skepticism about the Coase conjecture extends to some dynamic structural models.

Information design is presented as an active area in monopoly pricing. Firms control the information consumers receive. Examples contrast laptops (abundant information) with mattresses and wholesale used cars (intentionally minimal information). Intermediaries like Amazon or Yelp design information to maximize consumer surplus or their own objectives. A model illustrates a monopolist selling a product with values uniformly distributed. Under full information, the monopoly price is 2/3, selling to 1/3 of consumers. Providing no information homogenizes consumers, who then value the product at the mean; the monopolist sells to everyone at that lower price, earning higher profit by extracting all surplus but reducing social surplus. A partial information policy, where consumers are told whether their value is low, medium, or high, creates point masses that can shift the monopoly price downward. In the given example, this increases both consumer surplus and profit relative to full information. The lecture concludes by noting the next class will cover empirical papers on monopoly pricing.

The lecture presents examples of natural sandwich structures and radial density gradients as efficient mechanical designs. Iris leaves contain schlerchyma fibers at the top and bottom faces and a parenchyma foam core, behaving mechanically like a sandwich beam. Experiments on iris leaf beams applied the sandwich beam deflection equation; calculated stiffnesses were in the same order of magnitude as measured values, supporting the model. Cat tail leaves use a web-like core resembling I-beams. Other grasses similarly place dense schlerchyma fibers on the outside and parenchyma cells inside. Seakelp possesses a honeycomb-like core with gas-filled pockets for buoyancy, with faces acting as sandwich skins. Bird skulls, including those of pigeons, magpies, and long-eared owls, are sandwich structures with trabecular bone between inner and outer plates, reducing weight for flight. Owl skulls exhibit asymmetrical ear bones at different heights, which may enhance sound localization for hunting prey hidden under snow. Cuttlefish bone is a sandwich shell that controls buoyancy by regulating air in its pockets. Horseshoe crab shells and Galapagos tortoise shells also display sandwich construction. These examples illustrate how nature minimizes weight and material use through sandwich structures.

Palm stems maintain a constant diameter as they grow taller, unlike trees. They resist increasing bending loads by depositing additional cell wall layers over time, creating a radial density gradient with the densest material at the periphery. Data from Paul Rich showed that density varies with radius squared, Young’s modulus with density to the 2.5 power, and strength with density squared. A flexural rigidity analysis demonstrated that this gradient makes the stem 2.5 times stiffer than a uniform density distribution of the same mass. The bending stress distribution (proportional to radius⁶) closely matches the strength distribution (proportional to radius⁴), indicating efficient material placement. Bamboo also exhibits a similar radial density gradient.

The paper examines Temperature Scaling (TS) as a post-hoc calibration method for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) used in brain tumor classification from MRI scans, particularly under noisy imaging conditions. While CNNs achieve high accuracy, they often produce poorly calibrated probability estimates, which is problematic in healthcare. TS adjusts prediction confidences using a single temperature parameter optimized on a validation set, without altering classification accuracy. A lightweight CNN with four convolutional layers and two fully connected layers was trained on a composite dataset of T1-weighted brain MRI images from Figshare, SARTAJ, and Br35H, resized to 256×256×3 and preprocessed. The model was tested before and after TS under five synthetic noise types: Gaussian, Poisson, Salt & Pepper, Speckle, and Uniform noise, with varying parameters. Performance was measured using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL), and Expected Calibration Error (ECE). Results showed that TS consistently reduced NLL and ECE across all noise scenarios while preserving or slightly improving classification metrics. Optimal temperature values varied with noise type and level. Additional experiments with a ResNet50 architecture under selected noise parameters confirmed that TS also improved calibration for deeper models, reducing false positives and false negatives. The study concludes that TS effectively enhances model reliability in noisy medical imaging without sacrificing prediction quality, and suggests future comparisons with other calibration methods on larger datasets.

The lecture continues the proof of Cantor's theorem: for any set A, the cardinality of A is strictly smaller than that of its power set. An injection from A to its power set is given by mapping x to {x}. To show they cannot have equal cardinality, assume a bijection g: A → P(A) exists. Define B = {x ∈ A | x ∉ g(x)}. Since B ∈ P(A), surjectivity gives b ∈ A with g(b) = B. Then b ∈ g(b) implies b ∉ g(b), and b ∉ g(b) implies b ∈ g(b), a contradiction. Hence no such bijection exists, yielding an infinite hierarchy of infinite sizes.

The lecture then introduces the goal of describing the real numbers R. A theorem states there exists a unique ordered field containing Q with the least upper bound property, denoted R. The remainder of the lecture defines these terms.

An ordered set is a set S with a relation < satisfying: for all x, y ∈ S, exactly one of x = y, x < y, or y < x holds; and if x < y and y < z then x < z. Examples include the integers and rationals with their usual orders. The power set of N with the subset relation fails the first property. The dictionary order on Q × Q is an ordered set.

In an ordered set S, a subset E is bounded above if there exists b ∈ S such that x ≤ b for all x ∈ E; b is an upper bound. The least upper bound (supremum) of E is an upper bound that is ≤ every other upper bound. Lower bounds and the greatest lower bound (infimum) are defined analogously. Examples: in Z, E = {−1, 0, 2} has supremum 2 and infimum −1; in Q, E = {q ∈ Q | 0 ≤ q ≤ 1} has supremum 1 and infimum 0. Suprema and infima need not belong to E.

An ordered set S has the least upper bound property if every non-empty subset of S that is bounded above has a supremum in S. Finite sets and the negative integers (via the well-ordering of N) have this property; the integers also have it. However, Q does not. To demonstrate this, consider E = {q ∈ Q | q > 0, q² < 2}. If a supremum x ∈ Q existed, then x ≥ 1 and x² = 2. The proof begins by noting 1 ∈ E, so x ≥ 1. To show x² = 2, one first proves x² ≥ 2 by contradiction: assuming x² < 2, a positive h is defined as min(1/2, (2−x²)/(2(2x+1))). Then (x+h)² < 2, so x+h ∈ E, contradicting that x is an upper bound. Thus x² ≥ 2. The lecture ends before ruling out x² > 2.

Many schools maintain a monolingual norm, and educators often struggle to leverage translanguaging without additional training. This case study examined how two middle grades teacher candidates (TCs) in a year-long Professional Development School (PDS) experience viewed, experienced, and used translanguaging, and how their ESL-focused coursework prepared them. The TCs held asset-based views of translanguaging and felt their program provided necessary tools, but they encountered challenges in implementation. They expressed discomfort working with multilingual learners and noted a lack of translanguaging modeled by their cooperating teachers (CTs), who rarely used languages other than English. The findings revealed a theory-practice gap, as the TCs struggled to apply their coursework knowledge in classrooms. The study suggests teacher education programs must also train CTs to create linguistically inclusive spaces and calls for more research on translanguaging in middle grades.

The speaker observes that current conditions are satisfying and encouraging, with America leading the world in post-war readjustment. Burdens remain, but remedies are being comprehended and applied. Domestic confidence and business have revived, bringing prosperity. America has contributed resources and counsel to relieve European suffering and settle disputes, inspiring humanity. These successes stem from constant, enlightened effort over generations, and future success requires learning from the past, recognizing the constancy of human nature. The nation's history includes asserting independence, the Monroe Doctrine, westward expansion, making freedom a birthright, acquiring distant islands to safeguard interests while bestowing justice on less favored peoples, entering the Great War, and withdrawing unrecompensed save for duty done. America has enlarged freedom and strengthened independence, and must remain distinctively American by embracing comprehensive ideals rather than being narrowed by slogans. Although physically separated from the Old World, the common brotherhood of man unites all humanity. The country intends peace but should maintain a balanced, modern military force as an instrument of security. It promotes peace through friendliness, mutual understanding, and naval limitation, leading a new direction away from competitive armaments. International conferences and consultations, such as the Washington conference, have been beneficial, and their continuation is favored. The U.S. advocates arbitration and should adhere to the Permanent Court of International Justice, not withholding support over small differences while not bartering independence. It does not wish to interfere politically, especially in the Old World, but has hesitantly helped maintain order in small Western Hemisphere countries and provided private funds for Old World relief. Permanent peace requires addressing economic pressure to renew opportunity, and America has a duty to respond with counsel and resources. However, the most important element is the desire for peace and brotherly love in the human heart; only spiritual nature can triumph. America can best contribute by maintaining political detachment and independence, being at peace with all, assisting but requiring justice, and using its powers to trim the world's balance. Success abroad depends on home. The party system is fundamentally sound; responsible party government requires elected members to cooperate on broad principles, or elections become mockery. The Administration has a clear mandate to maintain constitutional guarantees, faith in courts, and reject public ownership of railroads and utilities; people want judicial determination and property in their own hands. The accepted policy is economy in public expenditure with tax reduction and reform. Extravagance burdens the people; economy is meant to save people, not just money. Taxes not absolutely required are legalized larceny; rewards belong to earners. Further tax reduction and reform are needed; high rates are wrong and produce little revenue. The country believes in prosperity and creating conditions for success, not destroying the successful. Moral issues emphasize the rights of persons, the right to hold property, and that waste leads to moral decay. Policies of better international understandings, economy, lower taxes, restrictive immigration, and a protective tariff have brought peaceful industrial relations, plentiful employment, and high pay. Transportation is recovering, agriculture slowly reviving. The most important problem is maintaining existing advantages; the constitutional system requires constant vigilance. The first rule of a republic is obedience to law; citizens make their own laws and must observe them. Congress is an independent and effective legislative body, collaborating with the President. America has not fully practiced its principles but has expressed determination to proceed in the right direction, with loyalty to common citizenship and toleration. In trading, divergence means price swings and indicator movement are not in phase. A divergence signal is generated when price makes a higher swing high but the indicator makes a lower high, or price makes a lower swing low when the indicator makes a higher swing low, indicating potential loss of momentum and likely reversal.

A Divergence Trading Strategy uses oscillators such as RSI, MACD, or Stochastic Oscillator to identify discrepancies between price and momentum. Bullish divergence occurs when price forms lower lows while the oscillator forms higher lows. Bearish divergence occurs when price forms higher highs while the oscillator forms lower highs. Divergence is classified into classical (regular) and hidden. Classical divergence: price makes a lower low and indicator a higher low, or price makes a higher high and indicator a lower high; it may indicate trend reversal or pullback. Hidden divergence: price makes a higher low in an uptrend but indicator a lower low, or price makes a lower high in a downtrend and indicator a higher high; it often indicates a pullback will reverse for trend continuation.

The best indicator for divergence is momentum and mean reversion oscillators, but backtesting is necessary. A simple divergence strategy was backtested on SPY. The optimization table showed profit factors of at least 1.75 for 2 to around 20 days, with impressive Sharpe Ratios. The equity curve for strategy number 2 showed low max drawdowns, only one losing year (2012), but relatively few trades.

Advantages of the strategy include capitalizing on momentum shifts before they are fully reflected, providing clear entry and exit signals, and versatility across time frames and instruments. Volume analysis can complement divergence signals; for example, decreasing volume alongside a bearish divergence may validate the signal. Common mistakes include not understanding divergence, relying solely on divergence signals, overtrading, failing to use proper risk management, and emotional decision-making. Market momentum helps identify divergence patterns by revealing discrepancies between price and momentum indicators.

Examples: A classical bullish divergence on the Nasdaq 100 H4 chart in March 2020 (lower swing low, RSI higher low, hammer trigger) preceded a rally. A hidden bullish divergence on TSLA D1 chart in March 2020 (higher swing low, RSI lower low, bullish engulfing trigger) preceded a rally. A classical bearish divergence on the S&P 500 H4 chart in February 2020 (higher swing high, RSI lower high, harami trigger) preceded a crash. A hidden bearish divergence on the Nasdaq 100 H4 chart in December 2018 (lower swing high, RSI higher high, harami trigger) preceded a downswing. The backtest suggests simple divergence ideas can be effective.

Make power traces short, direct, thick (min 15 mils/A). Place inductor, output capacitors, and output diode close to reduce EMI, lead inductance, resistance, and voltage errors. Connect IC, input/output capacitor, and diode grounds directly to a ground plane. Use ground planes on both PCB sides to reduce noise and ground loop errors, and absorb EMI. On multilayer boards, separate power and signal planes with a ground plane; use one via per 200 mA for inter-plane current. Arrange components so switching current loops curl in the same direction during both switch states to prevent magnetic field reversal and reduce radiated EMI. Output drivers deliver 2-A peak; careful layout and ground plane essential. Designate a unique power ground for high di/dt currents, connecting PGND. Power ground may be single-point connected. Bypass VCC directly to power ground with a high-frequency capacitor; connect power MOSFET sources, input power return, and bulk input capacitor to power ground. Clamp output with a high-current Schottky diode to VCC and PGND; nothing else on power ground. Bypass VREF directly to signal ground plane with a high-frequency capacitor. Use low ESR/ESL ceramic 1-mF capacitors for VCC and VREF. Bypass all analog circuitry to signal ground plane.

The paper introduces a new audio synthesis task: video object segmentation-aware audio generation, which aims to generate audio for a specific object in a video using visual segmentation masks, improving user control in Foley generation. The proposed model, SAGANet, extends the pretrained MMAudio model by adding a segmentation-aware control module. This module processes both global video and a focal crop around the masked object, along with their segmentation masks, through a shared Synchformer-based vision transformer with gated cross-attention to fuse global and local features. The fused features condition the audio generation process. A new dataset, Segmented Music Solos, is curated from solo musical instrument performance videos with segmentation masks, ensuring high audio-video correspondence. Experiments on multi-source test scenes show SAGANet significantly improves temporal alignment (DeSync) and semantic similarity (IB-score) compared to the base MMAudio model, which only uses text and full-frame video. Fine-tuning with LoRA further enhances performance. An ablation study demonstrates that combining global and local visual information with masks yields the best temporal synchronization and semantic relevance, while using only global or only local information degrades certain metrics. The work lays a foundation for more controllable Foley models.

Harvey F. Euge appealed a summary judgment in favor of the Bank of St. Louis and two former employees in his suit for malicious prosecution. Euge had been convicted of obtaining money by a bogus check, but the Missouri Supreme Court reversed the conviction, holding the check was not bogus because it was drawn on an existing account, though by a fictitious person. Euge sought damages, contending the reversal proved lack of probable cause and that the indictment was improperly procured. The Court of Appeals affirmed, stating that a conviction, even if later reversed, creates a presumption of probable cause. The undisputed facts showed Euge deposited $40 under a fictitious name, then used a $45 check from that account to reopen his own account and immediately withdraw $45; the check was returned for insufficient funds. The court held these facts established probable cause as a matter of law, and the reversal based on a narrow statutory exception did not negate it. Where facts are undisputed, probable cause is for the court, not a jury. The summary judgment was affirmed.

This paper addresses how robots can model and reason about differences between competing plans to infer which is better, and how they can narrate those inferences. It proposes a new ontological model extending OCRA to formalize plan qualities (cost, makespan, number of tasks) and relations for plan comparison, answering research question RQ1. For RQ2, it introduces ACXON, an algorithm that retrieves divergent knowledge from a time-indexed knowledge graph and constructs contrastive explanatory narratives at three specificity levels. The model is validated by answering competency questions. ACXON is evaluated against the AXON baseline using planning domains from IPC competitions. Results show ACXON significantly reduces the number of knowledge tuples used and communication times for specificity levels 2 and 3, though interaction times remain long for high specificity. Readability scores are similar, indicating college-level comprehension. A modification to restrict knowledge retrieval by object class is discussed to further shorten narratives and enable selective, potentially personalized explanations.

The Gretna Trust & Savings Bank, as dative testamentary executor, sued David Lewis to recover $505.58 withdrawn from Priscilla Lewis's bank account after her death, plus rent. David admitted the withdrawals but claimed he was a creditor and the funds were meant to repay loans. The trial court dismissed the suit. On appeal, the court found the account was in the mother's name and the withdrawals occurred after her death. The executor has the duty to collect assets; a creditor cannot self-satisfy a claim by taking succession property. The withdrawal was illegal. The bank is entitled to possession of the funds; David must assert any creditor claim through the formal succession process. The rent claim was not proved. The judgment was reversed, awarding the bank $505.58 with interest from October 20, 1930, and costs.

The passage examines the saying "Sell in May and come back in November" by analyzing US Treasury cash balance patterns. It identifies three annual peaks: January (Reverse Repurchase Agreement Operations), May (tax refunds), and November (Treasury buybacks). May's peak is most consistent, as tax refunds primarily go to wealthy individuals who invest the funds, causing a stock market pop. The author suggests that 2018's tax code changes and market retrace could amplify the May boost. November's pop results from Fed buybacks, with ex-bondholders investing in stocks. The article concludes that these liquidity spikes, not seasons or holidays, largely explain the adage. The February and November patterns are less consistent and require further research.

Restoration Affiliates (RA) was formed in 2011 as an equal partnership by Rich Piltch (ARS), Damon Gersh (Maxons Restoration), Ras Fenger (Disaster One), and Andy Goldberg (RestoreCore). Guided by a “Go-Giver” philosophy, RA aimed to help smaller regional restoration and reconstruction companies compete with national players like Belfor by offering a national service solution for clients such as large insurers and property management firms. By fall 2013, RA had 21 member organizations with combined revenues of $300 million.

ARS, founded by Piltch in 1987, shifted its customer focus from insurance companies to property management companies, emphasizing relationships, priority service agreements, and value-added services like disaster planning. RA’s structure as an LLC gave all members equal shareholder responsibility. Members paid annual dues and referral fees (10% for mitigation/restoration, 5% for reconstruction) on referred projects.

RA faced several strategic questions: who should ensure member contributions and enforce standards; how to handle overlapping service territories; whether the referral fee model was appropriate; how to achieve consistent service quality across independent companies; how to resolve competing disaster planning software offerings (SecureCore and faciliSmart); and how to market the organization. A national contract with Forest City Enterprises highlighted RA’s potential but also underscored the need to resolve these issues.

Weak gravitational lensing has become a competitive cosmological probe through recent cosmic shear measurements from KiDS, DES, and HSC, achieving percent-level constraints on S8. The parameters Ωm and σ8 are degenerate when probed by lensing alone, requiring additional data. Current precision is limited mainly by uncertainty in intrinsic alignment (IA) of galaxies and baryonic feedback; this paper focuses on IA. Unaccounted IA can bias cosmological parameters by 4-5σ, and inaccurate IA models impair inference. IA models include NLA, extended-NLA, TT, TATT, halo model, and effective field theory. Observations indicate a colour-dependence: red galaxies are strongly aligned, blue galaxies show no alignment, but selection effects cause large uncertainty. Some methods infuse IA into simulations for validation, beyond-2pt statistics, and mitigation tests. This paper presents a pipeline infusing NLA, extended-NLA, TT, and extended-TT models into the same N-body simulation (SkySim5000), coupling with HOD to probe non-linear galaxy bias. Existing beyond-2pt analyses only use NLA, insufficient for future surveys. The paper also studies source clustering impact on weak lensing probes. Section 2 describes cosmic shear statistics: two-point correlation functions (γ-2PCF) are predicted semi-analytically for validation, using the Limber approximation and an LSST Year-1 redshift distribution split into five tomographic bins. γ-2PCF are estimated from galaxy ellipticities with Treecorr in 20 angular bins. Non-Gaussian statistics access additional information and are measured on convergence or aperture mass maps generated from shear catalogues via Kaiser-Squires inversion.

The paper introduces a general method for deriving codensity presentations of monads, based on the principle that codensity monads arise from combining density and duality. A codensity setting is defined as a diagram where a functor F decomposes as F ≅ RG^op E, with a dual equivalence E, a dense functor G, and a right adjoint R. Theorem 3.2 states that in any codensity setting, the monad induced by the adjunction L ⊣ R is isomorphic to the codensity monad of F. This unifies and simplifies many known codensity presentations. Applications include ultrafilter monads on Set and Top, filter monads on Set and Top, double dualization monads (neighbourhood monad, double dualization on meet-semilattices and vector spaces, Pontryagin duality on abelian groups), Isbell duality, Vietoris monads on Stone spaces and Top, the sobrification monad, and probability monads (expectation, Giry, Radon, Kantorovich, and finitely additive measures in a finite semiring). The approach reduces codensity proofs to known density results and basic dualities.

Henry Clay was born on April 12, 1777, in Hanover County, Virginia, during the American Revolution, and his life paralleled that of the young nation. He died in Washington, D.C., and the nation mourned. A political opponent’s journal eulogized him, lamenting the loss of his majestic presence, mighty mind, and matchless eloquence, and declaring that his fame and character belonged to the whole country, not to any party. The journal noted his public career spanned a remarkable era, his voice influenced war and peace with Great Britain, and his name was invoked in struggles for liberty in Greece and South America. It credited him with quelling civil commotions on at least three occasions, including the recent internal discord that cost him his life.

His biography was well known. His early education was limited, but he continued learning throughout his life. He became a lawyer and moved to Lexington, Kentucky. He served in the Kentucky Legislature, filled vacancies in the U.S. Senate, and was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, where he was immediately chosen Speaker. He served as a peace commissioner in 1814, was again Speaker, and later Secretary of State under John Quincy Adams. He returned to the Senate, resigned in 1842, and served again from 1849 until shortly before his death. His official life spanned nearly half a century, with interruptions totaling less than ten years. He was repeatedly defeated for the presidency, yet remained a dominant figure long after those who defeated him had faded.

His pre-eminence stemmed from a combination of qualities: surpassing eloquence, excellent judgment, and indomitable will. His eloquence was deeply earnest and impassioned, rooted in sincerity and conviction, and aimed at practical effect. He avoided sectional ground, carefully weighed all interests, and was devoted to preserving the Union. His ruling passion was a deep devotion to human liberty and sympathy for the oppressed everywhere.

On the War of 1812, he more than anyone brought Congress to a decision, delivering speeches that aroused and inspired. One unrecorded speech was remembered by old men as astonishing. The Missouri question, arising from slavery, alarmed the nation by dividing it along geographical lines. Thomas Jefferson called it a fire bell in the night. Clay labored to secure a compromise, and after repeated failures and exhaustion, his modifications and eloquence achieved Missouri’s admission, averting dissolution. Thereafter, he was regarded as the man for a crisis, and in the Nullification crisis and the later slavery question tied to newly acquired territory, he devised adjustments that met public expectation.

Clay was on principle opposed to slavery, and both early and late in life advocated gradual emancipation in Kentucky. He owned slaves but saw no way to eradicate slavery immediately without greater evil. He opposed both extremes: those who would destroy the Union to end slavery, and those who ridiculed the Declaration of Independence to perpetuate it. He was an early member and president of the American Colonization Society, believing it could return free blacks to Africa and ultimately redeem the continent. The eulogy closes by urging the nation to trust in Divine Providence for future instruments of safety.

A virtual object machine learning system generates synthetic training data using 3D models of subjects with rigging structures that provide key point metadata. The system programmatically varies poses, applies different model textures, and renders the models within 3D environments using spherical high dynamic range images as backgrounds to simulate diverse lighting. Virtual cameras capture renders from multiple angles, producing labeled training images without manual labeling. A machine learning engine trains a classifier model on this data to classify dynamic objects and detect key points in real images, enabling gesture or pose identification, annotation overlays, or pixel mask generation. The system includes interface, model, gesture, model texture, environment, machine learning, and render engines. Training data generation uses nested loops over models, gestures, textures, and environment variables.

Upgrade is a sci-fi/horror/action film set in the near future. Logan Marshall-Green plays Grey Trace, a technophobic mechanic whose wife embraces advanced technology. After a savage attack leaves him paralyzed, he receives a secret AI implant called STEM that restores his mobility with mechanical precision, enabling him to pursue revenge. The paper introduces AI-Noether, a formal abductive reasoning system that reconciles a hypothesized polynomial formula with an incomplete background theory expressed as polynomial equations. Given a set of known axioms and a target hypothesis not derivable from them, the method identifies candidate missing axioms that, when added, allow the hypothesis to be derived. The approach consists of three steps: Encode (construct the ideal generated by the axioms and hypothesis), Decompose (perform primary decomposition to break the solution variety into irreducible components), and Reason (for each component, extract generators and test whether adding one as an axiom, after eliminating variables not in the hypothesis, makes the hypothesis derivable). The system returns candidate missing axioms or certifies that no single such axiom exists. It does not require data for the missing axiom or prior knowledge of its variables. The method is tested on several physical law systems (Kepler’s Third Law, Compton scattering, Einstein’s equations, escape velocity, light damping, Hagen–Poiseuille, neutrino decay, Hall effect, carrier-resolved photo-Hall effect), successfully recovering single removed axioms in nearly all cases. For multiple missing axioms, recovery success varies; a sufficient condition for recoverability based on common minimal associated primes is provided. The work aims to integrate machine-driven discoveries with existing scientific theory by automatically proposing modifications to the theory.

Regarding China, English military operations have ended with a treaty opening four new ports (Amoy, Foo-Choo-Foo, Ningpo, Chinghai) to British trade. U.S. trade is currently limited to Canton, and the treaty neither admits nor excludes other nations, so each must negotiate its own arrangements. U.S. imports from China have reached $9,000,000, and exports are growing. China has historically excluded foreigners, but the treaty's equal correspondence terms may extend to others. While cheap labor and fixed habits may limit sudden demand, the U.S. market in China has more than doubled in ten years, and new ports would likely boost demand. No permanent diplomatic missions are yet contemplated between England and China, and it is uncertain if Peking would receive a resident minister. The President recommends funding a commissioner to reside in China, to safeguard American commercial interests, protect citizens and property, engage local authorities, and, if instructed, address high functionaries or the Emperor. The commissioner should be a person of intelligence and character, with compensation matching the mission's importance.

Dr Henry Leung and a Nanyang Polytechnic team developed a method to convert coffee waste into biodegradable plastic. They add water and Cupriavidus necator bacteria to Nanyang coffee waste (roasted with butter and sugar, providing nutrients). After 7-10 days, the bacteria produce PHA biopolymer. Initially, heavy solvents yielded only 30% pure PHA (0.5-2.5g per 100g waste) and created organic waste. Switching to eco-friendly acetone and alkaline solvents reduced waste and cost but lowered yield. Genetically modifying the bacteria increased purity to over 50% (1-3g per 100g). PHA decomposes faster and releases fewer toxins than PVC. Lab experiments concluded; the team seeks industrial partners to commercialize within 3-5 years. Only one Australian company currently does this commercially.

The Iowa Supreme Court reversed the district court and held that the district court had jurisdiction because an application for rehearing under Iowa Code § 96.6(8) is not a prerequisite to judicial review, consistent with Ellis v. Iowa Department of Job Service. The court further held that the district court erred in reversing the Department's decision based on the appeal board's refusal to permit the employer to withdraw its protest, as withdrawal of a protest does not alter the factual determination of eligibility and any error was harmless. The court also held that the Department correctly disqualified Kehde from benefits for misconduct. Kehde was discharged for holding a lit marijuana cigarette on company premises. Although there was no evidence he knew the specific company rule, his possession of marijuana, a serious misdemeanor, was a deliberate violation of standards of behavior the employer has a right to expect, including not engaging in unlawful conduct or jeopardizing safety. Substantial evidence supported the misconduct finding. The case was remanded for entry of an order consistent with the opinion.

Industry-sponsored clinical trials have become excessively complex, with growing data collection burdens increasing trial duration and making recruitment difficult, especially for lower socioeconomic groups. ICH guideline E19 encourages reducing irrelevant data, but little progress has been made. Protocol design teams receive little feedback on how their choices affect participant time, staff complexity, or costs. Faro Health Inc. developed a tool that quantifies these impacts.

A major source of complexity is "copy-and-paste" of schedules of assessment (SoAs) from previous trials, with additions often made to anticipate regulatory questions without considering burden. Merck undertook a "Lean Design" project to simplify SoAs. The method starts with a "Ground Zero" SoA containing only the primary aim, then adds assessments based on principles: only include assessments with plausible biological effects, consider timing and frequency, use subsamples when appropriate, distinguish individual safety monitoring from adverse effect characterization, exclude routine clinical care data, and limit panel tests to relevant elements.

Six protocols from cardiovascular, psychiatry, oncology, and other areas were selected for workshops led by an expert and a Faro team member. Workshops were exercises; changes were not mandatory, and most protocols were in late development stages. The Faro tool quantified differences between original, workshop-recommended, and team-adopted SoAs.

Workshops recommended major reductions in assessments, saving 4 to 47 participant hours per trial and substantial costs. For example, a cardiovascular trial with 12,600 participants could save nearly $120 million from a $9,000 per-participant reduction. Oncology trials saw fewer recommended changes due to standardized assessments. Teams adopted some but not all recommendations, often limited by late-stage protocols, discomfort with uncertainty, and resistance from quality-of-life and pharmacology groups. Concerns about FDA expectations were noted, though ICH guidelines support data reduction.

Adopted changes still yielded significant savings. Earlier application of Lean Design would likely increase adoption. The Faro tool's real-time feedback on design choices is most impactful when used from the start. Estimated savings only covered SoA items, not downstream costs like monitoring and analysis. Face-to-face workshops were effective but impractical at scale; training multiple individuals with the tool could enable broader adoption. Merck launched a company-wide project to implement Lean Design principles across all therapeutic areas. The generalizability of the approach should be tested in other companies. The process of rebuilding protocols from Ground Zero with quantitative feedback may substantially reduce inessential elements, burdens, and costs.

A regulation American football field is 120 yards long and 53.3 yards wide. The playing field between end zones is 100 yards long and 53.3 yards wide. End zones are 10 yards deep and 53.3 yards wide. A ball carrier must break the plane of the end zone to score; a receiver catching a pass in the end zone must have control and one foot in bounds, or two in the NFL. Goal lines are 10 yards from the end line and 100 yards apart. Yard lines are marked every yard with short lines near the sideline; every five yards a solid line spans the field, with numbers every ten yards. Hash marks are reference points for ball placement; the ball cannot be spotted wider than them. Hash mark spacing: NFL 18 ft 6 in, college 40 ft, high school 53 ft 4 in. Field numbers: NFL bottom edge 12 yards from sideline, college 9 yards, high school 6 yards (may vary by state). Sidelines are 6 ft wide boundaries. Coaches are restricted to between the 25-yard lines on the sideline.

A non-occluding intravascular blood pump comprises a cylindrical shroud with an inlet and outlet, an impeller positioned inside sharing a central axis, a centrally disposed motor that rotates the impeller, and pillars coupling the motor to the shroud. To reduce hemolysis, design features include: a trumpeted shroud with a larger inlet than outlet; raked back leading edges of impeller blades such that the angle between the central axis and leading edge is less than 90°; a shroud inlet length sufficient to prevent turbulent flow detachment (e.g., at least 1.5 times the inner shroud diameter); a bare hub length of 0.2–0.3 times the inner diameter; matching the pillar angle to the outlet blade angle; matching the impeller base flare angle to the stator tip flare angle; a clearance between the shroud and impeller blades of 200–300 microns; and a wrap angle of approximately 100±10 degrees. The pillars may be curved, and their number may be mismatched with the number of impeller blades to avoid alignment.

Hotspot analysis identified the impeller, inflow shroud, and pillars as major sources of shear stress. Iterative optimization across multiple phases reduced shear stress and hemolysis. Extending the shroud prevented detached turbulent flow from reaching the impeller. Impeller modifications included an elongated hub, adjusted blade angles, wrap angle, and leading edge rounding. Aligning pillars with the outflow direction reduced mean shear stress. Transient CFD simulations and Lagrangian particle tracking estimated hemolysis. The final prototype P_31 showed a reduction in maximum shear stress of 150–200 Pa and average impeller surface shear below 400 Pa up to 30,000 rpm. In vitro testing demonstrated a 78% improvement in the Normalized Index of Hemolysis at 20,000 rpm compared to the reference design, while maintaining hydraulic output. The pump is suited for NYHA Class III–IVa heart failure patients.

Molecular dynamics simulations of radiation damage in pure niobium were performed for primary knock-on atom energies of 1–75 keV at 300 K using four interatomic potentials: EAM, FS-1, FS-2, and SNAP. Defect production followed a power-law relation with two energy regimes, transitioning near 20 keV where subcascade formation increased. Interstitial clustering rose with energy and was highest for SNAP; vacancy clustering was consistently high across all potentials, with EAM showing the highest fraction and largest vacancy clusters. Cluster morphologies differed: EAM produced a balanced mix of 1/2⟨111⟩ loops, C15 rings, and hybrid structures; FS-1 favored ⟨110⟩ dumbbells, crowdions, and small C15 rings; FS-2 predominantly formed 1/2⟨111⟩ loops; SNAP generated compact cascades with a high proportion of C15-like rings (up to nine atoms) that may act as precursors to dislocation loops. The stiffness-to-range ratio, threshold displacement energy, and defect formation energies influenced low-energy behavior, but subcascade formation dominated at higher energies. Older potentials produced more defects and gave the incorrect ground-state configuration of self-interstitial atoms compared to newer potentials.

Asteroid 2025 TF, measuring 1–3 meters in diameter, passed 428 ± 7 km above Antarctica on October 1 at 00:47:26 UTC. It was detected hours later by the Catalina Sky Survey and posed no danger. ESA’s Planetary Defence Office used the Las Cumbres Observatory telescope in Australia to track the object, determining its distance and timing with high precision. Small asteroids of this size are harmless, typically creating fireballs if they enter the atmosphere. The flyby highlighted the growing precision of planetary defense efforts and the ability to track tiny objects soon after discovery.

Current machine learning-assisted GWAS approaches, which impute missing phenotypes and then treat them as observed, can produce pervasive false-positive associations. A type 2 diabetes example showed an 81% replication failure rate for loci identified from imputed phenotypes, partly because predictors like HbA1c capture non-glycemic genetic effects. The authors introduce POP-GWAS, a statistical framework that combines GWAS on observed and imputed phenotypes in both labeled and unlabeled samples using a weighted estimator. POP-GWAS provides unbiased estimates and valid inference without assumptions about imputation quality or algorithm, is always more powerful than GWAS on observed phenotypes alone, and requires only summary statistics. Simulations and real-data benchmarking confirm its validity and power gains. Applied to DXA-derived bone mineral density across 14 skeletal sites, POP-GWAS identified 188 loci (39% more than conventional GWAS), revealed site-specific genetic architecture, and yielded 89 novel loci in meta-analyses. The method also provides a closed-form effective sample size formula for power calculation.

The passage introduces semirings as algebraic structures that generalize computational models, with applications in algorithms, automata, optimization, machine learning, and database provenance. Semirings like the Boolean, natural numbers, non-negative reals, tropical, and Łukasiewicz semirings are defined, with the paper focusing on commutative, positive, non-trivial semirings. It defines propositional logic (PL=K), first-order logic (FO=K), and existential second-order logic (ESO=K) under semiring semantics, where formulas evaluate to semiring values and truth is any non-zero value. The satisfiability problem SAT=K is defined for PL=K. The BSS machine model is adapted to semirings (BSSK), with non-deterministic computation defined via guessing additional semiring values. The complexity class NPK consists of languages decided non-deterministically by polynomial-time BSSK machines. The paper then presents a version of Fagin's theorem: Lemma 20 shows ESO=K ⊆ NPK, and Theorem 21 states ESO=K = NPK, with a proof sketch that encodes BSSK machine computations using second-order relations.

This work presents a method to design dilute viscoelastic Boger fluids with prescribed rheological properties. Using polyisobutylene dissolved in a polybutene/mineral oil solvent, the authors characterize fluids via the Zimm model, identifying shear modulus G₀, relaxation time τ, and polymer-solvent interaction parameter χ from small-amplitude oscillatory shear measurements. They experimentally determine power-law scaling relationships between these rheological properties and design parameters: polymer concentration c, molecular weight M, and solvent viscosity ηₛ. Observed dependencies deviate from ideal Zimm theory; for example, τ increases weakly with c, and the first normal stress difference coefficient ψ₁ is overpredicted by a factor δ. By compiling measured exponents into an invertible design matrix, the authors demonstrate independent control of G₀, τ, and ψ₁. They fabricate fluids with constant τ and varied G₀, constant G₀ and varied τ, and constant ψ₁ despite large viscosity variations, verifying the approach. The framework can be extended to other Boger fluid systems and may aid in inferring material parameters or testing viscoelastic flow theories.

The article compares the Pixel Watch 4 and Apple Watch Ultra 3. The Pixel Watch 4 costs $399 for the 45-mm model ($349 for 41-mm), while the Watch Ultra 3 costs twice as much. The Watch Ultra 3 battery lasts up to 42 hours, lasting from Friday morning to Sunday morning in testing. The Pixel Watch 4 battery lasts up to 30 or 40 hours and also lasted a full weekend trip; its 45-mm model charged from 16% to 100% in 45 minutes. The Pixel Watch 4 is 5ATM water-resistant, while the Watch Ultra 3 is 10ATM and can function as a dive computer. Both have manual water lock and ejection; the Ultra 3’s automatic water lock triggers under 10 centimeters of water, the Pixel Watch 4 requires a foot. Both watches offer satellite communication requiring an active carrier plan and clear sky view. The Pixel Watch 4 only supports emergency calls to 911 in the contiguous US. The Watch Ultra 3 allows regular texts and works in multiple countries. For offline maps, Apple uses topographic maps in Apple Maps, but the author found Google Maps easier to sync across devices with the Pixel Watch 4. Fitbit on the Pixel Watch 4 is described as more usable than Apple’s health apps. The Pixel Watch 4 adds an integrated bike computer and dual-band GPS. Fitbit’s sleep tracking is more detailed than Apple’s Sleep Score. The Apple Watch has hypertension notifications; the Pixel Watch 4 has a feature that can notify of cardiac arrest. Both watches include check-in features, fall detection, and crash detection, though a hard fall during testing was not detected by the Pixel Watch 4. The Watch Ultra 3 has more microphones and wind noise reduction; the Pixel Watch 4 lacks a wrist-flick gesture to dismiss calls. Overall, the Watch Ultra 3 is the better adventure watch with satellite texting and greater durability, but the Pixel Watch 4 offers better health features via Fitbit and a significantly lower price, making it a notable option under $500 with satellite communication, multi-day battery, and sleep tracking.

The article describes Enron's transformation from a stodgy pipeline company into a trading colossus and its subsequent decline. In 1985, Houston Natural Gas merged with InterNorth to form Enron, led by Ken Lay. Jeff Skilling, a McKinsey consultant, devised the Gas Bank, which guaranteed gas supply and price, turning Enron into a market-maker that bought and sold gas, assuming risk and earning transaction profits. This model succeeded, and Skilling joined Enron in 1990, creating a new culture that prized intellectual capital, aggressiveness, and rapid deal-making. Recruits from top schools were offered high salaries, bonuses with no cap, and perks like concierge services and adventure trips. A Performance Review Committee (PRC) ranked employees, with the bottom 15% replaced annually. Enron expanded into electricity trading, then into coal, paper, steel, weather, and broadband. EnronOnline handled $335 billion in commodity trades in 2000. The company used mark-to-market accounting on an unprecedented scale, booking profits upfront. It dominated markets and could set terms, often leaving counterparties at the altar. Internal competition intensified, loyalty eroded, and the culture became mercenary. Rebecca Mark, head of Enron International, built $20 billion in power plants but clashed with Skilling's asset-light vision. After her India project faced delays and costs, she was given Azurix, a water company, which failed and was folded back. Skilling became CEO in February 2001. Almost immediately, Enron was blamed for California's energy crisis, and its stock fell from $80 to $50. The telecom division suffered from the tech bubble burst, and the Blockbuster movies-on-demand deal collapsed. Analysts questioned accounting practices, and key executives sold stock. Skilling called an analyst an "asshole" during a call. By late August, the stock fell below $40. Skilling, unhappy, resigned after six months as CEO, citing personal sacrifices and a desire for family time. Lay returned as CEO, promising a kinder culture and a focus on core business. Skilling, with 90% of his net worth in Enron stock, planned to stay in Houston, believing in a second wave of technology that Enron would lead.

Emergency relief speed correlates with ideology: in 2024, conservative outcomes averaged 23 days, liberal 41 days.

The retail apparel industry is down ~20% in 52 weeks, attributed to e-commerce threats, overexpansion, and trade policy uncertainty including the U.S. leaving the TPP, NAFTA renegotiation, and Brexit. The author believes Francesca's Holdings Corp. (FRAN) can survive and emerge stronger. FRAN has $488 million in sales, a $320 million market cap, $48 million cash, no debt, and ~$57.6 million free cash flow. It operates 670+ stores in 48 states, targeting 900, with products for women aged 18-35. In 1Q17, sales rose 1% to $107.7 million due to new stores, but comparable sales fell 5%. EPS was $0.12 versus $0.18. Gross margin declined to 45.2% from 46.3%, and SG&A rose 10%. FY18 guidance: net sales $518-$537 million, comparable sales -2% to +2%, 60-65 new boutiques, 10-15 closures, EPS $1.07-$1.17. Analyst estimates: sales $520-$533.2 million, EPS $0.95-$1.10. The company has a strong balance sheet, quick ratio 1.4, current ratio 2.1, and F-Score 6. Valuation: P/E 8.4, lowest among profitable peers and below industry median; Price/Book above median and competitors. Growth rates explain valuation discrepancies; high growth is unsustainable. This study conducted a multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) using the METRO method and FOCUS fine-mapping to identify genes associated with general cognitive function, white matter hyperintensity (WMH), and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Gene expression data came from African American (AA) and European American (EA) participants in the GENOA study, and GWAS summary statistics were used. After fine-mapping, 266 genes were associated with general cognitive function, 23 with WMH, 69 with AD (using an EA GWAS), and 2 with AD (using an AA GWAS). The gene ICA1L was identified in both the WMH and AD analyses. Identified genes were enriched for pathways related to innate immunity, vascular dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. The study is noted as the first TWAS using expression mapping studies in multiple ancestries for these traits.
