This study reports that hybrid immunity from combined SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and natural infection yields superior neutralizing antibody responses compared to vaccination alone. Using two cohorts—one longitudinal with pre- and post-vaccination samples from previously infected and infection-naïve individuals, and a larger cross-sectional cohort including both infection-before-vaccination and vaccine-breakthrough cases—the authors measured antibody levels by ELISA and neutralizing titers by live-virus focus reduction neutralization tests against ancestral SARS-CoV-2 and variants (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Omicron BA.1, BA.2). Hybrid immunity significantly increased spike-specific total antibody, IgG, and IgA levels, and elevated neutralizing titers against all tested variants, with the largest fold-increases against vaccine-resistant variants Beta and Omicron. Neutralizing potency and variant cross-neutralization were also improved. The interval between vaccination and infection (exposure interval) was a key determinant: longer intervals, up to 400 days, correlated with higher neutralizing titers and greater cross-neutralization of variants, including Omicron, even though samples were collected before Omicron’s emergence. This relationship held for both infection-prior-to-vaccination and breakthrough groups. The findings indicate that the humoral immune response continues to mature over extended periods between antigen exposures, leading to enhanced antibody quantity, quality, and breadth.

Andrew W. Lo introduces MIT's 15.401 Finance Theory course for first-year MBA students. He defines finance as mathematics plus money, emphasizing that the required mathematics ranges from basic arithmetic to advanced topics. He presents three examples of successful individuals with different mathematical backgrounds: James Simons (quantitative hedge fund manager), Warren Buffett (investor using fundamental analysis), and Jack Welch (former GE CEO). The course will focus on four economic components: households, financial intermediaries, non-financial corporations, and capital markets.

The two fundamental challenges of financial analysis are valuation of assets and management of assets. Valuation involves determining what something is worth, while management involves choosing the more valuable option. A classroom auction of an unknown item demonstrates price discovery with limited information. Time and risk are the two factors that make finance challenging; without them, financial decisions reduce to basic microeconomics.

Lo outlines six fundamental principles of finance: no systematic free lunches; individuals prefer more money to less, money now to later, and less risk to more risk; all agents act in their own self-interest; and three additional principles to be discussed later. The course is divided into four sections: introductory material, valuation (discounting and net present value), risk, and applications to corporate finance. Course requirements include lectures, readings, class participation (10%), a case study (10%), a midterm (25%), and a cumulative final exam (55%). No problem sets are required; instead, a package of problems and solutions is provided, and the majority of exam questions will be drawn verbatim from it. Lo advises students to skim lecture notes in advance, take notes in class, review afterward, work on problems both in groups and alone, and ask questions.

A hardware database privacy device receives a query from a client device, identifies a level of differential privacy corresponding to the request (including a privacy parameter ε), accesses a set of data from a private database, modifies the set of operations based on the identified privacy level, performs the modified operations to produce a differentially private result set, and provides that result set to the client device for display. The device includes a privacy system with multiple engines (count, median, mean, variance, IQR, batch gradient, stochastic gradient, random forest, histogram, model testing, synthetic database) that generate differentially private responses by perturbing outputs or processes with noise (e.g., Laplacian, Gaussian, Cauchy random variables) or by using smooth sensitivity. A validation engine can certify whether a query satisfies differential privacy. A synthetic database engine transforms the data into a lower-dimensional synthetic database that preserves spatial relationships between entries. The client specifies privacy parameters and has a privacy budget that is decremented upon queries.

The public cloud is projected to become the most important HPC architecture for manufacturing enterprises, followed by hybrid cloud architectures that offer scalability for peak loads without outsourcing all data. Prebuilt architectures are also favored for ease of setup and reliability. IDC recommends a “make or buy” decision, noting OPEX-based public cloud HPC can provide technical and financial advantages over CAPEX-heavy in-house infrastructure. In-house HPC clusters face limitations in performance scaling, requiring costly hardware renewal or horizontal expansion, and often underutilize capacity outside peak periods. On-premises HPC also restricts agility and flexibility, hindering adaptation to new usage scenarios and limiting data analysis approaches, which impacts development of data-based products, services, and business models like digital twins. Over half of HPC users see optimizing HPC as important for enabling new solutions.

Improving security and resilience is important to over 80% of users; in-house environments suffer downtimes, and hybrid architectures can keep sensitive data on-premises while using the public cloud for non-critical workloads. HPC as a Service (HPCaaS) offers flexible maximum performance, cost optimization by shifting from CAPEX to OPEX or pay-as-you-go models, and is suitable for occasional users. HPCaaS supports global cooperation and hybrid workflows by providing configurable, scalable engineering workstations in the cloud with access to a common database, improving productivity and collaboration. It also enables new HPC-based business models, with 81% of current HPC users intending to implement them, allowing gradual customer base growth without upfront investment. 49% of respondents see HPCaaS as complete outsourcing of infrastructure operation, 42% as a way to use HPC without building their own, though skilled IT and analysis personnel remain necessary. Fast access to cutting-edge methods and hardware is a core innovation benefit cited by 52% of respondents.

IDC concludes that IT-based simulations, modeling, and data analytics are key enablers for addressing disruptive changes, and HPC technologies are becoming a prerequisite. Public cloud and HPCaaS unlock major potential by expanding agility and scalability or replacing in-house infrastructure entirely. Competitiveness hinges on creating a single source of truth across the product lifecycle, with high-quality data analysis driving new digital products, services, and business models. Recommendations include setting up virtual development, devising a holistic data strategy, evaluating HPC operating models based on utilization and flexibility, prioritizing scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and leveraging external expertise. The findings are based on a 2021 survey of 200 decision makers from industrial enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

The study examined adrenal veins and fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD)/segmental arterial mediolysis (SAM) lesions. Normal adrenal veins have asymmetrical longitudinal smooth muscle bundles without circular bundles, features indistinguishable from FMD in renal or carotid arteries. FMD is a radiographic diagnosis with non-inflammatory, non-atherosclerotic fibroplasia or smooth muscle changes; SAM is considered a precursor. In adrenal cortical adenomas, arterial walls were hyalinized with CD68-positive macrophages, intimal fibroplasia, and myxoid/fibrinoid medial degeneration, consistent with SAM and similar to acute atherosis of preeclampsia. In pheochromocytomas, arteries were thin-walled with myxoid/fibrinoid degeneration and fibroplasia; normal muscular arteries were uncommon. A retrospective review of 30 adrenalectomy specimens found asymmetrical muscle bundles in all normal adrenal tissues, while SAM was common in tumors. No FMD-like lesions occurred outside the adrenal gland. Fetal autopsy cases (9 fetuses, 15–37 weeks) showed no such vascular changes. The findings support unifying FMD and SAM as a spectrum, potentially related to adrenal hormones or hormone receptors. Morphologic similarities with Moyamoya disease and atherosis of preeclampsia suggest common pathogenic mechanisms involving adrenal hormone actions or receptor signaling. The authors conclude that adrenal vascular morphology may link the local adrenal milieu and hormones/receptors to FMD pathogenesis, guiding further investigation.

The Supertrend indicator, created by Oliver Seban, is a trend-following tool that signals trend direction, continuation, or reversal. It appears as a line on the price chart: green and below price during uptrends, red and above price during downtrends. The indicator reverses when a bar’s close crosses the previous period’s Supertrend value. Its formula uses the median price and the Average True Range (ATR) multiplied by a factor, with default parameters of 10 periods and a multiplier of 3. The indicator is lagging, deriving signals from historical data.

A backtest on the S&P 500 weekly data over 60 years, using only long trades and default settings without dividends or commissions, yielded a 65.79% win rate, a maximum drawdown of 24.6% (versus 56.24% for buy-and-hold), and an accuracy/success rate around 67%. The weekly timeframe is considered best, though the indicator can be applied intraday or daily. It performs well on instruments that trend for long periods. The trading rules are: buy when the price closes above the Supertrend line, sell when it closes below.

Supertrend adjusts to volatility via the ATR, widening the band in high volatility and tightening it in low volatility. It can be used in ranging markets by adjusting parameters and focusing on price crossovers near the line. The indicator can be combined with RSI, Moving Averages, or Bollinger Bands for confirmation. Limitations include false signals during choppy or highly volatile markets. The article concludes the Supertrend strategy is highly accurate for capturing upswings and avoiding downswings, with out-of-sample performance spanning roughly 40 years since its 1990s development.

A new study on in-flight transmission of cold and flu viruses advises passengers to choose a window seat and not move. The research, funded by Boeing and published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, involved testing surfaces and air on 10 flights, but found no viruses and observed only one coughing person. Mathematical modeling estimated that, on average, only one person on a 150-passenger flight would be infected by a hypothetical sick passenger in an aisle seat. The study found 38% of passengers never left their seats; 80% of aisle-seat occupants moved at least once, compared to 62% in middle and 43% in window seats. The 11 people nearest an infected person face the highest risk. Outside researchers noted the study is too small for broad conclusions but called it novel, as little prior research exists on airplane disease transmission.

The court denied plaintiffs' motion for a preliminary injunction seeking to bar NASD Regulation from compelling testimony, punishing invocation of the privilege against self-incrimination, or misusing grand jury materials. Plaintiffs, targets of a grand jury investigation, claimed Regulation's Rule 8210 demands were made as an agent of federal prosecutors, violating the Fifth Amendment and grand jury secrecy. After an evidentiary hearing consolidated with trial, the court found that Regulation's Division of Enforcement (DOE) conducted its own independent investigation into Cromwell and Pallet trading, and the Rule 8210 demands were not the product of government coercion, suggestion, or encouragement. Thus, Regulation's actions were not state action, and no Fifth Amendment issue arose. The court also found no credible evidence that grand jury materials protected by Rule 6(e) were disclosed to unauthorized Regulation personnel; documents shown to an employee were obtained via search warrant and not shown to be matters occurring before the grand jury. The court noted that physical and administrative separation between the DOE and the Criminal Assistance Prosecution Unit was imperfect, but that did not establish government control over the DOE's demands. The injunction was denied.

The Shepherd Express has criticized regulated monopoly We Energies for high rates and executive pay. As a monopoly, it lacks competition; the PSC sets rates guaranteeing over 10% return. Municipally owned power companies provide lower-cost energy and are accountable to customers, not investors. We Energies proposed a rate freeze through 2019, seen as locking in gains; the Metropolitan Milwaukee Association of Commerce supports it. ICE and CUB advocate a rate rollback. Scrutiny is overdue.

New research from Case Western Reserve University estimates the federal government spends $55 billion annually on the effects of childhood exposure to domestic violence. The study, published in The Journal of Family Violence, found such exposure leads to higher health-care costs, crime rates, and lower productivity. The CDC defines intimate partner violence as physical violence, sexual violence, stalking, or psychological aggression by a current or former partner. An estimated 15.5 million children are exposed yearly, with over 25% exposed in their lifetime. The average lifetime cost per exposed child by age 64 is nearly $50,000, including $11,042 in medical costs, $13,922 in crime-related costs, and $25,531 in productivity losses. For Ohio's 20-year-olds, the cumulative cost for the estimated 25% exposed is nearly $2.18 billion. This is the first study to quantify economic burden; researchers say policymakers can use it to push for preventive and therapeutic interventions.

The Simplified Specification is a subset of the complete SD Specification, provided "AS-IS" without warranties. Implementation may require licenses from SD-3C, LLC. The document defines SD Memory Card physical layer: card types include Standard Capacity (≤2GB), High Capacity (≤32GB), and Extended Capacity (≤2TB). Operating voltage is 2.7–3.6V (high voltage) or VDD1 2.7–3.6V / VDD2 1.70–1.95V (UHS-II). Bus speed modes range from Default Speed (25MHz, 12.5MB/s) and High Speed (50MHz, 25MB/s) to UHS-I modes (SDR12/25/50/104, DDR50) and UHS-II modes (FD156, HD312, FD312, FD624 up to 624MB/s). Speed classes (Class 0,2,4,6,10), UHS Speed Grade, Video Speed Class, and Application Performance Class indicate minimum performance. The card operates in identification mode (reset, voltage validation, CID/RCA assignment) and data transfer mode (point-to-point commands, single/multiple block read/write, erase, lock/unlock, switch function). Registers include OCR, CID, CSD, RCA, DSR, SCR. SPI mode is also supported. Additional features include cache, self maintenance, command queue, and content protection.

Nathan Calvin, general counsel of the three-employee AI policy nonprofit Encode, publicly accused OpenAI on X of using intimidation tactics to undermine California's SB 53 AI safety law while it was under debate. He alleged OpenAI used its lawsuit against Elon Musk as a pretext to target critics, implying Encode was secretly funded by Musk. Calvin's claims drew support from OpenAI's head of mission alignment Justin Achaim, former board member Helen Toner, and others. Tyler Johnston of The Midas Project also reported receiving a broad subpoena. OpenAI chief strategy officer Jason Kwon responded that Encode's support for Musk and undisclosed funding raised legitimate questions, and that subpoenas are standard litigation tools to investigate potential collaboration with parties having adverse commercial interests. Calvin was served a subpoena in August, as was Encode; OpenAI sought all his private communications on SB 53. Calvin stated Encode is not Musk-funded and believes OpenAI used the legal battle to intimidate. He said OpenAI's actions regarding SB 53 were inappropriate. The law, signed in late September, requires frontier AI developers to publish safety frameworks, transparency reports, and share catastrophic risk assessments. Calvin alleged OpenAI tried to weaken the law by proposing that compliance with federal or international frameworks would satisfy state rules, potentially exempting major developers. He delayed speaking out until the bill passed to keep focus on its merits. Encode, founded by then-15-year-old Sneha Revanur, formally refused to provide documents, citing no Musk funding, and OpenAI has not replied. Calvin urged constructive engagement, calling the episode his most stressful professional period, and questioned whether the tactics align with OpenAI's nonprofit mission.

This document defines the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for AMD SEV-ES and SEV-SNP encrypted virtualization features. It standardizes a 4KB shared memory area and MSR-based protocol for guest–hypervisor communication during Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs). Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement via a bitmap, GHCB GPA registration for SEV-SNP, and support for SEV-SNP operations including page state changes, guest requests, extended guest requests with certificate data, AP creation, restricted injection (doorbell, IPI, timer), APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL execution, SEV-TIO trusted device requests, and Secure AVIC backing page management. The specification details required NAE events, GHCB layout, MSR protocol request/response codes, negotiation examples, and handling of NMIs, debug registers, and SMP booting under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP.

In Hogg’s Estate, the court considered exceptions to an auditing judge’s decision regarding distribution of a trust principal. The testator’s will provided life estates to his four named children, with income provisions for their issue, and upon the death of the last surviving child, the principal to “grandchildren” per stirpes. After the will’s execution, three afterborn children were born; by law, the will was partially revoked as to them, and they received intestate shares. The trust was funded with the remaining estate. At distribution, three of the four named children had died without issue, one named child left three grandchildren, and one afterborn child left two grandchildren. The auditing judge awarded half the trust to the two grandchildren of the afterborn child and the other half in thirds to the three grandchildren of the named child.

The majority opinion (Bok, J.) affirmed, holding that the word “grandchildren” unambiguously means all grandchildren, including those of afterborn children. It reasoned that an heir cannot be disinherited except by express words or necessary implication, and the will contained no such language. The natural meaning of the term controls, and the “per stirpes” designation only determines shares, not which lines qualify. The court rejected arguments that the testator did not anticipate afterborn children, noting the language is clear and the statute letting in afterborn children does not exhaust the share their issue may take under a fitting description.

The dissenting opinion (Steakne, J., joined by Sinkler, J.) argued that the court’s duty is to ascertain the testator’s intent from the whole will and circumstances at execution. It contended the testamentary scheme showed the testator’s bounty was directed solely to his four named children and their issue; the only grandchildren contemplated were those of the named children. The dissent would read “grandchildren” as referring to the previously mentioned grandchildren, i.e., issue of the named children, to avoid an unjust distribution where afterborn children’s issue receive a larger share than the named children’s issue, contrary to the testator’s plain intent.

Lake Lugano, a glacial lake in Switzerland's Italian-speaking canton of Ticino, is a quieter alternative to the crowded Lake Como, which draws around 1.4 million visitors. About 40 kilometers west, it has a mild, sunny climate, palm-lined promenades, cobbled streets, and a waterfront free of tourist throngs. Guide Walter Di Liberto describes the deep blue water, soft romantic scenery, and golden sunsets. Tour operator Jacqué Gabellone notes Lugano is overshadowed by Como and Maggiore, offering Swiss precision and Italian charm, ideal for culture and nature without crowds. It straddles the Swiss-Italian border, reflecting both cultures with a relaxed pace. Lugano hosts music festivals, open-air markets, and cozy cafés. Villages like Gandria (fishing village, boat access, Olive Grove Trail), Morcote (old houses, church, Parco Scherrer, Locanda Gandriese), and Bré (funicular, medieval town, art) see fewer tourists. Monte San Salvatore and Monte Generoso offer funicular rides, hiking trails, and summit views. Parks include Parco Ciano, Parco San Grato with azaleas and rhododendrons. Recommended activities: wine tasting of Ticino's merlot, dining at Grotto Morchino or Grotto dei Pescatori Caprino (boat access only). Grand Hotel Villa Castagnola is a five-star resort in a 19th-century villa. Experts advise taking local ferries. Lake Lugano remains under the radar, emphasizing small moments like a coffee by the lake.

FULE logically erases the entire user area. The command sequence is CMD32 (argument 0), CMD33 (argument end of user area), then CMD38 (argument 00000002h). The host must check the FULE_SUPPORT bit; if unsupported, the host shall not issue FULE and the card executes ERASE. Out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET and reset the sequence. If the full user area is not provided, the card executes ERASE with a busy timeout. FULE is supported only on SDHC and SDXC cards, not via SPI. The card indicates progress by holding DAT0 low.

The COVIDFast assay is an extraction-free RT-qPCR method for rapid, high-throughput SARS-CoV-2 detection from anterior nares swabs (SwabFAST) or saliva (SalivaFAST). Conventional PCR requires a laborious, expensive nucleic acid extraction step that creates bottlenecks, contamination risks, and supply shortages. COVIDFast bypasses extraction using a proprietary buffer and proteinase K digestion. For swabs, the viral transport buffer (VTB) contains Tris-Borate-EDTA; for saliva, a Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine buffer improves proteinase K efficacy. VTB remained stable across temperatures from -80°C to 37°C for up to 32 weeks. The assay uses uniform 2 mL bar-coded cryovials with screw caps, enabling automated decapping and high-throughput processing. Analytical validation showed equivalent Cq values between extraction-free and extracted methods, and a limit of detection of 4 copies/µL with >95% positivity. Clinical validation on swab samples showed 100% positive and negative percent agreement versus extracted PCR; for saliva, 98.8% positive and 99.4% negative agreement. Compared to SalivaDirect, SwabFAST had 83.3% positive and 99.4% negative agreement (179 paired samples), while SalivaFAST had 95% positive and 100% negative agreement (40 samples). In real-world testing of 409,883 samples, 83.62% were SwabFAST, with an overall positive rate of 8.10%. The extraction-free, high-throughput system reduces costs and turnaround time, and the authors state it is the first direct-to-PCR assay for nasal swabs, with potential expansion to other pathogens.

The Dogs of the Dow (DOD) is a stock-picking strategy that selects the 10 highest dividend-yielding stocks from the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA). It attempts to beat the DJIA by investing equal dollar amounts in these stocks at the start of each calendar year, based on dividend yields at the last trading day of the previous year, and rebalancing annually. The strategy gained popularity in 1991 through Michael B. O’Higgins’ book 'Beating the Dow,' though the concept appeared earlier in a 1951 article by H. G. Schneider and in The Wall Street Journal in the early 1980s. Investors can implement the strategy by buying individual stocks, or through ETFs such as SDOG, IDOG, and EDOG, or mutual funds. Backtests show underperformance: a $10,000 investment from August 1998 grew to $32,000 for DOD versus $60,000 for the S&P 500 (CAGR 5% vs 7.7%). From April 2014, $10,000 in SDOG reached $19,000, IDOG $11,600, EDOG $11,200, compared to $23,300 for the S&P 500. All DOD-related ETFs underperformed the broad market. The strategy is simple but has underperformed significantly over the last couple of decades, and the passage suggests it should only be a small part of a portfolio due to poor diversification.

In Betteys v. Ætna Life Insurance Co., the beneficiary sued for death benefits and weekly disability indemnity under an accident policy. The insurer denied liability for the death benefit, claiming death resulted from disease, but offered to consider a disability claim. The court held that the insurer’s denial of liability excused the plaintiff from making proof of death, but did not waive the contractual time limit for bringing suit. The plaintiff failed to file suit within the required period (one year from the date proofs were due, effectively 14 months after death), despite having nearly eight months after the denial. Consequently, the death benefit claim was barred. The judgment was reversed and a new trial granted solely on the disability indemnity claim.

This paper proposes a hybrid deep learning framework, DNN-Transformer-AE, for corporate tax risk supervision and risk-level assessment. The model integrates three modules: a Deep Neural Network (DNN) for static enterprise features, a Transformer for temporal financial data, and an Autoencoder (AE) for anomaly detection via reconstruction error. Outputs are fused and mapped to risk scores, classifying enterprises into high, medium, or low risk. Experiments use a real-world dataset of approximately 12,000 enterprises across multiple industries, with static features, time-series financial indicators, and expert-assigned risk labels. The proposed model achieves accuracy of 0.91, recall of 0.86, and macro F1-score of 0.88, outperforming logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and DNN-LSTM baselines. Training loss curves show stable convergence, with validation loss consistently lower than training loss, indicating strong generalization. The framework captures complex risk patterns by combining static attributes, temporal dependencies, and anomaly signals, enabling more accurate identification of high-risk firms. The study notes practical relevance for precision supervision and resource allocation, but acknowledges limitations: input features are confined to financial and operational indicators, excluding macroeconomic conditions and inter-firm relationships, and computational complexity may hinder deployment in resource-constrained settings. Future work could integrate macroeconomic data and develop interpretable, lightweight models.

The passage investigates orbital degrees of freedom (ODF) in magnon–phonon coupled systems. It notes that while ODF in electrons and magnons has been studied, phonon ODF remains poorly understood. In hybridized magnon-polaron systems, ODF arises from two mechanisms: global rotation and quantum geometry of wavefunctions. The quantum geometric contribution is linked to the quasi–quantum geometric tensor. Focusing on a 2D antiferromagnetic honeycomb lattice with Néel order, the study shows that magnon–phonon coupling breaks combined parity-time (P⊕T) symmetry, enabling phonon-dominated portions of magnon-polarons to acquire finite intra-band orbital angular momentum (OAM). Out-of-plane phonon modes gain finite out-of-plane OAM through hybridization with magnons. This OAM, together with the magnetic moment of the magnon component, is predicted to produce a measurable transverse voltage under a temperature or strain gradient. The transverse voltage comprises spin Berry curvature and orbital moment contributions; under low magnetic fields in MnPS3, the orbital contribution can dominate, and total electric polarization is enhanced by 5–6 orders of magnitude compared to cases without magnon-phonon coupling. The effect persists at zero temperature and increases with temperature and coupling strength. The results demonstrate that magnon–phonon coupling converts ODF between bosonic quasiparticles via symmetry breaking and inter-band transitions, significantly enhancing electric activity and enabling electrical control over magnetization and phononic transport without external fields. The quantum geometric origin of ODF is universal for bosonic and fermionic quasiparticles. The work lays a foundation for phonon orbitronics and bridges phonon and magnon orbitronics.

The passage details SD card physical layer operations. A tuning block (CMD19) is used to tune the sampling point, mandatory for HOST-SDR-VD and optional for HOST-SDR-FD, compensating for static delays. CMD19 is a Send Tuning Block Command with R1 response, executed in transfer state at 1.8V signaling while the card is unlocked; otherwise it is illegal. The data block on DAT[3:0] contains a tuning pattern, block length is fixed, and CMD16 is not required. A tuning sequence consists of up to 40 consecutive CMD19 executions completed within 150ms, excluding host processing time.

During Card Identification Mode the host remains at fOD frequency. In Data Transfer Mode, the host may use fPP frequency. CMD9 obtains CSD, CMD4 configures driver stages, and CMD7 selects one card into Transfer State, releasing any previously selected card. CMD7 with RCA=0x0000 returns all cards to Stand-by State. Data transfer is point-to-point. Read commands (CMD17, CMD18, etc.) and write commands (CMD24, CMD25, etc.) can be aborted by CMD12. Write commands must be stopped before deselecting with CMD7. After data transfer, the card moves to Programming State or Transfer State. Block write may be buffered, with DAT0 held low when buffers are full. No buffering exists for write CSD, write protection, or erase. Parameter set and read commands are not allowed during programming. Reselecting a card during busy moves it to Disconnect State, releasing DAT; reselection reactivates busy. CMD0 or CMD15 resets the card, potentially destroying data. Wide bus (4-bit) mode is selected/deselected with ACMD6; default is 1-bit. A locked card treats ACMD6 as illegal.

For 2GByte cards, maximum block length is 1024 bytes, but CMD16 sets block length up to 512 bytes. Data blocks consist of start bits, payload, CRC, and end bits. Read commands are rejected on BLOCK_LEN_ERROR or ADDRESS_ERROR. CMD17 reads a single block, CMD18 reads multiple blocks until CMD12. Partial block misalignment causes ADDRESS_ERROR and aborts transmission. Write data blocks include CRC; write commands are rejected on errors. Block length set by CMD16 must be 512 bytes regardless of WRITE_BL_LEN. Partial write is allowed if WRITE_BL_PARTIAL=1. Misalignment aborts programming. Write over protected areas sets WP_VIOLATION. CSD programming requires matching ROM content. The host can poll status with CMD13; READY_FOR_DATA indicates readiness. Pre-erase (ACMD23) speeds multiple block write; ACMD22 reports the number of well-written blocks.

Erase is performed with CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38. Out-of-sequence commands set ERASE_SEQ_ERROR and reset the sequence. Write-protected sectors are skipped, setting WP_ERASE_SKIP. Erase busy is indicated by DAT0 low. DISCARD (CMD38 with argument 00000001h) is similar to erase, supported only on SDHC/SDXC, with a 250ms busy timeout. FULE (CMD38 with argument 00000002h) logically erases the entire user area, with a 1-second busy timeout. Both require checking support bits in SD_STATUS.

Write protection includes a mechanical switch (host responsibility), internal card protection (optional), and password protection. Password lock uses PWD and PWD_LEN registers; locked cards accept basic commands, ACMD41, CMD16, and lock card commands. If PWD is set, the card locks after power-on. Lock/unlock uses a single block write command with a data block containing mode, password length, and password. COP adds FEP and FEP_LEN registers. COP cards start in CMD42 Ver.1.0 compatible mode; if FEP=1, the card is COP locked and requires COP Unlock (CMD42[1Fh]) to enable Ver.2.0 mode. COP functions include FEP management, Force Erase (disabled when FEP=set), and FEP Force Erase (enabled when FEP=set). Force Erase erases all content and PWD; FEP Force Erase does the same but leaves FEP unchanged. ACMD6 is rejected when locked. Locked cards accept specific commands; others are illegal. Three lock/unlock card types exist, with Type 3 (COP) defined from Version 5.10.

APP_CMD (CMD55) makes the next command an application-specific command (ACMD). Reserved ACMDs include ACMD6, ACMD13, etc. ACMD41 response lacks APP_CMD status. CMD6 (Switch Function) manages access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. It operates in Mode 0 (check) and Mode 1 (set), returning 512 bits of status. Switching takes effect within 8 clocks. Power Limit default is 0.72W; higher limits enable better performance. UHS-II mode does not use function groups 1 and 3, requires group 4. High-Speed mode (25 MB/sec) uses 50 MHz clock and requires 1-to-1 connection. Command system expansion uses CMD34-37, CMD50, CMD57. CMD8 checks voltage compatibility in Idle state, returning R7. SDHC/SDXC use block addressing with fixed 512-byte blocks, disable partial/misalign access, and do not support write-protected groups.

The host can change or stop the clock, but must provide 8 clocks after a transaction. For ACMD41, continuous clock at 100–400 KHz or polling at <50ms intervals is required. CRC7 protects commands, responses, CSD, and CID; CRC16 protects data blocks. CRC errors cause no response and set COM_CRC_ERROR; illegal commands set ILLEGAL_COMMAND. Read timeout is the lower of 100× typical access time or 100ms; write timeout is the lower of 100× typical program time or 250ms. For High Capacity cards, busy maximum is 250ms for all writes.

This study investigates equilibrium vacancy concentrations in a nine-component refractory multi-principal element alloy comprising elements from groups 4, 5, and 6 of the periodic table. An embedded cluster expansion (eCE) model, parameterized using density functional theory calculations, accurately reproduces the ordering energetics of all nine elements and vacancies on the body-centered cubic crystal structure. A coarse-graining method is extended to compute finite-temperature equilibrium vacancy concentrations within the canonical ensemble using Monte Carlo simulations. Finite-temperature calculations reveal that alloys composed solely of group 5 and 6 elements exhibit extremely low vacancy concentrations, while the addition of group 4 elements significantly increases vacancy concentrations by a factor of 10–100. The equilibrium vacancy concentration shows a strong dependence on short-range order and bonding energies: element pairs that form strong bonds decrease vacancy concentrations, whereas unfavorable bonding increases them. Local elemental segregation around vacancies is predicted, with enhanced concentrations of Zr and Hf in the first nearest-neighbor shell and Mo in the second shell, consistent with dilute solute-vacancy binding trends. Comparisons with special quasi-random structure (SQS)-based methods show that SQS approaches underestimate vacancy concentrations due to neglecting short-range order and finite-size effects. The methodology neglects vibrational entropy and divacancy formation.

The value area trading strategy uses the volume profile to identify the price range where the majority of trading activity occurred. The value area is defined as the range where 70% of total trading volume took place, roughly one standard deviation from the mean. This area highlights key support and resistance levels. Traders use it to spot potential buying and selling opportunities, looking for price action that signals a breakout or reversal. The strategy is used in futures, stock, and forex markets, and can be applied to intraday, daily, weekly, or monthly timeframes. Benefits include a clear method to identify support and resistance. Risks include false signals, the value area changing over time, and the need to combine it with other factors. Risk management involves stop-loss orders, position sizing, portfolio diversification, and maintaining discipline. Price action around the value area provides information: a breakout above the high or below the low may indicate trending, while a failure to break through suggests consolidation or reversal. Traders can use value areas to set stop losses and profit targets, and to confirm signals from other strategies. Backtesting the strategy is difficult and requires specific trading rules.

In Waterhouse v. Gibson, the plaintiff sued for trespass after defendants removed a barn and blacksmith’s shop from land he had purchased. The land had been set off to Brooks under an execution against Jack, with the returns describing the land by metes and bounds and containing no exception of the buildings. The defendants sought to introduce parol evidence that the creditor’s attorney had intended to exclude the buildings (which stood on blocks without foundations), that the attorney accidentally omitted the exception from the returns, and that the plaintiff knew the buildings were not included. The trial judge rejected this evidence, and a verdict was returned for the plaintiff. On appeal, the court held that a levy by extent has the same effect as a deed, so buildings on the land pass with it. Exceptions for trade fixtures erected by lessees do not apply to buildings owned by the landowner. Parol evidence cannot be used to contradict the written returns. The evidence was properly rejected, and judgment was affirmed on the verdict.

The passage discusses bond trading strategies, focusing on Treasury bonds. A bond is a loan where the issuer pays interest and returns principal at maturity. A bond trading strategy is a systematic plan to buy/sell bonds for objectives like capital preservation, income, or appreciation. Strategies vary by time horizon, risk tolerance, and market conditions; common types include yield curve, duration, credit spread, and tactical asset allocation strategies. Common mistakes include insufficient market understanding, overreliance on historical data, neglecting risk management, chasing yield without assessing credit/liquidity risks, misjudging interest rates, inadequate diversification, inflexibility, and emotional biases. Bond prices fluctuate inversely with interest rates: an example shows a $1 million 10-year Treasury bought at 0.5% semiannual yield later worth $800,000 when rates rose, illustrating interest rate risk. Bond trading strategies offer diversification and uncorrelated returns relative to stocks; the 25-day rolling correlation between SPY (S&P 500) and TLT (20-year Treasury ETF) is around zero most of the time. Several backtested strategies on TLT are presented: a seasonal strategy called "Calendar Effects In Long-Term Treasuries" with simple rules, returning more than twice buy-and-hold with 61.8% time invested and a risk-adjusted return of 16.2%; a monthly trading edge from June 2021 with three buy variables and a straightforward exit; a seasonal short-side strategy from December 2022 using seasonal and intermarket variables; and a swing trade strategy from March 2023 with price action and seasonal variables. Combining TLT strategies 3 and 4 with an S&P 500 beginner strategy bundle increased annual returns from 11.5% to 18.6% and decreased drawdowns, demonstrating complementary diversification. The article concludes that adding complementary bond strategies improves overall trading performance. Interest rates significantly impact bond strategies: rising rates lower bond prices, leading to strategies like riding the yield curve; falling rates favor shorter-term bonds. Day trading bonds involves same-day buying/selling, is more challenging than stocks due to lower volatility and sensitivity to rates, and typically focuses on liquid government bonds. Bond trading strategies can be automated using algorithmic systems that analyze data and execute trades based on predefined criteria, but human oversight remains crucial. For beginners, dollar-cost averaging—investing a fixed amount regularly—is a specific strategy to reduce market fluctuation impact.

Molecular augmented dynamics (MAD) is introduced as an O(N) modified molecular dynamics method to obtain low-energy, ab-initio accurate atomistic structures matching experimental data. Standard Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations often fail to guarantee experimental agreement. Hybrid reverse Monte Carlo (HRMC) methods improve agreement but suffer from computational inefficiency and unphysical artifacts due to simple potentials. A recent HRMC with machine learning potentials achieved ab-initio accuracy and matched XPS spectra, but remained limited to a few thousand atoms and required many energy evaluations. Previous MD attempts with experimental potentials had scaling and accuracy issues, lacking analytic gradients and thermal broadening. MAD uses a Hamiltonian H = T + V + ˜V, where V is the interatomic potential and ˜V is an experimental potential measuring deviation from experimental data, enabling multi-objective optimization. The article provides derivations of analytic, linearly scaling forces for XRD, ND, PDF, and XPS observables that account for thermal broadening. The experimental potential is defined as ˜V = (γ/2) Σ w_i^2 (incomplete).

Researchers from the Institute of Synthetic Polymer Materials, MIPT, and elsewhere studied how polypropylene's molecular regularity (isotacticity) and thermal treatment affect mechanical properties. Isotacticity, measured by pentad content, indicates the proportion of isotactic five-unit segments that effectively form crosslinks, creating crystalline regions (crystallites) that increase hardness. They examined polypropylene samples with isotacticities from 25% to over 95%, prepared as films via quenching in ice water or slow cooling (3°C/min), then stretched them at 10 mm/min. Mechanical tests showed that strain behavior depended on isotacticity and cooling rate. The relationship was depicted as elastic modulus versus degree of crystallinity; higher elastic moduli correspond to tougher materials. Crystallite forms differed between quenched and slowly cooled samples. The findings enable synthesis of polypropylene with predetermined properties like elasticity or hardness. The major conclusion is that during synthesis, determining the molecule's structure also determines the network and thus the material's properties. The study was published in Polymer.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) allows the A100 to be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU instances, each with dedicated compute, memory, and cache resources, providing quality of service and fault isolation for multi-tenant environments. This study used spatial transcriptomics (Visium and CosMx) to analyze skin biopsies from patients with cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) from Sri Lanka, Brazil, and post kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis (PKDL) from India. IDO1 and CD274 (PD-L1) transcripts localized to myeloid cell-rich niches in the papillary dermis and T cell-rich regions. Mature dendritic cells (DC3) and CCL18+ macrophages were the predominant IDO1hi CD274hi cells. Neighbourhood analysis identified CD8+ memory T cells and regulatory T cells (Tregs) as the most common immediate neighbours of IDO1+/CD274+ myeloid cells. IL32 was highly expressed in these niches, primarily by CD8+ memory T cells and Tregs, while CXCL9 and CCL18 were expressed by myeloid cells. A core gene signature (IL32, LYZ, GBP1, IFI30, FTH1) correlated with IDO1 and CD274 across all three disease forms. In Sri Lankan CL patients, high abundance of IL-32+CD8+ T cells was associated with slower healing following sodium stibogluconate treatment, identifying it as a prognostic biomarker. The results suggest that IL-32+ T cells contribute to the generation of immunosuppressive IDO1/PD-L1 niches in CL lesions.

A study explored the empathic profile of 206 university teachers from Education faculties at University G in Spain using the Interpersonal Reactivity Index (IRI), which measures Perspective Taking, Fantasy, Empathic Concern, and Personal Distress. The Bearish Engulfing candlestick pattern is a two-candle formation appearing in an uptrend, consisting of a small bullish candle followed by a larger bearish candle that completely engulfs the previous body. It indicates a potential shift from bullish to bearish sentiment, with sellers taking control. Traders use it to identify possible trend reversals, close long positions, or enter short positions, typically placing a stop-loss above the high of the first candle. Backtesting on the S&P 500 since 1993 shows a success rate between 55% and 65%, with 311 occurrences, making it the third most frequent candlestick pattern. The pattern’s reliability can be improved by adding indicators; for example, filtering trades with a 5-day RSI above 60 raised the average gain per trade from 0.73% to 0.88%. It is considered reliable but not guaranteed, and should be used alongside other technical analysis tools and risk management. Risks include false signals, market conditions, and volatility. Risk management strategies include stop-loss orders, risk/reward ratios, position sizing, diversification, and hedging. Other bearish reversal patterns—dark cloud cover, evening star, and bearish harami—indicate weaker bearish sentiment. The Bearish Engulfing differs from the Bullish Engulfing, which signals a reversal from a downtrend to an uptrend. Despite its name, the pattern is described as “pretty bullish” in the stock market. Advantages include providing value for bullish reversals; disadvantages include subjectivity and false signals. Confirmation can be sought through other technical indicators, changes in market momentum, and the broader context.

The 50 EMA strategy is a simple, popular trend-following technical analysis strategy that uses the 50-day exponential moving average to identify medium-term trends and generate buy and sell signals. An upward-sloping 50 EMA with price predominantly above it indicates an uptrend; a downward-sloping EMA with price below indicates a downtrend. Traders often combine it with indicators like RSI or MACD for confirmation. A basic moving average crossover system backtested on GLD performed poorly. On the S&P 500 from 1960, it yielded 6.8% annual returns with a 32% max drawdown, versus buy-and-hold’s 7.3% and 56%. Adding a second indicator as a filter improved results: on QQQ, the strategy achieved 11.5% CAGR, 22% max drawdown, and was invested 27% of the time; on SPY, 8.9% annual returns, 16% max drawdown, invested 29% of the time. On TLT, the average gain per trade was 0.18%. The strategy is typically applied on 4-hour or daily charts. Effective use involves confirming signals, considering stop-losses (though backtests rarely show improvement), and adjusting for market conditions. The AMD Secure RNG Library provides an API for accessing hardware-generated random numbers from AMD processors. The hardware exposes RDRAND and RDSEED x86 instructions to read random values. The library abstracts low-level programming, allowing applications to request single random values or streams. It handles hardware failure checks and retry attempts. The library includes functions like get_rdrand16u, get_rdrand32u, get_rdrand64u, and corresponding array and byte-array versions, as well as RDSEED equivalents. Support for RDRAND and RDSEED can be checked via is_RDRAND_supported and is_RDSEED_supported APIs using CPUID. Random numbers are critical for HPC, cryptography, and seeding PRNGs. AMD Zen processors include a cryptographic co-processor for RNG. Accessing the hardware via MMIO is slower than software PRNGs, but for latency-sensitive applications a hybrid approach seeding a PRNG with hardware values can improve performance while maintaining security. The study assessed the effect of enforcing Kenya's national referral guidelines at Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) on orthopaedic facility referrals. A pre-post design compared 220 referrals before (February–June 2021) and 248 after (August–December 2021) the July 1, 2021 enforcement. Nairobi County and neighboring counties accounted for over four-fifths of referrals. Government facilities comprised about three-fifths of referrals, private facilities two-fifths. After enforcement, there was a statistically significant reduction in direct referrals from tier II and III health facilities, and an increase from tiers IV, V, and VI. Tier II referrals were 90.8% less likely compared to tier III. 43 facilities ceased referring, over two-thirds private and over four-fifths from tiers II–IV. Major factors associated with referrals were human resource capacity and availability, health facility infrastructure, orthopaedic equipment and implants, patient preference, and financial considerations. Patient preference was a significant factor for private facility referrals. The study concluded that enforcement reduced lower-tier facility referrals and that implementing referral guidelines is possible.

New research suggests probiotics may help protect the liver from drug- and alcohol-induced damage. The liver, the body’s largest internal organ, filters consumed substances and is downstream of the gastrointestinal tract, so gut bacteria composition could affect its function. Emory University researchers tested the probiotic Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) in mice. Mice fed an LGG-rich diet for two weeks before receiving high doses of acetaminophen showed an improved antioxidant response, protecting the liver from oxidative damage. Acetaminophen overuse can cause liver damage by increasing free radicals and oxidative stress. The study indicates the protein Nrf2 plays a pivotal role in this protection. While results in mice are promising, further studies are needed to replicate them in humans. Probiotics are not a substitute for medicine, and consulting a doctor before supplementation is advised.

The passage discusses the state of global education and the role of Comparative and International Education. Despite a 70-year education expansion, by 2020 deficiencies remained, aggravated by COVID-19. The field studies education systems in societal contexts and guides toward Sustainable Development Goal 4. The paper reflects on the pandemic's implications for the field in 2023. It outlines the 2030 vision: the UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals, with Goal 4 focusing on inclusive, equitable quality education and lifelong learning. The Incheon Declaration unpacked Goal 4, viewing education as a means to achieve other goals. By 2015, there was a massive shortfall: 258 million children were out of school; quality was lacking across input, process, output, and product dimensions (e.g., UK adults with primary-level numeracy); and stark inequalities existed along socio-economic, gender, and ethnic lines (e.g., gender wage gaps in Saudi Arabia). The COVID-19 pandemic caused school closures affecting 91% of students and a shift to distance learning, which ended education opportunities for many, reduced quality, and worsened inequalities, as illustrated by a South African survey showing lost teacher contact and inability to send homework, disproportionately affecting disadvantaged learners. However, the pandemic also forced the conservative education sector to embrace technology. The paper argues that Comparative and International Education should investigate these pandemic-induced changes and technology use across diverse contexts to generate recommendations for achieving the 2030 education goals. This effort could also address the field's shortcomings: unresponsiveness, the "black box syndrome" (overemphasis on societal context neglecting classroom processes), lack of autochthonous theory, inadequate university presence, Northern hegemony, and limited impact. In conclusion, while the pandemic made achieving the 2030 vision harder, it also spurred technological adoption. Comparative and International Education is pivotal in using these experiences to build new, better education systems that surpass pre-pandemic levels.

In Closson v. Billman, the plaintiff sought to foreclose a materialman's lien for lumber used in a house built by contractor Worley for the defendants. The defendants answered that the plaintiff had been a guarantor on Worley's bond, which was conditioned on Worley completing the residence according to his contract. The contract required Worley to furnish and pay for materials. The court held that the bond and contract, construed together, obligated Worley to deliver the building free of liens, so the guarantor was liable for the lien amount. The court ruled that one who joins in signing a contractor's bond conditioned on the contractor's performance is a guarantor, not a surety. The answer showing the plaintiff's liability on the bond was a sufficient defense to avoid circuity of action. A guaranty executed contemporaneously with the guaranteed transaction requires no notice of acceptance. The burden is on the guarantor to plead and prove any omission of notice of default and resulting damage. The judgment for defendants was affirmed.

The 1-2-2 zone is used against outside shooting, fast breaks, and to protect leads. Alignment: point at top of circle, wings at elbows, baselines above blocks. Defenders shift on passes. Ball in corner: ball-side baseline guards ball, other baseline covers low post, weakside wing drops to baseline, ball-side wing denies corner pass, point defends high post. Ball on wing: wing guards ball, point drops to ballside elbow, opposite wing moves to middle, ball-side baseline halfway to corner, other baseline in front of basket. Ball out front: point guards ball, wings at elbows, baselines above blocks. Ball in middle: all collapse. Baseline players work in unison; wings work opposite and rebound weakside on corner passes. Point defends high post when ball is on wing or corner. Adjustments include wing corner shift options (deny pass or help post), a corner trap, switching to a 2-1-2 zone on the first pass, and extending into a press.

The present disclosure relates to route planning for automated guided vehicles (AGVs) based on a topological map. A method includes obtaining a topological map corresponding to a scheduling system; preprocessing the topological map to obtain a modified topological map by modifying node information based on motion status information of other AGVs and nodes they occupy; determining a start node and a destination node of a current AGV in the modified topological map; determining total costs for nodes between the start and destination nodes using the modified node information; and performing route planning based on those total costs. The motion status information includes static and moving statuses. Preprocessing may involve a first preprocessing that modifies node information for static AGVs (e.g., setting high weight values, marking nodes as impassable or turn-incapable) and a second preprocessing that additionally modifies nodes on planned routes of moving AGVs. A target route is determined by iteratively selecting nodes with minimum total cost, where total cost may be computed from a first cost (from start to node) and a second cost (from node to destination), incorporating weight values, distance costs, and turn costs. The disclosure also describes a device, system, and computer-readable storage medium implementing the method. Additionally, a system for route planning obtains a start location and destination of a target vehicle, a map with node information, motion status information of other vehicles, and determines a target route based on these inputs. Task allocation to idle AGVs is also described.

The document describes AMD AGESA (AMD Generic Encapsulated Software Architecture) initialization procedures, interfaces, and build integration. It details Platform PEI Modules (PEIMs) and DXE drivers that perform processor, memory, and chipset initialization. Key PPIs (e.g., AMD_PEI_INIT_EARLY_PPI, AMD_PEI_INIT_POST_PPI, AMD_MEM_INIT_PPI) are published after specific initialization steps to coordinate module execution. A memory initialization PEIM calls AGESA entry points, publishes AmdInitPostPPI, and a reset PEIM coordinates warm resets. DXE drivers include AmdCpuDxeDriver (calls AmdInitLate, publishes AgesaDxeProtocol) and AmdGpuVgaControlDxe (monitors VGA decoding). Build integration requires setting environment variables (AGESA_ROOT, AGESA_OptsDir), copying platform option files, and using control files (e.g., AgesaPei0Libs.inf). Stack procedures (AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK, AMD_DISABLE_UEFI_STACK) establish and tear down pre-memory stacks. Entry procedures are listed in time-point order: AmdInitReset (minimal early init), AmdInitEarly (full pre-memory init), AmdInitPost (memory init and transition to post-memory), AmdInitEnv (transfer HOBs to main memory), AmdInitMid (graphics configuration), AmdInitLate (generate ACPI/DMI tables), AmdInitRtb (save state for suspend), AmdInitResume (re-init for resume), AmdS3LateRestore, and AmdS3FinalRestore. Required host environment call-outs include AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, AgesaReset, AgesaLocateBuffer, AgesaReadSpd, and AgesaRunAp/AgesaRunAps. Numerous platform configuration structures and build options customize processor, memory, graphics, and FCH settings.

W. T. Hay, after being adjudged a voluntary bankrupt and receiving a discharge, appealed an order that refused to stay a writ of execution levied on real estate conveyed to his wife, Matilda M. Hay, prior to the bankruptcy. The Deposit National Bank had obtained a judgment against Hay and later issued execution on that judgment, alleging the conveyance was fraudulent. The lower court stayed the writ as to Hay personally and his own property, but allowed the execution to proceed against the real estate in his wife’s name. The Supreme Court dismissed Hay’s appeal, holding that he lacked standing. Hay did not own or claim the property, it was not listed in his bankruptcy schedules, and the execution was in rem, not affecting him personally or involving him in costs. Whether the bank had a right to proceed despite Hay’s discharge, and whether a sheriff’s sale would pass title given the bankruptcy trustee’s authority to recover fraudulent conveyances, are questions that do not affect Hay’s rights and cannot be raised by him. The appeal was dismissed at appellant’s costs.

Cu-doped NiO thin films were synthesized on ITO-coated glass substrates using spray pyrolysis with a deposition time of 1.5 minutes at 450 °C. XRD confirmed a cubic NiO phase; the Cu-doped film showed a peak shift from 37.2° to 37.0°, lattice expansion (a from 4.18 to 4.20 Å) due to larger Cu²⁺ ionic radius, and a crystallite size decrease from 21 to 20 nm. SEM revealed well-dispersed cuboidal/polyhedral grains. UV-Vis spectroscopy showed enhanced absorbance in the visible region for NiO:Cu, and the direct optical bandgap narrowed from 3.70 eV (NiO) to 3.65 eV (NiO:Cu). Raman spectra indicated the disappearance of the TO mode and a red shift of the LO mode from 577 to 516 cm⁻¹, reflecting lattice disorder. Photoluminescence intensity decreased upon Cu doping, particularly in the 700–808 nm region, suggesting non-radiative recombination centers. I-V measurements exhibited p-type behavior; under LPG exposure (1 vol%), the current increased. At 5 V bias, the current rose from 249 to 327 mA for NiO and from 265 to 480 mA for NiO:Cu. Sensitivity (IG/IA) at 5 V was 1.3 for NiO and 1.8 for NiO:Cu. The enhanced gas sensing performance is attributed to improved charge transport, increased adsorption sites, and surface reactivity from Cu incorporation. The study demonstrates that ultra-fast spray-pyrolyzed Cu-doped NiO films are promising for low-cost, efficient gas sensors.

A new study suggests dopamine plays a role in mother-baby bonding. Researchers studied 19 mothers and their infants, video-recording interactions and scanning mothers' brains as they watched videos of their own or other babies. Mothers secreted more dopamine when viewing their own infants. Those who secreted more dopamine provided more optimal care, were more sensitive, and adjusted their behavior to meet needs. Less responsive mothers secreted less dopamine, offering clues to caregiving difficulties. Co-author Lisa Feldman Barrett said responsive care may support infant brain development; inadequate care could lead to poor school performance, lower achievement, and risk for mental and physical disease in adulthood. Fathers and other caregivers might also experience a dopamine boost, but more research is needed. Paul Zak noted the study is small and cannot determine if great mothers are born or made. The study was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

This study models the global risk of selection and spread of pfhrp2/3 gene deletions that cause false-negative malaria rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs). An individual-based transmission model was updated with new data on pfhrp3 dynamics, fitness costs, and cross-reactivity of HRP3 epitopes. Parameter estimates were sourced for malaria prevalence, treatment-seeking, RDT usage, and other factors across malaria-endemic regions. Model fitting to surveys in Eritrea and Ethiopia estimated a relative fitness of 96.4% for pfhrp2-deleted parasites and a 29.0% probability that pfhrp2-deleted infections with intact pfhrp3 still yield a positive HRP2-based RDT. Malaria prevalence was the most important driver of selection, with faster spread predicted at low prevalence. Two risk scores were produced: an Innate Risk Score (time for clinically misdiagnosed cases to rise from 1% to 5% assuming exclusive HRP2-RDT use) and a Prospective Risk Score (incorporating current deletion prevalence and RDT types). High innate risk was identified in many low-transmission regions, particularly in the Horn of Africa, East Africa, and parts of West Africa. Prospective modeling predicted deletions spreading south from the Horn of Africa through East Africa over 20 years. Countries with majority high-risk administrative units include Eritrea, Ethiopia, Senegal, Kenya, and Zambia. Considerable uncertainty remains due to data gaps and variability in malaria prevalence estimates. The authors provide an interactive tool to explore risk maps and emphasize the need for prioritized surveillance and potential switching to non-HRP2-based RDTs.

The lecture discusses protein folding modeled as fixed-angle linkages. The protein backbone is a chain with fixed edge lengths and fixed angles, allowing only dihedral spins around edges. Four main problems are addressed: span, flattening, flat state connectivity, and locked chains.

Span concerns the maximum and minimum distance between endpoints of a fixed-angle open chain. Finding the min or max span in a flat (2D) configuration is NP-hard, via reduction from partition. For 3D max span, the problem remains open, though structural characterizations exist. For orthogonal chains, max span can be computed in linear time using a shortest-path approach on a triangulated staircase.

Flattening asks whether a fixed-angle chain has any flat state without self-intersection. This problem is NP-hard, shown by a construction that forces endpoint alignment only if a partition exists. The reduction uses exponentially large length ratios; the case of equal or polynomially bounded link lengths is open.

Flat state connectivity asks whether all flat states of a fixed-angle chain belong to a single connected component of the configuration space. It is unknown whether every open chain is flat state connected. Positive results exist for chains with obtuse or orthogonal angles, and for equal acute angles under certain conditions. A disconnected example exists for a partially rigid fixed-angle tree with four arms, where two arms must move to the same side of the plane, leading to unavoidable collision proved via knot theory. For orthogonal and obtuse open chains, a simple algorithm lifts the chain into a canonical staircase or monotone state, proving flat state connectivity.

Locked chains: Fixed-angle linkages can be locked even with equilateral and equiangular constraints (e.g., a crossed-legs example with four edges and 45° angles, though a formal proof is pending). However, if the chain is also required to be obtuse, equilateral, and equiangular, the existence of a locked chain is open. The intuition is that obtuse fixed-angle chains may behave like universal joints, where equilateral locking is unknown.

The final part introduces producible protein chains, modeling protein creation by the ribosome. The ribosome is treated as a cone of half-angle alpha; the chain emerges link by link from the apex and cannot penetrate the cone. A chain with all turn angles ≤ alpha is called an ≤alpha chain. A canonical configuration (alpha CCC) is defined: starting from the cone's apex, each successive vertex is placed at the intersection of a vertical cone (half-angle alpha/2) and a cone determined by the fixed turn angle, choosing the counterclockwise-most intersection. This canonical configuration lies entirely within an alpha/2 half-angle cone.

Using the momento method (playing the production movie backwards), any producible configuration can be continuously moved into the canonical configuration while staying inside the ribosome cone and avoiding self-intersection. Tilting the canonical cone by at most alpha/2 ensures it remains inside the larger ribosome cone. Consequently, all producible configurations belong to one connected component. Flat states are shown to be producible, so producible chains are flat state connected. The entire process is algorithmic, offering a candidate mechanism for how proteins might fold mechanically.

Trauma, defined by SAMHSA as a harmful or threatening experience with lasting negative effects, includes adverse childhood experiences (ACEs). An estimated 50–70% of post-secondary students have experienced at least one ACE. Trauma can impair attendance, academic performance, behavior, cognition, and social functioning, and is associated with increased isolation and dropout risk. Studies of occupational therapy (OT) students found trauma affected daily routines and education, with many not disclosing trauma due to stigma.

The SAMHSA trauma-informed care (TIC) framework comprises six core principles (safety; trustworthiness and transparency; peer support; collaboration and mutuality; empowerment, voice, and choice; and cultural, historical, and gender issues) and ten implementation domains (e.g., governance, training, physical environment, policy, evaluation). The paper describes TIC models and interventions for health professions education, including the PATH simulation-based model, which increased OT students’ knowledge and self-efficacy regarding ACEs and TIC, and health and wellness coaching. Trauma-informed educational strategies for OT educators include seeking professional development, providing advance notice of triggering content, incorporating self-care modules and check-ins, ensuring equal participation, fostering safe physical and psychological environments, and using predictable routines and universal design. The paper concludes that TIC practices may mitigate trauma’s effects on learning and improve student support, retention, and academic success.

Robert Stuart's work alleges possible fabrications in the BBC Panorama documentary "Saving Syria's Children." The documentary originated from an August 29, 2013 BBC news segment claiming a Syrian jet dropped a napalm-type bomb on a school near Aleppo, with footage of victims at Atareb hospital. The passage highlights discrepancies: medical professionals questioned the injuries; victim numbers varied (Dr Ahsan: 25 then 40, Ian Pannell: 30, Hand in Hand For Syria: 50); and attack timing varied by up to six hours (Pannell: around 5:30, Conway: between 3 and 5). It notes Dr Saleyah Ahsan is a former British Army captain who served in Bosnia and Libya, and her ex-CO runs medical simulation training. Dr Rola Hallam is an executive at Hand in Hand For Syria; her father may be connected to the Syrian National Council, with conflicting statements. The passage asserts the evidence points to fakery, with questionable injuries, inconsistent narrative, and timing aligned with a pro-West agenda.

Researchers achieved a proof-of-concept for creating human egg cells from skin cells. They used somatic cell nuclear transfer, inserting a fibroblast nucleus into an enucleated egg, then fertilized it and added roscovitine to induce chromosome reduction. Some resulting cells formed early embryos, but all had abnormal chromosome numbers and were nonviable. The technique is inefficient and high-risk, not ready for clinical use. It could potentially treat infertility in women without eggs or enable same-sex male couples to have genetically related children, but clinical trials are at least a decade away and may not occur in the U.S. due to restrictions on genetic modification of embryos. The method requires donor eggs, unlike other reprogramming approaches. Experts call it a significant breakthrough in halving the human genome, though improvements are needed.

In People v Helzer, the Michigan Supreme Court held that sexual delinquency is an alternate sentencing provision, not a penalty enhancement, and requires a separate jury from the one deciding the principal charge. The second jury must be empaneled unless waived, and the defendant is entitled to 20 peremptory challenges because of the possible life sentence. The initial jury on the principal charge receives only the number of challenges appropriate to that offense’s penalty. The sexual delinquency charge must be brought in the original indictment before trial; amendments are allowed before trial but not after. No reference to the delinquency charge may be made to the first jury; if that jury learns of it, mistrial or reversible error results. The Court found no error in the trial on the principal charge, affirmed the conviction, but remanded for a separate jury hearing on sexual delinquency with 20 peremptory challenges. If the prosecutor does not pursue the charge or the defendant is found not guilty, resentencing on the principal charge alone will occur. Constitutional claims were not addressed. Chief Justice Kavanagh dissented, arguing the sexual delinquency statute is void for vagueness. The Court of Appeals decision was affirmed as modified.

The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture introduces GDDR6 memory, delivering 14 Gbps signaling rates and a 20% power efficiency improvement over GDDR5X. Combined with enhanced lossless memory compression techniques, Turing achieves a 50% increase in effective bandwidth compared to Pascal. Turing also features a new display engine supporting DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K resolution at 60 Hz with DSC 1.2, HDR processing with tone mapping, and an enhanced NVENC encoder supporting 8K HEVC encode at 30 fps with bitrate savings. Hardware support for USB-C and VirtualLink enables a single cable for VR headsets, carrying power, display, and data. NVLink replaces the SLI bridge, providing up to 100 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth for two-way SLI.

Turing introduces RT Cores for hardware-accelerated ray tracing, enabling real-time hybrid rendering that combines rasterization and ray tracing for reflections, shadows, and ambient occlusion. Tensor Cores accelerate AI-based features through NVIDIA NGX, including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) for performance and image quality, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. New shader capabilities include Mesh Shading with task and mesh shaders, Variable Rate Shading (VRS) for fine-grained shading rate control, Texture Space Shading (TSS) for decoupled shading, and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) supporting up to four views per pass. Turing also supports bindless resources and Tier 2 resource heaps.

The TU102 GPU contains 6 MB L2 cache, 12 ROP partitions, and two x8 second-generation NVLink links. TU104 and TU106 GPUs scale down these features, with TU104 supporting one NVLink link and TU106 lacking NVLink/SLI. The RTX-OPS metric combines FP32, INT32, RT Core, and Tensor Core operations weighted by typical hybrid rendering workloads.

The American Cancer Society updated its colorectal cancer screening guideline, recommending that average-risk adults begin screening at age 45. This change is based on rising CRC incidence in younger populations, microsimulation modeling showing a favorable benefit-to-burden balance starting at 45, and the expectation that screening performs similarly in ages 45-49 as in those 50+. The recommendation for ages 45-49 is qualified due to less direct evidence, while the recommendation for ages 50+ is strong. Screening options include stool-based tests (FIT, HSgFOBT annually; mt-sDNA every 3 years) and visual exams (colonoscopy every 10 years, CTC or FS every 5 years), with no prioritization. Positive non-colonoscopy tests require timely colonoscopy. Screening should continue through age 75 for those with >10-year life expectancy, be individualized for ages 76-85, and be discouraged after 85. CRC incidence has declined in those 55+ but increased 51% in under-50s since 1994, with rising death rates. Adults born around 1990 have double the colon cancer risk and quadruple the rectal cancer risk versus those born around 1950. New modeling incorporating these trends supported the earlier start age.

Gas colic is the least serious but very common form of colic, caused by gas buildup in the large colon when gas from normal fermentation in the hindgut fails to pass. It can lead to complications like colon displacement or twisting. Causes include inadequate forage, stall confinement, stress, ulcers, intestinal inflammation, inadequate exercise, dehydration, and abrupt feed changes. Two widespread practices contribute: 1) Limiting forage disrupts digestion—horses need 24-hour forage access to mimic natural grazing; restriction leads to hormonal imbalances, acid buildup, gorging, poor chewing, excessive gas, and ulcers that further impair motility. 2) Stall confinement reduces hindgut motility, preventing gas expulsion; lack of movement weakens colonic muscles, causing gas accumulation and pain. Stress exacerbates inflammation, leading to ulcers, malabsorption, and microbial changes that increase colic risk. Pasture turnout, even a few hours daily, reduces stress. Feed changes should be gradual—over a week for hay, 2-3 weeks for new feeds—and prebiotics can aid adjustment. Weekly bran mashes are dangerous; if fed, they must be daily and introduced slowly with calcium-fortified versions. Helpful supplements include B vitamins for digestive lining and stress reduction, yeast for hindgut bacteria health, and colostrum to heal ulcers and leaky gut. Clean feeding avoids inflammatory sugar and soy products common in commercial feeds. Slow feeders simulate grazing, promoting calm and self-regulation. Colic is rare on large pastures; improvements like increasing turnout, using slow feeders, and ensuring 24-hour hay availability help. The author, Juliet M. Getty, Ph.D., is an independent equine nutritionist whose research-based approach aligns physiology with correct feeding. She authored Feed Your Horse Like a Horse and the Spotlight on Equine Nutrition series, available at GettyEquineNutrition.com and Amazon. Her website offers a free e-newsletter, articles, forum archives, teleseminars, and a supplement store.

A cave rescue expert describes the Thai rescue of 12 boys and their soccer coach, found alive after nine days 1.2 miles inside Tham Luang Nang Non cave, as one of the toughest he has seen. The basic tenet of cave flooding rescue is to wait, as taking risks endangers rescuers. Most caves drain quickly after rain, but monsoon rains in Southeast Asia can keep caves flooded for months. In this case, the water may not recede for months. Unusually, contact took nine days, and the cave temperature is in the mid-70s, higher than typical caves, which likely prevented hypothermia. The group survived without food for nine days, leaving them weak with compromised gastrointestinal systems; food is being reintroduced gradually. Three primary extraction options exist: teaching them to dive out, which is extremely dangerous for novices due to blackout conditions, tight squeezes, and panic risks; drilling an entrance, which requires heavy equipment and precise mapping; or finding a new entrance, though searches over 10 days have diminishing odds. Waiting for water to drop is complicated by monsoon season and could take weeks or longer. If their location remains safe from further flooding and divers can supply food and care, they can stay indefinitely; otherwise, diving out may be the only option. Rescuers face pressure from families, officials, and media, and risk blame if the outcome is not successful.

The Arizona Supreme Court held that A.R.S. § 13-4033(B) prohibits a defendant from directly appealing a contested post-judgment restitution order entered pursuant to a plea agreement that capped the restitution amount. The court determined such an order is part of the “sentence” for purposes of the statute, and allowing a direct appeal would undermine the legislative goal of reducing appeals from plea agreements. The defendant’s constitutional right to appellate review is preserved through Rule 32 post-conviction relief proceedings. The court disapproved of prior appellate decisions that assumed jurisdiction over similar appeals without considering § 13-4033(B). The superior court’s dismissal of Hoffman’s appeal was affirmed.
