A blood-based test for detecting primary glial malignancy (GLI-M) in patients with intracranial space occupying lesions (ICSOL) is described. The test enriches circulating glial cells (CGCs) from peripheral blood using a proprietary enrichment medium and identifies them via multiplexed immunocytochemistry for co-expression of GFAP and OLIG2. Analytical validation showed ≥80% recovery up to 48 hours, linearity from 5–1280 cells/5 mL, limit of detection of 1 cell/5 mL, sensitivity of 92.5–95.0%, specificity of 100%, and precision with CVs of 13.7–23.5%. In Case Control Clinical Study-1 (189 samples), training set sensitivity was 99% and specificity 96.8%; test set sensitivity and specificity were both 100%. Case Control Clinical Study-2 (586 samples) yielded 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity for differentiating GLI-M from benign brain tumors (BBT), epithelial malignancies with brain metastases, and healthy individuals. Prospective Clinical Study-1 (68 patients with ICSOL) demonstrated 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Prospective Clinical Study-2 (31 patients with intra-axial ICSOL) showed 92.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Orthogonal FISH verification in 44 cases showed 100% concordance for EGFR gene amplification between CGCs and matched tumor tissue. The test is minimally invasive (5 mL venous blood draw) and provides evidence to support clinical decision-making, potentially reducing the need for invasive biopsy. It does not detect rarer subtypes such as CNS lymphoma or gliosarcoma, nor does it differentiate subtype or grade of malignancy. The authors conclude the test enables more effective diagnosis of glial malignancies.

Carleton University is hiring for a chair in the "conjuring arts" to research perception and deception. The position, funded by a $2 million matching grant from The Slaight Family Foundation and named after Allan Slaight, will investigate why people are susceptible to deception, such as fake news or political illusions. The role includes creating a digital archive of magic information. A University of London experiment asked 120 people to explain a card trick. When the magician faked a swipe, only 60% figured out the duplicate card solution, compared to 87% when no fake swipe occurred. Researcher Gustav Kuhn said people become stuck on initial assumptions. Magician Michael Close suggested that when people cannot logically explain a trick, they rationalize or invent stories, and that laziness plays a part.

Dr. Howard W. Ellzey, a Memphis physician, was convicted of conspiracy to illegally distribute controlled substances and eleven substantive counts of illegal distribution. He received concurrent three-year prison terms (except probation on one count) and $18,000 in fines. About half his patients were “diet patients” who paid $15 for brief visits, received a vitamin injection and an amphetamine prescription, usually without examination. People recruited overweight men to obtain prescriptions for resale, visiting both of Ellzey’s offices in one day. He kept separate records per office, allowing two prescriptions per person daily. A DEA survey found that of 39,000 schedule II prescriptions from six drugstores, 29,000 were written by Ellzey, nearly all for amphetamines. The court held there was substantial evidence for conviction, no error in admitting the 29,000 prescriptions as evidence of intent, and no defect in charging “distributing” rather than dispensing because his practices were outside professional norms. The conviction was affirmed.

Former U.S. Senator Mark Begich, a Democrat, has entered the Alaska governor's race, creating a three-way contest with independent incumbent Gov. Bill Walker and the eventual Republican nominee. Some Democrats and independents worry Begich and Walker will split the vote, allowing a Republican victory. Begich says he would not run if he did not believe he could win. The race echoes 2014, when Walker, then a Republican, bypassed the primary and formed a unity ticket with Democrat Byron Mallott to win. Walker and Mallott plan to skip the primary again and gather signatures for the general election. The Democratic Party backs Begich and insists a three-way race is winnable. Begich criticizes Walker for losing sight of Alaska's vision amid budget deficits, while Walker's campaign says they want to compete on vision. This study used 2019 NSECE data to identify CCEE search types via latent class analysis based on up to two information sources families reported using in a recent search for a child under 6. Five sources were considered: friends/family with children, known providers, social media, internet search, and CCR&R/local organizations. Five search types emerged: Type 1 (CCR&R or friends/family), Type 2 (internet search or social media), Type 3 (known providers or friends/family), Type 4 (social media or friends/family), and Type 5 (friends/family or internet search). About half of families used one source, half used two.

Search types varied in limited ways. Type 1 was more likely and Type 2 less likely than Type 5 to search for information on type of care. Types 1 and 3 were more likely to involve a child with a condition affecting care provision. Regionally, Type 3 was more common in the West, and Type 5 more common in the Northeast. No other significant associations were found with search content or family/child characteristics. The analytic sample differed from the full population, being higher-income, more often two-parent with both parents working, and more English-speaking. Limitations include recording only the first two sources and the non-representative subsample. Overall, search types were more similar than different, suggesting source use may matter more than the information sought or family characteristics.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU includes 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, SECDED ECC protection, and a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100) with residency controls and compute data compression offering up to 4x bandwidth improvement. It features third-generation Tensor Cores with 2x raw FMA power of V100, sparsity support, and 108 SMs. Data sharing across 32 threads, asynchronous copy instructions bypassing the register file, asynchronous barriers, and 164 KB shared memory per SM enhance efficiency. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions the A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated memory and compute, providing fault isolation and QoS. Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links at 600 GB/sec total bandwidth. PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV delivers 31.5 GB/sec. Additional hardware includes a 5-core NVJPG decoder, optical flow accelerator, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units. CUDA 11 supports task graphs, asynchronous copy, barriers, and L2 cache control. The DGX A100 system combines eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch for 5 PFLOPS. Fine-grained structured sparsity (2:4) maintains accuracy while increasing performance.

The lecture begins with demonstrations of the Shellshock bug and cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. Shellshock exploits how CGI servers set environment variables from HTTP headers, allowing arbitrary command execution. XSS attacks inject malicious scripts via unsanitized user input. Defenses discussed include browser XSS filters, HTTP-only cookies, privilege separation using separate domains for untrusted content, content sanitization (e.g., Django’s HTML entity encoding, Markdown), Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict resource sources and disable eval, and the X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header. SQL injection and path traversal attacks are also covered, emphasizing the need for rigorous encoding of untrusted data.

The lecture then examines cookies and session management, including stateless cookies using message authentication codes (MACs) as in Amazon Web Services, and alternatives like DOM storage and client-side certificates. Protocol vulnerabilities include URL parsing discrepancies between Flash and browsers, and the GIFAR attack where a file is both a valid GIF and JAR, allowing applet code execution in a victim’s origin. Finally, time-based covert channel attacks are described: CSS link color sniffing, cache timing, DNS timing, and rendering timing, all of which can reveal a user’s browsing history despite countermeasures.

Swarthmore students, aged 18-22, often take themselves too seriously, stressing over grades and appearing perfect. The author argues it is okay to make mistakes and advocates laughing at oneself, not as a call to party, but as a way to cope with high expectations. Mistakes like getting a B or embarrassing oneself are not life-altering; one learns from them. The campus is idiosyncratic and intense, so stepping back to find humor is beneficial. Additionally, students should forgive others' mistakes, give the benefit of the doubt in arguments, and assume good intent, as laughter helps deal with discomfort.

The professor notes that problem 8.2 lacks sufficient background and problem 8.3 is a BCJR algorithm decoding exercise, suggesting a noise variance of sigma squared equals 1. The lecture covers Hadamard transform realizations of Reed-Muller codes. The Hadamard transform over F2 uses a universal matrix Um, the m-fold tensor product of a 2x2 lower triangular self-inverse matrix. Reed-Muller codes are generated by rows of Um with weight at least 2^(m-r). A graphical realization of Um uses simple degree-3 constraint nodes (zero-sum and equality) and contains cycles. For the (8,4,4) code, fixing some internal variables to zero and reducing yields a realization with 12 simple constraints and cycles. Agglomerating constraints produces a cycle-free realization equivalent to a two-section trellis with higher branch complexity. The sum product algorithm for a posteriori probability (APP) decoding on cycle-free graphs is introduced. APP decoding computes the probability of each variable given the received sequence. The algorithm uses a past-future decomposition: in a cycle-free graph, an edge is a cut-set, and the APP of a state variable is proportional to the product of its past and future components, exploiting a Cartesian product sum factorization.

Panic disorder (PD) affects 2-3% of Americans, while 18.1% have anxiety disorders. The author, diagnosed with PD, manages it with therapy and medication but still experiences occasional panic attacks and has learned techniques to stop them. Professionals distinguish panic attacks from the lay term 'anxiety attack': anxiety is persistent worry, while a panic attack is a burst of intense fear lasting under 30 minutes. Panic attacks in PD occur without triggers, but anyone can have one with a clear cause. Symptoms include palpitations, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, choking sensations, chest pain, nausea, dizziness, chills, numbness, derealization, and fear of losing control or dying. A physical exam is advised to rule out other issues. Recommended coping strategies: write on an index card that panic attacks are not life-threatening and you have survived them before; prepare positive mantras to counter catastrophic thoughts; visualize panic as a wave that rises, peaks around 10 minutes, and falls; use smartphone games, relaxing music, or guided relaxation for distraction; practice slow, deep breathing daily—inhale deeply through the nose, imagine the body filling with air, exhale slowly through the mouth as if through a straw—and use this during an attack to slow heart rate and calm down.

A study found bumblebee queens exposed to the neonicotinoid thiamethoxam at field-realistic levels were 26% less likely to lay eggs. Neonics are systemic pesticides used as seed coatings on crops like corn, soybeans, and canola, and residues reach pollen. Researcher Nigel Raine said this could cause colony collapse and population decline, but noted other factors like nutrition and parasites also matter. The results may strengthen calls for further restrictions; the EU's temporary moratorium may become permanent, though pesticide companies and farmers argue it lowers yields and increases other pesticide use.

San Diego County confirmed its first West Nile case this year in a Spring Valley woman. Symptoms can appear 2-14 days after a mosquito bite. The virus, spread by mosquitoes from birds, can cause headache, fever, rash, and rarely death. California reported 231 cases, 12 deaths. Officials urge using repellent, wearing long sleeves, and eliminating standing water.

This study developed a deep learning model to predict disease duration (DD) from structural brain MRI in people with multiple sclerosis (MS), producing a brain-predicted DD gap as a measure of MS-specific brain damage. The model was trained on 4,392 patients from 15 European centers and validated on an external longitudinal cohort of 252 early MS patients. The DD gap showed low correlation with the brain-age gap (BAG) from a healthy ageing model, indicating relative independence. DD predictions were sensitive to lesion filling, unlike BAG. Both BAG and DD gap were associated with physical disability (EDSS) cross-sectionally and longitudinally; the DD gap added significant explanatory value beyond BAG for disability worsening. An alternative MS-specific ageing model (MS-age gap) correlated with BAG and did not significantly improve disability prediction. The authors conclude the DD gap is a clinically meaningful biomarker of MS severity and progression, complementing healthy brain ageing models.

The TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP have a configurable maximum duty cycle using the DCL pin, while the TPS7H5004-SP only supports a 50% maximum duty cycle. For 100% duty cycle, compatible devices should have DCL connected to VLDO. The CS_ILIM pin is driven by a signal representative of the transformer primary-side current and is used for peak current mode control and configuring the current limit. When the voltage on CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, the device enters cycle-by-cycle current limiting and hiccup mode, with timing controlled by a capacitor on the HICC pin. The FAULT pin allows for external fault protection, triggering a shutdown if its voltage exceeds 0.6 V. Slope compensation, set via a resistor on the RSC pin, mitigates subharmonic oscillation. The device uses a transconductance error amplifier, and Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation can be applied. Thermal shutdown occurs if the junction temperature exceeds 175°C. The document also details a design example for a synchronous push-pull converter using the TPS7H5001-SP, including component selection for frequency, output voltage, dead time, soft-start, transformer, FETs, output filter, current sensing, hiccup mode, frequency compensation, and slope compensation.

The paper provides a Situation Calculus formalization of an obligation taxonomy using non-Markovian theories. The Situation Calculus is a logical language for specifying dynamical systems, using fluents and actions. The frame problem—the need for many axioms stating what remains unchanged—is addressed by Reiter's successor state axioms, which rely on the Markov property (preconditions/effects depend only on the current situation). Gabaldon extended this to non-Markovian control, allowing dependence on past situations, suitable for domains like database transactions and smart contracts. Scherl and Levesque extended the solution to knowledge-producing actions. The paper focuses on smart contracts, which require formal obligation specifications. It adopts the obligation modality from [37], where obligation is expressed using a deontic accessibility fluent O(s', s) and the definition Oblg(ϕ, s) ≡ (∀s').O(s', s) ⊃ ϕ[s'], meaning in situation s it is obligatory that ϕ holds. A running example of a door-opening domain illustrates actions (unlock, pressButton, lock, moveTo, notify), fluents (open, locked, notifiedManager, at), and their precondition and successor state axioms. The paper is organized into sections on sequential temporal Situation Calculus, non-Markovian control, obligation formalization, obligation types, properties, violation and compensation, related work, and conclusion.

Five years after the confirmation that a skeleton found under a Leicester car park was Richard III, the discovery changed the lives of several individuals. He underwent combat and riding training, reenacting Richard's final moments, and gained confidence, later giving lectures. Michael Ibsen, a descendant of Richard's sister, provided a DNA sample that helped confirm the remains. He experienced media attention and was asked to make the king's coffin. Car park attendant Mike Mistry witnessed the excavation, painted the "R" marking the spot, and later spoke with visitors from around the world before being made redundant in 2016. Musician Ian Churchward was inspired to write multiple Richard III albums with his band The Legendary Ten Seconds, including a concept album, and performed at related events.

Researchers from the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology and collaborators reconstructed fungi's evolutionary timeline using fossil evidence and horizontal gene transfers (HGT). Because fungal fossils are rare, they combined a molecular clock with 17 HGT events, which established 'older than/younger than' relationships to constrain the timeline. The analysis indicates a common ancestor of living fungi dating to roughly 1.4–0.9 billion years ago, diversifying hundreds of millions of years before land plants. This suggests fungi were present long before plants, likely partnering with algae to break down rock, recycle nutrients, and create primitive soils. The study reframes land colonization: fungi acted as ecosystem engineers that prepared Earth's surface for plants, meaning plants did not colonize a barren wasteland but a world already altered by fungal activity. The research also notes that complex multicellularity evolved independently in five major groups: animals, land plants, fungi, red algae, and brown algae.

A collection of news articles from October 19–20, 2001, compiled under the subject "Enron Mentions," reports on multiple Enron-related developments. Enron disclosed a $618 million third-quarter loss, a $1.01 billion write-off, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity after repurchasing 55 million shares tied to LJM2 transactions. National Journal’s lobbying firm rankings listed Enron as a client of Quinn Gillespie & Associates, paying $525,000 to lobby on energy deregulation. Dow Jones Commodities Service reported Enron Metals would cut European staff by 10–20%. The Times of India noted a Bombay High Court hearing set for December 11 on a petition by Enron-promoted Dhabol Power Company challenging the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission’s jurisdiction. The Houston Chronicle mentioned Enron’s Ken Lay in connection with a campaign for public funding of a Houston arena.

In 1962, U.S. strategic superiority (8 to 1) forced Khrushchev to back down. Policymakers then ignored Soviet buildup intentions; in 1965 McNamara claimed Soviets accepted inferiority. Fifteen years later, Soviets lead in most strategic categories and cite a favorable "correlation of forces." The Carter administration showed weakness, inconsistency, vacillation, and bluff: a Soviet brigade in Cuba remains despite being called unacceptable; Soviet troops invaded Afghanistan after a warning; the President pledged Middle East defense then admitted lacking forces. The passage asks if this is Carter's incoherence or a consistent doctrine of not provoking the Soviets. It argues WWII stemmed from weakness, not strength; firmness deters, weakness provokes imperialist ambitions. The U.S. is isolated, allies losing confidence. The alternative path is restoring a margin of safety through strength, as under Eisenhower and Ford's budget. Carter cut defenses. The program must combat terrorism, rebuild conventional and strategic forces, consult allies, restore alliance cohesion, and uphold American principles to secure world peace.

This paper investigates blockchain technology programs in higher education by examining curricula of AACSB-accredited US universities. A search of 533 institutions in March 2024 identified 151 (approx. 28%) offering at least one blockchain course, totaling 361 courses. Data on offering department, course level, and descriptions were collected and categorized.

Blockchain integration in enterprises requires cross-functional collaboration across management, finance, supply chain, IT, law, procurement, and sales. Successful integration demands a multifaceted skill set including technical, social, methodological, and personal competences.

Courses were classified into categories: Fundamentals & Overview (140 courses), Digital Assets & Cryptocurrencies (71), Technical Development (66), Business Implications (33), Law and Compliance (29), Supply Chain and Governance (12), Interplay with Other Technologies (6), and Other (4). The largest scientific fields offering courses are Business (216 courses, with Information Systems and Finance/FinTech leading) and Computer Science (85 courses). Law, Arts & Sciences, and Engineering also offer courses. Uncommon departments like Biology, Literature, and Political Science also provide blockchain courses.

Most courses (72%) are undergraduate, 23% graduate, and 5% both. Public universities have more total offerings (89 vs. 62 private), but a higher percentage of private universities offer blockchain courses (36% vs. 24%). Larger undergraduate populations correlate with higher likelihood of offering blockchain courses; all universities with 40,001–50,000 students offer at least one.

Emerging technologies discussed include AI & Machine Learning (30 courses), Internet of Things (18), and Non-Fungible Tokens (15). The study concludes that blockchain education is interconnected with other emerging topics and that holistic competency development is crucial. Future research should evaluate course topics against industry needs and replicate the study in five years.

The passage describes noninvasive physiological monitoring devices and methods that combine data from optical sensors at multiple measurement sites to generate a single measurement of a physiological parameter. Conventional pulse oximeters typically measure at a single site, and stereo pulse oximeters process data from multiple sites independently. The disclosure combines raw or minimally processed sensor data from different sites into a signal processor to calculate a single measurement, providing more robust readings. The physiological parameter can include oxygen saturation, pulse rate, plethysmograph waveform, perfusion index, pleth variability index, methemoglobin, carboxyhemoglobin, total hemoglobin, glucose, and others.

A noninvasive physiological monitor may include at least two sensor interfaces, each receiving signals from a sensor at a measurement site, and a signal processor that combines the interface outputs. Sensors can have multiple light emitters and/or multiple photodetectors. In some embodiments, a sensor includes an optical source and more than one photodetector arranged in a three-dimensional configuration conforming to the measurement site contour, such as a finger, nose, or earlobe. The photodetectors are distributed throughout a sensor area, providing topology information for correct placement and diversity of light path lengths for improved robustness. The sensor may be a clip or adhesive tape.

The monitor can use a first sensor at a cephalic site (e.g., nose, earlobe) and a second sensor at a peripheral site (e.g., finger). Data streams are combined into combined sensor data, and the signal processor analyzes features like amplitude, phase, DC values, and ratiometric values to generate the single measurement. The signal processor may also independently process each sensor's data to produce separate measurements, and a final measurement can be derived from these. Combining data from multiple sites can reduce errors and noise and provide systematic physiological status. Methods include transmitting light through tissues of at least two measurement sites, detecting attenuated light with photodetectors, generating signal outputs, and combining them to determine the single measurement. A sensor with multiple photodetectors can also be used alone to measure a physiological parameter from multiple data streams.

A surgical robotic component comprises an articulated terminal portion with a distal segment having an attachment, an intermediate segment, and a basal segment. A first articulation between the distal and intermediate segments permits relative rotation about a first axis. A second articulation between the intermediate and basal segments permits relative rotation about a second axis. The intermediate segment includes a third articulation permitting relative rotation of the distal and basal segments about third and fourth axes, a first torque sensor for sensing torque about the third axis, and a second torque sensor for sensing torque about the fourth axis. The articulations are arranged such that in at least one configuration the first and second axes are parallel and the third and fourth axes are transverse to the first axis. The terminal portion may also include a third torque sensor for the first axis and a fourth torque sensor for the second axis. In that configuration, the third and fourth axes may be transverse or perpendicular to each other and perpendicular to the first axis; the first and second axes may be collinear. The first and second articulations may be revolute joints; the third articulation may be a spherical joint, a pair of revolute joints, or a universal joint. The attachment may be on the first axis. The component may be at the end of a surgical robot arm with an attached surgical instrument, or at the end of a surgical instrument with an attached end effector, both extending substantially along the first axis. The torque sensors enable measurement of forces applied to the instrument or end effector, allowing force feedback. The wrist design provides a range of motion similar to a human wrist and eliminates kinematic singularities. The robot arm may have a sequence of roll and pitch joints, and the wrist includes a roll joint proximally of crossed-axis pitch joints. Torque sensors may be strain gauges, piezoelectric, or magnetostrictive, with outputs processed to determine applied forces.

Education regulators are reviewing a whistleblower's claim that Ohio's former largest online charter school, the Electronic Classroom of Tomorrow (ECOT), intentionally inflated attendance figures to obtain more state funding. A former technology employee, speaking anonymously, said school officials ordered staff to manipulate student data using ActivTrak software, purchased after the state demanded repayment of $60 million in overpayments for 2015-2016. He reported this to the Ohio Department of Education and state auditor Dave Yost. His concerns were first raised in an August 3 email, before the state's 2017 attendance review found the software duplicated learning hours. ECOT's lobbyist dismissed the allegations as fabricated. The school closed in January 2018. State officials met with the whistleblower in December and will consider his information in a future review. The whistleblower described meetings where data was tweaked to reach desired outcomes. The Education Department previously found ECOT significantly over-reported students, resulting in the $60 million penalty plus $19 million for 2016-2017. ECOT installed ActivTrak to comply with a new rule requiring learning hours reporting.

CoreLogic reported that in May, LA County home prices rose 8.3% year-over-year, Inland Empire 8.2%, and Orange County 6.2%, marking the third straight month of such gains. US prices rose 7.1%, California 8.9%. Lean supply, particularly entry-level homes, and homeowners with low mortgage rates not selling are driving prices. In his final Oval Office address, the President expressed gratitude for two terms and thanked Vice President Gore, Cabinet, and staff. He said the nation transformed, with stronger social fabric, healthier families, and prosperity. He aimed to give Americans tools for a good society with a strong economy, cleaner environment, and a freer, safer world, guided by opportunity, responsibility, and community. He cited achievements: over 22 million jobs, low unemployment, high homeownership, long expansion, welfare and crime reductions, more college aid, better schools, health insurance for millions, reduced poverty, rising incomes, cleaner environment, and record land preservation. America was a global force for peace. He offered three future thoughts: maintain fiscal responsibility (turned deficits to surpluses, paid down $600 billion debt, on track to be debt-free); continue global leadership (more freedom, strong alliances, but integration brings threats like terrorism and a rich-poor gap requiring action); and unite domestically by weaving diversity into one America, overcoming differences, and treating all fairly regardless of race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, or arrival time. He wished the next President well and said he leaves more idealistic, confident, and proud to be a citizen.

The passage introduces a book aiming to standardize distributed system design through patterns. The first section focuses on single-node patterns because groups of co-located containers are the atomic elements of distributed systems. Motivations for splitting a single-node application into multiple containers include: resource isolation (e.g., separating a user-facing server from a background loader to manage priorities and prevent contention), team scaling (enabling small teams to own focused, reusable modules like a Git sync tool), and separation of concerns (improving understandability, testing, and independent deployment). These tightly coupled container groups, which can share resources and be coscheduled, are called pods in Kubernetes.

The passage documents AMD AGESA (AMD Generic Encapsulated Software Architecture) procedures, call-outs, and configuration structures for initializing processors, memory, and platform components during boot and resume. It describes stackless assembly routines for pre-memory stack setup and teardown, entry points for boot time points (e.g., AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitMid, AmdInitLate, AmdInitRtb, AmdInitResume, AmdS3LateRestore, AmdS3FinalRestore), and service functions like AmdCreateStruct and AmdReleaseStruct. Required host environment call-outs include AgesaAllocateBuffer, AgesaDeallocateBuffer, AgesaReset, AgesaRunFcnOnAp, and AgesaReadSpd. Optional call-outs provide hooks for customization. Platform configuration structures allow host modification of settings such as cache regions, power management, memory interleaving, and PCIe topology.

The Combo defense combines person-to-person and zone: three outside players deny passes, two inside zone. X1 protects middle, forces sideline; X2, X3 deny; X4, X5 zone baseline. After pass, X1 denies return, X5 pushes O5 baseline, X4 helpside. On middle penetration, X5 traps with X1, X4 supports, X2/X3 deny. A simultaneous ADF-EDS-EELS tomography method was developed to achieve 3D nanoscale mapping of structure, chemical composition, and valence states in beam-sensitive materials. Applied to LiNi₁/₃Co₁/₃Mn₁/₃O₂ (NCM111) cathode primary particles at pristine, 50-, 100-, and 200-cycle states, the approach eliminated multiple tilt series, reduced electron dose, and ensured precise spatial alignment across modalities.

Electrochemical cycling caused capacity loss, with complete failure after 200 cycles. ADF-STEM showed a structural progression from layered to spinel-like (100 cycles) to rock-salt (200 cycles). 3D EDS chemical composition maps revealed that oxygen and transition metal atomic percentages remained uniform throughout particles up to 100 cycles, then oxygen dropped sharply at 200 cycles, with 33.7% of the particle volume transforming to rock-salt. Transition-metal-rich regions were negligible up to 50 cycles, then increased to ~0.2–0.5% by 200 cycles, with segregation more pronounced near the surface. Depth profiles confirmed uniform composition across all cycles, except for minor inter-particle variation at 100 cycles.

3D valence state maps from EELS showed Mn⁴⁺ and Co³⁺ dominated in pristine particles. Up to 100 cycles, fractions were stable, but at 200 cycles Mn⁴⁺ dropped from 80.7% to 53.4% and Co³⁺ from 77.5% to 11.0%, with corresponding increases in Mn²⁺ and Co²⁺. Valence states exhibited strong depth dependence: in pristine and up to 100 cycles, Mn⁴⁺ and Co³⁺ increased with depth while lower states decreased; after 200 cycles this trend reversed. This depth dependence was not due to oxygen vacancies, excess lithium, or secondary phases, but to local transition metal segregation near the surface, confirmed by higher inhomogeneity (standard deviation of composition) at the surface that decayed with depth.

The evolution of Mn inhomogeneity and valence states was non-monotonic. From pristine to 50 cycles, both Mn⁴⁺ fraction and inhomogeneity decreased, attributed to layered-to-spinel transition and transition metal migration reducing spatial variance. From 50 to 100 cycles, both increased, explained by disproportionation reactions causing Mn dissolution and formation of Mn-rich secondary phases. From 100 to 200 cycles, rock-salt formation drove Mn²⁺ increase. Co showed similar trends. The interplay of structural phase transitions, transition metal migration, and dissolution-driven segregation governs degradation. Compositional changes occurred uniformly, while valence state evolution and inhomogeneity were surface-depth-dependent, indicating these are active contributors to stability. The simultaneous tomography platform is broadly applicable to other functional materials.

United Distributors, Inc. sued Airco Appliance & Hardware, Inc., Henry R. Burke, and Alfred R. Willis to recover on a note signed by Burke as president. Burke and the corporation did not contest liability. Willis denied liability on a guarantee he signed, asserting that the sole consideration was his prospective 50% stock interest in Airco, which never materialized and was known to plaintiff. The trial court dismissed the suit against Willis, and plaintiff appealed.

In January 1953, Burke formed Airco. Willis considered acquiring a half interest. Plaintiff’s salesman offered a budget plan, and Willis and Burke signed credit documents and later, at plaintiff’s office, each signed a duplicate guarantee. The guarantee was a form required by plaintiff’s president to hold individuals personally liable for the corporation’s debts. Two days later, Willis decided not to participate. Plaintiff was informed, and the salesman returned all signed papers except the guarantee, which he was unaware of. Willis and Burke destroyed the returned papers, believing the guarantee was included. The salesman knew Willis would not be associated with Airco.

The purchases underlying the suit occurred a year later under Burke’s continued operation. The note for $3,107.82 was given for air conditioning units. Willis’s guarantee, unknown to him, had been retained by plaintiff. Plaintiff contended the guarantee was unambiguous, required written revocation, and that it had relied on it.

The court found that the sole motive for Willis’s guarantee was his intended stock ownership and association. When that failed and plaintiff was notified, the motive failed, rendering the contract ineffective under Louisiana Civil Code articles. The judgment dismissing the suit against Willis was affirmed.

The Elliott Wave theory, discovered by Ralph Nelson Elliott in the 1920s–1930s after studying 75 years of stock data, is a technical analysis principle stating that asset prices move in recognizable wave patterns. These patterns consist of impulse waves (five sub-waves moving in the trend direction) and corrective waves (three sub-waves moving opposite). Impulse waves follow specific rules, such as wave 2 never retracing more than 100% of wave 1 and wave 3 never being the shortest. The theory is used by technical traders in stock, forex, and commodity markets, including day traders, swing traders, and long-term investors. It can be combined with indicators like moving averages, trend lines, and momentum oscillators. Criticisms include high subjectivity, difficulty in backtesting due to loosely defined rules, lack of clear entry and exit signals, and potential for curve fitting. No single timeframe is best; choice depends on trading style. The passage also notes that the website offers fully backtested strategies with strict rules.

In this tax case, Mumma Brothers Drilling Co. sought a refund of sales/use taxes paid on drilling equipment. The taxpayer drills water wells and installs pumps and plumbing, with the extracted water used by customers for personal consumption, not resale. The court previously held part of the claim time-barred and remanded for a factual determination of exemption. On remand, the trial court found the taxes properly paid. The Court of Appeals affirms, holding that the taxpayer is a contractor under Ind. Code 6-2-1-38(k) and that the claimed exemption under IC 6-2-1-39(b)(6) for extraction of tangible personal property does not apply because the water is not resold. The exemption is intended to prevent tax pyramiding at the wholesale level and requires resale; extraction for personal use does not qualify.

Treatment options for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) are limited, and resistance to taxanes is common. Androgen receptor (AR) splice variants differentially associate with microtubules (MTs): ARv567 is MT-associated and sensitive to docetaxel, while ARv7 shows reduced MT binding, resists paclitaxel-induced nuclear accumulation inhibition, and correlates with taxane resistance. Computational analysis of MT dynamics uses automated tracking of EB1 comets to measure polymerization rates and infer pause and shortening behaviors. In isogenic PC cell lines, ARv7 expression increases MT growth speeds by over 40% compared to AR-wild type, with no slowdown at the cell edge. Patient-derived organoids from primary and metastatic tissues are cultured, and Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor concentration is reduced to select for tumor cells, as benign cells are more dependent on it. In androgen-independent disease, circulating tumor cells can be small and detected via PSMA. The tumor suppressor pVHL and GSK3β regulate MT stability: loss of pVHL or GSK3β-mediated phosphorylation of pVHL increases MT turnover, while GSK3 inhibition attenuates dynamics. Both faster and slower MT turnover rates are associated with drug resistance. Paclitaxel treatment suppresses fast-polymerizing MTs and reduces overall polymerization rates. Circular Hough transform detects MT bundling as a taxane activity hallmark; BRCA1 knockdown reduces bundling and indicates resistance. The study proposes using MT dynamics signatures to anticipate drug resistance and identify therapeutic targets.

Alexis Perez pled guilty to conspiracy to commit mail fraud and was sentenced to 51 months. He appealed, arguing the district court erred by not applying a three-level reduction under U.S.S.G. § 2X1.1(b)(2) for an incomplete conspiracy and by not granting a minor-role reduction. The Eleventh Circuit affirmed. Regarding the incomplete conspiracy reduction, the court found that Perez and his co-conspirators had taken crucial steps: they had a detailed plan, the means to execute it, and were on the verge of execution when law enforcement intervened, so the reduction did not apply. Regarding the minor-role reduction, the record showed Perez played an important role, was intimately involved in planning, knew the fraudulent scheme, and was paid; he failed to show he was less culpable than most other conspirators. The court also noted that a sentence appeal waiver was not enforced because the district court did not specifically question Perez about it, and Perez could not adopt codefendants' arguments because his appeal was not consolidated and he did not file a motion for adoption.

The VIX is a real-time market index created by the Chicago Board Options Exchange in 1993 that measures implied volatility—the market’s expectations for volatility over the coming 30 days—in the U.S. equity market. It is also known as the fear index and serves as a barometer of market sentiment. VIX futures, introduced in 2004, are futures contracts whose underlying asset is the VIX Index. They are financial derivative products representing a contract to trade a specified unit of the index at a pre-agreed price on a future date, reflecting the market’s estimate of the VIX Index on various expiration dates. VIX futures trade on the Cboe Futures Exchange (CFE) and allow market participants to implement volatility trading strategies for risk management, alpha generation, and portfolio diversification.

A VIX futures strategy refers to methods and techniques for trading VIX futures, potentially using technical or fundamental indicators to determine entry and exit points, and should include risk management and position sizing. VIX futures can be used for portfolio diversification, speculative trading, and arbitrage trading.

VIX futures are available in two contract types: the full contract with a contract unit equivalent to the index value multiplied by $1,000, and the mini contract at one-tenth that size (index value multiplied by $100). Price quotation is in index points to three decimal places. The tick size for the full contract is $50.00 per contract, and the minimum price fluctuation is 0.05 per tick. Contracts exist for every month. Trading hours are Monday to Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 3:15 p.m. CT for the regular session, with an extended session from 3:30 p.m. to 8:30 a.m. the next day, except Monday when the extended session ends at 5:00 p.m. On expiry, the contract is financially settled. Trading terminates at 8:00 a.m. CT on the final settlement day, which is the Wednesday 30 days prior to the third Friday of the calendar month immediately following the contract month. The final settlement value is a Special Opening Quotation of the VIX Index calculated from opening trade prices during a special opening auction. The block minimum is 200 contracts.

The trading symbol for the index is VIX, and the product code for the futures contract is VX. Charts can be found on platforms like TradingView or Yahoo Finance. As of December 19, 2022, VIX futures were trading at 22.450.

Factors affecting VIX prices include the phase of the stock market cycle: during bullish phases the VIX Index and VIX futures decline, while during bearish phases they rise. Contango and backwardation effects also play a role; when the spot VIX is at very low values, futures contracts sell at a premium (contango), and when the spot index is at extremely high values, they sell at a discount (backwardation). Seasonality indicates the index tends to perform better during summer and fall, be stagnant in winter, and decline in spring.

The all-time high for VIX futures is 80.850, reached in March 2020. The highest level of the VIX Index was 89.53 in October 2008, and its lowest level was 8.56 in November 2017.

The biggest risk in trading VIX futures is adverse price movement due to leverage, which can magnify losses. For example, with 20x leverage, a 1% adverse move causes a 20% loss, and a 5% move could wipe out the account.

To start trading VIX futures, one must open an account with a futures broker that provides access to the Cboe Futures Exchange and fund the account. It is also possible to trade a CFD contract through an online CFD broker, though CFDs are simply contracts with the broker, have no expiry dates, and differ from exchange-traded futures.

VIX futures do not precisely track spot VIX. The S&P 500 VIX Short-Term Futures Index captures about half of the spot movement, and rolling from first-month to second-month futures creates a long-term performance drag, making long-term hedging costly. A backtest using the VIX spot index to trade SPY showed a strategy invested only 13.11% of the time, with a risk-adjusted return of 44.06%, a maximum drawdown of 23% (less than half of buy-and-hold’s 55%), and only two down years (2008 and 2022), though the annual return was lower than buy-and-hold. There are many VIX ETFs.

The passage describes the interface between AGESA software and host BIOS using a bridge/dispatcher model: host bridge code calls the AGESA dispatcher to execute functions, and a call-out port with a router allows AGESA to call host procedures. The host must provide a valid stack. The UEFI environment includes SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP phases with 16/32/64-bit modes. AGESA core files are organized into libraries for these phases, with additional UEFI libraries. Build targets use specific tools (MASM, ml, CL). Configuration is via <plat>Option.c files; no extra UEFI-specific user options exist. Porting requires redefining StdHeader content and using environment-specific library routines.

The SEC phase uses AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK to establish a C environment. PEI has two modules: AmdProcessorInitPeim (processor initialization, publishes AmdCpuEarlyInit, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost PPIs, and a memory info HOB) and AmdMemoryInitPeim (memory initialization, publishes AmdMemInit PPI). A reset PEIM coordinates warm resets. The DXE driver calls AmdInitLate, generates tables, and publishes AgesaDxeProtocol. AmdGpuVgaControlDxe manages iGPU VGA decoding. Reference files and UEFI build control files (.inf) are provided. Environment variables AGESA_ROOT, AGESA_OptsDir, and AGESA_PlatType must be set. Integration steps include copying option files, setting variables, enabling CAR before AmdInitReset, using 'ByHost' allocation, and not modifying SS/ESP or cache controls during CAR.

Build methods are binary modules or source integration. Stack macros AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK and AMD_DISABLE_UEFI_STACK manage the pre-memory stack. Service procedures include AmdCreateStruct (allocates/initializes parameter blocks with PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, ByHost methods), AmdReleaseStruct, AmdGetDataEye, AmdGetApicAddress, AmdGetExeCacheSize, AmdGetPciAddress, AmdIdentifyCore, AmdIdentifyDimm, AmdAddMmiRange, and AmdReadEventLog.

Entry points in time order: AmdInitReset (minimal init, execution cache regions, FCH settings); AmdInitEarly (full init, platform config, VRM, PCIe topology, power management); AmdInitPost (memory initialization, outputs memory info, numerous memory configuration options); AmdInitEnv (transfers HOBs to permanent buffer); AmdInitMid (graphics display config, IOMMU, LVDS settings); AmdInitLate (generates ACPI tables: DMI, PState, WHEA, IVRS, CRAT, CDIT); AmdInitRtb (saves processor context for S3 suspend, allocates buffer, provides NvStorage and VolatileStorage); AmdInitResume (re-initializes memory from S3 context); AmdS3LateRestore (restores registers after PCI restore); AmdS3FinalRestore (final restoration before OS handoff). The required call-out AgesaAllocateBuffer allocates a post-memory buffer, returning size, handle, and pointer.

Google honored German physicist Max Born's 135th birthday with a Doodle. Born contributed to quantum mechanics, which enabled computers, lasers, and medical imaging. He was born on Dec. 11, 1882, in Breslau, Germany (now Wrocław, Poland), to an upper-class Jewish academic family. As a professor at the University of Göttingen, he attracted physicists like Heisenberg, Fermi, and Oppenheimer. He was friends with Einstein, though they differed on quantum randomness. Born was forced to emigrate to England when Hitler rose to power; a 1935 letter from Hitler expelled him from Göttingen. He won the 1954 Nobel Prize for the Born Rule, which uses probability to predict particle locations. Born died on Jan. 5, 1970, from a heart ailment.

A day trading price action strategy uses patterns of price movements to determine trade entry and exit points. Price action analysis is a form of technical analysis that focuses solely on price movements, ignoring fundamental factors and typically avoiding indicators. It studies price swing highs and lows, individual price bar characteristics, and market sentiment inferred from price behavior. At the macro level, traders assess trend or range-bound conditions using trend lines, moving averages, and support/resistance levels.

Traders look for two main pattern types: chart patterns and candlestick patterns. Chart patterns include reversal patterns (e.g., head and shoulders, inverse head and shoulders) that signal potential trend changes after prolonged moves, continuation patterns that suggest the trend will persist, and harmonic patterns formed by four consecutive price swings. Candlestick patterns derive from the shape of individual or grouped candlesticks and may indicate session sentiment.

Some day traders rely purely on price action, using only tools like trend lines and pivot levels. Others combine price action with indicators such as moving averages for trend and dynamic support/resistance, the VIX for volatility, or the RSI for momentum.

The article stresses that backtesting is essential to evaluate any price action strategy, but coding such strategies is difficult and time-consuming. Manual backtesting is prone to cognitive biases. An example strategy based on entering after a series of lower lows and lower highs was backtested on WTI crude oil futures (2000–2021). The historical performance was poor, with a negative average gain per trade and a 47% win rate. However, an out-of-sample test on unknown data after July 2021 showed 21 trades with an average gain of 0.57%, suggesting the strategy began working in that period. The article warns that many price action traders rely on anecdotal charts and may lack long-term positive expectancy. It recommends backtesting, out-of-sample testing, and incubation periods to filter out random-looking strategies. Diversification across different strategies and markets is also advised to manage risk.

Frequently asked questions clarify that price action trading uses past prices alone to identify opportunities, can be applied to day trading via patterns and trends, and includes strategies like trend following, breakouts, reversal trades, and scalping. Backtesting involves simulating trades on historical data; coding specific rules helps assess effectiveness.

Mentoring relationships, both programmatic and naturally occurring with teachers and other adults, are crucial for student academic success. The COVID-19 pandemic caused significant learning disruptions, particularly for low-income students, students of color, and those with disabilities, leading to months of unfinished learning and increased disengagement. Meta-analyses and research syntheses consistently show that mentoring programs yield positive effects on academic outcomes such as attendance, grades, test scores, and classroom behavior. Mentors can enhance school connectedness, engagement, and educational self-confidence, and cross-age peer mentoring also improves school belonging and performance.

Representative studies of school-based programs (e.g., Big Brothers Big Sisters, Gear Up, AMPED, Project Arrive, Success Mentors, Check and Connect) demonstrate improvements in academic performance, attendance, credits earned, and graduation rates. After-school programs like Quantum Opportunities, Village Model of Care, and Pathways to Education show gains in GPA, graduation, and college enrollment. Naturally formed mentoring relationships with teachers and school personnel are also impactful: the Achievement Mentoring Program reduced disciplinary referrals and improved math and language arts; students with teacher mentors attain higher educational levels; developmental relationships with teachers correlate with stronger school connectedness and better GPAs. Such natural mentoring is especially beneficial for students of color, fostering positive racial regard and helping overcome systemic barriers.

Despite these benefits, access to mentors is inequitable: youth of color, low-income youth, and those whose parents have limited education report fewer mentoring relationships. The passage concludes that mentoring is an evidence-based strategy with broad positive outcomes, and expanding its availability through investment and policy is needed to support all students.

A longitudinal evaluation of 11 SARS-CoV-2-positive nursing home residents (median age 74, 64% male) during an outbreak in Georgia (October 2020–April 2021) characterized antibody responses post-infection and post-vaccination. Ten participants received two doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine; one refused. Post-infection, 9 of 10 had detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA antibodies, and 8 had IgM. Median time to detection was 13 days for Pan-Ig and IgG, 16 days for IgA. At first antibody detection, 67% were still RT-PCR-positive but none were viral culture-positive. Pan-Ig and IgG titers rose and remained elevated, while IgM and IgA declined after 31–60 days, with seroreversion in some by 50 days. The unvaccinated participant maintained detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA for at least 150 days. Post-vaccination, all 10 vaccinated participants had Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA antibodies; 6 had IgM. Post-vaccination geometric mean titers were substantially higher than post-infection, with IgG ratios up to 200.5-fold (31–60 days) and Pan-Ig up to 142.3-fold (15–30 days). Titers began to decrease 61–90 days post-vaccination. An immunocompromised participant had similar titers to others. No culturable virus was detected after antibody development, supporting seroconversion as a marker of non-infectivity. The findings suggest nursing home residents mount robust and diverse binding antibody responses that are augmented by vaccination, though limitations include small sample size, use of only the Pfizer vaccine, and evaluation before the emergence of Delta and Omicron variants.

The lecture concludes the course's coverage of stochastic methods. It addresses multidimensional integrals of the form ∫ p(x) f(x) dx, often with a known weighting factor w rather than p, as in Boltzmann distributions or Bayesian analysis where the likelihood times prior yields a weighting factor for parameters. Metropolis Monte Carlo requires choosing a step length; too-large steps cause repeated rejections, too-small steps limit exploration. Adaptive stepsizing can help, and knowing the expected answer beforehand is critical for detecting errors. Monte Carlo accuracy scales as 1/√n, providing quick rough estimates but requiring many samples for high precision. The homework reduced a 12-dimensional problem to 6 by eliminating rotational and translational degrees of freedom, illustrating the value of simplification.

Kinetic Monte Carlo (Gillespie algorithm) is used when the probability distribution is governed by a differential equation and the state space is enormous, such as a 10×10 catalytic surface with four possible states per site (4^100 total states). Each trajectory uses two random numbers to determine the time to the next event and which event occurs. Because the number of states is vast, many are never sampled; averages must be computed on the fly. Initial conditions are sampled from a Poisson distribution based on average occupancies. To make calculations feasible, fast processes like diffusion may be assumed infinitely fast or artificially slowed, and very slow processes (e.g., coking over hours) may be omitted. The margin of error is larger for low-probability events.

Molecular dynamics solves Newton's equations of motion using force fields, often with the velocity Verlet algorithm for energy conservation and thermostats to mimic a thermal bath. It can serve as an alternative to Metropolis Monte Carlo for static properties or to simulate time-dependent phenomena. Its time steps are on the order of femtoseconds, limiting total simulation time to nanoseconds, making it suitable for nanosecond-scale processes but not for slow conformational changes or long-time equilibration. Initial conditions must be carefully sampled across relevant conformations.

The lecture emphasizes that Metropolis Monte Carlo, Kinetic Monte Carlo, and molecular dynamics are distinct tools suited to different problem types, and using the wrong method is a common error. Additional topics include choosing weighting functions to make f nearly constant or p sharply focused, and using marginal integrals to eliminate uninteresting parameters. The session ends with announcements about office hours covering Kinetic Monte Carlo, a poll for the final review session, and the posting of homework solutions.

An outside day, or outside bar, is a two-bar price action pattern where the current bar has a higher high and lower low than the previous bar, and its open and close fall outside the previous bar's open and/or close, consuming the full previous bar. It signals rising volatility and stronger buyer or seller conviction: a down second bar suggests sellers in charge and potential further decline; an up second bar suggests buyers in charge and potential rise.

Configurations depend on whether the first and second bars are up or down. Patterns with opposite bar directions are called outside reversal patterns. Outside bars can function as continuation patterns when aligned with the prevailing trend (e.g., bullish outside day in an upswing) or as reversal patterns when the second bar closes opposite to the previous bar and the swing direction. A bullish outside day pattern (second bar bullish) is a stronger engulfing pattern indicating a shift to bulls; a bearish outside day pattern (second bar bearish) indicates a shift to bears. The outside reversal day pattern suggests a probable trend shift and is considered accurate, but it should be combined with trend, support/resistance, pivot, and Fibonacci levels.

Backtesting on SPY showed that after an outside day, the average open-to-close gain is zero, below a random day's 0.04%. Other ETFs also showed random price action. When the outside day's close was higher than the previous day, performance was -0.07%; when lower, +0.06% but not tradable. Overall, backtesting thousands of strategies found little use for outside days in day trading.

The court considered a motion for class certification regarding the drug Baycol. The court found the numerosity requirement was satisfied for all proposed classes. However, it determined that individual issues of law and fact predominated for the nationwide medical monitoring class (Class II), the nationwide injury class (Class III), and the Pennsylvania injury class (Class IV), thus failing the commonality requirement.

For the Pennsylvania medical monitoring class (Class I), the court found common questions of law and fact existed for the medical monitoring claim and a limited unjust enrichment claim for those who purchased Baycol but were told to cease use. The court found the UTPCPL claim failed the commonality requirement due to the need to prove individual reliance. The typicality requirement was met for Class I's medical monitoring claim but not for the unjust enrichment claim due to a lack of evidence. The court found the adequacy of representation requirement was satisfied for Class I.

The court concluded a class action was a fair and efficient method for adjudicating the medical monitoring claim. The court certified a class defined as all persons in Pennsylvania prescribed and ingested Baycol who have not been diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis or congestive heart failure, seeking medical monitoring relief. Arthur Conner, Milton Angert, and Lisa Frost were appointed class representatives. Certification was denied for all other classes.

This passage describes a study examining the influence of the COVID-19 pandemic on special education due process hearings involving city Local Education Agencies (LEAs) in Pennsylvania. In soccer, a defensive switch occurs when the first defender is beaten. The second defender calls for the switch, moves to take the ball carrier, and the first defender covers the opponent originally marked by the second defender, exchanging positions. The second defender positions behind and inside the first defender, goalside, at a distance to react without overrunning, blocking the direct path to goal and influencing the dribbler outside. The second defender announces arrival with calls like 'support' or 'you have help.' As the first defender jockeys, the second defender adjusts positioning. When ready, the second defender may say 'take him' or 'tackle' to allow a tackle. Most switches involve a crossing-pattern initiated by the second defender. Training progresses from stationary to movement, then half-speed with communication: support calls, jockey/delay/control/contain to manage the attacker and buy time, and challenge/tackle calls when support is set. Practice switches by having the first defender be beaten, the second defender call 'switch' or 'switch off,' and the first defender take the second defender's mark. Scenarios include down the sideline (first defender switches inside) and inside from the sideline (first defender switches to the second defender's mark). An alternative midfield switch may occur due to an offensive switch, with defenders trading marks to avoid open space or collision. The NVIDIA Blackwell architecture introduces FP4 precision, reducing VRAM requirements (e.g., FLUX.dev from >23GB to <10GB) and enabling local execution on more GeForce RTX GPUs. Fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add a Triangle Cluster Intersection Engine for Mega Geometry, which uses Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) and Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures (PTLAS) to accelerate ray tracing of high-detail geometry, including subdivision surfaces. Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) provide hardware-accelerated ray tracing for hair and curves, offering 2x speed and 5x VRAM reduction over DOTS. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 improves efficiency with twice the reorder logic efficiency. An AI Management Processor (AMP), a RISC-V-based context scheduler, offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU, reducing latency and improving multitasking. Video features include ninth-generation NVENC with 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC encode and AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, sixth-generation NVDEC with 2x H.264 decode and 4:2:2 support, and DisplayPort 2.1b UHBR 20. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation (up to three AI-generated frames per rendered frame) and transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving image quality and stability. Neural shaders, accessible via Cooperative Vectors API, enable RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Blackwell Max-Q enhancements include advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching (1000x faster), and low-latency sleep states. The architecture spans GB202 (92.2B transistors, up to 24,576 CUDA Cores), GB203, and GB205 GPUs, powering GeForce RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070.

In Clark v. Rau, the Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court's order modifying custody and child support, granting Ricky Rau sole legal and physical custody of the three minor children. Kathrine Clark appealed pro se. The majority opinion, authored by Judge Boggs, held that Clark's appellate brief failed to comply with Court of Appeals Rules 22 and 25, lacking a statement of facts, proper enumerations of error, and supporting arguments. Additionally, no transcript of the bench trial was included in the record. The court stated that it could not discern enumerations of error or argument from the brief, and that creating them would improperly cast the court as an advocate. Because of these deficiencies and the absence of a transcript, the court presumed the regularity of the proceedings and affirmed. The majority also rejected the dissent's argument that the trial court's order was facially deficient for not explicitly stating the modification was in the children's best interest. It noted that neither party requested specific findings of fact, and the order's finding of a material change in circumstances substantially affecting the children's welfare essentially applied the best-interest standard. The judgment was affirmed, with four judges concurring fully, one concurring in judgment only, and four judges dissenting. The dissent, led by Presiding Judge Barnes, argued that the trial court's order failed to include a best-interest determination, which is required when modifying custody, and that the appeal should be reviewed on the merits despite the brief's inadequacies, as the notice of appeal and brief sufficiently indicated the errors being appealed.

A bear market is defined as when the market is below its 200-day moving average. Bear markets occur on average about twice a year, last an average of 25 trading days, and the stock market spends about 30% of its time in them. Common cognitive mistakes include buying high and selling low, as illustrated by investors in a top-performing fund who lost money due to poor timing. To make money in a bear market, traders should stick to their plan and trade both long and short sides. Preparation involves backtesting strategies with strict rules across both bull and bear market cycles. Short strategies tend to work in bear markets, and long trades can also improve, possibly due to short-covering rallies. A backtested long-only strategy on QQQ showed consistent performance in bear markets, outperforming buy-and-hold by preserving capital and compounding efficiently. Long-term investors should continue buying during bear markets to take advantage of lower prices. The key is to follow a backtested plan, avoid emotional reactions, and view bear markets as opportunities rather than threats.

The output diode voltage stress is Vout + VinMAX; the selected diode has a 60 V rating. Main switching MOSFETs in a push-pull topology experience twice the input voltage plus ringing when off, requiring a voltage rating 2.5–3 times the input voltage. Output capacitance of approximately 1145 µF was chosen to limit ripple. An output filter with a 500 nH inductor and capacitors (six ceramics before the filter, then tantalum and small ceramics) further attenuates ripple. A 0.5 Ω damping resistor in parallel with the inductor prevents high-frequency peaking, though it reduces efficiency. Type IIB compensation adds a pole and zero; the zero is placed at least a decade before the 5 kHz crossover frequency, and the pole is placed at the output capacitor ESR zero. Compensation uses 4.75 kΩ, 2200 pF, and 0.12 µF, yielding a zero at 279 Hz and a pole at 15.23 kHz. The sense resistor senses ripple current and shuts down the switching cycle if peak current exceeds the limit; the CS pin threshold is about 1 V. The UC1825B-SP operates from a 10–30 V input and can be used in push-pull, forward, half-bridge, or full-bridge topologies. Layout guidelines: use low-EMI ferrite closed-core inductors; route feedback traces away from noise, on the opposite PCB side with a ground plane; place input ceramic and feed-forward capacitors close to the IC; place compensation components close to the IC and away from the inductor; make power traces short, direct, and thick (minimum 15 mils per ampere); keep the inductor, output capacitors, and output diode close together; connect grounds to a ground plane, ideally on both PCB sides; on multilayer boards, separate power and signal planes and use one via per 200 mA of current; arrange components so switching current loops curl in the same direction. A separate power ground (PGND) handles high di/dt currents; VCC is bypassed to power ground, MOSFET sources connect to power ground, and the output is clamped with a Schottky diode to VCC and PGND. VREF is bypassed to the signal ground plane with a low ESR/ESL ceramic 1-µF capacitor; all analog circuitry is bypassed to signal ground. The package is hermetically sealed with a metal lid. ESD precautions are required. TI provides resources as-is and disclaims warranties.

SOS Pressure Defense integrates switching, with automatic switching reducing hesitation and fouls. "Screen-Over-Switch" is the basic term. Off-ball screens are disrupted by aggressively attacking passing lanes; a "Hi-Lo" technique defends baseline screens. On-ball screens above the free throw line extended are aggressively switched, while those below are aggressively trapped.

Reasons for Contact Switching rules, in order of importance: more effective than "Show and Recover" or "Slide Thru" at denying passing lanes; automatic switching on all on/off-ball screens eliminates hesitation, denies quick catches, and negates open jump shots; it disrupts screening offensive flow, causing bewilderment and frustration; fewer fouls are committed; it denies first passing lanes, forces turnovers and rushed shots, increasing transition points. Mismatches are handled by immediate automatic traps using Near Player rotations.

SOS Switching Techniques: The defender guarding the screen calls "Screen," hedges "Over" one stride, then calls "Switch" as defenders exchange assignments. Off-Ball: Down and Back screens use a contact switch with defenders assuming SNUGGLE pass denial positions, leaving no daylight. Base Screen "Hi-Lo Switch Rule": defenders switch if the cutter goes baseline (low); if the cutter goes over the top (high), they do not switch. On-Ball above the free throw line: contact switch forces the ballhandler to a checkpoint, then SMOTHER and FRONT positions are applied, with weakside "I" positions. On-Ball below the free throw line: a baseline trap is set, forming a "Triangle I" with a 3/4 front, and on a pass out, defenders close out to the nearest offensive player.

Enron, a Houston-based energy company, transformed from a stodgy pipeline firm in 1985 into a trading colossus by 2000, with its stock price increasing 1,700 percent and revenues growing from $40 billion to $100 billion. This shift was largely driven by Jeff Skilling, a consultant hired by CEO Ken Lay, who devised the Gas Bank—a model that contractually guaranteed gas supply and price, making Enron a market-maker rather than a broker. The company came to dominate natural gas trading, then applied the model to electricity and other commodities.

Skilling fostered a culture that prized the “best and brightest,” recruiting aggressively from elite schools and offering high salaries, uncapped bonuses, and perks like concierge services and personal trainers. A Performance Review Committee (PRC) ranked employees on a 1–5 scale, with those rated 5 typically gone within six months; the division replaced about 15 percent of its workforce annually. The environment emphasized short-term profits, internal competition, and a mercenary attitude, with customers referred to as “counterparties.” Enron used mark-to-market accounting on an unprecedented scale, booking profits upfront.

Rebecca Mark, head of Enron International and a rival to Skilling, developed asset-heavy power plants abroad, including a troubled project in Dabhol, India. Skilling, who disdained long-term asset investments, pushed her out by giving her Azurix, a water company that quickly faltered. By late 2000, Skilling was in full control, and in February 2001 he succeeded Lay as CEO.

Almost immediately, problems mounted. Enron was cast as a villain in California’s energy crisis, drawing negative press and causing its stock to slide from $80 to $50. Its telecommunications division suffered after the tech bubble burst, and a high-profile deal with Blockbuster collapsed. Analysts began questioning Enron’s accounting practices. Skilling sold $33 million in stock; other executives sold significantly more. By late August 2001, the stock had fallen below $40.

In August 2001, Skilling abruptly resigned after just six months as CEO, citing personal sacrifices and a desire for family time. Lay returned, promising to refocus on core businesses and soften the culture, acknowledging that the PRC had created morale problems. Skilling, meanwhile, expressed optimism about a “second wave” of technological applications and said he was looking for office space in Houston.

A crystal structure prediction algorithm, TOPIC, was developed to efficiently generate oxide solid-state electrolyte (SSE) structures by enforcing corner-sharing (CS) bond topology constraints. Validated on known systems with up to 192 atoms per unit cell, TOPIC reproduced reference structures and discovered new polymorphs. Using a pretrained machine-learning interatomic potential (SevenNet-0), screening of quaternary Li-oxide compositions with octahedral and tetrahedral polyhedra revealed that a low lithium ratio (Li/non-Li metals ≤1.0) favors stable CS frameworks, which exhibit higher ionic conductivity than non-CS frameworks. Comprehensive screening identified 92 candidates with extrapolated room-temperature ionic conductivity above 0.1 mS cm⁻¹; 15 were further validated by DFT, including Li₄Hf₂Si₃O₁₂ with a conductivity of 14.09 mS cm⁻¹. The Li ratio serves as a key descriptor, and increasing Li content generally lowers activation barriers, though exceptions occur in certain framework types. TOPIC enables exploration of uncharted chemical spaces for next-generation oxide electrolytes.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU features 108 SMs and 432 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 312 TFLOPS of dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance—2.5x the mixed-precision Tensor Core performance of Tesla V100 and 20x V100’s standard FP32 throughput. A100 Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, INT4, binary, and add TF32, BF16, and FP64 formats. TF32 provides the range of FP32 with the precision of FP16, enabling up to 8x throughput over FP32 on A100 with no user script changes. FP16 or BF16 mixed-precision training yields up to 2x over TF32 and up to 16x over FP32 on A100. FP64 Tensor Cores deliver 19.5 TFLOPS, 2.5x V100 FP64 performance.

A100 introduces fine-grained structured sparsity with a 2:4 pattern, doubling compute throughput for deep neural networks by skipping zero-value computations. Sparse Tensor Core operations provide effective TOPS/TFLOPS using this sparsity feature.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions an A100 into up to seven GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute and memory resources (SMs, L2 cache slices, memory controllers, DRAM bandwidth), providing quality of service and fault isolation for multiple tenants. GPU Instances can be further subdivided into Compute Instances, enabling simultaneous context execution.

Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links per GPU at 50 Gbit/s per signal pair, yielding 600 GB/s total bandwidth. A100 supports PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV. Memory includes 40 GB HBM2 with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100), with 2.3x L2 read bandwidth. L2 cache residency controls allow programmers to manage persistent data caching. Compute Data Compression improves DRAM and L2 bandwidth and capacity.

The SM includes a combined L1 data cache and shared memory (192 KB/SM), separate FP32 and INT32 cores for simultaneous execution, and a new asynchronous copy instruction that loads global memory directly into shared memory, bypassing the register file. Asynchronous barriers enable efficient pipelining. CUDA 11 supports third-generation Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs with launch and execution dependency optimizations, asynchronous copy, and L2 cache controls. Cooperative Groups adds warp reduce and async copy collectives.

Additional features: a 5-core hardware JPEG decoder (NVJPG), an optical flow accelerator, improved FP16 and FP32 atomics throughput, and five NVDEC units for video decode. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitches, delivering 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, and includes a software stack with NGC containers, CUDA Toolkit, and container toolkit.

This prospective study enrolled 157 patients hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF). Bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS) was performed at admission and discharge to measure overhydration (OH) and the OH-to-extracellular water (OH/ECW) ratio. Patients were stratified by chronic kidney disease (CKD) and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). CKD patients exhibited higher OH and OH/ECW ratios at admission but showed no association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) or heart failure hospitalization (HHF). Greater reductions in OH/ECW were observed in HFrEF patients compared to non-HFrEF, indicating better diuretic response, but these changes did not translate into improved clinical outcomes. Across all subgroups, OH, OH/ECW, and their changes were not significant predictors of MACE or HHF during the 10.7 ± 7.1-month follow-up. BIS effectively monitors fluid status in ADHF, particularly in HFrEF, but its prognostic utility in CKD and HFpEF subgroups is limited.
