Kerberos is a cryptographically secure authentication protocol for clients and servers over an untrusted network. It introduces a trusted Kerberos server (KDC) that stores shared keys for every principal (users and services). User keys are derived from passwords; service keys are known only to the service and the KDC. The protocol has two interfaces: the initial Kerberos interface and the Ticket Granting Service (TGS). At login, a client sends its principal name and receives a ticket for TGS and a session key, both encrypted with the user’s key. The client decrypts this, then discards the password. To access a service, the client sends the TGS the desired service name, its TGS ticket, and an authenticator; it receives a ticket for that service and a new session key, encrypted with the TGS session key. Tickets contain server and client names, client IP address, timestamp, lifetime, and a session key. Authenticators contain client name, IP, and timestamp, encrypted with the session key. Applications use the ticket (encrypted with the service key) and encrypt requests with the session key; the server decrypts the ticket to learn the session key and client identity.

Kerberos version 4 had several problems: it assumed encryption provided integrity (fixed in v5 with explicit authentication); it allowed offline password guessing because the initial response is encrypted with the user’s key (mitigated by pre-authentication and expensive key derivation); it hardcoded DES, which became weak (v5 supports multiple ciphers); it relied on IP addresses; it used the same session key for both directions, enabling reflection attacks (v5 uses separate keys); authenticators were not bound to messages, allowing replay splicing (v5 binds them); and the password-changing protocol allowed an attacker who later learns an old password to decrypt the chain and obtain the new password (v5 uses Diffie-Hellman key exchange to prevent this). The KDC is a critical trust point; its compromise allows impersonation of any principal. Service key compromise allows both traffic decryption and impersonation to that service, requiring out-of-band key replacement. KDC replication provides availability. Dial-up machines perform a two-step login to verify the Kerberos server’s authenticity. Reusing principal names is dangerous because access control lists still reference old names.

The passage details aspects of the SD Memory Card Physical Layer Specification Version 6.00. Force erase does not erase the secure area; the card remains locked and retains Temporary and Group Write Protection during erase, clearing them after completion. ACMD6 is rejected when the card is locked; bus width can change only when unlocked. Locked cards accept a limited set of commands, and three lock/unlock function types are defined. The switch function command (CMD6) uses Mode 0 to query supported functions and Mode 1 to set them, across function groups: Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit. Power Limit settings control maximum card power consumption. Switch function status returns a 512-bit block with function support bits, selection results, and maximum current/power. High-Speed mode (25 MB/s) is optional, using a 50 MHz clock. CMD8 checks host supply voltage compatibility. SDHC and SDXC cards use block addressing with a fixed 512-byte block length, while SDSC uses byte addressing. Clock control allows stopping under restrictions; CRC7 protects commands and responses, CRC16 protects data. Commands are organized into classes; responses include R1, R1b, R2, R3, R6, and R7. Card Status and SD Status convey error and state information. Speed Class specifications define Allocation Units (AU) and Recording Units (RU). Performance is characterized by Pw (write), Pm (move), and Pr (read). Speed Classes 2, 4, 6, and 10 have specific measurement conditions and performance requirements. SDXC Speed Class uses larger AU sizes, no move performance, and includes FAT, Bitmap, directory entry, and CI updates. UHS Speed Grade and Video Speed Class are also defined.

The present disclosure relates to methods and systems for processing audio signals, specifically detecting and processing speech signals from multiple end points simultaneously. One method involves a group of networked data modules detecting an activation command, computing a score for the detected command, and receiving audio data from each detecting module with a score above a threshold. A request including this audio data is sent to a server, and audio data associated with a requested action is received from the server and communicated to each module in the group. The method may also involve combining the received audio data to generate the request, muting loudspeakers upon detecting the activation command, and activating microphones on modules with scores above the threshold.

Another embodiment relates to a system where each data module, upon detecting an activation command, computes a score and determines if its score is higher than a threshold number of scores from other detecting modules. If so, the module sends its recorded audio data to a server. The module then receives a requested action, determines a confidence level for it, and performs the action if its confidence level is higher than those determined by a threshold number of other modules. The computed score for a detected activation command can be based on signal power, a determined location of the command's source relative to the module, and whether the command corresponds to a previously stored activation command.

In Hill v. Levine, the plaintiff sought specific performance of a contract to sell land. The defendant refused to accept title, arguing that a deed provision requiring lots to have a frontage of at least fifty feet created a doubt about whether the restriction had expired. The deed stated that the premises were conveyed subject to restrictions lasting twenty years from August 20, 1896, including building stipulations and the frontage requirement. The plaintiff contended the frontage restriction expired in 1916; the defendant argued it might last until 1928 or that the doubt precluded specific performance. The Superior Court dismissed the bill, finding reasonable doubt. On appeal, the Supreme Judicial Court held: (1) nothing in the deed or circumstances suggested the frontage provision was part of a scheme benefiting other lots; (2) the provision was a personal agreement between grantor and grantee, and its omission from subsequent deeds indicated it was not for other lot owners' benefit; (3) it did not create an equitable easement appurtenant to remaining lots; (4) the mere possibility of a future claimant challenging a settled rule of law was not a defect justifying denial of specific performance; (5) although a decree would bind only the parties, the court should order specific performance because the question was one of deed construction with no reasonable doubt. The decree was reversed and specific performance ordered, with the plaintiff entitled to seek damages.

A year after Loper Bright overruled Chevron deference, three doctrinal shifts are emerging. First, courts now use independent judgment to find the single best meaning of statutes, leading to a textualist approach where justifications for agency action rely on dictionaries, ordinary meaning, grammar rules, and structural cues rather than broader statutory goals or legislative history. Second, Skidmore deference—where courts respect persuasive agency interpretations—was cited in Loper Bright but has since appeared only indirectly. The Supreme Court has invoked "Shadow Skidmore" by interpreting statutes first and then noting consistent agency views as confirmation, without citing Skidmore. Lower courts are divided, with some circuits questioning Skidmore's viability. Skidmore invocations are more common in immigration and labor cases than in environmental or health care, possibly due to recent executive branch changes. Courts may be using Skidmore to preserve agency expertise for difficult questions or as a legitimating tool, similar to how legislative history was used during the textualist transition. Third, the major questions doctrine (MQD) remains intact, but Justice Kavanaugh's concurrence in a recent case proposed an exception for national security and foreign policy, arguing that the MQD does not reflect ordinary congressional intent in those areas. This exception is relevant to an upcoming tariff case. The administrative state now operates under a text-based framework with an unclear MQD boundary and lingering Skidmore influence.

The scale-in trading strategy involves gradually building a position as entry opportunities arise, rather than entering all at once. It is a planned approach, not a reaction to a losing trade. For retail investors, scaling in typically means buying more as the price drops to lower the average purchase price, a form of dollar-cost averaging. Day traders use it differently: they start with a small position and add only if the market moves favorably, aiming to increase profits on winning trades while limiting initial risk. Institutional traders scale in to fill large orders discreetly, avoiding front-running and excessive price impact. The strategy differs from double-down or Martingale methods, which are reactive attempts to salvage losing trades by adding to them. Scale-out is the opposite process of gradually exiting a position to lock in profits and reduce risk. Advantages of scaling in include a better average entry price, reduced slippage, and efficient capital use; disadvantages include the risk of not fully entering before a trend reversal or sudden reversals causing losses on added positions. A backtest comparing a full investment at first signal to a scale-in approach showed that scaling in improved risk-adjusted return, with less time spent in the market. Swing traders may scale in using mean-reversion (adding at potential reversal levels) or trend-following (adding to winners) methods.

This study evaluated the German 17-item Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ17) for assessing hearing-related quality of life in unilateral Menière’s Disease (MD). In a multicenter prospective cohort of 97 patients (75% definite MD, mean age 56.2 years, 57% female), pure-tone and speech audiometry confirmed asymmetric hearing loss with worse thresholds and speech recognition in affected ears. The mean SSQ17 total score was 6.0 (subscales: speech 5.3, spatial 5.1, qualities 7.2). Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach’s alpha 0.960 for total, 0.904–0.956 for subscales). SSQ scores showed moderate negative correlations with pure-tone thresholds and positive correlations with speech recognition in the affected ear. No significant SSQ differences were found between diagnostic categories. The SSQ17 is a viable tool for capturing hearing disability in MD, complementing clinical audiometry, though it does not assess vertigo burden.

The volume covers the San Francisco Conference (April 25–June 26, 1945). It lists chapter headings for April 10–May 31, 1945, and topics such as U.S. efforts in the Preparatory Commission, selection of the U.S. as permanent seat, UNESCO, ILO, and the International Organizations Immunities Act. A guide to Dumbarton Oaks discussions is included. The historical note records the conference drafted the UN Charter; on June 25, fifty governments approved the Charter, Statute of the International Court of Justice, and Interim Arrangements. The Charter was signed June 26, with space for Poland. The Senate ratified July 28, Truman August 8, and the UN Participation Act was signed December 20. The Charter entered into force October 24, 1945. The conference had four commissions, twelve technical committees, and four general committees. Charter drafting occurred in closed committee meetings. Records were mimeographed, half a million sheets daily. Principal documents appeared in a 22-volume series in English and French; final documents are in five official languages. Volume 21 contains an index with legislative history and correspondence tables.

This scoping review examines anti-inflammatory strategies for treating depression. The introduction notes that inflammation is associated with depression, with elevated inflammatory markers like cytokines, and that anti-inflammatory drugs such as NSAIDs, Omega-3 fatty acids, and steroids have shown antidepressant effects in some studies. However, the translation of these findings into clinical practice remains unresolved.

The literature review covers 31 animal studies focusing on neuroinflammatory targets (NLRP3, NF-κB, P2X7R pathways) and interventions including pharmacological agents (e.g., empagliflozin, calcitriol, natural extracts) and non-pharmacological methods (acupuncture, exercise, light therapy). These studies suggest modulation of neuroinflammation can improve depressive symptoms, but long-term stability, individual differences, and clinical relevance are not established.

The scoping review of randomized controlled trials identified 11 studies (907 patients) published between 2008 and 2024, predominantly from the UK and China. Anti-inflammatory drugs used included fluoxetine, infliximab, ketamine, minocycline, vortioxetine with celecoxib, and others. Inflammatory markers measured included CRP, hs-CRP, IL-2, IL-6, TNF-α, and others, but many were below detection levels. Treatment duration ranged from 2 to 18 weeks. Benefits included potential symptom improvement and regulation of inflammatory state, but challenges included significant inter-patient variability in response, with baseline hs-CRP levels influencing outcomes, and safety concerns with drugs like celecoxib. Inflammatory markers showed some predictive value for treatment response.

The discussion highlights that immune mechanisms from animal models may not apply to human depression, as triggers in humans are diverse. The cost of inflammatory marker testing is high compared to traditional therapies. The authors propose a systematic approach to selecting inflammatory indicators and suggest artificial intelligence could assist in personalized treatment and monitoring. They also mention micro-robot technology for targeted drug delivery and monitoring. The conclusion states that pharmacological anti-inflammatory strategies for depression currently have limited research value and poor feasibility, and recommends shifting focus to non-pharmacological anti-inflammatory approaches like exercise and positive thinking, with an emphasis on low-cost, generalizable research.

The passage is a compilation of news headlines and articles from November 29, 2001, detailing the fallout from Enron Corp.'s financial collapse. Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle called for a congressional investigation. Enron was poised to file the largest-ever bankruptcy case, with over $15 billion in debt. Dynegy Inc. abandoned its acquisition after credit downgrades to junk status. Enron shares fell to $0.41, and bonds traded flat around 22 cents on the dollar without accrued interest.

Market impacts included: NYMEX restricted trading with Enron and raised margins; EnronOnline reopened only to unwind positions; IntercontinentalExchange saw trading volumes surge 65%. U.S. power and gas markets remained orderly but with some volatility. UK day-ahead electricity prices dropped sharply. German power prices were jumpy. Enron guaranteed European power delivery only through Friday. Enron's metals unit was close to being sold, with HSBC, Glencore, and others rumored as buyers. Enron's European arm entered administration.

Financial exposures were reported: Reliant Resources ~$80 million, Williams expected less than $100 million, Duke Energy ~$100 million, Centrica £30 million in contracts. German banks' exposures ranged from €10 million to $100 million. CSFB estimated Bank of America, Citigroup, and J.P. Morgan Chase each had $500 million in direct loan exposure. Bank sector bond spreads widened. Four Japanese money management funds fell below par value due to Enron bond losses, triggering large redemptions. European mutual funds generally had limited exposure, many having sold earlier. Enron's overseas assets, particularly in South America and Asia, were expected to complicate bankruptcy proceedings.

This retrospective single-center cohort study included 226 adult patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) admitted between 2020 and 2022. Rebleeding occurred in 33 patients (15%). Among previously identified predictors, only time from first symptoms to event was significantly associated with rebleeding in univariate analysis (OR 1.007 per hour, p=0.026), and this association remained significant in multivariate analysis (p=0.008). WFNS score also showed an independent linear relationship with rebleeding risk (OR 2.444, p=0.039). Other factors such as systolic blood pressure, aneurysm size, location, and presence of hematomas did not differ significantly between patients with and without rebleeding. The mean time to event (rebleeding or securing) was shorter in patients without rebleeding (36 vs 63 hours, p<0.001). Two-thirds of rebleeding events occurred more than 24 hours after symptom onset. Among patients whose aneurysms were secured within 24 hours, 9% rebled prior to securing, compared to 21% in those treated after 24 hours (p=0.021). The study concludes that time elapsed since headache onset is a significant risk factor for rebleeding, supporting early aneurysm securing as recommended by guidelines. Limitations include the retrospective design and limited number of events.

The article backtests calendar effects in long-term Treasuries using the TLT ETF from 2004 to August 2021. It identifies two effects: the first seven trading days of the month show strong negative returns, while the rest of the month has doubled the returns of buying and holding TLT. An end-of-month effect is also present. A combined strategy of being long the end-of-month effect and short the first few days yields an annual return of 10.2% (vs. 3.8% buy-and-hold) and a max drawdown of 24% (vs. 48%). A short-only strategy from the previous month's close to the close of the seventh trading day has a CAGR of 5.5%, average gain per trade of 0.6%, and profit factor of 2. A long strategy from the close of the seventh trading day to month-end doubles the buy-and-hold return while invested two-thirds of the time. The article explains the inverse relationship between TLT price and interest rates. The complete Python code for the strategies is provided, and the trading rules are available in a purchasable compilation of strategies.

Digital laggards fail to connect goals with strategy, leading to misalignment. Data culture aligns organizations vertically through data-driven metrics and horizontally via common data models and transparent access. Digital leaders emphasize data culture as central, aligning beliefs, espoused values, and day-to-day actions. At digital leaders, employee behaviors reflect company values driven by leadership beliefs. Digital laggards show misalignment between espoused values and behavior due to entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient top-down focus. Changing mindsets is the most challenging part of transformation. However, digital laggards are not doomed; some leaders transformed their cultures. Technologically mature firms enjoy business advantages and distinct data culture approaches, valuing learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement. Organizations fit into four patterns: data novice (recognize need but lack culture/systems), insight ready (accepting culture but limited capabilities), tech enabled (have technology but lack experimentation culture), and data reliant (over-rely on data, discouraging critical thinking). Companies can target actions based on their pattern. Keystone Strategy is a consulting firm specializing in technology-led strategy and digital transformation.

The Blackwell architecture introduces Mega Geometry, which uses clusters of up to 256 triangles as first-class primitives to build Cluster-level Acceleration Structures (CLAS) and a final BVH, reducing BVH build processing by two orders of magnitude. A Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structure (PTLAS) allows persistent TLAS updates by aggregating static objects into partitions and rebuilding only changed ones. Mega Geometry also enables fast ray tracing of subdivision surfaces by mapping tessellation to cluster generation. It is supported on DirectX 12 (via NVAPI), Vulkan (vendor extensions), OptiX 9.0, and all RTX GPUs starting with Turing. Blackwell’s 4th generation RT Cores add hardware cluster engines, new compression, and up to 2x ray-triangle intersection rate.

Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) are a new hardware-accelerated primitive that sweeps spheres along linear segments, supporting varying radii and spheres directly. LSS provides about 2x faster rendering and 5x less VRAM than DOTS for hair.

Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 doubles reorder logic efficiency, increases precision, and allows more application-specific knowledge, improving coherence for neural workloads and path tracing.

The AI Management Processor (AMP) is a RISC-V-based context scheduler that offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU, reducing latency and improving frame pacing, especially for concurrent AI and graphics workloads.

Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled video. The ninth-generation NVENC encoder improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, adds AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, and supports 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encoding. The sixth-generation NVDEC decoder offers 2x faster H.264 decoding and 4:2:2 decode support. DisplayPort 2.1b UHBR 20 enables up to 8K 165Hz and 4K 480Hz with DSC.

Max-Q power efficiency features include advanced power gating with multiple new levels, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, accelerated frequency switching that adjusts clocks 1000x faster, and low latency sleep states that are up to 10x faster to enter than Ada, enabling up to 50% power savings in some inference workloads.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame using a faster AI model that replaces hardware optical flow, and enhanced flip metering for precise frame pacing. Transformer-based models replace CNNs for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, detail in motion, and reducing artifacts.

Neural shaders, accessible via the Cooperative Vectors API in DirectX and Vulkan, allow AI models to run in graphics shaders. RTX Neural Materials use neural approximations for complex multi-layer materials. RTX Neural Texture Compression provides up to 7:1 VRAM compression. Neural Radiance Cache infers multi-bounce indirect lighting from single-bounce rays. RTX Skin enables real-time subsurface scattering for path tracing. RTX Neural Faces uses a generative AI model to infer natural-looking faces from rasterized input and 3D pose data.

The GB202 GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, 768 Tensor Cores, and a 512-bit memory interface. The GeForce RTX 5090 uses this chip. A Seattle Public Utilities (SPU) study finds that while Seattle's typical short showers and drizzle persist, extreme rainstorms have become more frequent and intense over the last 15 years. SPU has collected rainfall data for about four decades from 17 city gauges. The study updates a 2003 analysis. It shows that what was once considered a 100-year storm for a 24-hour period (4 inches) now occurs roughly every 25 years, and the new 100-year benchmark exceeds 5 inches. Similarly, a 6-hour 100-year storm (1.86 inches) is now a 25-year event. Extreme storms lasting six hours or three days at 5- and 10-year recurrence levels have also intensified. These events are sometimes called atmospheric rivers. Seattle's overall rainfall accumulation remains low nationally, as most rain comes from low, layered clouds. SPU meteorologist James Rufo-Hill said the data confirms anecdotal reports of worsening rain. Residents describe larger drops, all-day downpours, and construction challenges. SPU will use the findings to size drainage and wastewater infrastructure, which was originally built for light rain, not downpours. A storage tunnel under the Lake Washington Ship Canal is under construction to reduce polluted overflows. The study aligns with National Weather Service data and, according to officials, underscores the need for better flood preparation in Western Washington. Scientists link the trend to climate change, and Mayor Jenny Durkan cited it while promoting city climate actions.

The present invention relates to a driving assistance system for a vehicle that uses one or more sensors (such as cameras, radar, lidar) to capture data about the exterior environment. The system processes sensor data to detect surrounding vehicles, their speeds, and directions. When a rearward approaching vehicle is determined to be traveling faster than the equipped vehicle, the system can control the equipped vehicle to accelerate to at least the speed of that rearward vehicle and/or change lanes to avoid a collision. In one scenario, if the equipped vehicle is approaching a slower leading vehicle and a faster vehicle is approaching from behind in an adjacent lane, the system may accelerate to match the rearward vehicle's speed and change lanes into that adjacent lane ahead of it. In another scenario, if a faster vehicle approaches from behind in the same lane or an adjacent lane on a multi-lane road, the system may accelerate to match its speed or change lanes to the right to allow it to pass. The decision to stay in lane or change lanes is based on parameters such as distances, speeds, free space ahead and in adjacent lanes, speed limits, and other factors. The system can operate in driver-assist modes (SAE Level 2) or autonomous modes (SAE Level 3), and may provide alerts or instructions to the driver. It may also incorporate adaptive cruise control with speed limits that account for vehicle type, trailer towing, and driver license class.

The Seventh Circuit reversed the district court's dismissal of a putative class action challenging the practice of 19 Illinois counties imposing a bail fee, authorized by state statute, as a condition for release on bail. The district court had dismissed the entire action for lack of standing and denied class certification as moot.

The appellate court held that the named plaintiffs had standing to bring individual claims against Kane and DuPage Counties, the two counties where they were confined and paid the contested fees, because they suffered a monetary injury traceable to those counties' policies. The dismissal of those individual claims was reversed and remanded for reinstatement.

The court also reversed the dismissal of the putative class actions against Kane and DuPage Counties, noting that named representatives from those counties existed and that class certification should be evaluated under Rule 23 without regard to the likelihood of success on the merits. The district court was instructed to consider on remand the possible effect of related class actions, Ringswald v. County of DuPage and Coleman v. County of Kane.

Regarding the remaining 17 counties, the court discussed the "juridical link" doctrine, under which a plaintiff class might sue defendants with whom the named plaintiffs had no direct contact if the defendants are linked by a common legal rule, such as the state statute at issue. The court did not decide the applicability of the doctrine but held that the district court must first conduct a Rule 23 class certification analysis, as class certification issues are logically antecedent to Article III standing concerns. If a class is properly certified, standing is assessed with reference to the class as a whole. The case was remanded for the district court to perform the Rule 23 inquiry, including considerations of typicality, commonality, numerosity, and adequacy of representation, and to determine whether the named plaintiffs may represent a class against all 19 counties. The court observed that the named plaintiffs were personally injured by the same statute that allegedly injured the entire proposed class, so they were not attempting to acquire standing through the injuries of others.

A solid-state photon upconversion system is demonstrated using a bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) sensitizer composed of the squaraine donor DIB-SQ and the fullerene acceptor PCBM, paired with a rubrene or rubrene:DBP annihilator layer. The BHJ composition was optimized to a 1:3 weight ratio of DIB-SQ:PCBM, which maximized triplet state population in rubrene. Under 690 nm near-infrared excitation, the system exhibits upconverted photoluminescence in the visible range (550–650 nm for rubrene, shifted to 605 nm with DBP doping). The upconversion quantum yield reached 1.36% at excitation intensities above 69.7 mW/cm², with a low threshold intensity of 60.5 mW/cm². Time-resolved absorption measurements revealed that photoexcited singlet excitons dissociate into charge transfer (CT) states, and non-geminate recombination populates triplet CT states (³CT) and molecular triplets on PCBM. These triplets transfer energy to rubrene triplet states, which undergo triplet-triplet annihilation (TTA) to generate singlet excitons and upconverted emission. Magnetic field effect measurements confirmed the TTA mechanism, showing a decrease in upconverted emission under an external magnetic field. The approach repurposes the typically loss-associated ³CT formation in donor-acceptor BHJs as a triplet sensitization pathway for near-infrared-to-visible photon upconversion.

In 2017, the Woodland Trust’s Nature’s Calendar recorded 42 spring signs at over 1,000 UK sites, including snowdrops and song thrush. Fewer records than 2016 are attributed to colder January temperatures. The project aids climate change research by tracking seasonal changes.

In Valentine Vredenburg et al. vs. W. J. Behan et al., the plaintiffs moved to dismiss a devolutive appeal on five grounds: (1) the transcript was imperfect and incomplete; (2) not all parties to the judgment were made parties to the appeal; (3) after judgment, defendant M. Buck Miller died and his heirs were not made parties; (4) appellants failed to ask for citation on all parties; (5) several appellants had acquiesced in the judgment. The court denied the motion. It held that the law was substantially complied with when three partial transcripts were filed under the same docket number, with the clerk's certificate stating that together they contained all proceedings, evidence, and documents. Appellants were not bound to name appellees in their petition; it was sufficient to pray that appellees be cited, and the clerk had the duty to issue citations. The acquiescence of some appellants did not justify dismissing the appeal as to those who had not acquiesced. The omission to make Miller's representatives parties did not prejudice the remaining appellants, as they had done what the law required, and any irregularity could still be raised. The motion to dismiss was denied with costs.

The Supreme Court of Puerto Rico reversed a lower court judgment that had awarded damages to Ángel Bracero for injuries caused by falling bags of rice. In late 2011, Charley Dublin, VP of Engineering for Akamai’s intelligent platform and VP of international support and services, was tasked with solving the company’s “localization challenge.” Akamai, the world’s largest content delivery network (CDN) with 60% market share and $1.6 billion in revenue, provided content delivery and cloud infrastructure services to customers like Apple, Amazon, and Netflix. It operated over 100,000 servers in 78 countries, handling up to 30% of all Internet traffic.

Dublin had previously shown senior management that Akamai’s market share declined with distance from the United States, as local competitors in non-U.S. markets eroded its once-dominant position. The CEO charged Dublin and the international leadership team to develop a solution.

Akamai faced competitive pressure from new local CDNs offering simpler, cheaper solutions, as well as from major customers like Amazon and Microsoft building in-house capabilities. A federated CDN group called OCX, formed by telecoms, also posed a potential threat.

Internally, Akamai struggled with misalignment between its global functions and local markets. Products were developed in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with global pricing set there and only converted to local currencies. Local sales teams often found products ill-suited to local needs or faced unachievable sales targets based on U.S. work-week assumptions. For example, Japan rejected a newly acquired mobile-content technology because a superior version had existed there for nearly a decade. In South Korea, Akamai held only 10% market share against CDNetworks’ 70%, partly because its globally-set prices were far higher and its local network performance was not competitive for Korea-specific content. Brand awareness was also weak in some regions; a Chinese customer did not recognize Akamai despite knowing the CDN industry.

A 2011 reorganization into three geographic theaters and business units aimed to improve coordination and clarify customer ownership, but tensions persisted over pricing authority and product decisions. Dublin needed to determine where Akamai had to be local, how quickly, and to what extent, while integrating its global core. The challenge was balancing local responsiveness with the needs of global customers and centralized functions.

The passage introduces an evolutionary hypergame dynamics framework where individuals have heterogeneous strategy sets, reflecting limited knowledge or perception, rather than full access to all strategies. On a fast timescale, players update strategies via introspection reasoning; on a slow timescale, strategy set frequencies evolve. The model uses a three-strategy prisoner’s dilemma: cooperation (C), defection (D), and loner (L). Tournament competitions among strategy sets show that {C, L} outperforms others as introspection strength w and benefit-to-cost ratio b/c increase. Theoretical analysis confirms that {C, L} self-reciprocity increases with w, and it avoids exploitation by defectors when w exceeds a critical threshold. Evolutionary dynamics in well-mixed populations, modeled by replicator equations, reveal that under weak w, {D, L} or {L} dominates, while higher w leads to {C, L} dominance. On structured populations (lattices), similar patterns emerge: low w favors {D, L} or {L}, and high w favors {C, L}. The study concludes that heterogeneity and introspection strength reshape evolutionary outcomes, with higher rationality promoting cooperation.

This study reports ex vivo drug susceptibility and genotype-phenotype associations for Plasmodium falciparum isolates collected from eastern and northern Uganda between July 2019 and June 2024. A total of 1,113 isolates were successfully evaluated against nine antimalarials using a 72-hour growth inhibition assay. Median IC50 values were low nanomolar for chloroquine, monodesethylamodiaquine, piperaquine, dihydroartemisinin, lumefantrine, mefloquine, and pyronaridine, indicating potent activity, while quinine and pyrimethamine showed higher IC50s. Over time, susceptibility to chloroquine increased, whereas susceptibilities to dihydroartemisinin, lumefantrine, and mefloquine decreased, with more marked changes in eastern Uganda. Ring-stage survival assays showed many isolates had survival above established artemisinin resistance cut-offs, and survival increased over time. Genotyping of 80 genes revealed very low prevalence of PfCRT K76T and PfMDR1 N86Y mutations, moderate and increasing prevalence of PfK13 C469Y and A675V mutations, and high prevalence of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance mutations. PfK13 C469Y and A675V were associated with decreased susceptibility to dihydroartemisinin and lumefantrine based on IC50, but not with ring-stage survival assay results. The wild-type PfMDR1 N86Y allele was associated with decreased lumefantrine and mefloquine susceptibility. Additional polymorphisms, including PfCARL D611N and PfMDR1 Y500N, showed strong associations with lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin susceptibility, respectively. The findings indicate that while most antimalarials remain active, susceptibilities to the components of artemether-lumefantrine have decreased modestly, and the clinical implications are uncertain. Continued parasitological and genomic surveillance is a high priority.

The author argues that Nigeria's political system suffers from a lack of deep understanding of its ethnic configuration. They seek to explain this history, asserting that Nigeria is a nation of ethnicities misrepresented by a false North-South divide. The North was united by Usman Dan Fodio's conquest, common language, and religion, while the South's similarity stems only from shared colonial administration. Three foundational figures held differing views: Ahmadu Bello (Sardauna) prioritized the North, then Nigeria; Nnamdi Azikiwe envisioned a Nigeria without ethnicities; Obafemi Awolowo advocated a Nigeria of distinct ethnicities with a balanced federal system. The Sardauna's political stances, including alliance with emirs, were strategic responses to Aminu Kano's radical NEPU. Historical events such as Azikiwe's political alliances, the Niger Delta Congress's 1958 pact with the Northern Peoples Congress, and especially the 1966 coup—in which Sardauna and Tafawa Balewa were killed by an Igbo officer—deeply shaped Northern politics, fostering a lasting preoccupation with power. Four Northern political strands emerged: a conservative oligarchy, nationalists, Aminu Kano radicals, and middle-belt nationalists. Awolowo's push for minority regions led only to the Midwest's creation until later state creation. The Second Republic's nationalist NPN was overthrown in 1983 by a Northern oligarchy that installed Buhari. The PDP later emerged, but some feudalists remained. Opposition to Obasanjo's second term used political Sharia; he countered by elevating Northern successors. The Northern oligarchy subsequently engineered Buhari's candidacy at an ANPP convention, sidelining southern aspirants. The author stresses that not all Northerners support this oligarchy, citing allies who oppose Buhari, and warns against assuming Southern solidarity, insisting that national coalition-building is essential. InVirtuoGen is a continuous-time discrete flow model for fragment-based drug discovery that operates on fragmented SMILES. Unlike autoregressive or masked diffusion models, it refines all sequence positions simultaneously at each denoising step, decoupling sampling steps from sequence length. The model uses a linear scheduler and a time-weighted training objective emphasizing later timesteps, with a diffusion transformer backbone. The molecular representation extends the SAFE framework, employing BRICS decomposition, explicit attachment points, and random fragment shuffling to remove ordering bias, tokenized to a 204-token vocabulary. Pretraining uses ZINC and UniChem datasets. In de novo generation, InVirtuoGen achieves a superior quality-diversity Pareto frontier; smaller timestep sizes improve performance, and sampling directly from predicted token distributions outperforms the standard discrete flow update. For fragment-constrained generation, the model yields competitive average quality and diversity compared to GenMol and SAFE-GPT, though fixing fragment positions conflicts with its refinement philosophy. For target property optimization on the PMO benchmark, a hybrid approach combines a genetic algorithm (fragment recombination from high-scoring molecules) with PPO-based reinforcement learning adapted to discrete flows, approximating log-probabilities via Monte Carlo estimation over perturbed states. The framework achieves state-of-the-art results on PMO and improved lead optimization over prior baselines.

The lecture reviews Wald's equality: for IID random variables with mean X̄, if J is a stopping trial with finite expectation, then E[S_J] = X̄ E[J]. A stopping trial J satisfies that the indicator of {J=n} is a function of X₁,…,Xₙ. The proof uses independence of the indicator of {J≥n} from Xₙ. The elementary renewal theorem states that for a renewal process, lim_{t→∞} E[N(t)]/t = 1/X̄. A lower bound follows from Wald's equality by taking J = N(t)+1, giving E[N(t)] ≥ t/X̄ - 1; an upper bound requires a truncation argument.

Generalized stopping trials are defined for sequences of pairs (Xᵢ, Vᵢ), where the stopping decision can depend on both; Wald's equality still holds. This is applied to a G/G/1 queue with IID interarrival times Xᵢ and IID service times Vᵢ. The first arrival to an empty system is a generalized stopping trial, and intervals between such renewals form a renewal process, enabling renewal reward analysis.

Little’s theorem is derived: L = λ W, where L is time-average number in the system, λ is the arrival rate, and W is time-average waiting time per customer. The proof integrates L(t) over a renewal period, equates it to the sum of customer waiting times, and takes limits using the strong law of large numbers.

The Pollaczek-Khinchin formula for an M/G/1 queue (Poisson arrivals, general IID service times) gives expected waiting time in queue: W_q = λ E[V²] / (2(1-ρ)), with ρ = λ E[V]. Expected number in system follows from Little’s theorem. Examples show deterministic service times yield half the queueing delay of exponential service times, and heavy-tailed service distributions cause large delays due to residual life effects. The derivation uses the time-average residual life of the customer in service, (λ E[V²])/2, and the independence of queue length and service times.

A method is presented for generating and detecting magnetic monopoles on the surface of a 3D topological insulator (TI) using scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS). Magnetic monopoles are hypothetical particles whose existence was proposed by Dirac to explain charge quantization; while quasiparticle analogs have been realized, fundamental monopoles remain unobserved. The topological magnetoelectric (TME) effect in TIs (θ=π) allows an applied electric field to induce a magnetic monopole. In this work, a radially distributed electric field from an STM tip is applied to Bi(111), a 3D high-order TI, creating a pair of inverse magnetic monopoles at the interfaces via Hall circulation. Image potential states (IPS), Rydberg-like series formed by electrons and image charges, are used as probes. On topologically trivial √3-Bi and 2D TI Bi(110), IPS peaks show no splitting and their linewidths decrease with principal quantum number n. On Bi(111) (thickness 5–6 nm), IPS peaks for n>1 exhibit asymmetric shapes and splitting; the n=2 peak splits into two sub-peaks, and higher n peaks show unresolved splitting. The splitting is attributed to Zeeman coupling between the orbital magnetic moment of the IPS and the magnetic field of the induced monopole. Alternative explanations—symmetric/antisymmetric IPS series, quantum well states, and quantum dot confinement—are excluded. The splitting energy ΔE(n) follows a model where ΔE(n) ∝ √(n(n−1))/(n³(n−1/2)), and the measured n=2 splitting (~400 meV) is on the same order as theoretical estimates. Varying the tunneling current changes the tip electric field, continuously tuning the splitting; the dependence fits the Fowler-Nordheim relation, confirming electrical-field-induced magnetic polarization via the TME effect. The results demonstrate the successful generation and detection of magnetic monopole singularity fields in a solid-state system, offering a platform for exploring topological field theory and potential applications in quantum computing and novel electronic devices.

The present invention relates to an image encoding/decoding method, apparatus, and recording medium using motion vector refinement. A decoding method comprises deriving an initial motion vector of a current block (including an initial L0 motion vector and an initial L1 motion vector), deriving a refined motion vector using the initial motion vector, and generating a prediction block using the refined motion vector. The refined motion vector is derived by a merge mode-based motion vector refinement method or a prediction block-based motion vector refinement method.

In the merge mode-based method, information indicating the initial motion vector to be used is entropy-decoded, and magnitude information, direction information, and magnitude unit information (integer pixel or sub-pixel) of the refined motion vector may be entropy-decoded. The refined L0 motion vector is derived by adding a difference between the L0 initial motion vector and an L0 motion vector moved within a predetermined search area to the L0 initial motion vector. The refined L1 motion vector is derived similarly, with mirroring or scaling of differences depending on whether POC differences between reference pictures and the current picture are both negative, only one negative, or different from each other.

In the prediction block-based method, information indicating whether the method is usable is entropy-decoded. The method is performed only when the current block has a bi-direction prediction merge mode, when the POC differences between the L0 and L1 reference pictures and the current picture are equal, and when the vertical size of the current block is 8 or more and the area is 64 or more. The search area is set on a per integer pixel basis, ranging from −2 to 2 pixel positions horizontally and vertically from the position indicated by the initial motion vector. If the current block has a vertical or horizontal size greater than 16, it is divided into 16×16 sub-blocks and refinement is performed per sub-block. The refined L0 motion vector is derived from a distortion value (calculated by SAD, SATD, SSE, or MSE) between prediction blocks generated using motion vectors moved within the search area in the L0 and L1 reference pictures.

An encoding method similarly derives an initial motion vector and a refined motion vector, and entropy-encodes motion compensation information using the refined motion vector. The invention aims to improve compression efficiency and reduce computational complexity.

Suicide is a leading cause of death among young people globally and imposes economic burdens. In China, although overall suicide rates have declined, adolescent suicidal ideation and attempts remain concerning. The Ministry of Education advocates for mental health services and school-family partnerships. Gatekeepers (parents, teachers, peers) can identify at-risk students and intervene. School-based gatekeeper training programs, such as QPR and ASIST, aim to improve knowledge, reduce stigma, and promote referral, but evidence on their effectiveness in reducing suicide behavior or increasing gatekeeper behavior is inconclusive, partly due to small samples and short follow-ups. The theory of planned behavior may help bridge the gap between training and actual behavior.

In China, there is a lack of rigorously designed, localized gatekeeper training for secondary/high school teachers and parents. Existing studies are descriptive, and no parent training studies exist. Sociocultural factors like left-behind children and a shortage of qualified school counselors necessitate culturally adapted programs. This study employed the Delphi method to develop an evidence-based, localized suicide gatekeeper training program. The Delphi process involved expert consensus through iterative rating of statements. Content was initially developed from a literature review and discussions with school counselors and experts, organized into eight sections: severity of adolescent suicide, understanding suicide, risk factors, warning signs, communication, risk assessment, safety plan, teacher-specific and parent-specific modules, and barriers to help-seeking. A working group refined statements for comprehensibility. Panel members were selected based on experience in suicide intervention (e.g., crisis intervention committee members, psychiatrists, professors, school counselors, crisis line operators). Two rounds of online questionnaires were conducted between September and November 2022, where experts rated statements on importance, feasibility, and appropriateness using a five-point Likert scale. Statements with substantial consensus were retained for the training program. The study was approved by Tsinghua University's IRB.

An inside day occurs when today's price action is completely within yesterday's range (low higher than yesterday's low, high lower than yesterday's high). Inside days are frequent, occurring about 10% of the time in the S&P 500 since 1993. Backtests indicate that an inside day alone is a poor trading signal. Buying all inside days and selling at the next open produced only a modest average gain. Adding a five-day RSI filter (below 50) increased the average gain to 0.1% but remained untradeable. A swing trading strategy using changed parameters yielded 89 trades since 1993 with an average gain of 0.45% and a profit factor of 2.1, but this only worked in equity markets and performed oppositely in gold. Two consecutive inside days generated very few trades. The passage concludes that inside days are not a good standalone variable and require additional variables to build a viable strategy.

The passage addresses damages for the seizure of whaling ships. It notes the Williams case awarded passage money. Damages for the Cape Horn Pigeon's lost catch, seized at Vladivostok during the whaling season, are direct losses, not speculative profits. Unlike trading vessels, where demurrage compensates for detention based on freight earnings and trade can resume, a whaling ship's yearly earnings hinge on the brief season; missing it deprives owners of returns and the lay-paid crew of wages. The Cape Horn Pigeon returned with insufficient oil and bone to cover costs, leaving the crew in debt. The established rule for fishing vessels values the vessel's use during detention, using average catch as evidence. For whale ships, crew damages are included via their lay in the award. The Costa Rica Packet case is referenced: the arbitrator found the captain's detention caused him to miss the best season, but he could have returned by January 1892, and no proof compelled him to leave the ship until April or sell at a reduced price.

Strength training builds muscle mass, strength, and endurance, but using correct techniques and warming up and cooling down properly is crucial to avoid injuries. Warming up increases heart rate and blood flow, delivering oxygen to muscles and helping prevent injury; a rabbit study supported a protective mechanism. Cooling down regulates blood flow. Dynamic movements are recommended for warm-up, static holds for cool-down.

Common injuries include rotator cuff injuries (shoulder pain from repetitive overhead motions, such as in tennis or construction work), which can be tears or tendinopathy. Prevention includes good shoulder blade posture and adjusting exercise if there is discomfort. Hamstring injuries occur from sudden powerful movements like running or jumping, with three grades of severity; regular stretching and warming up reduce risk. A herniated disc (slipped disc) can result from sudden extreme movement or repetitive poor weightlifting form, causing pain, numbness, or weakness in the back and legs; good form is essential. Tendonitis is irritation from micro tears in tendons due to repetitive motions or sudden impact, causing persistent pain, burning, swelling; prevention involves gentle stretching, limiting forceful repetitions, and not ignoring pain. Tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis) causes outer elbow pain from repetitive wrist/arm motions, affecting athletes and others like painters; treatment includes rest, medicines, possibly physiotherapy or surgery.

Fitness coach Ollie Kerr notes injuries can also stem from lifting inappropriate weights or increasing intensity too quickly, so changes should be gradual. Recovery is aided by a good diet, hydration, and ice, compression, elevation. He advises warming up suitably, working within limitations, and allowing recovery time. Further tips: don't push beyond comfort, ask for help, consult a doctor if pain persists, and consider a qualified trainer before starting a new routine.

Prolonged sitting negatively affects health, but 22 minutes of moderate to vigorous exercise daily may reduce these impacts. Autumn is suggested as a good time to restart a fitness routine. The information is peer-reviewed by clinicians.

The NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture, including GA102 and GA104 GPUs, builds on Turing to deliver significant performance gains. The architecture provides up to 1.7x faster traditional raster graphics and up to 2x faster ray tracing compared to Turing.

The GA10x Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) doubles FP32 processing throughput by enabling FP32 operations on both datapaths, achieving up to 30 TFLOPS in RTX 3080. The second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection testing rate, supports concurrent RT and graphics or compute workloads, and adds hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur via a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit, making motion blur rendering up to 8x faster than Turing. Third-generation Tensor Cores introduce fine-grained structured sparsity, which can double matrix operation throughput, and support new data types including TF32 and BF16. RTX 3080 delivers 238 sparse Tensor TFLOPS (FP16) versus 89 non-sparse in RTX 2080.

The memory subsystem uses GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling, achieving up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth on RTX 3090. RTX IO enables GPU-based lossless decompression and, with Microsoft DirectStorage, offloads CPU work, improving I/O performance and reducing CPU utilization. Display support includes HDMI 2.1 with DSC 1.2a for 8K60 HDR, and DisplayPort 1.4a. The fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decode, and the seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware video encoding.

GeForce RTX 3090 offers 10496 CUDA Cores, 24 GB GDDR6X, and 8K gaming capability with DLSS 8K mode. RTX 3080 delivers up to 2x the performance of RTX 2080. RTX 3070 rivals RTX 2080 Ti. NVIDIA RTX A6000 and A40 feature 10752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-gen RT Cores, 336 third-gen Tensor Cores, 48 GB GDDR6, and support NVLink for up to 96 GB combined memory. A40 is optimized for data center visual computing, offering up to 2x FP32 throughput and up to 2x ray-tracing throughput over previous generation.

The passage describes an extension of an ab initio approach for simulating spin diffusion length (ls) to include the effect of an electric field along a periodic direction. ls is a key parameter for spintronic devices, and accurate simulation of the spin-drift effect under a longitudinal field is critical for predictive modeling. The authors previously developed a linearized density-matrix master equation method that successfully modeled ls in various materials, but treating a periodic-direction field was challenging. They now extend the method using a covariant derivative formalism. The paper outlines the derivation of a linearized steady-state quantum master equation under finite electric field, incorporating diffusion, coherent, drift, and scattering terms. To compute the drift term, a Wannier-representation finite-difference technique is employed to address issues with Berry connection and basis-function smoothness. The linearized equation is expressed with matrices for velocity, coherent evolution, and scattering, and the drift term is computed via finite differences of the Wigner function in the Wannier representation.

This protocol describes the creation of the Canadian Social Determinants Urban Laboratory (CSDUL), a multilevel, longitudinal virtual environment integrating over 15 surveys and administrative databases within Statistics Canada’s Research Data Centres. Guided by the WHO Social Determinants of Health framework, CSDUL initially covers 2011–2015 and will expand. It uses a hub-and-node model: a central hub at the University of Saskatchewan coordinates five nodes—Political and Economic Context, Environmental Context, Socioeconomic Context, Material Circumstances, and Health Systems. Each node develops and validates area-based indicators at macro, meso, and micro levels, merged with individual-level data from the Canadian Population Health Survey (CPHS), which links the Canadian Community Health Survey, hospital discharge, vital statistics, cancer registry, and tax records.

The primary outcome is self-reported health, dichotomized as better than “fair.” Predictor variables span demographics, health behaviours, comorbidities, health system access, and area-level measures including political/economic indicators, environmental factors (e.g., walkability, air pollution), social capital typologies, after-tax income, and health system performance. The project will replicate WHO/Europe’s decomposition analysis of income-related health inequalities using a twofold Oaxaca-Blinder method to estimate the proportional contribution of social determinant groups to differences in self-reported health between the lowest and highest income quintiles. Interaction effects by gender and ethnicity will be explored.

CSDUL aims to bridge WHO conceptual and action frameworks, identify the relative impacts of social determinants on health inequities in urban Canada, and provide a reusable data infrastructure to reduce costs for future population health research.

The lecture reviews Markov processes, defining them via an embedded Markov chain and exponential holding times with rates ν_i. Steady-state probabilities for the process are proportional to π_j/ν_j, normalized. If the sum of π_k/ν_k diverges, the transition rate goes to zero and no meaningful steady state exists; otherwise, the steady state satisfies rate-in equals rate-out equations. For birth–death processes, the up and down transition rates balance. An example of a “hyperactive” birth–death chain shows that when transition rates increase with the state, the sum diverges, the embedded chain probabilities become zero, and the steady state is meaningless; truncation analysis reveals probability concentrates in higher states as the truncation point increases.

Reversibility for Markov processes is introduced: backward transition rates are defined, and a process is reversible if backward rates equal forward rates. Under positive recurrence and finite Σ π_i/ν_i, the process is reversible if and only if the embedded chain is. A “guessing theorem” states that if one finds probabilities p_i satisfying detailed-balance equations and the sum condition, then those are the steady-state fractions, the process is reversible, and the embedded chain is positive recurrent.

Burke’s theorem for M/M/1 queues is stated: the departure process is Poisson with rate λ; the state is independent of past departures; for FCFS, a customer’s arrival time given its departure time is independent of departures before that time. For tandem M/M/1 queues, the second queue’s arrivals are Poisson (rate λ) and independent of its service times, making it M/M/1; the states of the two queues are independent.

The lecture then turns to random walks, defined as sums of i.i.d. random variables. Threshold-crossing problems are discussed: probability of ever crossing a threshold, which threshold is crossed first, and overshoot. A simple random walk (binary ±1) has crossing probability to level k equal to (p/(1−p))^k. Integer random walks, where increments are integer-valued, can be modeled as Markov chains. Renewal processes are a special case with nonnegative increments; their sample-path axes are typically reversed relative to random-walk plots.

For a G/G/1 queue, the waiting time w_n satisfies w_n = max(w_{n−1} + y_{n−1} − x_n, 0), where y_{n−1} is the previous service time and x_n the interarrival time. Defining u_n = y_{n−1} − x_n gives an i.i.d. sequence, making w_n behave like a random walk reflected at zero, with renewals each time the waiting time hits zero.

Finally, binary hypothesis testing is introduced: a hypothesis H ∈ {0,1}, observations Y_i i.i.d. conditional on H. Bayes’ law gives the posterior probability ratio as the prior odds times the likelihood ratio. The lecture notes historical controversy over Bayesian inference and sets up the connection to random walks for the next session.

They trade on ICE Futures Europe (symbol UHO, cash-settled) and CME Globex (symbol HO, physically deliverable). Contract size on both exchanges is 42,000 gallons (1,000 barrels). Minimum price fluctuation is $0.0001 per gallon ($4.20 per contract). On ICE, trading hours are 1:00 AM–11:00 PM London Time Sunday–Friday, with a pre-open at 12:45 AM. On CME, trading is Sunday–Friday 5:00 p.m.–4:00 p.m. CT with a 60-minute break at 4:00 p.m. CT. Settlement on CME is by physical delivery; on ICE it is cash settlement. Final settlement on ICE is cash, while CME supervises physical delivery. Last trading day is the last business day of the month prior to the contract month. Monthly contracts are listed for the current year plus next three calendar years and one additional month; on ICE up to 50 consecutive months.

The all-time high for HO is $5.2215 per gallon (April 2022); the all-time low is $0.2920 (February 1999). Heating oil exhibits seasonality: historically, a strategy buying January 11 and selling August 30 yielded a total return of 361.83% over 1999–2009, with better performance between February and August as people buy ahead of winter. Factors moving prices include weather, crude oil prices, refinery capacity, and alternative heating fuel costs. Biggest risk is adverse price movement amplified by leverage (e.g., 20x leverage means a 5% adverse move wipes out the account). A backtested strategy on TradeStation showed 168 trades with an average $370 profit per trade, profit factor 2.02, and 59% win rate. An ETF tracking the market is the WisdomTree HEAT ETF, based on the Bloomberg Heating Oil Subindex Total Return – USD. The block minimum is 25 contracts. Heating oil futures differ from CFDs: futures trade on regulated exchanges with expiry and possible delivery, while CFDs are broker-issued contracts without delivery concerns. To trade, one can use a futures broker (e.g., TradeStation) or a CFD broker (e.g., IG) for speculation. A heating oil futures strategy involves technical and fundamental analysis and risk management.
