The UHS-II supported host provides RCLK and STB.L to the D0 lane and waits for the D1 lane to change from EIDL to STB.L. If STB.L is detected within a host-determined timeout (based on a 200µs per-card value), UHS-II initialization starts; otherwise the card is initialized in SD Bus I/F mode. UHS-II initialization proceeds through PHY initialization (PLL activation, SD Bus I/F disabled), Device Initialization, Enumeration (assigning a unique Device ID), Configuration (setting UHS-II registers), and SD-TRAN Initialization (emulating SD commands in UHS-II packets). CMD0 restarts from SD-TRAN initialization. For SD Bus I/F initialization of a UHS-II card, the UHS-II interface is disabled before ACMD41 completes, and VDD2 must continue to be provided if supplied.

Bus speed modes for UHS-II cards are defined, with UHS-III (FD624) introduced. Application Performance Class specifies minimum random and sequential performance. Cache, Self Maintenance, and Command Queue features are described. Low Voltage Interface enables 1.8V IO initialization.

All communication is host-controlled using broadcast and addressed commands. Two operation modes exist: card identification mode and data transfer mode. After power-on or CMD0, cards enter Idle State with default RCA=0x0000 and 400KHz clock. CMD8 is mandatory before ACMD41 to initialize SDHC/SDXC cards, verifying voltage and interface condition. ACMD41 with HCS bit starts initialization; the busy bit indicates completion within 1 second. CMD2 and CMD3 assign CID and RCA, moving cards to Stand-by State. In data transfer mode, CMD7 selects a card for Transfer State. Data read/write commands, block operations, stop command (CMD12), and busy indication on DAT0 are described. Erase, Discard, and Full User Area Logical Erase (FULE) operations use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 with specific arguments and timeouts.

Write protection includes mechanical switch, internal card protection, and password-based lock/unlock. The password is stored in PWD and PWD_LEN registers. Locked cards accept only basic commands. Force Erase (CMD42 with ERASE bit) erases all data and PWD. Card Ownership Protection (COP) adds FEP and FEP_LEN registers. When FEP is set, Force Erase is disabled, and COP Unlock (CMD42[1Fh]) is required after power-on to access CMD42 functions. COP functions include setting/resetting FEP, FEP Force Erase, and inhibiting PWD reset while FEP is set. Detailed command sequences and state tables define behavior for Non-COP and COP cards.

Application-specific commands are invoked by CMD55 (APP_CMD). The switch function command (CMD6) operates in Mode 0 (check) and Mode 1 (set) to change functions in groups: Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit. Power Limit defaults to 0.72W; host sets it according to supply capability. In UHS-II mode, Function Groups 1 and 3 are not used, and Group 4 is mandatory. CMD6 returns a 512-bit status block with supported functions and maximum current/power consumption.

The author expresses confusion over accusations that the government doctored an electoral reform bill. A bill is a draft law, typically drawn up by a government department under a minister and approved by Cabinet. The Law Commission makes recommendations, but these pass through the Executive, where Cabinet mixes them with policies to frame the bill. The author argues the accusation only makes sense if the bill came from the Law Commission as an untouchable package, and concludes the accusations stem from misinformation.

The passage presents a theoretical framework explaining why spatial averaging can cause macroscopic dynamics of large-scale nonlinear systems to become linear. It notes that while individual subsystems (e.g., neurons) are nonlinear, linear models often effectively capture population-level behavior. The authors aim to provide rigorous mathematical proofs for this emergent linearity, extending prior work that assumed independent subsystems to heterogeneous and spatially correlated ones. They review literature supporting linear models in brain dynamics and artificial neural networks. The paper's contributions include extending central limit theorems for ρ-mixing sequences to multivariate processes, defining residual factors, and proving asymptotic linearity of averaged state dynamics under spatial averaging, yielding linear time-varying (and under stationarity, linear time-invariant) limit dynamics. They also analyze convergence rates. Notation and preliminaries on ρ-mixing sequences are provided. The problem is formulated as a population of nonlinear discrete-time subsystems with local interactions, and the goal is to show the average state dynamics become linear as the number of subsystems grows. The section then extends mixing sequence theory to vector-valued processes, defines residual factor to characterize variance growth, and proves its existence. Examples illustrate how correlation decay rates determine the residual factor.

Several Texas public universities instructed faculty to review syllabi and remove content not complying with federal and state laws and executive orders. San Jacinto College asked faculty to align with state manuals; a spokesperson denied a formal ban on teaching transgender identity, but a faculty member confirmed verbal instructions to teach only the male-female binary. In the Texas Tech system, verbal-only directives at Angelo State caused confusion, with some told pride flags and preferred pronouns were banned. By Friday, a directive prohibited employees from teaching, discussing, or acknowledging transgender identity, citing laws recognizing only two sexes. Angelo State’s president said no standalone policy exists, and the provost instructed removal of “outdated or noncompliant language” without specifying gender identity. Texas A&M also ordered compliance after firing a professor over a gender identity lecture. No federal or state laws prohibit teaching about transgender identity. A FIRE attorney called the directives a voluntary censorship effort, unsupported by executive orders and contrary to the First Amendment. The Texas AAUP urged faculty to report censorship to FIRE.

The passage argues that the brain should be treated like a muscle requiring regular training. Jamie states that managing one's mind is a skill, and happiness is a transient emotion; there are no bad emotions, only temporary ones. Accepting feelings reduces emotional impact. A seven-step daily process is presented to train the mind: 1) Internal check-in to label the emotion, which research shows initiates emotional processing. 2) Slow belly breathing for at least 30 seconds to activate the rest system. 3) Write down feelings and then rip up the paper to release them, as journaling calms the emotional center. 4) Reframe by writing a gratitude list to focus on the positive. 5) Play a mindful mini game like drawing or a puzzle to disrupt thinking. 6) Complete a compassion challenge, such as forgiving or complimenting, to trigger dopamine. 7) Send a positive note to someone else, as studies link thinking of others to greater happiness. The routine aims to release worries and provide a different metric for success.

The path integral master formula expresses any time-ordered product of operators as a ratio of path integrals. For an interacting theory with action S = S₀ + S_I, where S_I is small and contains no time derivatives, the correlation function can be written exactly as ⟨T x e^{i S_I}⟩₀ / ⟨T e^{i S_I}⟩₀, where ⟨·⟩₀ denotes free-theory expectation values. This is expanded perturbatively in powers of S_I. The free-theory correlation functions are evaluated using Wick’s theorem, reducing to products of free Feynman propagators.

To simplify, Feynman diagrams are introduced. For a λφ⁴ interaction with L_I = -λ/4! φ⁴, the two-point function is expanded. Disconnected vacuum diagrams cancel between numerator and denominator. Diagrams are drawn with lines representing free propagators G_F₀(x−y) and vertices representing the interaction. Combinatorial factors from the exponential and vertex factorials cancel modulo symmetries, leading to coordinate-space Feynman rules: each external point gets a line (factor 1), each propagator is G_F₀(x−y), each vertex is -iλ ∫ d⁴x, and one divides by the diagram’s symmetry factor.

In momentum space, the n-point function’s Fourier transform contains an overall momentum-conserving delta function. The free propagator is -i/(k²+m²−iε). Momentum-space rules: external lines carry momentum (factor 1), each propagator is -i/(p²+m²−iε), each vertex contributes iλ and enforces momentum conservation, undetermined loop momenta are integrated over with d⁴k/(2π)⁴, and the symmetry factor is applied. An example diagram with two vertices is evaluated in momentum space to illustrate the procedure.

On July 30, 2020, Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting its second quarter 2020 financial results. The press release is included as Exhibit 99.1, and information on non-GAAP financial measures is Exhibit 99.2. The report was signed by Senior Vice President and CFO Brian T. Olsavsky. The company's common stock (par value $0.01) trades on Nasdaq under AMZN. Its principal executive offices are at 410 Terry Avenue North, Seattle, Washington. The registrant is not an emerging growth company.

The author describes a friend's distress over a child's cellphone-related school trouble, then reviews the Netflix documentary “Unknown Number: The High School Catfish.” The film follows junior high student Lauryn Licari in Beal City, Michigan, who receives escalating vulgar, graphic, and threatening text messages from an unknown number. The sender appears to have intimate knowledge of her life. Local investigations stall, and the FBI gets involved, requesting a forensic dump of boyfriend Owen McKenny’s phone. The author criticizes the documentary’s brief treatment of cellphone forensics, noting that phones and provider data can reveal extensive personal information. The perpetrator is unexpected. The author, a parent and criminal defense attorney, expresses concern about kids and cellphones, and supports Oklahoma’s “bell to bell” no-cellphone policy for the 2025-2026 school year, citing cybercrime and felony cases originating from cellphone use.

This paper investigates ensuring 100% valid molecule generation from large language models (LLMs). It finds that while SELFIES guarantees validity, LLMs perform worse with it than with SMILES. Using LLMs as post-hoc correctors for invalid SMILES improves validity but degrades other metrics, with correction rates varying by model and error type. The proposed SmiSelf framework converts invalid SMILES into SELFIES via molecular graphs and back into SMILES, leveraging SELFIES’ robustness to correct errors. Experiments show SmiSelf achieves 100% validity, preserves molecular characteristics, and maintains or improves other metrics in text-based and class-specific molecule generation tasks.

On June 22, 2016, Apple Inc. consummated the issuance and sale of $1,377,000,000 aggregate principal amount of its 4.15% Notes due 2046. The notes were issued pursuant to a subscription agreement dated June 7, 2016 with Deutsche Bank AG, Taipei Branch and KGI Securities Co. Ltd. as managers, under an indenture dated April 29, 2013 with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. as trustee, and a registration statement filed April 28, 2016. Interest is payable semi-annually on June 22 and December 22, beginning December 22, 2016. The notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The report attaches the subscription agreement, officer’s certificate, form of global note, and legal opinion as exhibits.

A Business Insider virtual event sponsored by Fidelity Investments on September 30 featured experts discussing IPO strategies. Challenges include shifting investor expectations, new regulations, and maintaining culture. Staying private longer allows better preparation. Advice: don't underestimate focus; Hinge Health used dedicated experts, quarterly reviews, multi-year timeframes, and proactive investor meetings. New public companies face regulatory reporting, shareholder requirements, and compensation strategies. Becoming public takes 18–24 months, requiring right people, tools, and compensation for talent retention. CEOs should surround themselves with right investors. Post-IPO, companies must deliver quarterly results while rewarding employees. Capitalization tables and equity plans evolve. A broker is needed to unlock liquidity. Villar's Paycor ensured employees benefited, explaining quarterly results and linking daily jobs to success. IPOs are wealth creation opportunities; employees need financial/tax planning help, and right partners deliver excellent service.

The speaker acknowledges Mike Peca's Selke Trophy consistency, then discusses his own nine years with the North Stars/Dallas Stars organization, their goal of winning the Stanley Cup, and reaching the finals. He also describes unrestricted free agency as a team-building tool, noting early unsuccessful attempts but overall positive contributions from acquired players.

Fitch Ratings affirmed Marsh & McLennan Companies, Inc.'s (MMC) Long-Term Issuer Default Rating at 'A-', short-term ratings at 'F2', and revised the Rating Outlook to Positive from Stable. The actions reflect MMC's sustained trend of improved operating performance and stronger credit metrics, a strong balance sheet, financial flexibility, and excellent cash flow generation. MMC holds a top-tier competitive position as a diversified services firm in insurance brokerage and consulting. Contingent risks such as reputation, litigation, and regulatory actions are considered manageable. Liquidity remains strong with $1 billion in cash and equivalents at Dec. 31, 2016 and a $1.5 billion revolving credit facility expiring November 2020. Free cash flow is expected to grow, aided by expense reductions and earnings growth; restructuring expenses have been immaterial, and share repurchases are discretionary ($800 million in 2016). MMC's consolidated EBIT operating margin improved to 20% in 2016 from 19% in 2015. Debt-to-EBITDA was 1.5x (pro forma 1.8x after January 2017 debt issuance), and EBITDA-to-interest coverage exceeded 16x. Both Risk & Insurance Services and Consulting segments reported organic revenue growth and margin expansion. Rating sensitivities for an upgrade include sustained EBIT margins of 18% or better, debt-to-EBITDA near 1.5x, and EBITDA-to-interest above 14x. A return to Stable Outlook could result from failure to reduce debt-to-EBITDA to near 1.5x, EBITDA-to-interest coverage below 10x, material litigation or regulatory charges, or a material goodwill impairment. Fitch affirmed the 'A-' rating on all listed senior unsecured debt instruments.

OpenAI and Stripe introduced an Instant Checkout feature in ChatGPT, powered by a new open-source Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) they co-developed. ACP builds on Anthropic’s MCP standard, focusing on commerce and payments, with Stripe providing fraud prevention, global payment rails, and a vast merchant network. The feature launches with U.S. sellers and will expand to over a million merchants, including Glossier, Skims, Spanx, and Vuori. Because ACP is open source, any AI assistant could enable in-chat shopping, potentially shifting online shopping away from Google and Amazon. ChatGPT product lead Michelle Fradin said the protocol was designed for easy adoption by the entire ecosystem, including competitors, as a merchant-friendly approach. Adoption means merchants cede some customer relationship control and pay Stripe transaction fees. To be surfaced in ChatGPT’s recommendations, merchants must provide detailed, structured product feeds, giving rise to a new discipline called AIO. The article raises questions about how ChatGPT will determine recommendations and whether it could become pay-to-play.

The Beerepoot family's Melita Honey Farm home in Tasmania will be auctioned in three weeks due to unpaid council rates since 2010. They believe the land belongs to God and paying rates would be worshipping a false god. The Meander Valley Council set the auction for September 1 at 11am. Two other properties had rates paid in June, but not the Mole Creek home. $9332 was outstanding in March. The family reaffirmed their belief. Previous legal action resulted in seizure of an old vehicle. Sale proceeds minus rates go to the family. The mayor said the decision was difficult and the family could still pay.

SOS defense pressures ball to sideline, corner, or baseline checkpoints using SET, ON, SMOTHER. One pass away: contact SNUGGLE denial. Deep post: contact FRONTS with Slip Front, Helpside I in vision/point stances. Use Go Base post traps away from low block, Box Pressure on wing. Direct ball to corner/baseline, deny middle drives. Weakside defenders form Helpside I (double/triple) alignments; on traps, Triangle I. On pass out of trap, rotate as ball leaves hands: High Helpside I closes out to receiver, others to nearest opponent. Switch with contact on off-ball screens (Screen/Over/Switch). Contact traps: side screen/roll before screen, mid screens, dribble penetrations inside baseline checkpoint, mismatches, corner. Unstructured scenarios: Near Player rotations without hesitation. Shot attempts: box out, flood boards with five; rebounding stressed. Checkpoints: corners, free throw line extended, baseline, half court; keep ball from middle Red Zone into trap zones. Wing: push to corner/baseline; if middle drive, cut off and force to sideline (Wing Turn) into Smother. If penetration to free throw line, high I Cross Switch with on-ball defender. Helpside I provides backside help, ready to trap/rotate, deny weakside paint cuts. Three offensive players ballside: Double I (Low/High). Two: Triple I (Low/Mid/Top). Invert big/small in Helpside I when possible. On traps, three non-trappers form Triangle I (sideline/baseline) with specific positions and Near Player rotations.

Rock engravings at three Nefud Desert outcrops date to 12,800–11,400 years ago, featuring life-size camels and 150 petroglyphs. They were created in four phases: small stylized women, larger human figures, naturalistic animals up to 3 meters, and cartoonish animals. Made by early nomads when the region was wetter, the art likely marked territory or water. Stone tools link the artists to the Eastern Mediterranean, but the monumental style is unprecedented. The area became arid again 6,000 years ago.

Scientists observed brown recluse spiders using a sewing-like motion with their spinnerets to produce silk. Large spinnerets form a loop, then smaller ones clamp and release to close it, creating multiple micro-loops that enhance strength and toughness. The silk is uniquely thin and flat, like Scotch tape but 2000 times thinner, making it sticky and enabling self-adhesive loops. This web structure, evolved for catching prey on the ground, prevents the sticky silk from collapsing. Previous attempts to add loops to synthetic fibers failed due to breakage, but the spider's use of thin, flat nano-scale ribbon-shaped fibers offers a solution. Researchers have developed mathematical models and filed a patent, though no synthetic version exists yet. Potential applications include protective space webs against debris, lightweight bungee cords, improved parachute cords, and other materials requiring strength, lightness, and flexibility. The spider produces this silk sustainably, requiring only food and no toxic inputs.

The third Hero ISL 2016 finale drew 54,000 stadium attendees and 41 million TV viewers. Total viewership reached 216 million, a 41% increase over 2015. Rural viewership hit 101 million. Mumbai and Chennai saw over 50% growth, Tamil Nadu 20%. Overall viewer engagement rose over 25%, watchtime doubled, and average stadium occupancy exceeded 84%. The league expanded beyond traditional football regions, with strong digital growth.

The study reports the observation of a field-free superconducting diode effect (SDE) in NbSe2 induced by strain. NbSe2 is a centrosymmetric superconductor, but few odd-layered flakes are non-centrosymmetric. Local uniaxial stress was applied by bending NbSe2 over a curved aluminum nanoridge. Electrical transport measurements show significant SDE in stressed regions, with forward and reverse critical currents differing, while no SDE appears in non-stressed regions. In different devices, the SDE exhibits two distinct magnetic-field symmetries: B-even (ΔIc symmetric with respect to magnetic field) and B-odd (ΔIc antisymmetric), as well as a mixed case. The maximum ΔIc reaches 286 μA and the diode efficiency η reaches 6.76% at zero magnetic field, values that are high for traditional superconductors without junctions. The SDE decreases with increasing magnetic field and temperature, vanishing above 1000 Oe or near Tc (5.8 K). To explain these results, the authors propose two independent and spatially orthogonal non-reciprocal mechanisms. A stress-induced real-space polarization mechanism, activated solely by uniaxial stress, produces the B-even SDE when current flows along the armchair direction. A valley-polarization mechanism, requiring an external magnetic field to break time-reversal symmetry, produces the B-odd SDE when current flows along the zigzag direction. The study demonstrates an effective method to generate field-free SDE and provides a platform for investigating stress effects on superconductors and developing superconducting quantum devices.

Manufacturing enterprises use simulation, modeling, and data analytics to increase innovation, speed product development, reduce costs, and improve decision-making. Three-quarters of respondents view innovation as the most important business objective, while 57% see these tools as important for improving quality and avoiding defects. Deployment is currently around half of enterprises in product development and production planning, expected to rise to 90% within two years. Data silos from a lack of a holistic data strategy hinder optimal digital support; integrating data into a single source of truth is necessary.

High-performance computing (HPC) is considered a game changer for product and process innovation by 81% of decision makers. HPC enables complex calculations, increases quality and usage intensity, unlocks new scenarios, and boosts innovation and agility. Currently, 42% of respondents say their simulations are outdated or inaccurate, and half report iterations take too long due to limited computing capacity. Demand for high-performance calculations is projected to grow significantly.

Challenges in HPC usage include security concerns (72%), high energy consumption and sustainability issues (58%), inadequate computing power, and lack of internal expertise (42%). Most enterprises prefer external HPC infrastructures: 87% use or plan cloud providers, 74% use or plan colocation. Only 6% currently have on-premises HPC. Cloud-based HPC as a Service (HPCaaS) offers cost optimization, flexible performance, access to cutting-edge methods, and improved collaboration. 81% of HPC users intend to implement HPC-based business models.

The study, based on a survey of 200 enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, recommends virtual product development, a holistic data strategy, evaluating HPC operating models, considering scalability and security, and leveraging external expertise.

New research by astronomer Rory Barnes suggests many exoplanets to be discovered by future telescopes will likely be tidally locked, with one side permanently facing their star. Barnes challenged the assumption that only planets around smaller, dimmer stars could be tidally locked. Tidal locking occurs when a body's rotation period matches its orbital period, as with the Moon and Earth. By exploring a wider range of initial rotation periods, planet sizes, and eccentric orbits, Barnes found that tidal locking may be more common than previously thought. Planetary formation models indicate initial rotation could be weeks long, increasing the likelihood. He concluded tidal locking is a major factor in the evolution of most potentially habitable exoplanets. While once considered a barrier to life, an atmosphere with winds could moderate climate. Barnes also found that every potentially habitable planet NASA's TESS mission will detect will likely be tidally locked, including any Earth twin. He emphasized the need to determine tidal locking when searching for life.

Japanese Finance Minister Taro Aso warned the yen is vulnerable to North Korea tensions, calling it extremely unstable despite its safe-haven status. He noted high tensions over a possible nuclear test. Aso declined to comment on exchange rates. On trade, he said the 11 remaining TPP nations should proceed without the U.S., and that Washington will eventually rejoin, gaining no more from bilateral deals.

Oil prices rose about 1.5% after OPEC+ announced a smaller-than-expected production increase of 137,000 barrels per day starting in November, repeating October’s modest hike. Brent crude reached around $65.44 per barrel and WTI near $61.77. The decision, aimed at stabilizing prices after weeks of volatility, followed internal debate between members wanting larger hikes for market share and those favoring restraint due to subdued demand and rising inventories. Analysts warned gains may be short-lived given uneven demand, seasonal refinery maintenance, and slower consumption. OPEC+ signaled a readiness to defend prices and avoid a supply surge, with traders awaiting the next meeting for 2026 policy clues. The market remains balanced between cautious optimism and oversupply risk.

The lecture discusses the physical interpretation of temperature in black hole and Rindler spacetimes. In the previous lecture, extending the black hole metric and going to Euclidean signature showed that regularity at the horizon requires periodic identification of Euclidean time, giving a finite temperature. A similar procedure applies to Rindler space. Today’s focus is the meaning of this temperature: it is observer-dependent, tied to a specific choice of time. For a black hole, the vacuum obtained by this Euclidean continuation (Hartle-Hawking vacuum) is regular at the horizon, while the vacuum from straightforward canonical quantization without compactifying Euclidean time (Schwarzschild vacuum) leads to singular observables at the horizon. Thus the Hartle-Hawking vacuum is considered more physical.

The physical origin of the temperature is explained using the Rindler example. First, it is shown that the choice of periodic identification in Rindler space corresponds to selecting the standard Minkowski vacuum. Then, a derivation demonstrates that the Minkowski vacuum appears as a thermal state to a Rindler observer. Preparatory material reviews how a thermal state can be represented as an entangled pure state of a doubled system: tracing out one copy yields a thermal density matrix. For a harmonic oscillator, this entangled state is a squeezed state related to the vacuum by a Bogoliubov transformation.

The path integral representation of the vacuum wave functional is recalled: the Minkowski vacuum wave functional is given by a Euclidean path integral over the lower half-plane. In Euclidean signature, both Minkowski and Rindler spaces become the same two-dimensional Euclidean plane, just with different foliations. Consequently, Euclidean correlation functions are identical, and upon continuation back to Lorentzian signature, Rindler correlation functions are simply the Minkowski vacuum correlations restricted to the Rindler patch.

The Hilbert space structure is then examined. The Minkowski Hilbert space is the tensor product of left and right Rindler Hilbert spaces. The Minkowski vacuum wave functional, expressed via the Euclidean path integral using Rindler foliation, takes the form of a sum over Rindler energy eigenstates with weight e^{-π E_n}, entangling the left and right patches. Tracing out the left Rindler yields a thermal density matrix for the right Rindler with inverse temperature β=2π (in terms of the Rindler time η). Thus, the temperature arises because a Rindler observer cannot access the left patch; the Minkowski vacuum is an entangled state, and ignorance of the left part produces a thermal state on the right. The same reasoning applies to black holes.

The study analyzed how Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine affected foreign co-funding, authorship patterns, and citation impact of articles funded by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MESU), the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine (NASU), and the National Research Foundation of Ukraine (NRFU), using Scopus-indexed articles from 2020–2023.

The proportion of Ukrainian articles acknowledging funding increased, with MESU, NASU, and NRFU all seeing rises. Foreign co-funding was common, especially for NASU due to physics. Top co-funders included the EU, USA, Germany, China, and Poland; Russia disappeared from top lists in 2022–2023. New regional funders like Slovakia, Lithuania, and Kazakhstan emerged. About half of the articles involved foreign co-authorship or foreign co-affiliations. The share of authors with foreign co-affiliations grew in 2022–2023, while international co-authorship slightly declined. Poland, Germany, and the USA remained central collaborators.

Funded articles had higher citation impact than unfunded ones. Foreign co-funding was positively associated with higher impact, particularly for NASU. MESU-funded articles’ impact increased in 2022–2023, driven by highly cited outliers among authors with foreign co-affiliations. NASU-funded articles without foreign co-funding had citation impacts statistically indistinguishable from unfunded articles. Across all groups, international collaboration consistently enhanced impact. The findings underscore the need for reform in Ukraine’s research funding allocation and a centralized national funding database to improve tracking and evaluation.

British laboratory tests on building material fire safety are inadequate, according to insurance industry research following the Grenfell Tower fire that killed 71 people. Test fires use only wood, but actual fires contain 20% plastic; a test with 20% plastic was 100°C hotter. Cladding materials are tested as sealed units but installed with gaps, and tested in manufacturers’ conditions but pierced by vents. The Fire Protection Association urged urgent review of cladding test standards. The Association of British Insurers called for only non-combustible materials, reformed testing, and mandatory sprinklers in new schools, care homes, and warehouses over 2,000 square meters, noting sprinklers can cut premiums up to 50%. A government-commissioned review’s final report is expected soon.

A phase III, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial assessed a single heterologous booster dose of CORBEVAX™ (a protein subunit vaccine) in 416 adults aged 18–80 in India who had completed primary vaccination with two doses of COVISHIELD™ or COVAXIN at least six months prior. Participants were randomized 3:1 to receive CORBEVAX™ (n=156 per group) or placebo (n=52 per group). The primary endpoint was virus neutralizing antibody (VNA) titers at day 28. Adverse events were mild to moderate, with no serious adverse events, deaths, or discontinuations. In COVAXIN-primed subjects, 20.5% (vaccine) vs 13.5% (placebo) reported adverse events; in COVISHIELD™-primed, 17.9% vs 15.4%. Immunogenicity results showed superior responses with CORBEVAX™: the lower bound of the 95% CI for the ratio of GMTs of nAb and anti-RBD IgG was >1.0 versus placebo. The proportion with ≥2-fold rise in nAb titers was 71% (COVISHIELD™) and 68% (COVAXIN) in vaccine recipients. Against the Omicron variant, responder percentages increased from 43% to 91% (COVISHIELD™) and 33% to 75% (COVAXIN). Cellular immune responses (IFN-gamma) were enhanced. The study reports only day 28 data; long-term follow-up is ongoing.

A proximity sensor module is disclosed that uses a light sensor chip with a light source, such as a laser diode, mounted directly on top of the chip. Drops of optical resin are dispensed over the light source and the light sensor to form lenses. The assembly is then fully encapsulated in an opaque molding compound, which blocks all internal light cross-talk, eliminating the need for a plastic cap, central barrier, and associated glue. After encapsulation, the top surface is polished to expose the optical resin lenses, providing a flush optical surface. A baffle or metal cap may be added for protection and electrical isolation.

Alternative embodiments include placing glass lenses over the optical resin with an air gap, allowing independent lens shaping and filtering. A central glue stopper may be added to prevent mold contact with the die. Another embodiment mounts the light emitter on a separate conductive lead, with a reference light sensor on the same integrated circuit die as the data light sensor. The reference sensor receives light directly from the emitter each time it illuminates, providing a calibration signal to distinguish reflected light from ambient light.

A sensor stick is also described, comprising a printed circuit board substrate with contact pads at one end for insertion into a computing device. The stick carries multiple sensors, including environmental sensors (e.g., gas, UV, humidity, temperature, pressure), a light emitter or projector, proximity and ambient light sensors, motion sensors (magnetometer, gyroscope, accelerometer), and wireless connectivity circuits (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi). The sensors are encapsulated, with environmental sensors exposed to ambient air. The stick can be powered via the wired connection and transmit data wirelessly to the same or other devices. Manufacturing involves assembling an array of modules on a large substrate, applying optical resin, encapsulating, polishing, adding covers, and singulating.

Filing taxes late can result in IRS fees, and not filing at all may lead to forfeited refunds or jail. The tax deadline is April 17, with extensions available. Taxpayers owed a refund have three years to claim it; unclaimed money becomes U.S. Treasury property. The IRS reported $1.1 billion in unclaimed 2014 refunds for 1 million non-filers. Those with withheld taxes or eligible for credits like EITC may still get refunds even if not required to file. The IRS may file substitute returns but without considering deductions, causing overpayment. Owing taxes triggers collection: a letter demanding payment with penalties and interest, then possible installment agreements. After multiple notices, a representative may visit if debt exceeds $25,000, and the IRS can levy assets and seize property. Communicating with the IRS can help avoid serious trouble.

Automation Anywhere's Bot Store, an online marketplace for plug-n-play bots, saw 100% growth in bot numbers within two months of launch. The most popular category is artificial intelligence (24 bots), with speech-to-text leading downloads. The most common business process is finance and accounting, with "allocate payments against outstanding invoices" the most visited bot, and SAP is the most prevalent application (31 bots). IQ Bot adds computer vision, NLP, and machine learning capabilities. Pre-trained cognitive bots automate document processes like utility bills, bank statements, and tax forms. Bots run on the Enterprise platform and combine to automate complex processes.

UK median disposable household income was £27,300 in the financial year ending 2017, up 2.3% in real terms from the previous year and £1,600 above pre-downturn levels, per the Office for National Statistics. This follows the 2008 Northern Rock collapse and crisis that depressed wages and living standards. The poorest fifth of households saw the largest gains, with incomes £1,800 higher, while the richest fifth only just returned to pre-crisis levels. Income inequality has fallen slightly over the past decade. The improvement is driven by increased employment and wages. Despite this, a large gap persists: average disposable income for the richest fifth is £65,542 versus £12,748 for the poorest. Direct taxes reduce inequality, with the richest paying 23.2% of gross income in taxes and the poorest 12.7%. Retired households' median disposable income is £22,300 versus £29,900 for non-retired; the gap is widening as non-retired incomes grew 3.5% and retired 1.2%.

Colorado Governor John Hickenlooper will testify on February 14 before California's State Governance and Finance Committee about Colorado's experience with recreational cannabis implementation. California legalized recreational use last November and must establish regulations by January 1, 2018 under Proposition 64. Senator Mike McGuire, chairing the hearing 'California Cannabis in a Turbulent Time,' says the timeline is unrealistic, with the Track and Trace program not ready and tax collection issues unresolved. The hearing aims to set an implementation timeline and learn from Colorado's seed-to-sale program. It will be live-streamed at senate.ca.gov.

The passage reports the launch of a new life sciences investment firm backed by private equity billionaire Tony James, led by a former Flagship associate. It also lists other biotech news headlines, including pharma companies making deals with Trump, Sarepta's Medicaid coverage setback, a Supreme Court conversion therapy case, digital health M&A, Amgen's cholesterol shot results, tariff policy changes, and additional updates.

Arsenal visit Tottenham on Sunday for the 50th North London derby under Wenger, aiming to dent Spurs' title hopes. Arsenal's record in previous 49: 18 wins, 21 draws, 10 losses. Tottenham fan Mike Leigh predicts a tight 2-1 Spurs win, calling it the biggest British derby after the Auld Firm with a poisonous atmosphere. Arsenal fan Akhil Vyas says recent wins boosted confidence, predicts 1-1 or 2-1 Arsenal win, notes Spurs will finish above Arsenal for the first time in over 20 years, and says most fans want Wenger to leave, with a cup final win a possible perfect exit.

This document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP encrypted virtualization guests. It defines the GHCB as a 4KB decrypted page used to selectively share guest register state with the hypervisor during Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events. The GHCB format mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save state area, and a GHCB MSR protocol uses the lower 12 bits of MSR 0xc001_0130 to request actions before the GHCB page is established.

Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement via a FEATURES bitmap, support for SEV-SNP, XSS MSR value, restricted APIC emulation (IPI and timer), and a shared buffer area. Revisions add support for 64-bit guest request message sequence numbers, VLEK certificate GUID, multiple VMPL levels, APIC ID list retrieval, page state change for SEV-ES guests, SEV-TIO trusted IO, Secure AVIC, and termination requests. The hypervisor must supply the SEV page table encryption bit number and protocol version range via the GHCB MSR before the GHCB is established.

The GHCB MSR protocol defines request/response pairs for SEV information, CPUID register values, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration/unregistration, page state change, run VMPL, and feature support. For SEV-SNP, GHCB GPA registration is mandatory before first use; the guest may request a preferred GPA or register its own. The GHCB negotiation example shows how the hypervisor sets initial MSR values and the guest uses #VC exceptions or MSR protocol to obtain encryption bit position and negotiate protocol version.

The document lists supported NAE events with required guest state to expose in the GHCB. Standard VMGEXIT processing involves setting SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, SW_EXITINFO2, and valid bitmap bits. The hypervisor may return error codes in SW_EXITINFO1 to request exception injection or indicate malformed input. Specific NAE events include IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access (using reserved bits to trigger #VC), page state change (using a structure in the GHCB shared buffer to request private/shared/PSMASH/UNSMASH operations), SNP Guest Request and Extended Guest Request (for firmware requests with certificate data), AP Creation (to create/destroy/update AP VMSA pages), #HV doorbell page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and termination request.

For SMP booting under SEV-ES, the hypervisor cannot modify measured AP register state. The AP must use AP Reset Hold NAE event or MSR protocol to park, and upon SIPI, transition to real mode and execute at the supplied reset vector. An AP jump table is used to communicate the reset vector between UEFI and OS. Under SEV-SNP with AP Creation feature, the guest uses RMPADJUST to mark VMSA pages and creates/updates AP state directly, supporting vCPU hotplug. NMI handling requires the hypervisor to intercept #DB but not IRET; the guest sends an "NMI Complete" message via VMGEXIT when ready. Hardware debug virtualization is supported if enabled in SEV_FEATURES; otherwise, DR7 intercepts are used with a cached value. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The Restricted Injection feature for SEV-SNP uses a doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The host writes interrupt vectors or non-maskable event bits and delivers #HV. The guest acknowledges by clearing the vector, and EOI is optimized by atomically clearing NoEoiRequired or via explicit VMGEXIT. HLT with interrupts disabled is used to enter halt state, and the host re-enters the guest if events are pending. Doorbell page configuration is done via #HV Doorbell Page NAE event with GET_PREFERRED, SET, QUERY, and CLEAR actions. The host emulates APIC behavior faithfully, presenting the highest-priority ready interrupt and managing in-service/EOI semantics.

The Stochastic Indicator Strategy is a technical analysis tool that uses the Stochastic Oscillator to identify overbought/oversold conditions and potential trend reversals. It consists of %K (current price position within a range) and %D (a moving average of %K). Overbought conditions are indicated when %K rises above 80, oversold when %K falls below 20. Traders interpret crossovers of %K and %D, as well as divergence between price and the indicator, as signals. Bullish divergence occurs when price makes a lower low but the indicator makes a higher low; bearish divergence when price makes a higher high but the indicator makes a lower high.

A backtest on SPY (S&P 500 ETF) tested two styles: short-term mean reversion (overbought/oversold) and %K/%D crossovers. The short-term lookback period with low threshold worked best. The oversold/overbought strategy yielded 556 trades, average 0.57% per trade, profit factor 2.2, and maximum drawdown 19.8%. Crossover strategies were not as effective.

The strategy can be applied to various markets (stocks, forex, commodities, cryptocurrencies) and timeframes. Adjustable parameters include the lookback period, smoothing period for %D, and overbought/oversold thresholds. Sensitivity can be modified by changing moving average lengths or threshold levels. The strategy may perform better in trending or range-bound markets with regular oscillations, but can produce false signals in low volatility or strong trending conditions. Risk management involves setting stop-loss orders, diversification, and proper position sizing. Common mistakes include relying solely on the indicator without confirmation, using default settings without adjustment, and emotional decision-making.

The article describes an RSI and moving average trading strategy that combines the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and a Simple Moving Average (SMA) to confirm entry points with acceptable risk and reward. The RSI, developed by Welles Wilder, signals overbought conditions when above 70 and oversold conditions when below 30. The SMA is calculated as the average of the last n-days and is used to identify trends; when price is above the SMA, an upward trend is assumed, and when below, a downward trend. The strategy logic waits for the security to be oversold or overbought while the closing price is lower or higher than the SMA, confirming strong bearish or bullish sentiment for a trade in the opposite direction. Trading rules: buy when the 14-day RSI is below 30 and the closing price is greater than the 5-day SMA; sell when the 14-day RSI is above 70 and the closing price is lower than the 5-day SMA. The Python implementation imports libraries, downloads Walmart (WMT) daily closing prices from 2020-01-03 to 2022-01-10 using yfinance, calculates RSI by estimating Average Gain and Average Loss, and computes the SMA with a rolling mean. The equity curve plots strategy performance over time. Backtesting was performed on WMT, and the same strategy was applied to SPY and QQQ by changing the ticker. Performance is measured using metrics such as annual return, average gain per trade, win ratio, time invested, maximum drawdown, and risk-adjusted return.

This study investigated the impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) on cardiovascular outcomes in patients with cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD). Using the TriNetX database, 12,410 patients who developed non-ischemic cardiomyopathy after cardiotoxic antineoplastic therapies were identified, with 1,300 receiving GLP-1 RAs and 11,110 not. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 1,223 patients per cohort were analyzed. All patients received guideline-directed medical therapy. Over a 1-year follow-up, the primary composite outcome of heart failure exacerbation, all-cause hospitalization/emergency department visits, and all-cause mortality occurred in 55.7% of the GLP-1 RA group versus 68.9% of the non-GLP-1 RA group (OR 0.566, p<0.001; HR 0.701). Secondary outcomes showed significant reductions in mortality (OR 0.471), heart failure exacerbation (OR 0.661), and all-cause hospital admissions (OR 0.654) with GLP-1 RA. Atrial fibrillation/flutter and ventricular tachycardia were not significantly reduced. A falsification outcome (gastroenteritis) showed no significant difference. The study concludes that GLP-1 RAs may offer cardioprotective benefits in CTRCD patients, though limitations include the observational design, reliance on electronic health records, lack of data on chemotherapy combinations, limited demographic diversity, and a short 1-year follow-up.

This study analyzed Omicron lineage replacement dynamics in Connecticut from January 2022 to January 2023 using genomic surveillance data from Yale New Haven Hospital, covering 5-10% of state cases. Researchers estimated infections via the covidestim model, calculated growth rates, compared nasal swab viral copy numbers (Ct values) as a proxy for intrinsic transmissibility, and assessed vaccine breakthrough infections as a metric for immune escape. BA.1 exhibited the fastest growth, reaching 50% frequency in 10 days, and showed increased odds of breakthrough infection in individuals vaccinated with at least two doses more than five months prior. BA.2 replaced BA.1 with significantly lower Ct values (higher viral copies) but no significant immune escape advantage. BA.4 and BA.5 replaced BA.2 with higher Ct values; BA.5 showed a non-significant tendency for increased breakthrough risk in recently vaccinated individuals. XBB replaced late-stage BA.5 lineages with lower Ct values and a non-significant tendency for decreased breakthrough in those more than five months from vaccination. A conceptual SIR-based model suggests BA.1 opened a new antigenic space, BA.2 outcompeted via higher transmissibility, BA.4/BA.5 exploited immune escape into a second antigenic space, and XBB combined immune escape with higher transmissibility. The findings highlight the capacity of Omicron lineages to explore different fitness niches through varying combinations of transmissibility and immune escape depending on host population antigen exposure history, and demonstrate the utility of integrating genomic, epidemiological, and clinical metadata to evaluate variant fitness.

Frank Schilbach introduces the course 14.13 Psychology and Economics (Behavioral Economics). He is a faculty member in the Economics Department whose research integrates psychological issues to understand the lives of the poor, studying topics like financial constraints, sleep deprivation, pain, substance abuse, and mental health.

The class defines psychology economics as studying the joint influences of psychological and economic factors on behaviors, aiming to make economic models more realistic by integrating insights from psychology and other fields. The standard economic model assumes people have well-defined and stable preferences, are rational optimizers, are narrowly self-interested, have perfect self-control, apply exponential discounting, are risk-averse over final outcomes, and process information as perfect Bayesians with no taste for beliefs or information.

Numerous real-world examples are presented as potential violations of these assumptions, including limited self-control, demand for commitment, non-Bayesian information processing, social preferences, demand for information (illustrated by Huntington's disease testing), default effects (illustrated by organ donation rates), limited memory (illustrated by medication reminders), and limited attention.

A model is a simplified representation of the world. Good models are simple, tractable, conceptually insightful, generalizable, falsifiable, and empirically consistent. The goal of behavioral economics is not to replace standard economics but to find important, tractable deviations from its assumptions to improve predictions.

The issue of laptops in class is used as an example. Standard economic considerations include externalities and the benefits of choice and efficient note-taking. Psychological considerations include temptation, limited self-control, overconfidence in multitasking, and the cognitive resources spent resisting temptation. Evidence from randomized controlled trials shows that allowing computers in class reduces test scores. The course will implement an opt-in laptop section.

The lecture discusses entry in industrial organization, moving from models with a fixed number of firms to a two-stage framework where potential entrants pay a sunk fixed cost K and then compete. Solving by backward induction, second-stage variable profits π(N) determine equilibrium entrants: in pure strategies, N where π(N) ≥ K > π(N+1); in mixed strategies, expected π(N)=K. Lower fixed costs generally increase entry, though in some models (e.g., Cournot) entry remains finite even as K→0. Profits are a “rounding error” determined by where entry costs cut off the number of firms.

Regarding efficiency, with homogeneous goods entry is excessive (up to a rounding error). The social benefit of an additional firm is the increase in total output times price minus marginal cost, but the entrant’s profits include business stolen from incumbents, making private incentive larger. In heterogeneous goods, entry can be too high or too low. The welfare change from an N+1st firm equals its variable profit minus K plus the change in incumbents’ profits (business stealing, negative) plus the change in consumer surplus. If consumer surplus rises substantially from better match quality, entry may be insufficient. A Hotelling circle example yields exactly twice as many firms as socially optimal.

Shaked and Sutton’s vertical differentiation model shows two cases: a natural oligopoly where only a finite number of firms can enter because everyone prefers the highest quality, and a specialization case where different consumers prefer different qualities, allowing infinite entry as K→0.

Jovanovic’s model features a continuum of entrants with unknown cost types who learn through production. Firms update beliefs, choose output, and exit. Predictions: small firms grow faster and fail more often; larger firms have higher profits; industry concentration correlates with profits and profit variance due to cost heterogeneity rather than competition.

Vellodi’s model of rating intermediaries (e.g., Yelp, Amazon) uses continuous-time learning with reviews. Entrants have binary quality, set prices, and consumers choose. Low-quality firms price below cost to attract customers and generate reviews. The equilibrium distribution of posteriors shows mass at the prior where learning is slow, and rapid learning beyond a threshold. A consumer-optimal platform design partially reveals information: stop publishing reviews for firms above a threshold to increase new firms’ incentive to invest in reputation, raising consumer surplus.

Japan has a high life expectancy (84.7 in 2020), and pension reforms have addressed population aging and declining natality. Little is known about how individuals perceive their own life expectancy and work/employment factors. Subjective Survival Probabilities (SSP) are associated with mortality and differ from self-rated health; they are influenced by factors like family longevity and life situations, and are a predictor of mortality after adjusting for self-rated health. Socio-economic position is associated with SSP. SSP is important in late career and retirement decision-making, though it does not necessarily translate into retirement behaviors. This study examines the relationship between SSP and work/employment among Japanese aged 50+. Employment refers to labor market status, while work refers to tasks. Japan has a gap between the pension eligibility age (rising to 65) and the mandatory retirement age (60), leading to reforms (PEA and EESL) and reemployment as contract workers. Working time in Japan is high, and job satisfaction affects health, interacting with working hours. Knowledge gaps include confusion between work and employment, inconsistent job satisfaction definitions, and limited research on SSP in relation to employment categories and job satisfaction. The study uses JSTAR panel data from four waves (2007-2013) across ten municipalities, with 7,082 respondents and 16,932 observations. SSP is measured by asking the probability of living to specific ages (75–110); distributions show peaks at certain percentages and highest density at high probabilities for age 80 and low for age 90. Four research questions address SSP differences by employment status, job satisfaction and working time, the specific relationship of job satisfaction and employment category, and adjustments for confounders.

The GAO report examines comprehensive support and improvement (CSI) schools, their characteristics, how CSI plans address selected ESEA requirements, and Education’s monitoring. Based on a nationally generalizable sample of CSI plans, an estimated 42 percent appeared to address all three selected required elements: being based on a needs assessment, identifying resource inequities, and including evidence-based interventions. An estimated 73 percent appeared to be based on a needs assessment, 52 percent appeared to identify resource inequities, and 86 percent included at least one intervention. However, an estimated 18 percent included interventions shown to be ineffective by high-quality studies reviewed by the What Works Clearinghouse. Some school and district officials reported challenges developing these plan elements.

Education collects school improvement data but notes limitations due to state discretion. Through routine monitoring between February 2020 and July 2023, Education identified compliance issues and required corrective actions in several states. Education does not independently select CSI plans for review, relying on states to choose them. GAO recommends that Education update monitoring protocols to independently select CSI plans for review. Education agreed and stated it will begin doing so in spring 2024.

This study investigated sodium homeostasis in structural connectivity hubs in drug-resistant focal epilepsy (DRFE) using 7T 23Na MRI. Twenty-three patients undergoing SEEG and 21 healthy controls were included. Structural connectomes were built from diffusion MRI, and hub regions were identified. Sodium parameters measured were total sodium concentration (TSC) and sodium signal fraction (f). TSC was globally increased in patients compared to controls, irrespective of epileptogenicity, while f was increased specifically in the epileptogenic zone (EZ) and decreased in non-EZ regions. In both patients and controls, hub regions had higher TSC than non-hub regions, but f did not differ. Epilepsy did not differentially affect sodium measures in hubs versus non-hubs; TSC was elevated and f slightly reduced in all patient parcels. Patients without overlap between EZ and hubs showed a more pronounced TSC increase, but no significant differences in EZ extent or clinical features were found. The findings indicate that TSC elevation in hubs relates to microstructural differences rather than epilepsy-specific effects, while f increase in the EZ may reflect altered homeostasis associated with epileptogenicity. The study concludes that sodium signal fraction may be more closely linked to regional homeostasis than microstructure.

At the start of the presidential term, federal functions were suspended in South Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, and Florida, except the Post-Office. Forts, arsenals, dockyards, and other property had been seized and held in hostility, with only Forts Pickens, Taylor, Jefferson, and Sumter remaining in federal possession. Fort Sumter was besieged by superior batteries, and federal arms and revenue within those states had been seized. Many army and navy officers resigned and took up arms against the government. Ordinances declared these states separated from the Union, and a combined government called the Confederate States was formed, seeking foreign recognition.

The incoming Executive chose a policy of exhausting peaceful measures, holding remaining public places and property, collecting revenue, and relying on time, discussion, and the ballot box. On March 5, a letter from Major Anderson at Fort Sumter stated that reinforcement would require 20,000 men and could not be accomplished before provisions ran out. General Scott concurred. Abandoning the fort was deemed ruinous, so an attempt was made to reinforce Fort Pickens instead. An order to land troops there was delayed by a quasi-armistice from the prior administration. An expedition to provision Fort Sumter was prepared and sent, with notice to South Carolina’s governor that only provisions would be delivered unless resisted. The fort was attacked and bombarded before the expedition arrived.

The assault on Fort Sumter was not self-defense; the garrison could not commit aggression. The assailants knew only bread would be provided unless they provoked more. They attacked to drive out federal authority and force immediate dissolution. This began the conflict of arms, forcing the issue of “immediate dissolution or blood.” The question is whether a constitutional republic can maintain its integrity against domestic foes.

The government called out war power, calling for 75,000 militia and proclaiming a blockade of insurrectionary ports. Further calls for three-year volunteers and additions to the regular army and navy were made under public necessity. The Commanding General was authorized to suspend habeas corpus in certain cases, exercised sparingly. The legality was questioned, but it was argued that the Constitution allows suspension in cases of rebellion when public safety requires it, and the Executive acted because Congress could not assemble.

Foreign nations initially doubted the Union’s survival, but now U.S. sovereignty is respected. The Executive recommends providing legal means for a short, decisive contest: at least 400,000 men and $400,000,000. The people are willing; the government needs only to direct them.

The movement in the South is rebellion, not lawful secession. The sophism that a state may withdraw peacefully from the Union was used to debauch the public mind. States have no sovereignty outside the Union; they were created by the Union and never had independent existence. Secession would lead to disintegration and injustice regarding debts and territories. The contest is a people’s struggle to maintain a government that elevates human condition. Common soldiers and sailors have remained loyal. The government’s maintenance against internal overthrow is the remaining experiment. After rebellion suppression, the Executive will follow the Constitution and laws as expressed in the inaugural address, with no coercion or subjugation beyond preserving the Union and guaranteeing a republican form of government. The Executive performed his duty; Congress is now to perform theirs.

This study investigated biases in left ventricular (LV) volume and ejection fraction (EF) measurements due to different methods of handling trabeculations, focusing on individuals with excessive trabeculation (ET). Using cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) images from 15 ET patients and 15 publicly available cases, four LV components were labeled: compact wall, central cavity, trabeculations, and intertrabecular recesses. The intertrabecular recesses showed significantly greater systolic fractional volume change and higher EF than the central cavity. Including trabeculations in the blood pool (per guidelines) increased end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes and decreased EF; excluding intertrabecular recesses from the cavity (per Jacquier criterion) decreased all volumes and EF. Contouring trabeculations (the reference method) yielded higher EF values and reclassified patients: the number with EF <40% was halved, while those with EF >50% doubled. Theoretical calculations demonstrated that greater trabecular tissue volume lowers measured EF if uncorrected, and that variations in trabecular layer EF or measurement errors affect total EF. The study concludes that the trabecular layer operates at a high EF, and contouring provides more accurate volume and EF assessments, potentially impacting clinical management. Limitations include a small single-center sample, manual labeling, and the need for larger validation studies.

Current legal, political, and socioeconomic systems rely on trust-based governance structures that are inadequate for the digital economy's data security demands, leading to interest in blockchain for trustless transactions. Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology secured by cryptography and regulated by consensus, making it virtually immutable. There is debate on whether blockchain is a disruptive or foundational technology, and a critical question concerns how it can generate business value. This study uses the digital business model lens to conduct an exploratory multiple case study of five blockchain companies in mainland China that use permissioned consortium blockchains. The analysis derives a typology of five blockchain-inspired digital business models: Platformer, which creates value by offering a proprietary blockchain architecture as an open innovation platform and captures value by positioning itself as a primary standard; Disintermediator, which creates value by displacing incumbents from conventional value chains and captures value as a market equalizer; Transformer, which creates value by revolutionizing contemporary business practices and captures value by transferring lessons learned to other industries; Mediator, which creates value by resolving inefficiencies in conventional value chains and captures value by offering firm-specific benefits to each party; and Co-Innovator, which creates value by codeveloping rival blockchain solutions and captures value through licensing. Challenges for these models include compatibility with existing infrastructures, resistance from incumbents, acquiring buy-in for new routines, limited transferability of lessons, and high initial investments.

This study extended follow-up of COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness (VE) to 50 weeks after second dose or 31 March 2022, covering the omicron era. Using English primary care data, VE of BNT162b2 and ChAdOx1 was estimated across 12 consecutive 4-week periods in subgroups aged 65+, 18-64 clinically vulnerable, 40-64, and 18-39. Third dose uptake was high in older and clinically vulnerable subgroups (≥90% by 31-50 weeks), but lower in the 18-39 subgroup (73% by 38 weeks). In subgroups with high third dose uptake, estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for non-COVID-19 death in two-dose recipients versus unvaccinated increased markedly (e.g., from 0.61 to 2.40 in 65+ for BNT162b2), indicating selection bias from deferred vaccination due to recent infection or poor health. Consequently, VE estimates beyond 26 weeks for COVID-19 outcomes in these subgroups were not interpreted. In the 18-39 subgroup, HRs for non-COVID-19 death remained stable, allowing interpretation. Waning of HRs for COVID-19 hospitalisation was approximately log-linear, with VE negligible by weeks 35-38. Waning against positive SARS-CoV-2 test was log-linear until weeks 23-26, with VE negligible by weeks 15-18, but HRs for any test remained around 2, suggesting confounding by testing behavior. Waning did not appear affected by omicron. The study highlights challenges in estimating long-term two-dose VE when third dose uptake is high, and recommends considering reasons for non-receipt of additional doses and reporting non-COVID-19 outcomes to detect bias.

The described system provides weather forecasting, including precipitation, fog, and runway visual range (RVR), using a cadence-based processing architecture with four servers: information collection and normalization, offline/background processing, modeling and prediction, and information distribution and alerting. Data is collected from microwave links (terrestrial and satellite), radar, vehicle sensors, and numerical weather prediction models, then pre-processed and stored in tile layers organized by cadence instances. Each cadence instance represents a processing cycle with collection, post-processing, and iterative forecast stages, supporting forecast cycles as short as one minute. The system asynchronously collects and processes data, separating collection from forecast cycles to handle high-frequency inputs. It infers fog from microwave attenuation, blends precipitation estimates from multiple sources, and calculates RVR forecasts. To improve efficiency, a cadence manager can perform partial recalculation and propagation: when new collected data is similar to prior forecasts, unchanged portions are copied, and only affected tiles are updated, reducing computational load. Forecasts are verified against collected data, and confidence scores are updated. The system aims to improve forecast accuracy by 30–70% and speed by up to 50%.

The present application addresses the problem that a compromised or malicious certificate authority (CA) can arbitrarily change digital certificate permissions, affecting blockchain security. It proposes that after a CA issues a digital certificate to a node, the CA sends a transaction request to write the certificate into the blockchain. The blockchain performs consensus verification on the digital certificate, and responds to or rejects the request based on the consensus result. Consensus verification involves determining verification results of participating nodes, counting nodes whose verification succeeds or fails, and determining the consensus result based on these counts. A digital certificate is written into the blockchain only if consensus verification succeeds; otherwise, it is rejected. Similarly, for a certificate revocation list or a record of a revoked digital certificate, the blockchain performs consensus verification before writing. The CA may also receive an application request from a node, issue a digital certificate, and send a transaction request to the blockchain for consensus verification. Corresponding apparatus and system are described.

The C19-YRSm, a 17-item patient-reported outcome measure for Long Covid, was further validated using data from 1,314 patients in the LOCOMOTION study. The instrument comprises Symptom Severity (SS), Functional Disability (FD), Overall Health (OH), and Other Symptoms subscales. Results showed good internal reliability, convergent validity with the FACIT-Fatigue scale, and known-groups validity (discriminating by symptom burden, hospitalisation, and ICU admission). Responsiveness over 30 days was modest (effect sizes 0.22–0.50) and greater than the EQ-5D-5L. Test-retest reliability was good. Minimally important differences were estimated as SS=2, FD=2, OH=1, and minimal clinically important differences as 4 for SS and FD. A two-factor structure (SS and FD) showed reasonable fit. The study concludes the C19-YRSm is a valid, reliable, and responsive condition-specific tool suitable for clinical and research use to monitor Long Covid trajectory and interventions.

The lecture explains Independent Chip Model (ICM) theory, which accounts for the nonlinear value of chips in poker tournaments because players aim to survive and move up escalating payouts rather than simply maximize chips. ICM calculates a stack's monetary equity by assuming a player's chance of winning is proportional to their chip share, then recursively computing probabilities of finishing in other positions. An example with three players and payouts of 5, 3, 2 shows chip EV does not equal money EV. ICM is most relevant on the payout bubble and final table, and in satellite tournaments where only a top fraction qualifies, it can justify folding very strong hands like aces preflop. Big stacks have lower money EV than chip EV, while small stacks have higher. ICM encourages looser play when acting first because opponents are disincentivized to call, described as a "traffic intersection game." The speaker then plays through a final table, discussing specific hands, stack sizes, and ICM-driven decisions such as folding jack-ten offsuit to an all-in reraise, exploiting opponents' tightness, and adjusting as stacks change. Heads-up play eliminates ICM; the small blind has position, and strategies shift accordingly.

Chemical analysis of residue in pottery fragments from the Sicilian site of Castelluccio, led by Dr. Davide Tanasi, identified oleic and linoleic acids, confirming olive oil. The 400 fragments were reassembled into a 3.5-foot container with three handles on each side. The oil dates to the Early Bronze Age (end of the 3rd to beginning of the 2nd millennium BCE), making it the oldest olive oil recovered in Italy. This pushes back systematic olive oil production by at least 700 years. Other cooking utensils, including a terracotta plate and separating pottery, were also found. The study appears in Analytical Methods.

This passage introduces GeoFunFlow, a geometry-aware diffusion framework for solving inverse problems governed by PDEs on irregular geometries. Inverse problems aim to recover physical states from indirect observations and are ill-posed, especially on irregular domains. Operator learning methods like DeepONet and FNO have advanced PDE solution approximation but are mostly limited to regular domains; recent extensions to complex geometries focus on forward tasks, leaving inverse problems underexplored. Diffusion-based generative models have shown promise in scientific machine learning but also remain restricted to regular grids. The proposed GeoFunFlow combines a geometric function autoencoder (GeoFAE) with a Perceiver module to handle unstructured meshes and enable continuous reconstruction, coupled with a latent diffusion model for posterior sampling conditioned on sparse and noisy sensor data. The authors provide theoretical guarantees for accurate posterior approximations and demonstrate state-of-the-art accuracy on benchmarks with complex geometries. The passage also reviews operator learning and rectified flow preliminaries, and formally defines the problem setup: reconstructing physical fields from sparse noisy measurements across a family of irregular domains, with the goal of learning a conditional probabilistic operator.

This study addresses Medicare fraud and overutilization detection in ophthalmology using machine learning. It notes that over $100 billion is lost annually to healthcare fraud, with Medicare as a primary target. Existing detection relies on the LEIE dataset, which suffers from extreme class imbalance and focuses on overt fraud, missing subtle overutilization. The authors created a labeled dataset of 663 ophthalmologists (200 overutilizers, 463 non-fraudulent) through collaboration with experienced physicians and medical billers, using 2015 Medicare billing data. Features were engineered from Medicare Provider Utilization and Payment Data, including procedure counts, beneficiary counts, and ratios, resulting in 1028 features per provider.

Multiple supervised machine learning models were compared using repeated nested cross-validation. The stacking ensemble model achieved the highest AUROC score of 0.907 (95% CI: 0.896-0.918) and the best calibration. Applied to 2021 data for 17,013 ophthalmologists, the model predicted an 8.6% overutilization rate (1,457 providers). The estimated annual monetary loss in ophthalmology was $437.1 million, extrapolated to approximately $49.1 billion across Medicare. Overutilization rates and losses varied by Medicare jurisdiction, with Jurisdiction JE (including California) having the highest rate (14.01%) and JN (Florida, Puerto Rico, Virgin Islands) the highest monetary loss ($63.6 million). Feature importance analysis identified the ratio of total Medicare payments to total patients as the strongest indicator, along with excessive use of certain HCPCS codes.

The study highlights the value of domain-expert labeling and ensemble methods for detecting nuanced overutilization, while acknowledging limitations such as small labeled dataset size, reliance on model predictions, and the need for subspecialty-specific labeled data.

This statistical analysis plan describes the analyses for a multicenter study comparing dasiglucagon 0.6 mg, placebo, and GlucaGen® in patients aged 6–17 years with type 1 diabetes. The primary efficacy analysis uses the Full Analysis Set (FAS); supportive analyses use the Per Protocol Set (PPS). The safety analysis set is used for all safety evaluations.

The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery (first increase ≥20 mg/dL from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose). Recovery is censored at 45 minutes for patients receiving rescue IV glucose or not recovering. The primary analysis employs a stratified log-rank test (age group: 6–11, 12–17 years; injection site: abdomen/thigh) comparing dasiglucagon to placebo. Sensitivity analyses include no censoring for rescue and censoring at rescue time. Supportive analyses include a Wilcoxon test, discrete-time Cox proportional hazards model (with covariates age group, injection site, baseline plasma glucose), and linear interpolation of recovery times. Kaplan-Meier plots and histograms are produced.

Secondary efficacy endpoints are plasma glucose recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes (analyzed via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by age group and injection site) and plasma glucose changes from baseline at those time points (analyzed via ANOVA with factors treatment, age group, injection site). A hierarchical testing procedure controls multiplicity for dasiglucagon versus placebo comparisons; GlucaGen® comparisons are not part of the inferential hierarchy.

Safety analyses include extent of exposure (insulin administration, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, post-treatment rescue glucose), local tolerability, adverse events (TEAEs defined as events occurring/worsening after dosing; coded with MedDRA; summaries by system organ class and preferred term), clinical laboratory evaluations (hematology, biochemistry, coagulation, urinalysis), vital signs, 12-lead ECG (including categorical QTcF analyses), and immunogenicity (anti-drug antibodies). Concomitant medications and current diabetes treatment are coded using WHODrug and summarized by ATC class and preferred name.

Pharmacokinetic analyses of dasiglucagon and glucagon concentrations use non-compartmental methods. Pharmacodynamic analyses include plasma glucose AUE0-30min. Data handling rules for concentrations below LLOQ and sampling time deviations are specified. Baseline is the last non-missing value before first dose. No imputation for missing efficacy data is applied. The document also outlines programming conventions, QC requirements, and a list of planned tables, figures, and listings.

He dismisses the Entente note as a bluff and seeks to avoid spring offensive bloodshed. The Ambassador warns that immediate unrestricted U-boat warfare would make war with the US unavoidable, given US resources. He suggests delaying to improve diplomatic position, arguing that if Germany meets Wilson's proposal and it fails due to opponents, it would be difficult for Wilson to go to war even if unrestricted U-boat warfare starts later. He believes a better peace can be achieved through conferences than if the US joins the enemies, and requests wireless confirmation if a certain despatch is not to be carried out on February 1. Separately, the US Ambassador in France reports that the Socialist Party deputies passed a resolution approving Wilson's Senate address, stating peace should be based on the free will of the people, not force.
