The lecture recaps previous material: covariant derivative, Lie derivative, Killing vectors, and tensor densities. The Levi-Civita symbol is a tensor density of weight 1; the determinant of the metric is a tensor density of weight −2. Combining them allows conversion of any tensor density of weight w into a proper tensor by multiplying by |g|^(w/2), with absolute value used to keep the square root positive. This yields a covariant volume element: √|g| dx^0 dx^1 dx^2 dx^3.

A “party trick” shows that the contracted Christoffel symbol Γ^μ_μα equals (1/√|g|) ∂_α √|g| = ∂_α ln √|g|. The proof uses a linear algebra identity: for a small matrix ε, det(1+ε) ≈ 1+tr(ε), applied to variations of the metric. This simplifies the covariant divergence of a vector field to ∇_μ V^μ = (1/√|g|) ∂_μ (√|g| V^μ), which aids Gauss’s theorem in curved manifolds. For tensors, the same simplification only works for antisymmetric tensors; otherwise, Christoffel terms remain. The divergence of the stress-energy tensor gives a 4-vector, but integrating it over a volume is ambiguous because vectors in different tangent spaces cannot be compared without a path-dependent transport law, so local conservation does not straightforwardly become global conservation.

The lecture then turns to kinematics in curved spacetime. A test body (no charge, spatial extent, or spin, only mass) in a freely falling frame moves on a straight line, meaning it parallel transports its own tangent vector. This leads to the geodesic equation: d²x^μ/dλ² + Γ^μ_αβ (dx^α/dλ)(dx^β/dλ) = 0. If the right-hand side is zero, the parameter λ is affine; proper time is a good affine parameter for timelike trajectories. Only linear reparameterizations λ' = aλ + b preserve affine parameterization. A second derivation defines geodesics via extremal aging: the action I = ∫ dτ is varied, and requiring δI = 0 yields the same geodesic equation. The lecture concludes by noting upcoming topics: null trajectories and using Killing vectors to find conserved quantities along geodesics.

The Biorepository and Integrative Genomics (BIG) Initiative in Tennessee analyzed 13,152 genomes from a diverse Mid-South population, predominantly pediatric (87% under 18). 50% of participants had non-European or admixed ancestry, with 20% similar to African reference populations and 30% admixed. Ancestry was geographically stratified: African ancestry more common in urban areas, European in suburban. 771,717 novel single nucleotide variants (11.2% of total) were identified, enriched for high-impact functional consequences. Disease prevalence analysis showed higher odds ratios for asthma and obesity in minority groups, particularly in urban areas. This systematic review examines empirical studies on large language models (LLMs) in education, focusing on risks. It addresses four research questions: which educational applications are most frequently examined, what methods are used to assess them, which risks are reported, and what mitigation strategies are proposed. The review categorizes LLM applications into operational effectiveness (e.g., feedback generation, data processing, domain knowledge, teaching capability), personalized applications (e.g., grading, content generation, predictions), and interactive learning tools (e.g., student engagement, cognitive impact, academic performance). Methodologies include comparative evaluations, statistical analyses, mixed-methods, and neuroscientific measures. Frequently reported risks include superficial understanding, limited robustness, anthropomorphic characteristics, hallucinations, bias, cognitive and metacognitive risks, behavioural risks, and privacy concerns. Mitigation strategies are mapped to educators, developers, students, and governments. The paper introduces an LLM-Risk Adapted Learning Model (IMO) that traces how risks emerge across Interaction, Monitoring, and Outcome stages of the learning cycle. The review highlights the need for human-centred design, transparency, and interdisciplinary collaboration, and notes limitations such as short-term studies and English-language focus.

A Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) is trained via meta-learning to approximate the inverse Hessian operator in 4D-Var data assimilation, mapping the adjoint-derived vector f to the optimal initial state u0. Standalone FNO predictions are less accurate than the conjugate gradient (CG) method. The proposed FNO-CG approach uses the FNO output to initialize CG, improving both accuracy and efficiency. On a linear advection equation test set, FNO-CG reduces average relative error by 62% and iteration count by 17% compared to standard CG initialized with the background state. Gains are most pronounced for ill-conditioned problems. The method embeds sparse observations implicitly in f, simplifying training, and is noted as extendable to nonlinear PDEs via incremental 4D-Var.

A commodity trading advisor (CTA) is an individual or organization providing personalized advice and services for trading futures contracts, commodity options, and retail off-exchange forex contracts or swaps. CTAs can manage individual accounts (Managed Futures) or run a CTA fund—a hedge fund using managed futures strategies. They are professional investment managers seeking profits from global financial, commodity, and currency markets via exchange-traded futures and options and OTC forward contracts. Compensation includes management fees (annual percentage of equity) and incentive fees (percentage of new profits), with no incentive fees if profits do not exceed a hurdle rate or high-water mark. CTAs must register with the CFTC and be NFA members.

While some CTAs use discretionary strategies, many employ systematic approaches using trading algorithms based on technical analysis, trend following, momentum indicators, or fundamental factors. A true systematic CTA relies solely on algorithmic signals, reducing human emotion. The CTA business is large, managing $350bn. Trend following is the predominant strategy. Trend-following CTAs aim to systematically identify medium to long-term trends, involving signal generation and exposure sizing. An example is the Swedish fund Lynx, with a CAGR of about 10% since 2000 and returns mostly uncorrelated to the stock market. Many CTAs use momentum strategies across multi-asset universes, including cross-sectional momentum (winners-minus-losers), going long top performers and short bottom performers.

CTAs are limited to trading futures, options, and currency swaps, unlike hedge funds. Most CTA strategies are trend following, either systematic or discretionary. A simple 200-day moving average strategy on the S&P 500 showed a CAGR of 6.73% and max drawdown of 28%, capturing gains while limiting losses. The most important factor for a CTA is having many uncorrelated strategies that complement each other. The Brummer & Partners Multi-strategy fund achieved steady returns by investing in multiple hedge funds with low correlation, adding value even from mediocre funds if correlation is low. Backtests should consider correlation as much as performance. Risks include losses, market volatility, and inaccurate data; limitations include capital needs and market knowledge, though complexity does not necessarily add value. A good CTA produces good risk-adjusted returns and is systematic. Ultimately, a CTA trading strategy is mostly about correlation, not necessarily the most profitable strategy.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS ADC with a source-synchronous data interface supporting 2-lane and 4-lane modes with SDR or DDR options, configurable via SPI. Conversion results are output MSB first in 24-bit packets with the last six bits zero. Data clock and frame clock frequencies depend on sampling clock speed, data rate, and lane count. A data output randomizer XORs the conversion result with the LSB or a PRBS bit to reduce ground bounce correlation. Data averaging modes include simple average (halves output data rate) and moving average (no rate change). Test patterns (fixed, digital ramp, alternating) can replace output data for interface debugging, configurable per channel group. The device powers down via the RESET pin or register, and requires an initialization sequence after power-up or reset. A speed-boost mode allows up to 8MSPS for a selected analog input channel pair. SPI configuration uses 16-bit registers across three banks, with procedures for writes, reads, and daisy-chain operation for multiple devices. Register fields control interface modes, test patterns, averaging, speed-boost, analog input bandwidth, common-mode range, and power-down. Application information highlights use in ATE systems, with calibration achieving TUE <0.01%, wide-bandwidth mode settling to 99.95% FS in 7.5µs, and layout recommendations for decoupling and signal isolation.

NSCC faculty (55%) and support staff (64%) ratified six-year agreements with a 7% wage increase. Employees can collect service awards based on salary at retirement or March 31, 2018, despite a 2015 service-year freeze.

During Card Identification Mode, the host remains at fOD frequency; in Data Transfer Mode, it may use fPP. SEND_CSD (CMD9) retrieves Card Specific Data. SET_DSR (CMD4) configures driver stages and switches clock to fPP. CMD7 selects one card into Transfer State; with RCA=0x0000, all cards return to Stand-by. De-selection occurs automatically on common CMD line when another card is selected, or the host must manage it with separate lines. Data transfer is point-to-point with addressed commands.

Read and write commands can be aborted by CMD12. After data transfer, the card enters Programming State (success) or Transfer State (failure). Block write may buffer; when buffers full, DAT0 is held low (BUSY). No buffering for write CSD, write protection, or erase. Parameter set and read commands are forbidden during programming. Moving another card to Transfer State with CMD7 does not abort erase/programming; the card enters Disconnect State and releases DAT. Resetting (CMD0/CMD15) terminates programming and may destroy data. Wide bus (4-bit) mode is selected via ACMD6; default is 1-bit. Locked cards reject ACMD6.

For 2 GByte cards, maximum block length is 1024 bytes, but CMD16 block length is limited to 512 bytes. Data read: blocks have start bits, payload, CRC, end bits. CMD17 reads single block, CMD18 reads multiple blocks until CMD12. Misalignment causes ADDRESS_ERROR. Data write: blocks include CRC; card checks CRC before writing. Block length from CMD16 must be 512 bytes for block write commands. Partial block write allowed if WRITE_BL_PARTIAL=1. Multiple block write is faster. Misalignment or write to protected area aborts write. CSD programming is CRC protected; ROM portions must match. After write, card holds DAT0 low if buffer full; host can poll with CMD13. Deselecting with CMD7 releases DAT without interrupting write; reselecting reactivates busy. Simultaneous writes to multiple cards possible via interleaving.

Pre-erase with ACMD23 before multiple block write improves speed; the number of pre-erased blocks is defined. Remaining blocks after early termination are undefined. ACMD22 returns count of well-written blocks after error.

Erase sequence: CMD32, CMD33, CMD38. Out-of-sequence commands cause ERASE_SEQ_ERROR or ERASE_RESET. Write-protected sectors are skipped. Erase busy indicated by DAT0 low. Discard operation: sequence CMD32, CMD33, CMD38 with argument 00000001h; host checks DISCARD_SUPPORT. Contents become 'don't care'. Supported only for SDHC/SDXC, not SPI. Busy timeout 250ms. FULE logically erases entire user area: CMD32 (arg=0), CMD33 (arg=end), CMD38 (arg=00000002h). Host checks FULE_SUPPORT. Busy timeout 1 second. If unsupported, ERASE is executed.

Write protection: mechanical switch (host responsibility), internal (optional, blank), and password protection. Password in PWD and PWD_LEN registers; optional FEP and FEP_LEN for Card Ownership Protection (COP). Locked cards accept basic class, ACMD41, CMD16, lock card class. Lock/unlock command is a single block write in transfer state. COP prevents reuse without password; FEP disables Force Erase and Clear PWD. COP Unlock (CMD42[1Fh]) required after power-up when FEP=set. Non-COP Card: Force Erase (CMD42[08h]) erases all content and PWD. COP Card: if FEP=0, compatible with Ver.1.0; if FEP=1, locked until COP Unlock. In Ver.2.0 mode, FEP management, two Force Erase types, and PWD reset inhibit. Command sequences for setting, clearing, locking, unlocking PWD, and COP-specific functions are defined. Force Erase on locked card erases user area, clears PWD, unlocks; FEP Force Erase requires FEP. ACMD6 rejected when locked. Locked cards accept specific commands; others illegal. Three card types: Type 1 (earlier), Type 2 (v1.10+), Type 3 (COP, v5.10+).

Application-specific command: CMD55 (APP_CMD) makes next command an ACMD. Reserved ACMD numbers. Switch function command CMD6 uses function groups: Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, Power Limit. Mode 0 checks support and max current/power; Mode 1 sets functions. Default function 0. Power Limit default 0.72W; host sets based on capability. UHS-II mode: Function Groups 1 and 3 not used, Group 4 mandatory. Switch function status returns 512 bits with support bits, function selection, busy status. High-Speed mode (25 MB/s) achieved via CMD6, clock 50 MHz, requires 1-to-1 connection. Command system expansion via CMD34-37, CMD50, CMD57; switch function group 2 changes interpretation. CMD8 initializes v2.00+ cards, checks voltage, returns R7. Capacity types: SDSC uses byte address, block length by CMD16; SDHC/SDXC use block address, fixed 512-byte block length, no partial/misalign access, no write-protected groups. Clock can be stopped for power saving; after transactions, 8 clocks needed before shutdown. ACMD41 requires continuous clock or polling. CRC7 protects commands/responses/CSD/CID; CRC16 protects data blocks. Illegal commands or CRC errors cause no response and error bits. Read timeout: 100ms or 100× typical access (lower). Write timeout: 250ms or 100× typical program (lower); for SDHC/SDXC, busy up to 250ms (500ms in some cases). UHS-II data burst busy up to 1s. Host should use fixed timeout for writes.

Several Swedish hockey players react to the retirement of a legendary Swedish player. They describe him as arguably the best Swedish player ever, a great role model, and a low-key personality overshadowed by more marquee figures. He won four Stanley Cups and seven Norris Trophies while playing for Detroit, serving as the team's backbone for two decades. He is praised for his consistent greatness, durability, and all-around play. Adam Larsson, Henrik Tallinder, and Johan Hedberg all express admiration, with Tallinder calling him an icon and Hedberg noting his consistency sets him apart.

David Wybron, headteacher at Lord Williams’s School, appeals to the Government over a ‘Perfect Storm’ of issues. He criticizes the new GCSEs for imposing greater exam pressure on state school students while independent schools use less content-heavy IGCSEs with coursework, and questions why state schools face league table penalties for choosing IGCSEs. He highlights a teacher recruitment crisis, with the Department for Education missing targets for five years and a need for 47,000 secondary teachers by 2024. Immigration controls hinder hiring overseas teachers; he supports the ‘Let Them Teach’ campaign to add all teaching subjects to the shortage occupation list. Funding is also a problem: due to a 3% cap in the funding formula, Lord Williams’s students receive over £1,000 less per head than those in well-funded authorities. He calls for fairness, a rethink of exam content, no league table penalty for IGCSEs, honesty about recruitment, and visa policy changes to match health workers.

A TeamLease survey of nine Tier I cities finds Delhi has the highest job loss risk, followed by Bengaluru and Hyderabad; Pune has the lowest. By industry, industrial manufacturing & allied sectors have the highest risk, while healthcare and telecom have the lowest. Other low-risk sectors include retail, banking, financial services, insurance, fast-moving consumer and durable goods, power & energy, and agriculture.

The Triple RSI trading strategy is a modified RSI strategy with four key variables, three based on RSI. It focuses on mean reversion. Trading rules involve RSI readings, the 200-day moving average, and buy/sell signals. The strategy is inspired by Larry Connors' R3 strategy but modified. Backtesting on SPY (S&P 500 ETF) from 1993 yielded 83 trades, an average gain of 1.4% per trade, a win rate of 91%, and a profit factor of 5. The strategy can complement a long-term buy-and-hold portfolio and, with a margin account, potentially boost returns using a small amount of leverage.

This specification update for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 documents numerous hardware issues, their implications, and resolutions. Issues affect various components including LPC, SMB, GPIO, PIT, debug port, XPIC, DMA, thermal management, USB, ATA, audio, PCI, PIC, UART, KEL, RTC, and power management. Workarounds are provided for most issues.

The passage describes a low volatility stock strategy, which involves investing in stocks with lower price fluctuation than the overall market. Low volatility stocks are defined as having relatively stable prices and a beta of less than 1, indicating less volatility than the market. They are often found in sectors such as consumer staples, utilities, and healthcare. The strategy aims to minimize portfolio volatility while still achieving returns, and it may appeal to investors seeking reduced risk and more consistent returns, particularly those nearing retirement or with lower risk tolerance.

Benefits of low volatility investing include reduced portfolio volatility, lower risk of large declines, more consistent returns, and potential long-term outperformance. Empirical research over many decades has shown that low volatility stocks have outperformed high volatility stocks, contrary to financial theory. However, risks include the possibility of lower returns compared to higher-volatility stocks in certain periods, long periods of underperformance, and the strategy may not suit all investors. Past performance does not guarantee future results.

Implementation can be done by investing in low volatility ETFs or mutual funds (such as SPLV), or by selecting individual stocks with stable earnings, consistent dividends, and low beta. Building a low volatility portfolio requires a long time horizon (years to decades), diversification across sectors, and regular review and rebalancing. Backtesting the strategy involves analyzing historical market data to evaluate past performance, but it provides only a rough estimate and may not predict future results.

Strategies to potentially enhance returns include combining low volatility with other factors, using leverage, or focusing on small-cap low volatility stocks, though these add risks. Rebalancing involves adjusting portfolio weightings to maintain the desired risk and return profile.

The passage cites research: Professor Kenneth French’s data from 1964 to 2015 showed poor returns for the 10% most volatile stocks, and the three lowest volatility deciles never had a negative 10-year return since 1974. A study of US stocks from 1963 to 2018 found that stocks with the lowest market value and highest volatility produced negative returns. Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway exhibited a high Sharpe ratio, attributed to leverage and a focus on cheap, safe, quality stocks. The low volatility anomaly is confirmed internationally, as a study by Baker and Haugen across 21 developed and 12 emerging markets found low risk stocks outperformed. Possible explanations for low-beta outperformance include micro and macro effects and the uncertain business models of high volatility stocks. The passage concludes with FAQs defining low volatility stocks and summarizing implementation and portfolio building steps.

NVIDIA's Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) uses a deep neural network and Tensor Cores to construct high-quality images comparable to native resolution while improving performance. On Ampere architecture GPUs, DLSS is enhanced with third-generation Tensor Cores and a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor, making 8K gaming at 60 fps feasible on ray-traced titles.

GA10x GPUs introduce GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron, using PAM4 signaling to double I/O data rate over GDDR6. It delivers up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth, a 52% improvement over TU102, and features Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding to improve signal integrity. Pseudo-independent memory channels aid BVH ray traversal.

NVIDIA RTX IO is a suite of technologies for GPU-based loading and decompression of assets, working with Microsoft's DirectStorage API. It offloads CPU decompression work to the GPU, improving I/O performance by up to 100x compared to hard drives and traditional APIs, and enables faster game loading and reduced object pop-in.

The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU, based on GA10x Ampere architecture, delivers up to 2x FP32 throughput, 2x ray-tracing throughput, and up to 5x (10x with sparsity) AI training throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000. It features 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, PCIe Gen4, and supports virtual GPU software.

Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a for 8K60, and HDMI 2.1 for 8K60 and 4K120. The fifth-generation NVDEC decoder supports hardware-accelerated decoding of MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, with AV1 hardware decode being a first for GPUs. The seventh-generation NVENC encoder provides hardware-accelerated encoding with quality exceeding x264 Fast and on par with x264 Medium.

The GeForce RTX 3090 features 24GB GDDR6X, 10496 CUDA Cores, and is 1.5x faster than TITAN RTX. The GeForce RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and outperforms the RTX 2080 Ti. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X detects transmission errors and replays them, causing performance to plateau rather than crash during overclocking. The RTX A6000 professional GPU includes 48GB GDDR6, 10752 CUDA Cores, second-generation RT Cores, and supports NVLink for 96GB combined memory, offering significant performance gains in SPECviewperf, rendering, HPC, and deep learning workloads.
Naughty Dog's Uncharted: The Lost Legacy, starring Chloe Frazer and Nadine Ross, was highlighted over The Last of Us Part 2 at E3 2017. Work began weeks after Uncharted 4.

The passage defines command legality in SD card states, distinguishing defined/undefined and legal/illegal commands, with an exception for ACMD41 regarding APP_CMD status. It details the Switch Function command (CMD6), which uses function groups for access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. CMD6 operates in Mode 0 to query supported functions and maximum current/power, and Mode 1 to switch functions. Power Limit settings control total card power consumption, with default 0.72W and higher settings for UHS modes. Speed Class specifications define performance using Allocation Units (AU) and Recording Units (RU), with parameters Pw, Pm, Pr, and TFR. Speed Classes 2, 4, 6, and 10 are specified for SDSC and SDHC, while SDXC Speed Class requires entirely free AUs, uses CMD20 for control, and does not support Pm. UHS Speed Grades 1 and 3 and Video Speed Classes are also described. The passage lists command classes, response types (R1, R1b, R2, R3, R6, R7), CRC7 and CRC16 protection, card state transitions, and timing conditions for read, write, and erase operations.

Material properties are approximated by Density Functional Theory (DFT), but its high computational cost limits large-scale applications. Machine learning force fields trained on DFT data enable efficient predictions, with performance heavily dependent on atomic representation. Graph Neural Networks have become mainstream, evolving from pairwise local interactions to angular embedding and equivariant/invariant architectures for crystal property prediction. However, real-space encoders fail to capture long-term atomic interactions, often mapping distinct crystal structures to identical representations. Diffraction-space encoding offers a unique, lossless representation of infinite periodic structures. Traditional X-ray diffraction relies on fixed tabulated form factors that cannot distinguish atoms in different local chemical environments. This work introduces PRDNet, a multimodal framework that integrates graph embeddings with a learned pseudo-particle diffraction module, generating synthetic diffraction patterns invariant to crystallographic symmetries. Evaluations on Materials Project, JARVIS-DFT, and MatBench demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. Related work categorizes existing crystal representations into multi-edge graphs, atomic angular embedding, and periodic vector-based systems, all sharing the limitation of mapping distinct structures to the same representation.

The paper proposes Truthful Text Summarization (TTS), an incentive-aligned pipeline for LLM-based multi-source summarization. It addresses how LLM summarization reshapes content creator incentives, making value depend on representation in summaries rather than ranking, and how LLM weaknesses (hallucinations, prompt injection, difficulty with conflicting claims) enable strategic manipulation. TTS reframes summarization as a structured problem: instead of summarizing documents directly, it decomposes a leave-one-out draft summary from peer sources into atomic claims, extracts per-source stances (supports, contradicts, abstain) on those claims, and scores each source using a multi-task peer prediction rule that rewards informative corroboration beyond chance. Low-scoring sources are filtered out before generating the final summary from reliable sources. The leave-one-out construction ensures claims are exogenous to the scored source, preventing it from shaping its own evaluation. The scoring rule computes a reliability score by averaging, across claims and peers, the difference between on-task agreement and off-task agreement. Theoretical analysis shows that truthful reporting maximizes expected score, and the mechanism provides informed truthfulness (truthful weakly dominates, strictly better than uninformed strategies) and strong truthfulness (truthful strictly dominates significant deviations) with finite-sample bounds. Utility derives from inclusion in the summary via a hard threshold, not monetary payments. Experiments on Natural Questions and ClashEval datasets with six-source pools (reliable, deceptive, adversarial) demonstrate that TTS scores separate reliable from unreliable sources without ground-truth labels, significantly improving precision, recall, F1, and answer accuracy over baselines (initial synthesis, majority prompt, majority claims). TTS also resists coordinated uninformative behavior, correctly assigning near-zero scores to a bloc of sources that contradict every claim, unlike majority-based scoring which fails. The framework makes truthful, informative reporting the best strategy for inclusion, aligning source incentives with user needs.

China's official manufacturing PMI rose to 51.9 in May, an eight-month high, exceeding the forecast of 51.3. Production grew at the fastest rate in six months, and new orders hit an eight-month high. Export orders improved, though some economists suspected front-loading due to U.S. trade frictions. Economists expressed skepticism about the strength's sustainability, attributing it partly to temporary easing of pollution controls and noting slumping end-demand from infrastructure and property investment amid deleveraging. Small firms' activity contracted, and 40.1% of surveyed manufacturers raised funding concerns. Hi-tech manufacturing activity rose to 54.8 despite pending U.S. tariffs. The non-manufacturing PMI edged up to 54.9, while construction activity dipped to 60.1. The composite PMI rose to 54.6. Economists still expect China's growth to slow to 6.5% this year, citing rising borrowing costs, pollution limits, and local government debt crackdowns.

Lilly Nguyen and Phil De Carlos married in Texas Children’s Hospital chapel. Their son Lucas, born at 24 weeks weighing 1 lb 12 oz, now weighs 4 lbs 4 oz. De Carlos proposed in the NICU on Dec. 15 with a bib and sign. They wed on New Year’s Day to include Lucas, then visited him with Nguyen’s three other children.

Defensive tackles are interior defensive linemen who play a critical role in stopping the run and pressuring quarterbacks. Their blue-collar work often goes unrecognized in stats, involving taking on double teams, batting down passes, and making plays in short-yardage situations. In the run game, they penetrate the backfield, shed blocks, and force offenses to pass. They face frequent double teams, freeing up second- and third-level defenders. As pass rushers, they operate in tight spaces with few one-on-one matchups, earning sacks through effort and disrupting the quarterback by taking up double teams to free edge rushers. The position lines up inside, with defensive ends outside; its name evolved from nose guard. It is also called nose tackle or nose guard when aligned over the center. Required skills include strength, agility, recognition, and toughness. Typical body type: 6'2–6'4, 300–335 pounds, thick build. Notable defensive tackles include Aaron Donald (3 NFL Defensive Player of the Year awards, Pro Bowl every year, Super Bowl champion in 2022) and "Mean" Joe Greene (4 Super Bowl titles, 2 Defensive Player of the Year awards, 10 Pro Bowls). Defensive tackles are important because their work up front sets the tone, disrupts offensive rhythm, and allows defenses to pressure the quarterback without blitzing, enabling simpler coverages and lighter boxes against the run.

MIT and the Carnegie Institution for Science released a public dataset of nearly 61,000 measurements of over 1,600 nearby stars, gathered over 20 years by the Keck Observatory. The release includes open-source software and a tutorial, aiming to recruit the public to help hunt exoplanets. Researchers have already identified over 100 potential exoplanets from the data. The dataset will be periodically updated.

Turing GPUs feature an enhanced NVENC encoder supporting H.265 8K encode at 30 fps, offering up to 25% bitrate savings for HEVC and 15% for H.264. The NVDEC decoder adds support for HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing improves encoding quality over Pascal and software encoders, enabling 4K streaming.

Turing includes hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, an open standard delivering power, display, and data through a single USB-C connector for VR headsets, simplifying connectivity and enabling VR on small form factor devices.

NVLink replaces MIO and PCIe for SLI GPU-to-GPU transfers. TU102 has two x8 links (50 GB/sec bidirectional each), TU104 has one. Two-way SLI is supported; 3-way and 4-way are not. Increased bandwidth enables new display topologies.

Ray tracing is accelerated by RT Cores in each SM, which handle BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection tests, offloading the SM. Hybrid rendering combines rasterization and ray tracing, using ray tracing for reflections, refractions, and shadows. Denoising filtering reduces the number of rays needed. Turing achieves over 10 Giga Rays/sec, about 10x faster than Pascal's software ray tracing.

NGX technology uses Tensor Cores for AI-based features: DLSS (Deep Learning Super-Sampling) produces higher quality than TAA with lower input sample counts, improving performance; DLSS 2X approaches 64x supersampling quality. Other NGX features include InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Mesh Shading introduces Task and Mesh Shaders with cooperative thread models, allowing developers to eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks and use more efficient geometry processing, such as LOD selection and dynamic cutaways.

Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows shading rate to vary per 16x16 pixel region, with seven options from 1x1 to 4x4. Applications include Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering. VRS can also increase shading rate with MSAA.

Texture Space Shading (TSS) decouples shading from screen space by computing and storing shading values in texture space, enabling reuse and temporal stability. It supports stereo rendering by reusing left-eye shading for the right eye.

Multi-View Rendering (MVR) expands Pascal's SMP to up to four views per pass, supporting view-dependent attributes beyond X coordinate. Uses include canted HMDs, cascaded shadow maps, and character instancing.

Turing supports DX12 Resource Binding Tier 3 (bindless CBV/UAV) and Tier 2 resource heaps. VR improvements include VirtualLink, MVR, VRS foveated rendering, and VRWorks Audio accelerated by RT Cores.

TU104 GPU contains 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one NVLink link. TU106 GPU contains 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and no NVLink. RTX-OPS is a workload-based metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations weighted by typical frame time usage.

Ray tracing fundamentals: rays are cast from the camera through pixels; BVH acceleration structure reduces intersection tests; denoising improves image quality with fewer rays. Ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections overcome limitations of traditional techniques like shadow maps and screen-space methods.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended June 30, 2018. The report includes unaudited consolidated financial statements. For the three months ended June 30, 2018, total net sales were $52.9 billion, operating income was $3.0 billion, and net income was $2.5 billion. For the six months ended June 30, 2018, net sales were $103.9 billion, operating income was $4.9 billion, and net income was $4.2 billion. Operating segments are North America, International, and AWS. North America sales were $32.2 billion (Q2) and $62.9 billion (six months), International sales were $14.6 billion and $29.5 billion, and AWS sales were $6.1 billion and $11.5 billion. The company adopted new revenue recognition guidance on January 1, 2018, which affected the classification of Prime membership fees and advertising services. On April 12, 2018, Amazon acquired Ring Inc. for approximately $853 million. As of June 30, 2018, cash and cash equivalents were $19.8 billion, and total assets were $134.1 billion. Long-term debt face value was $24.7 billion. The company established a $7.0 billion commercial paper program and an amended $7.0 billion revolving credit facility in April 2018. Income tax provision for the six months ended June 30, 2018 was $361 million, including discrete tax benefits from stock-based compensation. The European Commission ordered recovery of approximately €250 million plus interest for state aid, which Amazon has appealed.

Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is married to Nathalie Guerrero; they have two daughters, Vlaimel and Vlaishel. His father is Hall of Famer Vladimir Guerrero Sr., a former MLB outfielder/DH with 2,590 hits, 2004 AL MVP, and nine All-Star selections. His mother is Riquelma Ramos; she returned to the Dominican Republic with him early in his life. His younger brother Pablo Guerrero is a Rangers minor-league prospect. His half-brother Vladi Miguel Guerrero signed with the Mets. His uncle Wilton Guerrero played in MLB from 1996–2004. His godfather is Hall of Fame pitcher Pedro Martinez. Another uncle, Julio Guerrero, played in the Red Sox minor-league system. Cousins Gabriel Guerrero (former MLB player with the Reds) and Gregory Guerrero (Mets minor-leaguer) also have baseball ties. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. was born in Montreal, Canada, and later moved to the Dominican Republic.

Smith Tower, Seattle’s oldest skyscraper, is automating its manually operated elevators after 103 years. Unico Properties, which purchased the building in 2015, began modernization in June to improve safety, reliability, and accessibility while preserving the elevators’ historic appearance. The Landmarks Preservation Board approved the alterations. At least one elevator operator will be retained for historic significance, but operators will no longer be required as of mid-2018. Hamilton Beale, an operator for 18 years, plans to move back to the East Coast. The building opened in 1914 with eight Otis elevators and was once the tallest building west of the Mississippi.

William Eckels first attended a Parent Cafe at The Opportunity Project (TOP), a nonprofit early education provider for children in poverty, lured by pizza. TOP serves ages 1-5 in three high-poverty areas in Wichita and Derby. A study in the Journal of Research in Childhood Education found TOP students outperformed a control group in academics, social skills, and attendance, with third-graders 19% more likely and eighth-graders 107% more likely to read at grade level. Author Linda Bakken, a Wichita State professor emeritus, stated long-term benefits through eighth grade. Executive director Cornelia Stevens, whose daughter attended TOP, advocates early education as key to reducing poverty. TOP follows a Reggio Emilia philosophy where children choose activities and teachers guide. Eckels, a single father who gained custody of his son after the mother's death, worked low-paying jobs and learned about TOP from a church friend. The program offers scholarships via grants, private donors, and state subsidies, serves about 600 children, and costs nearly $5.3 million annually, funded by public and private sources including an endowment from founder Barry Downing. Parents sign an 85% attendance contract and are connected to community resources. TOP partners with colleges to help parents pursue diplomas or degrees. Parent Cafe workshops use pizza incentives to teach about early childhood research and advocacy. Eckels, inspired, now considers pursuing an education degree to become a teacher.

The plaintiffs, executrices of Diedrick Grafing, appealed a judgment dismissing their complaint against Catharine Heilmann. Grafing had deposited $2,000 in a savings bank in his name in trust for Heilmann, retaining the pass book and drawing the interest during his life. The plaintiffs alleged no present trust was intended; rather, the money was to be distributed after his death according to a letter. Heilmann denied consenting to such terms and claimed the funds as her property. The trial court found for the defendant.

On appeal, the court held the deposit created a valid trust, not a gift. Retention of the bank book and receipt of interest by the depositor were not inconsistent with an intent to create a trust. Payment of part of the principal to the beneficiary was not evidence of a loan; the presumption was it satisfied an antecedent debt, recognizing her title. Even if the money was intended to go to the beneficiary only on the depositor’s death, the transaction was not testamentary because her interest vested at the time of deposit. Any obligation by the beneficiary to pay others must be enforced by those parties directly, not by the executors. The judgment was affirmed with costs.

The Trump administration initiated permanent layoffs (Reductions in Force) of federal workers on the 10th day of a government shutdown. OMB Director Russell Vought announced the RIFs on X, calling them substantial. President Trump stated the layoffs would be "a lot" and "Democrat-oriented," targeting programs favored by Democrats. RIF notices were sent to workers at Treasury, Health and Human Services, and other agencies including Commerce, Education, Energy, EPA, Homeland Security, HUD, and Interior. The 123 reversal pattern is a three-swing price formation indicating a potential trend reversal. In an uptrend, a bearish 123 forms when a swing fails to make a higher high, followed by a break below the prior swing low, confirming a lower low and a descending structure. In a downtrend, a bullish 123 forms when a swing fails to make a lower low, then breaks above the prior swing high, confirming a higher high and a rising structure. A 123 bottom is the bullish pattern in a downtrend. The pattern resembles double tops and bottoms, except the second swing does not reach the prior extreme.

Trading rules: Enter at the close of the bar that breaks point 2 (or next bar), with caution on very tall breakout bars (wait for retest). Stop loss is placed below point 3 for bullish setups or above point 3 for bearish setups, possibly beyond point 1 in volatile markets. Profit target is estimated by measuring the distance from point 2 to the midpoint of a line connecting points 1 and 3, then projecting that distance from the breakout point. Partial profits or trailing stops can be used.

The strategy can be applied to stocks, forex, commodities, and Bitcoin, but for stocks only the bullish 123 is recommended due to unlimited upside. A backtest on gold (GLD) with a time exit of N days showed a profit factor of 2.22 for the bullish reversal after 20 days. The bearish reversal backtest showed weaker performance. The strategy has subjective rules and may be improved with additional parameters.

A rival IoT malware named Hajime has been competing with Mirai, infecting poorly secured devices like cameras, DVRs, and routers. While Mirai's botnet launched a major DDoS attack on Dyn, Hajime has not been observed conducting attacks, and its purpose remains unknown—possibly cybercrime, research, or vigilante action. Hajime appears more widespread but targets a narrower range of devices (ARM architecture), whereas Mirai variants infect multiple platforms. Researchers note an ongoing territorial conflict between the two. Patching vulnerable IoT devices is the recommended solution, but many vendors have not issued patches, so both malware are expected to persist.

The UCLA High Post Rub Offense, successful under John Wooden and used at all levels, emphasizes sound principles, court spacing, and inside/outside attack. It suits teams lacking a strong low post player, leveraging a high post's passing/shooting and a point guard's posting. The 1-4 set is preferred against pressure. The basic action: point guard O1 passes to wing O3, then rubs off high post O5's screen. O3 looks to feed O1 for a layup or post-up; if unavailable, O3 reverses to O5. Execution depends on reading defenders and applying counters. High post rub reads: defender trails (O1 basket cut), denies outside (O1 cuts inside), goes behind (O1 pops out), shows & recovers (O5 slips), switches (O1 clears, O5 rolls or O1 isolates). If O3 can't feed O1, O1 can back screen for O5 for a lob or post isolation. Post play reads: high side (power lay-up), baseline side (baby hook), behind (turn & face triple threat), front (lob), double team (release to elbow or short corner). Phase 2 uses ball reversal down screens for open shots and mismatches. Down screen reads: chases (curl), chases late (basket curl), cheats over (fade), cheats over early (back cut), switches (screen and roll, post/wing isolation), shows & recovers (slip). Automatic counters punish defensive overplay on wing entry, post, or reversal passes. Teaching stresses execution, coordination, footwork, timing, and non-verbal communication, with drills like 2-on-2 and 3-on-3. Game strategies include scouting, staying alert to adjustments, varying alignments, and attacking weak defenders. Teams must be prepared to defend this common offense.

This study examined associations between the maternal gut microbiome, infant gut microbiome (3–6 months), and child gut microbiome (years one and three) and children’s neurodevelopment (ASQ scores at years one, two, and three) in 116 mother-child pairs from the VDAART cohort. Using multinomial regression with reference frames, the maternal gut microbiome showed the strongest predictive power for child neurodevelopment at year one (average Q2 ~0.21 at class level), outperforming infant and child microbiomes. This predictive power diminished for year two and was absent for year three. The infant gut microbiome was weakly associated with year one neurodevelopment, while child gut microbiomes showed limited or no relevance. Shared microbial taxa between maternal and infant gut microbiota sometimes exhibited opposite associations with ASQ domains, indicating different roles. The results underscore the importance of the maternal gut microbiome in early offspring neurodevelopment. Limitations include small sample size and the need for further validation.

The study developed and validated a Fluorescent Immuno-Lectin Assay (FILA) using five lectins (MGL, SNA, MAA, PNA, Gal-3) to measure lubricin glycoforms. Validation included spike-and-recovery, dilution linearity, and cross-validation with quantitative mass spectrometry on synovial fluid (SF) lubricin, showing good agreement. Matched SF and plasma from osteoarthritis (OA) patients revealed SF lubricin levels were 1–3 orders of magnitude higher than plasma, and glycosylation differed: plasma lubricin exhibited higher ratios of MAA, PNA, SNA, and Gal-3 to MGL (Tn-antigen), indicating greater sialylation and less truncation. In plasma from OA patients (n=183) versus controls (n=38), only SNA-binding glycoforms were significantly decreased in OA (p=0.0023); other lectins showed no significant difference. Plasma lubricin glycoforms correlated positively with BMI for Gal-3, MAA, and SNA, and negatively with age for MAA and SNA, while MGL correlated positively with age. The findings indicate that lubricin glycosylation in plasma and SF are distinct, likely reflecting different tissue origins, and that plasma lubricin glycosylation is influenced by age and BMI, with only SNA-detected glycoforms altered in OA plasma.

New observations show 14 of 16 dwarf galaxies orbiting Centaurus A move in a common plane, which does not align with the lambda cold dark matter model’s prediction of random orbits. Study author Marcel Pawlowski suggests this may indicate missing ingredients or flaws in the standard model, calling cosmological simulations into question. However, other astrophysicists, like Mike Boylan-Kolchin, argue the planar orbits could be a statistical fluke, noting the standard model explains the diverse ages and masses of satellites in known planar systems, while alternative theories do not. Another explanation posits that dark matter filaments on larger scales could create such quirks. Scientists agree more observations of distant galaxies are needed to resolve the issue.

This study evaluated pneumococcal transmission among community-dwelling older adults. Using a longitudinal design, 121 individuals aged 60+ from 61 households (no residents under 60) provided saliva samples every two weeks for 10 weeks across two seasons (2020/2021 and 2021/2022). Pneumococcal carriage was detected by qPCR targeting piaB. Overall, 4.8% of samples were positive, and 22.3% of individuals were colonized at least once. Point prevalence was higher among those reporting contact with children (10.4%) than those without (2.4%), especially contact with children under 10 years. The average time to acquisition was 358 days, and mean colonization duration was 17.7 days. Contact with children under 10 increased acquisition risk (hazard ratio 3.0), with daily or frequent contact further elevating risk. Few households had both members colonized, and no clear evidence of adult-to-adult transmission was found. The study concluded that adult carriage is primarily associated with child contact, suggesting adult PCV immunization mainly benefits by directly protecting exposed adults rather than interrupting transmission among adults. Limitations included skewed demographics, the COVID-19 pandemic context, and challenges in serotyping low-density samples due to non-specific assays.

All offensive corner kicks are planned restarts with a designed set play, a designated target area/player, and a proper service kick. Types include: Far Post Corner (traditional, lofted instep drive to far post area, often for a header, with inswinger/outswinger variations); Near Post Corner (directed to a receiver near the near post, waist-high service, for volley/header or redirection); Medium Corner (to areas in front of goal, like 6-, 12-, or 18-yard spots, lofted drive, targeting weak defenders or testing goalkeeper); Top-of-the-Arc Corner (to the farthest penalty area point, brisk ground service, exploiting undefended space); Short Corner (to a teammate within 10 yards, drawing defenders out, then crossing); Skip Header Corner (near-post flick-on header to back post); Direct Score Corner (inswinging kick directly into goal, rarely successful). Coaches select kick taker and target player based on service requirements and heading ability. Teaching progresses from no defenders to game conditions. Coaching tips address floated-ball corners, wind, goalkeeper challenges, double-touch rule, signals, offside, timing runs, and preparing for clearances and counterattacks.

The document details the GHCB protocol for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest–hypervisor communication. An example shows a #VC handler setting the GHCB physical address in MSR, clearing and populating GHCB fields, then the hypervisor handling the VMGEXIT by translating the GHCB address, processing the SW_EXITCODE, updating save state, and resuming the guest. For SEV-ES guests, unplanned NAE events must be avoided before long mode or 32-bit PAE because memory accesses are encrypted; the guest can discover the encryption bit position via CPUID or GHCBInfo.

The SEV-SNP secrets page contains a guest reserved area (offset 0x00a0–0x00ff) used to communicate message sequence numbers (now 64-bit, with upper 32 bits stored in previously reserved bytes) and a version number. An EFI configuration table GUID and structure are defined for communicating the secrets and CPUID pages to the OS.

NAE events trigger a #VC exception; the error code equals the VMEXIT code. The guest inspects the error code, copies state to the GHCB, executes VMGEXIT, and after VMRUN examines results. The document lists supported NAE events and their minimum state. The VALID_BITMAP field indicates which GHCB qwords are valid; its bit position is calculated from the field offset. The guest sets bits for SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, SW_EXITINFO2; the hypervisor sets bits for SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2. SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] non-zero indicates an error; specific codes request exception injection (with EVENTINJ in SW_EXITINFO2), or signal malformed input, unregistered GHCB address, invalid SW_SCRATCH, missing valid bits, invalid input, or hypervisor-specific reasons.

Standard VMGEXIT processing: copy faulting context registers to GHCB, set VALID_BITMAP bits, set SW_EXITCODE and SW_EXITINFO fields, set GHCB MSR, execute VMGEXIT, advance RIP, copy returned GHCB registers to the faulting context. If SW_EXITINFO1[31:0]==1, invoke the requested exception with error code from SW_EXITINFO2.

Specific NAE events:
- IOIO_PROT: guest parses instruction, constructs SW_EXITINFO1, supplies decrypted buffer (GHCB shared buffer at offset 0x800) via SW_SCRATCH for string operations.
- MSR_PROT: guest determines RDMSR/WRMSR and uses appropriate NAE table entry.
- VMMCALL: hypervisor-specific hypercalls; only documented registers are provided if no guest OS support.
- #NPF/MMIO: MMIO ranges must have a reserved bit set in nested page tables to cause #VC. Guest parses instruction, uses MMIO_READ or MMIO_WRITE NAE events, supplies decrypted buffer via SW_SCRATCH, and may issue multiple VMGEXITs.
- Page State Change: uses a structure in the GHCB Shared Buffer with header (cur_entry, end_entry) and entries (GFN, operation, page size, cur_page). Operations: private, shared, PSMASH hint, UNSMASH hint. The hypervisor processes entries, incrementing cur_entry and cur_page on success. Errors are indicated if cur_entry ≤ end_entry, with reason codes in SW_EXITINFO2 (interrupted, invalid header/entry, PSMASH/UNSMASH failure, already in requested state, RMP overlap, other error).
- SNP Guest Request: requires shared request and response pages. Hypervisor translates GPAs to SPAs, assigns response page to firmware via RMPUPDATE, invokes SNP_GUEST_REQUEST, reclaims page. Sequence numbers must be validated. SW_EXITINFO2 holds return code; 0x0000000200000000 requests retry. Extended Guest Request adds certificate data pages; a table at offset 0 of DATA GPA lists GUID, offset, length. If insufficient pages, RBX returns required count and SW_EXITINFO2=0x0000000100000000.
- AP Creation: allows creating/adding or destroying/removing vCPUs at a specified VMPL level. Guest uses RMPADJUST to mark a VMSA page. Create/Add can be pending INIT-SIPI or immediate run. Hypervisor validates VMPL and APIC ID, uses SPA of VMSA. Multi-VMPL requires hypervisor feature advertisement.
- #HV Doorbell Page: actions GET_PREFERRED, SET, QUERY, CLEAR. Used with Restricted Injection to register a doorbell page for #HV exception delivery.
- #HV Send IPI: sends IPI using SW_EXITINFO1 formatted as x2APIC ICR.
- #HV Timer: SET/GET actions using APIC timer registers and mask.
- APIC ID List: guest supplies contiguous shared pages; hypervisor returns count and APIC ID entries. If insufficient pages, RAX returns required count.
- SNP Run VMPL: requests running vCPU at a different VMPL, each with its own VMSA and GHCB.
- SNP TIO Guest Request: similar to Guest Request, with additional non-optional unencrypted data (PCI ID, MMIO range, TDISP status). Data pages optionally provide nonce for measurements; returned data includes measurements, certificates, TDISP attestation report.
- Secure AVIC: REGISTER_BACKING_PAGE and UNREGISTER_BACKING_PAGE actions to manage a private APIC backing page per vCPU.
- Termination Request: guest requests termination with reason code set and code in SW_EXITINFO1, and optional info in SW_EXITINFO2.
- Unsupported Event: used for NAEs not in the negotiated protocol version.

Guest identification of SEV-ES support uses CPUID properties: ECX[31] set, EAX[1] set, EBX[5:0] encryption bit position, EBX[11:6] physical address reduction.

AP booting under SEV-ES: hypervisor cannot modify measured register state. Solutions include using a memory location at the reset vector to hold the target address, or a predetermined initial CS:IP location. The hypervisor runs the AP with initial registers on first reset. For subsequent resets, the AP issues an AP Reset Hold request (via NAE event or MSR protocol) to halt; upon SIPI, the hypervisor completes the hold, and the AP transitions to real mode and jumps to the SIPI vector. An AP jump table (4K, encrypted, page-aligned) is used to communicate the reset vector from UEFI to OS. Under SEV-SNP with AP Creation, the guest uses VMGEXIT 0x8000_0013 to create/update AP state via VMSA pages, eliminating the need for AP Reset Hold and AP jump table. vCPU hotplug is supported.

NMI handling: hypervisor must not intercept IRET but must intercept #DB. Guest issues “NMI Complete” message via VMGEXIT when ready. An example uses TF flag before IRET to trigger #DB intercept, where the handler clears NMI state and sends the complete message.

Debug registers: if DebugVirtualization is supported, hardware saves/restores debug state; hypervisor clears intercepts. Otherwise, hypervisor intercepts DR7; guest caches writes and returns cached value on reads.

SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Restricted Injection: host delivers events via #HV exception using a doorbell page. The doorbell page contains PendingEvent (16 bits: NoFurtherSignal, reserved, #MC, NMI, vector) and NoEoiRequired (byte). Host behavior: presents highest-priority ready interrupt by writing vector; sets NoFurtherSignal and sends #HV if vector was zero and NoFurtherSignal was zero. If vector was non-zero, overwrites without new #HV. Sets NoEoiRequired if no other interrupts ready. For non-maskable events, sets appropriate bit and NoFurtherSignal, sends #HV if NoFurtherSignal was zero. Host observes guest clearing vector as acknowledgment, marks interrupt in service. Observes clearing NoEoiRequired as implicit EOI. Guest behavior: on #HV, atomically exchanges PendingEvent to retrieve vector and zero it; processes interrupt; for EOI, atomically exchanges zero with NoEoiRequired; if previous was zero, performs explicit APIC EOI via VMGEXIT. For non-maskable events with IF=0, atomically clears event flags and NoFurtherSignal while leaving vector unchanged. Guest must validate vectors. HLT convention: guest executes HLT with interrupts disabled; if host sees HLT intercept with pending events, it re-enters guest; guest then examines interrupt state as if #HV received.

In the AEGEAN study, 1162 subjects initiating apixaban for atrial fibrillation were randomized to a Primary Standard of Care (SOC) group (583) or an Additional Educational Program group (579). At 24 weeks, 1054 subjects completed the visit; 108 discontinued, mainly due to withdrawal of consent, adverse events (AE), serious AE, or death. Mean adherence to treatment at 24 weeks was 91.64% in the Primary SOC group and 91.88% in the Additional Educational Program group, with no significant difference. Persistence at 24 weeks was 91.7% and 91.3%, respectively. From 24 to 48 weeks, subjects were re-randomized to Secondary SOC (263) or Continued Additional Educational Program (261). At 48 weeks, 1003 subjects completed the visit; 50 discontinued. Adherence from week 24 to 48 was 87.59% in Primary SOC, 87.51% in Secondary SOC, and 88.41% in Continued Additional Educational Program, with no significant differences. Adherence decreased significantly over time in both groups. Predictive factors for non-adherence at 24 weeks in the Primary SOC group included alcohol consumption, technical occupations, and permanent atrial fibrillation, while higher MMSE score reduced non-adherence. At 48 weeks, non-adherence in Primary SOC decreased with MMSE score; in the Additional Educational Program group, non-adherence increased with age and in VKA-naïve subjects. Safety outcomes, including AEs and bleeding events, were similar between groups. The study concluded that adherence and persistence were high, and the educational program did not provide additional benefit.

The Triangle & Two defense uses a triangle zone and two chasers to deny outstanding shooters. The Double Stack offense counters by positioning posts at mid post and shooters behind them, giving shooters a head start. The basic option is a pop out off a screen for a jump shot. Against a late chaser, the shooter curls; if the chaser cheats out, the shooter fades to the corner or back cuts. On a switch, the screener posts up. Entries include crossing under the basket, fake crossing, and single/double screens. Continuity options flow into base screens or side screens. Success requires execution, coordination, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Drills include 4-on-4 shell and scrimmaging. Strategies: scout opponents, anticipate reads, vary alignments, and attack weak defenders.

This study used electronic health record data from over 8 million patients to compare the 2009 and 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equations for estimating glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and diagnosing chronic kidney disease (CKD). The 2009 equation included a race adjustment for Black patients, while the 2021 equation removed it. The study aimed to assess whether the 2021 equation reduced disparities in timing of CKD diagnosis and staging discordance between Black and non-Black patients.

Among 8,080,889 patients with serum creatinine results, 15.5% were Black. CKD (stages 3a–5) was identified in 15.3% using either equation. Significant staging discordance was found, particularly for Black patients. Nearly 50% of Black patients meeting stage 3a criteria with the 2021 equation did not meet CKD criteria with the 2009 equation; 50% of Black patients with stage 3b by the 2021 equation were stage 3a by the 2009 equation. Approximately 40% of stage 4 cases in Black patients were discordant. In contrast, 99% of non-Black patients staged as 4 by the 2021 equation were also stage 4 by the 2009 equation.

The 2021 equation identified CKD earlier for 24% of Black patients versus 0.7% of non-Black patients. Multivariate logistic regression showed Black patients were 126 times more likely to have an increased CKD stage with the 2021 equation (OR 126, 95% CI 120–133). Earlier identification with the 2009 equation was associated with higher odds of a higher stage with the 2021 equation (OR 5.23). Included social determinants of health (income, household size, distance to close ties, marital status) were not significantly associated with staging discordance. The study used Truveta data, excluded patients with acute kidney injury or polycystic kidney disease, and required at least three serum creatinine values over >90 days. Limitations include potential incomplete capture of events outside member health systems and use of the Elixhauser comorbidity index without validation for this population.

President Obama addressed the nation on Syria. He recounted that a civil war began after peaceful protests against Assad's regime, with over 100,000 killed and millions displaced. The U.S. provided humanitarian aid and supported a political solution but resisted military action. The situation changed on August 21, when Assad's government used chemical weapons, gassing over a thousand people, including children. He described the horrific images and noted that chemical weapons are banned by international agreement, which the U.S. Senate approved in 1997 and 189 nations joined.

He stated that no one disputes chemical weapons were used, and evidence shows the Assad regime was responsible: chemical weapons personnel prepared, gasmasks were distributed, rockets were fired from regime-controlled areas into opposition neighborhoods, and samples tested positive for sarin. He argued that failing to act would allow Assad to continue using such weapons, erode prohibitions, endanger troops and allies, and embolden Iran. Therefore, he determined a targeted military strike is in U.S. national security interests to deter and degrade Assad's chemical weapons capability.

Although he possesses authority to order strikes, he believed it right to seek Congressional approval, strengthening democracy and unity. He acknowledged war-weariness and promised no American boots on the ground, no open-ended action like Iraq or Afghanistan, and no prolonged air campaign. The strike would be targeted. He addressed concerns: it would not be a "pinprick" but a meaningful message; retaliation risks are limited; involvement is necessary because inaction would strengthen extremists; and diplomatic efforts had been tried but failed.

He then noted recent encouraging signs: due to the credible threat of U.S. force and talks with President Putin, Russia indicated willingness to push Assad to give up chemical weapons. Assad admitted possessing them and said he would join the Chemical Weapons Convention. He cautioned it is too early to tell if this will succeed, but it has potential to remove the threat without force. He asked Congress to postpone the authorization vote to pursue diplomacy, sending Secretary Kerry to meet Russian counterparts and working with allies on a UN Security Council resolution requiring Assad to surrender and destroy his chemical weapons under international control. The military would maintain pressure and be ready if diplomacy fails.

He concluded by stating that the U.S. has been the anchor of global security, and that while America is not the world's policeman, when modest effort and risk can stop children from being gassed and make Americans safer, the nation should act.

The Larisons appealed a summary judgment in favor of Public Water Supply District #1 in their personal injury suit. Mrs. Larison was injured when a water meter lid slid off its well while she mowed. They argued the dangerous-condition exception to sovereign immunity applied. The appellate court reversed summary judgment on the claim that the water operator negligently failed to properly secure the lid, finding a genuine factual dispute because a jury could disbelieve the operator’s routine and infer negligence. The court affirmed summary judgment on the claim that the Water District knew or should have known of a dangerous condition, as there was no evidence the mower caused the lid to loosen, only speculation. It also affirmed summary judgment on the res ipsa loquitur theory, because the Water District did not have exclusive control over the meter lid, which was accessible to tampering. The case was remanded solely on the operator-negligence theory.

The Strategic National Stockpile is a $7 billion government repository of drugs and supplies for bioterrorism, nuclear attacks, infectious disease outbreaks (including "Disease X"), and other public health emergencies. It contains antibiotics, vaccines for smallpox and anthrax, antivirals, and nerve agent antidotes. Created in 1999, its mission expanded to include natural disasters and emerging threats. Stored in secret warehouses (at least six), it can deploy a "12-hour push package" of 50 tons of materiel. For nearly two decades, the CDC managed the $575 million program. The Trump administration plans to shift oversight to the ASPR office within HHS, aiming to streamline decision-making and create efficiencies. Proponents say it will coordinate medical responses. Critics, including public health officials and bipartisan lawmakers, worry the move could disrupt state and local distribution relationships, politicize product selection by favoring expensive specialized drugs over broad-use medications like antibiotics, and question if it will improve safety. ASPR head Robert Kadlec says the change is about efficiency and visibility, not CDC performance, and that the program needs more funding. Congress has expressed concerns and urged a strong CDC role. The current CDC director says emergency response will not change regardless of location.

This study investigated the association between COVID-19 vaccination and audiovestibular conditions (hearing loss, vertigo, tinnitus) using two data sources: spontaneous reports to SAEFVIC in Victoria, Australia, and a self-controlled case series (SCCS) analysis of general practice data from the POLAR platform. The analysis included adults aged 18–65 (SAEFVIC) or 20–65 (POLAR) with symptom onset or presentation within 42 days post-vaccination, between January 2021 and March 2023.

SAEFVIC received 678 eligible spontaneous reports. Reporting rates per 100,000 doses were higher for adenovirus vector vaccine than mRNA vaccines for all audiovestibular conditions combined, vertigo, and tinnitus. No statistically significant difference in hearing loss reporting rates by vaccine type was found. Reporting rates were higher after dose 1 than dose 2 for the adenovirus vector vaccine, but not for mRNA vaccines.

The SCCS analysis found an increased relative incidence of all audiovestibular conditions in the 42-day risk window following both adenovirus vector and mRNA vaccines. Specifically, there was an increased relative incidence of vertigo following mRNA vaccines, and an increased relative incidence of tinnitus following both adenovirus vector and mRNA vaccines. No increased relative incidence of hearing loss was observed for either vaccine type.

The authors note that COVID-19 infection is a potential confounder, and that the SCCS dataset may not capture all vaccinations, possibly underestimating relative incidence. They conclude that there was an increase in vertigo presentations following mRNA vaccines, an increase in tinnitus presentations following both mRNA and adenovirus vector vaccines, and no increase in hearing loss presentations following any COVID-19 vaccine.

The lecture covers the Higgs mechanism. The Higgs boson was discovered in 2012, but the theoretical proposal dates to the mid-1960s by Peter Higgs and others to give masses to gauge bosons (W and Z) and fermions. A massive spin-1 gauge field requires mass terms that break local gauge invariance. Instead of adding explicit mass terms, one can break the local gauge symmetry spontaneously. Spontaneous symmetry breaking is illustrated by a pen bending or dropping to its ground state, breaking rotational symmetry. In a toy model, a complex scalar field with a potential where mu^2 < 0 yields a vacuum expectation value v, breaking the symmetry. Expanding around the minimum gives fields h and chi (Goldstone boson). The Lagrangian then contains a mass term for the gauge field proportional to the coupling e times v, and a mass term for h, while chi is massless. Choosing the unitarity gauge removes the Goldstone boson, which is “eaten” by the gauge boson, providing its longitudinal polarization and mass. The result is a massive gauge boson and one real massive scalar field. For the Standard Model with SU(2) × U(1) gauge group, a complex scalar doublet (four degrees of freedom) with mu^2 < 0 acquires a vacuum expectation value, spontaneously breaking the symmetry. Coupling to gauge fields yields mass terms: W boson mass is proportional to the SU(2) coupling times v/2; Z boson mass involves both couplings; the photon remains massless. The weak mixing angle relates W and Z masses. Three Goldstone bosons are absorbed by W+, W−, and Z, giving them mass. One remaining scalar is the Higgs boson. This understanding from the 1960s–70s was confirmed by the 2012 discovery.

The document describes GHCB negotiation for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. The hypervisor sets VMCB offset 0x00a0 with a GHCBInfo value indicating supported protocol version and the SEV page table encryption bit. For SEV-ES, the guest uses CPUID instructions that cause #VC exceptions; the #VC handler reads MSR 0xc001_0130 to extract maximum/minimum protocol versions and the encryption bit. For SEV-SNP, the guest uses CPUID leaf 0x8000001f and the MSR protocol to obtain the encryption bit and negotiate version. The guest then allocates a GHCB page, marks it shared, and writes its GPA to MSR 0xc001_0130.

A VMGEXIT example shows the guest #VC handler setting GHCB fields, executing VMGEXIT, and the hypervisor processing the exit based on SW_EXITCODE, updating the GHCB save state area, and resuming the guest.

The document lists supported NAE events, including IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV doorbell page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC backing page, and Termination Request. For Page State Change, the guest supplies a structure in the GHCB shared buffer to request page state changes (private/shared) with operations like PSMASH/UNSMASH hints. SNP Guest Request uses shared request and response pages for firmware requests, with sequence number handling. AP Creation allows an SEV-SNP guest to create, update, or destroy vCPUs at specified VMPL levels using VMSA pages. The #HV doorbell page, used with Restricted Injection, contains PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields; the host writes interrupt vectors and may signal #HV, while the guest acknowledges by atomically exchanging PendingEvent and can optimize EOI via NoEoiRequired. AP booting challenges are addressed with AP jump tables and the AP Reset Hold NAE event or MSR protocol. Secure AVIC uses a private backing page per vCPU, registered via NAE event.

Disparities in basic education quality in China are exacerbated by a siphon effect, where students and teachers move from economically depressed areas to those with superior resources, such as from Hebei to Beijing and Tianjin. To address this, education groups are formed, typically organized around a prestigious core school with ordinary schools as branch campuses. The core school sends administrators and anchor teachers to provide guidance and training, and teacher exchanges aim to improve professional levels and resource availability. Outcomes include enhanced overall education quality through resource sharing, management interchange, and coordinated research, supported by government policies (e.g., Shanghai's laws on funding and appraisal). Groups unify resources, facilitate collaborative teaching and teacher rotation, and use quality assessment centers to standardize evaluations. Teacher job satisfaction and professional competence improve: teachers report stronger identity, harmonious relationships, and professional growth through anchor teachers' demonstrations and research activities. Surveys show over 90% of teachers believe their abilities improved. Student development is facilitated by spreading advanced educational philosophies, emphasizing higher-order thinking, and enabling access to diverse courses and extracurricular activities, as illustrated by a joint maker culture festival. Education groups also relieve "school picking" fever by making prestigious schools more accessible, benefiting 90% of students in one district. Problems include the imposition of core school culture erasing non-core schools' individualities, difficulty for ordinary schools to apply prestigious schools' philosophies due to disparities in teacher and student abilities, and core school management lacking motivation because of resource dispersion, financial burdens, and government evaluation pressure. Suggestions: establish equal, democratic relationships via a standing committee of school leaders and improved communication; strengthen team building through incentive systems for teacher rotation, training at core schools, attracting qualified teachers, and online resource platforms; and win government support through funding, teacher recognition, and special financing for principals. The conclusion states that education groups are a form of deep contractual cooperation aimed at educational equity, but further study is needed on maintaining school distinctiveness and sustaining group motivation.

This study investigated perivascular space (PVS) burden in 467 people with various epilepsy types (temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis, TLE-HS; MRI-negative temporal lobe epilepsy, TLE-NEG; extratemporal focal epilepsy, ETLE; idiopathic generalized epilepsy, IGE) and 473 healthy controls. PVS were segmented from T1-weighted MRI using the PINGU algorithm, and volume fractions (PVS-VF) were calculated in white matter (WM) and basal ganglia (BG). All epilepsy subtypes had significantly higher PVS-VF in the BG compared to controls (effect sizes 0.95–1.37), with no differences in WM after accounting for age and sex. The TLE-HS group showed PVS asymmetry, with larger PVS on the contralateral side; this was not observed in other groups. No association was found between PVS-VF and illness duration. The authors conclude that PVS in the BG are enlarged in epilepsy and that longitudinal studies are needed to determine causality.

This document describes AMD's Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, an optional extension to System Encryption, SEV, and SNP that offloads page migration in tiered memory systems. TMPM copies page content and updates IOMMU virtual-to-physical mappings, enabling movement of frequently accessed data to faster memory tiers. It solves two key challenges: pausing DMA traffic during migration to allow safe movement of pages actively used by I/O devices, and acting as a trusted agent to migrate pages owned by guests using SEV or SNP.

The TMPM engine is accessed via a ring buffer interface. Software checks the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register to determine support. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement. The document defines two primary commands: PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates hypervisor-owned or default pages, supports concurrent DMA by coordinating with IOMMU host page tables, and can be used in both SNP and non-SNP systems. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages, requiring source pages in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state and destination pages in a new Pre-Migration state. After migration, destination pages take the source state, and source pages become Pre-Migration. A Pre-Migration state uses a platform-specific ASID and cannot be validated by a guest.

Commands support moving up to 128 pages per command via a Page Migration List. Multi-page commands are more efficient. The ring buffer holds 16-byte command entries; a single 4KB page holds 256 commands. Driver initialization involves checking ENGINE_READY, setting the ring buffer physical address (4KB-aligned, 1–255 contiguous pages), configuring queue parameters, setting write pointer to zero, hooking interrupts, and setting DRIVER_INITIALIZED. The firmware validates configuration and sets DRIVER_INIT_COMPLETE. The PS_ASID_VAL is reported in PM_ReadPtr after initialization. Shutdown requires waiting for queue empty or paused, clearing DRIVER_INITIALIZED, and cleanup.

The ring buffer supports pause/resume via PM_RBCtl[PAUSE]. Interrupt sources include: RBWritePtr_Err (tail pointer out of range), RBMem_Err (read error), QfreeIntStat (queue empty), QthreshIntStat (low-water mark), IntOnError (command error), and IntOnComplt (command completion). Interrupts can be enabled per command or queue-wide. Firmware may terminate the ring buffer under certain circumstances, setting RB_Terminated.

System physical addresses (SPAs) must be 4KB-aligned (except host page table entry addresses, which are 8-byte aligned). When SMEE or SME-MK is enabled, encryption information is encoded in SPAs. The document details command formats, status codes (e.g., PM_SUCCESS, PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS, PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE), and sub-statuses. Error handling covers command rejection, partial success, ring buffer errors reported in PM_Status, and hardware errors reported via MCA. Non-migratable data structures include IOMMU memory structures, vIOMMU pinned memory, and the ring buffer itself. TMPM firmware can be reloaded; the process varies by EPYC family, requiring pausing operations, tearing down the ring buffer, and using a BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol. Reload firmware must be the same or greater version.
