The passage discusses the use of gamification and game-based learning in academic education, based on four projects at the Institute of Pedagogy, University of Wrocław. It first outlines that higher education must provide knowledge, skills, and competences, and that the knowledge society and students' familiarity with games make innovative techniques like gamification crucial. Gamification uses game mechanics to increase motivation and dedication, requiring clear aims, feedback, fun, and competition. Game structure includes winning conditions, aims, actions, obstacles, and rules.

Four projects are presented:
1. Kulturalny Wrocław: a location-based game combining cultural education and IT. Students located cultural sites, solved riddles, and completed a crossword. It was well-received for outdoor learning, independence, and socializing, though some questioned efficiency. It required low costs and simple logistics.
2. Gamification in career management: a 5-day seminar with a sci-fi plot, missions, point systems, badges, and prizes, aiming to boost career management skills. Students showed high dedication, fast integration, and passed an exam well. Instructors noted high preparation effort, suggesting such programs are effective only if repeated.
3. Entrepreneurship project: a location-based game where teams completed quests to earn coins and minimize props, ending with tax payment. It was praised for socializing, combining movement and intellect, and developing soft skills. Competition and internet access received ambivalent evaluations. Weak points included weather dependence and unfamiliar terrain.
4. Learning through games: a LARP game where students played adventurers with character cards, including traitors, to develop soft skills. Students with prior RPG experience enjoyed it more; novices struggled with role assumption and complex rules. Educational goals were achieved, but complexity and lack of preparation lowered satisfaction. Organizers found it time-consuming and recommended pilot sessions and multiple runs.

The summary concludes that simple, clear-rules location-based games integrate well into curricula, while complex games suit subsidized projects for competence enhancement. Games should consider students' experience, topic, time, and costs. Overly long or complex games reduce satisfaction. Using city spaces and students' ICT skills is beneficial. Longer games require socializing activities and tutorials.

The New Jersey Supreme Court considered two consolidated appeals from denials of applications for costs and counsel fees under N.J.S. 2A:15-53, a provision of the Anti-Injunction Act. In the “strike case,” the employer obtained a temporary restraint and later an interlocutory injunction against mass picketing. The Appellate Division reversed the injunction solely on procedural grounds (delay in decision, lack of prompt findings, overly broad language) but expressly found that the employer had a substantive basis for injunctive relief. In the “arbitration case,” the employer sued to enjoin arbitration of a discharged striker’s grievance; the Appellate Division held the matter arbitrable and dissolved the restraint. The union and individual sought costs and counsel fees in both cases; the trial court denied them.

The Supreme Court affirmed. It held that the arbitration case did not fall within the scope of the Anti-Injunction Act because it was essentially a declaratory judgment action about arbitrability, not a suit to enjoin coercive labor activity. As to the strike case, the court interpreted the counsel fee provision: under the prior Westinghouse decision, mandatory fees are required only when the suit was unsuccessful on the merits, i.e., the plaintiff was not entitled to an injunction. Because the Appellate Division had found a substantive basis for relief and the reversal was for procedural violations not caused by the plaintiff, the suit was not “wrongfully brought,” and fees were not mandatory. The denials were affirmed. The court noted that the union could reapply for statutory trial costs as the prevailing party. Costs were awarded to the employer in the arbitration case only.

The Sansa® Fuze™ is a portable digital audio/video player featuring a 1.9” color screen, digital FM tuner (if applicable), built-in microphone, and a microSDHC™ card slot. It supports MP3, WAV, WMA, secure WMA, and audiobook formats. Video playback is compatible with MPEG4 (SP) QCIF+ 20fps, with additional formats supported via the Sansa Media Converter software. Photos are supported after conversion and transfer through the same software. The player includes an integrated FM radio, voice recording, and a rechargeable battery providing up to 24 hours of audio or 5 hours of video playback. A Hold switch prevents accidental operation, and the power switch turns the device on/off or resets it. The thumbwheel navigates menus and adjusts volume.

Music, audiobooks, and recordings are played from the Music menu, with options for repeat, shuffle, MusicEQ, adding/removing songs from a Go List, rating, and deleting. Audiobooks offer chapter mode and speed control. Videos are played from the Video menu, with options to add bookmarks, rate, adjust brightness, and delete. Photos and slideshows are viewed from the Photos menu; slideshow settings include shuffle, loop, slide duration, and music selection from a Go List. FM radio listening includes manual and auto preset scanning, with up to 30 presets, and region/mode settings. Voice recordings are made via the built-in microphone. Files are transferred by drag-and-drop or Windows Media Player for music, and via Sansa Media Converter for photos and videos. The player can be formatted directly or from a computer, which deletes all content. Firmware updates are available from the SanDisk website. The device is intended for home and personal use, with copying and commercial use of copyrighted material prohibited by law.

The Turing architecture features a new Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) design with 64 FP32 Cores and 64 INT32 Cores per SM, supporting concurrent execution of FP32 and INT32 operations. Each SM includes eight mixed-precision Tensor Cores and one RT Core. The SM is partitioned into four processing blocks, each with 16 FP32 Cores, 16 INT32 Cores, two Tensor Cores, a warp scheduler, and a dispatch unit. A combined 96 KB L1 data cache/shared memory is configurable as 64 KB/32 KB or 32 KB/64 KB. Turing adds a second parallel execution unit for integer instructions, providing an effective 36% additional throughput for floating point. The unified L1/shared memory design improves bandwidth and latency, contributing to a 50% improvement in delivered performance per CUDA core over Pascal.

Turing Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 precision modes, accelerating matrix-matrix multiplication for deep learning training and inference. TU102 contains 576 Tensor Cores; each performs up to 64 FP16 FMA operations per clock. Tensor Cores enable AI-based NGX features: Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) produces higher quality output with lower input sample counts, achieving up to 2x performance over Pascal; DLSS 2X mode approaches 64x supersampling quality. Other NGX features include InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Turing introduces RT Cores for hardware-accelerated ray tracing, performing BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection tests. This enables real-time ray tracing in a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization and ray tracing. RT Cores offload the SM, providing up to 10x ray tracing performance over Pascal. Ray tracing supports physically correct reflections, shadows, and ambient occlusion.

The memory subsystem uses GDDR6 memory, delivering 14 Gbps signaling rates and 20% power efficiency improvement over GDDR5X. TU102 has 6 MB L2 cache, double the prior generation. Lossless memory compression improvements yield 50% higher effective bandwidth over Pascal. The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, DSC 1.2, HDR, and tone mapping. The video engine adds HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 decode; NVENC encoder supports 8K encode with bitrate savings. VirtualLink via USB-C provides power, display, and data for VR headsets through a single connector. NVLink replaces SLI bridges, providing 25 GB/sec per direction per link (TU102 has two links, TU104 one).

Mesh Shading introduces Task and Mesh Shaders with cooperative thread models, enabling more efficient geometry processing and higher object counts. Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows shading rate to vary per 16x16 pixel region, supporting content adaptive shading, motion adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading (TSS) decouples shading from screen space, storing shading values in texture space for reuse, improving temporal stability and efficiency. Multi-View Rendering (MVR) supports up to four views per pass, expanding Pascal's Simultaneous Multi-Projection.

Turing GPUs include TU102 (72 SMs, 4608 CUDA Cores, 576 Tensor Cores, 72 RT Cores, 384-bit memory interface), TU104 (48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 256-bit), and TU106 (36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, 256-bit, no NVLink). Tesla T4 (TU104-based) delivers up to 130 TOPS INT8 and 260 TOPS INT4 inference performance, with up to 40X higher inference performance and 50X energy efficiency over CPU-based inferencing.

RTX-OPS is a workload-based metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations weighted by typical usage in hybrid rendering: Tensor 20%, FP32 80%, RT 40%, INT32 28%.

Ray tracing uses BVH acceleration structures and denoising filtering to reduce required rays. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection. Hybrid rendering uses rasterization for primary visibility and ray tracing for secondary rays. Denoising algorithms reduce the number of rays needed per pixel.

Eddie Woo, a Sydney maths teacher, gained fame through his YouTube channel "Wootube" and a series of awards. In January 2018, Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull named him Australia's Local Hero. He was also a top 10 finalist for the 2018 Global Teacher Prize, though the winner was Andria Zafirakou from the UK. The NSW Department of Education appointed him a 'master teacher' for maths innovation, requiring him to travel across the state to mentor students and teachers while retaining his position at Cherrybrook Technology High School, where he teaches a year 12 extension class each morning. His online presence began in 2012 when he filmed lessons for a seriously ill student; his channel now has over 200,000 subscribers and 12 million views. Education officials praise his ability to explain complex maths, likening him to Julius Sumner Miller. He views students who claim they "don't do maths" as a personal mission. His rising profile has downsides: his brother Kevin Woo calls it a "double-edged sword," noting the busier schedule keeps Eddie from his day job and family. Eddie says he feels no pressure, only tired legs, and enjoys sharing his love of maths. During a regional tour, he drew large, enthusiastic crowds.

A Harvard poll shows 65% of millennials favor Democrats, 33% Republicans. Only 14% say the country is on the right track. Trump's approval is 25% among them, down 12 points among young Republicans. 67% see internal threats as greatest, naming Trump, "ourselves," and racism. 61% support stricter gun laws.

This retrospective cohort study used the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project National Inpatient Sample (HCUP-NIS) database from 2017–2019 to examine the association between perinatal mood disorders and peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) and other cardiac events. Among over 2.2 million hospitalizations, 7.4% had a mood disorder diagnosis. Patients with mood disorders had a higher incidence of PPCM (0.12% vs 0.05%, p<0.001) and composite adverse cardiac events (0.36% vs 0.14%, p<0.001). After adjusting for demographic and clinical confounders, mood disorders remained independently associated with PPCM (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.36, 95% CI 1.03–1.80), the composite cardiac outcome (aOR 1.57, 95% CI 1.37–1.81), and pulmonary edema (aOR 1.62, 95% CI 1.39–1.89). No significant association with maternal death was found. The study concludes that perinatal mood disorders are associated with increased rates of PPCM and other cardiac events.

Charlie Alliston, 18, was riding a fixed-wheel track bicycle without a front brake on Old Street, London, on 12 February 2016, when he collided with Kim Briggs, 44, a mother of two, who was crossing the road during her lunch break. Alliston was travelling at about 20mph. The bike, a Planet X model, was not lawfully allowed on the road without a front brake. Mrs Briggs suffered two skull fractures and brain bleeding, and died on 19 February. The Old Bailey heard that Alliston posted online comments under the name 'CharlieFxckingA' blaming the victim, stating she stepped into the road while looking at her phone, ignored his warnings, and that he could not avoid her. He also wrote on a cycling forum that the collision was her fault. Prosecutors said reconstructions showed he could have stopped in time with a front brake. Alliston had removed the front brake from a previous bike and tweeted about it in 2015. He bought the Planet X bike in January 2016. The prosecution argues his riding was unlawful and dangerous, and that he is guilty of manslaughter. Alliston denies manslaughter and causing bodily harm by wanton or furious driving.

Central Huron Council heard a presentation from Meighan Wark, Huron County Acting CAO, proposing renovations to bring Clinton Library to accreditation and improve services. In 2015, 11 Huron County Library branches earned accreditation under Ontario Public Library Guidelines, but Clinton failed due to accessibility and square footage issues. Wark said renovations would help achieve accreditation and provide community upgrades. The county provides staff, materials, furniture, equipment, and services; the municipality provides the building, maintenance, and utilities. Standards from the Ontario Public Library Guidelines for rural county systems require minimum square footage and accessible features like lower shelves and wider aisles. Clinton Library lacked full accessibility and sufficient space to deliver full services. General prerequisites include adequate space for the population served, attractiveness, open layout, and reflecting community needs. Wark outlined a component approach: using standards documents, the county and municipality determine desired components, then design a facility with circulation desks, technology space, and flexible areas. Next steps: agree on components based on population, then work with an architect on draft drawings for council and community review. Mayor Ginn asked about provincial funding; Wark said a shovel-ready project would ease grant requests. If the municipality commits to changes, the county library will invest in the interior to match, similar to Huron East’s investment. Discussions will continue.

Elijah Brown scored 27 points, including 17 of New Mexico’s final 19, in a 78-73 win over Boise State. Brown made 13 of 14 free throws. Obij Ajet and Damien Jefferson each scored 14 points. Chandler Hutchison scored a career-high 31 for Boise State. New Mexico took control with a late first-half run. Boise State closed to 76-73 with 19.6 seconds left, but Brown’s free throws sealed it. The win tightens the conference race: Boise State, Colorado State, and Nevada all have four losses. New Mexico made 22 free throws to Boise State’s 13. Tim Williams missed his fourth straight game with a foot injury.

The speaker stated he would trade his individual award for the Stanley Cup and credited his teammates for his achievement. He acknowledged the loss was tough, praised the opposing team for deserving the win, and noted home ice advantage played a role. He reflected on playoff lessons about preparation, aggression, and hard work. He understood being booed in New Jersey, saying the award he received was not the ultimate goal. He congratulated an opponent as the best player since Patrick retired. Looking ahead, the team will take a one-game-at-a-time approach. He expressed sadness, as his main motivation was to win the Cup for his ailing mother, but he will move on.

Preempt announced new technology integrations for its Behavioral Firewall at RSA 2017. Data integrations include Okta, Azure Active Directory, and VPN gateways; enforcement integrations include SecureAuth, RSA SecurID, Duo, Google Authenticator, and HP Aruba ClearPass. These provide deeper context for internal network threat detection and more options to automatically stop threats. The Preempt Behavioral Firewall combines User and Entity Behavioral Analytics (UEBA) with adaptive response to protect against security breaches, malicious insiders, and risky behavior. The company says the integrations enable granular policies to block, notify, or challenge users to verify identity.

In card identification mode, the host resets cards, validates voltage, identifies cards, and requests RCA using the CMD line. CMD0 is a software reset that sets cards to Idle State, except those in Inactive State. After power-on or CMD0, cards are in Idle State with default RCA=0x0000, 400KHz clock, and default driver strength (3.3V: DSR if supported, highest current; 1.8V: type B driver). In UHS-II Mode, CMD0 does not clear RCA, keeping Device ID. The host issues CMD0 with assumed voltage, then CMD8 to verify operating condition. CMD8’s VHS field indicates supplied voltage; only one bit set. If the card can operate, it echoes voltage and check pattern; otherwise, no response and stays idle. CMD8 is mandatory before first ACMD41 for SDHC/SDXC cards, and its receipt indicates host support for Physical Layer Version 2.00 or later.

D.C. police to charge 12 Turkish security agents (7 felonies, 5 misdemeanors) for violence during Turkish president's visit. Two men arrested: Sinan Narin (aggravated assault) and Eyup Yildirim (assault, aggravated assault) for May 16 altercation outside ambassador's residence. U.S. criticized Turkey after Erdogan's forces broke up protest.

On Wednesday, May 30, 2018, U.S. stocks rebounded, with banks and energy companies surging and smaller companies making record gains. The recovery followed Italy's prime minister nominee saying there were "new possibilities" to form a government, easing fears of snap elections. The S&P 500 rose 1.3%, the Dow 1.3%, and the Nasdaq 0.9%. The Russell 2000 jumped 1.5% to a record high. Trade tensions continued as China criticized U.S. tariff threats and U.S.-EU talks occurred. Italian stocks and bonds rose, the euro gained. U.S. bond yields increased, helping bank stocks. Oil prices climbed, with U.S. crude up 2.2% to $68.21. Precious metals edged higher.

Apple's iOS 11.4 update delivers AirPlay 2 and Messages in iCloud. AirPlay 2 enables multi-room streaming, stereo HomePod pairing, a larger network buffer, and uninterrupted playback during calls or other media. Siri on HomePod gains calendar support but lacks individual voice recognition, allowing anyone to modify calendars. Users can ask Siri to move music between rooms. Third-party speakers will support AirPlay 2, though it requires an iOS device as a hub. Messages in iCloud syncs messages across devices, frees local storage, but consumes iCloud space, potentially problematic for free 5GB users. The update brings HomePod closer to competitors, but Siri remains largely unchanged.

On May 16, 2018, NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting that at its 2018 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, stockholders approved an amendment and restatement of the Amended and Restated 2007 Equity Incentive Plan to increase the available share reserve by 23,000,000 shares, and an amendment and restatement of the Amended and Restated 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan to increase the available share reserve by 13,500,000 shares. Stockholders also elected eleven directors, approved on an advisory basis the compensation of named executive officers, ratified the appointment of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the independent registered accounting firm for the fiscal year ending January 27, 2019, and approved the 2007 Plan and the 2012 Plan. The full text of the amended plans is filed as exhibits.

In China, time spent on short-form videos climbed 360% in 2017, yet 76% of consumers use only one such app. Leading apps Douyin and Kuaishou each have around 100 million daily active users and 52 minutes average daily usage. Long-form video ad budgets overtook network TV last year, and with short-form time approaching long-form, content providers should pay attention.

The appellate court modified the lower court's order, finding that summary judgment dismissing plaintiff's bad faith settlement negotiation claims was erroneous. Evidence showed defendant, the primary insurer, may have negotiated in bad faith by not timely offering policy limits, potentially causing plaintiff to settle for $1,350,000 instead of $1,000,000. Testimony on damages was direct and not speculative, creating a triable issue for a jury. The court affirmed dismissal of the Insurance Law § 2601 claim.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers support external synchronization mode by leaving the RT pin floating and applying a clock to the SYNC pin. The external clock frequency must be twice the desired switching frequency, within 200 kHz to 4 MHz, with a duty cycle between 40% and 60% (50% recommended). The controller internally inverts the applied clock, and the clock must be present before OUTA and OUTB become active.

In primary-secondary mode, two controllers can be synchronized. The primary device has its RT pin populated, and its SYNC pin outputs a clock at twice the switching frequency. The secondary device operates in external synchronization mode with RT floating, using the primary's SYNC output as its clock input. This mode can synchronize two independent converters or create an interleaved converter with parallel phases, requiring additional connections for VSENSE, COMP, SS, and HICC in the latter case. The secondary controller inverts the received clock, resulting in a phase shift of 90° or 270° between corresponding outputs.

Primary switching outputs OUTA and OUTB have approximately 150 mA peak current capability, and an external gate driver is recommended. OUTB is active only when the duty cycle limit is set to 50% by connecting DCL to AVSS, which is valid for TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP. OUTA and OUTB are not perfectly matched. Synchronous rectifier outputs SRA and SRB have similar current capability and also require external gate drivers. SRB is active only with the 50% duty cycle limit on TPS7H5001-SP. These outputs remain off during soft-start until the SS pin voltage exceeds 1 V, after which a small output voltage transient may occur.

Dead times between primary turn-off and SR turn-on (TDPS) and SR turn-off to primary turn-on (TDSP) are programmable on TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP via resistors on the PS and SP pins. Floating these pins sets a minimum 8 ns dead time; resistor values range from 10 kΩ to 300 kΩ. Leading edge blank time is programmable via a resistor on the LEB pin for all devices except TPS7H5003-SP, which has a fixed 50 ns. The LEB pin cannot be left floating, and resistor values range from 10 kΩ to 300 kΩ. The minimum on-time comprises the blank time and an internal logic delay. A pulse skipping mode prevents issues at high frequencies when the required duty cycle is less than the minimum on-time. Pulse skipping occurs when COMP voltage is below 0.3 V at the clock rising edge and the previous duty cycle was less than 25%. With a 50% duty cycle limit, skipped pulses are equal for OUTA and OUTB to maintain volt-second balance.

The maximum duty cycle is configured via the DCL pin: 100% when connected to VLDO, 75% when floating, and 50% when connected to AVSS. TPS7H5004-SP only supports 50%. The 50% limit activates OUTB and SRB. In external synchronization mode, a 50% duty cycle clock yields the most precise duty cycle limiting.

The CS_ILIM pin senses the transformer primary current. The COMP pin voltage, divided by two with a 150 mV offset, is compared to the sensed current to turn off the primary outputs. A resistor from CS_ILIM to AVSS sets the current limit threshold at 1.05 V nominal. When this threshold is exceeded, cycle-by-cycle limiting begins, and the HICC pin capacitor is charged by an 80 µA current. Once HICC reaches 0.6 V, the SS pin is discharged, switching stops, HICC is pulled to 1 V, and then discharged by a 1 µA current. When HICC falls to 0.3 V, a soft-start sequence is initiated. The HICC capacitor sets the delay and hiccup times; a minimum of 3.3 nF is recommended.

The FAULT pin triggers a shutdown if its voltage exceeds 0.6 V for a duration between 0.4 µs and 1.4 µs. The SS pin is discharged and outputs stop. After the fault clears (voltage below 0.5 V), a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles plus an internal logic delay occurs before soft-start restarts. If the fault reoccurs during the delay, the sequence restarts.

Slope compensation is added to prevent subharmonic oscillation at duty cycles above 50%. A resistor from the RSC pin to AVSS sets the slope compensation value, which is recommended to equal the inductor falling current slope.

Frequency compensation uses a transconductance error amplifier with Type 2A or 2B networks. Components RCOMP, CCOMP, and optional CHF are selected based on crossover frequency and power stage transconductance.

Thermal shutdown occurs if the junction temperature exceeds 175°C, with restart when the temperature drops below 160°C. The controllers use fixed-frequency peak current mode control, where the internal oscillator initiates primary output turn-on, and the sensed current compared to the stepped-down COMP voltage determines turn-off.

The TPS7H500x-SP series is designed for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge, with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz. A design example details a synchronous push-pull converter using GaN FETs, including component selection for frequency setting, output voltage, dead times, leading edge blanking, soft-start, transformer, FETs, RCD clamp, output inductor and capacitance, current sensing, hiccup capacitor, compensation, and slope compensation. Layout guidelines emphasize separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switch node area, and proper bypassing.

A new study in mice found that low doses of alcohol may improve brain health by enhancing the glymphatic system, which clears waste including proteins linked to Alzheimer's. Mice given a low dose (0.5 g/kg, equivalent to about 2.5 drinks per day) showed less brain inflammation and more efficient glymphatic function compared to teetotal mice, while performing equally on cognitive and motor tests. Intermediate (1.5 g/kg) and high (4 g/kg) doses decreased glymphatic function, with high doses also causing inflammation and cognitive/motor impairment. The suppression from intermediate doses was not permanent, recovering 24 hours after stopping. The results match a J-shaped model where low alcohol intake is beneficial and excessive intake is harmful. The study was published in Scientific Reports.

Andrew Lo notes that the stock market is down while T-bill rates are up, and the Fed is working to maintain liquid markets. Interest rates remain low overall; market freezing reflects banks awaiting clarity on a rescue package rather than structural problems. Fear is affecting markets, and Lo mentions that fear can paralyze decision-making. He suggests an opportunity: a website posting transaction prices of CDOs to improve transparency, which could be highly valuable. He strongly criticizes suspending mark-to-market accounting, likening it to telling people in a smoky theater to sit down instead of evacuating.

The lecture then covers forward and futures contracts as hedging tools. Companies face risks from currency and commodity price fluctuations; hedging can reduce uncertainty. Views on hedging differ: some argue it is irrelevant if shareholders can hedge themselves, others say it adds value by stabilizing cash flows and reducing distress costs. Examples include Homestake Mining (no hedging), American Barrick (hedging for stability), and Battle Mountain Gold (partial hedging). A 1997 survey found 57% of large firms used derivatives.

A forward contract is a customized, over-the-counter commitment to buy or sell an asset at a future date at a price agreed today. The forward price is set so the contract’s initial value is zero. As spot prices change, the contract gains value, creating counterparty risk because the losing party may default. Collateral may be insufficient if price moves are large. Forward contracts are illiquid and carry significant default risk.

Futures contracts address these issues by standardizing terms, trading on an exchange, and marking to market daily. Each day, the contract is effectively settled at a new forward price, with gains or losses exchanged, limiting exposure to one day’s movement. A clearing corporation acts as a central counterparty, further reducing risk. The passage details NYMEX crude oil futures: each contract is for 1,000 barrels, tick size is $0.01 per barrel ($10 per contract), initial margin is $4,050, maintenance margin is $3,000, and margin calls require additional funds if the account falls below maintenance. Margins have recently been increased due to higher volatility and credit concerns. While futures offer liquidity and safety, some firms still prefer forwards for customization and trusted counterparties.

To receive documentation update notifications, register on the device product folder on ti.com for a weekly digest. TI E2E support forums offer design help; linked content is provided 'AS IS' and does not constitute TI specifications. Trademarks include multiSPI and TI E2E. The integrated circuit can be damaged by ESD; handle with precautions. A glossary lists terms. Resources are for development only, and TI disclaims liability; users indemnify TI. Products are subject to TI's Terms of Sale. TI rejects additional terms. Mailing address: Texas Instruments, Dallas, Texas.

The lecture discusses light forces, focusing on the stimulated force using the dressed atom picture. In this picture, the atom–laser interaction is diagonalized first, yielding dressed states as superpositions of bare states with N or N+1 photons. Spontaneous emission couples these states, producing a Mollow triplet with carrier and sidebands, whose widths differ due to decoupled population and coherence relaxation rates in the strong-field limit. The dressed states experience opposite forces; the net dipole force depends on the population imbalance. For blue detuning, the atom mainly occupies the upper dressed state (correlating to the ground state), resulting in a repulsive force; red detuning gives an attractive force. When an atom moves through a laser beam, a time lag in population adjustment leads to a non-adiabatic friction force that cools for blue detuned light (blue molasses). Heating arises from force fluctuations when the atom switches dressed states via spontaneous emission, described by a momentum diffusion coefficient derived from force correlations. Sisyphus cooling is explained: in a blue detuned standing wave, the atom climbs potential hills and decays to the lower dressed state preferentially at the hilltops, losing kinetic energy. In the perturbative limit of large detuning, simple expressions for dressed states, transition rates, and potentials yield cooling and heating rates, showing the ultimate temperature is set by the lattice depth, so two-level atoms cannot be localized in an optical lattice by this cooling alone. The dipole potential can also be understood through harmonic oscillator response or refraction of light on a dielectric sphere (optical tweezers). The lecture concludes with an outlook on magnetic trapping, evaporative cooling, and quantum gases.

The lecture discusses trajectory optimization as a form of policy search, where control policies are parameterized by a vector alpha. It focuses on open-loop trajectories, where control actions are specified as a sequence over time. Two gradient computation methods are presented: backpropagation through time (adjoint method), which simulates forward then backward, and real-time recurrent learning (RTRL), which simulates only forward by carrying a matrix of state sensitivities to parameters. The lecture advocates using sequential quadratic programming (SQP) solvers like SNOPT for optimization due to ease of handling constraints and avoiding manual learning rate tuning. Two trajectory optimization approaches are covered: shooting methods, which simulate the system and iteratively adjust parameters, and direct collocation, which augments the parameter vector with state variables and enforces dynamics as explicit constraints. Examples on pendulum and acrobot swing-up tasks are shown, demonstrating fast convergence. Local minima are acknowledged, illustrated with a path-planning problem around obstacles, but considered acceptable if the goal is reached. The lecture concludes by previewing future topics: trajectory stabilization via LQR and iterative LQR methods.

A Norwalk, Iowa family has been without water for two months after an I-35 highway expansion project affected their 68-year-old well, despite a DOT promise not to dig near it. The Paschells, with two small children, cart in gallons daily and cannot bathe or do laundry at home. The DOT is investigating the breakdown. Hooking up to rural water was estimated at 30–60 days, so Mark Paschell and a contractor dug a trench and laid the water line themselves. The DOT has offered a hotel stay and reimbursement for cleaning supplies.

Sophomore forward Wenyen Gabriel announced he will remain in the 2018 NBA draft, forgoing his junior season at Kentucky. This leaves the 2018-19 roster without a scholarship junior or senior for now. Gabriel declared without an agent on April 18, despite not being in ESPN's top 100 prospects, and was the only UK draft entrant not invited to the combine. As a sophomore, he averaged 6.8 points and 5.4 rebounds, shot 39.6% from three, and led the team with 40 blocks. His season highlight was a 7-for-7 three-point performance in the SEC Tournament semifinals. Coach Calipari described him as a position-less big man. Since the season, UK lost Kevin Knox, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Hamidou Diallo to the draft, and two players to transfers. PJ Washington returned, and Stanford graduate transfer Reid Travis may join, both playing Gabriel's position, alongside Nick Richards and EJ Montgomery, limiting potential minutes. Gabriel is likely to begin his professional career overseas or in the NBA's developmental league. Currently, Washington, Richards, and Quade Green are the most experienced scholarship players.

The passage discusses how modern spread offenses and RPOs have led defenses to adopt multiple coverages, but an overlooked consequence is the complexity of run fits. Coaches need shared terminology ("coach speak") to communicate, but must translate terms like "front spacing" and "gapped out fits" into executable schemes, recognizing that run fits vary by talent and philosophy.

Run fits stem from two influences: front spacing (even or odd) and the coverage behind it. Even spacing has an open B gap (bubble away from the TE), while odd spacing moves open gaps to the C gaps (e.g., Tite/Mint front). The difference is also indicated by a head-up or shaded nose. Spacing is further described by 7, 8, or 9-man spacing, indicating the number of box defenders versus 12/21 personnel.

7-man spacing: The defense is minus one defender in the box ("out-gapped" or "light box"), typically with middle-of-the-field-open coverage. Overhangs are pass-first, leaving an open gap. Tools to compensate include 2-gapping a lineman, widening overhangs into B gaps, or post-snap stunts. Against zone, common second-level tools are "stack track and fallback" (linebackers stack targets and track the ball carrier). Against gap schemes with a puller, "spill-overlap" is used: the playside linebacker spills the kickout, the backside linebacker overlaps.

8-man spacing: The defense has equal numbers in the box ("gapped-out"), commonly with middle-of-the-field-closed coverage (cover 1 or 3). It employs one-gap run fits with an attack philosophy. Second-level tools include "indicator fitting" (fitting gaps based on tight end movement) versus zone, and "lever-spill-lever" versus gap schemes: the playside defender boxes the kickout, the middle defender spills the second puller, and the backside defender tempos the ball carrier.

9-man spacing: The defense has an extra defender ("maxed out"), associated with cover 0 blitz fits. Popularized by Narduzzi's quarters where safeties are "sky" force defenders in the fit (also called "4 mix"). The defense can play aggressive one-gap football, with an extra hat in the box.

The passage also details 3-4 defense run fits, noting that any spacing can be odd or even. In a Tite/Mint front, 7-man spacing versus zone uses a lag nose (backside A gap) and stack track fallback; versus power, spill-overlap is common. In 8-man spacing, overhangs may use "fill or freeze" rules based on running back location, allowing lever-spill-lever. 9-man spacing from an odd front resembles an already gap-exchanged even front, with the 5-technique starting in the B gap, and can use spill overlap or lever-spill-lever with an additional hat.

This retrospective study analyzed 377 percutaneous tracheostomies performed on intubated, mechanically ventilated COVID-19 patients at a single center in Kuwait between March 2020 and March 2022, representing the world’s largest reported single-center series. The mean duration from intubation to tracheostomy was 17.4 days. Patients had a mean age of 56.2 years, 59% were male, and common comorbidities included diabetes (50%) and hypertension (48%). On the procedure day, 29% were on ECMO and 23% on dialysis. Complications occurred in 23% of cases: intra-operative (6%), early (9%), and late (7%). Minor bleeding was the most frequent complication (14% overall). Other complications included tracheo-esophageal fistula (2%) and one tracheo-innominate fistula. Post-tracheostomy, 54% of patients were weaned from sedation (mean 7.5 days) and 41% from mechanical ventilation (mean 12.9 days). Overall mortality was 63%, all deaths attributed to COVID-19 complications; 37% were discharged, with 38% of those decannulated prior to discharge. The study concludes percutaneous tracheostomy can be safely performed in COVID-19 patients and suggests performing it as soon as possible after 7 days of intubation to reduce weaning times and complications. Limitations include lack of an open tracheostomy comparison group, no long-term outcomes, and no objective PCR testing of staff.

Wayne and Johnston counties’ Smart Start partnerships use a classroom-ready model funded by the Camber Foundation. Johnston’s three academies graduated 26, with 14 employed and 4 in higher education; cost $430 per student; next runs Oct. 6-24, prioritizing residents without child care experience.

Graduates can start debt-free, with credentials that transfer for further education. Officials note low pay but emphasize the heart for children and improved long-term outlooks.

Backtests indicate an end-of-month effect in Bitcoin, potentially a viable turn-of-the-month trading strategy. A formulated strategy yields average gain per trade 3.3%, CAGR 41.8%, time in market 16%, max drawdown 25%. The backtest is curve-fitted to some degree, but the average gain for the period (1.33% for random) is higher. The FAQ confirms backtesting methodology, acknowledges curve-fitting with a potential edge, and notes free resources for trading strategies are available.

The ADS9803 can be powered down via a logic 0 on the RESET pin or writing 1b to the RESET field (address 0x00, bank 0), or via a logic 0 on the PWDN pin or writing 11b to the PD_CH field (address 0xC0, bank 1). After reset or power-up, registers initialize to defaults and require a sequence of register writes for initialization, with a free-running sampling clock connected. A speed-boost mode allows up to 8MSPS for a user-selected analog input channel pair while other channels are idle; sampling rate equals the clock frequency. Register access uses SPI with 16-bit registers in three banks. Bank 0 is always accessible; banks 1 and 2 are selected via REG_BANK_SEL bits. Write operations: first frame writes to address 0x03 to select the bank, second frame writes to the target register. Read operations: with SPI_RD_EN=0b, select bank via 0x03; then set SPI_RD_EN=1b and SPI_MODE=1b in address 0x00; read a register with a 24-bit frame containing the register address; disable read by setting SPI_RD_EN=0. Multiple devices can be daisy-chained: CS and SCLK are shared, SDI of the first ADC connects to the controller, SDO to the next SDI, and the last SDO to the controller. Daisy-chain length is set in the DAISY_CHAIN_LEN register (number of ADCs excluding the first). Register writes in daisy-chain require N×24 SCLKs. For reads, after bank selection and enabling reads, send N×24-bit frames with 0xFE,0x00,address then N×24-bit frames of 0xFF to retrieve data. The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS DAQ system with a built-in analog front-end. In an ATE application, it achieves a TUE of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C post-calibration. It offers low-noise (22.7kHz) and wide-bandwidth (700kHz) modes; wide-bandwidth mode settles to 99.95% FS in 7.5µs. Power supplies are AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD, with no required power-up sequence. Use 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitors close to power pins, avoid vias between pins and capacitors. Place the reference decoupling capacitor near REFIO and REFM, connect GND and REFM to a ground plane with short connections, and avoid crossing digital lines with analog signals.

Yale-New Haven Hospital sued Clifford Mitchell and Laureen Wilczynski for unpaid medical bills. The defendants raised special defenses and counterclaims alleging the hospital violated the Hill-Burton Act and the state hospital bed funds statute, and that these violations constitute unfair trade practices under CUTPA. The hospital moved for summary judgment, arguing the special defenses and counterclaims were legally invalid.

The court denied the motions. It found the defendants have a private right of action under the Hill-Burton Act and can raise noncompliance as a defense, making the first special defense legally valid. It applied the same reasoning to the hospital bed funds statute defense. Regarding the CUTPA counterclaims, the court held that private causes of action exist under both statutes, and even if they did not, CUTPA claims can be based on statutory violations that lack a private remedy. The court also rejected the hospital's argument that the Hill-Burton Act preempts CUTPA.

The lecture discusses the computation of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and introduces the fast Fourier transform (FFT) algorithm. A direct DFT computation requires on the order of N² complex multiplications and additions. The FFT algorithm, for N a power of 2, reduces this to a number proportional to N·log₂N, offering dramatic efficiency gains. The algorithm decomposes the DFT by separating the input sequence into even-indexed and odd-indexed subsequences (decimation-in-time). An N-point DFT is expressed as the sum of an N/2-point DFT of the even points and an N/2-point DFT of the odd points multiplied by W_N^k. This decomposition is applied recursively until reaching 2-point DFTs. The resulting flow graph consists of butterfly computations. By recognizing that W_N^{N/2} = –1, each butterfly simplifies to a multiplication by a power of W, followed by an addition and a subtraction. In this form, the input sequence appears in a rearranged order (0,4,2,6,1,5,3,7 for N=8), while the output is in sequential order. The algorithm’s efficiency relies on the periodicity of the DFT. The lecture notes that the same approach applies to the inverse DFT and that the next lecture will address memory arrangement and further modifications.

Szemerédi's graph regularity lemma states that for any large, dense graph, one can partition its vertex set into a bounded number of parts so that the graph appears random-like between most pairs of parts. An epsilon regular pair (X,Y) is defined such that for all subsets A⊆X, B⊆Y with |A|≥ε|X|, |B|≥ε|Y|, the edge density between A and B differs from that between X and Y by at most ε. A partition is epsilon regular if the sum of |V_i||V_j| over all pairs (i,j) that are not epsilon regular is at most ε times the total number of vertex pairs. The lemma asserts that for every ε>0 there exists M=M(ε) such that every graph has an ε-regular partition into at most M parts, with M independent of the graph's size. A variant guarantees an equitable partition (part sizes differ by at most 1) with at least m0 parts.

The proof uses an energy increment argument. The energy of a partition is a weighted mean square density between parts, always between 0 and 1. Starting from the trivial partition, if the current partition is not ε-regular, one refines it by simultaneously cutting each part using witnessing subsets for irregular pairs. Lemmas show that energy never decreases under refinement, and that for a non-ε-regular pair, refining by a witnessing pair boosts energy by at least ε^4|U||W|/n^2. Consequently, each refinement step increases the total energy by at least ε^5. Since energy is bounded by 1, the process terminates after at most ε^{-5} steps, yielding an ε-regular partition. The number of parts becomes a tower of exponentials depending only on ε. This bound is essentially tight, as shown by Gowers. To obtain an equitable partition, one can further massage the partition after each refinement by rebalancing a small number of vertices, which may slightly decrease energy but still allows a net increase, so the same proof structure applies.

Digital piracy, initiated by Napster in 1999, has reshaped industries by providing free, convenient access to content, reducing revenues despite legal and technical countermeasures. This study investigates how firms can design business models to counter piracy, using Spotify and Netflix as case studies.

The passage examines digital piracy’s value proposition (free access, large catalogs, bypassing release windows) and its downsides (inconsistent quality, required skills). It compares content categories, finding audio and film most vulnerable due to easier copying and consumption.

Applying a business model framework of customer identification, engagement, monetization, and value chain linkages, Spotify and Netflix are analyzed. Both employ subscription-based streaming with free tiers or trials, intuitive interfaces, broad device compatibility, and personalized recommendations. Their models respond to piracy by offering “all-you-can-eat” access, improving convenience, ensuring consistent quality, and enabling social sharing and community features. A causal loop diagram shows how userbase growth, catalog expansion, and personalization create virtuous cycles that increase willingness to pay and competitive advantage.

Implications include technology’s dual role in enabling piracy and providing solutions, the importance of diversification, and network effects where strong community features can lead to “winner takes all” dynamics. The conclusion emphasizes that digital distribution outperforms piracy primarily by enhancing the consumption experience through accessibility, navigation, and social interactions, with potential applicability to other content categories.

The NHS offers free cancer screening to detect early signs of cancer before symptoms appear, improving treatment success. According to Cancer Research UK, screening saved around 90,000 lives in the last five years. Dr Alexandra Moorhouse advises attending screenings even when feeling healthy, as many cancers lack early symptoms.

The NHS has three main screening programmes. Cervical screening is offered every five years to women and people with a cervix aged 25–64, testing for high-risk HPV strains via a cervical sample. A negative result means very low cervical cancer risk and next screening in five years; a positive result leads to further analysis for abnormal cells. If none, screening repeats in one year; if abnormal cells are present, a hospital colposcopy is offered. Persistent high-chance HPV over two years without abnormal cells also leads to colposcopy. Breast screening is offered every three years to women and people aged 50–71 using mammograms. Those over 71 can continue screening by contacting their local service; people under 50 with high risk should consult a doctor. Bowel screening is offered every two years to people aged 50–74 using a home faecal immunochemical test (FIT) kit to detect tiny blood amounts. A negative result means low risk and re-screening in two years; a positive result leads to urgent colonoscopy. Screening beyond 75 can be requested, and those without a permanent address can collect a FIT kit at their local surgery.

Additional screening, such as for prostate cancer in men with concerns or urinary symptoms, can be discussed with a doctor. Benefits include early detection when treatment is more effective, detection of pre-cancerous changes, reassurance from normal results, and significantly reduced deaths for breast, bowel, and cervical cancers.

Eligible individuals automatically receive postal invitations. If missed, they can call their surgery to rebook. Cervical screening can be booked directly; breast screening invitations are sent by post; bowel screening FIT kits are sent and returned by post. For breast screening queries, contact the local service; for bowel screening, call 0800 707 6060. Screening start ages: cervical at 25, breast at 50, bowel at 50. Those with a family history may need earlier or additional screening. Women with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) should have yearly mammograms from age 40 per NHS guidance; if refused, they should persist or seek a specialist referral. Private screening is available for those not meeting NHS age criteria, based on personal choice or factors like family history or unusual symptoms. Speaking to a doctor can help assess symptoms and arrange checks.

This work extends Uustalu's characterization of monoid structures from non-indexed to indexed containers. Indexed containers, consisting of an indexed set of shapes S : I → Set and a family of position sets P, represent endofunctors on Set^I via an extent construction. They are a notational variant of generalized polynomials. The category ICI of indexed containers carries a monoidal structure corresponding to composition of extents. The authors generalize the combinatorial data and equations for a monoid in ICI, proving these correspond precisely to monad structures on the associated indexed container functors. Examples include products of indexed container monads, indexed state and writer monads, and a free monad yielding well-scoped λ-terms. The development is formalized in Cubical Agda. The paper reviews related work on containers, polynomials, and monads, noting that while some prior work focuses on Cartesian monads, this characterization handles general monads. The extent functor from ICI to endofunctors on Set^I is full and faithful.

Del Cid-Mendez appealed his conviction and sentence for illegal reentry, challenging the constitutionality of 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b) and the mandatory Sentencing Guidelines. Using a relative risk (RR) statistic that compares age-group proportions among ICU admissions before and after epidemic peaks, this study examined four Omicron waves in France in 2022. The highest RR values were: Spring wave – 10-19y (1.92), 40-49y (1.45), 0-9y (1.31); Summer wave – 0-9y (1.61), 10-19y (1.46), 20-29y (1.43); Autumn wave – 10-19y (1.64), 30-39y (1.35), 20-29y (1.21); Autumn-Winter wave – 30-39y (1.47), 40-49y (1.29), 80+y (1.27). The leading relative roles shifted from children and younger adults to persons aged 30-49y and over 80y. The authors recommend increasing booster vaccination for all adults and possibly children, and enhanced protection for the elderly. Limitations include testing inconsistencies and uncertainty in the RR–transmission link, though simulations support it. ICU data were used to reduce under-detection.

An international team led by Harald Ebeling discovered the distant galaxy eMACSJ1341-QG-1, magnified 30 times by gravitational lensing from the massive galaxy cluster eMACSJ1341.9-2441. Using the Hubble Space Telescope, they found this extreme magnification, which allows detailed study of a rare quiescent galaxy that does not form new stars. Gravitational lensing, predicted by Einstein, enables observation of faint distant sources. The magnification provides an opportunity to investigate stellar populations and reconstruct the galaxy's shape. Quiescent galaxies are common locally but rare at greater distances; understanding why this young galaxy stopped forming stars may offer clues about galaxy evolution. Follow-up observations are underway, and the findings are published in the Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Larry Connors’ Multiple Days Up (MDU) and Multiple Days Down (MDD) strategy, from Chapter 6 of his 2009 book “High Probability Trading,” is a mean reversion approach for ETFs. It buys when an ETF is above its 200-day moving average, below its 5-day moving average, and has dropped 4 of the last 5 trading days; sells when the ETF closes above the 5-day moving average, with no stop-loss. Tests on 20 original ETFs plus five added (inception to December 2020) and a portfolio simulation (2000–2020, max five positions, 20% equity each, compounded, no commissions/slippage) showed it had the lowest profit factor among Connors’ mean reversion strategies. Trading only SPY and QQQ (50% each) gave 287 trades, profit factor 1.82, drawdown 12%, CAGR 2.4%, market time 7.7%. Short-side: a five-position portfolio was not tradeable; only SPY and QQQ shorts had 65% win ratio and 0.68% average gain (gain in 2008). The strategy can likely be improved by ETF-specific tweaking and optimization.

A skull of the new species Cifelliodon wahkarmoosuch, a small, catlike animal with buck teeth and plant-crushing molars, was discovered in eastern Utah. The find suggests the supercontinent Pangea split 15 million years later than previously thought and that reptile-like mammals underwent an evolutionary burst across continents. The creature had hair, suckled its young, and laid eggs. Published in Nature, the study indicates early mammals occupied diverse ecological niches. The fossil was found on Bureau of Land Management land and is displayed at the Natural History Museum of Utah.

Virginia Chestnuts is a family-owned orchard in Nelson County, Virginia, in the Blue Ridge foothills. After American chestnut trees were devastated by blight in the early 1900s, most U.S. chestnuts were imported. David and Kim Bryant purchased land in 2003, planted test trees, then over 1,600 blight-resistant Dunstan hybrid trees. Despite harsh weather and cicadas between 2009 and 2014, a 2015 bumper crop allowed them to supply locavores and food hubs, driven by nostalgia. The orchard’s best harvest yielded at least 3,000 pounds. The Bryants belong to a five-orchard growers group in Nelson County. Harvest runs from mid-September to late October; nuts are machine- and hand-harvested, sorted, graded, washed, sanitized, dried, and cold-stored. Buyers can purchase whole or peeled nuts. In November, the family roasts chestnuts over apple wood at Dickie Brothers Orchard. Virginia Chestnuts participated in the Fire, Flour & Fork event in Richmond, roasting chestnuts at “Smoke on the Water” and serving them in paper cones. Chestnuts are used in breads, stuffing, beer, desserts, and appeal to vegetarians and vegans. The orchard has a social media presence and sells via its website.

The TPS7H500x-SP devices generate an internal 1.23-V bandgap reference, divided to 0.613 V for the error amplifier, which maintains regulation within +0.7%/-1%. A 470-nF capacitor is required at the REFCAP pin. Each controller uses a transconductance error amplifier comparing the VSENSE pin voltage to the lower of the SS pin voltage or the internal 0.613-V reference. Output voltage is set via a resistor divider to the 0.613-V nominal reference. The soft-start circuit uses the SS pin voltage as a reference until it rises above VREF; synchronous rectifier outputs become active once SS reaches 1 V.

The controllers have three switching frequency modes: internal oscillator (set by an RT resistor, 100 kHz to 2 MHz range), external synchronization (RT floating, clock applied to SYNC at twice the desired frequency), and primary-secondary mode (using the SYNC output of a primary device as the clock for a secondary device). Primary switching outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) are available depending on the device. Dead times and leading edge blank time are programmable for some devices via resistors on the PS, SP, and LEB pins. A pulse skipping mode prevents operational issues related to minimum on-time. Maximum duty cycle is configurable via the DCL pin.

The CS_ILIM pin is used for peak current mode control and overcurrent protection, triggering hiccup mode when the voltage exceeds 1.05 V. The HICC pin capacitor controls the cycle-by-cycle limiting delay and hiccup restart times. The FAULT pin provides external fault protection, initiating a shutdown when its voltage exceeds 0.6 V. Slope compensation is set via the RSC pin. Frequency compensation components are connected to the COMP pin. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C. An application example details designing a synchronous push-pull converter.

A Michigan State University study in Agricultural Systems compared adaptive multi-paddock (AMP) grass-fed and grain-fed feedlot beef systems. Led by Jason Rowntree, it found AMP grazing could offset greenhouse gas emissions, with the finishing phase as a net carbon sink, while feedlot emissions were higher due to fertilizer-related nitrogen. Feedlots were more land-efficient, producing the same beef on half the land. AMP yielded more beef per land than continuous grazing but less than feedlots, implying lower per capita consumption with greater environmental benefits. Carbon sequestration may decline over time. Best practices include reduced fertilizer and cover crops for feedlots, and AMP's high-density grazing with plant recovery to enhance soil organic matter and moisture. Rowntree stresses that both systems can improve environmental stewardship and coexist with healthy waterways.

The Second Circuit affirmed the denial of habeas corpus. Nicholson claimed that state courts violated due process by excluding Darnell Phelps's hearsay confession under Chambers v. Mississippi. Assuming Chambers applies to retrial motions, the court found no violation because the state courts did not mechanistically exclude reliable evidence. Phelps's confession lacked trustworthiness: it contradicted his earlier denial, could not be cross-examined at retrial, and could have been tailored to public forensics. An eyewitness testified against Nicholson and was deemed credible by the jury. The confession did not fully exonerate Nicholson and assigned him a more active role, yet he never disclosed Phelps's involvement before trial. Thus, the denial of a new trial did not offend due process.

Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) is off by default; customers must opt-in via BIOS configuration and may enable co-signing of update packages. During early boot, the BIOS passes a customer public signing key to the AMD Security Processor (ASP). If both customer and AMD keys are enabled, the SFS package authenticates first against the customer key, then the AMD key. The SET_CUST_SFS_SIGNATURE command provides an RSA public key (2048-bit or 4096-bit) using RSA-PSS signature scheme. Co-signing requires the customer to generate an RSA key pair and sign the package with the private key.

Each executable patch checks the existing System Patch Level and firmware versions to determine applicability. Update packages can patch registers, replace firmware images, or update portions of firmware. AMD SFS automatically commits SEV updates, preventing rollback; reverting requires a system reboot. If SNP is enabled, update pages must be HV-FIXED using RMPUPDATE. For attestation, SFS provides measurements to attestation data managers; some attestation schemes prevent modification of certain firmware components, and AMD will not attempt to modify that firmware.

Update packages ensure proper firmware versions exist before applying to avoid out-of-sync conditions. If any part of a package cannot fully apply, the update should not occur. Updates are non-persistent across reboots, so a mechanism is needed; they can be applied during OS boot, immediately after boot, or anytime during operation. SFS commands require memory alignment: the TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER must be at the start of a 2MB aligned page. For GET_FW_VERSIONS, the output page follows at +4k; for UPDATE_FW, the update package starts at +4k, with an optional co-signing header at that offset. A customer-provided deployment agent creates the buffer, appends the co-signing header (if used), the AMD update package, and the co-signing signature, then communicates the request via the TEE mailbox interface.

The ASP process: check DRAM protection, verify customer signature (if enabled), verify AMD signature, load and execute the patch, update patch level, and return status. The GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO command returns API version, current SFS patch level, system patch level, and firmware version entries. SFS packages are binary objects aligned to AGESA releases, named fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. The update process runs in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic, aiming for minimal performance impact with at most brief quiescence. SEV/ES virtual machines must stop and restart for an SEV firmware update; SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operation during the update.

The UC1825B-SP oscillator is a sawtooth; its rising edge is set by RT and CT, and the falling edge sets dead time. RT is selected first based on desired maximum duty cycle, then CT for frequency. Recommended RT range is 1 kΩ to 100 kΩ, and DMAX below 70% is not recommended. The device is a dual output controller with integrated drivers for push-pull topology and can support half-bridge and full-bridge with external high-side drivers; it supports voltage and current mode topologies using the RAMP and ILIM pins. A switching frequency of 215 kHz was chosen as a trade-off between bandwidth and efficiency, with RT = 10 kΩ and CT = 680 pF. Transformer turns ratio is limited by maximum duty cycle; a 30% duty cycle was targeted, and a turns ratio of 2.2 was used. The auxiliary winding turns ratio was 1.5. Primary inductance was 120 µH, selected based on magnetizing current (6% design value). The output inductor was 2.2 µH. Peak and RMS currents are calculated for continuous conduction mode. An RCD clamp is used, with Kclamp recommended as 1.5 for ~50% overshoot; starting resistor and capacitor values are found using clamp voltage and ΔVclamp (typically 10%). The output diode voltage stress is Vout + VinMAX; a 60 V diode was chosen. Main switching MOSFETs see twice the input voltage plus ringing, so a voltage rating of 2.5–3 times input voltage is recommended. Output capacitance of about 1145 µF was chosen to keep ripple low, with an additional output filter (500 nH inductor) to attenuate ripple; a 0.5 Ω damping resistor was used. Type IIB compensation was used, with a crossover frequency of 5 kHz; the compensation zero was placed at 279 Hz and the pole at 15.23 kHz. The sense resistor sets current limit based on a ~1 V threshold. Layout guidelines include using low-EMI inductors, keeping feedback traces away from noise, placing input/output capacitors and compensation components close to the IC, making power traces short and thick, using ground planes, separating power ground for high di/dt paths, and bypassing VCC and VREF with low ESR/ESL capacitors. The device operates from a 10–30 V input supply. Mechanical, packaging, and orderable information is provided, along with standard legal disclaimers.

Carson Palmer, a veteran quarterback with 175 career games, was traded from Oakland to Arizona in 2013 and led the Cardinals to a 10-6 season, throwing for 4,274 yards with a 63.3 completion percentage. After a torn ACL in 2014, he had a career-best 2015, setting highs in wins (13), passing yards (4,671), yards per attempt (8.7), and QBR (78.6), and was named a first-team All Pro by Pro Football Focus. In 2016, at age 37, his performance declined to career-low levels since his Oakland tenure. Palmer says he feels great and is excited for the upcoming season. He annually reassesses his future, telling his wife each year might be his last, but he takes it one year at a time and wants to continue as long as he has health and ability. He prefers the underdog role, believing the Cardinals’ 7-8-1 record in 2016 reduces pressure and allows more focus on his craft, and he thinks the team shares that preference.

Microsoft Corporation's quarterly report for the period ended December 31, 2022, includes unaudited financial statements and management's discussion. Revenue was $52.7 billion for the quarter and $102.9 billion for the six months, with net income of $16.4 billion and $34.0 billion, respectively. Operating income was $20.4 billion and $41.9 billion. The report highlights a change in accounting estimate effective fiscal year 2023, increasing the useful lives of server and network equipment from four to six years, which increased operating income by $945 million for the quarter and $2.0 billion for the six months. The company recorded $800 million in employee severance expenses related to a workforce reduction of approximately 10,000 jobs announced in January 2023. The Nuance Communications acquisition was completed on March 4, 2022, for $18.8 billion, and its results are included in the Intelligent Cloud segment. A definitive agreement to acquire Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion was announced, with closing expected in fiscal year 2023 subject to regulatory approvals. Segment performance: Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $17.0 billion, Intelligent Cloud $21.5 billion, and More Personal Computing $14.2 billion for the quarter. Microsoft Cloud revenue was $27.1 billion for the quarter. The effective tax rate was 19% for the quarter and 19% for the six months. The report also discusses debt, leases, contingencies, and share repurchases, with $31.5 billion remaining under the current $60 billion repurchase program.

The National Beer Wholesalers Association launched DeliveringLocalJobs.com to highlight the 135,000 employees in the beer distribution industry across all 50 states. Butterfield reported Q1 2018 results with core return on average tangible common equity improving to 24.3% from 22.3% in the prior quarter. Net interest margin increased to 3.05% from 2.87%, driven by loan repricing and higher volumes, as the Fed continued rate increases. Net interest income rose $3.8 million to $79.9 million. Non-interest income declined 6.1% sequentially due to seasonal factors. Core non-interest expense was $76 million, modestly lower, and the core efficiency ratio was 62.3%, trending toward a 60% target.

The bank closed the acquisition of Deutsche Bank's Global Trust Solutions business at the end of the quarter, adding a trust office in Singapore and a back-office operation in Mauritius. It expects to close the acquisition of Deutsche Bank's banking operations in Cayman and the Channel Islands by year-end, which could increase total deposits by up to 20% and add a new bank location in Jersey. Management noted a dislocation in offshore banking with more sellers than buyers, positioning Butterfield as an acquirer of choice.

Total assets were approximately $11 billion, up 1.9%. The balance sheet remains asset-sensitive, with 46% of assets in cash, short-term investments, and investment securities. Average deposits increased to $9.8 billion from $9.6 billion. Loans grew by $180 million to $4.0 billion, primarily from additional drawings on a sovereign loan and growth in the UK residential mortgage portfolio. Non-accrual loans decreased to $42.4 million, and the net charge-off ratio was 2 basis points. The investment portfolio was $4.5 billion, 4% lower than the prior quarter, with 94.6% of securities rated AAA.

Capital ratios remained strong: the Basel III total capital ratio was 19.2%, and the common equity to total assets ratio was 6.7%, approaching target levels. The board authorized a quarterly dividend of $0.38 per share. A share repurchase program became effective April 1, but no shares were purchased in Q1. An S-3 shelf registration was filed to provide flexibility for potential securities offerings.

Management indicated that first-year Sarbanes-Oxley costs had normalized, and they continued to focus on expense management toward the 60% efficiency ratio target. Fee income was described as stable and capital-efficient, with growth primarily from acquisitions. The bank expects asset sensitivity to increase after the Deutsche Bank banking acquisition closes, which will be managed by laddering deposits into investments. M&A discussions continue across various jurisdictions, with opportunities in both banking and trust businesses.

The passage discusses the Bollinger Band Squeeze trading strategy. Bollinger Bands measure volatility; the center is the average price, and the bands widen with high volatility and contract with low volatility. A squeeze occurs when bands contract, indicating low volatility and a potential breakout. The strategy involves trading in the direction of the breakout after such a period. Backtesting using an indicator of the band difference showed the strategy did not perform particularly well on any asset, except possibly consumer staples, and did not beat buy-and-hold on Pepsi (12.5% vs. 14.8% with 61% invested). Multiple variations were tried without success, leading to the conclusion that anecdotal evidence should not be trusted and other indicators may be better. The article provides a brief biography of John Bollinger, born 1950, author and financial analyst, who developed Bollinger Bands in the 1980s, published a newsletter in 1987, and wrote a book translated into 11 languages. The name originated from a TV interview. FAQs note the strategy is a breakout type with lower win rate and whipsaws, requiring backtesting for positive expectancy. Mistakes include lacking positive expectancy and not following the strategy; mechanical trading is recommended. Assets differ: stocks tend to mean revert, commodities do not, so the strategy may not work on all. The blog has over 1200 articles with backtestable trading rules, compiled into a purchasable package, with code from this article included. The strategies are from a landing page of profitable trading systems and come with plain English logic.

Cory Booker campaigned for Doug Jones in Alabama before the Senate election, with the 2020 presidential race as a clear subtext. The Board of Tax Appeals partially affirmed a deficiency determination against the taxpayer for 1931, including the fair market value of preferred stock distributed as a dividend on common stock that year. The majority opinion reverses, holding that Section 115(f) of the Revenue Act of 1928, which states “A stock dividend shall not be subject to tax,” exempts this preferred stock dividend. The court examines legislative history and prior cases, concluding the exemption is broad and unqualified. The Commissioner’s alternative arguments regarding the 1928 stock redemption are rejected because the issue was not properly raised. Judge L. Hand dissents, arguing that Congress intended to exempt only stock dividends not constitutionally taxable as income, and that preferred stock dividends on common stock create a substantially new right and are income; he believes the literal reading is inconsistent with the exemption’s purpose.

Pedro Russell, after a business bachelor's and roles at RSM, Cengage, and Juno, earned an MBA at MIT Sloan. The passage describes bonded optical devices for wearable electronics, addressing the challenge of creating multi-colored displays from monochromatic microLED wafers. It discloses directly bonding optical elements (e.g., monochromatic LED chips for red, green, blue) to at least one carrier (e.g., a processor element with active circuitry) without an intervening adhesive, using techniques like direct or hybrid bonding. This bonding enables fine pixel pitches. The bonded optical devices are optically coupled with a common optical pathway, such as a waveguide, which transmits a superposition of light from the different colored optical elements to an output, creating a polychromatic image for the user. The optical elements can be arranged side-by-side or at angles, and may include physical isolation structures to limit crosstalk between pixels or matrices of pixels.

The GA10x SM is partitioned into four processing blocks, each with a 64 KB register file, L0 instruction cache, warp scheduler, dispatch unit, and math units. The four partitions share a 128 KB L1 data cache/shared memory subsystem. Unlike TU102, which had eight second-generation Tensor Cores, GA10x includes four third-generation Tensor Cores (one per partition), each twice as powerful as a Turing Tensor Core. The combined L1 data cache and shared memory capacity is 33% larger than Turing, and for graphics workloads the cache partition capacity is doubled.

GA10x doubles peak FP32 throughput by including FP32 processing on both datapaths in each partition. One datapath has 16 FP32 CUDA Cores; the other has 16 FP32 CUDA Cores and 16 INT32 Cores, capable of executing either 16 FP32 or 16 INT32 operations per clock. Each partition can execute 32 FP32 operations per clock, or 16 FP32 and 16 INT32. All four partitions combined can execute 128 FP32 operations per clock (double Turing) or 64 FP32 and 64 INT32. Double-speed FP16 (HFMA) operations are supported, and standard FP16 operations are handled by Tensor Cores.

The unified L1 data cache/shared memory can be reconfigured. L1 data cache capacity per SM is 128 KB. In graphics and async compute, 64 KB is allocated to L1/texture cache, 48 KB to shared memory, and 16 KB reserved. Full GA102 contains 10752 KB of L1 cache, and shared memory bandwidth is doubled to 128 bytes/clock per SM. Total L1 bandwidth for RTX 3080 is 219 GB/sec. Ampere GPUs are up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing at the same performance level.

The second-generation RT Core includes dedicated hardware for BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, doubling the intersection rate over Turing. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates ray-traced motion blur, making it up to eight times faster than Turing. The GA10x SM supports concurrent RT Core and graphics or compute workloads, and RT Core-heavy workloads leave SM processing power available for other tasks.

Third-generation Tensor Cores add support for TF32, BF16, and fine-grained structured sparsity. Sparsity uses a 2:4 pattern to skip zero-valued elements, doubling math throughput for matrix multiplication. RTX 3080 delivers 119 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS (dense) and 238 with sparsity. DLSS leverages these Tensor Cores and a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor to enable 8K gaming.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling, achieving up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth (RTX 3090), a 52% improvement over TU102. MTA encoding limits signal transitions to improve SNR. Pseudo-independent memory channels assist BVH traversal. RTX IO provides GPU-based lossless decompression and works with Microsoft DirectStorage to offload CPU work, improving I/O performance up to 100x compared to hard drives.

The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU delivers up to 2x FP32, 2x ray tracing, and 5x (10x with sparsity) AI training throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, with 48 GB memory scalable to 96 GB via NVLink. Display support includes DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 for 8K60 and 4K120. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decode, and seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding up to 8K HEVC. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) on GDDR6X detects transmission errors and replays them, causing performance to plateau rather than crash during overclocking. The RTX A6000 features a GA102 GPU with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-gen RT Cores, 336 third-gen Tensor Cores, and 48 GB GDDR6.
