William Brock was convicted of molestation of a juvenile and sentenced to ten years at hard labor. On appeal, he challenged the sufficiency of the evidence and the excessiveness of his sentence. The appellate court affirmed. The evidence showed that Brock lived with his fiancée and her three-year-old child. The child complained of pain, and the mother found a pubic hair in the child's private area; the child later said Brock touched her. A medical examination revealed vaginal redness and abrasion consistent with manual digital manipulation, not self-inflicted. The mother and a neighbor testified that the child acted stiff and scared around Brock. Brock denied the act and stated no other men had access to the child. The court found the evidence sufficient to prove a lewd act by a person over seventeen on a child under seventeen with the requisite age difference, intent to arouse sexual desires, and use of influence by virtue of a position of control. Regarding the sentence, the trial court considered statutory factors, noted permanent harm, and imposed ten years, which was five years less than the maximum. The appellate court found no abuse of discretion. Conviction and sentence affirmed.

This study investigated the attitudes of education faculty students towards the Research Methods in Education (RME) course. The course, formerly Scientific Research Methods, was updated in 2018 and aims to teach research principles, processes, sampling, data collection, analysis, evaluation, designs, and ethics. The research used a mixed-method sequential explanatory design. The quantitative part employed a survey model with a purposive sample of 190 students from Turkish Teaching, English Teaching, and Pre-School Teaching departments at Bayburt University. An attitude scale developed by the researcher, consisting of 21 items across three factors (contribution to the profession, confidence, contribution to daily life), was administered online. Reliability and validity analyses were reported, including Cronbach’s alpha, KMO, and confirmatory factor analysis fit indices. Data were analyzed using Kruskal Wallis H and Mann Whitney U tests. The qualitative part involved focus group interviews with 10 pre-service teachers, analyzed via content analysis.

Findings showed that attitudes towards the RME course did not differ significantly by department. However, a significant difference was found by grade level, with fourth-grade students showing higher attitudes than first-grade students. In the qualitative findings, 9 out of 10 teacher candidates considered the course necessary, citing its role in understanding scientific research and other courses. Regarding gains, 50% reported personal gains, 30% proficiency in scientific research processes, and 20% profession-oriented gains. Concerning the teaching process, 60% stated the course duration was insufficient, 20% highlighted the lecturer’s approach, and 20% noted issues with tools and materials.

The study concluded that attitudes did not vary by department but did vary by class level, and that students generally found the course necessary while requesting extended duration. Recommendations included providing prerequisite courses, offering the RME course to 3rd or 4th year students, extending its credit and duration, or structuring it as a two-part course, and making it compulsory.

This study explored the mentoring needs and experiences of entry-level occupational therapy students, with a focus on those from historically underrepresented groups, to inform culturally sensitive mentorship programs. A cross-sectional survey of 133 students at a single urban university was conducted; 59 respondents identified as being from a historically underrepresented group. Results indicated that current mentorship programming was insufficient. Students desired mentors who demonstrated cultural humility, empathy, anti-racism allyship, and support for handling workplace discrimination, in addition to understanding the transition from academia to clinical practice. Key mentor qualities identified included personality, expertise with desired settings, availability, and similar interests; over a third of respondents valued a similar ethnic/cultural background. BIPOC students rated a mentor’s awareness of their own biases and prejudices as significantly more important than white students did. Hispanic/Latinx students were significantly more likely to report that their mentors did not work effectively across cultural differences and did not adequately help integrate personal life with school responsibilities. Students sought mentorship for career transitions, NBCOT preparation, networking, work-life balance, and navigating microaggressions and systemic racism. The study concludes that occupational therapy programs should implement culturally sensitive mentorship programs that integrate career support with emotional and social validation, offer both formal and informal components, and include training for mentors on implicit bias and anti-racism. Limitations include the single-institution sample, cross-sectional design, and primary focus on race and ethnicity without examining other intersecting identities. Future research should involve diverse institutions, longitudinal designs, and consideration of multiple identity dimensions.

In Edwin P. Whitmore et al., Executors v. The San Francisco Savings Union et al., the executors of Horace M. Whitmore's estate sought to enjoin the trustees under a deed of trust from selling land securing a promissory note, after the creditor failed to present its claim within the statutory ten-month period following publication of notice to creditors. The lower court perpetually enjoined the sale and decreed the defendants had no title. On appeal, the California Supreme Court reversed.

The headnotes state that failure to present a claim to an executor for allowance within the statutory time does not extinguish the debt but merely takes away the creditor's remedy, and that equity will not compel a creditor to surrender security or enjoin a sale under a deed of trust when the claim was not timely presented.

The complaint alleged that Horace Whitmore gave a $1500 note secured by a deed of trust on land; he died, his will was probated, notice to creditors was published, and more than ten months passed without the Savings Union presenting its claim. The trustees advertised the land for sale. The executors, in possession, offered to pay trust expenses and sought an injunction.

Appellants argued that a plaintiff seeking equity must do equity, that non-presentation is not payment but only a statute of limitations, and that the debt remains, so the creditor should not be forced to surrender security without payment. Respondents cited Probate Act sections barring unpresented claims, argued a deed of trust is equivalent to a mortgage, and contended the lien is lost if not presented; they asserted the maxim “he who seeks equity must do equity” did not apply because the executors fulfilled their duty and the creditor was in default.

The majority opinion by Chief Justice Wallace held that the failure to present the claim did not extinguish the debt; it only took away the remedy. Because the debt was still subsisting and unpaid, the estate could not invoke equity to compel surrender of the securities without payment. The court applied the maxim that he who seeks equity must do equity, noting it would compel surrender only upon payment or direct a sale with surplus to the debtor. The judgment was reversed with directions to sustain the demurrer.

Justice Crockett dissented, joined by Justice McKinstry. The dissent reasoned that under prior decisions, a creditor holding a mortgage or trust deed must present the claim to preserve the lien; failure abrogates the lien. Although the trustee holds legal title, the equitable title is in the estate and is assets for debts. The administrator cannot pay the barred debt, and the property may be needed for preferred claims like funeral expenses and family allowance. Allowing a non-presenting creditor to retain the property would defeat lawful administration. The dissent argued there is nothing inequitable in compelling release of the legal title when the lien is lost, and that a contrary rule would lead to anomalies, such as the estate being consumed by interest while preferred debts go unpaid, prejudicing diligent creditors.

In Kellner et al. v. District Court, the Colorado Supreme Court considered an original proceeding in the nature of prohibition. Plaintiffs in the underlying action sued defendants for fraud and rescission of a home sale. Defendants, formerly of Denver, had moved to Ventura, California. After an initial attempt at service in Colorado was quashed, plaintiffs served defendants in California under Rule 4(f)(1), which allows out-of-state personal service on Colorado residents. Defendants moved to quash, asserting they were California residents. The trial court denied the motion, finding the California service valid. Defendants then sought a writ of prohibition from the Supreme Court. The court first addressed its own jurisdiction, holding that a court proceeding without personal jurisdiction raises a question of great public importance, thus warranting original jurisdiction. On the merits, the court found the facts regarding residence uncontroverted, based solely on defendants' affidavits and depositions. Defendants had not been in Colorado for about eighteen months, left in September 1951 due to a heart condition requiring sea level, had no place of residence in Colorado after selling the home, and unequivocally intended to establish permanent residence in California. They settled in Ventura, obtained employment, purchased California automobile tags and operator's licenses, registered to vote in California in March 1952, and bought lots for a permanent home. The court stated that legal residence is determined by intention, supported by acts. Defendants' voter registration in California, which occurred before the action commenced, was compelling evidence of intent to change residence. The burden to prove Colorado residence shifted to plaintiffs, who failed to meet it. The trial court therefore erred in denying the motion to quash and lacked jurisdiction over defendants' persons. The rule to show cause was made absolute.

On October 29, 2018, Lion Air Flight 610, a Boeing 737 MAX 8, crashed into the Java Sea, killing all 189 people onboard. On March 10, 2019, Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, also a 737 MAX 8, crashed, killing all 157 onboard. Boeing's initial response to the first crash focused on Lion Air's maintenance and pilots, but the company later issued a bulletin about erroneous angle-of-attack data causing uncommanded nose-down movement. The new Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System (MCAS) was designed to automatically push the nose down when a high angle of attack was detected.

The 737 MAX was developed on a compressed timeline to compete with Airbus's A320neo. MCAS was revised during testing to operate at low speeds with increased stabilizer movement and relied on data from a single AOA sensor, creating a single point of failure. The AOA disagree alert was not operable unless an airline purchased an optional AOA indicator. Boeing positioned MCAS as a minor modification during FAA certification, and the FAA did not conduct a detailed review. Boeing did not communicate formal safety risk assessments or a significant MCAS revision to key FAA certification engineers. Boeing sought to avoid simulator training for pilots, and MCAS was not included in required training.

After the 1997 merger with McDonnell Douglas, some employees perceived a cultural shift from an engineering focus to a shareholder value focus. Internal communications later showed employees had expressed concerns about the hurried timeline and management undermining quality. Following the second crash, the 737 MAX was grounded worldwide. Boeing faced significant financial costs, including compensation to customers and lost orders. Multiple investigations followed, and the FAA later required simulator training for pilots operating the 737 MAX.

This study examined research expectations for US mathematics education faculty, focusing on institution type (R1, R2, Other), department type (education vs. mathematics), and research commitment (percent time for research). A survey of 404 target population respondents found that expectations vary. On average, faculty are expected to publish about 1.64 papers per year, with research journal articles valued most. R1 faculty typically expect about 2.25 papers per year and 40% research time, and they value research articles highly but other publication types less than R2 or Other faculty. R2 faculty expect about 1.5 papers per year and are more likely to have explicit written expectations. Other faculty expect about 1 paper per year with lower research time. Department type showed few differences, though mathematics departments reported 0.309 fewer expected papers and valued conference proceedings and pursuing funding more, while education departments valued first authorship more. Higher research commitment correlated with more expected papers, less explicit written documentation, and greater emphasis on sole/lead authorship and obtaining funding. Surprising results included variability in workload distribution, 11% of R1 faculty expecting three or more papers yearly, and R2 institutions more often having written expectations. The study suggests faculty and departments clarify and document research expectations.

This work studies the orbital and spin Edelstein effects (OEE and SEE) in doped monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) in the 2H structure, using MoS2 as a representative example, under an out-of-plane gate field. The gate field breaks the mirror symmetry σh, changing the point group from D3h to C3v and enabling a non-zero Edelstein effect. Both electron and hole doping are considered, as they have been experimentally realized. A minimal 5×5 Hamiltonian in the metal d orbital subspace is derived from a tight-binding model including chalcogen orbitals via Löwdin downfolding, with parameters fitted to density functional theory (DFT) bands. The Hamiltonian consists of an unperturbed part, an electric field part introducing parameters γ1 and γ2, and spin-orbit coupling. At the band edges, the effective Hamiltonian reduces to a combination of Ising and Rashba terms.

The gate field induces chiral orbital and spin textures with in-plane moments. For hole doping, at the Γ valley the orbital texture is counter-clockwise for both upper and lower valence bands, while the spin textures are opposite, causing the OEE from the two bands to add and the SEE to partially cancel. The Γ pocket dominates the Edelstein response when occupied, but requires a critical hole concentration. A small compressive strain reduces the energy separation between the Γ and K/K' valleys, allowing the Γ pocket to be populated at lower hole densities and significantly enhancing both OEE and SEE. For electron doping, the conduction band minimum at K/K' yields an OEE that is several times larger than the SEE, with the OEE increasing linearly with electron concentration. The computed Edelstein susceptibilities in TMDs are on the order of 10⁻⁸–10⁻⁷ µB V⁻¹ m, which is one to two orders of magnitude larger than values reported for other material systems, indicating that TMDs are an ideal platform for studying the orbital Edelstein effect.

The paper proposes a three-phase hybrid Constraint Acquisition (CA) framework to address over-fitting of global constraints. Constraint Programming faces a modeling bottleneck, and CA automates learning. Existing passive methods over-fit from limited examples, active methods have high query burdens, and hybrid methods lack mechanisms for over-fitted global constraints. The framework begins with a passive phase that generates candidate global constraints (e.g., AllDifferent, Sum, Count) from few positive examples via pattern detection and parameter inference, while pruning a fixed-arity bias. The core is a Query-Driven Interactive Refinement phase that assigns machine learning-based prior confidence scores, posts targeted oracle queries, updates beliefs via Bayesian updates, and accepts or rejects candidates based on thresholds. Rejected constraints undergo subset exploration, generating subconstraints by removing variables from first, middle, or last positions to recover valid substructures, with adaptive query budget allocation. A final active learning phase (MQuAcq-2) learns remaining fixed-arity constraints. Contributions include the dedicated refinement phase, subset exploration, and integration of ML priors with Bayesian confidence. Empirical validation shows high accuracy and manageable query complexity. The passage also reviews CSPs, global constraints, and related CA work, noting that existing hybrid approaches lack explicit over-fitting correction.

The Keltner Channel, created by commodity trader Chester W. Keltner in the 1960s, is a technical analysis tool consisting of three lines: a middle line (typically a 20-period exponential moving average of price) and upper and lower bands set at a multiple (commonly 2) of the Average True Range (ATR) above and below the middle line. It is also called Keltner Bands. Unlike Bollinger Bands, which use standard deviation, Keltner Channels use ATR, making them less responsive. They are viewed as leading indicators because they incorporate volatility. Traders use them for mean reversion (buying when price breaks below the lower band, selling when it breaks above the upper band) or momentum (buying on upper band breakouts). A backtest of a mean reversion strategy on SPY showed a 77% win rate and 6.3% CAGR, while a momentum strategy with a 30-day period and 1.3 ATR multiplier yielded a 3.6% CAGR. The indicator does not repaint. A Bollinger squeeze within the Keltner Channel refers to Bollinger Bands contracting inside the Keltner Channel, indicating consolidation and potential breakout. Common settings are a 20-period EMA and multiplier of 2, but optimal parameters vary by market. Traders should avoid over-reliance on the indicator and consider broader market context. Entry points often occur on band breakouts, exits when price reaches the opposite band. Position sizing should account for volatility, account size, and risk tolerance. The channel's purpose is to identify trends, volatility, and overbought/oversold conditions.

The lecture covers trabecular bone and osteoporosis modeling using Voronoi honeycombs. Finite element analysis of 2D Voronoi honeycombs showed elastic moduli close to analytical models, but compressive strength was lower than periodic honeycombs due to a broader distribution of strains, with a minimum strength near the transition between elastic buckling and plastic yielding (around 5% relative density). Models that removed struts caused greater reductions in modulus and strength than uniform thinning, reaching a percolation threshold where properties drop to zero; the 3D percolation threshold was 50%. Metal foams made from titanium or tantalum via processes such as replica, fugitive phase, foaming agent, freeze casting, and selective laser sintering were discussed as potential bone substitute coatings or implants. This study by Hanne Rinholm, Ida Heiberg Solem, and Inger Ulleberg explores dialogic classroom practices through two cases: a pre-service teacher music education choir project and an upper-primary mathematics class. The lecture covers linearized gravity, where spacetime is a small perturbation from flat spacetime. The perturbation is decomposed into gauge-invariant degrees of freedom; the spatial transverse-traceless part \(h_{ij}^{\text{TT}}\) satisfies a wave equation and represents radiative degrees of freedom, with only two independent components corresponding to gravitational wave polarizations.

To understand physical effects, the lecturer considers two nearby freely falling bodies. A naive geodesic calculation shows no acceleration because the coordinates follow the bodies. Instead, relative effects are examined. Bouncing light between the bodies yields a round-trip travel time that depends on \(h_{xx}^{\text{TT}}\), illustrating how a detector like LIGO could measure gravitational waves via timing. Using geodesic deviation, the separation vector’s acceleration is given by Riemann curvature components. For a ring of test particles, a sinusoidal \(h_{xx}\) (plus polarization) causes stretching along x and squeezing along y, alternating; \(h_{xy}\) (cross polarization) causes stretching along 45-degree lines. These are the two polarization states.

To compute \(h_{ij}^{\text{TT}}\) from a source, one solves the linearized Einstein equation in Lorentz gauge, obtaining a wave equation for the trace-reversed metric perturbation. The retarded solution is approximated for a distant source, replacing distance with \(r\). Using the tensor virial theorem, the integral of spatial stress-energy components becomes the second time derivative of the quadrupole moment \(I_{ij}\). The result is \(\bar{h}_{ij} = (2G/r) \, d^2 I_{ij}/dt^2\). To extract the TT part, one expands in plane waves, imposes transversality (orthogonal to the wave vector) using the projection tensor \(P_{ij}\), then removes the trace in the two-dimensional subspace orthogonal to propagation. The final quadrupole formula for \(h_{ij}^{\text{TT}}\) involves projection tensors acting on the second time derivative of the quadrupole moment, multiplied by \(2G/r\).

The study validated a Longitudinal Grade of Membership (L-GoM) model of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression, originally developed using clinic-based, non-Hispanic white patients with mild AD (Predictors 2). The model was applied to initial visit data to generate individual-specific predictions of survival and FTC prevalence over 7.5 years. For AD nonreverters (n=118) and MCI cases (n=123), predicted survival and FTC curves closely matched observed data, supporting model validity. The model did not fit AD reverters (n=32), who were likely misdiagnosed. Subgroup analyses by ethnicity and sex also showed good fit. The findings extend the model’s applicability to community-dwelling, multiethnic populations and to MCI, and validate a web-based calculator. Limitations include a small sample of non-Hispanic nonwhites and the impact of AD misdiagnosis.

Fibonacci trading involves using Fibonacci tools—retracement, expansion, and fan—to identify potential support and resistance levels on price charts. The expansion tool uses the size of a pullback to project how far the next impulse wave might extend, aiding profit target estimation. The fan tool draws trendlines at Fibonacci levels to show dynamic support/resistance. There is no universally best timeframe; choice depends on trading style, though higher timeframes may be more reliable, and backtesting is recommended to determine effectiveness. Despite anecdotal claims of success, the passage notes a lack of scientific evidence for why prices should adhere to Fibonacci ratios. A cited backtest by Clarissa Gunawan on Vanguard ETFs found that a passive buy-and-hold strategy outperformed an active Fibonacci-based strategy, suggesting Fibonacci retracements may not be a strong standalone tool, though they can still help mark support/resistance and profit targets when used cautiously with other indicators. The authors conclude that other, backtested strategies are preferable. FAQ responses reiterate that Fibonacci trading uses ratios from the Fibonacci sequence to spot reversal zones, list common ratios, and express skepticism about its effectiveness for day trading or crypto without positive backtests.

The present disclosure relates to wireless communications, specifically applying scheduling offset for power saving in next generation wireless networks. A method for a user equipment (UE) includes receiving a power saving signal comprising a minimum applicable K0min that indicates a minimum scheduling offset restriction between a physical downlink control channel (PDCCH) and a physical downlink shared channel (PDSCH), determining an application delay based on a predefined value, and applying the minimum scheduling offset restriction after the application delay. During the application delay, another scheduling offset may be applied, which may be configured by radio resource control (RRC) signaling. The power saving signal may be received through downlink control information (DCI). After the application delay, if a second DCI includes a K value, the UE applies the scheduling offset if K is larger than K0min, otherwise forgoes the restriction. The UE may send HARQ feedback for the power saving signal after a time offset specified in the signal or via RRC signaling. A UE apparatus with a processor and computer-readable media is also provided. The disclosure further addresses HARQ feedback mechanisms, including adding a bit in the HARQ codebook for the power saving signal, and default beam operation enhancements for power saving state, such as selecting spatial domain filters based on active antenna panels or control resource set (CORESET) configurations. Various implementations detail configurations for K timing sets, PUCCH resources, and CSI reporting associated with power saving indicators.

The Side Screen Offense is a two-player screen and roll isolation, the most used play in the NBA. It can be initiated by a point guard dribble-clearing the wing or passing to the wing and basket cutting to the weakside. Teams often run it on the left for right-handed players and right for left-handed players to enable strong-hand dribble penetration into the middle. The basic option is for the guard/wing to drive over the on-ball screen set by a post, with options to turn the corner for a layup, pull up if the defense goes under, return pass to the rolling post if they switch, or kick out to a shooter if a weakside defender helps.

The offense relies on eight defensive reads and counters:
1. Defender chases over: ballhandler drives to the basket; if baseline helps, drop pass to post; if wing sags, kick out for three.
2. Defender goes under: pull-up jumper.
3. Defender cheats over early: drive opposite; if baseline helps, drop pass.
4. Defender fights through: crossover or behind-the-back dribble back over the screen for a jumper or drive.
5. Defense shows and recovers: screener pops to the wing for a shot or drive; ballhandler can also drive hard.
6. Defense switches: feed the screener rolling/post-up (post isolation if smaller defender mismatched inside); if bigger defender mismatched outside, clear out for outside isolation; if defenders anticipate switch, screener slips the screen.
7. Defender denies/disrupts: screener back cuts for a lob pass.
8. Defense traps: ballhandler strings out the double team, screener pops, weakside post flashes to middle, forming a 2-1-2 alignment; move the ball with sharp passes.

Entry variations include High Post Rub (point guard passes to wing, rubs off high post screen, then side screen action if no pass), Power/Motion (out of 1-4 high, down screens for wings, then side screen), and Horns (point guard dribble clears, O5 slips a screen, O4 sets a second side screen; "Boston" option adds a back screen for the roller).

When the side screen does not yield a shot, teams flow into continuity options: Flex (pick-the-picker action), Triangle Game (pass to weakside, screen-the-screener), Single/Double Motion (back out, down screens, double screens), Weakside Double Screen (screener pops, weakside double back screens), or Baseline Down Screen (baseline down screen and weakside back screen).

Teaching emphasizes execution and coordination; the ballhandler and screener must function as one unit with proper footwork, timing, and non-verbal communication. Drills include 2-on-2 and 3-on-3 combinations and scrimmaging. Individual offensive skill development is integral. Game strategies: scout opponents to anticipate defensive reads, vary alignments and entries, attack weakest defenders, and use side screens as an organized continuity as the shot clock winds down. Even if not using the offense, one must know how to defend it, as it is widely used.

The lecture covers life cycle assessment (LCA) methodology, using a hand dryer study as an example. The goal is to understand LCA steps and the decisions involved, such as setting boundaries and handling uncertainty. LCA is defined by ISO standards as compiling an inventory of inputs and outputs, evaluating potential environmental impacts, and interpreting results relative to the study's objectives. It takes a cradle-to-grave view.

The methodology has four stages. First, goal and scope definition: deciding the product, purpose, and audience. The hand dryer study's functional unit was a pair of dried hands, enabling comparison of systems like the Dyson Airblade, Xlerator, and paper towels. The study had both internal (engineering) and external (comparative assertion) purposes, which drove requirements like third-party review. System boundaries included cut-off rules (e.g., excluding items under 1% of impact, with total exclusions under 5%) and excluding capital goods. Allocation issues arose with open-loop recycling of paper towels.

Second, inventory analysis: building a system model and quantifying inputs (raw materials, energy) and outputs (emissions). The study used bills of materials and matched them with inventory databases like ecoinvent. When data were missing, proxy data or estimates were used. Assumptions about manufacturing scrap rates were necessary.

Third, impact analysis: classification and characterization. The study used global warming potential, cumulative energy demand, water use, and the IMPACT 2002+ method. The latter aggregates multiple midpoint categories (e.g., carcinogens, ecotoxicity) into endpoint indicators like human health and ecosystem quality, ultimately into eco-points, which involves value judgments.

Fourth, interpretation: relating results back to goals. The study performed sensitivity analysis (one-factor-at-a-time), scenario uncertainty analysis (Monte Carlo simulations varying multiple parameters), and bill-of-activities uncertainty analysis. Key sensitive parameters were electricity grid and drying time. Despite overlaps in uncertainty distributions, the Dyson Airblade generally showed the lowest environmental impact under most scenarios.

Fusion trees are a static data structure for the predecessor problem on a word RAM, achieving O(log_w n) time. They use a B-tree with branching factor w^(1/5). Each node stores k ≈ w^(1/5) keys. To search in constant time per node, the structure employs sketching: only the “important bits” (the at most k−1 bit positions where the keys branch in a binary trie) are kept. An approximate sketch is computed by masking out non-important bits, then multiplying by a carefully chosen integer to compress the important bits into a range of size O(w^(4/5)) without collisions, preserving order. Sketches of all keys in a node are concatenated into a single word. A query sketch is compared in parallel to all key sketches via subtraction and masking, yielding a monotone bit sequence whose 0-to-1 transition indicates the predecessor rank. A de-sketchification step corrects errors when the query falls off the trie by finding the longest common prefix, constructing a corrected query, and repeating the sketch search. The most significant set bit operation, needed for longest common prefix, is implemented in constant time by splitting the word into √w clusters of √w bits, identifying non-empty clusters via subtraction and masking, perfectly sketching the summary vector, and using parallel comparison to locate the first 1 bit. The overall structure requires linear space and polynomial preprocessing.

This study investigated the association between malaria and malnutrition and the impact of intermittent preventive therapy (IPTsc) on nutritional status in school-age children in North-East Tanzania. It analyzed secondary data from a cross-sectional baseline survey and a randomized controlled open-label trial with three arms: dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP), artesunate-amodiaquine (ASAQ), and standard care. At baseline, malaria prevalence was 27%; among children ≤10 years, 23% were underweight, 21% were stunted, and 28% were thin. Malaria infection was significantly associated with stunting (AOR=1.78, 95% CI 1.36–2.33, p<0.001), and low socioeconomic status was associated with underweight (AOR=1.50, 95% CI 1.13–2.01, p=0.006). During the 20-month follow-up, changes in weight, height, and BMI over time did not differ significantly between the DP or ASAQ groups and the control group. Age and sex significantly influenced growth. The study concludes that malaria and malnutrition impose a double burden, and IPTsc did not improve nutritional status. It recommends integrated public health interventions combining malaria control with nutritional programs, including food availability in schools and community nutritional education.

The NVIDIA Tesla T4 is an inferencing solution for hyperscale data centers, featuring 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 130 TOPS INT8 and 260 TOPS INT4. The Tesla T4 includes 16 GB of memory and 320 GB/sec bandwidth, an enhanced video engine supporting HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 decode, and Multi-Process Service for improved small-batch inference.

The Turing GPU architecture introduces GDDR6 memory, delivering 14 Gbps signaling and 20% power efficiency improvement over GDDR5X, along with larger L2 caches and improved memory compression, resulting in up to 50% higher effective bandwidth. It also features an enhanced display engine with DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K support, and HDR tone mapping. NVLink replaces SLI bridges for GPU-to-GPU data transfers, providing up to 100 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth on TU102.

Turing includes RT Cores for hardware-accelerated ray tracing, enabling real-time hybrid rendering that combines rasterization, ray tracing, and AI. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection tests, offloading the SM. Denoising techniques reduce the number of rays needed. NVIDIA NGX technology uses Tensor Cores for AI-based features like DLSS (Deep Learning Super-Sampling), which improves performance and image quality, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Additional features include Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders for more efficient geometry processing, Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allowing shading rate control per 16x16 pixel region for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering, Texture Space Shading (TSS) decoupling shading from screen space, and Multi-View Rendering (MVR) supporting up to four views per pass. Turing also supports VirtualLink over USB-C for VR headsets, reducing cable complexity.

The TU104 GPU, used in Tesla T4 and GeForce RTX 2080, contains 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores. The TU106 GPU, used in GeForce RTX 2070, has 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores. A new workload-based metric, RTX-OPS, combines contributions from Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations to represent hybrid rendering performance.

A study compared immune responses to Covishield (adenovirus vectored) and Covaxin (inactivated, TLR7/8 agonist adjuvanted) in 691 Indian adults aged 18-45, stratified by baseline serostatus. In seronegative participants, Covishield elicited higher seroconversion rates (98.3% vs 74.4% after second dose) and higher anti-spike antibody geometric mean titers (1272.1 vs 75.4 BAU/ml). In seropositive participants, Covishield also showed higher seroconversion (91.7% vs 66.9% after second dose) and higher titers (2089.07 vs 585.7 BAU/ml). Covishield induced significant neutralizing antibodies in both groups, while Covaxin did not. Covishield generated spike-specific CD4 and CD8 T cell responses in seronegative individuals; Covaxin elicited only CD4 responses in antibody responders. In seropositive individuals, neither vaccine significantly expanded spike-specific T cells. Non-responsiveness was associated with higher pre-vaccination antibody titers. The Omicron wave overlapped with the study, preventing durability assessment, but data suggested Covaxin-induced antibodies remained near the seropositivity cutoff, while Covishield antibodies declined before increasing after asymptomatic Omicron infection. Covishield elicited broader and more potent ACE2 inhibition against wild-type, Delta, and Omicron variants than Covaxin. The study concludes Covishield induced stronger humoral and cellular immunity than Covaxin.

The Yankee concept is a pro-style shot play utilizing a post-dig combination to attack the deep middle of the field. An AI tool called Waldo scanned over 430,000 Reddit posts about cannabis use and flagged over 28,000 as potentially describing harmful side effects. Researchers verified that 86 percent of a sample of 250 flagged posts indeed represented problematic experiences. Waldo was trained on a smaller set of 10,000 posts that had been manually labeled. In testing, it outperformed ChatGPT by producing fewer false positives, but did not outperform human reviewers. Public health researchers note that social media contains unfiltered health experiences from people who may not report through official channels. Monitoring such posts could help protect consumers, though it remains uncertain if Waldo would work for other drugs or products. Future use would require ethical implementation and privacy protections, and could aid countries lacking robust side-effect reporting systems.

The passage argues that traditional construction apprenticeships are highly selective, favoring those with pre-existing skills and advanced coursework, which locks out motivated but less-prepared individuals. Pre-apprenticeships are short-term programs that provide career exposure, professional and technical skills, mentorship, and industry-recognized credentials, helping participants enter apprenticeships. However, pre-apprenticeships lack funding, limiting their capacity and ability to collect outcomes data, perpetuating underinvestment. Proposed solutions include financing wraparound support through zero-percent loans or emergency credit with repayment tied to earnings increases, and partnerships where employers repay loans. Collecting better data to demonstrate outcomes is key to attracting grants and philanthropic investment. The passage concludes that strategic investment in construction pathways will bolster the talent pipeline, promote economic mobility, and create best practices for other industries.

The present invention relates to video signal encoding and decoding methods and apparatuses. In a decoding method, it is determined whether a current block is merged with a neighbor block; motion information and a weight prediction parameter are obtained based on the determination; a reference block is selected using the motion information; and a prediction block is generated by applying the weight prediction parameter. If merged, the weight prediction parameter is set identical to the neighbor block's; otherwise, it is obtained from a bitstream. Motion vector precision may be upwardly adjusted using reconstructed pixels adjacent to the current block. For intra-prediction, information of an intra-prediction mode is decoded, intra-prediction is performed, and it is determined whether to correct a prediction sample; if so, the sample is corrected. Decoding the intra-prediction mode may involve generating candidate modes, checking if a candidate matches the current block's mode, and determining the mode based on that. Candidate modes may be based on frequency of use of upper and left neighbor blocks. Alternatively, a difference value between the current block's mode and a previous block's mode is decoded, and the mode is determined from the previous mode and the difference. In an encoding method, motion information and a weight prediction parameter are determined, and information indicating whether they are merged with a neighbor block is encoded. If merged, the weight prediction parameter is set identical to the neighbor block's; if not, information related to the weight prediction parameter is encoded. Motion vector precision adjustment information may be encoded. For intra-prediction, an intra-prediction mode is determined, a prediction sample is corrected, and information indicating whether correction is performed is encoded. Candidate modes may be generated, and information indicating whether a candidate matches the intra-prediction mode is encoded. A difference value between intra-prediction modes of the current and previous blocks may be encoded.

Microsoft Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended September 30, 2015. Swing trading involves taking positions for a short number of days, typically between one day and a few weeks. The article backtests six swing trading indicators on the S&P 500 using the SPY ETF: Relative Strength Index (RSI), Internal Bar Strength (IBS), Stochastic, Bollinger Bands, WilliamsVixFix, and Williams %R. Risk-adjusted return is calculated as the geometric annual return divided by the exposure percentage, and the RAR/MDD ratio is used to compare strategies. The best time frame for swing trading indicators is between 1 and 15 days. Based on the backtests, Williams %R is regarded as the best indicator because it showed the most stable and solid results across different variables and had the lowest average maximum drawdown, indicating better risk-adjusted returns.

Organized patriotism and national loyalty over local pride are essential for national greatness, requiring cooperation across sections and classes. An efficient education system is next in importance. The article demonstrates backtesting a MACD trading strategy in Python. It uses yfinance to download Apple historical data, pandas for manipulation, and matplotlib for plotting. The MACD indicator is calculated as the 12-period EMA minus the 26-period EMA of closing prices, with a 9-period EMA signal line and histogram (MACD minus signal). A regime column is generated: 1 when histogram ≥ 0, else 0, applied to the next row to avoid look-ahead bias. Strategy returns are computed. The MACD strategy achieved a 15.04% CAGR versus 19.07% for buy and hold, with only 51.13% time invested. The strategy is for informational purposes only.

The passage introduces 3DPCNet, a pose-only rectification module that maps any camera-centered 3D skeleton into a fixed body-centered canonical frame to address view-dependent variability in monocular 3D human pose estimation. The architecture uses a hybrid encoder with parallel graph convolutional and transformer branches, fused via gated cross-attention, to predict a continuous 6D rotation representation. This is converted to a valid rotation matrix in SO(3) using Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization, and an optional residual head fine-tunes joint positions. Training employs a self-supervised strategy with synthetically rotated poses and a composite loss including pose reconstruction, geodesic rotation, cycle consistency, perceptual, and regularization terms.

Experiments on the MM-Fi dataset show that 3DPCNet reduces rotation error from 20–22° to 3–4° and MPJPE by approximately 27%, with stable performance across cross-subject and cross-environment protocols. On the TotalCapture dataset, canonicalized poses from off-the-shelf estimators produce wrist acceleration signals that more closely match ground-truth IMU data than a geometric baseline, particularly under challenging lateral viewpoints. The method is estimator-agnostic and requires only 3D pose data.

Limitations include potential non-rigid deviations from the residual head, no absolute scale recovery, dependence on input pose quality, and training on pose-space augmentation rather than real multi-view imagery. Future directions involve constraining the residual toward rigid behavior, temporal extension, scale estimation, and clinical validation.

The use of ICT has fueled the rise of online education in African universities since the 1990s, coinciding with more flexible higher education policies. By 2007, online courses accounted for a significant portion of student enrollment. ICT policies and telecom deregulation improved infrastructure, yet Africa's internet penetration rate remains low compared to other regions. Online education faces challenges including weak ICT policies, poor infrastructure, limited internet access particularly in rural areas, lack of instructor digital skills, and resistance to technology. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed a lack of preparedness for online learning.

Africa has experienced significant turmoil from various conflicts, with more than three-quarters of nations facing warfare in the last three decades. These conflicts have caused displacement, trauma, and a brain drain of professionals. Wars have disrupted academic programmes, destroyed infrastructure, and hindered the deployment of ICT resources in educational institutions. Online education is presented as a lifeline during wartime, allowing continued learning and fostering digital skills.

A bibliometric analysis was conducted using the Scopus database, searching for publications on "wartime and online education" from 2000 to 2024. After screening, 53 documents were analyzed. The findings show the United States had the most publications, followed by Ukraine. No African countries were among the represented nations. Publications on the topic surged in 2023. The analysis reveals a significant research gap regarding the intersection of wartime and online learning in African higher education institutions, despite the continent's prolonged conflicts. The study calls for urgent research to address these challenges.

The lecture begins with a review of VCG mechanisms for private value social choice problems. It defines primitives (types, probability distribution, social alternatives, additively separable utilities) and the utilitarian solution. A mechanism consists of strategy sets, an outcome function, and transfers. The VCG mechanism asks players to announce types, chooses the utilitarian action based on announced types, and charges each player the negative externality they impose on others. The second-price auction is a special case. VCG implements the utilitarian solution in dominant strategies, is essentially the only way to achieve dominant-strategy implementation, is not budget balanced, and may be infeasible when the set of social alternatives is very large.

The lecture then focuses on Google. Google dominates search with over 90% worldwide market share, earns enormous revenues and profits, and uses those profits to enter other markets. The US Department of Justice and several states have filed antitrust suits. Google runs an auction for every search query to determine which ads to display. Early Yahoo! used a first-price auction that led to unstable, cycling bids. Google’s system allows advertisers to submit standing per-click bids; when a query occurs, Google multiplies each bid by a quality score, ranks by the product, and charges a clicked ad an amount equal to the lowest bid that would have maintained its position (a generalized second-price rule). Quality scores are crucial to prevent low-relevance ads from dominating.

The Edelman-Ostrovsky-Schwarz model treats ad positions as prizes with fixed click volumes. It models the auction as an English clock auction where bidders drop out. Truth-telling is not an equilibrium with multiple slots; bidders shade their bids. The equilibrium shading formula results in each bidder making exactly the same payments as in a VCG mechanism. This VCG equivalence implies the outcome is an ex-post equilibrium (bidders do not want to change bids after seeing others’ bids), the allocation is efficient, and the payments flow to Google, making it difficult for competitors to undercut on price without choosing inferior ads.

The Athey-Ellison model endogenizes consumer search. Consumers have a need and incur search costs per click. Advertisers have private quality (probability of meeting the need). If bids are monotone in quality, consumers search top-down. The bidding game remains tractable despite common-value elements. A key theorem shows that with uniformly distributed search costs, consumer surplus and social welfare are maximized at the same reserve price, and expected social welfare is three times expected consumer surplus. Reserve prices can improve welfare by signaling ad quality to consumers, increasing clicks. There is an inherent conflict: any departure from the consumer-optimal reserve price benefits Google but harms both advertisers and consumers.

The lecture briefly mentions two other papers. Anderson and Renault endogenize firms’ prices and find multiple equilibria where either high- or low-quality firms can occupy the top position, with the top firm setting low prices to deter further search. Armstrong and Zhou study platform information design, showing that the consumer-optimal outcome is unattainable because revealing product match information gives firms market power; the seller-optimal outcome can sometimes be achieved by revealing only which product is preferred, not by how much. Consumer- and profit-maximizing information structures differ, but there is limited scope to alter social welfare.

Under the new federal tax law, payroll withholding tables changed, with about 90% of workers expected to see extra cash in paychecks starting in February. Families with children under 17 benefit from the child tax credit doubling to $2,000 per qualifying child in 2018, with higher income limits for eligibility. Taxpayers may need to fill out a new W-4 later to avoid owing taxes in 2019. The IRS is updating its withholding calculator by end of February. The standard deduction increases to $24,000 for married joint filers and $12,000 for singles in 2018, leading many to stop itemizing. Some deductions change: home equity loan interest is no longer deductible, and there is a $10,000 cap on combined state and local tax deductions. The passage describes methods for localizing and classifying abnormalities in medical images. One embodiment uses a multi-task network with a localization network and a classification network that are jointly trained in a multi-phase procedure. Another embodiment detects an abnormality by deleting different portions of an input medical image to create incomplete images, generating synthesized images with a trained generative adversarial network, determining a normal image from the synthesized images, and detecting the abnormality based on the input and normal images. A further embodiment provides a method for training a deep learning model using multi-site datasets, involving a training stage that iteratively updates a pretrained model with reordered sub-datasets based on similarity, and a deployment stage that optimizes the trained model by selectively updating with reordered labeled deployment data based on uncertainty.

This study examined perineuronal nets (PNNs) and extracellular matrix (ECM) molecules in the hippocampus of human subjects with substance use disorders (SUD), major depressive disorder (MDD), comorbid SUD/MDD, and controls, and in rhesus monkeys with chronic alcohol self-administration. Postmortem hippocampal samples were analyzed using WFA lectin labeling for PNNs and WFA-glia, and qPCR for gene expression. In subjects with SUD, numerical densities of PNNs were significantly increased in CA1 stratum oriens (SO), CA2 SO and SP, CA3 SO, and CA4, with cocaine history as a significant covariate associated with decreased PNNs. WFA-labeled glial cells were increased in CA4 and dentate gyrus. Gene expression of parvalbumin (Pvb) and Vamp2 was increased, while Mmp9 and Ctss were decreased, and Chsy1 was increased. In subjects with MDD, PNN densities were decreased in CA1 SO and SP, increased in CA4; WFA-glia were increased in dentate gyrus, CA3 SP, CA2 SP and SO. Pvb, Vamp2, and Ctss expression were increased. In subjects with comorbid SUD/MDD, PNNs were decreased in CA1 SP, increased in CA2 SP; WFA-glia were decreased in dentate gyrus, CA4, CA3 SP, CA2 SP, CA1 SP and SO. Gene expression showed increased Pvb, Acan, Chsy1, and decreased Gfap. In rhesus monkeys with chronic alcohol self-administration, PNN densities were significantly increased in combined hippocampal subfields, CA1 SO, CA3 SO and SP, and WFA-glia were increased in dentate gyrus. The findings represent the first evidence for increased PNN densities in the hippocampus of subjects with SUD and monkeys with chronic alcohol, linking preclinical evidence to humans. Increased PNNs, decreased ECM proteolytic expression, and altered synaptic markers suggest that enhanced PNN composition may stabilize contextual reward-associated synapses in CA1, potentially contributing to context-induced relapse. In contrast, MDD showed generally opposite effects, and comorbid SUD/MDD showed mixed or absent changes, highlighting the importance of considering comorbidity in SUD neuropathology. The study suggests PNNs and ECM molecules as potential therapeutic targets for cue-induced relapse.

SOS full court pressure forces offensive reactions, wears down opponents, and exploits fatigue-induced errors for transition baskets. A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted at Tesseney Community Hospital, Eritrea, from June 2019 to May 2020, including 165 patients admitted for scorpion stings. The study aimed to describe clinical features and outcomes. Patients had a history of scorpion sting and had seen or killed the scorpion. The male-to-female ratio was 0.94:1, and 61.2% were older than 15 years. Most stings occurred on the foot (64.8%), at night (62.4%), and indoors (56.4%). Black scorpions were most commonly identified (38.8%). Common symptoms included localized pain (70.3%), sweating (56.4%), vomiting (33.9%), and paraesthesia (29.2%). According to Abroug’s classification, 43.6% had class III, 35.8% class II, and 20.6% class I. The case fatality rate was 4.8% (8 deaths), with fatalities largely associated with class III stings. Children under 15 had more severe symptoms (p=0.006). Treatment varied by class: class I received local anesthesia and oral analgesics; class II-III received nifedipine and/or scorpion antivenom (15.2%), diazepam, IV fluids, and antibiotics. Scorpion sting cases peaked in summer (93%), especially September and October. The study concluded that scorpion envenomation severity is higher in children, and recommended preventive education, equipping health facilities with prazosin, and further research on scorpion habitats and community awareness.

The report states that the United States consistently opposed foreign aggression in Hawaii and contemplated annexation as a contingent necessity. After the 1875 reciprocity treaty, policy was to assert exclusive commercial rights and support the Hawaiian Government as long as it protected US interests. Secretary Blaine in 1881 declared that if benevolent neutrality became impracticable, the US would seek an American solution. The report also notes the 1820 appointment of John C. Jones as agent for commerce and seamen, with general supervision of American interests.

Official fuel economy figures come from the outdated New European Driving Cycle (NEDC), which has not been updated since 1997 and contains numerous loopholes. These include no sustained motorway driving, allowing eco mode use, switching off ancillary loads, removing parts to reduce weight, overinflating tyres, and a 4% arbitrary reduction. From September 2017, a tougher Worldwide-harmonised Light vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) will replace the NEDC, with full compliance by September 2018.

Which? conducts its own mpg tests using the WLTP cycle, including cold and hot cycles and a sustained motorway cycle. Tests are run in a lab on a rolling road with realistic conditions: default driving mode, air conditioning and lights on, no weight removal, and tyre pressures per the manual. Results are not adjusted. Hybrid cars are tested with specific battery charge states. Air pollution emissions are also measured; cars with very high emissions cannot be Best Buys. To prevent cheating, suspicious NOx results are verified with on-road Portable Emissions Measuring System (PEMS) tests. Which? publishes accurate mpg data for over 700 vehicles, testing around 120 new cars annually.

The random walk theory, popularized by Burton Malkiel in *A Random Walk Down Wall Street*, assumes stock prices move completely unpredictably, with a 50% probability of rising or falling, making historical price analysis futile. The random walk trading strategy applies this by using random entries and exits, emphasizing diversification to spread risk across many stocks or a broad market index fund, rather than trying to time the market. The strategy aims to mitigate losses from poorly performing stocks and benefit from the market's long-term upward drift. The passage compares the random walk theory to the efficient market hypothesis (EMH), which states prices reflect all available information. Both conclude that consistently outperforming the market is nearly impossible and support passive investing, but they contradict each other: random walk implies irrational markets, while EMH assumes rational pricing. Both are based on strict, unrealistic assumptions, and Warren Buffett is quoted criticizing EMH. Backtests of a random entry strategy on S&P 500 (SPY) showed positive results (average gain 0.37%, profit factor 1.7, max drawdown 13%), attributed to the stock market's tailwind. A backtest on gold (GLD) produced a negative average gain (-0.08%), underperforming gold's positive drift. The passage concludes that most short-term price action is random, but the stock market offers an edge due to inflation and productivity gains, and advocates quantified backtesting to find viable strategies. The FAQ reiterates that the strategy relies on diversification and the 50% probability assumption, and that both random walk and EMH suggest difficulty in beating the market.

Anthurium filters ammonia and xylene. This South American plant has red, pink, or white flowers. It needs indirect light, dampness, 18-21°C, winter misting, and yearly repotting in a holed pot, then biennially. Sap may cause allergies.

An offensive goal kick aims to retain possession and launch an attack. It is awarded when the ball crosses the defenders’ end line last touched by an attacker, taken from the goal area (6 yards out). The ball must be stationary; opponents should be outside the penalty area (18 yards) until kicked. The ball is live upon being kicked and moving; the kicker cannot touch it again before another player, per Law 16.

For ages 10 and under, fields are smaller and build-out lines are used. This line, parallel to the goal line, requires defenders to retreat behind it before challenging, promoting playing out from the back and prohibiting long kicks. The simplest goal kick places the ball at the goal area corner and passes to the best dribbler nearby, who dribbles upfield. A more advanced setup uses a target receiver inside the sideline and a secondary receiver up the sideline inside the build-out line. The kick goes to the target, who can dribble or pass to the secondary based on coverage; if the secondary is open, the kick may go directly to them. Key concepts: keep the ball wide and upfield, never send it across the goal. The kicker ensures positioning and allows retreat time, but may kick before defenders are outside. A player guards the goal against turnovers.

For ages 11 and above, the secondary player becomes a direct target (Target #2), with the near-sideline player as Target #1. The kick targets the uncovered player; if both are covered, it is played short of Target #2 to create space. A midfielder (Target #3) may be added near the sideline, though this risks kicking toward the middle. If used, Target #1 runs up the sideline and Target #2 supports. Setups are taught for both sides; the goalkeeper may announce the side. A tactic of switching corners is used sparingly. Coaches introduce defenders in practice, stressing that targets must move to the ball and start closer than perceived.

Adults have all options: short kicks, deep targets, with the goalkeeper usually kicking. Deep kicks can be 50-50; kicking to a spot for a player to run onto avoids this.

A goal kick is a direct re-start; a goal can be scored without another touch. Wind can cause goals directly, blow the ball back for a corner, or lead to a goal after a goalkeeper touch. Players should consider field conditions.

This study investigates the effect of college teaching modalities on county-level COVID-19 cases and deaths. Many U.S. colleges reopened in the fall semester with in-person, online, or hybrid plans. College students aged 18-29 have a lower death rate but greater socialization, and reopening risks spreading the virus to faculty, staff, and the surrounding community. The study employs a quasi-experimental approach, matching colleges with similar characteristics to compare in-person vs. online, in-person vs. hybrid, and hybrid vs. online modalities. Results show that in-person teaching increases COVID-19 cases and deaths over time. The research addresses endogeneity in modality choice by using variation in reopening dates, cellphone mobility data, and re-weighting based on the probability of selecting a modality. The analysis focuses on county-level outcomes due to the policy concern of community spread.

The passage discusses post-war considerations for the Allies. It notes that economic exclusion threatens Austria-Hungary and Germany, and trade with Turkey won't solve their immediate problems. Intangible assets include the universal longing for peace, anti-Prussian sentiment against old diplomacy, hope for a league of nations, and fears of social revolution and insoluble war debts. Finally, German policy has shifted eastward due to the Russian debacle, and Germany may sacrifice other interests to secure Russian opportunities.

A hierarchical Bayesian multinomial model was developed to estimate SARS-CoV-2 variant growth rates and prevalence across countries, addressing data sparsity from uneven global sequencing capacity. The model pools sequence data across geographic regions and variants, using two levels of hierarchy to share information: country-specific fitness advantages are drawn from a global variant distribution, and variant means are drawn from a shared normal distribution. This approach produces robust estimates even in settings with few sequences. Applied to GISAID data, the model estimated variant proportions and weekly fitness advantages for BA.1, BA.2, BA.2.12.1, BA.4, and BA.5. Global estimates showed BA.5 had the highest fitness advantage relative to BA.2, followed by BA.4 and BA.2.12.1, while BA.1 was less fit. Country-specific fitness advantages were heterogeneous. Retrospective validation using BA.5 emergence in Portugal demonstrated that the multicountry model provided more stable and accurate early estimates than single-country multinomial regression, with lower Brier scores and reduced overfitting bias. The method is generalizable to other pathogens and geographic scales.

The paper studies Gorenstein-projective modules over the ring of dual integers Z[ε], as classifying all modules is infeasible. The category G-proj Z[ε] is equivalent to torsionless Z[ε]-modules, perfect differential structures of abelian groups, and orbits of bounded complexes of free abelian groups; it lacks the Krull-Remak-Schmidt property. The stable category G-proj Z[ε] modulo projectives is of particular interest. Theorem 1.2.1 establishes equivalences among this stable category, the stable category of submodules of free Z[ε]-modules modulo projectives, the orbit category Db(Z)/[1], and two categories of perfect differential structures. This result extends to any principal ideal domain. A chain of categories Cb(F) → G-proj Z[ε] → Db(Z)/[1] → Ab is linked by dense functors. Composing functors modulo shift, projectives, and stalk objects yields a commutative cube of categories.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum effects in an electric circuit. In the 1980s, they showed quantum tunneling and energy quantization in a Josephson junction, a device involving billions of electrons on a chip, challenging the expectation that quantum effects are limited to individual atoms. The discovery underpins superconducting qubits used in quantum computers. The prize is 11 million Swedish kronor.

For the synchronous rectifier, an 80-V rated GaN FET was conservatively chosen. A Schottky diode can be used in parallel to reduce current during soft-start and mitigate reverse conduction losses. An RCD clamp circuit can limit switch node voltage, with initial resistor and capacitor values determined by equations and optimized through testing. The output inductor value selected is 0.47 μH. Output capacitance calculations for voltage deviation and ripple requirements indicated at least 1.3 mF is required, but approximately 2.3 mF was used for the design example to account for single event transients (SET). An additional output filter can further reduce output voltage ripple. Cycle-by-cycle limiting begins at roughly 35 A output current, and a 7.5-Ω resistor was selected for RCS. The hiccup capacitor value used is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation was used with a target crossover frequency of 10 kHz; selected component values were 40.2 kΩ for RCOMP, 15 nF for CCOMP, and 47 pF for CHF. A resistor value of 102 kΩ is connected between RSC and AVSS for slope compensation.

The power management unit (PMU) generates internal core supplies, supervises the external supply, and contains a bandgap voltage reference. It features a brown-out reset monitor with programmable thresholds, a core regulator supporting RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY modes, and parity-protected trim. The clock module provides oscillators including LFOSC, SYSOSC, LFXT/LFCKIN, HFXT/HFCKIN, and SYSPLL, and distributes clocks such as MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, MFPCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, CLK_OUT, HFCLK, HSCLK, and CANCLK. The DMA controller moves data without CPU intervention, featuring full-feature and basic channels, various transfer sizes, a transfer counter, configurable triggers, active channel interruption, early interrupt generation, cascading channels, and stride mode. The event manager transfers digital events between entities using publishers and subscribers, handling peripheral-to-CPU, peripheral-to-DMA, and peripheral-to-peripheral events. Flash memory offers hardware ECC protection, in-circuit program and erase, small sector sizes, up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on select sectors, and bank address swap. SRAM includes two banks, with Bank 0 providing ECC or parity protection and Bank 1 being selectively enabled, and supports a write-execute mutual exclusion mechanism for partitioning. GPIO supports set/clear/toggle operations, wake from SHUTDOWN mode, and a FastWake feature. IOMUX enables IO pad configuration and digital pin muxing. The ADC modules support 12-bit conversions, simultaneous sampling, hardware averaging, internal channels, and configurable references. The temperature sensor provides a voltage output connected to an ADC channel, with a factory calibration value provided. VREF offers selectable 1.4V and 2.5V internal references and supports an external reference. The comparator compares voltage levels, supports blanking sources, device wakeup, and fault handling. The DAC converts digital values to analog voltage with selectable resolution, self-calibration, a FIFO, and DMA support. Security features include an AES accelerator, firewalls, secure key storage, and a CRC module. The TRNG generates 32-bit random numbers. The AESADV accelerator performs AES encryption/decryption with 128-bit or 256-bit keys and supports various modes. The Keystore controller manages AES keys securely, supporting up to four keys. The CRC-P module provides a signature for input data sequences. The MATHACL accelerates 32-bit math functions. UART peripherals support standard asynchronous communication, LIN mode, and FIFOs. I2C peripherals support multiple addressing modes, controller/target modes, various speeds, SMBus, and wakeup on address match. SPI peripherals support controller/peripheral modes, configurable chip select, programmable data frames, and FIFOs. The CAN-FD controller supports CAN2.0 and CAN-FD communication with configurable FIFOs and buffers. The Low-Frequency Sub-System (LFSS) contains a real-time clock (RTC_B) and an independent watchdog timer (IWDT). The RTC_B provides calendar counters, customizable alarms, periodic interrupts, and calibration. The IWDT_B is a watchdog timer with a fixed clock source and selectable periods. The WWDT is a windowed watchdog timer with selectable periods and an interval timer mode. Timers include general-purpose (TIMGx) and advanced (TIMAx) types, with features like various counter modes, prescalers, shadow registers, QEI support, complementary PWM with dead band, and fault handling. The boot strap loader (BSL) enables device configuration and programming via UART or I2C, protected by a password, and can be invoked through a pin, blank device detection, or software command. Device factory constants are stored in a memory-mapped region providing read-only data.

Twenty years ago, the Open Source Definition (OSD) was published, building on Richard Stallman's "free software" advocacy. The Open Source Initiative dates the term's inception to February 3, 1998, when Christine Peterson proposed "open source" as an alternative to "free software" to avoid confusion over "free" meaning liberty versus price. Both concepts involve making source code available under a license favoring user freedom. Bruce Perens, who adapted the Debian Free Software Guidelines into the OSD, announced it on February 9, 1998. Open source became a more commercially palatable form than the ideologically rigid free software movement. Perens stated open source promotes free software to business people. This messaging succeeded: many businesses, including Apple, Amazon, Facebook, Google, and Microsoft, depend on open source; Android and iOS rely on Linux and Darwin. Microsoft, once calling Linux a cancer, now embraces open source. Tim Burke of Red Hat noted open source now leads innovation rather than cloning proprietary software.

Storage, particularly batteries, is promoted as a way to integrate renewables and reduce fossil fuel reliance. Storage systems take power from the grid or local generation and return it later. Costs include capital and running costs (electricity for charging, round-trip efficiency losses). Technologies vary: lithium-ion batteries suit small-scale, have good efficiency but are expensive; pumped hydro is cheap, large-scale; flywheels offer fast dispatch and frequency stability; other options include compressed air, liquid air, flow batteries, and hydrogen. Lithium-ion costs fell from US$1,200 to $600/kWh in five years. For a home with a 4.5kW PV system and variable tariff, a 7kWh battery must cost under A$7,000 installed (A$1,000/kWh) to break even; current costs are A$1,000-3,000/kWh. However, retail rate spreads exaggerate wholesale differences (5-10c/kWh). If retailers cut variable rates, batteries would need to be cheaper—around A$300/kWh with a flat 25c rate. Batteries might reduce network upgrade costs only if demand grows, but overall demand in the National Electricity Market has declined since 2009, limiting grid benefits. Pumped hydro costs ~A$100/kWh and already provides 1,500 MW, but distributed lithium-ion storage may prevail due to human behaviour, similar to rooftop solar's popularity.

The speaker addresses the nation after a week of violence and tragedy. He appoints a special Advisory Commission on Civil Disorders, chaired by Governor Otto Kerner and vice-chaired by Mayor John Lindsay, with members from Congress, labor, industry, civil rights, and law enforcement. The Commission will investigate the origins of the disorders and recommend prevention measures, with access to FBI facts. The FBI will continue investigating riots and conspiracy.

He states that looting, arson, and violence are crimes, not civil rights protests, and must be punished. The immediate job is to end disorder using local police, state officials, and federal power if needed. He directs new riot control training for the National Guard. He emphasizes that lasting peace cannot come from force alone; it requires attacking conditions like ignorance, discrimination, slums, poverty, disease, and lack of jobs. He lists many laws passed in the past 3.5 years, including the Model Cities Act, Voters Rights Act, Civil Rights Acts, Medicare, Medicaid, and various educational and job programs, and mentions pending legislation like the Safe Streets and Crime Control Act and Gun Control Act.

He criticizes Congress for rejecting a $20 million rat control bill, cutting model cities funding by two-thirds, and opposing additional teachers, housing, and education. He calls for legislative action to improve city life. He warns that the tragedy could lead to hatred and fear, and urges acknowledgment without exaggeration. He notes most Americans, Negro and white, lead decent lives and seek harmony, and law-abiding Negro families suffer most from riots. He announces a proclamation for a national day of prayer on Sunday, July 30, for order and reconciliation, appealing to governors, mayors, preachers, teachers, and parents to lead it.

He tells those tempted by violence they will not succeed and will suffer from their crimes. He calls on those wanting progress to stand against hatred. He tells public officials to bring peaceful change, not business as usual. He urges clearing rubble, caring for victims without rewarding rioters, and stopping violence. He calls for building faith between races and working for better jobs, housing, and education. He concludes by urging action in Congress and communities to achieve "one nation under God—with liberty and justice for all."

This manual covers the Sansa® Fuze™ player. To transfer music, use drag-and-drop by connecting the player, opening Windows Explorer, and dragging files to the MUSIC folder. Alternatively, use Windows Media Player: add music files to the library, create playlists, then sync them to the player. Audible files require Audible Manager. For photos and videos, use the Sansa Media Converter software to convert and transfer files, with options to crop, rotate, and resize photos; do not convert both media types simultaneously.

Playback: The player supports MP3, WMA, secure WMA, Audible, and podcasts. Select music from categories like Artists, Albums, Playlists, etc. Use buttons to skip, fast-forward, rewind, and adjust volume. Music options include Repeat, Shuffle, MusicEQ, Add/Remove Song to Go List, Delete Song, and Rate Song. Audiobooks are under Music > Audiobooks; options include Chapter Mode and Speed (Normal, Slow, Fast). Videos are played from Video menu; options include Add Bookmark, Rate Video, Brightness, and Delete Video. Photos can be viewed individually or as slideshows; slideshow options include Shuffle, Loop, Slide Time (2–30 seconds), Slideshow Music (Current Song or Music Go List), Add/Remove from Photo Go List, and Delete Photo.

FM Radio: The integrated FM radio allows listening to live broadcasts. Use buttons to search frequencies. Presets can be added manually or via Auto Preset (which erases existing presets). Radio options include Add/Delete Preset, View All Presets, and Recording (Record Now, Play Recording, Delete a Recording). FM region (USA, Japan, World) and mode (Mono/Stereo) can be set in Settings.

Voice Recording: Use the built-in microphone via the Voice menu. Recordings are for personal use; copying copyrighted material without permission may be prohibited.

Deleting Content: Delete files directly on the player by pressing Submenu during playback and selecting Delete, or connect to a computer, open the device in Windows Explorer, and delete files from the MUSIC, RECORDING, PHOTO, or VIDEOS folders.

Settings: Customize via System Settings. Options include Wallpaper Color, Display Art in Lists (on/off), Backlight timer, Power Saver timer, Language, Date & Time, Brightness, Volume (Normal/High), Reset Factory Settings, Info (firmware, memory, song count), USB Mode (Auto Detect, MTP, MSC), Format (deletes all content), and Press and Hold (assign to Add Songs to Go List or Rate Song).

Tips & Troubleshooting: Drag WMA/MP3 files to the Music folder. Supported bit rates: MP3 32-320kbps, WMA 32-256kbps. Format via Settings > Format or computer. Update firmware via Sansa Updater. Use Sansa Media Converter for videos/photos. Supported formats: MP3, WAV, WMA, secure WMA, Audible. If a song won't play, rights may be missing. Podcasts in MP3/WMA with appropriate bit rates appear under Podcasts if genre tag is set or stored in Podcasts folder. Unknown artist/album usually means missing ID3 tags. The player supports microSD and microSDHC cards. Power reset: hold power button up for ~10 seconds.

Warranty & Legal: One-year limited warranty against material defects. Contact SanDisk support. Software license is limited, non-exclusive, for personal use with the product. Restrictions apply; no reverse engineering. Software provided "as is" without warranties. Liability limitations and export controls apply.

This retrospective study aimed to develop a predictive model for shunt-dependent hydrocephalus (SDHC) after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). It included 109 patients who underwent aneurysm clipping or coiling between January 2013 and October 2021, all of whom received external ventricular drainage (EVD) and an EVD challenge protocol. Univariate analysis identified age ≥65 years, clipping (vs. coiling), and Hunt and Hess scale (HHS) ≥3 as significant predictors. Multivariate logistic regression confirmed these factors: age ≥65 (OR 3.94, 95% CI 1.41–11.00, p=0.009), clipping (OR 4.36, 95% CI 1.81–10.53, p=0.001), and HHS ≥3 (OR 3.59, 95% CI 1.50–8.61, p=0.004). A nomogram based on these three variables was constructed, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.753 (95% CI 0.66–0.84). Fisher grade, aneurysm location, and inflammatory markers (NLR, PLR, PNR) were not significant predictors in this cohort. The nomogram provides a tool to estimate SDHC risk.
