This Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) describes analysis methods for a trial comparing dasiglucagon, GlucaGen, and placebo. All statistical tests are 2-sided at a 0.05 significance level. Analyses are a priori; post hoc analyses after unblinding will be labeled. Data are summarized using tables, listings, and figures (TLFs) with ICH numbering. Continuous variables are summarized with mean, SD, median, min, max; categorical with counts and percentages. Summary tables are presented by treatment group with a total column. SAS version 9.4 or higher is used; Phoenix WinNonlin for PK/PD.

Treatment groups: dasiglucagon (liquid, 1 mg/mL, 0.6 mL), GlucaGen (lyophilized powder), placebo (liquid, 0.6 mL). Analysis sets: Safety set (randomized, received ≥1 dose, analyzed as treated), Full Analysis Set (FAS; all safety set, analyzed as randomized), Per Protocol Set (PPS; FAS without relevant protocol deviations). Primary efficacy analysis is on FAS, secondary on PPS; safety on safety set. Protocol deviations are determined before unblinding.

Primary endpoint: time to plasma glucose recovery (first increase ≥20 mg/dL from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose). Secondary endpoints: recovery within 30, 20, 15, 10 minutes; plasma glucose changes from baseline at those times. Baseline is the last non-missing value before first dose. Covariates: age group (6-11, 12-17) and injection site (abdomen/thigh). No imputation for missing data.

Confirmatory testing uses a hierarchical order: primary endpoint, then secondary recovery endpoints (10-30 min), then secondary change endpoints. Only dasiglucagon vs placebo comparisons are in the hierarchy; GlucaGen comparisons are supportive. The primary analysis is a stratified log-rank test (by age group and injection site) on time to recovery, with censoring: patients receiving rescue IV glucose are censored at 45 minutes; non-recovery by 45 minutes is censored at 45 minutes. Kaplan-Meier curves are produced. Sensitivity analyses: without censoring for rescue, and censoring at actual rescue time. Supportive analyses include a stratified Wilcoxon test and a discrete-time Cox proportional hazards model (if hazards proportional) with treatment, age group, injection site, and baseline glucose. Additional CPH models assess homogeneity by sex, BMI class, ethnicity, race, US/non-US. Linear interpolation of recovery times is used as a supportive analysis.

Secondary recovery endpoints are analyzed using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests stratified by age group and injection site (or Fisher's exact if needed). Plasma glucose changes are analyzed via ANOVA with treatment, age group, and injection site; if rescue IV glucose is given before the timepoint, the value at rescue is used. Least-square means and 95% CIs are presented.

Pharmacokinetic parameters (Cmax, Tmax, AUC, etc.) are calculated by non-compartmental analysis. Plasma concentrations are summarized and plotted. Pharmacodynamic analysis includes AUE0-30min and glucose concentration summaries.

Safety analyses include extent of exposure (insulin administration, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, rescue glucose), local tolerability, adverse events (TEAEs defined as after dosing or worsening, coded with MedDRA), laboratory evaluations, vital signs, ECG (including QTcF categorical thresholds), and immunogenicity (ADA incidence). TEAEs are summarized by SOC and PT, with overview and specific tables for AESIs, injection site reactions, related events, SAEs, etc. Laboratory data are summarized with descriptive statistics and change from baseline. ECG includes categorical analysis of QTcF >450/480/500 ms and changes >30/60 ms.

The SAP also details presentation standards, programming specifications, and QC requirements.

Soumya Swaminathan, ICMR chief, will become WHO Deputy Director General (programmes) in November, the first Indian in the post. Her priorities align with the WHO Director General's: universal health coverage, epidemic handling, non-communicable diseases, and access to diagnostics and drugs. She aims to contribute to global health, noting countries must lead on universal health coverage with WHO in a stewardship role. On India, she cites commitment to universal health coverage but notes disparities in health indicators across states, and stresses preventive and promotive healthcare via health and wellness centres. Her father, M S Swaminathan, sees international exposure as providing perspective and learning; she hopes to gain insights to later contribute in India.

Changing lifestyles and hectic schedules are driving demand for convenient cheese snacks. The global cheese snacks market is projected to grow at a 5.2% CAGR from 2017 to 2025. Savory snacks like extruded snacks and salted chips are most popular, while frozen and processed cheese gain traction. Despite health trends, cheese addiction fuels growth. Health consciousness is increasing preference for baked snacks, and cheese is marketed as a nutritional whole food. Key players include Sargento Foods, PepsiCo, McCain Foods, TINE SA, UTZ Quality Foods, ITC Limited, and General Mills.

New research finds that using smiley emojis in work emails can harm career prospects. A Ben-Gurion University study with 549 participants showed that smileys decrease perceptions of competence and do not increase warmth, unlike face-to-face smiles. In formal emails, responses were more detailed without smileys. Smileys also led to assumptions the sender was female. Researchers advise avoiding smileys in initial workplace interactions.

This paper describes a qualitative study within a quality improvement project exploring perspectives on regional teaching for Stage 1 anaesthetic trainees in a UK deanery. Following a 2021 curriculum change and low GMC survey scores, no regional teaching programme existed. Semi-structured focus group interviews were conducted with six trainees and eight trainers (college tutors, school board members) across five hospital trusts. Thematic analysis identified that Stage 1 training was viewed as complicated due to the new curriculum, high demands including the primary FRCA exam, and trainee heterogeneity. Interviewees reported significant variation in teaching between hospitals, leading to perceived unfairness and siloed working. Logistical challenges for a regional programme included location, funding, rota organisation, and quality control. Despite wariness, both groups expressed support for a regional programme, citing potential benefits such as standardised exam-focused teaching, fairness, shared resources, and social networking. Trainers were willing to collaborate and adapt based on trainee input. The study concluded that a well-executed regional programme could address disparities but requires engagement and investment, and the findings directly informed subsequent QIP actions.

Labor force participation among 22- to 27-year-olds without a college degree has dropped more steeply than for degree holders, per Goldman Sachs. Over 30 years, non-graduates citing inability to work for reasons other than school, childcare, disability, illness, or retirement doubled to nearly 5%, versus under 1% for graduates. Disconnected youth (18-24, not in school, working, or looking) reached roughly 12% as of May, higher than any year 1989-2009, per the Dallas Fed.

Experts cite economic, cultural, and psychological factors. Zachary Mabel notes the share of non-graduates out of the labor force because they couldn't find work held steady, so the increase is from those choosing not to seek available jobs. Carol Graham points to a mindset of hopelessness: friends are miserable, lack benefits, can't afford things. Mabel adds that family-sustaining earnings concentrate among degree holders, and a cultural bias stigmatizes non-degree jobs like trades that pay well. Graham highlights rising despair, isolation, and loss of purpose, sometimes involving drugs or alcohol. Longer transitions to adulthood, with more living at home on family support, enable opting out. The gig economy may undercount some freelancers who don't consider themselves employed.

Solutions include education with internships/apprenticeships and campaigns to reduce stigma against non-degree paths. Experts hope for future generations but say helping those 25-30 is an uphill battle.

A genome-wide association study of neonatal jaundice was conducted using nearly 30,000 parent-offspring trios from the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort. Two loci reached genome-wide significance in the neonatal genome: the UGT1A* region and CHRDL1 on the X chromosome. The lead UGT1A* variant (rs17868338) is in near-perfect linkage disequilibrium with a missense variant in UGT1A4 (rs6755571, p.Pro24Thr), which was associated with a five-fold lower risk of neonatal jaundice (OR=0.2). This locus replicated in Danish cohorts. Colocalization analyses with eQTLs indicated the association may be driven by regulation of UGT1A1 expression in the colon, not the liver. The CHRDL1 locus (rs12400785) had an OR of 0.80 and also replicated. Analysis of parental transmitted and non-transmitted alleles showed the UGT1A* effect was neonate-only, while the X-chromosome locus effect was from transmitted alleles.

A maternal GWAS of offspring jaundice identified three loci: the UGT1A* region (driven by transmitted alleles), the X-chromosome locus, and the ABO gene region. The ABO association (rs687621) was explained by maternal-fetal ABO blood group incompatibility; after adjusting for incompatibility, effect estimates attenuated. The protective effect of the UGT1A4 missense variant was not modified by ABO incompatibility but was stronger in full-term neonates.

Comparison with adult bilirubin levels revealed distinct genetic architectures. The adult lead variant at UGT1A* (rs887829) was not associated with neonatal jaundice after conditioning on the neonatal lead variant, and colocalization showed different causal variants. The SLCO1B1 locus, strongly associated with adult bilirubin, showed virtually no association with neonatal jaundice. A polygenic score for adult bilirubin levels was associated with neonatal jaundice only when including chromosome 2; excluding the UGT1A* region rendered the score’s effect near null. The study concludes that genetic effects on bilirubin metabolism are highly context-dependent, with neonatal jaundice involving pathways distinct from those in adults.

A hard-sided, collapsible shelter or camper is described, comprising a roof section, a floor section, and rigid wall panels including side, front, and rear wall panels. The shelter is transitionable between an expanded configuration, where the wall panels are perpendicular to the floor and roof sections to form an enclosure, and a collapsed configuration, where the wall panels are folded and enclosed within an interior formed by the roof and floor sections. The side wall panels may be bi-fold or multi-fold panels. The front and rear wall panels may be hinged to the roof or floor section and latch to the opposite section when expanded. An optional mid-section connector can join upper and lower pairs of side wall panels. The shelter may contain a mattress and a movable bed system that can be raised or lowered. It can also include interior fixtures such as a kitchenette, bathroom, and dinette. The structure may be insulated, weather-tight, and lockable in both configurations. In the collapsed configuration, the shelter forms a portable, low-profile case transportable by various vehicles, including bicycles.

The SPREAD Offense is a 3-2 no post motion offense requiring all players to be skilled passers/handlers. Success relies on reading and countering defensive overplays. Continuity: O1 passes to O2 and cuts; O2 to O3 and cuts; O3 to O5/O4 and cuts. Cutters clear to corners if no pass, with replacements. Overplayed players back cut immediately; if no pass, clear same side corner. Ball handler drives if overplayed, kicks out against help and clears opposite corner. Back door: corner breaks middle if wing overplayed/shot clock low; left O1 feeds O5, right O2 feeds O4.

U.S. Border Patrol agent Larry O’Neal, 44, was indicted for possessing child pornography. He pleaded not guilty. Agents traced a suspected file to his home IP, and a search found a computer and external drive with sexually explicit images of girls 12-14. He admitted downloading it using search terms “young,” “rape.” No evidence on work computer. He is out on bail, next court date June 6. If convicted, he faces up to 10 years, a $250,000 fine, and sex offender registration.

On January 26, 2016, Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting under Item 2.02 that it issued a press release, data sheet, and supplemental materials regarding its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2015. The information is not deemed “filed” under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and will not be incorporated by reference except by specific reference. The exhibits include the press release (99.1), data sheet (99.2), and supplemental materials (99.3). The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Chief Financial Officer.

The lecture introduces the stress-energy tensor, motivated by the energy density of a dust cloud. In the rest frame, rest energy density ρ₀ = m n₀. In a moving frame, energy density ρ = γ² ρ₀, showing it is neither a scalar nor a four-vector component, but a component of a tensor. The stress-energy tensor for dust is T^αβ = ρ₀ u^α u^β, interpreted as the flux of four-momentum component α in the β direction. T^00 is energy density, T^0i is energy flux, T^i0 is momentum density, and T^ij is momentum flux. The tensor is symmetric; a torque argument on a small cube shows T^xy must equal T^yx to avoid a physical absurdity as size goes to zero.

A perfect fluid is defined as having no energy flow and no lateral stresses (no viscosity) in its rest frame. Its stress-energy tensor in that frame is diag(ρ, p, p, p). The covariant form is T^αβ = (ρ + p) u^α u^β + p g^αβ. Dust is a perfect fluid with zero pressure.

The Newtonian gravitational field equation uses mass/energy density, a single tensor component, which is not relativistically covariant. The relativistic theory will require the full stress-energy tensor as the source. Conservation of energy and momentum is expressed covariantly as ∂_α T^αβ = 0, which separates into energy and momentum conservation laws in a chosen frame. Integral forms are also given.

Other examples include the stress-energy tensor for a point particle, using a Dirac delta function along its world line, and for electromagnetic fields, built from the Faraday tensor, yielding energy density, the Poynting vector, and spatial stresses.

The lecture concludes by transitioning to mathematical tools for curvature, beginning with flat spacetime in curvilinear coordinates (polar coordinates). In a coordinate basis, basis vectors are not normalized (e_φ·e_φ ≠ 1). Transformation matrices between Cartesian and polar coordinates have elements with different dimensions, and the metric will acquire a non-constant functional form.

RWE Supply & Trading expects to double or triple its LNG derivatives trades this year from 2017, citing risk management for physical cargoes and Asia's shift from oil-linked prices. Physical LNG trading rose to 6 million tonnes last year. Fragmented Asian demand and power market uncertainty boost short-term trading. RWE traded 7-10 physical cargoes on the JKM index so far this year. JKM swaps volumes quadrupled in 2017.

Deepa Das Acevedo, a legal anthropologist and associate professor of law at Emory University, argues that politicians implementing checks on tenure are solving a problem that “didn’t need fixing in the first place.” She notes that at least five tenured faculty members were terminated or put on leave for social media comments after the killing of Charlie Kirk, indicating an erosion of tenure protections. Her book, “The War on Tenure,” responds to what she describes as a strategic, intentional war on tenure that began decades ago with attacks on labor structures. She reviews two decades of state legislation and university policies aimed at weakening tenure, often justified by the claim that tenured faculty are too hard to fire.

Das Acevedo identifies two enduring justifications for tenure: employment security as in-kind compensation for lower pay and hardships, and the protection of academic freedom. She says current events, including reactions to the Kirk assassination and Israel-Gaza speech, make academic freedom especially persuasive, while economic pressures and COVID-19 highlight the importance of employment security.

Addressing the criticism that tenure reduces productivity, she states that empirical data, though sparse and mostly focused on publication outputs, does not support this stereotype. She argues that academics are highly committed and that any post-tenure productivity changes resemble normal promotion-related patterns. Internal critics may rely on the availability heuristic, citing a single unproductive colleague.

On tenure protecting bad actors, she explains that tenure is a form of just-cause employment, not a guarantee against firing. Employers can terminate for just cause, including predatorial behavior or academic misconduct like plagiarism. The barrier is often the university’s willingness to act, not tenure itself.

Regarding recent rapid dismissals of tenured faculty with minimal due process, Das Acevedo observes that tenure’s protections depend on universities’ willingness to follow agreed-upon processes involving faculty input. She notes that universities are increasingly disregarding these processes, showing that the meaning of tenure and academic freedom is largely within institutional purview to change or ignore.

Pivot points are defined as the average of the previous trading day's high, low, and close, from which support and resistance levels are derived. The author backtested six simple pivot point trading strategies using 1-minute futures data from 2010 onward for the S&P 500, Nasdaq, Russell 2000, and USD/CHF. None of the strategies proved consistently tradeable. The best result was in Nasdaq futures, with 172 trades averaging a 0.16% gain and a 62% win rate, but the equity curve was erratic. Other strategies performed worse, though some showed potential if the trading direction were reversed (e.g., going long instead of short). The article concludes that pivot points are largely hyped and create market noise, but a couple of day trading ideas might be worth further research. Pivot points were invented by floor traders and are not as widely used today. Their pros include ease of use, objectivity, versatility, and confirmation of support/resistance; cons are that they lag price and have a low win ratio based on backtests. Lewis Borsellino, a successful pit trader in the 1980s and 1990s, mentioned using pivot points daily but did not detail his method. The article tested only the first support and resistance levels and acknowledges many other pivot point variations exist.

Disagreeing with Curtis, the speaker says limiting puck time and keeping it out of their end is key. They forechecked well down low. Brett's absence would be a bonus. Mike and Joe Nieuwendyk are dangerous, needing less room, time.

Mental health care is available in over 80% of Minnesota public school districts. Nonprofits like Know the Truth and Restoration for All provide additional, specialized support. Know the Truth offers peer recovery services for substance use, with peer support specialist Tiffany White using a harm reduction approach and sharing her personal addiction story. She works in schools, meeting students individually and in groups. Restoration for All, supported by a state health department grant, delivers culturally specific mental health care to African immigrant and refugee youth, including therapy, African mind-body practices, and suicide prevention. It also conducts workshops to help educators understand trauma and ask “What happened to you?” instead of “What is wrong with you?” Federal funding cuts eliminated White’s contract at one school.

Mike Kimel notes that much research education is poor, but highlights a cogent article. The article describes the widespread belief that minority children are overidentified as disabled and overrepresented in special education, leading to federal legislation and policies to reduce minority disproportionate representation (MDR). However, the study's Model 1 found no evidence of overidentification; instead, minorities were underidentified for some impairments. Model 2, adjusting for SES, academic achievement, and behavior, showed that racial/ethnic minority children are significantly less likely than similar White children to be identified with various disabilities (e.g., Black children 58% less likely for learning disabilities, Hispanic children 29% less). Language-minority children were also less likely for some impairments. The study concludes that minority children are underrepresented in special education, contrary to federal efforts. Kimel questions who loses when a child who could benefit from special education is mainstreamed, given policies aimed at reducing minority representation.

South Korea's spy agency suspects two female North Korean agents assassinated Kim Jong Nam, half-brother of Kim Jong Un, in Malaysia. South Korean intelligence says he was poisoned; lawmakers said Kim Jong Un had a standing order for his assassination, with a failed attempt in 2012. Kim Jong Nam lived in Macau and had criticized the family's dynastic rule. Malaysian police said the 46-year-old, traveling under the name Kim Chol, died en route to hospital from Kuala Lumpur airport. Cause of death unknown, autopsy ongoing. CCTV showed a woman involved. South Korean media reported needle poisoning by two women operatives who fled by taxi, unconfirmed. North Korean embassy in Kuala Lumpur refused comment. Malaysia has close ties with North Korea, including visa-free travel.

Tom Belcher et al. appealed a Kitsap County Superior Court judgment. The Washington Court of Appeals, Division Two, affirmed in an unpublished opinion on March 18, 1991, later published at 60 Wn. App. 949.

Second Wolverine mural panel was unveiled at Lawton High by Kenneth Hobbs. Funded by the 2014 class, it shows the school and a Wolverine. It joins a 2006-class mural (2010) of buildings and timeline of state and one national championship, with 1927 women's basketball team and 1993 wrestling champions and two coaches.

Adrienne Motley passed Octavia Blue for seventh on Miami's all-time scoring list with 1,724 points as No. 16 Miami beat Clemson 81-57. Jessica Thomas also reached 1,200 career points. Miami (19-6, 8-5 ACC) led for over 36 minutes, tying season bests in first-half points and field-goal percentage, and outscored Clemson 17-4 in the third quarter. The game was the annual Play4Kay game honoring Kay Yow. Motley scored 15 points, Thomas 18, and Laura Cornelius 14. Miami's bench outscored Clemson's 28-13, the 21st time this season. The Hurricanes next play at No. 14 Duke.

After a child's death and student AED fundraiser, Kelly Elliot pushes the TVDSB for defibrillator policy. The board declined installation; a meeting will discuss a board-approved device. Elliot says TVDSB is the only Ontario board without AEDs. Funds secured; board hasn't commented.

The October 12, 2000 edition of "Inside UT Football" by Chip Brown of The Dallas Morning News previews Texas's game at Colorado. Major Applewhite is named the sole starting quarterback; Chris Simms will play only on a "need-to-win" basis, ending the rotation for this week. Receivers Roy Williams and B.J. Johnson are promoted to start, and running back Kenny Hayter is expected to get more carries. Colorado coach Gary Barnett calls Texas the most talented team they will face and praises Mack Brown's recruiting. Brown answers fan questions, noting the game is do-or-die for the Big 12 South title, that no recruits attended the Oklahoma game because Texas was the visiting team, and that the Missouri game start time is not yet set. He addresses criticism of coaching and play-calling, stating offensive coordinator Greg Davis is re-evaluating his approach and that the one-minute offense conflicts with the goal of balance. Brown attributes recent losses to opponents having more motivation and says Texas needs better on-field leadership. He also provides updates on players Courtnee Garcia and Miguel McKay.

Stocks rebounded Wednesday as hopes rose that Italy would avoid new elections. Banks, energy, and small-cap stocks led gains. The S&P 500 and Dow rose 1.3%, the Nasdaq added 0.9%, and the Russell 2000 soared 1.5%.

Travis Phippen, wounded in the Las Vegas mass shooting, sued the estate of gunman Stephen Paddock. His father John was killed. The suit, filed Friday in Clark County, Nevada, by Rick Patterson, seeks control of all assets of Paddock's estate, including funds, safe deposit boxes, goods, and real property. The shooting at Route 91 Harvest festival killed 59 and wounded 527. John Phippen died Monday from a back wound; Travis was shot in the arm. Three other SCV residents remain hospitalized but recovering.

Alexandr Wang, the 28-year-old Scale AI cofounder and youngest self-made billionaire, advises 13-year-olds to spend all their time "vibe-coding"—using AI to generate and refine software through natural language prompts. He likens this to the early PC era when Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg gained an advantage by immersing themselves in the technology. Wang says 10,000 hours of deep practice with AI tools can become a huge career advantage. He notes that jobs are shrinking due to automation, causing anxiety among young people. Wang now leads Meta’s AI superintelligence team as chief AI officer and says he has been radicalized by AI coding, urging maximal use of the tools.

A petition to save Gresford Health Centre from closure has over 600 signatures. Alyn Family Doctors propose shutting the branch and merging patients with its Llay and Rossett surgeries due to manpower shortages. They have applied to Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board. Patients fear travel issues and appointment pressure. The petition had 614 signatures by Tuesday. Concerns also include proposed housing (365 homes in Llay, 132 in Rossett) overloading services. Three other Wrexham surgeries recently returned contracts. The health board is facilitating feedback via letters, forms, post, or email.

An unidentified Salvadoran woman fled gang violence with her common-law husband after losing two children, fearing the gang wanted to wipe out her family. They crossed into Texas on May 13, were captured by Border Patrol within an hour, separated, and she was deported back to El Salvador with about 100 others. Thousands flee gangs in El Salvador, Honduras, and Guatemala, only to be caught and returned under the Trump administration's zero-tolerance policy. President Trump tweeted that illegal immigrants "infest our Country, like MS-13," but U.S. Customs and Border Protection statistics show only 0.09 percent of 310,531 detentions in fiscal 2017 were gang members; most are people fleeing gangs. In 2000, 98 percent of 1.6 million apprehended migrants were Mexican; in 2017, nearly 163,000 were from El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, and roughly 128,000 were Mexican. Researcher Kathy Bougher said the vast majority are fleeing violence and need safety.

The woman's 19-year-old daughter disappeared after meeting a friend; her 15-year-old son vanished after going to a store. Police and prosecutors did not follow up. In El Salvador, gangs like MS-13 and Barrio 18 control neighborhoods, extort businesses, and kill those who refuse. An Uber driver avoids areas where an ID address can reveal rival gang ties; a lawmaker proposed address-free identity cards. In 2015, gang members outnumbered police and army 60,000 to 50,000. Security forces cause 10-15 percent of threats and violence. Henry Cubias, 22, was threatened by hooded police with disappearance if he didn't inform; his aunt saved him. Moving within the small country offers no refuge. An estimated 90 percent of deportees try to re-migrate within days. The woman returned to her empty house, unsure if she would try again, with no one waiting for her.

When a penalty kick is awarded during normal play, it is a re-start and the ball is live once kicked. Defenders other than the goalkeeper must be at least 10 yards from the penalty mark, behind the mark, inside the field, and outside the penalty area and arc. They must wait until the ball is touched and clearly moves forward before entering the area. Defenders should immediately take positions to box out attackers and react to any rebound, moving toward the goal to clear the ball if the goalkeeper blocks or saves it, or if it rebounds off the goal. If the goalkeeper blocks the ball without capturing it, the kicker may follow up, so defenders must get to the ball first. After securing or clearing, the defending team should transition quickly to attack. Sanctions: if a defender enters the area or arc early, a goal stands if scored; otherwise the kick is retaken. A rare "tap" penalty kick involves the kicker tapping the ball forward for a teammate to shoot. Coaches should practice defensive positioning, reaction to rebounds, and clearing, including defending against tap kicks. This applies only to in-game penalty kicks, not shoot-outs, where follow-up is not allowed.

A gaming machine includes a display, a speaker, a storage device storing tempo data (beat information of entire background music (BGM)) and sound data of the BGM, and a controller. The controller starts display of a game progression including at least one event while outputting the BGM. It determines a timing to display the event based on the tempo data, dynamically configures animation data so the event is displayed at that timing, and causes the display to show the animation. This synchronizes the event display timing with the beat of the BGM. In embodiments, the timing may be determined based on a player's operation and the tempo data, or the event content may be randomly determined. Event sound data may be output at the determined timing. A rhythm pattern defining a rhythm for sequentially displaying multiple events may be used to determine timings for the events. The game may be a slot game with reels, and the event may be reel spin and stop. An illumination may be lighted up at the determined timing. A control method and program for the gaming machine are also disclosed.

This study explored stakeholder perspectives on using metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for infectious disease diagnostics (IDD). Ten participants from various UK locations and professions were interviewed using an interpretive phenomenological approach. Five themes emerged. Diagnostic choice highlighted that mNGS would be an additional tool, not a panacea, with cost and speed as critical factors; funding disparities and turnaround times limit implementation. Infrastructure barriers included reliance on centralized sequencing causing delays, lack of local bioinformatics training and workforce, difficulties with accreditation due to research-use-only reagents, and inadequate digital storage and reporting systems. Open data sharing presented a conflict between patient privacy and the public health benefits of data sharing for surveillance. COVID-19 served as proof of concept, demonstrating sequencing's impact and building manufacturing capacity. Communication was identified as a driver, with needs for better intrahospital, interhospital, and public-commercial sector collaboration. The study concludes that cost, speed, and infrastructure are key considerations for integrating mNGS into routine clinical use, and that COVID-19 provides a learning resource for advancing IDD.

NHS staff recreated a 1927 photograph found in a broom cupboard to mark the health service's 70th anniversary. The original, taken at Sandwell Hospital (then Hallam), showed a matron, assistant, and nurses in old-fashioned caps. Fourteen employees recreated the scene in the same spot nearly 90 years later. The images, along with others from 1927–1966 found by ward service officers, will be displayed at a tea party at the hospital tomorrow.

Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in chemistry for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), structures with gaps that store gases and chemicals. Applications include collecting water from air, capturing greenhouse gases, and extracting forever chemicals. Robson in the late 1980s combined copper ions with organic compounds to create a hole-filled crystalline structure. Kitagawa later made MOFs that take up gases like methane. Yaghi in 1999 created a MOF with surface area of a soccer field in a few grams. The prize is 11 million Swedish kronor. Yaghi, a Palestinian refugee, credited U.S. public schools.

The lecturer auctioned two wrapped packages: a smaller one containing an iPod sold for $45, and a larger one containing a book sold for $60. The iPod retailed for $150, so the low price demonstrated how lack of information affects value. The lecturer then discussed the weekend's federal takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, two government-sponsored entities that purchased mortgages to provide a secondary market and expand credit. Due to the housing downturn, they faced severe pressures and could not stand alone. The Treasury stepped in to back their obligations to prevent default and major repercussions. The government can print money to pay claims, raising inflation concerns, and American taxpayers are liable for tens of billions of dollars. The situation was compared to the auction: when information is absent, assets sell at steep discounts, similar to the uncertainty surrounding Fannie and Freddie's paper.

The lecture then defined an asset at time t as a sequence of current and future cashflows, excluding past cashflows. This applies to both tangible and intangible assets. Valuing an asset uses a value operator V_t, which takes a cashflow sequence and outputs a number; one example is the market price. Cashflows at different times are like different currencies and cannot be added directly. A base currency (numeraire), such as today's dollars, must be chosen, and exchange rates (discount factors) convert future dollars to present dollars. The net present value (NPV) is the sum of all cashflows multiplied by their respective discount factors, expressed in today's dollars. These exchange rates are obtained from the market by auctioning securities that pay $1 at future dates. Under assumptions of perfect certainty, known cashflows, known market exchange rates, and no frictions, any asset can be valued.

The interest rate r was introduced: $1 today grows to (1+r)^T in year T, and the discount factor for year T is 1/(1+r)^T. This single number r unifies all time exchange rates and is also obtained from the market. The lecturer stressed the importance of drawing timelines to correctly time cashflows. Future lectures will apply these concepts to annuities and perpetuities.

The November 7, 2000 issue of VentureWire reports top stories: Broadcom acquires SiByte for up to $2 billion in stock; Alta Partners is raising a $275–325 million third fund; online retailer Furniture.com shuts down, laying off 76 of 88 workers; and eStellarNet raises $30 million in its first institutional round. Additional sections cover numerous funding rounds (New Money), layoffs at Divine interVentures and closure of Foodoo.com (Bad News), product launches and name changes (New Products), mergers and acquisitions (M&A), board appointments (New Directors), executive hires (New People), venture capital fund news (VC Fund News), personnel moves at VC firms (VC Personnel), and a correction regarding Tantivy’s location.

At Puerto Cortés, a busy container port, Sergio Romero visits the Avontuur, a 97-year-old sailing schooner using wind instead of bunker fuel. It arrived from Europe with a small crew, carrying small cargo, unlike modern freighters.

The speaker expresses gratitude for being called to the high office, acknowledges his deficiency and anxiety, but vows not to shrink from responsibility. Following predecessors, he explains principles by examining the causes of the nation's happy condition.

Nearly forty years since the Revolution and twenty-eight since the Constitution, self-government has produced flourishing beyond example. Under the Constitution, commerce is regulated, new states admitted, territory enlarged by treaty, and states protected while enjoying sovereignty. Individuals enjoy full rights, no oppression, and no capital punishment for treason. The government proved equal to foreign trials, standing aloof from European wars, demanding justice, and ultimately succeeding in inevitable war.

The government is elective, merit-based, discord-free, and protective of rights and against foreign injustice. The Union must be cherished. The country is blessed with varied climates, a vast domain, fertile soil, and surplus produce. Agriculture, navigation, and manufactures prosper mutually.

Dangers include the potential ignorance and corruption of the people, which would lead to usurpation; intelligence must be promoted to preserve liberty. Foreign dangers threaten commerce, navigation, and fisheries; national honor must be upheld. To counter these, coast and frontiers should be fortified, the army and navy kept moderate but adequate, and the militia well-organized as the primary defense. Fortifications are a permanent investment cheaper than invasion. The army garrisons and meets initial invasions; the navy maintains neutrality and protects property in peace, and aids defense and offense in war. The militia, organized in peace, harnesses patriotism without oppression.

Internal improvements like roads and canals, with constitutional sanction, will bind the Union closer. Manufacturers need fostering to reduce dependence on foreign supplies; domestic capital and a home market benefit agriculture and industry. This report examines Title IX staffing trends in higher education, focusing on placement, frequency, composition, and pay equity. Title IX regulations, expanded in 2020 and 2024 to address sexual harassment and assault, have created complex compliance requirements. The incoming Trump administration is expected to repeal the 2024 rule, further underscoring the need for dedicated staff.

A poll found most Title IX staff are housed in Human Resources (29%) or Student Affairs (28%), with smaller percentages in Compliance (11%), DEI (11%), and other areas. The report analyzes three dedicated positions: Head of Institutional Title IX Compliance, Deputy Head, and Title IX Investigator.

From 2019-20 to 2023-24, the share of institutions with at least one dedicated full-time Title IX position rose from 33% to 43%. However, 56% still lack such a position, integrating Title IX duties into broader roles. By position, Heads are most common (31% of institutions in 2023-24), followed by Investigators (16%) and Deputy Heads (12%); all three grew over the period.

By Carnegie Classification, doctoral institutions are most likely to have dedicated Title IX staff (64%), compared to baccalaureate (45%), master’s (39%), and associate’s (19%). The total Title IX workforce grew 38% (542 to 746 positions), with Deputy Heads up 58% and Investigators up 85%, while Heads increased only 7%. Most institutions (56%) have no dedicated Title IX staff, 26% have one, and 17% have two or more; multiple staff are most common at doctoral institutions.

Women hold 77% of Title IX positions (versus 62% of all professional staff), and Black women are particularly overrepresented (13% vs. 6% overall). Median salaries are $96,714 for Heads, $84,931 for Deputy Heads, and $75,000 for Investigators, all above the overall professional median of $66,000. Pay equity analyses show women and people of color are compensated equitably or better relative to White men, unlike broader trends in higher education.

Recommendations include reassessing Title IX officers’ responsibilities to ensure sufficient focus on compliance, increasing staffing where needed, and monitoring legal and regulatory developments to maintain compliance with prevailing standards.

This study investigated kindergarten teachers' views on the importance and teaching of visual arts in early childhood, and challenges in integrating them into the pre-school curriculum. A mixed-type questionnaire was administered to 65 kindergarten teachers in the Municipality of Piraeus. The sample was predominantly women (81.5%), aged 33-42 (38.5%), with a four-year degree (70.8%), 1-5 years of experience (53.8%), and no specific visual arts training (89.2%). Results showed that 56.9% strongly agreed the role of visual arts is crucial. 89.2% reported that visual arts affect children's development, particularly imagination and creativity. 83.1% indicated toddlers respond well to art activities. Teachers strongly agreed that visual arts promote intellectual development (53.8%), social interaction (41.5%), emotional expression (67.7%), social skills through group cooperation (60%), and creativity (73.8%). Regarding curriculum integration, 41.5% strongly agreed visual arts are well integrated. The most effective teaching method was the free approach (33.1%), followed by use of various materials and tools (30.7%). Positive feedback was seen as encouraging participation (47.7% strongly agreed). Children's interest and participation were rated high (53.8%) or very high (23.1%). The main challenge was child management (86.1%), with solutions including individual guidance, patience, and diverse materials. Demographics did not significantly influence teachers' views. The study concludes that teachers recognize the value of visual arts for holistic development, but face challenges like resource limitations and classroom management. Recommendations include professional development and dedicated art resources. Limitations include the electronic questionnaire method and lack of in-depth qualitative data.

SOS on-ball side screen disruption has two scenarios: above and below the free throw line. Above, an aggressive contact switch denies jump shots and middle penetration. Below, an aggressive trap is used near base/corner checkpoints. Below the line: When O5 sets a screen and O3 is below the line, X5 traps O3 with X3 before the screen. X1, X2, X4 rotate to 'I' positions. On passes out, defenders close out, deny, and front accordingly. Skip passes and passes to the post trigger specific rotations, including double teams and snuggle denials. Above the line: X4 bumps screener O4 and hedges into ballhandler's path; X3 moves inside screener. X4 forces ballhandler to corner and smothers; X3 snuggle denies passing lane, then fronts screener with slip front; others go weakside 'I'. All Out disruption: Defense traps point guard O1 with X1 and X5 before any screen, forcing free lance. X4 helps on O5 roll, X2/X3 triangle 'I'. On pass to O2, X5 dives to O5, X1 snuggle denies O1, X2 sets on O2, X3 denies O3, X4 returns to O4. If O1 passes to O5 on roll, X5 and X4 trap O5; subsequent rotations follow. All rotations occur as ball leaves passer's hands.

This cross-sectional study investigated the relationship between self-esteem and physical activity among 10th and 11th grade students at Capa Science High School in Istanbul. Data were collected from 225 students (80.93% of the targeted 278) using a questionnaire that included sociodemographic questions, the International Physical Activity Questionnaire Short Form (IPAQ-SF), and the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (ROSE). Height and weight were self-reported. 71.60% of participants were male and 27.60% female. Males had significantly higher ROSE scores (p=0.002) and higher MET scores (p=0.031). Regular exercise was associated with higher ROSE scores (p=0.034). A positive correlation was found between ROSE scores and height (p=0.029, r=0.146), and students with higher self-reported school success had higher ROSE scores (p=0.001). No significant differences in ROSE scores were observed across BMI groups (p=0.066). There was a positive correlation between ROSE and MET scores (p=0.045, r=0.140). MET scores were higher among students living in a dormitory (p=0.01). The study notes the population was specific: students at a science high school requiring a competitive nationwide exam, located in Istanbul, with many parents holding university degrees. Limitations include self-reported height, weight, and school success, and a lower number of female participants due to dormitory evacuation after earthquakes. The conclusion states that higher physical activity correlated with higher self-esteem, and that self-esteem was associated with male sex, regular exercise, school success, and height.

Disclosed are devices, systems, and methods for modifying basal insulin dosages using automated insulin delivery records. A processor determines a total amount of insulin delivered over a predetermined time period as the sum of total basal and total bolus dosages. It calculates the proportion of total insulin attributed to basal delivery and determines whether that proportion exceeds a threshold. If the threshold is exceeded, an average basal dosage approximately equal to the threshold is determined for a subsequent time period. An instruction is generated to deliver a modified basal dosage that substantially maintains that average, and the instruction is output to actuate a pump mechanism of a wearable drug delivery device. Amounts delivered as boluses and basal dosages within a preset period of a bolus may be omitted from the total. The threshold may be based on clinical data, such as approximately 70% of total daily insulin, and can be adjusted based on user activity level or glucose control performance (e.g., time in hypoglycemic range). Time-of-day clustering algorithms can be applied to historical basal delivery data to produce time-dependent basal profiles with segment-specific modified dosages. The system may include a wearable drug delivery device, a continuous glucose sensor, and a personal diabetes management device executing an artificial pancreas application, which uses blood glucose measurement values to determine recommended basal dosages and implement the modification process.

A study of over 2,800 Toronto residents found celiac disease prevalence at about one percent, with 90 percent of cases undiagnosed, consistent with international data. Celiac disease is a genetic autoimmune disorder where gluten damages the small intestine, causing symptoms like abdominal pain, bloating, and fatigue, and may lead to nutrient malabsorption. Diagnosis requires antibody tests and a duodenal biopsy while consuming gluten; many undiagnosed individuals follow gluten-free diets, complicating diagnosis. Published in BMJ Open, the study is deemed important for health care planning. Researchers caution that gluten-free foods are often costlier and less nutritious, leading to needless spending. A conflict of interest was noted: the lead researcher owns a genetic testing company for gluten intolerance. Further research is needed to determine if findings apply nationally.

This qualitative study aimed to identify pre-service physical and health education (PE) teachers’ overall anticipated challenges, their specific challenges regarding supporting student motivation, and their needs for better preparation during teacher education programs. Four focus groups were conducted with 18 pre-service PE teachers (mean age 25) from francophone Quebec universities. Results showed that overall anticipated challenges were classroom management and students’ lack of motivation. Five specific challenges related to student motivation emerged: student heterogeneity, designing learning activities to sustain motivation, student engagement, managing disengaged students, and gender differences. Regarding their needs in initial training, participants wanted to learn how to plan motivational strategies, receive more concrete guidance on implementing these strategies, and have additional opportunities for practice. The discussion links these findings to Quebec’s professional competency framework, emphasizing the importance of addressing pre-service teachers’ beliefs, creating program coherence, and integrating motivational content across courses. The conclusion notes that pre-service teachers feel current programs insufficiently prepare them to motivate students, and recommends more practice opportunities and explicit connections between course content and motivational processes.

The passage discusses tail risk hedging strategies. Tail risk, or fat tails, refers to distributions where rare events occur more frequently than a normal distribution suggests, often manifesting as left tail risk (negative skewness) that can cause severe losses. Nassim Nicholas Taleb is credited with popularizing the concept. Investors may hedge tail risk to avoid losses, survive long-term, and prevent behavioral mistakes during market meltdowns. Tail risk protection involves managing a portfolio to be immune to left tail events while still participating in right tail gains, but it involves trade-offs and typically requires giving up some return, akin to paying insurance. Six hedging alternatives are presented: buying out-of-the-money put options on broad indices, diversifying into foreign assets, holding cash, using Cambria’s Tail Risk ETF (TAIL), adopting Ray Dalio’s All Weather Portfolio, and employing trend-following strategies. Put options act as insurance but come with ongoing costs. Cash, though eroded by inflation, can be valuable during market declines. The TAIL ETF invests in out-of-the-money puts and U.S. Treasuries, aiming to mitigate downside risk; it has delivered negative returns since inception (CAGR -6.92%) but provided gains during market downturns like Q4 2018, March 2020, and 2022. Backtests show that allocating 10% or 25% to TAIL reduces drawdowns but lowers overall returns compared to holding the S&P 500. Trend-following strategies have a different risk profile, with many small losses and occasional large gains, and performed well in early 2022. The All Weather Portfolio diversifies across asset classes to lower risk. The passage notes that tail risk strategies are psychologically difficult because they involve frequent small losses while waiting for rare large payoffs, and most investors are risk-averse. A personal experience is shared of abandoning a put-hedging strategy in 2019 due to the pain of watching options expire worthless, only to miss the Covid-19 crash. The conclusion states that tail risk strategies may be more suitable for those nearing retirement, while young investors might simply accept drawdowns. The trade-off between risk and return is a personal decision.

This thesis analyzes web services for digitized event organization and management, and presents a mobile application concept using sensors and drone cameras. It discusses electronic business, distinguishing e-business (all online business processes) from e-commerce (online buying/selling), and introduces d-business as creating value through new combinations of people, businesses, and things. Negative aspects include business consolidation, income disparity, and internet security risks; protections include firewalls, antivirus, encryption, and digital certificates. Key technologies are cloud computing, Web 2.0 (user-generated content), Internet of Things (machine-to-machine communication), and mobile technology (e.g., m-banking in Africa).

The research analyzed 200 event management websites (17 Croatian, 183 foreign from the US, UK, Australia, Canada, Ireland, South Africa, Austria, India) collected via web mining from August to September 2017. A model with five categories—website content, social networks/Web 2.0, public relations/user support, multimedia/mobile technologies, and user experience/technical specification—was applied using 103 Boolean-graded attributes.

Results showed foreign websites more frequently used pop-ups (25% vs 0% in Croatia), privacy policies (83%), terms & conditions (89%), and feedback options (22%). Croatian sites displayed more bureaucratic information. Social media links: Facebook (90%), LinkedIn (78%), Instagram (42%), Pinterest (36%), Vimeo (14%). Organizational presence: Twitter (92%), Facebook (90%), LinkedIn (81%); all had blogs but only 78% were up-to-date. Public relations: 14% had media releases, 83% newsletters, 4% corporate social responsibility; customer support mainly via email (100%) and phone (99%). All sites used photos, 86% animations, 19% video. User experience: 56% had performance grade over 80%, 78% loaded under 3 seconds, 39% bounce rate under 50%. Technical: all used HTML and Java, 56% Flash, 27% multilingual, 4% HTTPS.

The conclusion states Croatian event organizations lag behind, with the highest-ranked Croatian site at 40th out of 200. Improvements are needed in user experience (loading times, content), social media presence (especially newer platforms like Instagram), mobile applications, and multimedia content. The study is limited to selected countries; future research should examine customer perspectives and the link between marketing and event management strategies.

Photographer Mark Bickerdike spent several years documenting Ricky’s School of Rock in Linthwaite, capturing young musicians during 10-week RockJam courses that culminate in a gig. The lecture develops the operator-field mapping in AdS/CFT, focusing on the relation between the scaling dimension of a boundary operator and the mass of the dual bulk field. Working in the semiclassical gravity regime (large N limit), the gravitational coupling is small, so matter fields can be canonically normalized and, to leading order, treated as free fields. For a massive scalar field in AdS, the near-boundary (z→0) asymptotic behavior yields two independent solutions: φ ∼ A z^{d−Δ} + B z^{Δ}, where Δ = d/2 + √(d²/4 + m²R²). The A term dominates.

Remarks: (1) The exponents are real provided m²R² ≥ −d²/4 (the BF bound); AdS allows negative mass squared above this bound without instability, unlike Minkowski spacetime, because curvature forbids constant modes. (2) The inner product for a scalar in curved spacetime defines normalizability. The B mode is always normalizable; the A mode is non-normalizable for ν ≥ 1, but for 0 ≤ ν < 1 both are normalizable. Boundary conditions must ensure energy conservation. In standard quantization one sets A=0 (non-normalizable) and keeps B; in alternative quantization one sets B=0 and keeps A. “Normalizable” henceforth denotes the mode kept in quantization. (3) Normalizable modes build the Hilbert space and map to states of the boundary theory. Non-normalizable modes, if present, deform the background and correspond to changing the boundary theory action.

Connecting to the previous lecture, the boundary value of the bulk field acts as a source for the dual operator. In standard quantization, the non-normalizable mode A determines the boundary value: φ₀(x) = lim_{z→0} z^{Δ−d} φ(z,x). This yields a term ∫ φ₀ O in the boundary action. Using the scaling symmetry of AdS (x → λx, z → λz) and the scalar transformation property, one deduces that O scales as O′(x′) = λ^{−Δ} O(x), so Δ is precisely the scaling dimension of O. Thus the mass-dimension relation is Δ = d/2 + √(d²/4 + m²R²) for standard quantization. For m=0, Δ=d (marginal operator); m²<0 gives Δ<d (relevant); m²>0 gives Δ>d (irrelevant). This matches RG expectations: near the boundary (UV), the source term for a relevant operator vanishes, for an irrelevant operator diverges, and for a marginal operator remains constant.

Summary of the mapping: φ is dual to O. Normalizable modes correspond to different states; non-normalizable modes correspond to different theories (deformations). In standard quantization, A(x) maps to the source ∫ A(x) O(x), and B(x) maps to the expectation value ⟨O⟩. In alternative quantization, the roles of A and B are swapped, and the dimension becomes d−Δ.

Other examples: a bulk Maxwell field dual to a conserved current has asymptotic behavior A_μ ∼ a_μ + b_μ z^{d−2}, leading to dimension d−1, consistent with a conserved current. The stress tensor is dual to metric perturbations and has dimension d.

Finally, correlation functions are discussed. The field theory generating functional Z[φ₀] = ⟨exp(∫ φ₀ O)⟩ equals the gravity partition function with the boundary condition that the bulk field approaches φ₀. In the semiclassical limit, the gravity path integral is evaluated by a saddle point approximation: Z_grav ≈ exp(−S_E[classical solution with boundary condition φ₀]). This allows explicit computation of the generating functional in the large N limit.

Lindsay Gottlieb, a white UC Berkeley coach, said a Southwest employee asked her to prove her biracial 1-year-old son was hers on a flight from Denver to Oakland. In this appeal, appellee recovered land and rents based on a chain of title including an 1850 transfer of a land certificate from Willard Chamberlain by agent Louis C. Clemons to Joseph P. Sneed, and a deed from Sneed to appellee. Appellant challenged the transfer's admissibility, citing lack of agent authority, insufficient proof of age and custody, and failure to identify the certificate. The court held the transfer was admissible as an ancient instrument over thirty years old from proper custody, with no suspicious circumstances; the jury found it genuine. The transfer sufficiently identified the one-third league headright certificate, and a conclusive presumption of the agent's authority applied. The court excluded a third-party affidavit and an augmentation certificate offered to dispute identity, and refused to allow appellant to introduce his own character evidence based solely on conflicting testimony. The jury was properly instructed on genuineness and limitations, and the evidence supported the verdict. The judgment was affirmed.

The passage describes an intelligent automated assistant for media exploration providing an auditory-based interface. Example methods include receiving a first natural-language speech input with a search parameter, providing a first media item, and while providing it, receiving a second speech input to refine the request and identify a second media item. Another method involves providing a speech output indicative of a verbal response while simultaneously playing back a corresponding media item. A further method includes suggesting media items in response to a request, and if a number of consecutive non-affirmative responses satisfies a threshold, foregoing further suggestions and requesting user input; otherwise, suggesting a different media item. Additionally, the assistant can detect physical presence of multiple users, obtain their preference profiles, merge them, and identify a media item based on the merged profile. The passage also describes electronic devices and non-transitory computer-readable media configured to perform these methods.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, is built on a 7nm process and features the GA100 GPU with 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores. It includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory providing 1555 GB/s bandwidth and a 40 MB L2 cache. The SM’s third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data types, delivering up to 2.5x dense FP16/FP32 performance over V100. A fine-grained structured sparsity feature doubles throughput for sparse matrix operations. New asynchronous copy instructions load data directly from global memory to shared memory, bypassing the register file, and asynchronous barriers enable efficient producer-consumer models and synchronization at various granularities. CUDA Task Graphs are accelerated with hardware features for faster graph launch and reduced grid-to-grid latency. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions the GPU into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, memory, and L2 cache resources, providing fault isolation and QoS for multi-tenant environments. Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links with 600 GB/s total bandwidth, and PCIe Gen 4 doubles bandwidth over PCIe 3.0. Additional features include hardware JPEG decode, an optical flow accelerator, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units. The A100 delivers significant performance gains for AI training, inference, and HPC workloads.

The paper presents a new algorithm for computing exact Nash equilibrium in multiplayer imperfect-information games. The approach formulates the problem as a nonlinear complementarity problem (NCP) using a generalization of the sequence-form representation, then models it as a quadratically-constrained feasibility program solved with Gurobi's non-convex quadratic optimizer. Experiments focus on 3-player Kuhn poker, a simplified poker variant. After removing dominated actions, the reduced game has 48 information sets and 415 nodes. The new method solves this reduced game in 2.47 seconds, yielding a strategy profile where no player can gain more than 1.4×10⁻¹⁷ by deviating. The full game (without removal) could not be solved within 24 hours. In comparison, Gambit's logit quantal response equilibrium (QRE) tracing algorithm solved the reduced game in over 40 seconds with a maximum deviation gain of 1.67×10⁻⁵, and solved the full game in about 2.5 minutes. Other Gambit algorithms were inapplicable or ineffective. The computed equilibrium differs from a previously known infinite family only at unreached information sets, indicating additional equilibria exist. On strategic-form games, the NCP-based bilinear program outperformed a prior mixed-integer bilinear approach. The authors conclude that their exact method is best for small games, while logit QRE is more scalable for moderate-sized games, and iterative self-play algorithms remain the only option for very large games despite lacking convergence guarantees.

The 20-day EMA trading strategy uses the 20-day exponential moving average to generate buy signals when price surpasses it and sell signals when price falls below. A backtest on SPY (S&P 500 ETF) showed a low CAGR, significant drawdown, and poor performance despite ~70% time invested. Adding another technical indicator (details behind a paywall) improved the equity curve, yielding a sizable performance increase and nearly matching buy-and-hold CAGR on a risk-adjusted basis, though drawdown remained the same. The same simple crossover rules backtested on Bitcoin from 2014 produced much better results due to Bitcoin’s momentum. The article concludes that the standalone 20 EMA strategy performed poorly but improved with an additional indicator.

The design requires an alert (logic high) when amplifier output exceeds 1.1V, configured per Figure 7-7. Use a low ESR 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitor directly between V+ and ground pins to prevent supply ringing and oscillations from fast output edges. The device accepts split or single supplies; with single supply, apply GND to V- pin. Input signals must stay within recommended range. Maintain stable power, minimize output-input coupling, avoid parallel traces without V+ or GND separation, place input resistors close, and optionally add a <100Ω series output resistor to dampen ringing.

Iron sulfate heptahydrate (ferrous sulfate heptahydrate, copperas) is a water-soluble compound produced as a co-product of titanium dioxide manufacture or by crystallization. It contains 18-20% iron, max 3% free acid, and at least 4% moisture. Uses include medical treatment of iron deficiency (WHO essential medicine), historical textile/leather/ink applications, water purification via flocculation and phosphate removal, treating iron chlorosis, reducing chromium ions in cement, and as an agricultural iron supplier.

The professor discusses the Asymptotic Equipartition Property (AEP) as a difficult concept. For a discrete memoryless source, symbols are independent and identically distributed. The log pmf random variable is minus log of the symbol probability, and its expected value is the entropy. The sample average of log pmfs over a sequence equals minus the log probability of the whole sequence. The weak law of large numbers bounds the probability that this sample average deviates from the entropy. The typical set is defined as sequences where the sample average is close to the entropy. As the sequence length n increases, the probability of the typical set approaches 1, and the distribution function of the sample average approaches a step function. The number of typical sequences is approximately 2^{n H(X)}, and each typical sequence has probability roughly 2^{-n H(X)}. Thus entropy determines the behavior of long sequences.

Fixed-length to fixed-length source coding is conceptually useful. It can achieve an expected number of bits per source symbol near H(X) with rare failures. Attempting to use fewer bits per symbol results in error probability asymptotically equal to 1.

Markov sources are introduced as models with memory. A finite-state Markov chain produces symbols where each letter depends on the previous state, governed by a transition probability matrix. A Markov source associates outputs with transitions. An example binary source with two-state memory is given, where the state and source output sequences are isomorphic. Ergodic Markov chains are aperiodic and have all states accessible from each other; they possess steady-state probabilities that are unique and approached from any starting state.

Coding for Markov sources using a separate prefix-free code for each prior state is ineffective for binary alphabets. Instead, block coding is used. The conditional entropy H(X|S) is the average over states of the entropy of the next letter given the state. Using n-to-variable-length codes, the expected length per symbol can approach H(X|S). The AEP applies similarly, and H(X|S) characterizes the compressibility.

The Lempel-Ziv universal algorithm (LZ77) is described. It requires no probabilistic model. A window of size W (a power of 2) is used. The first W symbols are sent uncompressed to fill the window. The algorithm then repeatedly finds the longest match of length n ≥ 2 between the upcoming unencoded string and any string starting in the window. The match length n is encoded with a unary-binary code (a prefix of floor(log2 n) zeros followed by the binary representation, yielding a prefix-free code with length about 2 log n). The match position in the window is encoded using log W bits. If no match of length at least 2 is found, a single symbol is sent uncompressed. The pointer advances by n, and the window slides forward by discarding the oldest n symbols. An asymptotic analysis suggests that the typical match length n* is about log W / H(X|S), so the number of bits per symbol approaches H(X|S). Practical considerations include choosing W based on processing speed, the algorithm's slow adaptation to changing statistics with a large window, and the possibility of initializing the window with zeros instead of wasting the first W symbols.

The IMF’s mission chief told Ukraine its pension system is unsustainable, supporting nearly a third of the population, and must limit retirees. Ron van Rooden said reforms have been delayed too long. Ukraine resists raising the pension age. The system supports 30% of the population and operates at a loss. Van Rooden suggested limiting early retirements and targeting companies avoiding pension tax, without explicitly conditioning loans on raising the age. Ukraine seeks $4.5 billion from the IMF this year; the IMF warned it must do more.

President George H.W. Bush addressed the Corps of Cadets at West Point, thanking military leaders and joking about the Navy's recent loss to Army. He stated that losing is hard but one should fight hard and learn from it. As he prepared to leave office, he shared his views on the world the cadets would enter and their chosen life. He emphasized that the President's most important role is Commander in Chief, as decisions affect lives worldwide. While the end of the Cold War is a blessing, with democratic governments more numerous and nuclear holocaust less likely, threats remain: violence, chaos, dictators with weapons of mass destruction, and terrorism. The U.S. must exploit the opportunity to build a new world order of democratic, tolerant, economically free governments that settle differences peacefully. Isolationism is folly; the U.S. must engage and lead. Leadership takes many forms and should not be confused with unilateralism or universalism; the U.S. should not be the world's policeman. As the sole superpower, it must marshal resources to promote democratic peace. Leadership requires demonstrated goals, persuasion, and working with Congress and the American people. The Bush administration acted in the Gulf War by galvanizing the UN and building a coalition, and in Somalia by organizing humanitarian efforts. Leadership may require military force, as a backdrop to diplomacy or a temporary alternative. He used force in Kuwait, northern and southern Iraq, and Somalia, with limited deployments under UN authority. Sometimes not using force is equally difficult, as in former Yugoslavia, where limited force might not have worked; options are constantly reassessed. There are no fixed rules for using force; each case requires judgment. Principles can inform decisions: force makes sense when stakes warrant, it can be effective, no other policies work, application is limited in scope and time, and benefits justify costs. When using force, act with maximum international support, sharing burdens, but sometimes a great power must act alone, as in Panama and the Philippines. Every use of force needs a clear mission, realistic plan, and withdrawal criteria. Adequate military forces are necessary, requiring defense spending. He credited past Presidents and Ronald Reagan for a strong military, and passed on a military second to none to President-elect Clinton. A military's true effectiveness comes from leadership, training, and people. U.S. troops showed caring in Iraq and Somalia. The All-Volunteer Force is a success, based on choice and meritocracy, breaking barriers of race, religion, and offering equal opportunity. Military training builds skilled, confident individuals with discipline and responsibility. Joining the Armed Forces is the highest calling, demonstrating duty, honor, country. Public service benefits society and ennobles the giver. He recounted enlisting in the Navy on his 18th birthday in 1942, ignoring advice to finish school, and never regretting it. He told the cadets they would not regret their choice, noted the new world's potential, and granted amnesty to the Corps of Cadets.

GDDR6X memory uses PAM4 signaling, transmitting two bits per clock edge via four voltage levels, and employs Maximum Transition Avoidance (MTA) encoding to limit signal transitions and improve SNR. It supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps, delivering up to 936 GB/sec peak memory bandwidth on GA10x GPUs, a 52% improvement over TU102.

NVIDIA RTX IO is a suite of technologies enabling GPU-based loading and decompression of game assets, accelerating I/O performance by up to 100x compared to hard drives and traditional storage APIs. It works with Microsoft’s DirectStorage API, offloading CPU work to the GPU, improving frame rates, enabling near-instantaneous loading, and reducing object pop-in. RTX IO uses GPU-based lossless decompression, keeping data compressed until it reaches the GPU, and leverages DMA, copy engines, and compute kernels on Turing and Ampere architectures.

The NVIDIA A40 data center GPU, based on GA10x Ampere architecture, delivers up to 2x FP32 throughput, 2x ray-tracing throughput, and up to 5x (10x with sparsity) AI training throughput compared to Quadro RTX 6000. It features 48GB of GPU memory, scalable to 96GB via NVLink, PCIe Gen4 interface, three DisplayPort 1.4 outputs, and supports NVIDIA vGPU software and Quadro Sync. It is compatible with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

Ampere architecture GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, enabling 8K at 60Hz, and HDMI 2.1 with up to 48 Gbps bandwidth, supporting 8K60 and 4K120. They include a fifth-generation hardware decoder (NVDEC) supporting MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, and AV1, with AV1 hardware decode being a first for GPUs. The seventh-generation NVENC encoder provides hardware-accelerated video encoding, exceeding x264 Fast quality and matching x264 Medium, with support up to 8K HEVC encoding.

The GeForce RTX 3090 incorporates the GA102 GPU with 82 SMs, 10496 CUDA Cores, and 24GB of GDDR6X memory. The GeForce RTX 3070 uses the GA104 GPU with GDDR6 memory, delivering performance faster than the RTX 2080 Ti. Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology on GDDR6X detects data transmission errors and retries them, allowing overclocking until performance plateaus rather than crashing.

The NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU includes a GA102 GPU with 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, and 48GB of GDDR6 memory, with NVLink support for up to 96GB combined memory. It offers performance improvements in SPECviewperf 2020, rendering, HPC, and deep learning compared to the RTX 6000.

Damian Lillard became the fastest Trail Blazer to reach 10,000 career points, but Portland's four-game win streak ended with a 130-105 loss to Toronto. DeMar DeRozan scored 35 points and matched his career high with six 3-pointers as the Raptors made a season-high 19 threes. Lillard scored 32 points, CJ McCollum had 21, and Jusuf Nurkic added 20. The passage forwards an article from Texas Monthly (November 2001) titled "How Enron Blew It" by Mimi Swartz. It details Enron's transformation from a pipeline company into a trading colossus under Jeff Skilling, who created a "Gas Bank" model and a culture prizing aggressive, smart recruits. The company dominated energy markets and expanded into areas like broadband. This culture featured a harsh "rank and yank" performance review system, replacing 15% of the workforce annually, and an intense focus on immediate profits, leading to internal competition and mercenary attitudes. Skilling forced out rival Rebecca Mark by giving her the ultimately unsuccessful water company Azurix. After Skilling became CEO, the company faced trouble: its stock fell from $80 to $35, it was blamed for California's energy crisis, its telecommunications division imploded, and analysts questioned its accounting. Skilling abruptly resigned after six months as CEO, citing personal sacrifices. Ken Lay returned, promising a company focused closer to its core.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted on rape and criminal sex act charges. Manhattan DA Cyrus Vance Jr. said the indictment brings him closer to accountability. Weinstein declined to testify, citing insufficient preparation time. The DA's office will try the case in court, expecting the jury to reject attacks on survivors.

The speaker addresses the Foreign Service Institute, expressing gratitude to Americans preparing to serve abroad and noting the shift from past diplomacy to a task of building world order through reason and moderation. The job is peace. Europe’s transformation from 1945 devastation to abundance and partnership is attributed to a design of common action, interdependent institutions, and collective security. NATO, a living institution born from fear of Communist aggression, must adapt through consultation and unity, not isolation. It is an alliance to keep peace, deterring war through integrated military power and political unity of shared values. Deterrence succeeds because collective readiness makes aggression too costly. Division and independent action led to past world wars; collective action has deterred war since 1945. The United States is determined to strengthen NATO’s deterrent and urges allied participation. The Atlantic community’s strength offers hope for reconciliation with Eastern Europe. The speaker calls for abandoning national rivalries and embracing human solidarity, urging the Foreign Service to make this their task.

Coach Quenneville discussed line combinations, noting that players sometimes mix based on matchups or merit, and decisions are made quickly in playoffs. He described Johnny as an ultimate player who excels in all zones, plays well without the puck, brings speed and puck possession, and draws top defensive matchups; his offensive numbers may be down but he contributes scoring chances and complements the team game. Dunks was called a thoroughbred with exceptional conditioning, able to handle big minutes; the team tried to reduce his minutes during the tight regular-season schedule, but his ice time increased in the playoffs and he thrives on playing more. Bolly took time to get up to speed in the playoffs but likes the challenge of more responsibility; his line offers defensive reliability and offensive skill, and he is predictable defensively with the ability to score. He reflected on the coaching profession’s lack of job security and the challenges of a winning business, recalling how the team had to change half its roster after a championship and progressed over subsequent years. This season featured an amazing start and high expectations; the team faced adversity, including being down against Detroit, but responded well and improved. A penalty-kick tiebreaker (shoot-out) is used to determine a winner when a soccer match remains tied after regulation and extra time, typically in single-elimination tournaments. The procedure is governed by IFAB Laws 10 and 14. Each team selects five players to take alternating kicks from the penalty spot 12 yards from goal. If one team leads after five kicks (or an insurmountable lead earlier), they win. If still tied, sudden death begins: teams alternate single kicks until one scores and the other misses. Only players on the field at the end of extra time are eligible. The referee conducts coin tosses to choose the goal and which team kicks first, and records kickers and results. Teams must reduce to equate numbers if one has fewer players due to red cards. All eligible players must kick before any player takes a second kick. Goalkeepers can be replaced if injured, and any eligible player may switch to goalkeeper. Shoot-out goals do not count toward individual statistics; the result is recorded as part of the match score.

Coaches should prepare in advance: review Law 10, designate players for coin tosses, practice penalty kicks for all players, identify and rank five primary and six secondary takers based on composure and success rate, simulate shoot-outs under pressure, analyze opponents’ tendencies, and reassure goalkeepers to treat each kick independently. In-match, avoid a late letdown, ensure best shooters are on the field, confirm the kicking order, and encourage calm. After the shoot-out, provide positive feedback and later review performance. Additional rules: a goal is valid if the ball’s motion from the initial kick results in it crossing the line, even after touching the goalkeeper or posts; a player who leaves the field and delays their kick forfeits it; a team may intentionally play for a tie to reach penalties, often using defensive tactics, which should be countered.
