The 4th Gen RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and introduce Mega Geometry technology, which accelerates ray tracing of cluster-level structures, supports Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures (PTLAS) for high object counts, and enables real-time subdivision surfaces. Hardware-accelerated Linear Swept Spheres (LSS) improve ray tracing of hair and curves, offering 2x speed and 5x VRAM reduction over DOTS. Shader Execution Reordering (SER) 2.0 improves efficiency and coherence for divergent workloads. An AI Management Processor (AMP), a RISC-V-based scheduler, offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU for lower latency and smoother multitasking. Video features include 4:2:2 hardware encode/decode, a 9th-gen NVENC encoder with AV1 UHQ mode, and DisplayPort 2.1b UHBR 20 support. Max-Q enhancements include advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching, and faster low-power state entry for improved efficiency. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame, and new transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving image quality and stability. Neural shaders, accessible via Cooperative Vectors, enable techniques like RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The GB202 GPU features 92.2B transistors, 24,576 CUDA Cores, and a 512-bit memory interface; the GeForce RTX 5090 is the first product. In this case, plaintiffs sought execution against defendant Allen as a stockholder of the Illinois and St. Louis Bridge Company to satisfy a judgment against the corporation. The court held: 1. Creditors must be preferred to stockholders in matters of corporate assets; personal profits of members that diminish the common fund must be held for the corporation until creditors are paid. Bonus stock issued to stockholders without actual payment rendered them liable to creditors for the unpaid amount. 2. The corporation issued second-mortgage bonds to stockholders who paid calls beyond the initial 40%, increasing liabilities without valuable consideration. Stockholders who sold such bonds were liable to creditors for the amount realized. 3. Under the statute, a stockholder’s liability to execution is measured by the shares owned at the time the motion for execution is filed and notice given, not at the return of nulla bona against the corporation. The Circuit Court erred in measuring liability by shares held at the return; the judgment was reversed and remanded.

A dry, self-supporting electrode film for energy storage devices includes a microparticulate non-fibrillizable binder with particle sizes of about 0.5 μm to 40 μm, and a fibrillizable binder. The non-fibrillizable binder may be carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) or polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF); the fibrillizable binder may be polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE). The film can contain active materials such as graphite. The smaller particle size improves distribution uniformity, reduces defects like holes, cracks, and surface pits, and increases tensile strength. Methods include jet milling the non-fibrillizable binder to achieve the desired particle size, and parallel processing where a bulk active material mixture (non-fibrillizable binder and active material) is combined with a structural binder mixture (fibrillizable binder and active material after high-shear mixing), then calendered into a free-standing film. Example 1 shows that using jet-milled CMC with a D50 of about 10 μm in a dry anode film (graphite, PTFE, PVDF) resulted in fewer defects and higher tensile strength (1.74 N) compared to as-received CMC with D50 of about 70 μm (0.936 N), while maintaining similar specific capacity and slightly improved first cycle efficiency. The electrode films can be used in lithium-ion batteries.

The 3-3-5 defense uses 3 defensive linemen, 3 inside linebackers, and 5 defensive backs; it is also called a 3-5-3 or 3-3 stack. It relies on faster, more athletic players, sometimes dropping bigger linebackers to the line and bigger defensive backs to linebacker. Its biggest strength is flexibility and versatility, allowing multiple coverages (Cover 1 or Cover 3) from the same pre-snap shell and the ability to add rushers from different spots. Weaknesses include vulnerability on the edges against runs like Buck Sweep or outside zone. Offenses attack it through the seams with passes (e.g., four verts against Cover 3) and off the edge with runs, and the trips formation can leave a vulnerable one-receiver side. Common blitzes include the Sam Blitz (slanting the line and sending a stack backer off the edge) and the SAW Blitz (sending two stack backers and pinching the line to create a Bear front). Common coverages are Cover 1 (man coverage with a rat player) and Cover 3 (three deep, two flats, curl/hook zones). Joe Lee Dunn is credited as the inventor. Notable users include Matt Campbell at Iowa State, Tony Gibson at NC State, and high school coach Tim Racki, who won eight state titles with the defense.

New York’s early intervention providers, including special education teachers and therapists, have not received a substantive raise in three decades. Emily Lengen, a special education teacher with a master’s degree, earns less now than when she started, despite increased caseloads and reporting requirements. Reimbursement rates have declined: a standard visit averaged $79 in 1994 versus $69 in 2022, and The Children’s Agenda estimates rates would need a 240% increase to match original spending power. While New York’s minimum wage and public school teacher salaries rose significantly, early intervention pay stagnated or was cut, with across-the-board cuts of 10% in 2010 and 5% in 2011. Providers typically earn $50,000–$70,000 annually, far less than comparable roles elsewhere, prompting many to leave the field. This exodus has caused service delays for children with developmental delays and disabilities, especially in rural areas. In 2024, the state authorized a 5% rate increase for in-person services and a 4% increase for underserved areas, but the 5% increase awaits federal Medicaid approval and remains unimplemented. A 2025 telehealth rate cut, intended to fund the in-person increase, led virtual providers to quit, further reducing access. Similar challenges exist in Illinois, Texas, and Rhode Island. Potential federal Medicaid cuts could worsen the situation. Advocates cite the invisibility of affected children and the predominantly female workforce as reasons for the pay crisis. Some providers, like Lengen, continue in the field despite the financial strain.

The author argues that Apple's current valuation does not align with its growth rates. A DCF model suggested $190 per share is adequate, but that only captures long-term potential. Examining multiples, the author finds positive correlations between P/E and EPS growth (R²=0.05), EV/EBITDA and EBITDA growth (R²=0.32), EV/Operative FCF and operative FCF growth (R²=0.18), and EV/FCF and FCF growth (R²=0.57). The best model (EV/FCF vs. FCF growth) shows the current EV/FCF significantly above the balanced level. A survey of 2,000 British adults by Tweak Mattress found the average Brit wakes three times a night, with one in ten waking 7-10 times. Ten reasons were identified: needing the toilet (47%), snoring (41%), being edged out by a partner (25%), discomfort (19%), bad dreams/nightmares (11%), tossing and turning (10.5%), bedroom talk (10%), phone light (10%), anxiety (6%), and a partner watching TV/reading (4.6%). Psychologist Robert Stewart attributes sleep quality to sleep hygiene (consistent bedtime, avoiding food/drink and screens before bed) and sleep cycles, noting REM sleep is lightest. A comfortable environment, like earplugs or a good mattress, helps.

Some animal partnerships are bizarre. Pearlfish live in sea cucumber anuses for protection, emerging at night to hunt; some parasitize the cucumbers by eating their gonads. Pistol shrimp and gobies have a mutualistic relationship: gobies guard the burrow while shrimp digs and maintains it. The shrimp keeps an antenna on the goby for danger signals and cleans the goby of parasites. Some species share similar colourings. The arid bronze azure butterfly larvae emit a chemical mimicking queen ants, tricking bearded sugar ants into carrying them into their nurseries, where the larvae then eat the ant babies.

Evidence shows not all protein sources are equal, challenging dietary guidelines that treat them as equivalent. U.S. adults eat 35–55% more protein than the 0.8 g/kg recommendation, but guidelines equate an ounce of meat to an egg, a quarter cup of beans, a tablespoon of peanut butter, or half an ounce of nuts. Research by Rob Wolfe and others indicates animal foods (meat, dairy, eggs) provide higher-quality protein than plant foods (legumes, nuts, seeds) due to essential amino acid composition and digestibility. A study of 56 adults found animal proteins led to greater muscle protein synthesis than plant proteins at guideline-equivalent amounts.

Protein quality depends on essential amino acid profiles and bioavailability. The body needs nine essential amino acids from food; if one is limiting, excess others are discarded. Donald Layman's EAA-9 tool scores foods: an egg scores 15.77, a tablespoon of peanut butter 4.04. Matching an egg's protein benefit requires about four times the peanut butter or more than twice the recommended legumes (e.g., over half a cup of kidney beans instead of a quarter cup).

Older adults are vulnerable: up to half of U.S. adults over 70 may lack enough high-quality protein, risking muscle loss, weakness, and falls. Inadequate amino acid intake can cause sarcopenia, affecting over a quarter of people over 60 globally. Some scientists propose raising protein recommendations for ages 65+ to 1.5 g/kg. Older adults may need more leucine and have less efficient muscle protein synthesis; a study of adults 65–85 found 47% higher muscle protein synthesis after an omnivorous meal versus a vegan meal with similar protein and amino acid profiles.

The Netherlands revised guidelines to reduce meat consumption for environmental reasons, advising vegetarians to use dairy and eggs, and vegans to eat more protein. Pregnant, breastfeeding individuals and older adults may face challenges reducing meat. Experts suggest improving plant protein quality by combining complementary foods (e.g., beans and rice), using cereals like sorghum or millet, and processing methods (soaking, sprouting, fermentation) to reduce antinutrients. Older adults can choose ground meat or soft foods like yogurt to ease chewing and improve protein availability.

Nutritionists recommend personalized guidelines: a young adult's plate might have chickpeas, rice, vegetables; an older adult's plate could add a small portion of meat, an egg, or yogurt. Most younger adults in developed nations can replace some animal protein with plant protein, offering health benefits like improved blood sugar control and lower cholesterol. Reducing meat consumption addresses greenhouse gas emissions and land use. Clear guidance is needed to help people meet protein quality needs while eating more plant-based foods.

The lecture covers gender, discrimination, and identity. The agenda includes an overview of the gender wage gap, technological solutions to reduce discrimination, beliefs and updating about skills by gender, gender identity norms, and demand and supply for non-promotable tasks.

The gender gap in wages is defined as women earning less than men for equal work. A graph shows that even for recent cohorts, a gap of 20–30% remains after controlling for work time and education. The gap emerges early and widens until around age 40–45. Reasons for past reductions include narrowed education gaps, technological innovations like the pill and dishwasher, labor demand shifts toward services, and lower discrimination due to regulation and market competition.

A study by Goldin and Rouse examines whether blind auditions in orchestras increased the proportion of women. Many orchestras introduced blind auditions in some rounds during the 1970s–1980s, coinciding with sharp increases in female musicians. The data suggest blind auditions fostered impartiality and helped women get hired, though results are less clear in later rounds due to small sample sizes and selection effects from discrimination in earlier non-blinded rounds.

Despite technological advances, substantial gender gaps persist. Researchers have examined less traditional factors, including beliefs and social norms. A paper by Bertrand and Mullainathan (2004) found that job applications with white-sounding names received 50% more callbacks than those with African-American-sounding names, demonstrating discrimination.

Sarsons (2019) studies how physicians update beliefs about surgeons based on gender. After a bad patient outcome, referrals to female surgeons decrease by 34%, while referrals to male surgeons stagnate. After a good outcome, referrals to male surgeons double, but increase only 70% for female surgeons. Additionally, a bad outcome involving a female surgeon reduces referrals to other female surgeons, indicating group-level updating. These asymmetries can lead to fewer opportunities for women to accumulate skills and be promoted, and biased evaluations may not be corrected over time.

Algorithms can also be biased if trained on biased human decisions, but they can potentially be fixed by incorporating equity concerns into their objective functions.

Bertrand et al. (2015) examine gender identity norms, specifically the prescription that men should earn more than their wives. Using US data on couples with positive earnings, they find a missing mass in the distribution of relative income just above 50%, where the wife earns slightly more. This suggests couples avoid forming, divorce more, or women reduce labor market work to keep earnings below their husband’s. Women in such couples also do more nonmarket and childcare work (the “second shift”).

Kleven et al. study child penalties using Danish data, finding that after the first child, women’s earnings drop by about 20% in the long run relative to men, with similar patterns for hours worked and wages. Child penalties are transmitted from parents to daughters. Gender-neutral tenure clock stopping policies intended to involve men in childcare were found by Antecol to reduce female tenure rates and increase male tenure rates, worsening gender inequality.

Bursztyn et al. show that unmarried female MBA students suppress ambition when actions are observable by peers, particularly single male peers, to avoid signaling undesirable traits on the marriage market. This is evidenced by lower participation grades (observed) compared to exams (unobserved), and by reporting lower desired salaries and willingness to travel when responses are public.

Vesterlund et al. study non-promotable tasks. A field study found women faculty more likely to volunteer for university committees. In a laboratory public good game where one person must invest to benefit the group, women are more likely to invest in mixed-gender groups, but no gender difference appears in single-sex groups. Further experiments show that women are asked to invest more often, and women comply more when asked (76% vs. 14% when not asked, compared to 51% vs. 14% for men). This creates a feedback loop: women are expected to say yes, so they are asked more, amplifying the difference.

In summary, large gender wage and earnings gaps have been reduced but persist. Biased beliefs, identity concerns, and feedback mechanisms in task allocation contribute to these gaps. Understanding these issues may help mitigate the gender gap.

The device moves from ACQ to CONV state on the rising edge of CONVST/CS, ignoring further transitions during conversion time (tconv). After conversion, it enters ACQ state. A data transfer frame begins at the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends at the subsequent rising edge. During the frame, data is shifted in on SDI and out on SDO-x pins with SCLK. A frame with exactly 32 SCLK cycles is optimal for read/write operations; shorter frames invalidate write operations, and longer frames use the last 32 bits as the command. Input commands, including CLEAR_HWORD, WRITE, and SET_HWORD, must be 32 bits long and are executed on the CONVST/CS rising edge. Output data for a frame is determined by the command in the previous frame and DATA_VAL bits, potentially containing register data, a fixed pattern, or conversion results with configurable appended flags. The device supports legacy SPI-compatible protocols and source-synchronous protocols for data transfer, with options for single or dual SDO-x bus width. It features nine configuration registers.

This article surveys selected results on transformer expressivity using logic, automata, and circuit complexity. Transformers are formalized as compositions of sequence-to-sequence transformations with piecewise linear functions and attention layers (softmax, unique hard attention UHAT, average hard attention AHAT), incorporating positional information via masking or position embeddings (PEs). UHAT with PEs is strictly contained in AC0 and cannot express PARITY or MAJ. FO[Mon] is expressible by UHAT with PEs; masked NoPE-UHAT coincides with FO (star-free languages). UHAT with PEs includes all regular languages in AC0 and Palindrome. Masked NoPE-UHAT verification is decidable (EXPSPACE-complete). AHAT languages are in TC0. Counting LTL with unary numerical predicates is in AHAT with PEs; Kt[#] is in masked NoPE-AHAT. NoPE-AHAT recognizes exactly permutation-invariant languages with semi-algebraic Parikh images, making emptiness undecidable. Limitations include unclear softmax/hard attention relationships; AHAT[U] approximates SMAT, and Kt[#] and permutation-invariant semialgebraic languages are SMAT-recognizable. Trainability differs from expressibility: PARITY is expressible but hard to train, MAJ is efficiently trainable. A formal RASP-L conjecture variant links length generalization to Kt[#]. The article targets logic, automata, verification, and programming languages researchers, highlighting open problems.

This study aimed to co-produce a community-based approach to identify people with probable Long Covid who lack a clinical diagnosis, and to understand the barriers and stigma they face when seeking care. Long Covid is defined by WHO as symptoms lasting at least two months, three months post-infection, not explained by alternative diagnoses. In the UK, an estimated 1.9 million people were living with Long Covid in March 2023. Health inequalities exist, with some evidence suggesting higher Long Covid prevalence in deprived areas and ethnic minority groups, yet these groups may be underrepresented in post-COVID services. Stigma associated with Long Covid can include enacted, anticipated, and internalised forms.

The study, part of the NIHR STIMULATE-ICP project, used a Community Advisory Board (CAB) of people with lived experience, healthcare professionals, and stakeholders to co-produce the research. An active case finding approach was used in Camden, Merton, and Derbyshire, England, via leaflets distributed with community organisations. Twenty-three semi-structured interviews were conducted with individuals meeting eligibility criteria for probable Long Covid. Thematic analysis identified four key themes.

Theme 1: Uncertainty and Long Covid awareness. Participants often lacked awareness of Long Covid as a condition, did not attribute symptoms to it, or downplayed symptoms. Self-doubt was common, with symptoms attributed to ageing, menopause, or stress. Healthcare professionals sometimes reinforced this self-doubt, and participants trusted HCPs’ assessments.

Theme 2: Barriers to engagement with healthcare. Hesitancy to seek care stemmed from fear of investigations, not wanting medication, concerns about parenting judgements, not wanting to burden the NHS, and a non-help-seeking identity. Perceived primary care problems included long waits, limited appointment times, and focus on single symptoms. The fluctuating, multi-system nature of symptoms made accessing care difficult; symptoms could be absent during consultations, or one prominent symptom overshadowed others. Some participants reported symptoms being attributed to mental health conditions.

Theme 3: Experiences and perceptions of stigma and discrimination. Participants described perceived discrimination in healthcare and community settings, including ageism, gender discrimination, and dismissal of symptoms. Lack of understanding and support from others, employers, and colleagues was reported. Anticipated stigma included fear of being dismissed, labelled a hypochondriac, or judged, which prevented help-seeking. Some feared discussing mental health due to cultural or religious reasons. Employment worries were common, with concerns about performance and lack of legal protections. Internalised stigma manifested as shame about symptoms, feeling less valuable, and comparing oneself unfavourably to others who recovered quickly.

Theme 4: Sources of support. Just under half of participants accessed treatment outside the NHS, including alternative therapies, supplements, private healthcare, and behavioural changes. Social and community support, such as peer groups, physical activity groups, and pharmacies, were valued. Most participants were receptive to social prescribing referrals. Desired healthcare improvements included easier appointments, longer consultations, feeling listened to, dedicated Long Covid services, and ways to access support without visiting a GP.

The discussion frames findings within epistemic injustice: hermeneutical injustice (lacking concepts to interpret experiences) and testimonial injustice (credibility deficits due to prejudice). Stigma can prevent help-seeking and reinforce self-doubt. Recommendations include raising awareness, mitigating stigma, listening to lived experience, and improving signposting to support.

The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture introduces a new memory subsystem featuring GDDR6 memory with 14 Gbps signaling, a 20% power efficiency improvement over GDDR5X, and a 40% reduction in signal crosstalk. TU102 includes 6 MB of L2 cache, double the prior generation, and higher L2 bandwidth. Lossless memory compression improvements, combined with raw bandwidth increases, deliver a 50% effective bandwidth increase over Pascal.

A new display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K resolution at 60 Hz, VESA Display Stream Compression 1.2, and native HDR processing with tone mapping per ITU-R BT.2100. The enhanced NVENC encoder adds H.265 8K encode at 30 fps, providing up to 25% bitrate savings for HEVC and 15% for H.264. The NVDEC decoder supports HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing GPUs include hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, delivering power, display, and data for VR headsets through a single USB-C connector.

NVLink replaces MIO and PCIe for SLI GPU-to-GPU data transfers. TU102 has two x8 second-generation NVLink links, each providing 25 GB/s per direction (50 GB/s bidirectional), enabling 100 GB/s total bidirectional bandwidth. Two-way SLI is supported; 3-way and 4-way configurations are not.

RT Cores in each SM accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, offloading the SM. This enables real-time ray tracing with hybrid rendering, combining rasterization and ray tracing. Turing achieves over 10 Giga Rays/sec, approximately 10x faster than Pascal's software-based ray tracing. Denoising filtering reduces the number of rays needed per pixel. Ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections are demonstrated.

Tensor Cores accelerate deep learning-based NGX features, including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) for performance and image quality, DLSS 2X mode, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS uses a neural network trained on 64x supersampled images to produce high-quality output with roughly half the shading work.

Mesh Shading introduces task and mesh shaders with a cooperative thread model, enabling elimination of CPU draw call bottlenecks and more efficient geometry processing, such as rendering hundreds of thousands of objects and dynamic level-of-detail selection.

Variable Rate Shading (VRS) allows developers to vary shading rate per 16x16 pixel region, supporting content adaptive shading, motion adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading (TSS) decouples shading from screen space, storing shading values in texture space for temporal stability and reuse. Multi-View Rendering (MVR) expands Pascal's Simultaneous Multi-Projection to support up to four views per pass, with flexible view-dependent attributes.

Turing supports bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views (DX12 Tier 3) and resource heap Tier 2. VR improvements include VirtualLink, MVR for canted HMDs, VRS for foveated rendering, and RT Core-accelerated VRWorks Audio.

TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPU specifications are detailed. The RTX-OPS metric is introduced as a workload-based measure combining Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations based on typical frame time distribution.
The Ninth Circuit dismissed the appeal in Rice v. Bradford upon stipulation and ordered mandate forthwith.

Moldova’s economy grew 1.1% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2025, reversing a 1.2% contraction in the first quarter. The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development forecasts GDP growth of 1.5% for 2025 and 3.8% for 2026, conditional on reforms. New York City’s per-pupil spending rose 40% since 2008-09 to $25,087, yet student performance stagnated or declined. A 2015-16 analysis found 30.3% of operating expenses went to fringe and pension benefits, and 23.4% to teacher salaries. The city led the nation’s 100 largest school systems in per-pupil spending in 2015. Rising costs are attributed to a pension fund guaranteeing 7% returns, with 2,215 retired educators receiving over $100,000 annually, and alleged waste, including $350 million for broadband that left schools dissatisfied and a lack of expense documentation. The Absent Teacher Reserve costs $100 million yearly, and the Renewal Program, projected at $784 million, saw 17 of 94 schools abandoned. NAEP scores showed fourth-grade math and reading declines, and eighth-grade scores remained below national averages. The graduation rate reached 72.6%, but only half of graduates were college- or career-ready. Teacher top pay increased to $119,000 under a 2014 contract.

The 3 Days Down Overnight Trading Strategy enters a trade at the close of the third consecutive down day on the S&P 500 and exits at the next day’s open. Backtesting from 1993 shows a 65% win rate, 8% maximum drawdown, and 0.13% average gain per trade. Exiting at the next close instead raises the average gain to 0.24% but lowers the win rate to 61% and increases maximum drawdown to 17%. A modified version from March 2022 achieved a 0.35% average gain, 60% win rate, and 10% maximum drawdown. In the 2022 bear market, it executed 35 trades with a 0.3% average gain. The strategy also works on Nasdaq 100 but less effectively.

The passage describes a monthly momentum-based rotation strategy between SPY (S&P 500) and TLT (20-year Treasury bonds). Momentum strategies, which perform best on 1-12 month timeframes, rank assets by past performance and buy the top performer. Sector rotation involves tactically switching assets; this strategy switches to the ETF with the best prior-month return. TLT often serves as a safe haven during stock market weakness, but not always, as seen in 2022. Backtesting from 2003 shows a CAGR of 9.2% with dividends reinvested. Maximum drawdown was 22% until 2022, when it reached 41% as both SPY and TLT declined sharply. The strategy is not a hedge against tail risk. Trading rules: at each month-end, rank SPY and TLT by last month’s performance, go long the better performer, hold for one month, then repeat. The backtest assumes no slippage or commissions and is best suited for tax-deferred accounts. Drawbacks of momentum include large drawdowns and survivorship bias.

In 1886, a Hawaiian loan bill was opposed by the U.S. under reciprocity treaty privileges. In early 1887, Mr. Bayard rejected a proposed Hawaiian-Samoan political alliance. On December 23, 1887, Britain proposed that the U.S., England, and Germany jointly guarantee Hawaiian neutrality and equal port accessibility, citing the 1843 Anglo-French convention. Bayard replied on February 15, 1888, that the Pearl Harbor concession did not impair Hawaiian sovereignty, and existing U.S.-Hawaii treaties with special reciprocities and a prohibition on ceding territory without U.S. consent made such a guarantee unnecessary. The passage notes Britain's motives likely included an Anglo-German Pacific understanding and jealousy of the U.S. Meanwhile, the British commissioner in Honolulu protested the exclusive U.S. use of Pearl Harbor as a coaling station, arguing it violated a British treaty granting equal harbor access and would threaten Hawaiian independence. The Hawaiian government ratified the supplementary convention, with notes clarifying the article granted no territorial cession, property right, or commercial exclusivity, and would end with the 1875 treaty.

The NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture introduces third-generation NVLink with four x4 links providing 56.25 GB/sec each direction and 112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth between two GPUs, enabling memory scaling up to 96GB with two A40 or RTX A6000 cards. PCIe Gen 4 doubles bandwidth to 64 GB/sec peak via x16 slot.

The full GA102 GPU contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, and 84 SMs. Each GPC includes a Raster Engine and two ROP partitions (16 ROPs per GPC, 112 total), improving raster operations. Each SM contains 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, 128 KB L1/Shared Memory, and a 256 KB Register File. The SM doubles FP32 throughput by enabling FP32 on both datapaths, capable of 128 FP32 operations per clock. L1 cache capacity is 128 KB per SM, with configurations supporting up to 128 KB shared memory in compute mode. The memory subsystem uses twelve 32-bit controllers (384-bit) with 512 KB L2 cache each, totaling 6144 KB.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection testing rate and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit for hardware-accelerated ray-traced motion blur, up to 8x faster than Turing. Concurrent RT Core and graphics/compute workloads are supported.

Third-generation Tensor Cores introduce Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity with a 2:4 pattern, doubling throughput. New data types include TF32 and BF16. With sparsity, GeForce RTX 3080 delivers up to 238 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS.

GDDR6X memory uses PAM4 signaling, achieving up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth on RTX 3090. RTX IO enables GPU-based lossless decompression and fast loading via Microsoft DirectStorage, offloading CPU work.

The independent watchdog timer (IWDT) in the LFSS has its own power and clock source, a 25-bit counter with closed and open window, is driven from LFOSC with a programmable divider, offers eight selectable periods, and generates a POR reset if not reset in time. The windowed watchdog timer (WWDT) supervises code execution, can generate a reset or interrupt, provides eight selectable periods, supports automatic stop in sleep mode, and has an interval timer mode. The real-time clock (RTC_B) operates from a 32kHz input, provides counters for seconds through year, a customizable alarm based on minute, hour, day of week, and day of month, interval alarms at various frequencies (every minute, hour, midnight, noon, and periodic from 4096 Hz to 0.5 Hz), calibration for crystal offset and temperature drift up to ±240ppm, and RTC clock output to a pin. A table confirms support for leap-year correction, BCD format, and interrupt capability down to STANDBY mode.

General-purpose timers (TIMGx) feature a 16-bit counter with repeat-reload, 8-bit prescaler, quadrature encoder interface, synchronization and cross-trigger among instances, interrupt and cross-peripheral trigger capability, and cross-trigger for Hall sensor inputs. Advanced timers (TIMAx) add a clock doubler, repeat counter, shadow registers, asymmetric PWM with dead band insertion, fault handling, and two additional capture/compare channels.

The double-down trading strategy entails adding another position to a losing trade, doubling the position when the stock price falls to improve the average entry price. For a losing long position, buying the same number of shares allows breakeven if the price recovers half the decline. Example: buying 100 shares at $136, price drops to $100, buying another 100 shares means a $18 rise breaks even. However, the stock may keep declining. The strategy focuses on price rather than odds of success; the average price is a mental bias. It differs from the Martingale strategy, which adds a larger position after each loss and increases risk more, and from the repair strategy, which uses call options. Backtests on SPY (mean-reverting) showed doubling down improved average gain per trade from 0.56% to 0.97% and improved performance metrics, indicating it works in mean reversion strategies, though a big loser can cause ruin. Backtests on HYG (trending junk bonds) showed average loss worsened from 0.19% to 0.22%, indicating it is a bad idea in trending assets. The article concludes doubling down sometimes works in mean-reverting assets and not in trending ones, but it is rarely part of a rational trading plan and is often a trading bias. Traders might consider it when expecting a reversal, but should assess market conditions and have risk management. A trading plan should focus on overall strategy, risk management, and probability of success.

The passage describes a low-side current sensing circuit using an amplifier and a high-speed comparator. The amplifier amplifies the shunt resistor voltage drop, and the comparator output changes state when the over-current threshold is reached. Design requirements specify an alert (logic high) when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1V. Bypass capacitors are critical: a low ESR 0.1µF ceramic capacitor must be placed directly between the V+ and ground pins to prevent supply ringing, false triggers, and oscillations. The device can be powered from split or single supplies; with a split supply, the output low swings to V- potential. For accurate comparator applications, a stable power supply with minimized noise is needed, and the bypass capacitor must be close to the supply pin with a solid ground plane. Output rise/fall times are tens of nanoseconds. To prevent oscillations, minimize coupling between outputs and inputs, avoid parallel traces without a V+ or GND trace between, place series input resistors close to the device, and optionally add a <100Ω resistor in series with the output. For long traces, use controlled impedance with back-terminations. The document references other design resources. Documentation updates can be received via ti.com notifications. TI E2E forums provide support. ESD precautions are required. Mechanical and packaging information is subject to change. TI provides resources "as is" and disclaims warranties.

The passage examines the Internet of Things (IoT) and a potential new productivity paradox. It notes that while IoT promises benefits and new business models, capturing its full potential may lag, echoing earlier ICT productivity paradoxes. The computer-initiated paradox was resolved by the late 1990s, but the dramatic advancement of the Internet introduced a new paradox: free digital goods and services provide utility not captured by GDP, leading to “uncaptured GDP.” Sources of this uncaptured value include online intermediaries, consumer surplus, disruptive innovations, and online piracy.

The IoT transforms products and requires digital business strategies that fuse ICT and business strategy. Analysis of 500 global ICT firms from 2005–2016 shows that high R&D-intensive firms experience declining marginal productivity of ICT due to the Internet’s two-faced nature (freebies, easy copying, standardization). To counter this, these firms activate a self-propagating function by harnessing soft innovation resources—such as sleeping resources, trust, past experiences, and untapped potential—to develop supra-functionality beyond economic value. This shift increases dependency on uncaptured GDP.

Leading firms (e.g., Samsung, Intel, Google, Microsoft, Huawei, Apple, Amazon) demonstrate transformative directions by leveraging such soft resources. The study suggests that ICT firms should recognize the trap of ICT advancement, embrace trust-based ICT-driven disruptive business models with consolidated challenge to social demand, and effectively utilize soft innovation resources to address uncaptured GDP. Future research should further explore soft innovation resources and novel business concepts.

Nuclear binding energies are discussed, starting with solar system abundances showing mostly hydrogen and an iron excess. Binding energy is the sum of constituent masses (protons, neutrons, electrons) minus the nuclear mass. Average binding energy per nucleon versus mass number is stable at 7.5–9 MeV, peaking at iron, enabling energy release via fission (heavy to iron) or fusion (light to iron). The binding energy is parameterized by the semi-empirical Weizsäcker formula (liquid-drop model) with five terms: a volume term proportional to A (~16 MeV/nucleon, indicating short-range force); a surface term ∝ A^(2/3) reducing surface nucleon binding; a Coulomb term ∝ Z²/R reducing binding from proton repulsion; an asymmetry term reducing binding when N≠Z, explained by Pauli exclusion favoring N=Z; and a pairing term favoring even proton/neutron numbers, with odd-odd least bound. The combined terms produce a binding energy curve peaking at iron.

The overlap in soccer aims to send an unmarked player from the back into the attack. Traditionally, the wing fullback sprints along the sideline past the midfielder. If the overlapping player is marked, the defender likely leaves another attacker free. The overlap is not a vertical offensive switch because the midfielder stays forward. It usually occurs near the sideline to provide space for the run. The fullback initiates the overlap, either with a straight run or a give-and-go pass. The typical result is the overlapping player receiving the ball and crossing from the end-line, or passing to the midfielder if covered. Overlaps can occur anywhere in the attacking end but are rare in the congested middle. A corollary underlap involves the fullback sprinting inside the midfielder, often leading to a shot on goal or a pass to the midfielder. After either play, the defender returns to position.

Ross Nelson appealed a judgment sustaining a demurrer and dismissing his action for specific performance of a contract to convey land. The land had been allotted to John Salerhand, a Puyallup Indian, under an 1854 treaty and patented in 1886 with restrictions on alienation: the land could not be alienated or leased for more than two years, was exempt from levy, sale, or forfeiture, and the restrictions would continue until a state legislature removed them with Congress's consent. In 1892, John Salerhand and his wife Chekudakai entered into an agreement with Nelson purporting to convey a portion of the land, with a two-year lease and a provision for absolute conveyance upon approval. John died intestate in 1893 or 1894, Chekudakai died in 1900; their son Peter John was the defendant. Nelson argued that the restrictions were void as repugnant to a fee grant, that the Bland Act impliedly repealed them, and that they were removed by a Washington statute of 1890 and a federal act of 1893. The court rejected these arguments, holding that the restrictions were valid because Indians are wards of the government and the policy of restricting alienation was necessary; the Bland Act did not impliedly repeal the restrictions; and the 1893 federal act provided that the removal of restrictions would not take effect until ten years after its passage, so the 1892 contract was made before removal and was void. The judgment was affirmed.

This preprint presents a rigorous analysis of an SEIR-like model for COVID-19 with a time-dependent transmission parameter. The model comprises nine compartments (susceptible, exposed, vaccinated, asymptomatic, mildly, severely, critically infectious, recovered, deceased). Transmission rates are parameterized by the mild infectious rate, with others as fixed proportions. Under continuous and strictly positive parameters, the direct problem is well-posed: a unique non-negative solution exists on any interval [0,T] and on [0,∞) if parameters are bounded. The parameter-to-solution map is defined, and its properties—injectivity, continuity in H1, sequential closedness, and Fréchet differentiability—are established. The inverse problem of estimating the transmission parameter from daily infections using Tikhonov regularization is mentioned. The main contribution is a rigorous mathematical foundation for estimating time-dependent transmission parameters.

Scientists at Washington University School of Medicine have identified a hidden “backup heater” in brown fat that helps burn calories. This system relies on peroxisomes, small cellular structures that process fats, and a protein called acyl-CoA oxidase 2 (ACOX2). When the usual mitochondrial heat production via uncoupling protein 1 is impaired, peroxisomes multiply and generate heat by metabolizing certain fatty acids. Mice lacking ACOX2 in brown fat showed reduced cold tolerance, lower body temperatures, poorer insulin sensitivity, and greater weight gain on high-fat diets. Mice engineered to overexpress ACOX2 exhibited increased heat production, better cold tolerance, improved insulin sensitivity, and weight control. The fatty acids involved are also found in dairy products, human breast milk, and are produced by gut microbes, raising the possibility of dietary or drug interventions to activate this pathway. The findings, from mouse studies, may inform new approaches for obesity and metabolic diseases.

RTX Neural Texture Compression (NTC) uses neural networks and neural shaders to compress material textures more efficiently than traditional methods. A Neural Materials demo shows memory usage reduced from 1110 MB to 333 MB—over 3x savings—with higher visual quality. Stochastic Texture Filtering (STF) introduces randomness into texture sampling to reduce aliasing and moiré patterns, and can provide higher-order filtering like cubic or Gaussian at the cost of a single point sample; it runs fast on Blackwell GPUs due to 2x point-sampled texture filtering rate improvements.

Neural Radiance Cache (NRC) uses a neural shader to cache and approximate radiance, enabling high-quality global illumination and dynamic lighting. It takes path-traced rays after one bounce and infers final lighting for many bounces, training tiny neural networks on live game data in real time. This improves performance by avoiding full ray tracing and enhances indirect lighting quality, adapting to game scenes.

RTX Skin addresses translucent material rendering by applying film-derived subsurface scattering in real-time path tracing, making it the first ray-traced example of subsurface scattering in games. RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model to infer natural-looking faces from a simple rasterized face and 3D pose data. The model is trained on thousands of offline images under varied conditions, using real or AI-generated images and a diffusion model, then optimized with TensorRT.

The passage investigates choked gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) in blue and red supergiant (BSG/RSG) progenitors as possible high-energy neutrino sources. It notes that jets from core-collapse supernovae may be choked by extended envelopes, producing shock breakout signatures and neutrinos while remaining gamma-ray dark. The authors perform relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations using the PLUTO code with a density profile combining a polytrope and power law. They estimate breakout and choking times via 1D numerical integration, finding linear scaling relations and providing formulas. A jet with luminosity 10⁵¹ erg/s, initial Lorentz factor 7, and low magnetization is injected for 5 seconds into a BSG of 50 solar radii and 15 solar masses. A shock-finding algorithm flags cells with converging flow, pressure jump, aligned temperature and density gradients, and Mach number >1. Preliminary results show that during injection, a cocoon forms with external, termination, and collimation shocks. After engine shutdown, the collimation shock fades, the cocoon shock accelerates, and the jet chokes roughly a minute after launch. Strong shocks persist, potentially accelerating particles, with neutrino and electromagnetic signatures expected primarily from forward-propagating shocks after tens of seconds. Future work will extend the parameter study to BSG and RSG progenitors with varied jet properties to optimize detectability of high-energy neutrinos from choked GRBs.

The Turing GPU architecture introduces a GDDR6 memory subsystem with larger L2 caches (TU102 has 6 MB, double the prior GP102) and improved lossless memory compression, delivering a 50% effective bandwidth increase over Pascal. The new display engine supports 8K resolution at 60 Hz via DisplayPort 1.4a with VESA DSC 1.2, HDR processing with tone mapping per ITU-R BT.2100, and can drive two 8K displays. An enhanced NVENC encoder adds HEVC 8K encode at 30 fps and offers bitrate savings; the NVDEC decoder supports HEVC 4:4:4 and VP9 HDR. VirtualLink, using USB-C alternate mode, provides power, display, and data through a single connector for VR headsets. NVLink replaces the SLI bridge, with TU102 having two x8 links (50 GB/s bidirectional each) and TU104 one link, enabling new display topologies; 3-way and 4-way SLI are not supported.

Ray tracing is accelerated by RT Cores within each SM, which perform BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection tests, offloading the SM. Hybrid rendering combines rasterization and ray tracing, using denoising to reduce the number of rays needed. Tensor Cores accelerate AI, enabling Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) that infers high-quality images from lower sample counts, providing up to 2x performance over Pascal. NVIDIA NGX uses DNNs for features like InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. Mesh shading introduces task and mesh shaders with cooperative thread models, reducing CPU draw call bottlenecks and supporting dynamic LOD and geometry culling. Variable Rate Shading allows per-16x16-pixel region control of shading rate for content adaptive, motion adaptive, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples shading from screen space, storing results in texture space for reuse across frames and views. Multi-View Rendering expands Pascal’s SMP to support up to four views per pass with flexible view-dependent attributes. Turing also includes Tier 3 bindless resource binding and Tier 2 resource heaps. TU104 and TU106 GPUs incorporate RT Cores, Tensor Cores, and the new SM architecture; TU106 lacks NVLink. An RTX-OPS metric weights Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations based on typical hybrid rendering workload distribution.

The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index (EWI) was created in January 2003 by Standard & Poor’s. It includes the same 500 companies as the traditional S&P 500 but weights each equally (0.2% at quarterly rebalance) instead of by market capitalization. The market-cap-weighted S&P 500 tilts heavily toward mega-caps, while the equal-weight index gives every stock the same weight, so sector weight depends on the number of companies. ETFs tracking these indexes are Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP) for EWI and State Street SPDR S&P 500 (SPY) for the market-weighted index. RSP requires rebalancing to maintain equal weight. Historically, the equal-weight index has outperformed the market-weighted index, attributed to the small-cap effect: smaller companies grow faster. A $10,000 investment in RSP in 2004 grew to $60,000 over 18 years versus $55,000 for SPY (dividends reinvested). RSP has a higher expense ratio (0.2% vs. 0.0945% for SPY), which reduces the outperformance difference. Daily return differentials between RSP and SPY can be large during turbulent periods like 2008 and 2020. Equal-weight ETFs offer more protection when large tech stocks decline, as smaller companies can offset losses. The outperformance is well known, but higher expense ratios on equal-weight funds partially offset the advantage.

The lecture continues the discussion of the massive Sudakov form factor in SCET₂, where an additional regulator beyond dimensional regularization is needed due to rapidity divergences, leading to 1/η poles and logarithms of ν. Scale choices are identified: collinear diagrams require ν ~ p⁻ (hard scale) and μ ~ m; soft diagrams require ν and μ both ~ m. The factorization theorem includes a hard function, collinear functions, and a soft function, all depending on both μ and ν. Renormalization group evolution occurs in a two-dimensional (μ, ν) space. Hard modes depend only on μ and q, not ν. Soft modes live at μ=m, ν=m; collinear modes at ν=q, μ=m. Evolution kernels U_h, U_n, V_n, U_s, V_s connect these points, and path independence follows from the commutativity of μ and ν derivatives.

Counterterms are derived via minimal subtraction, and anomalous dimensions for μ and ν are obtained by demanding bare objects be independent of μ and ν. The μ anomalous dimensions involve cancellations of 1/ε poles; the ν anomalous dimensions are finite and simple, yielding log ν terms. Consistency conditions relate the anomalous dimensions.

Examples are given: gg → Higgs with transverse momentum distribution is a SCET₂ process with rapidity divergences, factorized into a hard function, gluon PDFs, and a soft function. Drell-Yan is discussed in three kinematic limits. The inclusive limit (τ ~ 1) has hard radiation and factorizes into a hard function and standard PDFs. The endpoint/threshold limit (τ → 1) restricts radiation to soft, factorizing into a hard function, soft function, and PDFs, capturing singular terms in 1−τ. The isolated limit constrains small plus momenta in two hemispheres, yielding a SCET₁ picture with collinear, anti-collinear, and ultrasoft modes. Its factorization theorem involves a hard function, beam functions (depending on a large and a small momentum component), and a hemisphere soft function. Beam functions are proton matrix elements of collinear fields with both momentum components measured. They are further factorized into a perturbative matching coefficient (jet function) and a standard PDF. Glauber gluons are mentioned as a potential complication.

This study analyzed predictors of intention to adhere to COVID-19 preventive measures among 15,131 adults in Spain during the first wave of the pandemic, using data from the cross-sectional PSY-COVID online survey conducted May–June 2020. The sample was 66.8% female, 75% had university education, and mean age was 38.4 years. Measures included sociodemographics, personality traits, and prevention-related cognitions and behaviors (post-confinement behavior intention, experience, self-efficacy, outcome expectations, social norms, adherence to avoid infection/sanction, proxy control, barriers/facilitators, future threats, perceived vulnerability, information level). A linear mixed model identified the most influential predictors of post-confinement prevention behavior intention: self-efficacy, outcome expectations, general adherence, information level, experience with prevention behaviors, perceived vulnerability, proxy control (scientists), and social norm. Perceived severity of the pandemic moderated the effects of adherence to avoid infection and perceived vulnerability of others. Region of residence had a small but significant effect. The discussion highlights that self-efficacy and outcome expectations were primary predictors, information level was strongly related to intention, and trust in scientists was high while proxy control for government was low. Implications for public health include promoting self-efficacy, ensuring communication consistency, and addressing regional disparities.

This paper proposes a weighted expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm for estimating transition probability matrices (TPMs) in Markov cohort-state-transition models. The standard EM approach by Craig and Sendi uses uniform weighting when combining 1-step count estimates from multiple observation intervals, which may increase variance. The authors hypothesize that different estimated count matrices have non-identical distributions due to varying data sources and missingness. They propose a weighted combination step, motivated by best linear unbiased estimators, and use a computational grid search to find weights that minimize the variance of a chosen function of the TPM, such as the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER). A proof-of-concept example with a 3-state model and fictitious treatment demonstrates a 15.2% reduction in ICER variance and a 3-percentage point increase in cost-effectiveness probability at a given threshold, with similar ICER means. The discussion notes the method requires similar data sources to avoid bias and recommends further validation with real-world data.

This document describes the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, an optional extension to SEV and SNP APIs for page migration. Page migration copies page content and updates virtual-to-physical mappings. TMPM off-loads this process and addresses two challenges: pausing DMA traffic during migration and acting as a trusted agent for guest pages under SEV or SNP. Support is determined via the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register; IOMMU enablement is required.

Tiered memory systems use multiple performance tiers; software monitors access patterns and migrates pages between tiers, updating IOMMU mappings. TMPM commands migrate pages between system physical addresses while maintaining the same guest physical address. They enable migration of pages that are concurrent DMA targets and SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the HV/OS. Commands support moving groups of pages efficiently, with multi-page commands handling up to 128 pages via a Page Migration List. Entries must have no order-dependence.

The PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO command migrates pages with concurrent DMA, requiring the IOMMU host page table entry location. It can migrate Hypervisor state pages in SNP systems, returning them in Hypervisor state. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates guest pages in SNP systems; source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, destination pages in Pre-Migration state. After migration, source pages become Pre-Migration, destination pages take the original source state. A new Pre-Migration state is defined, similar to Guest-Invalid but with a platform-specific ASID and ignored GPA; it cannot be validated by a guest. RMPUpdate converts Pre-Migration pages back to Hypervisor state.

Per-page status is provided; PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking individual statuses. PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE indicates a retryable conflict. Performance guidelines: commands with 16+ pages yield higher bandwidth, maximum at 128 pages. Keeping the ring buffer full and using interrupts sparingly (e.g., NOP or Interrupt on Complete) improves efficiency. Non-migratable structures include IOMMU data structures, vIOMMU private address space page tables, pinned buffers, and the ring buffer. For PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, source pages must be DMA-mapped via a single IOMMU host page table, and a host page table virtual address space maps the page tables themselves. The TMPM engine may modify IOMMU host page table entries non-atomically; host software must avoid concurrent modifications.

The lecture reviews the decoder's goal to minimize error probability, leading to the minimum distance decision rule under AWGN and equally likely signals. The union bound estimate approximates error probability as the average number of nearest neighbors times Q(d_min/(2σ)). Effective coding gain is introduced as the gap between a given signal set and the baseline 2-PAM at a fixed probability of bit error (10^-5) in the power-limited regime. Using the union bound estimate, the probability of bit error is expressed with parameters K_b(A) (nearest neighbors per bit) and nominal coding gain γ_c(A) = d_min^2/(4E_b). Plotting on a log-log scale, γ_c(A) shifts the curve horizontally, while K_b(A) shifts it vertically. A rule of thumb gives effective coding gain ≈ γ_c(dB) - 0.2 log2(K_b(A)). Examples: 2-PAM and 4-QAM have 0 dB effective coding gain. Removing two points from 4-QAM yields a 2-PAM constellation, still 0 dB. A 3D constellation with four points (vertices of a cube) achieves a nominal coding gain of 4/3 (≈1.3 dB) and effective coding gain ≈1 dB.

Orthogonal signal sets consist of M signals with equal energy E(A) and zero inner product between distinct signals. Every point is equidistant, d_min^2 = 2E(A), and the number of nearest neighbors is M-1. Nominal coding gain = (1/2) log2(M), which goes to infinity as M increases, but effective coding gain remains bounded and approaches the Shannon limit (11.2 dB as M→∞). The mean of the constellation goes to zero. However, orthogonal signal sets have drawbacks: spectral efficiency 2log2(M)/M goes to zero sharply, and implementation complexity (e.g., using Hadamard transforms) requires M log M operations per symbol, which is exponential in the number of information bits. Simplex signal sets are derived by subtracting the mean, improving performance; bi-orthogonal signal sets add the negatives of each point, doubling the size but also increasing nearest neighbors. Both approach the Shannon limit but share similar practical limitations.

In the bandwidth-limited regime, the trade-off is probability of error per two dimensions vs. SNR_norm, with baseline M-PAM. The union bound estimate yields parameters K_s(A) (nearest neighbors per two dimensions) and nominal coding gain γ_c(A) = d_min^2/(6E_s) * (2^ρ - 1). Plotting similarly involves horizontal and vertical shifts. The rule of thumb is γ_eff = γ_c(dB) - 0.2 log2(K_s(A)/4). The chapter concludes with a preview of binary block codes: an encoder maps K input bits to N bits (N≥K), followed by binary signaling mapping 0→α, 1→-α. This separates coding and modulation. For binary signaling, this architecture is efficient; for non-binary signaling, combined coding and modulation may be better. The power-limited regime is the focus because spectral efficiency ≤ 2 bits per two dimensions. Comparing the Shannon limit and the binary-constrained limit shows that at spectral efficiency around 1 bit per two dimensions, the additional E_b/N_0 required is at most 0.2 dB, so the binary signaling constraint incurs little loss. Future chapters will develop binary block codes and convolutional codes, requiring finite field theory.

This document is a Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) for study ZEA-DNK-02170. It specifies that plasma glucose is measured at multiple time points after dosing, with strict sampling time windows. The pharmacodynamic endpoint is the area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes (AUE0-30min), calculated using SAS. Individual glucose results will be listed, and summary statistics by treatment group and time point will be presented, including change from pre-dose. Mean and individual glucose concentration curves will be plotted.

Safety analyses are based on the safety set. Extent of exposure covers insulin administration prior to hypoglycemia induction, the induction procedure itself, trial medication administration, and post-treatment rescue glucose infusion, with summary tables for each. Time to first IV glucose infusion after IMP administration is described with descriptive statistics. Local tolerability at the injection site is assessed at 30, 120, and 300 minutes post-dose, with a summary table of counts and percentages by time point, symptom, and grade.

Adverse event (AE) summaries are restricted to treatment-emergent AEs (TEAEs), defined as AEs occurring or worsening after dosing. Verbatim terms are mapped to MedDRA preferred terms and system organ classes. Causal relationship and severity are assessed. An overview AE summary table will present numbers and percentages for various categories (e.g., TEAEs, AESIs, injection site reactions, study drug-related TEAEs, SAEs, deaths). Frequency tables by MedDRA terms will be prepared for TEAEs, AESIs, other important events, injection site reactions, study drug-related TEAEs, and TEAEs by causal relationship. A special search category includes MedDRA terms for QT prolongation and drug-related hepatic disorders. Listings and narratives for deaths and serious AEs are planned.

Laboratory evaluations (hematology, biochemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, pregnancy test, alcohol breath test) will be tabulated with descriptive statistics, reference range flags, and change from baseline. Vital signs will be summarized descriptively, with categorical analysis of pulse rate. ECG data will include overall interpretation, descriptive statistics of parameters, and categorical summaries of QTcF values (>450, >480, >500 ms) and changes from baseline (>30, >60 ms). Immunogenicity analysis will descriptively assess ADA occurrence, counting treatment-induced and treatment-boosted ADA-positive patients.

Changes from the protocol include rewording of the primary efficacy analysis and addition of sensitivity/supportive analyses, and terminology change for secondary efficacy variables. Appendices provide specifications for data presentation (tables, figures, listings), SAS programming QC requirements, and a planned list of tables, figures, and listings for the clinical study report.

The paper presents a multi-criteria integer model for ambulance station location that maximizes the population reachable within two driving times (r1=5 minutes, r2=10 minutes) while ensuring all demand points are covered within a legal maximum of r3=15 minutes. The model was applied to a real-world case study in Southwest Germany, optimizing the locations of 11 outdated stations across two emergency service areas for two district councils. Demand points were 20,444 road segments weighted by inhabitants, and travel times were computed on a detailed OpenStreetMap road network with ambulance-specific speed profiles. The model was solved using the ε-constraint method, yielding 16 Pareto-optimal solutions. Results show that maximizing coverage within 5 minutes concentrates stations in urban areas, whereas maximizing coverage within 10 minutes distributes stations more evenly, including rural areas. The trade-off between the two objectives is demonstrated, and the model serves as a decision support tool, leaving the moral choice of urban versus rural placement to decision-makers. The static approach was used as a first stage, with further evaluation via discrete event simulation. Future work may extend the model to include investment costs and multiple coverage.

This study investigated resting-state information flow in epilepsy networks using stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) in 43 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients. Within-frequency directed transfer function and cross-frequency directionality analyses revealed dominant directional information flow from non-seizure-onset zone (non-SOZ) to SOZ across multiple frequencies. SOZ electrodes exhibited a more negative 1/f power slope compared to non-SOZ, suggesting lower excitability. Larger asymmetry in within-frequency information flow—weaker SOZ to non-SOZ and stronger non-SOZ to SOZ—was associated with favorable seizure outcome (Engel I). A balanced random forest classifier using within-frequency inward information flow predicted SOZ at the individual electrode level with an accuracy of 0.85 and AUC of 0.94. Seizure outcome prediction using mean non-SOZ to SOZ information flow achieved an accuracy of 0.77 and AUC of 0.78 when SOZ was clinically identified, and 0.72 accuracy with AUC of 0.75 when SOZ was model-estimated. The findings indicate that brief resting-state SEEG connectivity analysis may localize the SOZ and predict seizure outcome without requiring prolonged ictal recordings.

The passage details NVIDIA's Turing GPU architecture, emphasizing its role in deep learning inference and real-time ray tracing. NVIDIA GPUs are the standard for deep learning training, with GPU-based inferencing gaining adoption. The Tesla T4 GPU, based on Turing, delivers up to 40x higher inference performance and over 50x greater energy efficiency than CPU-based solutions, using Tensor Cores for multi-precision computing. Turing introduces RT Cores that accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray/triangle intersection, enabling real-time ray tracing for effects like shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, often combined with rasterization in a hybrid rendering model. Tensor Cores also power AI features through NVIDIA NGX, including Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) for image enhancement, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. The architecture includes a new GDDR6 memory subsystem with improved effective bandwidth, an enhanced video engine supporting more decode formats and higher concurrent streams, Multi-Process Service improvements, and NVLink for GPU interconnects. New shading technologies include Mesh Shading with task and mesh shaders, Variable Rate Shading for fine-grained control, Texture Space Shading for decoupled shading, and Multi-View Rendering for efficient multi-viewpoint rendering. Virtual Reality benefits from VirtualLink USB-C support, foveated rendering via VRS, and accelerated audio ray tracing. The RTX-OPS metric is introduced to quantify hybrid rendering workloads. The document also describes the TU104 and TU106 GPU variants and their specifications.

A short squeeze happens when a heavily shorted stock’s price rises instead of falling, forcing short sellers to buy back shares at higher prices to return borrowed stock, which further drives up the price. Short squeezes are rare and random; backtesting a specific short squeeze trading strategy is practically impossible. Short selling is difficult because potential losses are theoretically unlimited, while gains are capped at 100%. A short squeeze typically lasts 2–4 weeks, often less than a month. The Volkswagen squeeze lasted about 31 trading days, and the GameStop squeeze lasted under a month. The opposite of a short squeeze is a long squeeze (or bear squeeze), where a heavily shorted stock’s price declines, forcing short sellers to sell at increasingly lower prices to cut losses. In the U.S. stock market, a short squeeze may be illegal if there is manipulation; naked short sales are illegal. In derivative markets, there is no requirement to borrow shares before selling short. A short squeeze exit strategy involves monitoring price movements and short interest ratio, using stop-loss orders or trailing stops to exit before a sharp reversal. High short interest stocks underperform low short interest stocks, and backtests show no indication that high short interest predicts an imminent short squeeze. The passage includes an anecdote from Victor Niederhoffer about losing money on a short squeeze in RH Doe stock. An example is the GameStop short squeeze in early 2021, where retail investors on WallStreetBets drove the price from $17 to a peak of $483 within a month, causing heavy losses for short sellers. Short squeezes receive significant media attention, leading to a mistaken impression that they occur more frequently than they do.

The professor declines to repeat material on discrete coding, encourages specific questions, and announces a problem set due October 14th covering problems 1–7 and 26. The lecture then contrasts Riemann integration (partitioning the time axis) with Lebesgue integration (partitioning the vertical axis into intervals of size ε and measuring the set of times the function falls in each interval). Lebesgue defined the measure of an interval (a,b) as b−a, regardless of endpoint inclusion, and the measure of a countable union of disjoint intervals as the sum of their measures. Any subset of a zero-measure set also has zero measure; a set has measure zero if it can be covered by intervals of arbitrarily small total measure. The set of rationals in (0,1) is shown to have measure zero via two covering arguments. An uncountable set of measure zero is constructed by removing all ternary expansions containing a 1, leaving sequences of 0s and 2s, which has measure zero but is uncountable.

A function is measurable if for every interval, the set of times where the function's value lies in that interval is measurable. For a non-negative measurable function, the Lebesgue integral always exists (finite or infinite). The functions |u(t)| and |u(t)|² are measurable if u is measurable. L1 functions are measurable with finite integral of |u|; L2 functions are measurable with finite integral of |u|². For time-limited functions, L2 implies L1. For an L2 time-limited function, its Fourier coefficients exist and are finite. The Fourier series converges in mean square (limit in the mean, l.i.m.) to the function: the energy of the difference between the function and the finite series goes to zero as the number of terms increases. Given any sequence of coefficients with finite energy, there exists an L2 function satisfying this mean-square convergence. An arbitrary L2 function can be segmented into intervals of length T, and each segment expanded in a Fourier series, yielding a double sum of orthogonal time-limited exponentials. The lecture ends by noting that the Fourier transform will be discussed next.

The paper proposes a new anti-unification technique for variadic nominal terms, which combine binders and variadic expressions. Anti-unification computes generalizations that preserve similarities and abstract differences, with applications in program analysis, code clone detection, and automated program repair. Existing methods struggle with non-trivial differences and overemphasize local variable names. The algorithm operates on terms with atoms (which can be bound) and variables (individual and hedge), computing least general generalizations (lggs) along with difference information. It is parametrized by a rigidity function to control similarity granularity. A running example illustrates code clone detection (types 1–4). The formal framework defines variadic nominal syntax, permutations, substitutions, freshness constraints, and equivalence. The rule-based VNAU algorithm uses rules for decomposition, solving, merging, and narrowing, and is proven terminating, sound, and complete. An example shows it handles code clones by renaming bound atoms and providing a generalization term, a store of differences, and reconstruction mappings. However, the algorithm suffers from high nondeterminism and limited control over similarity selection, which a refined version with a rigidity function aims to address.

The President addresses Congress on the urgent financial condition of the Treasury, citing increasing embarrassments and the need to maintain public faith. The Secretary of the Treasury estimates a deficit of about $14,000,000 after exhausting probable resources. Congress authorized $5,000,000 in Treasury notes, but a pending loan bill would still leave a $2,500,000 deficit. The disproportion between public responsibilities and means is not transient and will increase under existing laws unless defenses are impaired, which is deemed unacceptable. Foreign relations are critical, requiring maintained means of asserting rights.

The President urges vigorous and decisive measures, not mere palliatives, expressing confidence in the country’s abundant resources and the people’s energy. He expects Congress will need to lay additional duties on imports, possibly advancing some above 20 percent, for revenue and incidental protection to manufacturing. He recommends a spirit of mutual harmony in revising the tariff.

An additional reason for increasing duties beyond 20 percent is to fund adequate appropriations for defenses. By express provision, the act distributing proceeds of public land sales to the States ceases if duties exceed the prescribed limit. The President regrets the necessity of departing from the act of 1833, as some States will be disappointed, but states that establishing the credit of the General Government on durable foundations is the highest priority, affording more effectual support to State credit than direct distribution. The distribution law was passed when a real surplus was anticipated; continuing it without a surplus and while needing to borrow and increase duties would be an unwise alienation of the public creditor’s security.

American credit has been depressed to an unprecedented degree due to conditions of State banking institutions, vast foreign debt from speculation, and the doctrine of repudiation of contracts by States. To contract a loan, securities should be tendered that inspire confidence. A pledge of a specific fund, such as the land fund, would better satisfy capitalists. The land fund is ample to secure interest and ultimately reimburse principal; a debt of $18,000,000 or $20,000,000 could be extinguished by surplus sales within a reasonable time. To relieve the Treasury and aid requisitions until new tariff duties become available, it seems necessary to fund a debt approaching $15,000,000. The President submits whether the proceeds of public land sales should be pledged for interest payments, and the Secretary of the Treasury authorized to use surplus proceeds to purchase stock to extinguish the debt and prevent surplus accumulation while distribution is suspended.

The disorder at the heart of the Federal system paralyzes every part. Restoring the credit and finances of the Federal Government is the first great want; without it, attempts to better conditions will be fruitless. Confidence in the Government is the source of all credit; its diminution causes distrust and derangement. Maintaining good faith and punctuality in the General Government’s operations will rectify partial irregularities by example; debasing that standard could lead to widespread degradation. The representatives of the people need only to will it for public credit to be restored. The President has frankly expressed his views; the Executive can do no more. If credit is questioned, defenses weakened, or administration embarrassed for want of means, he trusts this department will be found to have done all in its power to avert such evils and be acquitted of blame.

This document describes optional extensions to SEV and SNP for page migration, using the Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine. TMPM copies page content and updates mappings, supporting tiered memory systems where data is moved between performance tiers. It can pause DMA traffic during migration, enabling safe movement of pages used by IO devices, and acts as a trusted agent for migrating SNP-protected guest pages. Commands allow migration of multiple pages (up to 128) while maintaining guest physical addresses. A Pre-Migration state is defined for SNP guest pages, using a platform-specific ASID. Performance is optimized with commands of 16 or more pages, maximum at 128. Non-migratable data structures include IOMMU memory structures, the ring buffer, and argument pages. IOMMU mapping requires source pages to be DMA-mapped via a single host page table. TMPM firmware can be reloaded after pausing operations and tearing down the ring buffer; the reload procedure varies by EPYC family, determined via PM_GET_CAPABILITIES. For debugging, single commands can be sent by keeping the ring buffer tail pointer within one entry of the head pointer.

The device performs data write operations synchronously to the external SCLK clock. It supports one-byte or two-byte (half-word) read/write commands. Output data in a frame depends on the previous frame's command and DATA_VAL bits, providing fixed patterns, 8-bit or 16-bit register data, or the latest conversion result. Data flags (device address, range, alarms, parity) can be appended to the output word.

The multiSPI interface uses legacy SPI-compatible protocols (SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, SPI-11-S) for device configuration. Nine configuration registers are mapped: DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG (reset, NAP, power-down modes), SDI_CTL_REG (SPI protocol selection), SDO_CTL_REG (SDO mode, SRC, dual SDO), DATAOUT_CTL_REG (output control, flags, parity, test patterns), RANGE_SEL_REG (reference and input range), ALARM_REG (alarm flags), ALARM_H_TH_REG (hysteresis and high threshold), and ALARM_L_TH_REG (low threshold).

This study examines the knowledge, attitudes, and effectiveness of AI tools in Hungarian education, focusing on programming. Interviews with 14 high school teachers/university lecturers and a questionnaire with 53 university students revealed that participants are familiar with a range of AI applications, most notably ChatGPT, Copilot, DALL-E, Midjourney, and Bard/Gemini. They use these tools for debugging, explaining steps, information search, code generation, task generation, and summarization. Opinions on AI's capability to support education were mixed; some found them capable for small tasks but not larger ones, and foundational knowledge is needed to verify correctness. Advantages cited include time savings, faster debugging, more time for creative tasks, easier self-learning, and immediate answers. Disadvantages include cheating, excessive reliance, impaired learning effectiveness, undermined critical thinking, and legal data issues. Overall, 91% of participants held a positive attitude toward integrating AI into education.

The study also evaluated the accuracy of free, multilingual chatbots (Gemini, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot) on programming tasks. For beginner tasks involving programming theorems, ChatGPT achieved 92% correct responses, Copilot 74%, and Gemini 64%. In more complex tasks (HTML, JavaScript game, PHP/AJAX pagination, C file operations with fork/pipe/message queue), ChatGPT solved all tasks after additional prompts, while Gemini and Copilot failed to provide complete solutions for the C task. None of the tools achieved 100% accuracy. The findings indicate that AI tools can assist learning if users possess critical thinking and minimal prior knowledge to recognize errors; otherwise, they may mislead novices. Thus, AI can be useful for instructors (task generation, lesson preparation) and learners (practice, assessment) but is not fully reliable for those lacking subject knowledge.
