The TPS7H500x-SP controllers include a FAULT pin for implementing external protections such as input overcurrent or overvoltage. A fault shutdown occurs if the pin voltage exceeds 0.6 V for a duration between 0.4 µs and 1.4 µs. After the fault clears (voltage below 0.5 V), a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles plus internal logic delay is initiated, followed by a soft-start sequence. Slope compensation is provided to mitigate subharmonic oscillation in peak current mode when duty cycle exceeds 50%. It is a voltage ramp subtracted from the error amplifier output, with a recommended slope equal to the inductor falling current slope. Frequency compensation uses a transconductance error amplifier with Type 2A or 2B networks; component values are selected based on crossover frequency and power stage transconductance. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C junction temperature, with restart at 160°C. The devices are radiation-hardened PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge, with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz. A design example for a synchronous push-pull converter using GaN FETs at 500 kHz and 5 V output details component selection: RT resistor for frequency, feedback divider, dead-time resistors, leading edge blank time resistor, soft-start capacitor, transformer turns ratio and primary inductance, main and synchronous rectifier FETs, RCD clamp, output inductor, output capacitance (including SET mitigation), current sense resistor for overcurrent, hiccup capacitor, frequency compensation components, and slope compensation resistor. Layout guidelines recommend separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switch node area, routing feedback away from noise, placing bypass capacitors close to the controller, and filtering the sensed current signal.

The passage describes methods and systems for automatically generating orthodontic treatment plans by applying user-specific clinical preferences. A database of user preferences is created by analyzing historical treatment data, including user-provided text instructions and corresponding clinical behaviors. Key preference text statements are identified using machine learning (e.g., bag-of-words models) and similarity search (e.g., Damerau-Levenshtein distance) to match reference key preferences with user instructions. Statistical preference analysis detects consistent clinical behaviors over time by clustering treatment features and identifying recent stable patterns, even when explicit text instructions are absent. The database links each user with verified key preference statements and associated clinical behaviors. When a dental professional submits a new case with patient dentition data and treatment instructions, the system automatically generates a treatment plan by matching the instructions to the user’s key preferences in the database and incorporating the corresponding clinical behaviors. Monitoring tools evaluate the accuracy of automatic preference application and update the database as user behavior changes, reducing manual processing time and plan modifications.

This study investigates human-AI interaction in conversational information-seeking (CIS) with ChatGPT, focusing on three levels: user prompting strategies, ChatGPT’s communication style adaptation, and the influence of ChatGPT’s responses on user perceptions and attitudes. A 3 (issue: health, science, policy) × 2 (issue controversy: controversial, non-controversial) between-subject experiment was conducted with a nationally representative sample of 937 U.S. adults. Participants engaged in at least five turns of information-seeking with GPT-4o. Communication styles (self-revealing, information-seeking, fact-oriented, action-seeking, cognitive complexity) were extracted using the Symanto Psychology API and LIWC. Prompting strategies were annotated by ChatGPT, with high inter-coder reliability (IRR = .814, weighted F1 = .903). Key findings: 19.1% of users employed at least one prompting strategy, predicted by education level and party affiliation. Issue controversy influenced ChatGPT’s communication styles (e.g., action-seeking, cognitive complexity) and citation count, while user prompts’ communication styles remained consistent across controversy. ChatGPT’s cognitive complexity shaped user perceptions: more cognitively complex responses were perceived less favorably but led to more positive issue-relevant attitude changes.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU accelerates General Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) operations central to neural network training and inference. Each A100 Tensor Core executes 256 FP16 fused multiply-add operations per clock, computing an 8x4x8 mixed-precision matrix multiplication. With four Tensor Cores per SM and 108 SMs, the A100 delivers up to 312 TFLOPS of dense FP16/FP32 performance—2.5x the Tensor Core performance of Tesla V100 and 20x V100’s standard FP32 throughput.

A100 Tensor Cores support new data formats: TF32 (FP32 range, FP16 precision, 8x throughput vs FP32), BF16, and FP64. FP64 Tensor Core acceleration provides 19.5 TFLOPS, 2.5x V100 FP64. Fine-grained structured sparsity with a 2:4 pattern doubles compute throughput by skipping zero-value entries, using a pruning and fine-tuning recipe that maintains inference accuracy.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions the A100 into up to seven GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute, memory paths, and L2 cache slices, providing quality of service and fault isolation for multi-tenant environments. Third-generation NVLink offers 12 links at 50 Gbit/s per pair, yielding 600 GB/s total bandwidth, with non-posted writes and improved error detection.

The A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache (6.7x larger than V100), and L2 cache residency controls. Compute data compression improves bandwidth and effective capacity. CUDA 11 introduces asynchronous copy instructions that bypass the register file, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, and cooperative groups enhancements. The DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs with NVSwitch and Mellanox InfiniBand, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS.

The instructor outlines course logistics: no textbook, no recitation, office hour Monday 3:30–4:30, materials on the course website, grading based on five problem sets (75%) and a final 8–10 page paper (25%), no exams. The lecture then addresses why gravity is special: other interactions are described by gauge theories in fixed spacetime, while quantum gravity lacks a complete theory, with unresolved questions about spacetime fluctuations, continuity, and black holes. The holographic duality proposes that quantum gravity equals ordinary field theories on a fixed spacetime, implying gravity and dynamical spacetime can emerge from non-gravitational systems. This echoes earlier ideas by Sakharov and parallels with hydrodynamics. The Weinberg-Witten theorem states that a theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved current cannot contain massless charged particles of spin greater than 1/2, and a theory with a conserved Lorentz-covariant stress tensor cannot contain massless particles of spin greater than 1. The theorem does not forbid the graviton in general relativity because GR lacks a conserved Lorentz-covariant stress tensor, but it rules out emergent gravity in ordinary QFTs in the same spacetime. The holographic duality circumvents this because gravity lives in a higher-dimensional spacetime. A proof of the theorem is begun using one-particle states, helicity, and matrix elements, showing that if a massless spin-j particle exists with a conserved current or stress tensor, the spin must be ≤ 1/2 or ≤ 1 respectively to avoid contradiction.

Judges have historically disclaimed immunity from criticism. Lord Chancellor Parker invited public scrutiny of his judgments. Judge W. H. Taft in 1895 stressed that free public criticism of judicial action outweighs immunity from unjust attacks. Fair, informed criticism makes judges careful and solicitous of exact justice. Professional criticism from legal writers and law reviews serves as an impartial tribunal. Nonprofessional criticism is also useful, as average men's protests may expose defects in judicial reasoning. Public comment spurs judges to examine their conscience; for life-tenured judges, it is the only practical means to keep them responsive. Unjust attacks must be answered, but courts should rely on the strength of their opinions. If the best citizens and the bar prohibit all criticism, the people will embrace intemperate criticism from agitators. Just, temperate criticism guards against widespread judiciary antagonism that would menace the Republic. The passage then addresses crime and lynching. Each section should correct its own faults. Corruption requires an awakened public conscience and legislation for swift, certain law enforcement. The BioRecall study protocol presents a biobank-recall pilot to collect lifestyle and environmental exposure data via an electronic questionnaire, combined with existing genotypes, biological samples, and clinical outcomes. Strengths include low-cost scalability, extensive dataset, and automated feedback; limitations are the limited pilot sample size, inclusion of only one biobank, and lack of wearable data.

The power management unit (PMU) generates internal core supplies, supervises the external supply, and contains the bandgap voltage reference. The clock module (CKM) provides internal oscillators (LFOSC, SYSOSC) and supports external crystal or digital clock inputs, distributing various clocks (MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, etc.) for the processor, bus, and peripherals. The DMA controller allows data movement without CPU intervention, supporting features like repeated transfer modes and various triggers. The event manager transfers digital events between entities using publishers and subscribers. Flash memory stores program code and data, supporting in-circuit programming and small sector sizes. SRAM provides zero wait state access and retains content in RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY modes. The GPIO peripheral supports up to 45 pins with set/clear/toggle and wake features. The IOMUX enables IO pad configuration and digital signal routing. The 12-bit ADC supports fast conversions with internal channels and a configurable reference. The temperature sensor provides a voltage output internally connected to an ADC channel, with a factory calibration value provided. The Low-Frequency Sub-System (LFSS) contains a Real Time Clock and an independent watchdog timer. The VREF module provides a configurable voltage reference buffer. The comparator compares voltage levels on two inputs and supports blanking sources and wake-up. Security features include flexible firewalls and a CRC module. The UART, I2C, and SPI peripherals support standard communication protocols with DMA data transfer. The IWDT and WWDT are independent and windowed watchdog timers for code execution supervision. The RTC_B provides a time base with calendar, alarm, and calibration features. Timers (TIMx) include general-purpose and advanced timers with PWM, QEI, and cross-trigger capabilities. The DEBUGSS interfaces the SWD two-wire debug interface to multiple debug functions. Device factory constants are stored in a memory-mapped FACTORY region providing read-only device data.

DNA origami uses DNA base-pairing to self-assemble nanostructures. A team led by Ralf Jungmann applied a super-resolution microscopy method called DNA-PAINT to visualize all strands in these structures individually. They found that assembly is robust across varying conditions, but the probability of a staple strand incorporating depends on its target sequence position. DNA-PAINT employs dye-linked imager strands that bind transiently, producing a blinking signal for high-resolution imaging. Results showed not all sites are occupied in every structure; using excess staples and selecting positions based on incorporation efficiency mapping is recommended. The technique can optimize DNA nanostructure construction and has potential in quantitative structural biology for measuring labeling efficiency of antibodies, proteins, and nucleic acids.

The passage discusses combining dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) with Gaussian process (GP) regression to model noisy, nonlinear dynamical systems. Transfer operator theory and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces provide analytical tools. DMD, a Galerkin method using linear regression and eigenvalue decomposition, can linearize nonlinear systems globally but requires dictionary learning. Kernel methods, including GP regression, offer non-parametric flexibility, probabilistic predictions, and model selection. The work develops a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator, yielding a modified Extended DMD (EDMD) that handles measurement noise and provides uncertainty estimates for multi-step predictions. Kernel-based DMD algorithms face high computational cost (O(N³)); the variational free energy method is considered to improve scalability. The proposed algorithm is a special case of EDMD, inheriting its limitations, but integrates hyperparameter optimization and sparse dictionary learning within a coherent Bayesian framework. A lifted observation model with operator-valued kernels is introduced to handle infinite-dimensional output spaces.

This paper studies modal extensions of lattice semantics, where the necessity operator is interpreted as the greatest lower bound of values in accessible worlds. It defines regular modal extensions (where necessity means true in all accessible worlds) and normal modal valuations on complete lattices. A normal modal valuation yields a unique regular extension if and only if the set of designated values is a filter containing its own meet. The formula (2ϕ ∨ 2ψ) → 2(ϕ ∨ ψ) is valid on all frames exactly when the designated set is implicative. For axiom K, with a strictly deductive implication, validity on all frames is equivalent to the lattice being linear outside the filter. When implication is defined as −x+y, validity of K on all frames corresponds to the designated set being implicative, provided the lattice is anti-monotone, involutive, and has down-distribution. An example using twist algebras from Boolean algebras illustrates these results, showing that a specific filter yields validity of K.

An Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) machine learning potential was developed for YBa₂Cu₃O₇₋ₓ (YBCO), trained on a DFT dataset of 1368 configurations including defects, vacancies, interstitials, amorphous-like structures, and oxygen Frenkel pairs. The potential achieves energy and force RMSEs of ~10 meV/atom and ~70 meV/Å, and accurately reproduces the equation of state, lattice parameters, and oxygen Frenkel pair energetics, improving upon a prior Buckingham+Coulomb classical potential. NPT molecular dynamics simulations with ~25000 atoms show a spontaneous orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition at approximately 800 K, driven by oxygen migration from O1 and O4 sites to O5 interstitial sites in the basal plane, breaking CuO chain order. The transition is entropy-driven, facilitated by a decreasing formation energy of O1v-O5i Frenkel pairs with thermal expansion. The simulated transition temperature is lower than the experimental ~1000 K, partly attributed to the conserved particle number in simulations versus oxygen loss in experiments. The potential enables accurate investigation of oxygen diffusion and may aid in optimizing annealing strategies for radiation-damaged superconducting tapes.

The professor compares ion and neutral atom trapping: ions are confined via Coulomb forces with electric fields, easily trapping room-temperature ions, whereas neutral atom traps have depths on the order of microkelvin to kelvin. Cooling methods include Doppler, evaporative, and sideband cooling; sideband cooling is now also applied to neutral atoms in tight dipole traps. Clocks, quantum information, and quantum simulation are pursued with both ions and neutral atoms. The lecture focuses on dynamic ion traps because static electric potentials cannot confine ions in all directions due to zero divergence of the electric field. The Paul trap alternates between confining and anti-confining potentials; net trapping results from the particle's micromotion, analogous to alternating positive and negative lenses producing a net focusing effect. The trapping potential is the kinetic energy of the micromotion. For quantum computation, single-qubit operations are Rabi oscillations. The Cirac-Zoller gate uses the center-of-mass vibrational motion as a data bus. The sequence: cool the center-of-mass mode to the ground state, swap the qubit state of one ion into the center-of-mass motion using a pi pulse on a sideband, perform a controlled phase gate on another ion via a laser resonant only with the first vibrational excited state of the qubit's excited state (a 2π pulse imparting a -1 phase shift), then swap the information back. This realizes a two-qubit gate between any two ions. The Cirac-Zoller gate requires ground-state cooling and is limited by the slow center-of-mass motion; other gates like geometric or Sørensen gates exist.

The professor recaps that planning is dynamic, goals are to create and harvest value, and investors ask “why this, why now, why this team, and why won’t it work.” He introduces speaker Bob Jones.

Bob Jones states that the only non-negotiable requirement for a successful business is customers. He recounts a failed product launch: Regain, a nutrition bar for dialysis patients. He surveyed clinicians who endorsed it, but the actual customers—patients—did not want it, could not afford it, and retail pharmacies demanded high slotting fees. The failure stemmed from misidentifying the customer.

He then describes a successful launch: NiteBite, a timed-release glucose bar for people with diabetes to prevent nocturnal hypoglycemia. He spoke directly to patients and parents, learning their fear of dying in their sleep and desire for peace of mind. Customers did not want a medical label, so he gave it a non-medical name. He built demand by calling certified diabetes educators, who recommended the product to patients. Patients then called the company to order. He leveraged this customer demand to persuade retail pharmacies and wholesalers to stock the product without paying slotting fees. He segmented the market, starting with those most motivated by the problem.

He emphasizes finding out what customers want and giving it to them, selling benefits rather than features, and focusing on those who feel the most pain. He advises making a minimum viable product to test if it works before refining branding. The key lesson is to identify who will write the check, understand their needs, and use customer demand to drive sales.

This study investigated race differences in the relationship between blood pressure (BP) and longitudinal cognitive decline using data from 2284 Black and White older adults from three harmonized cohort studies. Participants were categorized into normal, high, or variable BP groups based on mean systolic BP and standard deviation. Cognitive performance was assessed across global cognition and five domains (episodic memory, visuospatial abilities, processing speed, semantic memory, working memory). Linear mixed effects models examined cognitive change over time, controlling for age, sex, education, and baseline diagnosis. Results showed no racial differences in cognitive decline among those with normal BP. White adults with high BP declined faster than Black adults with normal or high BP in global cognition, processing speed, semantic memory, and working memory. White adults with variable BP declined faster than all Black groups across all cognitive domains. Secondary analyses indicated that lower baseline cognitive performance did not explain these race differences. The findings indicate that older White adults exhibit greater susceptibility to cognitive decline associated with elevated or fluctuating BP compared to Black counterparts.

In Wiechmann v Wiechmann, the Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed a divorce judgment that split physical custody of four children. The trial court awarded physical custody of the two older children to the plaintiff father and the two younger children to the defendant mother, with shared legal custody. A custody specialist had recommended that all children be placed with the defendant. The defendant appealed, arguing the children should remain together and she should have custody. The Court of Appeals held that while keeping siblings together is generally in the best interests of each child, the best interests of each individual child controls. The trial court properly considered the statutory best-interest factors and did not abuse its discretion in concluding that separating the siblings was in each child's best interests. The decision was affirmed.

The Covid-19 pandemic forced many countries to interrupt formal education and adopt distance education, revealing it as an alternative and supplement to face-to-face instruction. The research aims to discuss artificial intelligence-assisted or AI-based training as a form of distance education. Artificial intelligence refers to systems that automatically perform tasks, and through machine learning and deep learning, computers can now learn from large data sets. Examples include IBM's Watson, which won Jeopardy and diagnoses oncology, and AlphaGo, which defeated a human in Go. Key terms are algorithms, machine learning, and artificial neural networks that imitate the human nervous system; projects like BabyX demonstrate categorization and reaction abilities. Deep learning now enables machines to analyze big data, though not yet at human levels. Google's autonomous car exemplifies AI progress.

In education, AI is increasingly used and may be applied in personalized teaching, student affairs, game-based learning, and more. Intelligent Education Systems (IES) use domain, pedagogy, and learner models to provide step-by-step teaching adapted to individual needs, with data capture and analysis enabling decision-making. A further step is a system where AI creates all modules without human effect. Three types of AI education are identified: AI-supported face-to-face, face-to-face with AI (machine as teacher), and simulation education with AI. Andriessen and Sandberg's scenarios include transmission (fixed goals), studio (flexible materials), and negotiation (interactive, evolving goals). In IES, the first choice is AI assisting humans; the second is face-to-face education by a robot or screen animation; the third is simulation. Methods can be controlled fixed algorithms or fully deep learning-based. Supervised learning relies on human-defined algorithms and curricula, reducing ethical concerns. Unsupervised deep learning would create an AI that trains itself and decides how to educate humans, fitting the negotiation scenario.

Learning environments can be face-to-face with AI (real learners, virtual teacher) or online simulation. Simulation education, a type of distance education, can use tools like VR glasses or, in the future, neural integration such as Neural Link, allowing individuals to experience artificial classrooms or social environments. AI can offer rich, realistic learning experiences.

Discussion notes that AI and Smart Teaching Systems may bring efficiency, reduce costs and risks, and improve learning outcomes. Simulation can eliminate peer bullying and discipline problems, and one AI could train many individuals simultaneously. However, concerns include the fear of AI surpassing human intelligence (singularity), potential control or enslavement of humans, privacy issues, cyber-attacks, isolation, educator unemployment, and psychological effects like reality confusion. Conclusions state that alternative education systems are needed for emergencies, and AI-based education should be researched more. While computers have not reached human mental capacity, progress suggests it is no longer utopian. Education may increasingly be entrusted to machines, necessitating serious discussion.

The Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) specification defines a secure method for non-persistent runtime updates to AMD-provided firmware and settings without requiring a BIOS reflash or system reset. SFS addresses high-benefit/low-risk issues to improve system stability and mitigate some security issues, but does not patch x86 code (e.g., SMM, AGESA, UEFI) or run-once code like ABL. Its scope is limited to priority runtime concerns affecting AMD binary firmware components in AGESA releases, such as ASP firmware, modules, and register settings. Updates are non-persistent across reboots and serve as interim steps between BIOS releases.

SFS packages are cryptographically signed by AMD. Customers may optionally co-sign packages, requiring a public key to be sent to the ASP during early boot. The ASP acts as root of trust for detection, verifying AMD’s signature before applying updates. The system designer (OEM/ODM) owns the root of trust for update; co-signing allows them to maintain that role. BIOS must be compiled with SFS enabled and co-signing configured if desired.

Applying an SFS package changes three version numbers: the SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), which monotonically increases and identifies the applied package; individual firmware component versions and Security Patch Levels (SPL); and the System Patch Level (SYSPL) for run-once code modifications, also monotonically increasing. Version information is available to the host OS via a command.

SFS updates are applied at runtime and must be reapplied after each reboot. In multi-socket systems, the first socket’s ASP receives the patch and ensures correct application across sockets. Multiple updates must be applied sequentially. A customer-provided SFS Deployment Agent (SFSDA) uses the PSP/ASP driver to communicate with the ASP. Commands require a 2MB-aligned TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER in DRAM, with specific memory layouts for different commands. The ASP process involves verifying signatures, loading and executing the patch, updating patch level information, and returning status.

SFS packages are binary objects aligned to AGESA releases, named with family, AGESA release number, and a monotonically increasing integer. Release is coordinated through AMD customer channels. Updates must match the specific firmware combination on the system. The update process runs in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic, aiming for minimal performance impact, typically requiring no OS quiescing. Some operations, like SEV/SNP updates, may require VM stop/restart but not a system reboot.

El neuromarketing, definido como la aplicación de técnicas de neuroimagen para entender la conducta del consumidor, se encuentra en una etapa inicial. La industria audiovisual, ante la aparición de plataformas digitales y nuevas formas de consumo, busca en estas técnicas un método complementario para mejorar su competitividad y el retorno de la inversión. Empresas internacionales como Viacom, Cartoon Network o ESPN ya utilizan neuromarketing para testar contenidos, promociones y bloques publicitarios. Un análisis de webs de la NMSBA reveló que un 18% de las empresas ofrecen servicios al entretenimiento, concentradas principalmente en Estados Unidos y Reino Unido.

En España, se investigó el perfil del profesional del neuromarketing audiovisual mediante 18 entrevistas a consultoras, representantes del sector audiovisual, neurocientíficos y académicos. Los resultados confirman que es factible estudiar al consumidor audiovisual con técnicas neurocientíficas, aunque existen limitaciones éticas, de interpretación de datos y de tamaño muestral. Se requiere un equipo multidisciplinar (neurocientíficos, expertos en marketing, ingenieros) y seguir el método científico.

El neuromarketing en España es incipiente. Las causas incluyen desconocimiento, desconfianza, mala praxis de terceros, falta de actitud innovadora y precio. Todas las consultoras entrevistadas han realizado estudios para el sector audiovisual, con una media del 33% del volumen de trabajo y 38% de facturación. La cuota de mercado ha crecido exponencialmente en el último año, pero se concentra en pocos clientes. Los servicios se orientan al análisis de contenido y a la mejora de bloques publicitarios. Los principales clientes son los grupos privados Atresmedia y Mediaset España. Mediaset testa ficción en prime time con pulseras de actividad electrodérmica y encuestas, en fases iniciales de producción. Atresmedia ha empleado EEG, EMG y otras medidas para bloques publicitarios, pero abandonó el test de contenido al no poder identificar causas. TVE dejó de usar estas técnicas por motivos económicos. Las productoras cinematográficas y de televisión muestran interés, pero no invierten debido a bajos presupuestos y falta de personal intermediario.

La proyección futura se considera positiva, condicionada al desarrollo tecnológico, estandarización, mejora en la interpretación de datos, abaratamiento y demostración del retorno de inversión. Se prevé que las consultoras que no aporten valor desaparecerán y que la transferencia universidad-empresa será clave. Las principales limitaciones actuales son tecnológicas y de interpretación, y los retos futuros se centran en avanzar en la interpretación de datos y en la monitorización electrodérmica de la emoción.

Research indicates that improving air quality in schools can significantly enhance student outcomes. Following a 2015 gas leak in Aliso Canyon, California, air purifiers installed in classrooms led to math score gains equivalent to three months of learning and similar English gains, with effects persisting over time. This intervention cost approximately $30 per student, less than 1% of the cost of class-size reduction programs yielding comparable results. Additional studies found portable air cleaners reduced student absenteeism by 12.5%, and illness-related absences dropped 55% in Swedish daycare centers with air cleaners. Improved ventilation and mold removal also boosted English and math scores and pass rates. Benefits include direct cognitive gains by reducing inhalation of fine particulate matter that can cause inflammation and breach the blood-brain barrier, health improvements that decrease respiratory infections and sick days for students and staff, and addressing inequalities as low-income schools often face higher pollution. The administrative burden is minimal—devices are simply plugged in with annual filter changes. Schools are urged to reconnect or install air purifiers, targeting a Clean Air Delivery Rate of 30 cubic feet per minute per student and noise below 50 decibels, while monitoring test scores, absenteeism, nurse visits, and teacher satisfaction.

The study simulates the transition from ICE vehicles to BEVs using one year of telematics data from 10,441 users in Asti, Italy, comprising over 10 million trips. Four BEV models (Fiat 500e, Renault Megane E-Tech, Tesla Model 3, Audi A6 e-tron) with varying battery capacities and consumption profiles are evaluated under four charging scenarios: Scenario 1 (workplace AC charging, SoC<75%, weekdays 8-20h, parking ≥6h), Scenario 2 (AC charging whenever SoC<25%, parking ≥6h), Scenario 3 (overnight AC charging 20-8h, SoC<75%, parking ≥6h), Scenario 4 (50 kW DC fast-charge whenever SoC<25%, parking ≥20min). Trips are replicated exactly without altering itineraries; a trip is infeasible if SoC reaches 0.

Results show Scenario 1 yields the lowest average feasible trip percentages (64%–88% across models), with only 43% of users suitable (≥99% trips feasible) even with the Audi A6 e-tron. Scenarios 2, 3, and 4 perform better. Scenario 4 achieves the highest feasibility, with average feasible trips exceeding 98% for all models except the Fiat 500e; 95% of users are suitable with the Audi A6 e-tron, and 72% can complete 100% of trips. However, even under the best conditions, 5% of users cannot meet all trips. Overnight charging (Scenario 3) provides the highest average post-trip SoC (above 70%), potentially reducing range anxiety despite slightly lower feasibility than Scenario 4. The number of monthly charging sessions varies: for the Audi A6 e-tron, Scenarios 2 and 4 require about half the charges of Scenario 3 (median 1.1 charges/month in Scenario 2). The Fiat 500e requires many charges (third-quartile >12/month under Scenario 3) and suits only 35% of users with overnight charging. The study assumes constant consumption, constant charging power, full charging infrastructure availability, and omits cost analysis. It concludes that current BEV technology can serve many but not all users in the studied province.

A retrospective cohort study used the All of Us Research Program dataset v7 to predict healthy aging among 99,935 participants aged 50 and older with SDOH survey responses and EHR data. Healthy aging was defined as a composite score of zero for comorbidities (modified Charlson Comorbidity Index), cognitive conditions (no mild cognitive impairment), and mobility function (not in assisted living) for those aged over 75. Three machine learning algorithms—logistic regression, multi-layer perceptron, and XGBoost—were trained. The XGBoost model with random oversampling achieved the best performance (AUROC 0.793, F1 score 0.697). The model demonstrated predictive parity across race and sex groups, with positive and negative predictive value ratios between 0.86 and 1.06. Feature importance analysis using SHAP values identified health insurance type as the most predictive feature, followed by employment status, substance use, and health insurance coverage. A secondary cohort with a stricter definition (age over 85) showed consistent results. The study concludes that XGBoost accurately predicts healthy aging and highlights the significant role of health insurance. Limitations include the lack of a unanimous healthy aging definition, potential selection bias from volunteer participants, and unmeasured confounders.

Research in Nature Climate Change reports sudden, catastrophic ecosystem shifts across Australia from combined gradual climate change and extreme weather events. Near-pristine ecosystems are experiencing abrupt, potentially irreversible changes. Australia has warmed ~1°C since the 19th century. Gradual change and extreme events act as a ‘press’ and ‘pulses’ pushing systems to collapse, exemplified by kelp forest loss, Gondwanan refugia destruction, floodplain forest dieback, alpine forest conversion, arid zone boom-bust, and mangrove dieback. Only one site had prior human disturbance, showing undisturbed systems are not necessarily resilient. Collapses can result from single events or cumulative pressures, with cascading effects. Consequences include lost ecosystem services. Predicting collapses is nearly impossible. Interventions like assisted recolonisation are costly and less likely to succeed as extreme events become more frequent. The risks of inaction may outweigh those of acting, as many seemingly healthy ecosystems may be at a tipping point.

Linebackers require toughness, athleticism, and intelligence. Key skills are vision, agility, change of direction, block shedding, explosiveness, tackling, strength, violent hands, and high motor. Typical body type is 5'10"–6'5", 215–255 lbs, lean-muscular. Notable linebackers include Ray Lewis (2× Defensive Player of the Year, 2× Super Bowl champion, 13× Pro Bowl, Hall of Fame 2018), Chuck Bednarik (first overall pick in 1949, 2× NFL champion, 10× All-Pro, played center and linebacker, Hall of Fame 1967), and Lawrence Taylor (2× Super Bowl champion, NFL MVP, 3× Defensive Player of the Year, 132.5 sacks, Hall of Fame 1999). This study tested whether role-taking and literacy interventions could reduce the influence of demographic and appearance-based cues on trust and risk-taking in social engineering contexts. An online experiment with 139 participants across four groups (Persuader, Persuadee, Literacy, Control) found no significant changes in trust or risk-taking behaviors from pre- to post-intervention, supporting the null hypothesis. The intervention did not significantly alter reliance on cues like age, gender, ethnicity, or attire. While participant feedback indicated the intervention raised awareness and was engaging, the results suggest short-term interventions may be insufficient to produce measurable behavioral change, highlighting the challenge of modifying deeply ingrained cognitive biases.

This work constructs strong pseudorandom unitaries (PRUs) in the quantum Haar random oracle model (QHROM). The construction, on input security parameter λ and key k = k1||k2||k3 (three λ-bit strings), is GU(1λ, k) = Xk3 · Uλ · Xk2 · Uλ · Xk1, where Uλ is the λ-qubit Haar random oracle. It makes two queries to the Haar random oracle and requires sampling O(log1+ϵ(n)) bits of randomness for security against poly(n)-query adversaries.

The security proof employs the path-recording framework of Ma and Huang, replacing Haar-random unitaries with path-recording isometries V and V† that simulate oracle access using relations stored in purification registers. An approximate isometry S is defined to merge two independent databases (from an ideal experiment with two Haar unitaries) into a single database while simulating keys, mapping the ideal experiment’s state close to the real experiment’s state. A query-by-query analysis with a progress measure shows that operator norm bounds such as ∥(VS − SV1)Π≤t∥op are negligible, establishing statistical closeness.

Simplifications include using unitary invariance of the Haar measure to rebalance oracle complexity, working with non-norm-preserving operators instead of isometries, and decoupling the L and R registers by replacing VL, VR with FL, FR. The proof proceeds through hybrids: from the real experiment (oracles U and Xk3UXk2UXk1) to H1 (transformed oracles Xk3UXk1 and UXk2U), H2 (replace U with V), H3 (use decoupled F operators), H4 (apply S to transition to ideal oracles F1, F2), H5 (return to V1, V2), and finally the ideal experiment with independent Haar unitaries U1, U2. The main technical contribution is proving closeness between H3 and H4 via the isometry S and the query-by-query analysis.

CEMEX, a Mexico-based building materials company, attributed much of its success from 1992 to 2007 to its acquisition and post-merger integration (PMI) process, known as the CEMEX Way. This process standardized business processes, technology, and organizational structures across all countries while granting local operational flexibility and making a concerted effort to learn best practices from acquired companies. The company's internationalization occurred in four stages: Laying the Groundwork, Stepping Out (beginning with the 1992 acquisition in Spain), Growing Up, and Stepping Up (including the 2005 acquisition of RMC and the 2007 acquisition of Rinker). The PMI process involved dispatching multinational teams of functional experts to integrate acquisitions, cataloging retained practices, and benchmarking them to identify superior processes that became new enterprise standards. The duration of the PMI process was reduced from 25 months to less than five months. A significant step in consolidating the process occurred in 1996 when the PMI process was applied to CEMEX's own Mexican operations.

The passage analyzes the problem of Germany organizing Middle Europe to use its resources and manpower for its foreign policy. It identifies four critical political problems: Poles, Czechs, South Slavs, and Bulgaria. If these peoples become accomplices or servants, Berlin would dominate the continent. The US interest is not to prevent economic unification but to disestablish imperialistic control by groups in Berlin, Vienna, and Budapest that would use the area's resources for selfish foreign policy. The present control rests on an alliance of interests among ruling powers in Vienna, Budapest, Sofia, Constantinople, and Berlin, including subjection of Poles, Czechs, and Croats; German control of Austria-Hungary's resources; German-Magyar ascendency; exploitation of Bulgaria's grievances; Turkish integrity; and post-war debts. To render Middle Europe safe, the US has assets: an economic weapon—commercial control and the threat of German exclusion from raw materials and markets, which could cause demobilization problems, revolution, financial ruin, and prolonged hardship, and can be used to threaten and lure; and assets in Austria-Hungary—nationalist discontent among Czechs and South Slavs, the Emperor's desire to preserve the patrimony, adoption of no annexations and a league of nations due to financial inability to maintain armaments. The policy should stir up nationalist discontent but refuse dismemberment, threatening the German-Magyar combination while offering safety, to reduce resistance and accelerate independence from Berlin. Austria-Hungary must be good to survive.

The DAWN-plasma study is a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard of care (SOC) versus SOC alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. The primary endpoint is the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints include clinical status, time to improvement, mechanical ventilation or death, and safety. The study hypothesizes that early high-volume convalescent plasma with high neutralizing-antibody titers reduces mechanical ventilation need. Patients are randomized 2:1 to receive 800-1000 mL convalescent plasma (4 units) with titers ≥1/160, first dose within 12 hours, second 24-36 hours later. Eligible adults ≥18 years have confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, radiographic infiltrates or SpO2 ≤94% with rales, and provide consent. Exclusions include prior mechanical ventilation, severe plasma allergy, treatment restrictions, or recent anti-CD20 therapy. The study was ethically approved, follows Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP. Six patients withdrew or were screen failures before intervention and were substituted; no post-intervention loss to follow-up.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are fixed-frequency, peak current mode PWM controllers. The EN pin can be enabled by tying it to VLDO, an external signal, or a resistor divider from VIN to program undervoltage lockout (UVLO) thresholds. An internal 1.23-V bandgap reference is divided down to a 0.613-V error amplifier reference. The output voltage is programmed via a resistor divider to the VSENSE pin. Soft-start time is set by a capacitor on the SS pin. Switching frequency is configured through internal oscillator mode (resistor on RT pin), external synchronization mode (clock on SYNC pin, RT floating), or primary-secondary mode. Primary outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) vary by device. Dead times and leading edge blank time are programmable via resistors on PS, SP, and LEB pins. A pulse skipping mode prevents issues related to minimum on-time. Maximum duty cycle is configurable via the DCL pin. The CS_ILIM pin senses current for PWM generation and overcurrent protection, triggering hiccup mode when a threshold is exceeded. The FAULT pin allows for external fault protection. Slope compensation is set by a resistor on the RSC pin. Frequency compensation components are connected to the COMP pin. A thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C junction temperature.

Texas administrators, parents and experts worry a new law replacing STAAR could increase student stress and testing time. The law, passed in a second overtime session, replaces the single STAAR with three shorter tests at the beginning, middle and end of the year and bans practice tests. TEA will create the end-of-year test; schools may choose from TEA-approved nationally recognized assessments for the first two. Scores must be released within about two days. The law directs TEA to study reducing testing's weight on school accountability ratings and to factor the three tests into ratings, but the report is not due until 2029-30 and TEA need not implement findings. Critics fear ratings will still heavily depend on the end-of-year test, resulting in 'same pressure, more testing.' Experts say the new system will likely resemble the current one when it launches in 2027-28 and 'basically codifies what school districts are already doing' since many already conduct multiple exams. A progress metric from the three tests won't be ready at launch, so accountability weight will remain similar. Ratings are high-stakes, with sanctions for failing grades. Supporters call the system vital; critics say it ignores extracurriculars and other work. HB 8 instructs TEA to track pre-K, extracurriculars and workforce training participation, but these won't affect ratings. Some worry stress could increase if all three tests follow STAAR's lockdown protocols (three to four hours, seating charts, restricted breaks). Superintendent Holly Ferguson said the high-pressure environment makes some students ill. Florida's switch to three tests saw testing minutes almost double. Retired teacher Jim Ekrut worries banning practice tests removes anxiety-reducing preparation and wants educator input in test creation. HB 8 requires an educator committee to review the new test. Some districts hope the menu includes MAP exams, which they already use. MAP is a norm-based growth measure, a 'checkup' versus STAAR's 'autopsy.' Parent Rachel Spires said MAP tests cause less pressure, with no modified schedules or review packets. Ferguson said a relaxed environment is key and opposes a 'compliance-driven system' that harms students.

The 1956 Hungarian revolt was a nationwide event brutally repressed by the Soviet Union. After 1944 Soviet overrun, Communists won unopposed in 1949. Rákosi imposed collectivization and industrialization. After Stalin's death, Nagy briefly became PM but was replaced. Discontent grew from leadership uncertainty, economic failure, and events in Poland. A 22 October student rally issued a manifesto; the next day, a rally turned violent after Rákosi's speech, and the AVH fired on the crowd. Revolutionary councils demanded nationalism, neutrality, and Soviet withdrawal. The Politburo summoned Soviet troops and reappointed Nagy. Soviet tanks entered on 24 October, worsening matters. Soviet envoys replaced the old guard with Kádár and confirmed Nagy. Nagy formed a government on 27 October; tanks left on 29 October; sovereignty promised on 30 October was a ruse. The Suez Crisis diverted attention; on 1 November Soviet forces surrounded Budapest. After fake concessions, the USSR attacked on 3/4 November. Hungarian resistance was defeated. Fighting ended by 14 November, resistance by 30 November. About 25,000 Hungarians and 7,000 Soviet soldiers died.

The passage proposes a Language-Guided Change Detection model (LG-CD) for remote sensing change detection, integrating visual and textual information. It uses a pre-trained SAM2 encoder to extract multi-scale features from bi-temporal images, fine-tuned with lightweight adapter layers. Text prompts are encoded via CLIP to obtain word-level and global embeddings. A Text Fusion Attention Module aligns text and visual features through multi-head cross-attention, and a visual-semantic fusion decoder generates change masks. The introduction reviews traditional and deep learning methods, noting limitations like sensitivity to interference and inability to capture long-range context, and highlights that combining language and vision improves accuracy and robustness.

Coppin State University, a historically Black university in Maryland, launched the Expand Eagle Nation program, offering in-state tuition to students from 41 U.S. states and territories without an HBCU, plus D.C. In 2024, the first year, students from qualifying states more than doubled to 195 from 81. This fall, 416 of the 1,000 incoming students came from those states, and overall enrollment rose 26 percent, including in-state growth. The program also raised the university's profile among local students. Coppin's out-of-state push comes amid a national demographic cliff of declining high school graduates, though Maryland projects an 11 percent increase. Other institutions like UConn also seek out-of-state students. HBCUs have seen increased interest after the Supreme Court's 2023 affirmative action ban, with officials citing a sense of belonging. HBCUs are often cheaper; Coppin is the least expensive in Maryland, partly due to lower research costs and faculty salaries. To attract students, Coppin advertised on buses and billboards, visited high schools, formed transfer partnerships with community colleges, and reached out to college-search organizations. The university prepared for growth by ensuring sufficient courses and faculty, constructing a new dorm, and offering off-campus apartments with resident assistants and shuttles. A challenge was convincing prospective students that the in-state tuition offer was real.

The lecture focuses on post-flop poker strategy. It explains that players often check to the preflop aggressor because the aggressor's range is stronger, containing hands like pocket aces. When betting, a recommended sizing is half the pot on the flop, increasing to around 60% on the turn and 70% or more on the river; betting too small is discouraged because it gives opponents a free chance to check-raise. The "Fundamental Theorem of Poker" is introduced: a bet should be either a value bet with strong hands to get called by worse, or a bluff with the worst hands to fold out better hands; middle hands should check. This is illustrated with a 9-8-2 flop: with ace-queen, both betting and checking are reasonable; with king-queen, betting is better to fold hands like ace-jack; with pocket queens, betting for value is correct; with pocket sevens, checking is correct. Continuation betting advice includes not bluffing on highly coordinated, scary flops and not betting into many opponents with nothing.

Regarding calling bets, the general rule is to fold most hands to a half-pot bet unless the hand has sufficient equity or draw potential. Numerous examples are given of hands to fold, such as no pair/no draw, ace-high on scary boards, small pairs, and weak straight draws. Calling is reasonable with hands like ace-9 high on a paired board with backdoor draws, bottom pair on a safe flop, second pair with a good kicker, and top pair with a weak kicker in way-ahead/way-behind situations. With deep stacks (40 big blinds or more), a hand generally needs to be two-pair or better to raise; with shallower stacks, one-pair hands can be played more aggressively.

Leading into the preflop aggressor is presented as an advanced play, used when the flop hits the caller's range better than the raiser's, especially with shallow stacks. Examples include leading with a pair on a low flop or with a flush draw on a coordinated board. This strategy is tricky to balance because it weakens the checking range.

Implied odds and reverse implied odds are discussed. When short-stacked and all-in, calling with a weak hand like 7-2 offsuit can be mathematically correct based on pot odds. With deeper stacks, the same hand is folded due to reverse implied odds—the difficulty of playing it postflop. Hands like suited connectors have good implied odds because they can make strong hands and win large pots. Set mining (calling with small pocket pairs to hit a set) requires deep stacks to be profitable, as the set hits only about 1/8 of the time. An example with a flush draw shows calling a turn bet without direct odds because of the implied odds of getting paid on the river; a similar situation with a one-card flush draw on a paired board is a fold due to worse implied odds and the risk of drawing dead.

Bluffing strategy emphasizes using draws. Good draws (open-ended straight draws or flush draws) are ideal for bluffing because they have many outs against hands that call. An example shows check-raise all-in with 10-9 on a J-10-5 flop with 20 big blinds. Two bluffing epiphanies are given: first, when bluffing before the river, the number of outs matters more than current hand strength; second, it is important to consider what hand you are representing. If the board develops in a way that hurts your perceived range, you should give up the bluff. An example with jack-9 of hearts on a 10-7-2 flop illustrates check-raising with a draw, then giving up when the turn pairs the seven, because a seven is not in your check-raising range. The lecture concludes by summarizing the covered concepts: continuation betting, the Fundamental Theorem of Poker, analyzing flops, leading, implied and reverse implied odds, set mining, and bluffing with draws.

The lecture discusses discrete symmetries in quantum field theory. For a complex scalar theory, classical discrete symmetries include parity (P, flipping spatial directions), time reversal (T, flipping time), and charge conjugation (C, taking φ to φ*). At the quantum level, these are implemented by unitary operators, except time reversal, which requires an anti-unitary operator. The anti-unitary nature is derived by requiring that a time-reversed wavefunction satisfies the Schrödinger equation with t → −t, forcing the time reversal operator to be anti-linear (passing through i gives −i) and its adjoint defined with an extra complex conjugate.

For complex scalar fields, the transformations are φ'(x) = η_P φ(Px) for parity, similarly for time reversal, and φ'(x) = η_C φ*(x) for charge conjugation. The phases η are constrained (e.g., η_P² = 1, giving scalar or pseudoscalar). The unitary operators act on creation/annihilation operators, e.g., parity sends a_k to η_P a_{−k}, time reversal sends a_k to η_T a_{−k}, and charge conjugation exchanges particle and antiparticle operators.

For Dirac fields, parity transformation is ψ'(x') = D ψ(x) with x' = Px, where D is a matrix acting on spinor space. Requiring the transformed field to satisfy the Dirac equation in the reflected space forces D to commute with γ⁰ and anticommute with γⁱ, so D ∝ γ⁰. Charge conjugation is ψ' ∝ C ψ̄ᵀ, with matrix C satisfying γ^{μT} = −C γ^μ C^{−1}. Such C exists because −γ^{μT} also satisfies the Clifford algebra. Time reversal for Dirac fields involves a matrix D_T satisfying γ^{μT} = D_T γ^μ D_T^{−1}, related to C via D_T ∝ C^{−1} γ⁵.

The lecture then introduces path integrals for fermions. Because fermion fields satisfy anti-commutation relations, the path integral requires integration over anti-commuting classical analogues, i.e., Grassmann variables. Grassmann variables anti-commute (θ² = 0). Functions of Grassmann variables are at most linear: f(θ) = f₀ + f₁θ. Differentiation is defined, with left/right derivatives differing by a sign; the convention is left derivatives. Integration rules are defined by requiring linearity and that the integral of a total derivative vanishes. These imply ∫ dθ · 1 = 0 and ∫ dθ θ is fixed to 1, so ∫ dθ f(θ) = f₁, identical to differentiation. For multiple variables, integration respects anti-commutation. A change of variable θ' = aθ yields dθ' = (1/a) dθ, opposite to ordinary calculus.

A system includes a rotating LIDAR sensor and one or more cameras. The LIDAR sensor emits light pulses and detects reflections while rotating about an axis. The cameras detect external light and together provide rows of sensing elements aligned with the axis of rotation. A controller operates the cameras to obtain a sequence of image pixel rows, where each row corresponds to measurements by a row of sensing elements during a respective exposure time period. The order of obtaining the sequence can be based on the LIDAR's pointing direction, emission order of light beams, or rotation characteristics to improve temporal and spatial synchronization between LIDAR data and image pixels. The cameras may operate in a rolling shutter mode, with staggered exposure start times. The device may include a camera ring arranged around the axis. A method involves rotating the LIDAR sensor, obtaining the sequence of image pixel rows, and optionally associating LIDAR data with image pixels to generate a combined representation of the environment.

The passage examines the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education. It notes that AI's presence has increased, partly due to COVID-19, and that education is now inseparable from technology. The goal of AI in education is to develop human capital with 21st-century skills, guided by principles of learning, self-correction, and reasoning. Higher education institutions are influenced, with AI bringing both anxiety and innovation potential. AI offers personalized learning, intelligent tutoring, performance analysis, and personalized recommendations. It also aids research (literature review, data analysis) and administrative tasks (enrollment, timetabling). The paper proposes discussing AI's transformation of teaching-learning, research, management, and external relations. The methods involved document analysis from two databases and author self-reflexivity. Li and Yang (2023) highlight differences between traditional and AI-driven higher education: gaps in keeping pace with AI, governance (empirical vs. big data), training models (large-scale vs. personalized), and research modes. However, AI integration faces challenges: equity and inclusion, ethical and privacy issues, teacher training, student learning styles, financial costs, organizational conservatism, and AI's limitations (no out-of-the-box thinking, no regard for emotions). Advantages include high accuracy, speed, reliability, digital assistants, quick feedback, adaptive platforms, automated grading, plagiarism detection, predictive analytics, and virtual reality. Aldosari (2020) lists ten rules, such as automating basic activities and changing teachers' roles. Overcoming challenges requires developing AI literacy—critical evaluation, communication, and use of AI—for all stakeholders. Teachers need specific competencies: understanding AI's learning facilitation, data analysis, and critical perspective. Intentional use requires recognizing professors and students as actors. Action-research is proposed to improve teaching-learning. AI will shape soft skills, necessitating AI literacy and reshaping the teacher's role. The conclusion emphasizes that AI will affect all higher education dimensions; institutions must not remain static. They should balance technology adoption with academic freedom, encouraging stakeholder discussion and future research on AI competencies.

Prof. Cyril Dim, a lecturer at the University of Nigeria, discusses cervical cancer. Cervical cancer is a malignant condition of the cervix (the neck of the womb). It is caused by human papillomavirus (HPV), specifically oncogenic types, particularly HPV 16 and 18, which are sexually transmitted. There are over 100 HPV types, about 30 sexually transmitted. Apart from HPV, nothing else causes cervical cancer. The disease has a pre-cancer stage (precancerous lesions) with no symptoms, detectable by Pap smear. Pap smear is recommended every three years for women of reproductive age, later every five years. Precancerous lesions can be treated to prevent invasive cancer. Early-stage cervical cancer may be asymptomatic, then symptoms like post-coital bleeding, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and abnormal vaginal bleeding appear. Late-stage symptoms include weight loss, weakness, anaemia, pelvic pain, incontinence, and unconsciousness, ultimately death. Diagnosis of cancer requires tissue biopsy and histology after speculum examination; without it, cancer is only suspected. A man having sex with a woman with cervical cancer faces no harm, though he can acquire HPV; men are the reservoir and vaccination targets in developed countries. Survival: most women present late, mortality often within one to two years. Early-stage cancer is curable with radical surgery or radiotherapy; late-stage is managed with radiotherapy and chemotherapy to prolong life, survival may reach five years depending on stage, but terminal cases with organ spread last only months. Cervical cancer is a disease of developing countries due to lack of structured screening. Globally, about 500,000 new cases and 200,000 deaths occur annually, 80% in developing countries. In Nigeria, after breast cancer, cervical cancer is the second most common cancer in women, but may be the leading cause of cancer death. An estimated 15,000 new cases and 10,000 deaths occur yearly. In Enugu, 67% of female genital cancers are cervical. The pre-cancer stage develops slowly, but once cancer starts it can progress to late stage within months. Pregnancy is possible in early-stage disease. Treatment choice considers factors like age and sexual activity; radiotherapy may cause vaginal fibrosis. Myths sometimes attribute the disease to witchcraft. Health facts add that risk factors include multiple sexual partners, smoking, birth control pills, and early sexual contact. HPV infection may cause cervical dysplasia. Regular pelvic exams and Pap testing detect precancerous changes, which can be treated with cryosurgery, cauterization, or laser. Symptoms also include increased vaginal discharge, postmenopausal bleeding, pain during sex, and pelvic pain. Diagnosis can use Pap smear or other cervix tissue sampling; staging may involve chest X-ray, CT, MRI, PET scan. Treatment options include radiation therapy, surgery, and chemotherapy. A vaccine prevents HPV infection with common cancer-associated types. Prognosis depends on stage, type, and tumour size.

An electronic smoking device includes a housing, a liquid supply, and one or more woven fiber tubes. At least one woven fiber tube has an electrically conductive heating section and end sections, with a first side of the heating section connected to a first lead and a second side connected to a second lead, both leads connectable to an electrical power source. The end sections contact the liquid supply. The entire woven fiber tube may be electrically conductive and made of materials providing desired electrical conductivity, liquid conductivity, and strength. The tube has a hollow interior for liquid transport via capillary action, and liquid can also move through the porous fiber wall. The tube can be U-, C-, or L-shaped, with ends in the liquid. Multiple tubes may be used, positioned parallel and/or in direct contact, with same or different diameters; the heating section may have a different diameter from end sections. The liquid supply may contain free-flowing liquid or a porous medium storing liquid. The woven fiber tube can be made of carbon fibers, nickel-chromium, steel, titanium, silicon carbide, ceramic fibers, or composites thereof. A coil-less atomizer thus replaces separate heating wire and wick. The heating section may have higher electrical resistance than adjacent conductive sections. A manufacturing method includes installing woven fiber tubes on a board between leads, masking a portion, applying a modifying agent to unmasked portions to lower resistance, and removing the mask. The device may include a battery, control electronics, an airflow sensor, an LED, and a mouthpiece. Air flows through a central passage, and the heating element vaporizes liquid drawn from the supply.

The court denied Randall Fincke’s motion to reconsider its earlier finding that he violated Massachusetts General Laws ch. 110A, § 410(a)(2) by falsely stating in an October 2002 Business Plan that Access had been advised by patent counsel that its product did not infringe any known patents. The court reaffirmed that no such advice, formal or informal, was given.

On damages, the court determined which securities sales were made “by means of” that misstatement. It found the Investors’ testimony that they relied on the Business Plan for all subsequent investments not credible. Only Joseph Zimmel’s purchases of $1,000,000 in October 2002 and $500,000 in November 2002 were made “by means of” the Business Plan. Investments made in the April 2003 Transaction and later were not connected to that misstatement; they resulted from a new company document, extensive negotiations, and changed circumstances after the Investors assumed control.

The court will enter judgment against Fincke and in favor of Zimmel for $1,500,000 plus six percent annual interest from May 25, 2007, plus costs. It will also enter judgment against Fincke and in favor of Access for $281,534.62 plus twelve percent annual interest from July 6, 2004, plus costs, based on Fincke’s waiver of objections to the fiduciary duty breach judgment. Postjudgment interest at the federal rate will run on both awards.

The Ohio Supreme Court upheld the constitutionality of the one-year durational residency requirement for divorce in R.C. 3105.03. The court held that the requirement does not penalize the constitutional right to interstate travel, distinguishing divorce from welfare benefits and voting rights as not a basic need. The state has a compelling interest in regulating marriage and divorce, including ensuring its laws apply only to residents, encouraging marital stability, and verifying domiciliary intent. The one-year period was found to be the least restrictive means to prevent nonresidents from using Ohio courts. The judgment was affirmed. A concurring justice agreed based on the facts, noting the decision might be re-examined if grounds for divorce arise after establishing residence.

The DAWN-plasma trial was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 proof-of-concept multicenter study evaluating the addition of convalescent plasma to standard of care (SOC) versus SOC alone in hospitalized adult patients with COVID-19. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Between May 2, 2020 and January 26, 2021, 489 patients were randomized 2:1 to receive four units of convalescent plasma with high neutralizing antibody titers (n=326) or control (n=163). The primary endpoint did not differ significantly between groups (convalescent plasma: 83.7% vs control: 84.1%; odds ratio 0.99, p=0.976). No statistically significant differences were found for any secondary endpoints, including mortality, clinical status, time to sustained improvement, or incidence of venous thromboembolism. Adverse events, serious adverse events, and fatal adverse events occurred at similar rates in both arms. Transfusion-related side effects were reported in 6.0% of the plasma group, with no TRALI cases. Neutralizing antibody titers increased from baseline to Day 6 in both groups, with no influence from the intervention; higher titers at baseline and Day 6 correlated with better outcomes. The study concluded that early administration of high-titer convalescent plasma did not alter the disease course in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

Electron-photon interactions in an optical cavity are described by the Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian. Standard quantum chemistry methods are inapplicable due to the non-local, long-range coupling term. The sinc basis set is orthonormal, systematically improvable, and represents molecular orbitals on a uniform grid. Direct two-electron integral computation is O(N^4), but off-diagonal decay enables sparse/low-rank approximations. The sinc function is the Fourier transform of momentum-space eigenfunctions in a finite box, band-limited.

This study used NHANES data (2009-2020, n=32,498 adults >20 years) to identify empirical dietary patterns via principal components analysis and examine their associations with prevalent cardiovascular disease (CVD), social determinants of health (SDOH) score, and SNAP participation. Four patterns were identified: American (refined grains, meats, added sugars; 33.7% of adults), Prudent (vegetables, meat, poultry, seafood; 22.6%), Legume (vegetables, legumes; 15.8%), and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy (fruits, whole grains, dairy; 27.9%). The American pattern had the lowest HEI score (42.4), while Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy had the highest (62.0). Prevalent CVD (8.3%) was associated with a higher proportion consuming the American pattern (37.1% vs 33.3% without CVD), with no significant differences for other patterns. Higher SDOH score was associated with greater alignment with American and Legume patterns and lower alignment with Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns. SNAP participants had higher American pattern prevalence (40.2%) than income-eligible non-participants (35.1%) and non-eligible adults (31.9%), lower Prudent pattern prevalence, higher Legume pattern prevalence, and lower Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy pattern prevalence. Associations of SDOH score and SNAP status with dietary patterns varied significantly by race/ethnicity; for example, the SDOH-American pattern association was absent in Hispanic individuals, and SNAP status was not associated with Legume pattern in White individuals or American pattern in Hispanic and Asian individuals. Sensitivity analyses supported the findings. The study concludes that empirical dietary patterns vary by cardiovascular health and socioeconomic vulnerability, suggesting nutrition initiatives should consider these patterns.

The Wham play is a complementary run concept similar to Trap, but uses a Tight End or Fullback to pull and kick out a Defensive Lineman instead of a Guard. Its main strength is quickly creating favorable, unexpected angles, serving as an effective change-up since defenses may not practice against it often. Weaknesses include complex, time-consuming installation requiring the offensive line and Fullback to correctly identify the front and assignments; any mistake can free a defender. Teams often use specific formations to get predictable fronts, and the blocker must be a thicker, powerful player. Against a 3-4 Odd Front, the Fullback identifies the first Defensive Lineman outside the Center pre-snap, goes into short motion, and kicks him out; the Tailback aims for the inside hip of that block and runs behind the Right Tackle's second-level block. Against a 4-3 Even Front, assignments adjust, with the Tailback running behind the Right Guard's second-level block. Variations include Gun H-Back Wham RPO, where the Fullback kicks out the Nose Tackle while the Center releases to the second level and the Quarterback has a run-pass option, and Shotgun Influence Wham, where the Fullback traps a 3-tech defender who widens expecting a down block.

A cross-sectional study assessed horizontal HCV transmission among household members of HCV-positive patients attending CUSP in Huye district, Rwanda. The study aimed to evaluate whether household transmission contributes to increased HCV prevalence, compare risk factors, and assess awareness. Of 180 planned participants, 148 individuals from 30 families were tested using HCV Ab rapid tests with ELISA confirmation. The prevalence of HCV was 10.8% (16/148). Significant associations were found with HBV co-infection (p=0.001), HIV co-infection (p=0.001), and unprotected sex (p=0.016). Blood transfusion was not significant (p=0.058). Awareness of HCV transmission was low (93.9% provided wrong answers) but not significantly correlated with infection (p=0.079). The study concluded that household transmission contributes to elevated HCV prevalence, with unprotected sex as the primary risk factor. Recommendations include early screening of household members, education, and improved follow-up. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, preventing determination of infection origin.

This open-label randomised controlled trial in Cambodia compared the efficacy of low-dose (3·5 mg/kg total, 0·25 mg/kg/day for 14 days) and high-dose (7·0 mg/kg total, 0·5 mg/kg/day for 14 days) primaquine with a no-primaquine comparator in G6PD-normal patients with Plasmodium vivax malaria. Patients were relocated to a malaria-free area for 90 days to prevent reinfection. The primary outcome was the proportion with at least one P. vivax recurrence within 90 days. In the no-primaquine arm, 81·4% (95% CI 69·6–89·2) had recurrence. Recurrence was 24·4% (95% CI 14·2–38·7) in the low-dose arm and 4·7% (95% CI 0·8–15·5) in the high-dose arm, a statistically significant difference (p=0·0141). The hazard ratio for high-dose versus low-dose was 0·17 (95% CI 0·04–0·79, p=0·0229). Both primaquine regimens were well tolerated, with no serious adverse events. The findings indicate that 7·0 mg/kg primaquine over 14 days is more effective at preventing P. vivax recurrence than 3·5 mg/kg, supporting its recommendation for G6PD-normal patients in Cambodia and likely other Southeast Asian countries.

The passage introduces the Construction Defining Functionality (CDF) framework, a formal model for analyzing the layered structure of computational problems. It distinguishes between intensional (internal generative rules) and extensional (observable outcomes) perspectives. CDF defines three spaces for a function f: syntactic space Ssyn(f) (formal definition), semantic space Ssem(f) (configurations/models satisfying constraints), and logical space Slog(f) (inferential outcomes). These are connected by mappings: αf: Ssyn→Ssem, βf: Ssem→Slog, and γf: Ssyn→Slog. The coherence and stability of these mappings determine problem classification. Compositionally coherent CDF (ComCDF) requires γf = βf∘αf with stable αf, indicating polynomial semantic growth and tractability. Explosive CDF (ExpCDF) occurs when γf ≠ βf∘αf or αf is unstable, leading to exponential semantic explosion and intractability. A semi-explosive intermediate class also exists. The framework is applied to compare 2SAT and 3SAT. 2SAT clauses (l1∨l2) can be rewritten as binary implications, enabling local, compositional reasoning and stable γf, placing it in P. 3SAT clauses (l1∨l2∨l3) cannot be decomposed into binary implications, creating non-local dependencies. This syntactic non-locality causes the semantic space to grow exponentially (O(2^n)), making αf explosive and γf unstable, aligning 3SAT with NP-completeness. The semantic explosion is an intrinsic structural consequence of 3SAT's generative syntax, not an algorithmic artifact. Stabilizing 3SAT would require altering its fundamental structure, destroying its identity. Thus, CDF reveals structural reasons behind computational tractability and intractability, grounding complexity in the geometry and logic of problem construction rather than runtime bounds.

The passage states Bollinger Bands are somewhat profitable in the stock market, work as a breakout indicator in gold, but no useful strategies were found for stock indices. Limitations include delayed signals, false overbought/oversold indications, and the need for confirmation with other indicators. Traders manage risk with stop-loss orders and adjust settings such as lookback period and standard deviations. Shorter timeframes generate more signals but more false positives; longer timeframes reduce noise.

The Council of Regional Accrediting Commissions (CRAC), representing seven accrediting agencies that oversee 3,000 degree-granting institutions, released a statement backing the use of artificial intelligence to reduce credit loss during transfer. AI can analyze course descriptions, enrollment, and learning outcomes to streamline evaluation. He launched a pilot with 59 institutions using AI to analyze course equivalencies. CRAC’s statement urges institutions to default to applying credits unless learning outcomes are not met, and to use AI for evaluation, avoiding decisions based on anecdotes or assumptions. John Fink of the Community College Research Center said AI could flip the default to courses being transferable if they meet predictive algorithm criteria, though reliability at scale needs attention.

CRAC suggests AI can reduce credit loss, provide timely degree-applicable credit information, reduce administrative burden, and free faculty time. Heather Perfetti, CRAC chair, said the statement encourages examining current practices and that AI can address slow processing, inequity, and credit loss without good reason. Stephen Pruitt of the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools said the goal is to enhance human decision-making and provide uniformity. The statement signals accreditors’ encouragement to embrace AI for student success, amid slow institutional adoption of AI guidelines. George Railey Jr. said it puts the accrediting commission’s force behind efforts to move institutions forward with AI.

This document is a legal agreement between Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD) and the recipient for the attached AMD Specification concerning the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block. It permits review of the Specification solely to assist in designing products that interface with AMD products in compliance with the Specification and to provide feedback to AMD. All other rights are retained by AMD; duplication, removal of notices, or transfer of the Specification is prohibited. The Specification is provided “AS IS” with no warranties, and AMD disclaims all liability for damages. Feedback voluntarily provided may be used by AMD without restriction. The recipient must comply with applicable export laws, including U.S. EAR and E.U. regulations. The agreement is governed by California law, with disputes resolved in Santa Clara County.

The technical Specification standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for Secure Encrypted Virtualization-Encrypted State (SEV-ES) and SEV-SNP guests. The GHCB is a 4KB decrypted memory area enabling communication between the guest and hypervisor during Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs). It defines a GHCB MSR protocol using the lower 12 bits of MSR 0xc001_0130 to request actions such as GHCB address registration, SEV information, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, page state changes, and hypervisor feature support. Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement via a FEATURES bitmap and adds support for SEV-SNP, including SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, SNP AP Creation, Restricted Injection, and Secure AVIC.

The document lists supported NAE events with required guest state to expose in the GHCB, including IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, #NPF/MMIO access, page state change, and various SNP-specific exits. It details protocols for SMP booting under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, handling of non-maskable interrupts, debug register support, and the absence of SMM and nested virtualization support. The SNP Restricted Injection section defines a doorbell page format for #HV exception delivery, including pending event and EOI assist fields, and specifies host and guest behaviors for interrupt injection.
