MSPM0G MCUs provide five operating modes: RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN. The CPU is active in RUN mode. Peripheral interrupts can wake the device from SLEEP, STOP, or STANDBY to RUN mode. SHUTDOWN mode disables the internal core regulator, with wake-up only via NRST, SWD, or certain IOs. The devices implement two power domains: PD1 (CPU, memories, high-performance peripherals) and PD0 (low-speed, low-power peripherals). PD1 is powered in RUN and SLEEP modes; PD0 is powered in RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY modes. Both are disabled in SHUTDOWN mode. The power management unit (PMU) generates regulated core supplies, supervises the external supply, and includes a brown-out reset monitor and core regulator. The clock module provides oscillators including LFOSC, SYSOSC, and SYSPLL, and distributes clocks such as MCLK, CPUCLK, and ULPCLK. The DMA controller allows data movement without CPU intervention, supporting features like repeated transfer modes and configurable triggers. The event manager transfers digital events between entities, including peripheral-to-CPU interrupts, peripheral-to-DMA triggers, and peripheral-to-peripheral triggers.

Blackwell's clock gating for entire clock and memory trees, and a separate GPU/memory voltage rail, enable independent control and leakage reduction. Frame-granularity rail-gated states and turning off idle GPU cores lower power for battery gaming.

A Berliner Testament is a joint will where spouses appoint each other sole heirs and children final heirs. It secures the surviving spouse financially, as children inherit only after both parents die. Its strong binding effect prevents unilateral changes, even after divorce or new relationships. Clauses can ease this. Tax allowances may be exceeded if one spouse inherits alone. Legal advice is recommended.

Delta executives said premium cabin revenue could overtake main cabin sales for at least a quarter or two next year. Last quarter, premium revenue rose 9% to $5.8B, main cabin fell 4% to $6B. CEO sees no slowdown. Main cabin share fell to 43% of 2024 revenue from 60% in 2010, with premium and loyalty generating nearly 60%. Adding elaborate premium seats has delayed plane production.

The 3-4 defense consists of 3 down linemen, 4 linebackers, and 4 defensive backs, with a mirrored base alignment. It requires bigger defensive linemen using a two-gap approach and hybrid outside linebackers who can rush or drop into coverage. The secondary uses two corners and two safeties.

Its main strength is the ability to pressure from many places due to the extra linebacker. Blitzing both outside linebackers creates a 5-man rush. The two-safety set allows multiple coverages and can disguise blitzes by rotating a safety down, changing the picture for quarterbacks.

Weaknesses emerge against modern spread offenses. When outside linebackers must cover receivers, the defense is left with a 5-man box, vulnerable to the run. Spreading the defense out and using trips formations can cause confusion against speedy slot receivers, leading to the rise of the 3-3 stack defense.

Common blitzes include the Weakside Edge Blitz, where an outside linebacker rushes off the edge with the defensive line slanting away, creating a 4-man rush, shifting from 2-high pre-snap to cover 3 post-snap. The Crossfire Blitz sends both inside linebackers on a crossing blitz while an outside linebacker drops, showing a 4-rusher pre-snap look that becomes cover 3.

Common coverages are Cover 4 (four deep, four underneath, vulnerable flat) and Cover 2 Man (man coverage with two deep safeties, similar pre-snap).

The defense is associated with Bill Parcells and Bill Belichick (two Super Bowls with the Giants). The coaching tree includes Nick Saban (7 national championships) and Kirby Smart (back-to-back national championships at Georgia). Since 2005, this tree has won 9 college national championships and 7 Super Bowls, totaling 16 major championships from Belichick, Saban, and Smart.

The opioid overdose epidemic in the U.S. has caused over 450,000 deaths in eight years. This study aims to help public health departments make short-term forecasts of future overdose events at the census tract level to enable targeted interventions. The study forecasts fatal opioid-related overdoses in Cook County, Illinois (2015-2022) and Massachusetts (2001-2021). It compares various forecasting models, including simple baselines, statistical models, and neural networks, using error-based metrics (RMSE, MAE) and a new intervention-focused metric called "best possible reach" (BPR). BPR assesses a model's ability to recommend a limited set of regions for intervention by measuring the proportion of actual fatalities in the recommended regions compared to a perfect hindsight selection. Results show that simple historical average baselines performed competitively with more complex models in both locations. The study also found that using the BPR metric can lead to different model rankings than error-based metrics, potentially identifying more overdose events for preemptive intervention. Limitations include the study's generalizability from only two locations and the specific intervention budget used for the BPR metric.

The passage describes host environment requirements for implementing BIOS interfaces to access the AGESA software. The host must establish a valid stack before any call, use module dispatchers, and create standard header data. Calls to AGESA are made via bridge procedures that locate the binary image entry point and call the AMD dispatcher. A call-out router function must be implemented to translate function numbers into execution addresses for call-out procedures. The UEFI BIOS environment includes SEC, PEI, DXE, and RTP stages, with AGESA core files arranged into libraries and build targets using specific Microsoft tools. Configuration options are set via platform-specific files. The SEC phase uses AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK to set up a C environment. PEI phase includes two PEIMs: one for processor initialization (AmdCpuEarlyInit) publishing PPIs, and another for memory initialization (AmdInitPost) publishing PPIs and HOBs. A reset PEIM coordinates warm resets. The DXE driver performs late initialization, calls AmdInitLate, and publishes a protocol for table access. A GPU VGA control driver monitors VGA decoding. Reference files and build control files are provided. Environment variables AGESA_ROOT and AGESA_OptsDir must be set. Stack procedures (AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK, AMD_DISABLE_UEFI_STACK) are provided as macros for pre-memory stack management. Service procedures include AmdCreateStruct (allocates and initializes parameter blocks), AmdReleaseStruct, and various query functions (AmdGetDataEye, AmdGetApicAddress, AmdGetExeCacheSize, AmdGetPciAddress, AmdIdentifyCore, AmdIdentifyDimm, AmdMergeMmioRange, AmdReadEventLog). Entry procedures are listed in time-point order: AmdInitReset (minimal processor init), AmdInitEarly (full processor init, HyperTransport, power management), AmdInitPost (memory initialization, transition to post-memory), AmdInitEnv (artifact data transfer, HOBs), AmdInitMid (graphics display config), AmdInitLate (late init, generate ACPI/DMI tables), AmdInitRtb (ready-to-boot, save state for S3), AmdInitResume (resume path memory re-init), AmdS3LateRestore (restore registers after PCI), AmdS3FinalRestore (final restore before OS). Required call-out functions are AgesaAllocateBuffer (allocate memory buffer) and AgesaDeallocateBuffer (de-allocate buffer).

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a momentum indicator on a 0–100 scale used to assess whether a security is overvalued or undervalued and to signal trend reversals or pullbacks. A Contract for Difference (CFD) is a financial contract based on the price difference of an underlying asset, enabling speculation without ownership; CFD trading is a zero-sum game. In CFD trading, RSI helps identify overbought (typically above 70) and oversold (below 30) conditions and supports mean-reversion strategies. For day trading, shorter time frames and more extreme thresholds (e.g., 15 for oversold, 85 for overbought) are often used for higher sensitivity, though readings may become more erratic. Backtesting is essential to validate strategies. Three strategies backtested on SPY: a basic strategy produced 313 trades averaging 0.86% per trade with hard drawdowns; an enhanced two-day RSI strategy with a QS exit (buy when two-day RSI <10, sell when close > yesterday’s high) yielded 355 trades averaging 0.67% per trade and smoother drawdowns; an RSI Momentum strategy uses a 100-day look-back and 14-day RSI for trend-following, generating fewer signals for longer-term trends. Tips include combining RSI with other indicators, backtesting on specific assets, favoring shorter time frames (e.g., 2–3 days) for stocks, adjusting thresholds per asset and time frame, cautiously combining time frames, monitoring RSI divergences (bullish: price makes a new low while RSI does not; bearish: price makes a new high while RSI does not), and prioritizing risk management (commissions, slippage, stop-losses, though stop-losses may worsen performance).

Cam Schlittler shut out Boston for eight innings in Game 3 of the AL Wild Card series. Scout Matt Hyde, who discovered him at Northeastern, called the performance 'unbelievable.' Schlittler, a 2022 seventh-round pick, made history with eight scoreless innings, no walks, and 12 strikeouts.

This study compared Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) and a machine learning (ML) approach using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with SHAP explanations for detecting outliers in plantar pressure data. The ML approach outperformed the SPM approach, achieving a higher F1-score and Matthews Correlation Coefficient. For the SPM approach, pathological but valid samples were often misclassified as outliers, and false negatives largely arose from the Incorrect Side Annotation class. For the ML approach, the lowest label accuracy was for the General Acquisition Error class, which was most frequently misclassified as valid.

In a human-centered evaluation using a semantic differential survey, both approaches were rated positively on attributes like clarity, correctness, and usefulness, with no statistically significant differences observed. SPM explanations were descriptively rated as simpler, while ML explanations were considered more complex. Experts perceived a relatively high level of agreement between the two approaches. The ML approach with SHAP explanations received the highest subjective preference from experts. The study concludes that both approaches are promising for detecting technical errors, and it provides a first step toward human-centered evaluation of interpretability in this domain.

The author criticizes the common percentage-based definitions of bull and bear markets (e.g., 20% drop) as arbitrary and unhelpful for risk management or capital deployment. He proposes alternative definitions: a secular bull market is a 10-20 year period driven by economic shifts, rising earnings, and increasing investor willingness to pay more for earnings (multiple expansion); a secular bear market is the opposite, with increased volatility and decreasing willingness to pay for earnings. He argues that multiple expansion, not earnings growth, drives most market gains, citing the 1982-2000 bull market where three-quarters of the rise came from P/E ratio expansion. He advises focusing on the psychology of earnings multiples rather than pundits.

Pharma tariffs that President Trump said would take effect Wednesday did not go into effect. A White House official said the administration will now begin preparing tariffs on companies that don't build in the U.S. or make a drug pricing agreement, with no new timeline given. In Thuro v. Meredith, real estate brokers sued for a commission. The trial court directed a verdict for the plaintiffs, and the reviewing court affirmed. The defendants employed the plaintiffs to find a purchaser. Della B. Thuro signed a sale contract with Mrs. Charles Tallman, also signing for her absent husband George without written authority. The Tallmans took possession, made payments, later abandoned the contract, and the defendants repossessed the property. On appeal, the defendants argued that George Thuro could not ratify without a writing, that Charles Tallman was not bound, and that a variance existed between pleading and proof. The court held these issues immaterial. A principal cannot defeat a broker’s right to a commission by refusing to be bound by a contract with the purchaser the broker produced. The plaintiffs fulfilled their duty by procuring Mrs. Tallman as a purchaser. Any variance was harmless and did not affect substantial rights. The trial court properly refused requested instructions on immaterial issues, and overruling motions to strike was harmless error. The judgment was affirmed.

The Montecito Union School District, a single-school district in Santa Barbara County serving about 350 students, settled a sexual abuse lawsuit for $7.5 million with two brothers, now 65 and 68. The brothers alleged that former superintendent and principal Stanford Kerr molested them in the 1970s, including rape. Kerr died in 2013 without facing criminal charges. The brothers had sought $35 million in damages. The settlement equals about 40% of the district’s 2025-26 budget, and the superintendent acknowledged a budget impact. The trial was set to start Monday. The settlement came after a 2019 state law, AB 218, removed the statute of limitations for childhood sexual abuse claims against public agencies. A bill to restore a statute of limitations, SB 577, died in the legislature weeks earlier. The California School Boards Association gave the district a $50,000 grant for legal costs. The district admitted no liability and said it had no insurance coverage for the period. It will manage costs through a hiring freeze, staff reductions via attrition, and redirecting capital repair funds, avoiding layoffs. A third plaintiff settled earlier for $1 million. The brothers’ case relied on their testimony; there was no physical evidence. The district had no records of the boys’ attendance or accusations against Kerr. A final hearing is scheduled for Nov. 19 to confirm payment.

Deutsche Bank is seeking to sell its 8.8 percent stake in Dubai-based Abraaj Holdings, a private equity firm embroiled in an investor dispute over alleged misuse of funds. The potential sale, long considered, has gained urgency amid Deutsche's restructuring and Abraaj's troubles. Deutsche views the stake as non-core; a past valuation disappointed. Sources say any sale now would be at a steep discount. Abraaj faces an investigation by four investors, including the Gates Foundation and IFC, over a $1 billion healthcare fund. The firm denies wrongdoing and is considering selling its investment business unit. It has cut jobs, suspended new investments, and seen executive resignations. A survey study investigated 333 Turkish teachers’ knowledge, perceptions, and readiness regarding metaverse integration in education. Teachers’ average knowledge of the metaverse concept was 5.25 out of 9, and 78.1% reported prior experience, mostly with virtual reality or three-dimensional virtual worlds rather than current metaverse applications. Attitudes toward educational use were positive (6.23/9), and perceived advantages included creating engaging materials (76.3%), enabling practice in realistic environments (74%), and supporting learning by doing (67.8%). Concerns centered on technical problems (76.9%), psychological issues like addiction (69.5%), inequality of opportunity (67.8%), and data security (57.1%). Willingness to use the metaverse in lessons scored 6.37/9, and interest in training scored 8.08/9. Teachers considered information technology, physics, biology, chemistry, and mathematics most suitable for metaverse application. Most predicted widespread educational implementation within 3–5 years (37.2%). The study concludes that while the metaverse holds transformative potential for immersive and safe learning, successful integration requires robust infrastructure, teacher training, and attention to health and equity challenges.

The High Post Split Offense consists of a high post split followed by down screens. Defenders must be skilled in guarding the high post and countering down screens. Two defensive strategies are outlined: Basic NBA Show & Recover and All Out SOS Disruption. In Show & Recover, when the ball is passed to the high post, defenders sag off in front, forcing cutters wide; the post defender (X5) drops to protect against splits. When the high post faces, X5 jams and forces toward the weakhand corner. On down screens, defenders show to force shooters wide, then recover to three-quarter pass denial positions, avoiding switches to prevent mismatches. In SOS Disruption, the defense first pushes the ballhandler to the sideline and denies the high post feed. On the high post split, defenders sag off but switch on guard splits, forcing cutters wide, and X5 smothers the high post. On down screens, contact switches and strong pass denial are used. SOS also employs traps: on a wing pass, the wing defender and post defender double team, while others rotate to front the post and assume triangle "I" positions. The "Flash/Back Door" offense attacks a Box & One defense by flashing a baseline post player into the middle to exploit vulnerability. The passage presents LUKB Disease Trajectory (LUKB DT), a web tool built on R Shiny and integrated into the LUKB platform for identifying disease trajectories from electronic medical records. The tool implements a four-step workflow: disease filtering using Cox regression with time-varying exposure, disease pair detection via binomial tests, validation with conditional logistic regression, and concatenation of confirmed pairs into trajectories. It requires input data with participant IDs, diagnoses, and dates, and can be deployed locally without extensive programming. A case study using UK Biobank ICD-10 data for COVID-19 identified trajectories primarily involving SARS-CoV-2-related conditions and other medical care, but did not capture immune-related diseases, possibly due to data limitations. The tool is recommended for investigating risk factors and disease mechanisms rather than patient clustering.

Children with language vulnerabilities, such as developmental language disorder, neuropsychiatric conditions, or migrant backgrounds, require tailored language support. Speech-language therapists (SLTs) often use game-based interventions like the Alias word retrieval game to target morphological structures, but providing consistent, diverse examples in real time is demanding for both SLTs and educators. Robot-Assisted Language Learning (RALL) has emerged as a potential alternative, but traditional systems are rigid, struggle with speech recognition and turn-taking, and lack adaptability for children with unclear speech. The authors developed TalBot, a robot application integrating a large language model (LLM, ChatGPT) with the Furhat conversational robot, and tested it with preschool children with language vulnerabilities and educators. TalBot leads the Alias game, manages turn-taking via LLM-generated labels, provides feedback, handles mispronunciations, and uses Furhat for non-verbal cues like gaze and facial expressions. This approach addresses prior RALL limitations by enabling adaptability, interpreting faulty speech recognition, and dynamically managing the game through prompts. The next phase expands TalBot to morphological learning, leveraging the LLM to generate unlimited linguistic material, provide a consistent and tireless linguistic model, and act as a role model for educators. Planned studies include lab and field comparisons of robot versus educator production of morphological structures during gameplay, and a feasibility study assessing pre- and post-intervention morphological skills in children with clinically significant language vulnerabilities. Considerations include data protection, the EU AI Act, ethical frameworks, and practical challenges such as cost and potential resistance. The long-term goal is a robust LLM-based RALL intervention for teaching morphological structures across languages.

An image processing method obtains a to-be-processed video with m frames. A target three-dimensional model is placed on a target plane of the first frame, with multiple feature points of a model surface falling on that plane. Three-dimensional coordinates of the feature points in a world coordinate system and their pixel coordinates on the first frame are determined. A pose of the camera coordinate system of the first frame relative to the world coordinate system is determined from these coordinates. For subsequent frames, poses of camera coordinate systems relative to the world coordinate system are determined by tracking the target plane using homography matrices and the known coordinates. The target three-dimensional model is then replaced with a target model placed in the world coordinate system, and a target video including the target model is generated according to the poses of each frame's camera coordinate system.

Gary Gensler's lecture introduces the technical foundations of blockchain technology through Bitcoin. He focuses on cryptography, covering two main primitives: hash functions and digital signatures. Hash functions map input of any size to a fixed-size output, are deterministic, efficient, and have cryptographic properties like preimage resistance (one-way), collision resistance, and an avalanche effect. They secure data and link blocks together. Timestamped append-only logs form a chain of blocks, with block headers containing a previous block hash, Merkle root, timestamp, difficulty target, and nonce. Merkle trees efficiently compress many transactions into a single root hash. Asymmetric cryptography involves generating a key pair (public and private keys), creating digital signatures with a private key, and verifying them with the corresponding public key; it is infeasible to derive a private key from a public key. Bitcoin addresses are derived from public keys by double hashing and encoding for added security and shorter length. Transactions consist of inputs and outputs, with value measured in Satoshis. The lecture frames blockchain technology as combining cryptography, a consensus mechanism, and a transaction ledger.

The lecture provides an overview of equity, defined as ownership in a corporation with cash flows from dividends and capital gains. Key characteristics include residual claim (unlimited upside after bondholders are paid), limited liability (loss limited to investment), voting rights, access to public markets, and the role of short sales in market efficiency. It distinguishes primary markets (new issues) from secondary markets (trading existing securities) and focuses on secondary market price formation. The Dividend Discount Model values a stock as the present value of expected future dividends discounted at risk-adjusted rates that can vary over time and by cash-flow risk. Simplifications yield a perpetuity formula for constant dividends and the Gordon growth model for dividends growing at a constant rate, showing price sensitivity to growth expectations and requiring the discount rate to exceed the growth rate. Rearranging gives the required return as dividend yield plus growth rate, highlighting that value derives from both current dividends and growth opportunities. The lecture notes the difficulty of forecasting future dividends and discount rates, and that companies tend to maintain stable dividend policies because cuts are viewed as bad news.

The device features analog inputs with resistive impedance ≥1MΩ, independent of sampling or signal frequency, simplifying driving without low-output-impedance amplifiers or high-voltage supplies. For DC accuracy, match external source impedance on AIN_P and AIN_M. Each input has internal overvoltage protection using input resistors and antiparallel diodes, withstanding up to ±20V when powered (AVDD=5V) and low source impedance; higher source impedance increases protection range but adds gain error. Protection limits also apply when AVDD is floating.

A programmable gain amplifier converts single-ended or differential inputs, adjusts common-mode, and is configured via RANGE_SEL[3:0] bits (default ±3V×VREF). A second-order antialiasing low-pass filter with 500kHz cutoff follows the PGA. An integrated high-bandwidth, low-noise ADC driver ensures proper charging of sample-and-hold capacitors.

The device uses an internal or external 4.096V reference, selected by the INTREF_DIS bit. Internal reference requires a ≥4.7µF decoupling capacitor on REFIO, is factory-trimmed, temperature-compensated, and may shift from solder reflow. External reference mode applies 4.096V to REFIO; the internal buffer drives REFCAP, requiring 10µF and 1µF capacitors. Buffer drift is typically 0.5ppm/°C, maximum 2ppm/°C.

The ADC outputs straight-binary conversion data. LSB size equals full-scale range divided by 2^16. Alarm features include an active-high output on the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin when configured. Input alarms have user-programmable high/low thresholds and hysteresis; AVDD alarms have fixed thresholds (4.7V low, 5.3V high). Both alarms are enabled by default and can be disabled. The multiSPI digital interface supports various data transfer protocols. Device states are RESET (application or power-on reset via RST pin), ACQ (acquisition, with optional NAP low-power mode), and CONV (conversion initiated by CONVST/CS rising edge, returns to ACQ after conversion). A data transfer frame begins at CONVST/CS falling edge, uses SCLK for shifting, and ends at rising edge. Optimal frame length is 32 SCLKs; shorter frames invalid for writes, longer frames use the last 32 bits as command. Input commands are 32-bit words for register writes, reads, and bit set/clear operations. Output data can include conversion results, fixed patterns, register data, and appended flags (device address, input range, alarm, parity) based on configuration.

Data write protocols are four SPI-compatible modes selected via SDI_MODE bits. Data read protocols include legacy SPI with single or dual SDO-x, and source-synchronous (SRC) modes where RVS provides the output clock, selectable as external or internal, with single or dual SDO-x. Dual SDO mode uses SDO-1 pin.

Nine configuration registers control device ID, reset/power (NAP, power-down), SPI modes, SDO configuration, data output formatting, input range and reference selection, and alarm thresholds/hysteresis. Power-down mode deeply reduces power while retaining register contents; exit requires clearing the PWRDN bit and waiting tPWRUP.

An application example shows an 8-channel analog input module for PLCs using the ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 differential multiplexer, leveraging fast settling, integrated AFE, and alarm features. The offside trap is a defensive maneuver where all defensive backs move upfield in unison just before an opponent passes to a leading striker, placing the striker in an offside position. If the striker receives the ball and gains an advantage, an offside violation is called, awarding an indirect free kick. Introduced in the 1900s, its effectiveness has been reduced by recent offside law changes and the prevalence of short-passing attacks. The trap is a calculated risk: success wins the ball without a tackle, but failure leaves the goalkeeper exposed. Common failures include a defender not moving simultaneously or an attacker standing still to avoid involvement. Coaches must consider player maturity, understanding of the offside law, and whether benefits outweigh risks. The trap is more effective against teams that use through balls and long balls, and can demoralize them; teams using short, quick passes with fast, skilled strikers are less vulnerable. A flat-back-four formation aids execution, while a stopper-sweeper system often keeps attackers onside. The trap can be used in normal play or free kicks. A single designated defender (upfield defensive coordinator, usually a center-back) calls the trap with a unique verbal or non-verbal signal (e.g., raised arm). All back defenders must be in a straight line, know each other's and strikers' positions, and move as one unit. At least one attacker must be in the defensive half and ahead of the ball, with sufficient space. Execution involves a quick, unified 3-5 yard sprint forward to create clear space. Clues include attackers starting forward runs and the passer looking down. Practice is essential; the trap may only work once per game against well-coached opponents, as overuse increases risk. Only the designated coordinator or possibly the goalkeeper may call it. Signals may need changing if scouted. Midfielders may cover space behind the trap. Defenders must avoid ball watching. Teaching the trap is hard because defenders must learn to let opponents go past.

This protocol describes a systematic review of observational cohort studies on the implementation or redesign of Rapid Response Team (RRT) services. The review will include studies where the intervention is a novel RRT service or service redesign in healthcare systems, with no restrictions on comparator or outcome measures. Data will be extracted on study characteristics, team characteristics, implementation methods (novel vs. redesign, reason for change, time frame, simulation/technology use, dissemination), and system outcome assessments (measures of success, ascertainment method, follow-up timing/duration, quantitative/qualitative measures). The primary objective is to describe methods of implementation; secondary objectives are to report reasons for change, implementation time frames, and key outcome measures. Risk of bias will be assessed using the JBI checklist. Synthesis will be primarily narrative, with simple statistics on the range and frequency of implementation methods. The review does not require ethical approval. Results will be disseminated via scientific meetings and a peer-reviewed journal. Limitations include expected heterogeneity in team nomenclature, composition, resources, and outcome reporting, as well as a potential lack of studies on service implementation/change management. The protocol is registered on medRxiv.

A geoarchaeological study analyzed 61 sediment cores and tens of thousands of ceramic fragments from Egypt's Karnak Temple complex. It found the site originated as an island formed by ancient Nile channels, with the eastern channel more defined and possibly larger than previously supposed. Prior to about 2520 BCE, regular flooding made the area unsuitable for permanent occupation; earliest occupation likely occurred during the Old Kingdom. Over time, diverging and silting channels allowed the temple to expand, and ancient Egyptians dumped desert sands into channels to create building land. The island setting resembles the creation myth of high ground emerging from primeval waters, suggesting the location may have been chosen for its religious significance. Researchers plan further work across the Luxor floodplain.

Air containerization, an intermodal process where goods stay in containers, is used by civil airlines and military forces. Custom containers are carried on lower decks of passenger aircraft and both decks of cargo aircraft. The air cargo container market grows due to demand for rapid global transport and lightweight containers meeting IATA standards. It is hindered by the global economic slowdown (GDP declines in Asia Pacific, Latin America, Middle East) and rising aviation fuel restricting flight hours. Future opportunities include increasing commercial airlines and defense demand for quick military equipment transport. The market is segmented by container type, aircraft type, end user, and geography. Major vendors include companies from Norway, France, Netherlands, U.S., and Germany.

The passage advocates letting children pursue their own interests. It also stresses learning to give with love, as actions return to oneself. Manual labor and sports are deemed necessary for health, with a Laozi quote. Family atmosphere and joint activities like outings, travel, and entertainment help bridge generation gaps. Religious education, particularly Buddhism, provides faith, values, and standards for right and wrong, fostering positive thinking. Women's status is addressed: working parents have less time for children, but mothers' behavior influences children. The conclusion calls for emphasis on morality, humanity education, parental guidance, and inheriting traditional moral education.

The TPS7H500x-SP series are radiation-hardened PWM controllers. Output voltage is set by a resistor divider from VOUT to the VSENSE pin, dividing down to a 0.613 V reference. Soft-start time is controlled by a capacitor between the SS pin and AVSS. Switching frequency is configured in three modes: internal oscillator mode using a resistor from RT to AVSS (100 kHz to 2 MHz), external synchronization mode by leaving RT floating and applying a clock (200 kHz to 4 MHz, 40–60% duty cycle) to SYNC, and primary-secondary mode where one controller’s SYNC output clocks a second controller with RT floating. Primary outputs (OUTA/OUTB) and synchronous rectifier outputs (SRA/SRB) are device-dependent. Dead times between primary turn-off and SR turn-on (TDPS) and SR turn-off to primary turn-on (TDSP) are programmable via resistors on PS and SP pins; leading edge blank time is set by a resistor on LEB. Maximum duty cycle is configurable via the DCL pin (50%, 75%, or 100% depending on device). Peak current mode control uses the CS_ILIM pin; overcurrent triggers hiccup mode with timing set by a capacitor on HICC. Fault protection is provided via the FAULT pin. Slope compensation is set by a resistor on RSC. Frequency compensation uses Type 2A or 2B networks on the COMP pin. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C. An application example details a synchronous push-pull converter design with GaN FETs, including component selection. Layout guidelines recommend separating analog and power grounds, minimizing noise coupling, and proper bypassing.

The article presents backtests of trend following and momentum strategies on Bitcoin (BTC-USD) from 2015 to April 2021, using free Yahoo Finance data without commissions, slippage, or taxes. It finds that simple moving average strategies beat buy-and-hold. A short exponential average (optimized to 5 days) yielded a 145% CAGR. A 100/250-day simple moving average crossover produced a 115% CAGR with a 65% max drawdown, outperforming buy-and-hold's 94% CAGR. A momentum strategy (close vs. 25 days ago) also beat buy-and-hold while reducing drawdown. Bitcoin's max drawdown matched Nasdaq's 82% post-dot-com, but Bitcoin recovered faster. The strategies rely on Bitcoin's volatility. Code for these strategies is available for purchase.

Engineers at UC San Diego developed ultrasound-powered nanorobots that swim through blood to remove bacteria and toxins. The nanorobots consist of gold nanowires coated with a hybrid membrane of platelet and red blood cell membranes. Platelet membranes bind pathogens like MRSA, while red blood cell membranes absorb and neutralize toxins. Ultrasound propels the nanorobots without chemical fuel, enhancing mixing and detoxification. The hybrid coating also prevents biofouling. In tests, treated blood samples contaminated with MRSA had three times less bacteria and toxins after five minutes. The work, published in Science Robotics, is a proof-of-concept for detoxifying biological fluids. Future steps include live animal tests and using biodegradable materials.

The passage describes patent application technology for classifying splice sites and detecting aberrant splicing using deep learning. It claims priority to multiple earlier applications and incorporates various documents by reference. The technology employs atrous convolutional neural networks (ACNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on large sets of donor splice sites, acceptor splice sites, and non-splicing sites. Input sequences consist of a target nucleotide sequence flanked by upstream and downstream context nucleotides. The ACNN architecture includes groups of residual blocks with batch normalization, ReLU layers, atrous convolutions, and skip connections; atrous convolution rates progress non-exponentially and convolution window sizes vary between groups. The network outputs triplet scores for each target nucleotide indicating likelihood of being a donor, acceptor, or non-splicing site. For aberrant splicing detection, a classifier processes a reference sequence and a variant sequence through the trained ACNN, then compares the resulting splice site scores position-wise. A difference exceeding a predetermined threshold classifies the variant as causing aberrant splicing and pathogenic. The document also details training procedures, specific ACNN configurations (SpliceNet80, SpliceNet400, SpliceNet2000, SpliceNet10000), and the use of one-hot encoding.

The Nobel Prize, created by Alfred Nobel and first awarded in 1901, recognizes discoveries in physics, chemistry, and physiology or medicine, but excludes fields like ecology, oceanography, and geology. Only three people can share a prize, leaving many contributors unrecognized. The selection process involves a 50-member committee and global nominations to reduce bias, yet winners are mostly white men from wealthy regions. By 2023, only 13 women had won the medicine prize, and one Black person (W. Arthur Lewis, 1979, economics) had won a science prize. Underrepresented groups face barriers accessing large labs at major universities. Victor Ambros, 2024 medicine laureate for microRNA, said his wife Rosalind Lee, who manages his lab and contributed equally, did not share the prize because she lacks her own lab. The Nobel Foundation is bound by Nobel’s will, so categories likely won't change. Despite limitations, the prize is seen as important for celebrating science and sparking public curiosity.

Kickers are often undrafted and minimally paid, assisting the offense with extra points and field goals. Their job is pressure-packed, demanding elite mentality and skill. Primary duties: extra points (1 point after touchdowns), field goals (3 points, 25-60 yards), kickoffs (touchbacks, directional kicks to aid coverage), and onside kicks (recovery chance). NFL kickers are expected to make about 80% of field goals and 90% of extra points (now a 33-yard kick). They usually differ from punters but sub in if the punter is injured. The position is called kicker or placekicker because kicks are set by a holder or tee. Required skills: accuracy, lower body power/strength, consistent technique, flexibility. Typical body type: height 5'10-6'2, weight 180-210 lbs, slim build. Notable kickers: Justin Tucker (most accurate, 91%, record 66-yard field goal), Morten Andersen (2nd all-time field goals, 565, 80%, Hall of Fame 2017, former leading scorer), Adam Vinatieri (most "clutch," game-winning Super Bowl kicks, all-time leading scorer 2,673 points, record 44 consecutive field goals). Kickers influence coach's 4th-down decisions, provide peace of mind, and are crucial in tight games. Missed kicks waste offensive opportunities and give opponents good field position. Kickoffs and onside kicks are important for special teams success and can be game-changing.

A machine learning approach was developed to accurately predict the ionic dielectric constant (εion) of oxides, crucial for high-κ materials in electronics. High-κ materials require both high dielectric constant and wide band gap, but these properties often trade off. The static dielectric tensor includes electronic (εele) and ionic (εion) contributions; εion, determined by Born effective charges (BECs) and phonon properties, can be large and is pivotal for screening. Previous ML models struggled with εion accuracy.

The proposed "joint model" factorizes εion into BECs and phonon properties. An equivariant graph neural network (EGNN) predicts BEC tensors, and a pretrained machine learning potential (MLP) provides the force constant matrix; these are combined analytically via εαβion = (4π/V₀) Σ Z* (Φ⁻¹) Z*. The EGNN was trained on 928 oxides containing 45 elements, achieving high accuracy for BEC eigenvalues (R²=0.982, RMSE=0.369). Among four evaluated MLPs, SevenNet-MF-ompa gave the best εion prediction (R²=0.906) and was selected. The joint model significantly outperformed a direct prediction model (R²=0.843 vs. 0.418).

Virtual screening started with 8,717 non-magnetic, non-metallic oxides from the Materials Project database, after excluding dynamically unstable ones. Using ML-predicted dielectric constants and r2SCAN band gaps, a figure of merit FoM = εave·Eg was applied with threshold FoM ≥ 200, yielding 240 candidates. After DFPT validation and DDH band gap calculations, 38 oxides met FoM ≥ 350, a fourfold increase over the 9 such oxides in the training set. Twelve have higher FoM than the best training oxide KTaO3. Most identified oxides contain d⁰ transition metals and oxygen octahedral networks (perovskite, pyrochlore, etc.). Ten have been experimentally synthesized; five of those have reported high experimental dielectric constants. LiBi4Nb3O14 and LaYO3 are experimentally accessible but unexplored high-κ oxides. The approach demonstrates the effectiveness of physics-based factorization for predicting material properties.

The higher highs and higher lows pattern signals an uptrend. Backtesting on SPY, GLD, and TLT using a strategy of entering after two consecutive daily bars with higher highs and higher lows and exiting after 1-10 bars showed weak short-term gains. In SPY, the two-week average gain was 0.23%, half the random gains. GLD had poor returns, with the two-week average significantly lower than random. TLT showed a negative short-term return, with the two-week return matching random. Increasing consecutive days did not improve results. The pattern is a short-term reversal pattern but not powerful enough on its own to use as a trading signal, and it does not work as a short strategy.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture and fabricated on TSMC’s 7nm N7 process, contains 54.2 billion transistors and a die size of 826 mm². It features third-generation Tensor Cores that support TF32, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary data types, and introduces fine-grained structured sparsity (2:4 pattern) to double math throughput. The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache (nearly 7× larger than V100), and compute data compression. Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology partitions the A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated memory paths, providing quality of service and fault isolation for multi-tenant environments. Third-generation NVLink offers 600 GB/sec total bidirectional bandwidth, and PCIe Gen 4 doubles bandwidth over PCIe 3.0. New asynchronous copy instructions and asynchronous barriers improve data movement efficiency, and task graph acceleration reduces launch and execution latency. The A100 delivers significant speedups over Tesla V100 for AI training, inference, and HPC workloads. The NVIDIA DGX A100 system integrates eight A100 GPUs connected via NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 petaFLOPS of AI performance.

In late 2015, Medora Brown, communications manager at Sanergy, was tasked with creating a social media strategy for the organization. Sanergy, founded by three MIT MBA graduates, addresses sanitation in Nairobi’s slums through a value chain: its non-profit Fresh Life brand franchises pre-fabricated toilets to local entrepreneurs, collects waste daily, and its for-profit Farm Star brand converts waste into organic fertilizer (Evergrow) and insect-based animal feed. By 2015, 615 Fresh Life toilets served about 32,000 people, with ambitious growth targets. Brown needed to allocate limited resources across platforms, demonstrate ROI, and engage three distinct audiences: slum dwellers, farmers, and global investors/donors.

Kenya’s technology sector was growing rapidly, with rising internet and mobile phone penetration, though smartphones remained a minority. Social media use was increasing, led by Facebook, Twitter, and LinkedIn, but slum dwellers accessed Facebook infrequently via cyber cafes for practical purposes, and few franchisees had profiles. Farmers were adopting Facebook and WhatsApp for agricultural discussions. Kenyan culture emphasized trust built through personal contact.

Fresh Life’s business objectives were recruiting franchisees and generating consumer demand, both of which relied heavily on in-person events and personal relationships; leadership questioned social media’s ability to build the necessary trust. Farm Star used Facebook to generate leads at a lower cost than in-person methods and was testing WhatsApp to connect farmers and support consultative selling, aiming to demonstrate Evergrow’s superior effectiveness over manure. Sanergy’s corporate brand focused on fundraising from foundations and large donors, using a blog, email, and speaking engagements; while some advisors advocated thought leadership through media, the co-founder responsible for fundraising doubted social media’s effectiveness for securing major donations. Brown had to consider these factors and Kenya’s cultural context to develop a social media plan that supported each brand’s goals.

U.S. mortgage applications fell 0.8% to 403.6 in the week ended March 24, a second weekly decline, even as borrowing costs dropped sharply. The average 30-year fixed conforming rate fell to 4.33% from 4.46%, the biggest drop since January. Refinancing applications decreased 2.9%, with its share at the smallest since October 2008, while purchase applications edged up 1.2%.

A University of Edinburgh study identified 287 genetic signals linked to male pattern baldness by analyzing DNA from over 52,000 men in the UK BioBank. Forty signals were on the X chromosome, inherited from mothers. The genetic pattern was only somewhat predictive: among men with fewer-than-average baldness genes, 14% were bald and 39% had no hair loss; of those with the top 10% of baldness genes, 58% had some hair loss. Male pattern baldness affects about 80% of men by age 80. Researchers say accurate individual prediction remains distant, but the findings advance understanding of genetic causes.

Minister Mailis Reps signed a directive to create two state upper secondary schools in Viimsi and Rapla, opening next September. A hiring round for leaders has begun. Construction is in the detailed project phase.

A CORAF report details results from the SRI-WAAPP project, the largest System of Rice Intensification (SRI) initiative, involving over 50,000 farmers across 13 West African countries. Coordinated by Mali’s National Center of Specialization on Rice and Cornell University, the project used participatory design. An independent evaluation found yield increases of 54% (irrigated), 65% (rainfed lowland), and 153% (rainfed upland), with a 41% average income rise. The project team reported 56% and 86% increases for irrigated and rainfed lowland systems. In the 2015-2016 season, SRI produced an additional 20,000 tons of milled rice worth about US$10 million; full adoption in 2017 could have eliminated imports. SRI is an adaptable, principle-based methodology. Concerns about increased labor burdens on women led to adoption of a labor-saving weeder from India. The regional scale fostered cross-border collaboration and innovation sharing. Authors advocate further scale-up with local adaptation.

The Mercy University School of Education has been strengthened by several federal, state, and local grants. The GRAD-PRO grant, a 5-year, $2.8 million award from the U.S. Department of Education (2023) under the PPOHA Program, aims to expand graduate opportunities for Hispanic and underserved populations, improve academic attainment, enhance faculty mentoring, and provide scholarships. It focuses on health sciences, education, faculty mentoring, and business. An event co-hosted with BranchED addressed mental well-being in schools, and a Faculty Mentoring Fellowship offers professional development. The BranchED grant, a 3-year award from 2023, seeks to enhance teacher preparation at Minority Serving Institutions, guided by beliefs in caring teachers, quality with diversity, and collective efforts. It involves district partnerships, curriculum reviews, and data-informed practices, with a partnership with the Public Schools of the Tarrytowns. It provides biweekly coaching and professional learning. In Year 1, Mercy achieved a 100% success rate, becoming the first institution to complete the Transformation Center process. The grant collaborated with GRAD-PRO on events, and its final year will focus on sustaining practices. The MISTI program, sponsored by NSF Noyce since 2013, prepares STEM teachers for high-need schools. Eligible fourth-year undergraduates or first-year master’s students in math or science observe in partner schools, take courses, and attend seminars on racism and social justice in year one. In year two, they complete student teaching, earn a master’s degree and certification. Support continues into their teaching careers with meetings and coaching. Research indicates the program effectively promotes teacher persistence. The NSF Master Teaching Fellowship (2019-2024) supported 14 PK-12 teachers from high-needs districts to become STEM teacher leaders. Fellows completed 9 graduate credits in STEM pedagogy, including courses on enhancing mathematics with STEM, engineering for the classroom, and leadership in STEM education. Faculty formed a professional learning community to improve courses. Fellows led initiatives like after-school programs, community gardens, and professional development for other teachers, resulting in publications and presentations. The CR-ITI/ESOL program, a 5-year, $687,500 NYSED grant (2023-2028), prepares ESOL teachers to address shortages in NYC. It leads to an Advanced Certificate in TESOL, involves clinical practice with school district partnerships, and provides mentoring and professional development. This is the second time Mercy has received this grant. Program co-directors attended the 2024 Voices United Conference. Completers receive continued support. These grants collectively advance the School of Education’s mission to prepare educators for diverse PK-12 populations through program improvement, professional learning, career readiness, mentoring, and collaboration.

This systematic literature review examined 15 peer-reviewed empirical articles from WOS and Scopus databases (2015–2022) on robotic coding in science education. The reviewed studies primarily focused on cognitive skills, including 21st-century skills (communication, problem-solving, scientific creativity, cognitive process skills) and computational thinking skills (computational thinking, algorithmic thinking, mathematical understanding). Application studies involved integration into science and engineering disciplines, using tools such as Arduino and tablet applications. Affective variables studied included interest, motivation, and opinion. Suggestions from the studies emphasized integrating robotic coding into STEM fields, different subjects, and teacher training; applying it at various learning levels; conducting large-scale research; using diverse data collection tools; and addressing gender. The review found no studies related to the psychomotor domain and noted a need for curriculum development, studies on other 21st-century skills, and in-service teacher training.

They are examining his contact with a prostitute, cruises, and a cryptic note, but reviews of his politics, finances, and social behavior yielded little. The FBI is putting up billboards seeking tips. Paddock meticulously planned the attack, stockpiling weapons and cameras, and had booked rooms at other festivals. He purchased tracer rounds. His girlfriend, sent abroad, was unaware and saw no warning signs. No accomplice is suspected.

The appellees, 1515 Broadway Associates, L.P. and Equitable Life Assurance Society, moved to dismiss as moot the appeals of the New York City Department of Finance and the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance from a bankruptcy court order confirming the debtor’s Chapter 11 reorganization plan. The appellees argued that the plan had been substantially consummated and no effective remedy could be fashioned. The district court denied the motion in part and granted it in part.

The debtor owned a commercial office building and filed for bankruptcy in 1990. The confirmed plan settled litigation, restructured the partnership, and provided for possible sale or foreclosure of the building in 1995 or 1996 if additional funding proved inadequate. The City objected that the reorganization of the general partner into a limited partnership and the provision for future liquidation were transfers subject to the City’s Real Property Transfer Tax. The State objected that the exercise of an option to purchase land under a groundlease might be subject to the New York Gains Tax. The bankruptcy court confirmed the plan over these objections. No stay pending appeal was sought.

The court discussed the mootness doctrine, noting that failure to obtain a stay does not automatically moot an appeal. Under the standard from In re AOV Industries, an appeal is not moot if granting relief would not harm other creditors or impact the reorganized debtor and if funds remain available. The court then addressed each claim.

The City’s challenge to the reorganization of the general partnership into a limited partnership was found moot. That restructuring was at the core of the plan, part of an integrated settlement, and could not be altered without affecting other plan provisions.

The City’s challenge to the possible future foreclosure was not moot because the transaction had not yet occurred, no funds had been disbursed, and effective relief could still be possible.

The State’s appeal regarding the Gains Tax was not moot. The Second Circuit’s subsequent decision in In re 995 Fifth Avenue held that the Gains Tax is not a stamp or similar tax exempt under 11 U.S.C. § 1146(c). Because this issue could not have been considered by the bankruptcy court at confirmation, the appeal could proceed.

Accordingly, the motion to dismiss was denied, but the appeals were limited as described: the City’s appeal could address only the future foreclosure issue, and the State’s appeal could proceed on the Gains Tax question.

The author recalls Weaver's 1947 claim that Russian is coded English, so translation is decoding. While Google Translate is useful, it lacks understanding. Machine translation avoids meaning, questioning if understanding is needed. The author will describe experiments.

Marcel Strigberger, a retired civil litigation lawyer, decided to declutter his house by discarding his McGill University law schoolbooks from over 50 years ago. He considered each book carefully. One book by Cheshire and Fifoot covered contract cases, including Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co. and an 1860s case where a contract with a prostitute was unenforceable for promoting immorality. He tossed it. Another book by Magarry and Wade on property law discussed fee simple and fee tail, concepts he never used in practice. He tossed it, later discovering a used copy sold for over $1,000 Canadian. He also discarded a book about a cargo ship explosion case. He disposed of the books in the blue recycle bin. He kept one 5-inch-thick volume to use as a reading stand.

Plaintiff System Management Arts Incorporated (Smarts) moved under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b) to revise the court’s prior opinion (Smarts I) that denied Smarts’ motion for partial summary judgment, citing newly-discovered evidence about the Klener Declaration. Smarts I had found a triable issue on whether the Delphi program qualifies as prior art, relying in part on the Klener Declaration as corroboration. Smarts later deposed Igor Klener and learned that shortly before he signed the declaration, Avesta Technologies, Inc. invited him to participate in a private stock placement ahead of an anticipated initial public offering; his investment later increased in value. Klener was also friends with Avesta executives. Klener denied any quid pro quo and stated the investment offer preceded his awareness of the lawsuit.

The court first held the motion procedurally proper under Rule 54(b) because it was based on newly-discovered evidence, making it timely despite Local Rule 6.3’s time limit. The court rejected defendants’ argument that Rule 54(b) applies only to adjudication of claims, noting the rule covers “any order or other form of decision.”

On the merits, the court explained that defendants must prove patent invalidity by clear and convincing evidence, and corroboration is required for testimonial evidence of prior art. The Federal Circuit applies a “rule of reason” and considers factors including the witness’s relationship, interest, and bias. The court rejected Smarts’ argument that an interested corroborating witness’s testimony is per se insufficient as a matter of law. Bias is a credibility factor for the jury, not a basis to exclude evidence. The court distinguished Woodland Trust v. Flowertree Nursery, where biased witness testimony was held insufficient as a matter of law, noting that in that case the witnesses appeared before the fact finder and the decision did not mandate exclusion of biased evidence. The court concluded that even if Klener were as biased as Smarts alleged, the declaration is not per se deficient; the jury should consider bias in weighing credibility. The court also found that the extent of bias and passage of time did not eliminate all genuine issues of material fact, as defendants offered contrary evidence (Klener’s denials) and credibility determinations are for the jury. The motion to revise was denied.

The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture introduces RT Cores for hardware-accelerated ray tracing and Tensor Cores for AI, enabling a hybrid rendering model that combines rasterization, ray tracing, and AI. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection tests, working with denoising to achieve real-time ray tracing. Turing supports Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) for AI-based image enhancement, NGX neural graphics features, Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. The TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs implement these features. Ray tracing techniques like ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections are demonstrated. The RTX-OPS metric quantifies hybrid rendering performance.

Smoky River FCSS seeks families with babies aged 2-4 months in October for the 2017-2018 Roots of Empathy program. This Canadian program, created in 1996, uses classroom baby visits to teach children empathy, increasing positive social behavior and reducing aggression. Contact Crystal at 780-837-2220.

The study presents a semi-empirical Bayesian framework to improve sex-specific Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses when one sex group has a smaller sample size, by adaptively borrowing information from the larger group. The approach yields shrinkage estimators for variant-exposure effects, including a fixed-effect meta-analysis estimate and an adaptive posterior mean (APM) that accounts for sex differences. Simulations demonstrated that using these shrinkage estimates, particularly APM, improves the efficiency of causal effect estimates for the smaller female group without loss of efficiency for males. Applying the method to sleep phenotypes from the Million Veteran Program and cardiovascular outcomes from All of Us, several sex-specific causal associations were identified: insomnia was associated with increased chronic kidney disease risk in females, long sleep with higher hypertension risk in females, and short sleep with higher coronary artery disease risk in males. A significant sex difference was found for the effect of obstructive sleep apnea on chronic kidney disease. Using APM for instrumental variable selection revealed additional significant causal effects, including OSA on several cardiovascular outcomes and distinct sex-difference patterns for long sleep.

The @YesYoureRacist Twitter account, which gained 271,000 followers over the weekend, aims to identify participants of the Charlottesville protest that included men with tiki torches and racist agendas. The account's moderator offered to make alt-right protesters "famous."

The President addresses Congress, noting his recent inauguration and calling for cooperation to build a better America. He presents a plan with four features: attention to urgent priorities, investment in the future, deficit reduction, and no new taxes. Thanks to economic growth, $80 billion in new revenues is expected without tax increases, allowing modest spending increases, investment in key priorities, and a nearly 40% deficit cut in one year to meet Gramm-Rudman-Hollings targets. He pledges to work with Congress and urges budget process reforms: two-year budgets, a line-item veto, a balanced budget amendment, and required votes on rescission proposals.

He emphasizes that economic growth, fueled by low taxes, is essential. He advocates greater individual choice in housing, schools, and child care, and believes government should not replace private-sector solutions. He commits to fighting discrimination and strengthening family and faith.

Proposals include: $2.2 billion for the National Science Foundation, a permanent R&D tax credit, a competitiveness task force, a $2.4 billion increase for NASA (manned space station, shuttle, commercial space), a capital gains tax rate cut, and urban enterprise zones. For education, he proposes a $500 million merit schools program, Presidential teacher awards, National Science Scholars, expanded magnet schools, alternative certification, and calls for an “Education Congress.”

He requests almost $1 billion more for the drug war, funding treatment, border protection, prosecution, the death penalty for kingpins, prison capacity, and demand reduction education. He asks $1.6 billion for AIDS education and research. Environmental measures include a new Clean Air Act to reduce acid rain, clean coal technology funding, park acquisitions, ocean dumping penalties, cautious energy development (postponing three lease sales, proceeding safely in ANWR), and tougher toxic waste enforcement.

He proposes full Medicaid funding with a $3 billion increase and coverage for near-poor pregnant women, a child care tax credit for low-income families without discriminating against stay-at-home mothers, preserving choice for relative and community care, a doubled $3,000 adoption tax deduction, full Social Security funding with a COLA, and increased support for the homeless. He favors a Puerto Rican referendum on statehood.

He calls for savings and loan reform within 45 days, protecting insured depositors, major reforms, and punishment for corruption. He proposes doubling the effort to clean up nuclear weapons plant waste. On defense, he supports a one-year budget freeze, with future increases above inflation, conditioned on a comprehensive deficit-reduction agreement without tax hikes and with budget reforms. He orders a national security review and Pentagon procurement improvements, and asks for less congressional micromanagement.

On foreign policy, he will review Soviet changes, proceed with caution, pursue the Strategic Defense Initiative, seek chemical weapons bans and nuclear nonproliferation, support democracy in Central America, strengthen alliances, and plans trips to Europe and the Pacific Basin. He announces a youth service program (YES), urges long-term business thinking, thanks the military, farmers, parents, and disabled Americans, and closes by quoting Churchill: “Give us the tools, and we will do the job.”

The passage discusses software engineering and the importance of requirements, distinguishing between functional requirements (actions the software must perform) and non-functional requirements (NFRs, characteristics like usability, reliability). It notes increasing demand for automatic document classification and describes classifiers: K-NN, Naïve Bayes, decision tree, and SVM. Related work includes approaches for generating domain NFRs, prioritizing NFRs, effort estimation considering NFRs, interplay of NFRs in software projects, and reusing NFR knowledge. The proposed methodology identifies potential NFRs by clustering keywords from functional requirements using semantic similarity measures and clustering techniques, then applies a decision tree classifier with an NFR matrix. Implementation on an IVR dataset classifies null and non-null functions. Results show the proposed method (decision tree with NFR matrix) achieves higher accuracy and lower execution time compared to using only the NFR matrix. The conclusion states that null functions reduce project efficiency and the proposed approach demonstrates improved performance.

The passage introduces HARMONY, an entropy-based metric that measures how uniformly model performance is distributed across subdomains of a benchmark. It highlights that benchmark reliability is critical for accurate evaluation, yet auditing receives less attention than model development. HARMONY involves partitioning a benchmark into semantic clusters, gathering per-cluster accuracies, and computing performance uniformity. High harmony indicates aggregate scores reflect broad competence, while low harmony obscures strengths and weaknesses. The authors recommend reporting HARMONY alongside accuracy to improve distributional reliability. Contributions include the metric and a large-scale empirical mapping of 19 multiple-choice question answering benchmarks across five model families. The passage also provides preliminaries and intuition, but the formal definition is cut off.

Patient advocacy groups asked the U.K. antitrust regulator to investigate several large drugmakers and their lobbying organization for suspected coordinated efforts to drive up medicine prices. The complaint arises amid a dispute over mandatory rebates, with the rate rising from 10% to 23%. In response, AstraZeneca, Merck, and Eli Lilly halted or scrapped expansion plans worth a combined $2.6 billion. The NHS spent $18.6 billion on brand-name medicines in the 2023-2024 financial year.

A dynamically-controllable x-ray interferometer for Mössbauer science is introduced, using two α-iron targets enriched in ⁵⁷Fe inside a high-purity polarimetry setup. The interferometer operates in a dark-fringe mode where, for identical targets with magnetizations at α₁=π/4 and α₂=−π/4 relative to the π̂ direction, the transmitted intensity ideally vanishes. Only two co-propagating pathways contribute to the detection signal: polarization-changing scattering in either the first or second target. Radiative couplings between targets cancel. A relative displacement of the targets, achieved by moving the first target with a piezoelectric transducer, continuously tunes the relative phase between the pathways, enabling dynamic control. Experimentally, event-based detection measures the effect of sudden target displacements on transmission up to ~7.5 µs (~50 nuclear lifetimes). Applications demonstrated include controlling transmitted x-ray intensity on nanosecond timescales and measuring relative target displacements on x-ray wavelength and nanosecond scales by observing mechanical wave propagation and reflection over >10 µs. The setup also allows exploration of polarization-dependent phase shifts.

This ebook, generated May 26, 2018, is part of the Office of the Historian's program to release ebook editions of the Foreign Relations of the United States (FRUS) series. Machines evolved from single-purpose to general-purpose, then to time-sharing and networking, leading to client-server architectures. In the early 2000s, internet and datacenters spurred distributed systems, composed of multiple applications/replicas communicating. Distributed systems offer inherent reliability and scalable organizational models but are more complex and require higher engineering skills. The growing need for reliable distributed systems drives demand for tools, patterns, and practices. Containers and orchestrators have become popular as foundations, enabling patterns and reusable components to build systems more reliably.

Penn Medicine researchers found that psilocybin calms brain circuits tied to pain and mood in animal studies. The compound acts in the anterior cingulate cortex, bypassing injury sites. In mice with chronic nerve injury and inflammatory pain, a single dose reduced pain and anxiety/depression-like behaviors for nearly two weeks. Psilocybin gently activates serotonin receptors like a dimmer switch. Injecting psilocin into the anterior cingulate cortex provided the same relief as whole-body psilocybin, while spinal cord injection did not. The non-addictive compound may inform therapies for addiction or PTSD. Further research is needed on safety, dosing, and long-term effects.

The lecture continues the discussion of the weak Hamiltonian for the process b → c ubar d, focusing on renormalization group equations. Anomalous dimension equations for Wilson coefficients are derived from the mu-independence of the Hamiltonian. The equations are solved in the plus-minus basis by changing variables from mu to alpha using the beta function, leading to a solution that sums leading logarithms (LL) of Mw/Mb. The physical picture involves evolving the Hamiltonian from a high scale of order Mw down to a scale of order Mb, separating scales.

To go to next-to-leading log (NLL), one needs one-loop matching and two-loop anomalous dimensions. A comparison of full theory (Standard Model) and effective theory calculations shows that the infrared structures agree, confirming the correct degrees of freedom. One-loop matching is obtained by subtracting the renormalized calculations, yielding Wilson coefficients that encode the high-scale physics.

Scheme dependence is discussed: at NLL, Wilson coefficients, matrix elements, and anomalous dimensions are scheme dependent, but the product C(μ)O(μ) is scheme independent. A specific combination of the effective theory constant B1 and the evolution factor J is scheme independent, ensuring consistency. The lecture notes subtleties in full calculations, including the treatment of γ5 in dimensional regularization and the need for evanescent operators in d dimensions.

The study investigated urinary proteomics profiles in hereditary angioedema (HAE) patients. Different profiles were identified among type 1 HAE, type 2 HAE, and healthy controls. Enriched biological processes and pathways in HAE included complement and coagulation cascades, cell adhesion molecules, immune response, proteolysis, and bradykinin catabolic process. A urinary biomarker panel consisting of C1-INH, KNG1, and EGF was identified as a promising noninvasive diagnostic tool for HAE. HAE is characterized by recurrent swelling attacks, caused by SERPING1 mutation leading to C1-INH deficiency, with type 1 (decreased C1-INH) and type 2 (dysfunctional C1-INH). In China, type 1 predominates and type 2 is <5%. HAE has a prevalence of 1/50,000, is often misdiagnosed, and carries a risk of fatal laryngeal attacks. Diagnostic delay is 8-13 years. Urine was used as a sample source due to its noninvasive collection and ability to reflect systemic changes. No urine biomarkers were previously available for HAE. The study applied data-independent acquisition (DIA)-based proteomics for discovery, with bioinformatics analysis, and validated biomarkers using parallel reaction monitoring (PRM)-based targeted proteomics in an independent cohort. In the discovery phase, 20 HAE patients (15 type 1, 5 type 2) and 29 healthy controls were recruited; the validation phase included 24 type 1 HAE patients and 18 healthy controls. Urine samples were processed by centrifugation and filter-aided preparation.

The experiment uses a hard ferromagnetic sphere levitated in a type I superconductor trap at 4.2 K, with motion detected by a dc SQUID and actuated by driving coils. Levitation relies on Meissner repulsion, modeled as a dipole-image dipole interaction, providing intrinsic translational trapping. Rotational motion exhibits librational modes due to anisotropy and a residual horizontal field. A synchronous driving technique, using feedback from the SQUID signal, spins the magnet. Free spin-down follows an exponential decay with rate γ, which under gas damping is proportional to pressure. The damping rate γ was measured as a function of room-temperature gauge pressure Pg, showing roughly linear behavior. A low-pressure linear fit gave γ = (8.2 s·mbar⁻¹)Pg + intercept, with the intercept attributed to residual air outgassing. Using a renormalization factor between Pg and cryogenic pressure P, the experimental γ/P = 11.6 s·mbar⁻¹ agrees with the theoretical prediction of 12 s·mbar⁻¹ for a 24 µm radius magnet. The lowest achieved damping rate was γ = 4.75×10⁻⁷ s⁻¹ (decay time ~24 days), corresponding to P = 4×10⁻⁸ mbar, demonstrating a pressure sensor range from 10⁻³ to 10⁻⁸ mbar. The quality factor reached Q = 1.33×10¹³. Maximum spinning frequency was 2.3 MHz (tangential speed 466 m/s), limited by SQUID electronics bandwidth; material disintegration limit estimated at ~5.5 MHz. A low-frequency precession peak was observed, with frequency fl = f_x²/f_s, where f_x ≈ 240 Hz relates to the librational frequency. This is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor, with advantages of passive trapping and low-heating synchronous driving, enabling operation as a cryogenic pressure sensor at 4.2 K. Potential applications include gyroscopes, gravimeters, material science, and torque-based precision measurements such as magnetometry with 1×10⁻¹⁶ T/√Hz sensitivity for axion-like dark matter searches. Lower temperatures may yield nHz damping. Elongated rotors could test collapse models, gravity, and quantum field effects like the Zel'dovich and Unruh effects. The system offers ultralow thermal noise for fundamental and quantum science.

At Lansdowne High School, students have produced live morning announcements from a television studio since 2005, streaming reminders, sports scores, an SAT word, and a college of the day. They also create a monthly variety show for the school system's cable channel and YouTube. About 100 of Baltimore County's 161 schools have studios, half digital, part of construction projects for nearly 20 years. Wolf's goal for digital studios in all schools is five to six years. This year, broadcast production facilitator became a union-negotiated extra-duty role with set pay. Inadequate projectors and speakers have caused mixed viewing, which Wolf hopes future budgets fix. Sheila Wells of Wide Angle Youth Media says media education builds teamwork, creativity, and critical thinking. Jason Loviglio of UMBC notes video production skills are increasingly vital as online video demand grows. Hillcrest Elementary recently opened a studio run by librarian Jacqueline Schoen, where students handle all broadcast tasks and use it for class projects. Wolf wants studios to be instructional tools beyond morning shows. Arbutus Middle School also started a studio using extra equipment and an unused office.

Researchers at Columbia University developed a silicon chip that converts a single multimode laser diode into a frequency comb—dozens of evenly spaced, high-power light channels—by using a locking mechanism to purify the laser's output. It may also advance portable spectrometers, optical clocks, quantum devices, and LiDAR. The TPS7H500x-SP controllers offer three switching frequency modes: internal oscillator (RT resistor sets frequency, SYNC outputs a 2× frequency clock), external synchronization (RT floating, SYNC receives a 2× desired frequency clock, 200 kHz–4 MHz, 40–60% duty cycle), and primary-secondary (primary uses internal oscillator, secondary uses external sync from primary’s SYNC output, resulting in 90° or 270° phase shift). Primary outputs OUTA/OUTB and synchronous rectifier outputs SRA/SRB are available depending on device variant. Dead times (TDPS, TDSP) are programmable via PS and SP pins; leading edge blank time is set by the LEB pin. Pulse skipping occurs when COMP voltage is below 0.3 V at the clock rising edge and the previous duty cycle was under 25%. Maximum duty cycle is configurable via the DCL pin: 100% (DCL to VLDO), 75% (floating), or 50% (DCL to AVSS); 50% limit is only for TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP, enabling OUTB/SRB.

Peak current mode control uses the CS_ILIM pin: the sensed current is compared to COMP/2 with a 150 mV offset. Overcurrent protection triggers when CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, initiating cycle-by-cycle limiting and charging the HICC capacitor. When HICC reaches 0.6 V, switching stops and SS discharges; after HICC rises to 1 V, a 1-µA discharge begins, and switching restarts when HICC falls to 0.3 V. The FAULT pin provides external protection: a voltage above 0.6 V for a minimum pulse width (0.4–1.4 µs) causes shutdown, with a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles after the fault clears. Slope compensation is set by a resistor on RSC, recommended equal to the inductor falling slope. Frequency compensation uses a transconductance error amplifier with Type 2A or 2B networks; component selection equations are provided. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C junction temperature.

The controllers are radiation-hardened PWM devices for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. A design example details a synchronous push-pull converter using GaN FETs, including calculations for RT, feedback divider, dead time, leading edge blank time, soft-start capacitor, transformer turns ratio and primary inductance, FET voltage ratings, RCD clamp, output inductor, output capacitance (including SET mitigation), current sense resistor, hiccup capacitor, compensation components, and slope compensation resistor. Layout guidelines recommend separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switch node area, placing bypass capacitors close to pins, routing feedback away from noise sources, and using RC filtering on CS_ILIM if needed.
