The lecture focuses on the spring-loaded inverted pendulum (SLIP) model for running. The model consists of a point mass on a massless leg with an ideal lossless spring of rest length r₀ and spring constant k. The system is completely conservative, with perfectly elastic collisions because the leg has no mass. The leg is assumed to instantly reset to a desired touchdown angle θ and rest length upon takeoff. The state space includes r, θ, ṙ, θ̇ during stance and x, y, ẋ, ẏ during flight. By choosing the apex (maximum height) as a surface of section, the dynamics reduce to a 1-D iterated map: at apex, ẏ=0, and ẋ is determined by total energy and y, so the entire state is captured by the apex height y.

The lecture justifies the model through comparative biomechanics, noting that animals ranging from cockroaches to horses (spanning five orders of magnitude in mass) exhibit dynamic similarity when analyzed with non-dimensional quantities like the ratio of kinetic to potential energy and relative spring constant. Their center-of-mass trajectories resemble SLIP behavior, and biological tendons act as physical springs.

To obtain a closed-form return map, a small-angle and small-displacement approximation is used for the stance phase. The resulting map shows one stable and one unstable fixed point. The unstable fixed point corresponds to vertical bouncing and bounds the stability region. A failure mode occurs when the system compresses deeply and bounces forward without reaching an apex high enough to place the leg ahead, causing a fall.

A variant model adds a toe mass, introducing energy loss at touchdown, and uses spring control to add energy. Simulations yield similar stable and unstable fixed points. The lecture also discusses preflexes: in cockroaches, a perturbation experiment using a small cannon showed that the animal recovers its center-of-mass trajectory in less than a step, faster than the monosynaptic reflex time, indicating passive musculoskeletal compliance provides stability.

Videos of Raibert’s hopping robots from the 1980s and 1990s are shown, including a monopod, a biped running at 2.2 m/s, a biped performing a front flip, and a quadruped. These robots used similar spring-mass principles. Finally, SLIP walkers are mentioned, where a compass gait with springy legs can transition between vaulting (walking) and bouncing (running) as spring stiffness varies, and humans naturally switch gait at the point where running becomes more efficient.

Whole-exome sequencing was performed on CTC pools from 29 mCRC patients (25 newly enrolled, 4 from a prior dataset). Multiple diversity metrics were computed, including mutational burden, proportion of aberrant genome, mutant allele tumor heterogeneity (MATH) score, and mutations in CRC driver genes. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards analyses showed that higher MATH scores and non-silent mutations in BCL9L were significantly associated with poorer overall survival. A custom 55-gene panel yielded MATH scores that correlated with whole-exome sequencing results and also predicted survival, suggesting a cost-effective alternative for clinical use. The authors state this is the first demonstration of a relationship between CTC genomic diversity and survival in mCRC.

PointState Capital LP purchased 6,057,459 shares of Peabody Energy Corporation (BTU) in the second quarter, valued at approximately $148.1 million, making it 1.6% of its portfolio and a 6.26% ownership stake. Other hedge funds, including FNY Partners Fund LP, BNP Paribas Arbitrage SA, Pacific Heights Asset Management LLC, Martingale Asset Management L P, and Legal & General Group Plc, also initiated new positions. Institutional investors and hedge funds collectively own 97.98% of BTU. Major shareholder Discovery Capital Management sold 12.8 million shares at $27.10 each. Analysts issued ratings ranging from hold to buy, with an average target price of $35.00. The stock traded at $29.59, down 0.84%, with a market cap of $2.97 billion. Peabody reported a quarterly EPS of ($0.18), missing estimates, on revenue of $1.26 billion. The company operates coal mining segments including Powder River Basin, Midwestern, Western, and Australian operations.

A study estimated monthly SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence among pregnant women attending first antenatal care (ANC) visits in four Zambian districts (Chadiza, Chipata, Chongwe, Lusaka) from September 2021 to September 2022. Zambia had reported nearly 350,000 COVID-19 cases over four waves, but confirmed cases underreport true infections. Previous serosurveys found 10.6% seroprevalence in July 2020 and 33.7% in February 2021, with no studies after the Delta and Omicron waves. ANC clinics have been used for SARS-CoV-2 surveillance elsewhere in Africa. COVID-19 vaccination rollout complicates seroprevalence interpretation, but assays targeting nucleocapsid and spike proteins can distinguish infection from vaccination. In Zambia, 97% of women attend ANC, and ANC attendees have been sentinel populations for other diseases. The study aimed to estimate monthly seroprevalence using repeated cross-sectional surveys. Data collection began after the Delta wave and included the Omicron wave. Four districts were selected to represent urban and rural areas and points of entry. A sample size of 200 women per district per month was chosen, with ten facilities per district randomly selected. Participants were pregnant women aged 15-49 years at first ANC; those with acute COVID-19 symptoms were excluded. Dried blood spots were tested with a multiplex bead assay detecting IgG against nucleocapsid (N), receptor binding domain (RBD), and N-RBD fusion protein. Positivity required signal ratios ≥1.2 for all three targets. Seroprevalence was adjusted for assay sensitivity (89.8%) and specificity (100.0%). Sub-analysis categorized antibody responses using vaccination status and anti-N/RBD results. Logistic regression identified factors associated with seropositivity.

Between September 2021 and September 2022, 9,221 women were enrolled; 8,304 had valid antibody results. Median age was 25 years. Overall, 63.8% were seropositive. Seroprevalence was highest in Lusaka (rising from 61.8% to 100.0% in August-September 2022) and lowest in Chadiza (peaking at 77.2% in April 2022, then declining to 56.6% by July 2022). In Chipata and Chongwe, seroprevalence peaked near 100% in August 2022. The greatest monthly increase in urban districts occurred December 2021 to January 2022 during the Omicron wave, while rural districts saw increases in March-April 2022. Among participants with anti-RBD antibodies and valid vaccination status, 77.7% had infection-induced antibodies only, 20.6% had hybrid immunity, and 1.6% vaccination-only. Hybrid immunity became more common over time. Vaccination was associated with higher odds of seropositivity in all districts. Among vaccinated women, serostatus did not differ by vaccine type or series completion. Prior COVID-19 was significantly associated with seropositivity only in Chadiza. District-level cumulative incidence ranged from 1.1% to 3.5%, while estimated infections were much higher, yielding seroprevalence-to-case ratios of 29:1 in Lusaka, 31:1 in Chadiza, 39:1 in Chipata, and 92:1 in Chongwe.

The study concluded that SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence was high, with nearly all ANC attendees in three districts showing evidence of infection. Lower seroprevalence in rural Chadiza was expected. The rise during Omicron mirrored patterns in South Africa. Most antibodies were infection-induced due to low vaccination coverage. Hybrid immunity produced the strongest antibody response. The ratios of seroprevalence to reported cases were lower than the 92:1 found in July 2020, suggesting improved case detection. Limitations included non-representative sampling, waning antibodies, conservative assay criteria, and cross-sectional design. Strengths included the 13-month duration covering the Omicron wave, use of a multiplex assay to distinguish infection from vaccination, inclusion of previously unsurveyed districts, and demonstration of integrating serosurveillance into routine ANC. The authors suggested that seroprevalence studies remain valuable for monitoring waning immunity and variant susceptibility, and that longitudinal cohorts via ANC could be useful.

BerkeleyGW is a software package for first-principles quantum many-body materials simulations based on the GW approximation. It achieves performance portability across AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPU architectures on Frontier, Aurora, and Perlmutter, with excellent strong scaling and high fractions of peak performance for core kernels. Innovations include GW perturbation theory (GWPT) for correlated electron-phonon coupling, a fast full-frequency GW method using a static subspace approximation, a mixed stochastic-deterministic pseudobands approach to reduce computational scaling, and optimized GPU kernels for diagonal and off-diagonal self-energy matrix elements using HIP, SYCL, and CUDA. Performance was measured on systems such as silicon divacancy (up to 2,742 atoms), lithium hydride defects (up to 17,574 atoms), and a twisted BN moiré bilayer (867 atoms). On Frontier’s full 9,408 nodes, the off-diagonal GPP kernel reached 1.069 ExaFLOP/s double-precision throughput (59.45% of theoretical peak); on 9,600 Aurora nodes, it reached 707.52 PetaFLOP/s (48.79% of attainable peak). These capabilities enable systematic large-scale computation of quasiparticle excited-state properties and electron-phonon coupling for complex materials with thousands of atoms, relevant to quantum devices.

Kerala, the first state to announce a transgender policy, has directed state and affiliated universities to reserve two seats for transgender students in undergraduate and postgraduate Arts and Sciences courses, and to prevent discrimination. The move aims to stop the trend of transgender students discontinuing studies due to social issues and pressure.

Investor optimism over U.S. tax reform and global economic growth pushed Wall Street and world stock markets to record highs on Thursday. The Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq, and MSCI all-country index all set closing highs for a fourth consecutive session. The S&P 500's eighth straight gain marked its longest streak since 1997. The dollar rose after data showed a falling trade deficit and lower jobless claims. Gold dipped on heightened December rate hike expectations. Oil prices climbed as signs of extended output cuts by Saudi Arabia and Russia offset record U.S. exports. A Reuters poll found global stocks are expected to keep rising, though a slim majority of strategists see the bull run ending in 2018.

The ASP SFS process: checks DRAM address protection, verifies signatures, loads/executes patch, updates patch level, returns status. The ASP interface provides firmware/patch levels. GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO uses a two-page buffer; output includes API version, SFS patch level, system patch level, and firmware version entries (type enum, version, security patch level). An update sub-command loads, verifies, and executes an SFS package after full validation. SFS packages are binary objects aligned to AGESA releases, named with family, AGESA release, and a monotonically increasing number. Update packages must match the system's firmware combination. The update process runs in parallel with x86/DMA traffic, aiming for minimal impact (brief quiescence at most). SEV/ES VMs require stop/restart for SEV firmware updates; SEV/SNP VMs continue operation.

A federal judge ordered Alabama to release its lethal injection protocol, with redactions for security, by June 7. The order came after news organizations sought the records following the halted February execution of an inmate due to difficulty connecting an IV line to his damaged veins.

Mr. Otori requested a council to consider his proposals; after delay, he demanded its appointment within three days. Advice was given to grant the council only power to listen and report. The Korean government refused the proposals due to Japanese military occupation. The King appointed his own council, which decided to abolish needless taxes. Foreign representatives sought Chemulpo’s neutrality; China consented, but Japan imposed conditions preventing it. Russian representative Waeber returned. USS Monocacy arrived, and Commander Impey offered cooperation. The Baltimore was reported at Chemulpo. Chinese action was anticipated after imperial ceremonies, and Chinese nationals left. Ye Cha-yun was appointed vice-president of the foreign office. Later, Acting Consul-General Gardner reported that he, his wife, Mr. Brown, and Mr. Fox were assaulted by Japanese soldiers. He was struck and dragged after giving his name under protest; later, his wife’s chair was pushed into a ditch. Minister Otori acknowledged the complaint and promised investigation. He subsequently forwarded General Oshima’s report denying any assault, stating no lady was perceived. The Japanese report described two foreigners approaching a sentinel, ignoring orders to stop, forcing into the bivouac, and being confronted by corporals.

Nnamdi Ogba, 26, was fatally shot while walking to his car in a Toronto Community Housing complex. Two men shot him from behind and fled in an SUV. Ogba, an electrical engineer with no criminal record, did not live there and did not know his attackers. Police believe the suspects came from another area seeking vengeance against the neighbourhood. Police released clips of two suspects and a Nissan Rogue, called the attack cowardly, and urged cooperation.

The President reports a year of national prosperity interrupted by a financial crisis, diminished political partisanship, and a threatened conflict over the seizure of the U.S.-flagged vessel *Virginius*, now under satisfactory adjustment. Foreign relations remain friendly with most powers. The U.S. participated in the Vienna International Exhibition and a conference on patent protection. The Emperor of China received Western diplomats, and slight progress was made against the cooly trade. The Geneva arbitration award was paid by Britain and used to redeem public debt. The President renews recommendations for a commission to settle direct losses from the *Alabama* claims and for payment of the recent mixed commission award of $1,929,819 in gold to Britain, while noting that all other British and U.S. claims were disallowed. Boundary lines with British possessions have been partly determined and surveyed. A special court is proposed for alien claims from the insurrection. Neutrality was observed in the Dutch-Acheen war. The Mexican claims commission resumed, with the British minister serving as umpire. Texas herd forays and Venezuelan obligations are under consideration. The Ottoman and Egyptian governments seek to change consular judicial powers, requiring congressional assent. Santo Domingo requests a U.S. protectorate. Treaties with Denmark, Mexico, the Orange Free State, and Ecuador were proclaimed. The President urges legislation on expatriation and citizenship, noting confusion over the status of children born abroad and the need to define acts of expatriation.

Regarding Spain, the Republic freed slaves in Porto Rico, released many illegally held in Cuba, and restored sequestered American estates, but slavery in Cuba persists due to opposition. The *Virginius*, registered in New York, was seized on the high seas by a Spanish gunboat, and 53 passengers and crew were executed. The U.S. demanded and Spain agreed to return the vessel, surrender survivors, salute the flag, punish offenders, and provide indemnity. The Navy was placed on a war footing. The President attributes Cuba’s condition to slavery and hopes for its abolition.

Treasury receipts exceeded expenditures last fiscal year, but a decline is expected due to the panic. The President recommends economy in public buildings, river and harbor improvements, and fortifications, and warns against fraudulent war claims. He discusses currency contraction, the need for elasticity, and steps toward specie payments, suggesting possible modifications to national bank note issuance and reserves. Shipbuilding increased slightly, but foreign vessels still carry much U.S. trade. He proposes that if New York and Illinois open their canals to large vessels, the federal government maintain connecting waterways. He also suggests exploring the Amazon via the Madeira River to Bolivia, tariff revision, and more mints.

The War Department report highlights the need for seacoast armament and reopening promotions in staff corps. The Navy has repaired old ships and built new sloops; recent Caribbean events prompted readying all available force. The Post-Office Department saw revenue and expenditure increases, with expanded service. Recommendations include extending free delivery, prepayment of newspaper postage, uniform postage on miscellaneous matter, adjusting postmaster compensation, and establishing postal savings depositories. Postal telegraphy is again mentioned.

In Utah, court decisions have practically abolished jury trials; Congress is asked to provide a mode of obtaining jurors and limit probate court jurisdiction. The President believes the involuntary bankruptcy provisions of the 1867 act worsen financial distress and recommends their repeal. He warns of accumulating and fraudulent claims against the government and urges early presentation and personal testimony requirements.

Indian policy continues to collect tribes on reservations, with a goal of concentrating them in the Indian Territory and eventually providing a territorial government. The Patent Office needs more room. Public land disposal increased, with over 13 million acres disposed. A large Russian colony desires to emigrate; the President invites attention to this. Pension expenditures decreased slightly, but recent law changes may absorb that reduction; fraud detection is ongoing. The Bureau of Education is active, and the Ninth Census is complete; a quinquennial census is recommended. Washington, D.C., has been greatly improved under the board of public works; the President recommends liberal federal support and suggests establishing a national university there.

Civil-service reform needs congressional cooperation to make rules binding. The President recommends admitting Colorado as a State and supporting an irrigating canal from the Rocky Mountains to the Missouri River, with land grants. He renews calls for general amnesty and for legislation to better secure the civil rights of freed slaves.

First Solar senior vice president Tymen deJong was reviewing the company's 2011 Form 10-K, which revealed a net operating loss of $39 million—its first year-end loss in seven years—and slowing revenue growth. First Solar had been the largest and lowest-cost photovoltaic manufacturer for nearly a decade, using proprietary thin-film cadmium telluride technology and breaking the $1.00 per watt manufacturing cost record in 2009. However, its cost advantage was eroding. Chinese crystalline-silicon manufacturers, subsidized by their government, were flooding the market with low-price panels. Global demand weakened as the 2008–2009 financial crisis reduced European solar subsidies and bank financing for projects. Falling silicon raw material prices benefited silicon-based competitors but not First Solar's cadmium telluride panels.

First Solar produced thin-film modules by depositing cadmium telluride on glass substrates, controlling all production in-house. It operated plants in Ohio, Germany, and Malaysia, with new facilities under construction. By 2011, it was producing below capacity due to Chinese competition. The company had vertically integrated into the systems business through acquisitions starting in 2007, offering project development, engineering, construction, and financing. This systems segment grew to 25% of sales but brought higher SG&A expenses. First Solar maintained a conservative financial strategy with low debt and high cash reserves.

The PV market comprised residential, commercial, and utility segments, with utilities predicted to be the fastest-growing. Purchase criteria varied by segment, but levelized cost of electricity was key. Global PV installations had grown rapidly, driven by government incentives like feed-in tariffs and renewable portfolio standards, though many subsidies were shrinking by 2012. Chinese producers had expanded to manufacture nearly 60% of global supply. U.S. and European manufacturers faced bankruptcies, including Solyndra, Evergreen Solar, and SpectraWatt. An anti-dumping lawsuit was filed against Chinese firms.

DeJong faced questions about whether First Solar's competitive advantage was permanently eroded, how to counter Chinese competitors, whether the systems business was an advantage or distraction, and which market to focus on. He needed to prepare for an upcoming board meeting amid the company's financial underperformance.

A player who fell into the boards is fine and will play tomorrow. The speaker felt the team started well but the powerplay passing was not good enough and they lost focus. The powerplay has been a key reason for reaching the Stanley Cup Finals, and special teams are important. They did well on penalty killing and scored a first goal, but could not generate another. They plan to refocus for a better performance. The team's success has come from discipline, sticking to the game plan, and not panicking. They have faced adversity before and answered well. They learned from the Devils in the first two games. The game featured a quick momentum change with many penalties; the Devils capitalized while they did not. They did not play well enough to win. The Devils' pressure was better, and their own passing and focus were lacking. They are missing a player but have moved on and won without him, refusing to use his absence as an excuse. Shots were even, and both teams play strong defense, limiting space and scoring chances. The two goals against came right after special teams situations. Momentum can swing quickly, and mental mistakes like discipline will be key. The first period had many penalties, making it a special teams period. Two high sticks were missed by referees because the game is fast and they did not see them. The speaker mentions the Rockies won in San Francisco and they aim to repeat that. They reflect on past playoff success and approach the next game positively as a good challenge.

U.S. District Judge Esther Salas temporarily halted deportation proceedings against Indonesian Christians in the U.S. illegally but seeking legal status. The order, issued Friday in response to an ACLU lawsuit, applies to Indonesians with pre-2009 removal orders and affects about 50 people in New Jersey who identified themselves to ICE in 2009 for a work authorization and deportation stay program. The lawsuit followed enforcement actions targeting Indonesian Christians, including the arrest of two men last month after dropping their children at school. Harry Pangemanan, in the U.S. since 1993, sought sanctuary at the Reformed Church of Highland Park, where he is an elder and spent nine months in 2012. Arthur Jemmy and Yohanes Tasik were already living there to avoid detention. Pangemanan, who organized volunteers after Superstorm Sandy, came on a tourist visa; his wife arrived in 1998 during anti-Christian turmoil. They cite religious persecution, including church burnings, as a reason not to return. He missed the one-year asylum application window. After Sept. 11, he and Jemmy complied with registration rules but failed to gain legal status. Salas ordered briefs filed within a month. Pangemanan’s family joined him at the church after their home was vandalized.

UCLA, a team that started 0-4, upset No. 7 Penn State 42-37, marking the first time since 1985 that a team 0-4 or worse beat a top-10 opponent. UCLA’s pregame win probability was 2.1%; Penn State’s defense allowed 42 points, and the loss dropped its SP+ projected most likely record to 7-5. Vanderbilt missed upset chances against Alabama, losing a fumble at the 8 and an interception at the 7 in a 20-14 game before Alabama pulled away. Florida State’s turnovers prevented a closer contest against Miami, and QB Castellanos’s performance has regressed. Cincinnati beat Iowa State to join the Big 12 race, while Texas Tech dominated Houston and is projected as a double-digit favorite in all remaining games. The lecture demonstrates sampling, aliasing, and discrete-time linear systems using a programmable digital filter. The setup consists of a sampler, continuous-to-discrete converter, digital filter, discrete-to-continuous converter, and a smoothing low-pass filter. Initially, the digital filter is an identity system, reducing the setup to sampling and reconstruction. With a bandlimited input, sampling produces a periodic spectrum; low-pass filtering recovers the original signal if the bandwidth is less than half the sampling frequency. Aliasing occurs when the bandwidth is too large, causing spectral overlap. Using a sinusoidal input, as frequency increases, the output frequency increases until half the sampling frequency, then decreases due to aliasing. Near half the sampling rate, a beating effect appears because the low-pass filter is not ideal.

A low-pass digital filter with symmetric impulse response (linear phase) and cutoff at π/5 is then inserted. The equivalent continuous-time frequency response is the digital filter’s response with the frequency axis rescaled: 2π maps to the sampling frequency, so the cutoff becomes one-tenth of the sampling frequency. Demonstrations show the overall impulse response is symmetric and smoothed by the D-sampling filter. Frequency response sweeps reveal attenuation past the cutoff and periodicity when sweeping from 0 to the sampling frequency. Changing the sampling frequency proportionally changes the effective cutoff frequency. Audio demonstrations illustrate low-pass filtering with varying sampling rates, altering the audible bandwidth.

The paper presents ABXLAB, an open-source man-in-the-middle framework that transforms arbitrary websites into controllable behavioral testbeds for studying LLM agent decision-making. It intercepts and modifies real-world web content in real-time to manipulate choice architectures. The framework is applied to consumer behavior in a 2-alternative forced choice setup using product pairs from an online shopping environment. Experiments systematically varied product attributes (ratings, prices) and injected nudges (authority, social proof, scarcity, negative framing, incentives) across 17 state-of-the-art models in over 80,000 trials. Results show LLM agents exhibit strong, systematic biases: higher ratings increased selection probability by 30–80 percentage points, cheaper prices by 15–34pp in original conditions, and nudges shifted choices by 10–60pp when ratings and prices were matched. Order effects were heterogeneous, with some models showing near-deterministic preferences for first or second position. Compared to a human baseline (effects of 4–9.9pp), agents showed 3–10× greater susceptibility. Sensitivity analyses indicated that even modest differences in price or rating trigger effects, and larger differences do not strongly magnify them. User profile experiments revealed that explicit preferences act as categorical switches, dominating decisions and suppressing other attributes. The authors note limitations in ecological breadth, domain specificity, and the binary forced-choice design, and emphasize the need for a behavioral science of AI agents to ensure predictable and aligned behavior.

On January 30, 2019, Tesla announced that CFO Deepak Ahuja intends to retire after serving since 2008 (with a 14-month gap). He will remain briefly and then advise. Zachary Kirkhorn, VP of Finance, will succeed him. Kirkhorn joined Tesla in 2010, leading cost reduction for the Roadster and contributing to Gigafactory 1, Model X, and Model 3 launches. CEO Elon Musk thanked Ahuja and expressed confidence in Kirkhorn. Ahuja cited recent profitability, and Kirkhorn emphasized cost management and operational efficiency.

Titus pleaded guilty to hydromorphone possession and probation violations. A 2017 police raid found him trying to escape a bedroom with drugs and paraphernalia. The judge noted his outstanding transformation, sentencing him to three months' house arrest with curfew, a year's probation, counseling, and drug abstinence. He received six days' time-served. He has attended daily sobriety meetings for eight months.

The passage describes sample handling for the DAWn-plasma study: nasopharyngeal swabs are to be refrigerated then frozen, with residual material sent to a central lab in Leuven for later qPCR. It cites a correction notice for the trial protocol (Trials, 2020), a report on early high antibody titre convalescent plasma (European Respiratory Journal, 2022), a meta-analysis on convalescent plasma (JAMA Network Open, 2022), and a treatment benefit index study (JAMA Network Open, 2022). It lists figures and tables from the trial, covering mechanical ventilation, CRP, ferritin, D-dimer, body temperature, antibody titers, protocol violations, baseline characteristics, endpoints, and adverse events including transfusion-related effects.

Sun Waa, a Chinese takeaway in Littleover, received a one-star food hygiene rating from Derby City Council inspectors after they found a container of rice left at room temperature for six hours, an obstructed wash basin, food debris buildup, cross-contamination risks from using the same sink for raw meat and ready-to-eat foods, improper cleaning with bleach, insect webbing, and a broken probe thermometer. The business has since improved hygiene practices significantly, with a revisit in January confirming progress, and expects a re-score to five stars in March. The inspection occurred in November 2017, but the report was only recently released following a Freedom of Information request.

Michelle Munson of NYU and Sarah Narendorf of the University of Houston have been studying the mental health narratives of marginalized young adults. They find that how these individuals make sense of their condition and its origins significantly influences their engagement with treatment and self-care. The research focuses on young adults facing added challenges like poverty, reliance on safety-net systems, disabilities, and discrimination. Munson and Narendorf argue that providers should work collaboratively with young adults to uncover their personal interpretations, as this is critical to keeping them invested in healing. They use in-depth, face-to-face interviews with open-ended questions to learn about young adults' experiences. Their studies, published in the American Journal of Orthopsychiatry and forthcoming in the Journal of the Society for Social Work and Research, suggest that training providers to closely consider these narratives could transform mental health care. The researchers are also developing technology-based interventions to help shape narratives. They emphasize that many marginalized young adults do not feel heard or understood by mental health providers, and that listening to their stories is essential to avoid continuing to fail them.

Sixteen-year-old Murad Rahimov, who dreamed of becoming a NASA astronaut since age three in Uzbekistan, toured NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center. His family immigrated to the U.S. in 2010 and became citizens in January, a story NPR profiled. Listener Aaron Schnittman heard it and connected Murad with his brother Jeremy, an astrophysicist at Goddard. Jeremy gave Murad and his mother Limara a private tour, showing them the clean room, cryo-vac chamber, acoustic chamber, and laser lab. They discussed black holes, Einstein, and time travel. Murad, now a U.S. citizen, is an accelerated high school junior aiming for Cal Tech and a Mars mission. His mother feels grounded by citizenship and the pledge of allegiance. Murad plans to watch the upcoming total solar eclipse in Kansas City.

Players discussed their mindset ahead of a potential Stanley Cup-clinching game. Jonathan Toews emphasized focusing on the game and ignoring external buzz, noting the playoff journey passes quickly and that it is easier to play than to watch due to nerves. He said the team improves as series progress and praised coach Joel Quenneville for making adjustments that strengthen the team. Toews also highlighted the importance of proper recovery to avoid injuries, and remarked on the team's ability to repeatedly compete for the Cup.

Brad Richards noted that experience makes preparation easier, and the core group's familiarity reduces the need for speeches. He described the opponent, Tampa Bay, as a talented team that makes plays in difficult situations, expecting another tight, grinding game. Richards stressed the need for patience and smart puck management, and said the team's job is to take away the opponent's belief. He also praised a teammate's all-around game, noting his defensive prowess and leadership.

Kris Versteeg called the playoff run tough, acknowledged Tampa Bay's skill, and said every game is expected to be close. He spoke positively about his new line combination building chemistry and emphasized staying ready and maintaining confidence among players outside the lineup.

Anita Anand, presenter of Radio 4’s Any Answers, was dropped from yesterday’s edition because it was to discuss the BBC gender pay dispute, after she publicly criticized the pay gap and tweeted support for equal pay. BBC bosses cited impartiality rules. The programme was presented by Julian Worricker. Critics accused the BBC of insulting women journalists; MP Andrew Bridgen likened it to Soviet Pravda. Anand is the latest affected by impartiality rules, following Jenni Murray’s removal from Woman’s Hour. Anand was reportedly disappointed. A BBC spokesman said editors decide case-by-case on impartiality.

This study benchmarks 15 summary-level Mendelian randomization (MR) methods using real-world genetic datasets. Evaluations focus on type I error control under three confounding scenarios (population stratification, pleiotropy, and family-level confounders), accuracy of causal effect estimates (using trait pairs where exposure and outcome are the same trait, true effect = 1), and replicability/power (LDL-C and CAD case study with six LDL-C GWAS datasets). In type I error control, MR-APSS, Egger, Weighted-mode, and CAUSE generally performed better, though CAUSE showed deflated p-values and failed under strong population stratification at its default IV threshold. Most other methods exhibited inflated type I errors, especially with looser IV selection thresholds. IV selection threshold strongly influenced performance; many methods showed increased inflation and bias as thresholds relaxed. For accuracy, MR-APSS produced estimates closest to the true value with confidence intervals covering it across thresholds, while most other methods were biased toward the null when weaker instruments were included. In replicability, CAUSE and MR-APSS yielded consistent causal estimates across datasets and thresholds. The study recommends using negative controls, multiple IV selection standards, and multiple independent data sources to improve reliability. Limitations include potential coexistence of confounders, limited positive controls, the same-trait design not testing pleiotropy, and the exclusion of individual-level MR methods.

The NRA claimed YETI cut ties, but YETI stated it ended outdated discounting programs for the NRA Foundation and others, offering an alternative customization program. YETI called the NRA-ILA's statement inaccurate. NRA supporters planned a boycott, and Bryan Atkinson destroyed a cooler with explosives, starting the #YetiCoolerChallenge. The dispute follows other businesses distancing from the NRA after shootings. YETI reaffirmed its support for the Second Amendment.

The present disclosure provides for articles exhibiting structural colors through optical elements, where structural colors are produced by physical optical effects like scattering, refraction, reflection, interference, and/or diffraction, without requiring inks or pigments. The optical element can be used alone or in combination with a textured surface and/or a primer layer to impart structural color. The optical element can be disposed on a component of an article, such as a footwear upper or sole, to impart a structural color differing from the underlying surface's color. The article can be footwear, apparel, or sporting equipment. The optical element can include one or more optical layers, such as a multilayer reflector or filter. The structural color can be characterized using CIE 1976 color space measurements, where, for example, the range of combined a* values may be less than about 40% of the overall scale, the ΔE*ab between two measurements may be less than or equal to about 100, or the range of combined h° values may be less than about 60 degrees. The optical element can include a textured surface with profile features and flat areas, and a primer layer which can have a dark color. The component can comprise a thermoplastic material, such as a thermoplastic polyurethane.

Asparagus (1 cup boiled) provides 33% daily folate. Broccoli (1 cup) ~14%. Citrus fruits: orange ~50 mcg; also papaya, grapefruit, grapes, banana, strawberries. Legumes (beans, peas, lentils) provide most daily needs. Avocado (1 cup) 110 mcg (28%). Lady's finger (½ cup cooked) ~103 mcg. Nuts/seeds: pumpkin, sesame, sunflower, flax seeds, peanuts, almonds. Cauliflower (1 cup) ~55 mcg (14%). Beetroot (1 cup) ~14%. Carrots (1 cup raw) ~5%. Corn (1 cup cooked) ~34 mcg.

Zita Kovács, a winemaker for seven years, initially faced prejudice and was mistaken for a hostess, but now feels respected and designs labels. Zsófi Laposa noted the profession was once male-centered and physically demanding, but technology opened doors; she studied in Bordeaux and believes women bring gentleness and invigorate the community. Krisztina Csetvei founded a winery in Mór in 2011 and balances winemaking with raising her daughter Panna, who accompanies her to events; they will present a wine named Panna Rose at VinCE Budapest. Andi Gere co-manages her family winery with her father, feels femininity refines wines, balancing heavier styles elegantly.

The MSPM0C1105/6 MCUs are cost-optimized, ultra-low-power 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ devices operating up to 32MHz. They feature up to 64KB flash, 8KB SRAM, an on-chip oscillator, 3-channel DMA, CRC-16 accelerator, 12-bit ADC, comparator with DAC, temperature sensor, advanced and general-purpose timers, watchdog timer, and communication peripherals (UART, SPI, I2C) supporting protocols like LIN, IrDA, DALI, SMBus. Part of the MSPM0 family, they operate from -40°C to 125°C and 1.62V to 3.6V. An ecosystem includes a LaunchPad kit, free MSP SDK, and online training and support.

The present disclosure provides methods, apparatuses, and systems for transmitting paging information in wireless communication systems using beamforming. To address the problem that a UE in idle state cannot foresee beam scheduling, making DRX for paging complex, a first communication node calculates a time domain position of a paging occasion (PO) for a second communication node. The PO comprises a group of paging resources for transmitting paging information on one or more preset beams or ports, and corresponds to a synchronous signal burst set or sweeping resources. The PO is calculated using parameters including a discontinuous reception cycle, a paging transmission interval, a number of paging transmissions, a device identifier, and a PO offset. The first communication node transmits paging information (paging downlink control information and/or a paging message) within the PO. Corresponding methods for the second communication node to calculate the PO and receive the paging information are also provided. Additionally, quasi-co-location relationship information between a signal related to paging information and other sweeping signals or channels is used to determine a receiving manner.

Options trading in IWM involves buying and selling call and put options contracts. A call option gives the buyer the right to buy a certain number of shares at an agreed-upon price on or before the expiration date, while a put option gives the right to sell. Investors may buy calls or puts to profit from expected price movements. Advantages include leverage for large gains with small investments, hedging against market risks, and speculating without owning shares. Options work like insurance; a premium is paid, for example, to buy puts as a hedge. Trades are not permitted if the stock’s closing price is below $2.00.

Available order types are market, limit, stop, and trailing stop orders. Strategies include buying calls when expecting a rise, buying puts when expecting a fall, selling covered calls (selling calls while owning the underlying stock), and buying protective puts to guard against declines. Risks involve potential loss of the entire investment if the price moves opposite to predictions, the premium paid, and unlimited risk for short calls. A trading plan outlining entry and exit should be based on strategy and include technical indicators such as moving averages, relative strength index, and Bollinger bands; monitoring news and economic data is advised, and backtesting is emphasized.

Short selling is allowed, involving selling a stock not owned to buy back at a lower price; both calls and puts can be sold short, with high risk. Taxes may include short-term capital gains for trades held one year or less, long-term for over one year, and taxes on the premium; capital gains are sourced to the resident’s country. Risk management should include stop-loss orders, limiting risk per trade, and diversifying options. When selecting contracts, consider length, expiration date, and strike price based on strategy and expected price movement.

Requirements include being at least 18, having a valid address, sufficient funds, and a margin account. Investors must understand contract terms, risks, and regulations. IWM does not require FINRA Level 2 approval. Margin trading is allowed but risky, especially for the inexperienced. Minimum account balance varies by broker, typically around $2,000. Allocation should generally not exceed 10% of the total portfolio. Prior research should cover the underlying company, financials, competitors, available option contracts, and strategies. Technical indicators like moving averages, Bollinger Bands, MACD, RSI, and stochastics can be combined with fundamental analysis; backtesting is crucial. Fees depend on the broker, typically commissions and possible additional charges. Up-to-date information can be obtained from online news, research websites, financial publications, and forums. Option types include calls, puts, and specialized ones like butterfly spreads and straddles. Profit-maximizing strategies depend on goals and risk tolerance, often combining buying/selling, spreads, technical analysis, and risk management. The article advises beginners to avoid options trading and to backtest strategies before committing funds.

The passage presents several container patterns for building distributed systems.

The sidecar pattern uses a sidecar container to augment an application container. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy service via an nginx sidecar that terminates HTTPS and proxies to localhost; configuration synchronization where a sidecar manages dynamic configuration from an API and updates a shared file; a topz sidecar sharing the PID namespace to provide resource introspection; and building a simple PaaS with a git-sync sidecar. For modularity and reusability, sidecars should be parameterized via environment variables, have a clear API surface, and be documented with Dockerfile directives like EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

The ambassador pattern brokers interactions between the application container and the external world. Examples include a sharding ambassador proxy (twemproxy) for sharded Redis or memcached, routing requests to appropriate shards; a service broker ambassador that discovers and connects to services (e.g., MySQL) in different environments; and request splitting for experiments, using nginx to send a percentage of traffic to an experimental service.

The adapter pattern modifies the application container’s interface to conform to a standardized interface. Examples include monitoring adaptation with a Prometheus exporter sidecar; logging normalization with Fluentd to transform various log formats (Redis slowlog, Storm) into a consistent stream; and health monitoring by adding an adapter container that runs rich health checks (e.g., for MySQL) and exposes an HTTP health endpoint.

Replicated load-balanced services are a pattern for stateless services where identical replicas sit behind a load balancer. Readiness probes indicate when a replica is ready. Session tracking can use consistent hashing. Application-layer replication can include a caching layer (Varnish) as a separate tier to improve hit rate, and an SSL termination layer (nginx). Rate limiting and denial-of-service defense can be implemented at the caching layer.

Sharded services split data across multiple shards because state is too large for a single machine. A sharded cache increases memory utilization. Cache hit rate affects system capacity and latency; shard failures degrade performance. Replicated sharded caches combine replication within each shard for resilience. Sharding functions use hashing and modulo; key selection groups identical requests while separating different ones. Consistent hashing minimizes remapping when resharding. Hot sharding dynamically scales individual shards under uneven load.

The scatter/gather pattern uses replication for time scalability by parallelizing requests across many leaves. The root distributes a request to all leaves, each processes a portion, and the root combines results, enabling faster servicing than sequential processing.

A pump and dump scheme involves a promoter acquiring a position in a stock, typically a penny stock, and artificially increasing its share price by spreading false or misleading information. As the price rises, the promoter sells to latecomers, causing the share price to drop significantly. The scheme is similar to a Ponzi scheme and is driven by the fear of missing out (FOMO), which can sustain it for days, weeks, or months. Pump and dump strategies are illegal on regulated exchanges and are considered immoral, benefiting only a few at the expense of the majority; short-term trading is described as a zero-sum game where the last to join incur losses.

An example given is "John Lebanon," who as a teenager made almost a million dollars through pump and dump promotions via chat rooms and message boards, later settling with the SEC. Historically, such schemes used boiler rooms and word of mouth; now they spread through social media. A chart of penny stock JAMN illustrates the pattern: volume increases during accumulation and the pump, then drops before the share price collapses back to pre-pump levels.

Pump and dump schemes are much more likely in the crypto market, particularly among low-volume "shitcoins" on small exchanges, often organized via Telegram. The unregulated nature of the crypto market allows these schemes to persist, even though they are illegal in regulated markets. Almost all pumps and dumps occur in the OTC market and the crypto market; they have been largely eradicated from major exchanges.

A study of German bank accounts from 2002–2015 found that nearly 6% of sampled investors participated in at least one pump-and-dump scheme, with an average return of -28% and estimated losses of at least €1.2 million. Additionally, pump and dump schemes account for 15% of spam emails. The passage advises staying away from such scams, avoiding FOMO, and focusing on long-term investing or systematic trading with backtesting.

The ultimate oscillator (UO) is a momentum indicator that measures price momentum across three timeframes (7, 14, and 28) using a weighted average, with the shortest timeframe receiving the most weight. It was developed by Larry Williams in 1976 and oscillates between 0 and 100; levels below 30 are considered oversold and above 70 overbought. Trading signals require divergence: a buy signal needs a bullish divergence starting from oversold territory and the oscillator rising above the divergence high; a sell signal requires the opposite conditions. The multi-timeframe approach reduces false signals. A backtest using default parameters (buy when crossing below 40, sell when crossing above 50) on SPY produced poor results. An optimization of the three timeframe settings (excluding buy/sell thresholds) yielded impressive results, with only one simulation showing a profit factor below 2. One optimized backtest had a profit factor of 2.5, 355 trades, an average gain of 0.77%, a 78% win rate, and a 25% maximum drawdown, with only two down years. The ultimate oscillator proved consistent and stable as a mean reversion indicator and qualifies as one of the best. A rising oscillator indicates strong buying pressure; a falling oscillator suggests weak buying pressure and a potential sell signal.

The passage discusses the threat of automation to jobs, particularly truck drivers, and explores human augmentation as a potential safeguard. It notes that 3.5 million US truck drivers may be out of work in a couple of decades due to autonomous vehicles, and that the Fourth Industrial Revolution could eliminate over five million jobs in five years. The Bodyhacking Conference highlighted augmentations like RFID implants and bionic parts. Brain augmentation is examined through Elon Musk's neural lace concept—a digital layer to enhance brain input-output—and Harvard's injectable electronic mesh tested in mice. Such technology could allow humans to compete with AI computationally while retaining intuition. Body augmentation is presented via exosuits: SuitX's MAX system reduces force on body areas by up to 60%, and Harvard's soft exosuit reduces walking effort by 23%. These combine human decision-making with robotic strength for unstructured jobs. For immediate steps, Tom Davenport and Julia Kirby's "Beyond Automation" advises knowledge workers to develop skills outside codifiable cognition or learn to work with machines. Davenport is optimistic for knowledge workers but pessimistic for physical laborers like truck drivers, who may struggle to transition. He distinguishes narrow AI from artificial general intelligence, stating that if AGI emerges, "all bets are off."

Meb Faber is co-founder and chief investment officer of Cambria Investment Management, an author of white papers and five books, and a graduate of the University of Virginia. His Tactical Asset Allocation strategy is an active trend-following approach that uses market timing across four asset classes: stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities. These are divided into five categories: U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities. The strategy is implemented with five well-diversified index ETFs, allocating 20% to each position and moving to cash when no signal is present. Backtesting over 16 years shows a maximum drawdown of -13.24%, significantly lower than the 40–50% drawdowns of passive portfolios. The timing model is described as universal and applicable to other asset classes and ETFs.

Richard Berg appealed a trial court order increasing his child support. The parties divorced in 1981; Nancy Berg received custody of three children, and Richard was ordered to pay $145 per child per month. In 1985, Nancy moved to increase support to the guidelines level of $516 per month for the two remaining minor children, and to extend support for the oldest child past age 18 until graduation and for the mentally retarded middle child past emancipation. The trial court increased support to $516 per month, denied extended support for the oldest child, and Nancy withdrew the motion for the middle child. Richard argued his income had not increased substantially and Nancy’s expenses had not increased substantially while her income rose. The Court of Appeals held that the trial court’s findings were inadequate under Moylan v. Moylan, which requires specific findings addressing statutory factors for modifying child support. The case was remanded for further factual findings consistent with Moylan.

Seven months after Trump administration cuts to Education Department staff and contracts, education researchers see cautious optimism. The Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) canceled over 100 research contracts in February; the department plans to reinstate 20. A lawsuit gives a short reprieve to 10 regional education labs (RELs). The department seeks public input on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES).

Tabbye Chavous of the American Educational Research Association called developments "cautiously encouraging," rating IES at 3-4 out of 10 (10 before cuts, 1 a month ago), but warned severe staff shortages threaten data quality. The administration brought in Amber Northern, a researcher from the Thomas B. Fordham Institute, to advise on reforming IES until December, giving researchers hope. One scholar said they are more hopeful about reinvention than death of federal education research. Mike Petrilli of Fordham said DOGE did great damage before anyone could stop it, but sees Northern's role as a sign they want to rebuild. Officials acknowledged early chaos and are shifting to performance-based contracting.

IES began advertising high-level NAEP jobs, surprising some, but NCES staff was cut from about 100 to three. Robert Kelchen, a University of Tennessee professor, said limited NCES resources make optimism hard, and an executive order requiring massive data collection on admissions practices retroactively is challenging. Poor NAEP results catalyzed support; reporting functions have been cut to save costs, and district-level reporting for some subjects ended. Cuts to databases could compromise NAEP after 2026.

The 10 RELs, funded at $336 million and closed over alleged wasteful spending, are expected to restart. Educators cited the REL Southeast's help in improving Mississippi reading scores. A researcher questioned if the money yielded exceptional change and noted an "education improvement industrial complex" that lobbies for funding was undercut. Some say IES should continue regardless of the department's fate. Kelchen said disruptions haven't heavily impacted his work but created classroom and university uncertainty.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed the district court's dismissal of an antitrust and tortious interference suit brought by Sea Breeze Salt, Inc. and Innofood, S.A. de C.V. against Mitsubishi entities and Exportadora de Sal, S.A. de C.V. (ESSA). ESSA, a Mexican salt producer 51% owned by the Mexican government, allegedly decided to sell its salt exclusively to Mitsubishi after terminating a director who had entered distribution contracts with Innofood. The court held the act of state doctrine barred the action. The doctrine precludes U.S. courts from judging official acts of a foreign sovereign performed within its own territory when relief would require invalidating that act. ESSA's choice to distribute substantially all of Mexico's salt exports through a single buyer constituted a sovereign act concerning the exploitation of natural resources, as sea salt is a state-owned resource under Mexico's constitution. Each of the five claims challenged that exclusive distribution policy, so granting relief would require a U.S. court to declare Mexico's sovereign decision invalid. The court also considered the Sabbatino factors: there is no international consensus condemning such exclusive arrangements, the case implicates foreign relations by potentially insulting Mexico and interfering with executive branch diplomacy, and the Mexican government still exists. The court declined to decide whether a commercial exception to the act of state doctrine exists because the challenged conduct involved powers peculiar to a sovereign, not purely commercial acts. Sea Breeze's appeal was not dismissed despite a temporary corporate suspension, as its status was normalized during the appeal. The holding is narrow, limited to the specific facts challenging Mexico's policy for disposing of its entire salt output.

UDMA write CRC corruption results from a corrupted state left by a previous UDMA read with host termination. After a device termination during a UDMA write, the ATAC fails to restart the CRC, causing errors. A host termination after device termination restarts the CRC, but this is unreliable. UDMA writes become generally unusable. Use UDMA I/O blocking (bit 8, ATAC Error MSR).

The double bottom chart pattern consists of two swing lows ending around the same level and a swing high between them. The swing lows establish support; the line connecting the swing high with the preceding swing high forms resistance called the neckline. The pattern is considered complete when price breaks above the neckline. It appears in a downtrend and may signal the end of the downtrend or a prolonged pullback in an uptrend, thus a bullish reversal pattern. Traders typically seek long positions upon a neckline breakout. Profit targets are estimated by measuring the pattern’s size and projecting upward from the neckline. Stop-loss can be placed in the middle for a 2:1 reward/risk ratio or below the pattern for safety but a poorer ratio. Aggressive traders may enter on the second low, looking for reversal signs like bullish candlestick patterns or RSI exiting oversold. Conservative traders wait for a confirmed breakout above the neckline with a close above it and increased volume. Backtesting is important but the strategy is difficult to quantify. Thomas Bulkowski's research in The Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns (2000) studied 500 stocks over five years, manually identifying patterns. The study may have survivorship bias, covered a bull market period, and relied on human interpretation, so results are only an indication. According to that research, 68% of double bottom formations reached their target, nearly twice the rate of double top patterns. The double bottom strategy outperformed the double top short strategy, expected due to stock market tailwinds. The author prefers a fully quantified backtest with 100% specific rules rather than relying on manually detected patterns.

This study used untargeted metabolomics to analyze hepatic vein and peripheral vein blood samples from 22 participants undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement, aiming to identify metabolite changes associated with post-TIPS hepatic encephalopathy (HE). The metabolome changed more in peripheral vein samples post-TIPS than in hepatic vein samples, with bile acids as the major contributors; bile acid levels dropped immediately after shunt placement but recovered by discharge. Participants who developed more severe HE had greater dissimilarity between pre- and post-TIPS hepatic vein metabolomes, suggesting less pre-existing intrahepatic shunting. Three conjugated hydroxylated bile acids in post-TIPS peripheral blood were inversely correlated with HE grade. In two participants readmitted for HE, these bile acids decreased at exacerbation and increased after treatment. Chemical proportionality analysis revealed that TIPS altered ratios of glycerophosphocholines and bilirubins, with biliverdin reduction and oxidation changes linked to HE severity. The findings indicate that intrahepatic shunting may protect against HE and that bile acids may play a protective role. Limitations include limited metabolite coverage, annotation level, and small cohort size.

Interferometric second-harmonic generation (SHG) polarimetry is used to resolve antiparallel domains and assess crystalline quality in CVD-grown hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). Conventional methods (TEM, STM, LEED, Raman) cannot efficiently detect antiparallel domains over large areas. SHG, a coherent process with a third-rank tensor susceptibility, is sensitive to orientational polarity: antiparallel domains produce out-of-phase SH fields, causing destructive interference. Ten types of CVD-grown hBN films on SiO₂/Si were compared with mechanically exfoliated references. SHG intensity varied by up to three orders of magnitude among samples, while Raman intensity varied only fourfold. Dual-polarization SHG imaging mapped crystallographic orientation, revealing domain structures. A polycrystalline few-layer sample showed two dominant orientations with a broad spread (~4.6°). A monolayer sample grown on Cu exhibited nearly unidirectional alignment but with meandering boundaries of weak SHG. A few-layer sample on Fe-Ni displayed randomly oriented domains with narrow orientational spread. Correlated SHG-Raman analysis showed that Raman intensity, SHG intensity, orientational spread, and Raman linewidth serve as quantitative crystallinity indicators; SHG intensity and orientational spread are more sensitive to disorder. Numerical simulations with a mixed-domain model indicated that random orientation alone cannot explain the large SHG reduction; instead, antiparallel domains (UP/DOWN populations) cause destructive interference, with intensity dropping sharply as the antiparallel fraction approaches 0.5. Interferometric SHG using a local oscillator confirmed antiparallel domains: phase shifts of π were observed at boundaries in the Cu-grown sample, and in a sample with sub-diffraction-limit domains, some spots showed a π phase shift despite uniform orientation. The framework uses Raman intensity and linewidth as initial quality indicators, orientational SHG imaging to visualize domains, and SHG intensity as a metric for antiparallel domain size. The methodology is broadly applicable to other non-centrosymmetric 2D materials.

The passage presents container patterns for distributed systems. The adapter pattern uses sidecar containers to adapt existing services to monitoring interfaces (Prometheus), normalize logging formats (Fluentd), and add health checks (MySQL). Replicated load-balanced services provide stateless serving with readiness probes, session tracking, caching layers (Varnish), and SSL termination (nginx). Sharded services partition data across replicas for scalability, employing sharding functions and consistent hashing; they can be combined with replication for reliability. The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes requests across leaves to reduce latency but faces straggler issues; sharding can be applied to leaves. James D. Rone sued Boncar Construction Co. for injuries sustained at an Indiana sewer project. His complaint included Count I under the Illinois Structural Work Act, Count II under an Indiana statute requiring communication systems, and Count III for wilful and wanton negligence (later dropped). The trial court struck Count I, ruling the Illinois Act did not apply to an out-of-state accident. After an earlier appeal was dismissed without prejudice, a jury returned a verdict for Boncar on Count II.

On appeal, the court held: (1) The order striking Count I was final and appealable when entered, but Rone waived appeal by not perfecting it then. (2) The trial court properly submitted negligence and proximate cause to the jury because conflicting inferences could be drawn from undisputed facts regarding whether a signal system existed and whether its absence caused the injury. (3) The court correctly refused to direct a finding for Rone on contributory negligence; it was a jury question, and the Indiana Employers Liability Act did not apply because the suit was not against Rone’s employer. (4) No error occurred in refusing two proposed jury instructions, as their substance was covered by other instructions. The judgment was affirmed.

Opening range breakout (ORB) strategies involve trading when price breaks above the high or below the low of a defined opening range, often based on the first few minutes of a session. Backtests on S&P 500 futures using minute bars show that simple ORB strategies produce minuscule average gains (best 0.04% per trade) and low win rates. Flipping to short breakouts yields even worse results. Tests on Nasdaq, gold, silver, and oil futures also gave negative results. The article states that ORB strategies no longer work well without additional filters. Reasons include multiple false breakouts, most gains occurring during the night session, computer power quickly arbitraging away opportunities, and daily highs and lows often occurring in the first and last hour, making ORB entries late. Adding daily filters (based on longer trends, volume, reversal patterns, etc.) can improve performance. An example strategy using one daily filter on 1-minute bars showed 198 trades, 0.27% average gain, 65% win rate, and a profit factor of 2. The article suggests that specific stocks may yield better results than indices. Traders can find their own ORB strategy through strategy optimization but must avoid curve fitting. Overall, ORB strategies are much less relevant now for the most traded futures contracts or ETFs, and daily filters are recommended without overfitting.

The Amoeba defense, created by Jerry Tarkanian, was crucial for UNLV's 1990 NCAA Championship. It is an aggressive, trapping match-up zone from a 1-1-3 alignment, designed to disrupt opponents. The on-ball defender applies extreme pressure while the other four zone. It requires quick guards and generates steals and transition baskets. Initial alignment: point guard pressures the ballhandler near midcourt, X2 at the free throw line, wings X3 and X4 between the line and baseline, X5 protects the basket. The defense employs various traps and rotations. On a wing pass, X2 pressures, X3 fronts the post, X5 denies lobs, X4 takes a low Helpside I, X1 drops to high post. Corner traps involve X2 following the pass to trap with X3, forming a Triangle I with other defenders. Wing traps on dribble have X3 trapping with X2, also forming a Triangle I. A post/wing exchange (X cut) occurs when X5 pressures the corner and X3 dives to front the post. Skip passes trigger close-outs and role exchanges. Ball reversal requires X1 to hesitate before pressuring. Against a two-guard front, X1 and X2 match up, and a high post entry is triple-teamed by X1, X2, and X5, while X3 and X4 deny wings. If the post passes out, X3 pressures, X1 denies return, X5 drops low.

AEGEAN study: time to apixaban initiation ~1.6-1.8 days. Exposure and interruptions comparable across groups. Most received 5 mg BID; dose modifications infrequent. Compliance >95% at Weeks 4-24, >94% at Week 48.

Mean 24-week adherence: 91.64% (Primary SOC) vs 91.88% (Additional Educational Program), no significant difference. Adherence declined significantly over time (p<0.0001). At 48 weeks, adherence from Week 24-48 was 87.59%-88.41% across groups, no differences. Persistence at 24 weeks ~91%, at 48 weeks 85.2%-87.8%, no differences.

Logit models: In Primary SOC, non-adherence at 24 weeks increased with alcohol, technical occupations, permanent AF, decreased with MMSE; at 48 weeks, decreased with MMSE. In Additional Educational Program, no predictors at 24 weeks; at 48 weeks, increased with age, VKA-naïve status, permanent AF.

Subgroup analyses: no interaction for adherence at 24/48 weeks. For Week 24-48 adherence, significant interactions by AF type (Secondary vs Primary SOC difference: permanent 7.05%, persistent 0.69%, paroxysmal -3.64%) and sex (Continued Additional Educational Program vs Secondary SOC: males 4.53%, females -4.18%).

Safety similar between groups. Before Week 24: any AE 51.2% vs 52.0%, serious AE 12.4% vs 14.7%, bleeding 6.5% vs 9.0%, major bleeding <1.1%, one fatal bleed. After Week 24: any AE 33.8%-40.8%, serious AE 11.8%-14.0%, bleeding 3.2%-4.1%, major bleeding ≤0.7%, two fatal bleeds. 24 deaths total. No pregnancies or hepatic/renal signals.

Conclusion: high adherence and persistence through 48 weeks; educational program did not improve outcomes.

Momentum investing buys stocks with the best historical performance over 3-12 months and periodically rebalances to hold the highest momentum stocks, based on the hypothesis that past medium-term returns correlate with future returns. Research by Eric Crittenden found that from 1989 to 2015, approximately 20% of stocks accounted for all market gains, while 80% had zero lifetime returns, showing a negatively skewed distribution. A simple monthly momentum strategy for the S&P 500 using a moving average crossover was backtested from 1960 to February 2023. Starting with $100,000, it grew to $5.575 million, an annual return of 6.6% versus buy-and-hold’s 7%, but was invested only 69% of the time with smaller drawdowns (26% vs. 55%). The risk-adjusted return was 9.5%. The average loss was under 5% and average winner nearly 25%. The S&P 500 Momentum Index (ticker SP500MUP) measures stocks with relative strength. The blog offers over 1200 articles and a compilation of trading strategies for purchase, with logic in plain English for Python backtesting.

The passage describes various design patterns for distributed systems using containers. It begins with the adapter pattern, using Fluentd to normalize logs from different sources like Redis and Storm into a consistent format, and adding health checks to a MySQL container via an adapter container. It then introduces microservices as loosely coupled, multi-node architectures that improve reliability and agility but complicate debugging. The replicated load-balanced service pattern is detailed, covering stateless services with readiness probes, session-tracked services using consistent hashing, and application-layer enhancements like caching layers (Varnish) and SSL termination (nginx). Sharded services are presented for scaling stateful data, using sharded caches with memcache and an ambassador or shared routing service, along with considerations for sharding functions and consistent hashing. The scatter/gather pattern is explained for parallelizing requests across leaves, with examples of document search, and issues like the straggler problem. Event-driven processing with FaaS is discussed, highlighting benefits, challenges, and patterns such as the decorator pattern for request transformation, event handling for two-factor authentication, and event-based pipelines for user signup. Finally, the master election pattern is introduced for distributed ownership, contrasting it with a singleton approach and noting reliability trade-offs.

Overbought means the stock market has risen significantly over a defined period, indicating potentially weaker short-term returns. It can be defined using indicators like the Relative Strength Index (RSI), for example when the 2-day RSI is above 95. Overbought is bearish, suggesting a possible price correction. Mean-reversion, or regression to the mean, is the statistical concept that strong deviations from a trend tend to reverse and move toward the average. Overbought conditions primarily predict short-term results, not long-term weakness. The media can amplify overbought conditions by publishing positive articles, creating FOMO, while negative articles during downturns may cause panic. A backtest showed lower returns in the first five days after an overbought signal, with returns later gravitating toward the long-term average. Short-selling based on overbought signals is difficult and not a tradeable strategy.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers offer three oscillator modes: internal oscillator mode (RT resistor sets 100 kHz–2 MHz switching frequency, SYNC outputs a 2× frequency clock), external synchronization mode (RT floating, external clock 200 kHz–4 MHz with 40–60% duty cycle at SYNC), and primary-secondary mode (primary controller's SYNC output drives secondary's SYNC input). Primary outputs OUTA/OUTB and synchronous rectifier outputs SRA/SRB vary by device. Dead times TDPS and TDSP are programmable via PS and SP resistors for TPS7H5001/2-SP; TPS7H5003-SP has fixed 50 ns. Leading edge blank time is programmable via LEB resistor (fixed for TPS7H5003-SP). Duty cycle limit is set by DCL pin: 50% (DCL=AVSS, only TPS7H5001/4-SP), 75% (floating), or 100% (DCL=VLDO). Current sense at CS_ILIM compares sensed current to COMP/2; overcurrent at 1.05 V triggers hiccup mode with delay and restart times set by HICC capacitor. FAULT pin initiates shutdown when >0.6 V. Slope compensation is set by RSC resistor. Frequency compensation uses Type 2A or 2B network. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C. A synchronous push-pull converter design example details component selection for RT, feedback resistors, dead time, blank time, soft-start, transformer, FETs, clamp, output inductor, output capacitance, current sense resistor, hiccup capacitor, compensation, and slope compensation. Layout guidelines recommend separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switch node area, and placing bypass capacitors close to the controller.

The lecture covers coherent (collective) Thomson scattering, where the scattering wavelength (2π/k, with k = ks − ki) is larger than the Debye length, sampling collective plasma motion. The relevant modes are ion acoustic waves (ω = √((Z Te + Ti)/mi) k) and electron plasma waves (ω² = ωp² + 3 vte² k²), which exist as thermal fluctuations. The scattered power spectrum is proportional to the spectral density function S(k,ω) = (1/(ne V T)) ⟨|ne(k,ω)|²⟩. Using a Klimontovich distribution and a test-particle treatment, S(k,ω) is derived as (2π/(k ne)) [ |1 − χe/ε|² fe(ω/k) + |χe/ε|² Σi (Zi² ni/ne) fi(ω/k) ], where ε = 1 + χe + χi is the permittivity, χ are susceptibilities, and f are one-dimensional velocity distributions. Peaks occur when ε = 0, corresponding to normal modes. To obtain χ, the Vlasov equation is solved for a warm plasma including Landau damping, giving χj = (qj²/(ε0 mj k)) ∫ (∂fj/∂v)/(ω − k v) dv. For a Maxwellian, χj = (1/(k² λDj²)) (nj Te)/(ne Tj) w(ζj), with ζj = ω/(k vth,j) and w(ζ) a complex function containing an integral and a Landau residue term, related to the plasma dispersion function and tabulated for computation.

This document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. It defines the GHCB as a 4KB decrypted page used to share register state during Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs). Version 2 introduces hypervisor feature advertisement via a FEATURES bitmap, support for SEV-SNP, and enhancements like XSS MSR handling. The GHCB MSR protocol uses the lower 12 bits of MSR 0xc001_0130 for requests such as SEV information, CPUID, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration, page state change, and termination. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before use. The document lists supported NAE events, required guest state, and error handling. It also covers SNP Guest Request and Extended Guest Request events, which use shared request/response pages and certificate data pages, respectively. Additional topics include SMP booting, restricted injection, and the SEV-SNP secrets page layout.

Dr. Jeanine Wiener-Kronish, chief of anesthesia at Massachusetts General Hospital, convened a task force in June 2009 to address persistent inefficiencies and long patient wait times in the Pre-Admission Testing Area (PATA). A patient letter described a nearly four-hour visit with only 1.5 hours of face time, prompting urgency. PATA, an outpatient clinic with 12 exam rooms, completed pre-admission work-ups for 43% of surgical patients, prioritizing complex cases due to limited capacity. The process involved a lab technician (vitals, EKG), a registered nurse (nursing assessment), and an anesthesiologist (health assessment, consent), followed by blood work. Appointments were scheduled every half-hour, averaging 55 patients daily. Manual tracking via a charge nurse and index cards led to communication gaps and delays. Providers often stayed late, and only 65% of out-patients were seen, with the rest worked up on surgery day, causing operating room delays. The task force, led by Executive Director Susan Moss, had previously failed to secure additional resources. During the meeting, suggestions included extending clinic hours, reducing patient volume, or improving efficiency with existing resources. An MBA intern offered to analyze time-study data to evaluate scenarios. Moss urged challenging all assumptions and preparing to discuss changes based on the analysis.

The Imperial Russian Government acknowledged the seizure of the bark Cape Horn Pigeon was unjustifiable and some indemnity was due, but rejected the principal claim for loss of services. Claimants later submitted all expenses. In 1899, the U.S. offered a $42,000 compromise, stating refusal would not prejudice full recovery rights. Russia rejected this and offered $2,500. Additional evidence included treaty obligations. The Okhotsk Sea, a vast North Pacific arm, had never been effectively occupied by Russia, which never publicly asserted a right to prohibit fishing or whaling beyond ordinary jurisdiction. Treaties of 1824 and 1825 with the U.S. and Great Britain, and long foreign whaling use, indicated no intent to claim prohibition. Affidavits confirmed it was a common whaling ground. The captain stated the Russian commander declared the sea closed and seized the vessel. Such a claim would be hard to maintain under international law, even without the treaties. The 1824 treaty guaranteed freedom of navigation and fishing in the Pacific.

A cross-sectional study investigated associations between personal health literacy, school health literacy environment, and health outcomes among 7,264 Chinese schoolteachers from 11 schools in Zhengzhou, Henan Province. Personal health literacy was measured with the HLS19-Q12, and school health literacy environment with the OHLS-Q-SF. Health outcomes included health status, health-compromising behaviours (smoking, alcohol, physical inactivity), health service use, and healthcare cost. 56.9% of teachers had inadequate or problematic health literacy. Personal health literacy varied by school type, age, marital status, teaching duration, subject, health awareness, chronic conditions, and medical insurance; school health literacy environment showed similar sociodemographic differences. After adjusting for covariates and the other health literacy component, teachers with inadequate health literacy had higher odds of poor health status (OR=5.79), at least one health-compromising behaviour (OR=2.90), at least one health service use (OR=2.73), and healthcare cost ≥1000 RMB (OR=2.51) compared to those with excellent health literacy. Teachers perceiving a less supportive school health literacy environment also had higher odds of these outcomes (ORs 1.13–1.78). The study concludes that both personal health literacy and school health literacy environment are associated with teachers’ health outcomes, and promoting health literacy at individual and organizational levels may improve health and reduce disparities.
