Ronald L. Johnson appealed the denial of his habeas corpus petition, which challenged the admission of his confession at a 1964 trial that occurred before Escobedo and Miranda. The First Circuit applied the Procunier v. Atchley “totality of the circumstances” standard for voluntariness. The court independently reviewed the undisputed facts: Johnson was arrested after a car chase, was injured, belligerent, and refused to sign a telephone rights form, stating he knew his rights. He participated in line-ups, was identified, and after about 8.5 hours in custody gave a 40-minute confession without being advised of his rights. The court considered his prior police contacts, hostile demeanor, and the absence of police-inflicted injury. It concluded his will was not overborne and the confession was voluntary, even under the Lego v. Twomey preponderance standard. The denial of the writ was affirmed.

University of Utah scientists mapped the near-surface geology of Old Faithful, revealing a hydrothermal reservoir that feeds the geyser. Using a dense network of 133 portable seismometers and new analysis techniques, they studied ground shaking. The reservoir, a network of cracks and fractures, has a diameter of about 200 meters and holds approximately 300,000 cubic meters of water. Each eruption releases around 30 cubic meters. The study found that seismic tremors, caused by imploding hot pressurized bubbles as the reservoir refills, last about 60 minutes; the eruption occurs at the end of the tremor period, just before quiet. The team used ambient seismic noise and hydrothermal features as sources. The research, published in Geophysical Research Letters, was led by doctoral student Sin-Mei Wu and involved long-time researcher Robert Smith. The Park Service requested the survey due to buildings over thermal features. Future work includes studying air temperature effects, earthquake wave reverberation, and applying similar analysis to Norris Geyser Basin.

The Healthy Davis Together (HDT) program, later expanded to Healthy Yolo Together (HYT), provided free saliva-based asymptomatic COVID-19 testing in Yolo County, California, from November 2020 to June 2022. A total of 770,165 tests were conducted among 89,924 residents, reaching approximately 41.1% of the county population and 78.4% of Davis residents. Study periods were defined by variant dominance: Pre-Delta, Delta, Omicron, and Post-Omicron.

Testing participation varied over time. The Omicron period had the highest daily testing rate (895 per 100,000 population) and the highest number of positive cases (50.3% of all program positives). New tester enrollment declined across periods, from 39,819 in Pre-Delta to 2,788 in Post-Omicron. Overall, 43.1% of participants were female and 37.3% male. The highest positivity rates were observed among American Indian/Alaska Native (7.6%), Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander (5.6%), Latinos (4.5%), and individuals aged 20–44 years.

Frequent testers (multiple tests within 15 days) were most prominent during Omicron (39.7% of that period’s testers). Among all frequent testers aged 18 and older, 59% were women, 39.8% were aged 19–34, and 52.2% were White. Participation from women and younger adults remained consistently higher throughout the program. After Omicron, testing participation dropped considerably. The discussion notes that observed patterns align with existing literature on gender differences in risk perception and that pandemic fatigue, vaccines, and at-home tests may have influenced later participation. The data do not allow conclusions about the reasons for observed differences.

Flu season in Indiana has caused 278 deaths and can last until mid-April. Infectious diseases like flu, colds, and gastrointestinal illnesses spread through contact. Flu virus can survive on surfaces for about a day, while norovirus can remain viable for days or weeks on doorknobs, faucets, and toilets. Touching contaminated surfaces then the face can cause infection. A handwashing experiment found no significant difference in bacteria before and after washing, indicating insufficient scrubbing. IU Health recommends washing with regular soap for 20-30 seconds, scrubbing front, back, wrists, and under nails, then rinsing. A cell phone test revealed only normal skin and mouth bacteria, but bringing phones to the face can transfer pathogens. Proper handwashing is the easiest way to prevent illness and transmission.

This study explored how walking can be transformed into an aesthetic experience through art-based practices, involving seven prospective teachers in a 10-week online undergraduate course in western Türkiye following the 2023 earthquake. Participants integrated walking into their daily routines, created visual and textual diaries, took photographs, and engaged in aesthetic inquiry focused on Francis Alÿs’ performance “The Collector.” Data were collected from visual diaries, course recordings, participant texts, and interviews, and analyzed using thematic analysis. Three themes emerged: from conceptual perception to sensory experience, artistic inquiry of walking, and place in art-based practices. Initially defining walking as a simple act, participants expanded their meanings to include freedom, self-discovery, and social critique. They developed sensory awareness by noticing sounds, sights, and rhythms of their environments, and produced artworks such as videos, collages, and digital pieces reflecting personal and social issues. The process helped them connect everyday life to art and pedagogy, fostering multiple perspectives and critical thinking. The study suggests that walking can enhance environmental awareness and serve as a teaching tool in teacher education.

Diluted earnings per share were $1.26 for the quarter and $4.67 for the nine months.

Net sales by category for the quarter: iPhone $39.7 billion, Mac $6.8 billion, iPad $5.8 billion, Wearables, Home and Accessories $8.3 billion, and Services $21.2 billion. Services net sales increased 8% year-over-year. Products gross margin percentage was 35.4% (up from 34.5%), and Services gross margin percentage was 70.5% (down from 71.5%). Total gross margin percentage was 44.5%. Operating expenses were $13.4 billion, including $7.4 billion in research and development. The effective tax rate was 12.5% for the quarter.

The Company announced new products including a 15-inch MacBook Air, Mac Studio, Mac Pro, and Apple Vision Pro, expected in early calendar 2024. The Company repurchased $18.0 billion of common stock in the quarter and paid dividends of $0.24 per share. As of July 1, 2023, cash and cash equivalents were $28.4 billion, marketable securities were $138.1 billion, and total term debt was $105.3 billion.

Segment net sales: Americas $35.4 billion (down 6%), Europe $20.2 billion (up 5%), Greater China $15.8 billion (up 8%), Japan $4.8 billion (down 11%), and Rest of Asia Pacific $5.6 billion (down 8%). The European Commission’s State Aid Decision appeal was heard in May 2023, with an ECJ decision expected in 2024. In the Epic Games litigation, the Ninth Circuit affirmed the District Court’s ruling, and the Company’s motion to stay an injunction pending appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court was granted.

India's Supreme Court ordered that parties cannot seek votes based on religion, caste, creed, community, or language. The author finds this problematic. He argues that identity-based politics arises from discrimination and has helped marginalized communities organize as vote banks, challenging hierarchies. The constitution itself provides for reserved seats. While rabid communalism exists, the solution is stronger rule of law, not judicial orders. The order is un-implementable because caste, language, and religion pervade elections at all levels. The author concludes that the judiciary should allow electoral democracy to evolve naturally, as identity cleavages express themselves in politics globally.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2018. The unaudited consolidated financial statements show net sales of $56.6 billion for the third quarter and $160.5 billion for the first nine months of 2018, with net income of $2.9 billion and $7.0 billion, respectively. Operating income was $3.7 billion for the quarter and $8.6 billion for the nine-month period. Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaled $21.0 billion at quarter-end.

The company operates in three segments: North America, International, and AWS. North America sales grew 35% in Q3, International sales grew 13%, and AWS sales grew 46%. Operating income increased in North America and AWS, while the International segment reduced its operating loss. The results include Whole Foods Market from its August 2017 acquisition date.

The report details accounting policies, including the adoption of new revenue recognition guidance effective January 1, 2018, which increased retained earnings by approximately $650 million and reclassified certain Prime membership fees and advertising services. Recent acquisitions include Ring Inc. and PillPack, Inc. for approximately $839 million and $753 million, respectively. Long-term debt face value was $24.8 billion. The company also discusses income tax contingencies, including a European Commission state aid decision requiring a recovery amount deposited into escrow, and ongoing IRS transfer pricing litigation.

The #MeToo movement led to resignations of Canadian politicians Jamie Baillie, Patrick Brown, and Kent Hehr after allegations of impropriety, none proven in court. Backlash compared it to McCarthyism, with fears of capricious accusations against men. The author argues women distinguish between sexual coercion and clumsy passes, and that parties should hold leaders to a higher standard, as a response reflects how they value women. The prime minister’s stance of starting from belief is discussed; fairness is said to include a presumption of truth-telling by the alleged victim. The timing of accusations is questioned but explained by women now being believed. The movement must be fair, and the historical silencing of women by disbelief must change.

Abraaj, the largest private equity firm for developing economies managing $13.6 billion, and its founder Mr. Naqvi were praised by Mr. Kim for their model of using large capital pools to profit from investments like hospitals in Pakistan and Nigeria. Abraaj’s $1 billion health care fund drew $545 million to buy hospitals in Nigeria, Pakistan, and India. In September, investors discovered over $200 million in uninvested cash and requested bank statements, citing a requirement to return unused funds within 60 days. Mr. Naqvi said the cash was needed to buy hospitals globally and cited regulatory delays, but investors were unconvinced; he returned more than $100 million in December. Investors, including Proparco and CDC Group, sought an independent auditor and forensic proof the money was not used for Abraaj’s operations. Abraaj hired KPMG for its own audit. The U.S. Overseas Private Investment Corporation had a $150 million loan exposure. The World Bank invested $300 million with Abraaj, including $100 million in the health fund via the IFC, and the Gates Foundation invested $100 million. A World Bank corruption investigation closed without finding wrongdoing. Mr. Kim continued praising Mr. Naqvi during a November video conference. The health fund was already struggling, having invested half its capital; its largest investment, a $145 million purchase of CARE hospitals in India, saw earnings drop from $14 million to $8 million, and its value was not marked down. Mr. Naqvi founded Abraaj in 2002 and is now raising a $6 billion fund for society-improving investments in 30 developing countries.

Indiana is turning to outcomes-based contracting to address middle school reading struggles, hiring private tutoring companies with pay tied to student improvement. State education secretary Katie Jenner, finding no successful models from other states, challenged vendors to "put your money where your mouth is" after reading scores fell. Contract details are undecided, but the state may draw on examples from Texas, Florida, Arkansas, and the Southern Education Foundation's Center for Outcomes-Based Contracting (established 2024). The model ties at least 40% of pay to student gains, though results are mixed: in 2025, about half of learning goals were met, with vendors earning 68% of possible bonuses. The approach has grown from a 4-district pilot in 2022 to 60 districts/agencies testing it. Research is limited and anecdotal; Stanford researchers noted "promising" findings like closer collaboration and data tracking, but cited financial risks for vendors and implementation complexity. Examples include Duval County's continued use of 50% guaranteed/50% incentive pay, boosting math growth, while Ector County and Denver saw mixed results. Indiana's contracts will target struggling students, who often face attendance and motivation challenges. The state may use vetted vendor lists and seek donations and grants. Jenner touted the strategy at a U.S. Senate hearing as a way to ensure return on investment.
